entries.zh: 世祖在晉陽，旣居舊殿，少帝未有別所，詔子琮監造大明宮。
entries.en: When Shizu was at Jinyang, he occupied the old palace, while the young emperor had no separate residence, so he ordered Zicong to supervise construction of the Daming Palace.
entries.literal: When Shizu was at Jinyang, he already occupied the old palace, and the young emperor had no separate quarters, so he ordered Zicong to supervise construction of the Daming Palace.

entries.zh: 宮成，世祖親自巡幸，怪其不甚宏麗。
entries.en: When the palace was completed, Shizu personally toured it and was surprised that it was not especially grand or splendid.
entries.literal: When the palace was completed, Shizu personally toured it and wondered that it was not very grand and splendid.

entries.zh: 子琮對曰：「至尊幼年，纂承大業，欲令敦行節儉，以示萬邦。
entries.en: Zicong replied, "The sovereign is young and has inherited the great enterprise; I wanted him to practice sincere frugality as a model for the realm.
entries.literal: Zicong replied, "The sovereign is young and has inherited the great enterprise; I wanted him to practice sincere frugality and show it to the ten thousand states.

entries.zh: 兼此北連天闕，不宜過復崇峻。」
entries.en: Moreover, this palace connects northward to the Heavenly Gate, so it should not be made too lofty and imposing."
entries.literal: Moreover, this palace connects northward to the Heavenly Gate, so it should not again be excessively lofty and imposing."

entries.zh: 世祖稱善。
entries.en: Shizu approved.
entries.literal: Shizu praised this.

entries.zh: 肅宗作相，除黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: When Gao Yan was made chief minister, Yong was made attendant of the yellow gate.

entries.zh: 於華林園射，特賜金帶寶器服玩雜物五百種。
entries.en: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.
entries.literal: At the Hualin Garden archery review he was specially given five hundred kinds of gold belts, precious vessels, robes, playthings, and miscellaneous goods.

entries.zh: 天統初，除侍中、幷州大中正，又拜護軍，餘如故。
entries.en: Early in Tiantong he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province, and was again appointed General Who Protects the Army; his remaining offices stayed as before.
entries.literal: Early in Tiantong he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province, and was again appointed General Who Protects the Army; his remaining offices stayed as before.

entries.zh: 邕以軍民教習田獵，依令十二月，月別三圍，以為人馬疲敝，奏請每月兩圍。
entries.en: Yong thought military and civilian field-hunt instruction, which by statute ran three hunts each month in the twelfth month, wore out men and horses, and memorialized for two hunts each month.
entries.literal: Yong, because military and civilian instruction in field hunts followed the statute of the twelfth month with three hunts each month, thought men and horses were worn out and memorialized asking for two hunts each month.

entries.zh: 世祖從之。
entries.en: Gao Zhan approved it.
entries.literal: Gao Zhan followed it.

entries.zh: 後出為趙州刺史，餘官如故。
entries.en: Later he went out as governor of Zhao; his other offices remained as before.
entries.literal: Later he went out as governor of Zhao province; his other offices remained as before.

entries.zh: 世祖謂邕曰：「朝臣未有帶侍中、護軍、中正作州者，以卿故有此舉，放卿百餘日休息，至秋間當即追卿。」
entries.en: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Protects the Army, and Grand Rectifier while serving as a provincial governor; this move is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days of rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once."
entries.literal: Gao Zhan said to Yong, "No court minister has yet held Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Protects the Army, and Grand Rectifier while serving as a provincial governor; this move is because of you. I give you more than a hundred days of rest; in autumn I shall recall you at once."

entries.zh: 遷右僕射，又遷尚書令，封晉昌王，錄尚書事。
entries.en: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to right vice director, then again to director of the masters of writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Jinchang, and made recorder of the masters of writing affairs.

entries.zh: 屬周師來寇，丞相高阿那肱率兵赴援，邕配割不甚從允，因此有隙。
entries.en: When Zhou troops came to raid, Chancellor Gao Anaigong led an army to relieve the siege; Tang Yong's supply allotments were not fully approved, and the two fell out.
entries.literal: As Zhou troops came to raid, Chancellor Gao Anaigong led troops to the relief; Yong's allocations and distributions were not fully approved, and on this account a rift opened.

entries.zh: 肱譖之，遣侍中斛律孝卿宣旨責讓，留身禁止，尋釋之。
entries.en: Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing with an edict of rebuke; Tang Yong was held in custody, then soon released.
entries.literal: Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing to proclaim an edict rebuking and reproaching him; Yong was detained in custody and soon released.

entries.zh: 車駕將幸晉陽，勑孝卿總知騎兵度支，事多自決，不相詢稟。
entries.en: As the emperor was about to visit Jinyang, an edict put Hulü Xiaoqing in overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters himself and did not consult or report upward.
entries.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to visit Jinyang, an edict ordered Xiaoqing to take overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters on his own and did not consult or report upward.

entries.zh: 邕自恃從霸朝以來常典樞要，歷事六帝，恩遇甚重，一旦為孝卿所輕，負氣鬱怏，形於辭色。
entries.en: Tang Yong relied on having held pivotal posts since the hegemonic court, served six emperors, and enjoyed heavy favor—yet was suddenly slighted by Xiaoxiaoqing; bitter and sullen, he showed it in speech and face.
entries.literal: Yong relied on himself—from the hegemonic court onward he had constantly held pivotal posts, served six emperors, and received very heavy favor—yet was suddenly slighted by Xiaoxiaoqing; resentful and sullen, he showed it in word and countenance.

entries.zh: 帝平陽敗後，狼狽還鄴都。
entries.en: After the emperor's defeat at Pingyang, he fled back to Ye in disarray.
entries.literal: After the emperor's defeat at Pingyang, he returned to the capital Ye in disarray.

entries.zh: 邕懼那肱譖之，恨斛律孝卿輕己，遂留晉陽，與莫多婁敬顯等崇樹安德王為帝。
entries.en: Tang Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and resented Hulü Xiaoqing's slight; he stayed at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.
entries.literal: Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and hated that Hulü Xiaoqing slighted him; he therefore remained at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.

entries.zh: 信宿城陷，邕遂降周，依例授儀同大將軍。
entries.en: Within a day or two the city fell; Tang Yong surrendered to Zhou and, by precedent, was made Yitong Grand General.
entries.literal: Within a day or two the city fell; Yong then surrendered to Zhou and was appointed, by precedent, Yitong Grand General.

entries.zh: 卒於鳳州刺史。
entries.en: He died as governor of Feng Province.
entries.literal: He died while serving as governor of Feng Province.

entries.zh: 唐邕，字道和，太原晉陽人，其先自晉昌徙焉。
entries.en: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.
entries.literal: Tang Yong, styled Daohe, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan; his ancestors had moved there from Jinchang.

entries.zh: 父靈芝，魏壽陽令。
entries.en: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.
entries.literal: His father Lingzhi was Wei magistrate of Shouyang.

entries.zh: 邕少明敏，有治世才具。
entries.en: Yong was bright and keen from youth and had the talent to order an age.
entries.literal: Yong from youth was bright and keen and had the talent and equipment to order an age.

entries.zh: 太昌初，或薦於高祖，命其直外兵曹，典執文帳。
entries.en: In the first Taichang year someone recommended him to Gao Huan, who had him attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taichang someone recommended him to Gao Huan; Gao Huan ordered him to attend the outer military affairs bureau and manage written registers.

entries.zh: 齊朝因高祖作相，丞相府外兵曹、騎兵曹分掌兵馬。
entries.en: In Northern Qi, when the Grand Ancestor became chancellor, the grand chancellor's external military bureau and cavalry bureau divided control of troops and horses.
entries.literal: In Northern Qi, because the Grand Ancestor was made chancellor, the Grand Chancellor's office external military bureau and cavalry bureau divided control of troops and horses.

entries.zh: 及天保受禪，諸司監咸歸尚書，唯此二曹不廢，令唐邕、白建主治，謂之外兵省、騎兵省。
entries.en: When Tianbao received the mandate, all office supervisors went to the Masters of Writing, but these two bureaus remained; Tang Yong and Bai Jian headed them, called the External Troops Department and Cavalry Department.
entries.literal: When Tianbao received the mandate, all office supervisors were folded into the Masters of Writing, but these two bureaus were not abolished; Tang Yong and Bai Jian were put in charge of them, called the External Troops Department and Cavalry Department.

entries.zh: 其後邕、建位望轉隆，各為省主，令中書舍人分判二省事，故世稱唐、白云。
entries.en: Later Yong and Jian rose higher; each became head of his department, with secretariat gentlemen to divide their affairs—hence the age called them Tang and Bai.
entries.literal: Later Yong and Jian's standing grew ever loftier; each became head of his department; secretariat gentlemen were assigned to divide decisions on the two departments' affairs—hence the age called them Tang and Bai.

entries.zh: 尉瑾 馮子琮 赫連子悅 唐邕 白建
entries.en: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian
entries.literal: Yu Jin; Feng Zicong; Helian Ziyue; Tang Yong; Bai Jian

entries.zh: 潛從祖兄懷仁，字子友，魏司徒司馬道將之子。
entries.en: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.
entries.literal: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.

entries.zh: 懷仁涉學有文辭，情性恬靖，常蕭然有閑放之致。
entries.en: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.
entries.literal: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.

entries.zh: 歷太尉記室、弘農郡守，不之任，卜居陳留界。
entries.en: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.
entries.literal: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.

entries.zh: 所著詩賦銘頌二萬餘言，又撰《中表實錄》二十卷。
entries.en: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.
entries.literal: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.

entries.zh: 懷仁有行檢，善與人交，與瑯邪王衍、隴西李壽之情好相得。
entries.en: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.
entries.literal: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.

entries.zh: 曾語衍云：「昔太丘道廣，許劭知而不顧；
entries.en: He once told Yan, "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;
entries.literal: He once told Yan: "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;

entries.zh: 嵇生性惰，鐘會過而絕言。
entries.en: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.
entries.literal: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.

entries.zh: 吾處季、孟之間，去其泰甚。」
entries.en: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."
entries.literal: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."

entries.zh: 愆以為然。
entries.en: Yan thought it so.
entries.literal: Yan thought it so.

entries.zh: 武平末卒。
entries.en: He died late in Wuping.
entries.literal: He died late in Wuping.

entries.zh: 陽斐 盧潛 崔劼 盧叔武 陽休之 袁聿修
entries.en: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu
entries.literal: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu

entries.zh: 李稚廉，趙郡高邑人也。
entries.en: Li Zhilian came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
entries.literal: Li Zhilian, a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

entries.zh: 齊州刺史義深之弟。
entries.en: He was the younger brother of Yishen, inspector of Qi province.
entries.literal: Younger brother of Yishen, inspector of Qi province.

entries.zh: 稚廉少而寡欲，為兒童時，初不從家人有所求請。
entries.en: Zhilian from youth was sparing in desire; as a child he would not ask his family for anything.
entries.literal: Zhilian from youth was few in desires; as a child he would not at first ask anything of his family.

entries.zh: 家人嘗故以金寶授之，終不取，強付，輒擲之於地。
entries.en: His family once deliberately gave him gold and jewels; he never took them, and when they forced them on him he threw them to the ground.
entries.literal: His family once deliberately gave him gold and jewels; he never took them, and when they forced payment he would throw them to the ground.

entries.zh: 州牧以其蒙稚而廉，故名曰稚廉。
entries.en: The provincial governor, because he was young and yet frugal, gave him the name Zhilian.
entries.literal: The provincial governor, because he was young and yet frugal, therefore named him Zhilian.

entries.zh: 聰敏好學，年十五，頗尋覽五經章句。
entries.en: Clever and fond of learning, at fifteen he had already worked through the chapter-and-commentary texts of the Five Classics.
entries.literal: Clever and fond of learning; at fifteen he had already gone through the chapter-and-commentary texts of the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 屬葛榮作亂，本郡紛擾，違難赴京。
entries.en: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion the native commandery was in turmoil; he fled the troubles and went to the capital.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion the native commandery was in turmoil; he fled the disaster and went to the capital.

entries.zh: 永安中，釋褐奉朝請。
entries.en: In the Yong'an era he left private life and was made court gentleman attendant.
entries.literal: In the Yong'an era he doffed commoner's dress and was made court gentleman attendant.

entries.zh: 普泰初，開府記室、龍驤將軍、廣州征南府錄事參軍，不行。
entries.en: Early in Putai he was made establishment-office recorder, dragon-prancing general, and recorder in the Guangzhou expeditionary-south establishment office, but did not take office.
entries.literal: Early in Putai he was made establishment-office recorder, dragon-prancing general, and recorder in the Guangzhou expeditionary-south establishment office; he did not take office.

entries.zh: 尋轉開府諮議參軍事、前將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to consulting aide in the establishment office and former general.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to consulting aide in the establishment office and former general.

entries.zh: 天平中，高祖擢為泰州開府長史、平北將軍。
entries.en: In the Tianping era Gao Huan promoted him to chief of staff in the Taizhou establishment office and general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era Gao Huan promoted him to chief of staff in the Taizhou establishment office and general who pacifies the north.

entries.zh: 稚廉緝諧將士，軍民樂悅。
entries.en: Zhilian harmonized officers and men, and army and people were pleased.
entries.literal: Zhilian harmonized officers and men; army and people were pleased.

entries.zh: 高祖頻幸河東，大相嗟賞。
entries.en: Gao Huan frequently visited Hedong and greatly admired him, praising him aloud.
entries.literal: Gao Huan frequently visited Hedong and greatly admired him in sighs of praise.

entries.zh: 轉為世宗驃騎府長史。
entries.en: He was transferred to chief of staff in Gao Cheng's swift-cavalry establishment office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to chief of staff in Gao Cheng's swift-cavalry establishment office.

entries.zh: 詔以濟州控帶川陸，接對梁使，尤須得人，世宗薦之，除濟州儀同長史。
entries.en: An edict said that because Jizhou controlled rivers and roads and received Liang envoys, an especially capable man was needed. Gao Cheng recommended him, and he was made acting chief of staff in Jizhou with insignia equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: An edict said that because Jizhou controlled rivers and roads and received Liang envoys, an especially capable man was needed; Gao Cheng recommended him, and he was made acting chief of staff in Jizhou with insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 又遷瀛州長史。
entries.en: He was again moved to chief of staff in Ying province.
entries.literal: He was again moved to chief of staff in Ying province.

entries.zh: 高祖行經冀州，總合河北六州文籍，商校戶口增損。
entries.en: Gao Huan was passing through Ji province and gathered the documents of the six Hebei provinces to compare and verify increases and decreases in household registers.
entries.literal: Gao Huan was passing through Ji province and gathered the documents of the six Hebei provinces to compare and verify increases and decreases in household registers.

entries.zh: 高祖親自部分，多在馬上，徵責文簿，指景取備，事緒非一。
entries.en: Gao Huan personally directed the work, mostly on horseback, demanding documents and pointing to scenes to require completeness—affairs of many kinds.
entries.literal: Gao Huan personally directed the work, mostly on horseback, demanding documents and pointing to scenes to require completeness—affairs of many kinds.

entries.zh: 稚廉每應機立成，恒先期會，莫不雅合深旨，為諸州準的。
entries.en: Zhilian each time responded on the spot and finished at once, always meeting the deadline in advance; nothing failed to match the deep intent, and he became the standard for all provinces.
entries.literal: Zhilian each time responded on the spot and finished at once, always meeting the deadline in advance; nothing failed to match the deep intent, and he became the standard for all provinces.

entries.zh: 高祖顧謂司馬子如曰：「觀稚廉處分，快人意也。」
entries.en: Gao Huan turned to Sima Ziru and said, "Watch how Zhilian disposes affairs—it satisfies the mind."
entries.literal: Gao Huan turned to Sima Ziru and said: "Watch how Zhilian disposes affairs—it satisfies the mind."

entries.zh: 因集文武數萬人，令郎中杜弼宣旨慰勞，仍詰諸州長史、守令等，諸人並謝罪，稚廉獨前拜恩，觀者咸歎美之。
entries.en: He then gathered civil and military officials numbering tens of thousands, had gentleman Du Bi proclaim the edict to comfort and reward them, and still questioned the chiefs of staff, magistrates, and the rest of the provinces. All others bowed in confession of fault, but Zhilian alone stepped forward to bow in thanks for grace, and the onlookers all sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: He then gathered civil and military officials numbering tens of thousands, had gentleman Du Bi proclaim the edict to comfort and reward them, and still questioned the chiefs of staff, magistrates, and the rest of the provinces; all others bowed in confession of fault, but Zhilian alone stepped forward to bow in thanks for grace, and the onlookers all sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 其日，賜以牛酒。
entries.en: That day he was granted oxen and wine.
entries.literal: That day he was granted oxen and wine.

entries.zh: 高祖還幷，以其事告世宗。
entries.en: Gao Huan returned to Bing and told Gao Cheng of the affair.
entries.literal: Gao Huan returned to Bing and told Gao Cheng of the affair.

entries.zh: 世宗喜而語人曰：「吾足知人矣。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng was pleased and told others, "I am quite able to know men."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was pleased and told others: "I am quite able to know men."

entries.zh: 世宗嗣事，召詣晉陽，除霸府掾。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng took up affairs he summoned Zhilian to Jinyang and made him a staff member of the hegemon's office.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng took up affairs he summoned Zhilian to Jinyang and made him a staff member of the hegemon's office.

entries.zh: 謂杜弼曰：「幷州王者之基，須好長史，各舉所知。」
entries.en: He told Du Bi, "Bingzhou is the king's foundation; a good chief of staff is needed—each of you recommend someone you know."
entries.literal: He told Du Bi: "Bingzhou is the king's foundation; a good chief of staff is needed—each of you recommend someone you know."

entries.zh: 時互有所稱，皆不允。
entries.en: At the time each recommended someone else; none was approved.
entries.literal: At the time each recommended someone else; none was approved.

entries.zh: 衆人未答。
entries.en: The crowd had not yet answered.
entries.literal: The crowd had not yet answered.

entries.zh: 世宗乃謂陳元康曰：「我教君好長史處，李稚廉卽其人也。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng then told Chen Yuankang, "I will teach you where to find a good chief of staff—Li Zhilian is the man."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng then told Chen Yuankang: "I will teach you where to find a good chief of staff—Li Zhilian is the man."

entries.zh: 遂命為幷州長史。
entries.en: He then appointed him chief of staff in Bing province.
entries.literal: He then appointed him chief of staff in Bing province.

entries.zh: 常在世宗第內，與隴西辛術等六人號為館客，待以上賓之禮。
entries.en: He was constantly within Gao Cheng's residence, and with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was called lodge guests, treated with the courtesy due a superior guest.
entries.literal: He was constantly within Gao Cheng's residence, and with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was called lodge guests, treated with the courtesy due a superior guest.

entries.zh: 封述，字君義，渤海蓨人也。
entries.en: Feng Shu, styled Junyi, came from Tiao in Bohai.
entries.literal: Feng Shu, styled Junyi, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.

entries.zh: 父軌，廷尉卿、濟州刺史。
entries.en: His father Gui was director of the court of justice and inspector of Ji province.
entries.literal: His father Gui was director of the court of justice and inspector of Ji province.

entries.zh: 述有幹用，年十八為濟州征東府鎧曹參軍。
entries.en: Shu had administrative ability; at eighteen he was armor-bureau aide in the Ji province expeditionary-east establishment office.
entries.literal: Shu had administrative ability; at eighteen he was armor-bureau aide in the Ji province expeditionary-east establishment office.

entries.zh: 高道穆為御史中尉，啟為御史。
entries.en: Gao Daomu was attendant censor-in-chief and opened a post for him as censor.
entries.literal: Gao Daomu was attendant censor-in-chief and opened a post for him as censor.

entries.zh: 遷大司馬清河王開府記室參軍，兼司徒主簿。
entries.en: He was moved to recorder in Prince of Qinghe's grand-marshal establishment office, concurrently chief clerk in the ministry of the masses.
entries.literal: He was moved to recorder in Prince of Qinghe's grand-marshal establishment office, concurrently chief clerk in the ministry of the masses.

entries.zh: 太昌中，除尚書三公郎中，以平幹稱。
entries.en: In the Taichang era he was made gentleman in the ministry of the three excellencies; he was known as fair and capable.
entries.literal: In the Taichang era he was made gentleman in the ministry of the three excellencies; he was known as fair and capable.

entries.zh: 天平中，增損舊事為《麟趾新格》，其名法科條，皆述刪定。
entries.en: In the Tianping era he revised old precedents into the New Statutes of the Linzhi Hall; its legal articles and clauses were all edited and fixed by Shu.
entries.literal: In the Tianping era he revised old precedents into the New Statutes of the Linzhi Hall; its legal articles and clauses were all edited and fixed by Shu.

entries.zh: 梁散騎常侍陸晏子、沈警來聘，以述兼通直郎使梁。
entries.en: Liang scattered-cavalry regular attendant Lu Yanzi and Shen Jing came on embassy; Shu was made concurrent direct-communication gentleman and sent to Liang.
entries.literal: Liang scattered-cavalry regular attendant Lu Yanzi and Shen Jing came on embassy; Shu was made concurrent direct-communication gentleman and sent to Liang.

entries.zh: 還，遷世宗大將軍府從事中郎，監京畿事。
entries.en: On return he was moved to aide in Gao Cheng's great-general establishment office and overseer of capital-district affairs.
entries.literal: On return he was moved to aide in Gao Cheng's great-general establishment office and overseer of capital-district affairs.

entries.zh: 武定五年，除彭城太守、當郡督，再行東徐州刺史。
entries.en: In the fifth Wuding year he was made administrator of Pengcheng and supervisor of that commandery, and again acting inspector of eastern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the fifth Wuding year he was made administrator of Pengcheng and supervisor of that commandery, and again acting inspector of eastern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 武定七年，除廷尉少卿。
entries.en: In the seventh Wuding year he was made vice director of the court of justice.
entries.literal: In the seventh Wuding year he was made vice director of the court of justice.

entries.zh: 八年，兼給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was concurrently supervising gentleman of the yellow gate.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently supervising gentleman of the yellow gate.

entries.zh: 齊受禪，與李獎等八人充大使，巡省方俗，問民疾苦。
entries.en: When Qi received the mandate he, with Li Jiang and seven others, served as great envoys touring the regions to inquire into local customs and ask after the people's hardships.
entries.literal: When Qi received the mandate he, with Li Jiang and seven others, served as great envoys touring the regions to inquire into local customs and ask after the people's hardships.

entries.zh: 天保三年，除清河太守，遷司徒左長史，行東都事，尋除海州刺史。
entries.en: In the third Tianbao year he was made administrator of Qinghe, moved to left chief of staff in the ministry of the masses, acting director of eastern-capital affairs, and soon made inspector of Haizhou.
entries.literal: In the third Tianbao year he was made administrator of Qinghe, moved to left chief of staff in the ministry of the masses, acting director of eastern-capital affairs, and soon made inspector of Haizhou.

entries.zh: 大寧元年，徵授大理卿。
entries.en: In the first Daning year he was summoned and appointed director of the great court of justice.
entries.literal: In the first Daning year he was summoned and appointed director of the great court of justice.

entries.zh: 河清三年，勑與錄尚書趙彥深、僕射魏收、尚書陽休之、國子祭酒馬敬德等議定律令。
entries.en: In the third Heqing year an edict ordered him together with recorder of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, vice director Wei Shou, minister Yang Xiuzhi, and director of the imperial academy Ma Jingde and others to deliberate on laws and ordinances.
entries.literal: In the third Heqing year an edict ordered him together with recorder of the masters of writing Zhao Yanshen, vice director Wei Shou, minister Yang Xiuzhi, and director of the imperial academy Ma Jingde and others to deliberate on laws and ordinances.

entries.zh: 天統元年，遷度支尚書。
entries.en: In the first Tiantong year he was moved to director of the revenue ministry.
entries.literal: In the first Tiantong year he was moved to director of the revenue ministry.

entries.zh: 三年，轉五兵尚書，加儀同三司。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to director of the five armies ministry and given added rank as acting insignia equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to director of the five armies ministry and given added rank as acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 武平元年，除南兗州刺史。
entries.en: In the first Wuping year he was made inspector of southern Yanzhou.
entries.literal: In the first Wuping year he was made inspector of southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 更滿還朝，除左光祿大夫，又除殿中尚書。
entries.en: When his term ended he returned to court and was made left grand master of gleaming fortune, then again director in the palace ministry.
entries.literal: When his term ended he returned to court and was made left grand master of gleaming fortune, then again director in the palace ministry.

entries.zh: 許惇，字季良，高陽新城人也。
entries.en: Xu Dun, styled Jiliang, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang.
entries.literal: Xu Dun, styled Jiliang, was a man of Xincheng in Gaoyang.

entries.zh: 父護，魏高陽、章武二郡太守。
entries.en: His father Hu was Wei administrator of Gaoyang and Zhangwu commanderies.
entries.literal: His father Hu was Wei administrator of Gaoyang and Zhangwu commanderies.

entries.zh: 惇清識敏速，達於從政，任司徒主簿，以能判斷見知，時人號為入鐵主簿。
entries.en: Dun had clear judgment and quick wit, skilled in government; he served as chief clerk in the ministry of the masses and was known for his ability to decide cases; men of the time called him the Iron-Entering Registrar.
entries.literal: Dun had clear judgment and quick wit, skilled in government; he served as chief clerk in the ministry of the masses and was known for his ability to decide cases; men of the time called him the Iron-Entering Registrar.

entries.zh: 稍遷陽平太守。
entries.en: He was gradually moved to administrator of Yangping.
entries.literal: He was gradually moved to administrator of Yangping.

entries.zh: 當時遷都鄴，陽平卽是畿郡，軍國責辦，賦斂無準，又勳貴屬請，朝夕徵求，惇並御之以道，上下無怨，治為下天第一。
entries.en: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was then a metropolitan commandery, and military and state requisitions and tax levies had no standard; moreover meritorious nobles made requests, seeking day and night—Dun governed all by principle, above and below without resentment, and his governance ranked first under Heaven.
entries.literal: At the time the capital was moved to Ye; Yangping was then a metropolitan commandery, and military and state requisitions and tax levies had no standard; moreover meritorious nobles made requests, seeking day and night—Dun governed all by principle, above and below without resentment, and his governance ranked first under Heaven.

entries.zh: 特加賞異，圖形於闕，詔頒天下。
entries.en: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict distributed it throughout the realm.
entries.literal: He received special reward and distinction; his likeness was painted at the palace gate and an edict distributed it throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 遷魏尹，出拜齊州刺史，轉梁州刺史，治並有聲。
entries.en: He was moved to metropolitan magistrate of Wei, went out and received appointment as inspector of Qi province, transferred to inspector of Liang province—wherever he governed there was reputation.
entries.literal: He was moved to metropolitan magistrate of Wei, went out and received appointment as inspector of Qi province, transferred to inspector of Liang province—wherever he governed there was reputation.

entries.zh: 遷大司農。
entries.en: He was moved to grand director of agriculture.
entries.literal: He was moved to grand director of agriculture.

entries.zh: 會侯景背叛，王思政入據潁城，王師出討，惇常督漕，軍無乏絕。
entries.en: It happened that Hou Jing rebelled; Wang Sizheng entered and held Ying city; the royal army went out to attack; Dun constantly supervised transport, and the army never lacked supplies.
entries.literal: It happened that Hou Jing rebelled; Wang Sizheng entered and held Ying city; the royal army went out to attack; Dun constantly supervised transport, and the army never lacked supplies.

entries.zh: 引洧水灌城，惇之策也。
entries.en: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was also Dun's stratagem.
entries.literal: Drawing the Wei River to flood the city was also Dun's stratagem.

entries.zh: 遷殿中尚書。
entries.en: He was moved to director in the palace ministry.
entries.literal: He was moved to director in the palace ministry.

entries.zh: 惇美鬚髯，下垂至帶，省中號為長鬛公。
entries.en: Dun had a fine beard hanging down to his belt; within the ministry he was called the Long-Beard Lord.
entries.literal: Dun had a fine beard hanging down to his belt; within the ministry he was called the Long-Beard Lord.

entries.zh: 顯祖嘗因酒酣，握惇鬚髯稱美，遂以刀截之，唯留一握。
entries.en: Gao Yang once, when drunk with wine, grasped Dun's beard and praised it, then took a knife and cut it off, leaving only one handful.
entries.literal: Gao Yang once, when drunk with wine, grasped Dun's beard and praised it, then took a knife and cut it off, leaving only one handful.

entries.zh: 惇懼，因不復敢長，時人又號為齊鬚公。
entries.en: Dun was afraid and therefore no longer dared let it grow long; men of the time again called him the Trimmed-Beard Lord.
entries.literal: Dun was afraid and therefore no longer dared let it grow long; men of the time again called him the Trimmed-Beard Lord.

entries.zh: 世祖踐祚，領御史中丞，為膠州刺史。
entries.en: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.
entries.literal: When Gao Zhan ascended the throne, he concurrently served as Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief and became Inspector of Jiao Province.

entries.zh: 尋追為司農卿，又遷大理卿，再為度支尚書，歷太子少保、少師、光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、特進，賜爵萬年縣子，食下邳郡幹。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as director of the ministry of agriculture, again moved to director of the great court of justice, again director of the revenue ministry, and served in succession as junior guardian and junior tutor of the heir apparent, grand master of gleaming fortune, acting insignia equal to the three excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and specially advanced; he was enfeoffed as baron of Wannian county with dry fief salary from Xiapi commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as director of the ministry of agriculture, again moved to director of the great court of justice, again director of the revenue ministry, and served in succession as junior guardian and junior tutor of the heir apparent, grand master of gleaming fortune, acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and specially advanced; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wannian county with dry fief salary from Xiapi commandery.

entries.zh: 以年老致仕於家，三年卒。
entries.en: Because of old age he retired to his home and died three years later.
entries.literal: Because of old age he retired to his home and died three years later.

entries.zh: 李稚廉 封述 許惇 羊烈 源彪
entries.en: Li Zhilian; Feng Shu; Xu Dun; Yang Lie; Yuan Biao
entries.literal: Li Zhilian; Feng Shu; Xu Dun; Yang Lie; Yuan Biao

entries.zh: 張華原 宋世良 弟世軌 郎基 孟業 崔伯謙 蘇瓊 房豹 路去病
entries.en: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, his younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing
entries.literal: Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, younger brother Shigui, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, Lu Qubing

entries.zh: 崔伯謙，字士遜，博陵人。
entries.en: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, came from Boling.
entries.literal: Cui Boqian, styled Shixun, was a man of Boling.

entries.zh: 父文業，鉅鹿守。
entries.en: His father Wenye had been administrator of Julu.
entries.literal: His father Wenye was administrator of Julu.

entries.zh: 伯謙少孤貧，善養母。
entries.en: Orphaned young and poor, Boqian was devoted to supporting his mother.
entries.literal: Boqian was orphaned young and poor, yet good at supporting his mother.

entries.zh: 高祖召赴晉陽，補相府功曹，稱之曰：「清直奉公，真良佐也。」
entries.en: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and made him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, saying, "Pure, upright, and devoted to the public—he is a true fine assistant."
entries.literal: Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang and appointed him staff merit officer in the chancellor's office, praising him: "Upright, pure, and devoted to public duty—a true fine assistant."

entries.zh: 遷瀛州別駕。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to vice governor of Ying province.

entries.zh: 世宗以為京畿司馬，勞之曰：「卿騁足瀛部，已著康歌，督府務殷，是用相授。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and told him, "You have already distinguished yourself in the Ying region and won popular praise; the supervisory office's business is heavy—so I entrust this post to you."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng made him metropolitan-area marshal and comforted him: "You have galloped through the Ying region and already won songs of praise; the supervisory office's duties are heavy—therefore I entrust this to you."

entries.zh: 族弟暹，當時寵要，謙與之僚舊同門，非吉兇，未曾造請。
entries.en: His clansman Xian then held favor and power; though they had been colleagues and schoolmates, Boqian never called on him except for weddings or funerals.
entries.literal: His clansman Xian was then in favor and power; Boqian had been his colleague and schoolmate, yet except for good or ill fortune he never paid a visit.

entries.zh: 後除濟北太守，恩信大行，乃改鞭用熟皮為之，不忍見血，示恥而已。
entries.en: Later appointed administrator of Jibei, he won wide trust through kindness and replaced the whip with one of soft tanned leather, unwilling to draw blood—shame alone was the aim.
entries.literal: Later he was made administrator of Jibei; kindness and trust spread widely, and he changed the whip to one made of soft tanned leather, unwilling to see blood—shame alone was the point.

entries.zh: 有朝貴行過郡境，問人太守治政何如。
entries.en: A court noble traveling through the commandery asked how the prefect governed.
entries.literal: A court noble passing through the commandery asked how the administrator governed.

entries.zh: 對曰：「府君恩化，古者所無。
entries.en: They answered, "Our lord's gracious rule is unlike anything of old.
entries.literal: The reply was: "Our lord's gracious transforming power is like nothing in antiquity.

entries.zh: 因誦民為歌曰：『崔府君，能治政，易鞭鞭，布威德，民無爭。』」
entries.en: They recited the people's song: 'Prefect Cui governs well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel.'"
entries.literal: Then they recited the people's song: 'Prefect Cui can govern well; change the whip, spread authority and virtue, and the people do not quarrel.'"

entries.zh: 客曰：「旣稱恩化，何由復威？」
entries.en: The guest said, "If you call it gracious rule, how can there also be authority?"
entries.literal: The guest said: "If you call it gracious transforming power, how can there also be authority?"

entries.zh: 曰：「長吏憚威，民庶蒙惠。」
entries.en: They said, "Officials fear his authority; common people receive his kindness."
entries.literal: The reply was: "Senior officials fear his authority; the common people receive his kindness."

entries.zh: 徵赴鄴，百姓號泣遮道。
entries.en: When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.
entries.literal: When he was summoned to Ye, the people wept and blocked the road.

entries.zh: 以弟讓在關中，不復居內任，除南鉅鹿守，事無巨細，必自親覽。
entries.en: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he took no further inner post and was made administrator of southern Julu, personally reviewing every matter large or small.
entries.literal: Because his brother Rang was in Guanzhong, he no longer held an inner appointment and was made administrator of southern Julu; in affairs great or small he always examined them himself.

entries.zh: 民有貧弱未理者，皆曰：「我自有白鬚公，不慮不決。」
entries.en: If the poor and weak had cases unsettled, they all said, "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry it will go undecided."
entries.literal: When the people were poor or weak and their cases unsettled, all said: "We have our White-Beard Lord—we need not worry that it will not be decided."

entries.zh: 後為銀青光祿大夫，卒。
entries.en: He later became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.
entries.literal: Later he became silver-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue and died.

entries.zh: 先王疆理天下，司牧黎元，刑法以禁其奸，禮教以防其欲。
entries.en: Former kings divided the realm and tended the people, using penal law to forbid wickedness and ritual teaching to guard against desire.
entries.literal: The former kings divided and ordered the realm, shepherded the black-haired people, used penal law to forbid their wickedness, and used ritual teaching to guard against their desires.

entries.zh: 故分職命官，共理天下。
entries.en: Therefore they divided offices and appointed officials to govern the realm together.
entries.literal: Therefore offices were divided and officials appointed to govern the realm together.

entries.zh: 《書》云：「知人則哲，能官人安人則惠。」
entries.en: The Book of Documents says: "To know men is wisdom; to place men in office and settle the people is grace."
entries.literal: The Book says: "To know men is to be wise; to be able to place men in office and settle men is to be gracious."

entries.zh: 睿哲之君，必致清明之臣，昏亂之朝，多有貪殘之吏。
entries.en: A wise ruler wins clear-minded ministers; a benighted court breeds greedy, cruel officials.
entries.literal: A wise and perspicacious lord is sure to obtain clear and bright ministers; a benighted and chaotic court has many greedy and cruel clerks.

entries.zh: 高祖撥亂反正，恤隱為懷，故守令之徒，才多稱職。
entries.en: Gao Huan set the realm right after chaos and held pity close, so many prefects and magistrates proved fit for their posts.
entries.literal: Gao Huan set right the disorder and turned back to the proper, with pity for the hidden in his breast, so among prefects and magistrates many were fit for their posts.

entries.zh: 仍以戰功諸將，出牧外藩，不識治體，無聞政術。
entries.en: Yet he still sent battle-hardened generals to govern the outer marches—men who knew nothing of governance and had never learned the arts of rule.
entries.literal: Yet he still sent generals of battle merit out to pasture the outer marches; they did not know the substance of governance and had not heard of the arts of rule.

entries.zh: 非唯暗於前言往行，乃至始學依判付曹，聚斂無厭，淫虐不已，雖或直繩，終無悛革。
entries.en: They were blind not only to precedent but even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by template; insatiable in levies, relentless in cruelty—though the law was sometimes enforced, they never truly reformed.
entries.literal: Not only were they dark to words and deeds of old, they even began by learning to hand cases to clerks by precedent; insatiable in exaction, unceasing in debauchery and cruelty—though sometimes the straight cord was applied, in the end there was no repentance or reform.

entries.zh: 於戲！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 此朝廷之大失。
entries.en: This was a grave loss for the court.
entries.literal: This was a great loss of the court.

entries.zh: 大寧以後，風雅俱缺，賣官鬻獄，上下相蒙，降及末年，黷貨滋甚。
entries.en: After the Daining era, refinement vanished; offices and judgments were sold, court and country deceived one another, and in the dynasty's last years venality grew worse still.
entries.literal: After Daining, elegance and refinement were both lacking; offices and prisons were sold, above and below deceived one another, and down to the final years venal goods grew still worse.

entries.zh: 齊氏循良，如辛術之徒非一，多以官爵通顯，別有列傳。
entries.en: Northern Qi had good officials—Xin Shu was not alone—many of whom won rank and fame and have their own biographies.
entries.literal: Among Qi there were good officials such as Xin Shu—not one alone—many of whom rose to prominence through rank and title and have separate biographies.

entries.zh: 如房仲幹之屬，在武平之末能，卓爾不群，斯固彌可嘉也。
entries.en: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, who at the end of Wuping still stood apart from the crowd, are all the more praiseworthy.
entries.literal: Men such as Fang Zhonggan, able at the end of Wuping to stand out from the crowd, are all the more worthy of praise.

entries.zh: 今掇張華原等列於《循吏》云。
entries.en: Here Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered under Good Officials.
entries.literal: Now Zhang Huayuan and the rest are gathered and listed in Good Officials.

entries.zh: 張華原，字國滿，代郡人也。
entries.en: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was from Dai commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Huayuan, style Guoman, was a man of Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 少明敏，有器度。
entries.en: As a youth he was bright and keen, with real capacity.
entries.literal: In youth he was bright and keen, with capacity and measure.

entries.zh: 高祖開驃騎府，引為法曹參軍，遷大丞相府屬，仍侍左右。
entries.en: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he made Huayuan a legal-cases staff officer, then a staff member of the Grand Chancellor's office, still attending at his side.
entries.literal: When Gao Huan opened the Rapid Cavalry Office he brought him in as legal-cases staff officer, promoted him to staff of the Grand Chancellor's office, and still attended at his side.

entries.zh: 從於信都，深為高祖所親待。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan to Xindu and was deeply favored.
entries.literal: He followed him to Xindu and was deeply favored and treated by Gao Huan.

entries.zh: 高祖每號令三軍，常令宣諭意旨。
entries.en: Whenever Gao Huan commanded the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim his intent.
entries.literal: Whenever Gao Huan issued orders to the three armies he often had Huayuan proclaim and explain his intent.

entries.zh: 周文帝始據雍州也，高祖猶欲以逆順曉之，使華原入關說焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still hoped to persuade him with the logic of loyalty and rebellion and sent Huayuan through the passes to argue with him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first held Yong province, Gao Huan still wished to enlighten him with right and wrong and sent Huayuan into the passes to persuade him.

entries.zh: 周文密有拘留之意，謂華原曰：「若能屈驥足於此，當共享富貴，不爾，命懸今日。」
entries.en: Zhou Wen secretly meant to detain him and said: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs to stay here, we shall share wealth and honor; if not, your life ends today."
entries.literal: Zhou Wen secretly intended detention and said to Huayuan: "If you can bend your swift horse's legs here, we shall share wealth and honor together; if not, your life hangs on this day."

entries.zh: 華原曰：「渤海王命世誕生，殆天所縱，以明公蕞爾關右，便自隔絕，故使華原銜喻公旨。
entries.en: Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven itself set him free. Your lordship holds only the western passes and has cut yourselves off; Huayuan was sent to carry your message.
entries.literal: Huayuan said: "The Prince of Bohai was born to order the age—perhaps Heaven set him free. With your lordship's petty hold on the western passes you have cut yourselves off, so Huayuan was sent to carry your lordship's message.

entries.zh: 明公不以此日改圖，轉禍為福，乃欲賜脅，有死而已。」
entries.en: If you will not change course today and turn calamity into blessing, but mean to coerce me, there is only death."
entries.literal: If your lordship will not on this day change your plan and turn calamity into blessing, yet wish to bestow coercion, there is only death."

entries.zh: 周文嘉其亮正，乃使東還。
entries.en: Zhou Wen admired his candor and sent him back east.
entries.literal: Zhou Wen admired his candor and uprightness and sent him back east.

entries.zh: 高祖以華原久而不返，每嘆惜之，及聞其來，喜見於色。
entries.en: Gao Huan had long sighed over Huayuan's absence; when he heard of his return, joy showed on his face.
entries.literal: Gao Huan, because Huayuan had long not returned, often sighed in regret; when he heard he had come, joy showed in his face.

entries.zh: 孟業，字敬業，鉅鹿安國人。
entries.en: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was from Anguo in Julu.
entries.literal: Meng Ye, style Jingye, was a man of Anguo in Julu.

entries.zh: 家本寒微，少為州吏。
entries.en: His family was poor; in youth he was a provincial clerk.
entries.literal: His family was originally poor and low; in youth he was a provincial clerk.

entries.zh: 性廉謹，同僚諸人侵盜官絹，分三十疋與之，拒而不受。
entries.en: Honest and cautious, when colleagues who stole official silk offered him thirty bolts he refused.
entries.literal: His nature was honest and cautious; colleagues who stole official silk divided thirty bolts for him and he refused and would not receive them.

entries.zh: 魏彭城王韶拜定州，除典籖。
entries.en: When Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao took Ding province, Ye was made records-and-keeper.
entries.literal: Wei Prince of Pengcheng Shao was appointed to Ding province and made Ye records-and-keeper.

entries.zh: 長史劉仁之謂業曰：「我處其外，君居其內，同心戮力，庶有濟乎。」
entries.en: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi told Ye: "I stand outside, you within; with one heart we may succeed."
entries.literal: Chief Administrator Liu Renzhi said to Ye: "I stand outside, you dwell within; with one heart and shared strength, perhaps there can be success."

entries.zh: 未幾仁之徵入為中書令，臨路啟韶云：「殿下左右可信任者唯有孟業，願專任之。
entries.en: Soon Renzhi was summoned to the Secretariat; leaving, he told Shao: "Of those around you, only Meng Ye can be trusted—put sole trust in him.
entries.literal: Before long Renzhi was summoned in as director of the Secretariat; on the road he told Shao: "Among those around Your Highness whom you can trust there is only Meng Ye—wish to put sole trust in him.

entries.zh: 餘人不可信也。」
entries.en: The rest cannot be trusted."
entries.literal: The rest cannot be trusted."

entries.zh: 又與業別，執手曰：「今我出都，君便失援，恐君在後，不自保全。
entries.en: Parting from Ye he took his hand: "I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear you cannot preserve yourself afterward.
entries.literal: He also parted from Ye, took his hand, and said: "Now I leave the capital and you lose support; I fear that afterward you cannot preserve yourself.

entries.zh: 唯正與直，願君自勉。」
entries.en: Only uprightness and straightness—urge yourself."
entries.literal: Only uprightness and straightness—wish you to urge yourself."

entries.zh: 業唯有一馬，因瘦而死。
entries.en: Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.
entries.literal: Ye had only one horse; it died from thinness.

entries.zh: 韶以業家貧，令州府官人同食馬肉，欲令厚償，業固辭不敢。
entries.en: Because Ye's family was poor, Shao ordered officials to eat the horse's flesh and meant to compensate him generously; Ye firmly declined.
entries.literal: Shao, because Ye's family was poor, ordered the provincial and commandery officials to eat the horse's flesh together, wishing to give generous compensation; Ye firmly declined and dared not accept.

entries.zh: 韶乃戲業曰：「卿邀名人也。」
entries.en: Shao jested: "You court a famous man's reputation."
entries.literal: Shao then jested to Ye: "You invite a famous man's reputation."

entries.zh: 對曰：「業以微細，伏事節下，旣不能裨益，寧可損敗清風。」
entries.en: Ye answered: "I am minute and low, serving in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear reputation?"
entries.literal: He answered: "Ye is minute and low, serving Your Highness in attendance; since I cannot benefit you, how could I damage your clear wind?"

entries.zh: 後高祖書與韶云：「典籖姓孟者極能用心，何不置之目前。」
entries.en: Later Gao Huan wrote Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely attentive—why not keep him before your eyes?"
entries.literal: Later Gao Huan wrote to Shao: "The records-keeper surnamed Meng is extremely able in intent—why not place him before your eyes."

entries.zh: 韶，高祖之婿也。
entries.en: Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law.
entries.literal: Shao was Gao Huan's son-in-law.

entries.zh: 仁之後為兗州，臨別謂吏部崔暹曰：「貴州人士，唯有孟業，宜銓舉之，他人不可信也。」
entries.en: When Ren later became governor of Yanzhou, he took leave of Personnel Director Cui Xian and said, "Of the men in this province, only Meng Ye deserves selection and promotion; the rest are not to be trusted."
entries.literal: After Ren became governor of Yanzhou, on parting he said to Personnel Director Cui Xian: "Among the province's men, only Meng Ye should be selected and recommended; others cannot be trusted."

entries.zh: 崔暹問業曰：「君往在定州，有何政績，使劉西兗如此欽歎？」
entries.en: Cui Xian asked Ye, "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?"
entries.literal: Cui Xian asked Ye: "When you were in Dingzhou, what achievements made Liu of Western Yanzhou admire you so?"

entries.zh: 答曰：「稟性愚直，唯知自修，無他長也。」
entries.en: He answered, "By nature I am blunt and honest; I only know how to improve myself—I have no other talents."
entries.literal: He answered: "By nature I am blunt and straight; I only know how to cultivate myself—no other strengths."

entries.zh: 蘇瓊，字珍之，武強人也。
entries.en: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, came from Wuqiang.
entries.literal: Su Qiong, styled Zhenzhi, was a man of Wuqiang.

entries.zh: 父備，仕魏至衛尉少卿。
entries.en: His father Bei served Wei as far as junior chamberlain for the palace guards.
entries.literal: His father Bei served Wei up to junior chamberlain for the palace guards.

entries.zh: 瓊幼時隨父在邊，嘗謁東荊州刺史曹芝。
entries.en: As a boy Qiong followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.
entries.literal: When Qiong was young he followed his father to the frontier and once called on Eastern Jingzhou inspector Cao Zhi.

entries.zh: 芝戲問曰：「卿欲官不？」
entries.en: Zhi asked playfully, "Do you want an office?"
entries.literal: Zhi asked in jest: "Do you want an office?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「設官求人，非人求官。」
entries.en: He answered, "Offices are established to seek men, not men to seek offices."
entries.literal: He answered: "Offices are set up to seek men—not men to seek offices."

entries.zh: 芝異其對，署為府長流參軍。
entries.en: Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.
entries.literal: Zhi marveled at the reply and appointed him senior adjutant in the office.

entries.zh: 文襄以儀同開府，引為刑獄參軍，每加勉勞。
entries.en: Gao Cheng, holding the rank of fifth-order palace guard, opened a staff office and made him penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging him.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng, with the rank of palace guard of the fifth order, opened a staff office and brought him in as penal-affairs staff officer, often encouraging and commending him.

entries.zh: 幷州嘗有強盜，長流參軍推其事，所疑賊並已拷伏，失物家並識認，唯不獲盜贓。
entries.en: In Bing Province there had been bandits; the senior adjutant investigated, and every suspect had confessed under torture while the owners identified them—yet the stolen goods were never found.
entries.literal: Bing province once had bandits; the senior adjutant investigated the matter, and all the suspected thieves had already confessed under torture; the owners of the lost goods all identified them, yet the stolen goods were not recovered.

entries.zh: 文襄付瓊更令窮審，乃別推得元景融等十餘人，並獲贓驗。
entries.en: Gao Cheng put Qiong on a fresh exhaustive inquiry; he traced the case separately and found Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with the loot recovered.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng handed the case to Qiong for a further exhaustive inquiry; he then traced it separately and obtained Yuan Jingrong and more than ten others, all with stolen goods verified.

entries.zh: 文襄大笑，語前妄引賊者曰：「爾輩若不遇我好參軍，幾致枉死。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng laughed and told those who had wrongly implicated the thieves, "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would almost have been executed unjustly."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng laughed loudly and said to those who had earlier wrongly implicated the thieves: "If you had not met my fine staff officer, you would nearly have died wrongfully."

entries.zh: 路去病，陽平人也。
entries.en: Lu Qubing was a native of Yangping.
entries.literal: Lu Qubing was a man of Yangping.

entries.zh: 風神疏朗，儀表瓌異。
entries.en: His manner was open and lucid; his looks were singular and striking.
entries.literal: His spirit and bearing were open and clear; his appearance was singular and striking.

entries.zh: 釋褐開府參軍。
entries.en: He doffed the hemp and became an opening-office staff officer.
entries.literal: Upon doffing the hemp he became an opening-office staff officer.

entries.zh: 勑用士人為縣宰，以去病為定州饒陽令。
entries.en: An edict required that cultivated men serve as county magistrates, and Qubing was appointed magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that literati be used as county magistrates; Qubing was made Magistrate of Raoyang in Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 去病明閑時務，性頗嚴毅，人不敢欺，然至廉平，為吏民嘆服。
entries.en: Qubing understood the affairs of the age and was by nature stern and firm; none dared cheat him, yet he was utterly fair, and officials and commoners alike marveled.
entries.literal: Qubing was clear and adept in affairs of the time; his nature was rather stern and firm—men did not dare deceive him, yet he was utterly fair and incorrupt, and officials and commoners alike sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 擢為成安令。
entries.en: He was promoted to magistrate of Cheng'an.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Cheng'an.

entries.zh: 京城下有鄴、臨漳、成安三縣，輦轂之下，舊號難治，重以政亂時難，綱維不立，功臣內戚，請囑百端。
entries.en: Below the capital stood Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an—three counties long notorious under the imperial hub. Disorder piled on hard times; law's net hung slack, and meritorious ministers and imperial kin pressed requests from every side.
entries.literal: Near the capital lay three counties—Ye, Linzhang, and Cheng'an. Under the chariot-hub they had long been called hard to govern; compounded by chaotic government and hard times, the net of law was not established, and meritorious ministers and imperial affines made requests from every quarter.

entries.zh: 去病消息事宜，以理抗答，勢要之徒，雖廝養小人莫不憚其風格，亦不至嫌恨。
entries.en: Qubing tracked every matter and answered on principle. Men of influence—even grooms and petty servants—feared his bearing, yet none bore him a grudge.
entries.literal: Qubing kept himself informed of affairs and answered requests with reason; men of power—even grooms and petty servants—all feared his integrity of style, yet none came to resent him.

entries.zh: 自遷鄴以還，三縣令治術，去病獨為稱首。
entries.en: After the court moved to Ye, among the three magistrates' ways of rule, Qubing alone was ranked first.
entries.literal: From the move to Ye onward, among the three county magistrates' methods of governance, Qubing alone was ranked first.

entries.zh: 周武平齊，重其能官，與濟陰郡守公孫景茂二人不被替代，發詔褒揚。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi, he prized their competence in office. Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao, administrator of Jiyin, were the two not replaced; an edict singled them out for praise.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou pacified Qi, he valued their ability in office—Qubing and Gongsun Jingmao, Administrator of Jiyin, were the two not replaced; an edict was issued to praise and commend them.

entries.zh: 隋大業中，卒於冀氏縣令。
entries.en: In the Daye era of Sui he died in office as magistrate of Jishi.
entries.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, he died while serving as Magistrate of Jishi.

entries.zh: 後神武自太原來朝，見之曰：「此人宋遊道耶？
entries.en: When Gao Huan came from Taiyuan to court he said: "Is this Song Youdao?
entries.literal: Later Gao Huan came from Taiyuan to court and on seeing him said: "Is this man Song Youdao?

entries.zh: 常聞其名，今日始識其面。」
entries.en: I have often heard the name; today I first see his face."
entries.literal: I have often heard the name; today I first know his face."

entries.zh: 遷遊道別駕。
entries.en: Youdao was transferred to vice governor.
entries.literal: Youdao was transferred to vice governor.

entries.zh: 後日，神武之司州，饗朝士，舉觴屬遊道曰：「飲高歡手中酒者大丈夫，卿之為人，合飲此酒。」
entries.en: Days later at Si province Gao Huan feasted court gentlemen, raised his cup to Youdao: "He who drinks Gao Huan's wine is a great man; you fit this cup."
entries.literal: Some days later, when Gao Huan was in Si province feasting court gentlemen, he raised his cup and turned to Youdao: "He who drinks wine from Gao Huan's hand is a great man; your person fits drinking this wine."

entries.zh: 及還晉陽，百官辭於紫陽。
entries.en: Returning to Jinyang, officials took leave at Ziyang.
entries.literal: On returning to Jinyang, the hundred officials took leave at Ziyang.

entries.zh: 神武執遊道手曰：「甚知朝貴中有憎忌卿者，但用心，莫懷畏慮，當使卿位與之相似。」
entries.en: Gao Huan took his hand: "I know nobles hate you; use your heart, fear nothing—I shall make your rank like theirs."
entries.literal: Gao Huan took Youdao's hand and said: "I know well that among court nobles some hate and envy you; only use your heart, do not harbor fear—I shall make your rank resemble theirs."

entries.zh: 於是啟以遊道為中尉。
entries.en: He memorialized to make Youdao commandant.
entries.literal: Thereupon he memorialized to make Youdao commandant.

entries.zh: 文襄執請，乃以吏部郎中崔暹為御史中尉，以遊道為尚書左丞。
entries.en: Gao Cheng pressed the request; Cui Xian became censor-in-chief and Youdao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng pressed the request; thus Cui Xian was made censor-in-chief and Youdao Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 文襄謂暹遊道曰：「卿一人處南臺，一人處北省，當使天下肅然。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng told them: "One holds the Southern Terrace, one the Northern Bureau—make the realm stand in awe."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng told Xian and Youdao: "One of you holds the Southern Terrace, one the Northern Bureau—you should make the realm stand in awe."

entries.zh: 遊道入省，劾太師咸陽王坦、太保孫騰、司徒高隆之、司空侯景、錄尚書元弼、尚書令司馬子如官貸金銀，催徵酬價，雖非指事贓賄，終是不避權豪。
entries.en: Entering office, Youdao impeached Grand Tutor Tan, Prince of Xianyang, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Education Gao Longzhi, Minister of Works Hou Jing, Director Yuan Bi, Director Sima Ziru and others for official loans of gold and silver—though not direct bribery, he did not spare the powerful.
entries.literal: Youdao entered the province and impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan, Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister Hou Jing, Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Bi, Director Sima Ziru and others for official loans of gold and silver, pressing for repayment; though not pointed bribery, in the end he did not avoid the powerful.

entries.zh: 又奏駁尚書違失數百條，省中豪吏王儒之徒並鞭斥之。
entries.en: He memorialized hundreds of Masters of Writing failures; powerful clerks Wang Ru and others were flogged and driven off.
entries.literal: He also memorialized and rejected several hundred failures of the Masters of Writing; powerful clerks Wang Ru and the rest were all flogged and driven off.

entries.zh: 始依故事，於尚收省立門名，以記出入早晚，令僕已下皆側目。
entries.en: By precedent a gate register recorded comings and goings at the Masters of Writing; from servants down all looked askance.
entries.literal: At first according to precedent, at the Masters of Writing reception a gate name was set to record coming and going morning and evening; from servants downward all looked askance.

entries.zh: 夫人之性靈，稟受或異，剛柔區別，緩急相形，未有深察是非，莫不肆其情欲。
entries.en: Human nature differs at birth; rigidity and softness, urgency and ease shape one another—few truly weigh right and wrong, and nearly all indulge feeling and desire.
entries.literal: Man's nature and spirit, what he receives at birth, may differ; rigidity and softness are distinct, urgency and ease take shape against each other—few deeply examine right and wrong, and none fail to give full play to feeling and desire.

entries.zh: 至於詳觀水火、更佩韋弦者鮮矣。
entries.en: Those who watch fire and water closely and wear the girdle of restraint are rare indeed.
entries.literal: As for those who closely observe fire and water and again wear the girdle-weights of caution, they are rare.

entries.zh: 獄吏為患，其所從來久矣。
entries.en: Prison clerks as a scourge—their origin is ancient.
entries.literal: Prison clerks as a scourge—their origin is of long standing.

entries.zh: 自魏途不競，網漏寰區，高祖懲其寬怠，頗亦威嚴馭物，使內外羣官，咸知禁網。
entries.en: When Wei lost hold of the realm the law's net gaped wide; Gao Huan punished lax rule and governed with stern majesty until every official, within and without, knew the prohibitory mesh.
entries.literal: From the time Wei lost the contest for the realm, the net leaked across the world; Gao Huan punished its lax slackness and also used stern majesty to master things, so that inner and outer officials all knew the prohibitory mesh.

entries.zh: 今錄邸珍等以存《酷吏》，懲示勸勵云。
entries.en: Here Di Zhen and the rest are recorded under Cruel Officials, as warning and encouragement.
entries.literal: Now Di Zhen and the rest are recorded to preserve Cruel Officials, as warning and encouragement.

entries.zh: 文宣受禪，除治書侍御史，彈射不避勳親。
entries.en: When Gao Yang took the throne he was made attending censor for drafting and in impeachment spared no meritorious kin.
entries.literal: When Gao Yang received the abdication he was made Attending Censor for Drafting; in impeachment he did not avoid meritorious kin.

entries.zh: 累遷御史中丞，繩劾更切。
entries.en: He rose to censor-in-chief, and his restraints and impeachments grew still harsher.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief; restraints and impeachment grew still sharper.

entries.zh: 然豪橫不平，頻被怨訟。
entries.en: Yet he was domineering and unjust and was sued again and again out of spite.
entries.literal: Yet he was overbearing and unfair and was repeatedly sued in resentment.

entries.zh: 前為汲郡太守翟嵩啟列：「義雲從父兄僧明負官債，先任京畿長吏，不受其屬，立限切征，由此挾嫌，數遣御史過郡訪察，欲相推繩。
entries.en: Earlier, as administrator of Ji commandery, Zhai Song had memorialized: "Yiyun's cousin Sengming owed official debt; when Sengming was metropolitan chief clerk he refused Yiyun's men and set harsh collection deadlines; nursing a grudge, Yiyun kept sending censors through the commandery to investigate and impeach him.
entries.literal: Formerly as Administrator of Ji Commandery, Zhai Song memorialized listing: "Yi Yun's paternal cousin Sengming owed official debt; having first served as metropolitan-area chief clerk, he did not accept Yi Yun's subordinates and set strict deadlines for collection; thereby nursing a grudge, he repeatedly sent censors through the commandery to investigate, wishing to impeach each other.

entries.zh: 又坐私藏工匠，家有十餘機織錦，並造金銀器物。」
entries.en: He was also charged with hiding artisans privately—more than ten brocade looms at home and gold and silver work besides."
entries.literal: He was also charged with privately hoarding artisans; his household had more than ten looms weaving brocade, and moreover made gold and silver vessels."

entries.zh: 乃被禁止。
entries.en: He was then placed under detention.
entries.literal: He was then detained.

entries.zh: 尋見釋，以為司徒左長史。
entries.en: He was soon released and made Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: Soon he was released and made Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 尚書左丞司馬子瑞奏彈義雲，稱：「天保元年四月，竇氏皇姨祖載日，內外百官赴第吊省，義雲唯遣御史投名，身遂不赴。
entries.en: Left vice director Sima Zirui impeached Yiyun, writing: "In the fourth month of Tianbao year one, on the burial day of Empress Dowager Dou's imperial aunt, officials inside and out went to mourn; Yiyun only sent a censor to register his name and did not attend.
entries.literal: Master of Writing Left Vice Director Sima Zirui memorialized to impeach Yi Yun, stating: "In the fourth month of the first year of Tianbao, on the day of the Empress Dowager Dou's imperial aunt's burial, inner and outer officials of every rank went to her residence to mourn; Yi Yun only sent a censor to submit his name and himself did not go.

entries.zh: 又義雲啟云：『喪婦孤貧，後娶李世安女為妻。
entries.en: Yiyun had also reported, 'My wife died and I am poor and alone; I later took Li Shi'an's daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Moreover Yi Yun reported: 'My wife died and I am poor and alone; I later took Li Shi'an's daughter as wife.

entries.zh: 世安身雖父服未終，其女為祖已就平吉，特乞暗迎，不敢備禮。』
entries.en: Though Shi'an is still in mourning for his father, his daughter had already passed the grandfather's peaceful day; I beg a secret welcome and dare not hold full ceremony.'
entries.literal: Though Shi'an's person is still within mourning for his father, his daughter for her grandfather had already passed the peaceful day; I specially beg a secret welcome and dare not prepare full rites.'

entries.zh: 及義雲成婚之夕，衆儲備設，克日拜閤，鳴騶清路，盛列羽儀，兼差臺吏二十人，責其鮮服侍從車後。
entries.en: Yet on his wedding night the stores were piled high; on the appointed day he bowed at the gate, runners cleared the road, feathered guards paraded in splendor, and twenty bureau clerks were sent to demand fresh dress and follow his carriage.
entries.literal: Yet on the night Yi Yun's marriage was completed, the crowd was fully stored and set out; on the fixed day he bowed at the gate, outriders cleared the road, feathered insignia were arrayed in splendor, and moreover twenty bureau clerks were dispatched to demand fresh clothes and attend behind his carriage.

entries.zh: 直是茍求成婚，誣罔干上。
entries.en: It was plainly a shameless rush to marry and a lie pressed on his superiors.
entries.literal: It was plainly a shameless demand for marriage and deception importuning superiors.

entries.zh: 義雲資產宅宇足稱豪至，忽道孤貧，亦為矯詐。
entries.en: Yiyun's property and house were lavish enough to count as grand; to call himself poor and alone was fraud as well.
entries.literal: Yi Yun's assets and dwellings were enough to be called grand and extreme; suddenly to speak of poverty and solitude was also pretense and fraud.

entries.zh: 法官如此，直繩焉寄？
entries.en: If judges behave thus, where is upright law to be found?
entries.literal: When judges are like this, where can upright rule be entrusted?

entries.zh: 又駕幸晉陽，都坐判：『拜起居表，四品以下五品已上令預前一日赴南都署表，三品以上臨日署訖。』
entries.en: When the emperor went to Jinyang, the chief seat ruled: 'For the bowing-salutation memorial, officials from fourth rank down through fifth rank and up must sign at the southern capital office the day before; third rank and above sign on the day itself.'
entries.literal: Moreover when the emperor visited Jinyang, the chief seat ruled: 'For bowing the salutation memorial, those of fifth rank and above from fourth rank down are to go the day before to the southern capital office to sign the memorial; those of third rank and above sign it on the day itself.'

entries.zh: 義雲乃乖例，署表之日，索表就家先署，臨日遂稱私忌不來。」
entries.en: Yiyun broke precedent: on signing day he had the memorial brought home and signed first, then on the day itself pleaded private taboo and stayed away."
entries.literal: Yi Yun then violated precedent; on the day of signing the memorial he demanded the memorial and signed it first at home, and on the day itself then claimed private taboo and did not come."

entries.zh: 於是詔付廷尉科罪，尋勑免推。
entries.en: An edict sent him to the Court of Judicature; soon another order halted the case.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict handed him to the Court of Judicature for sentencing; soon an order excused further prosecution.

entries.zh: 子瑞又奏彈義雲事十餘條，多煩碎，罪止罰金，不至除免。
entries.en: Zirui impeached him again on more than ten petty counts; punishment stopped at a fine and did not cost him his post.
entries.literal: Zirui again memorialized to impeach Yi Yun on more than ten matters, mostly trivial; the crime stopped at a fine and did not reach removal.

entries.zh: 子瑞從兄消難為北豫州刺史，義雲遣御史張子階詣州采風聞，先禁其典籖家客等。
entries.en: Zirui's cousin Xiaonan was inspector of North Yuzhou; Yiyun sent censor Zhang Zijie to gather rumors and first detained his registry keeper, household agents, and the like.
entries.literal: Zirui's cousin Xiaonan was Inspector of North Yuzhou; Yi Yun sent Censor Zhang Zijie to the province to gather hearsay and first detained his registry keeper, household clients, and the like.

entries.zh: 消難危懼，遂叛入周。
entries.en: Terrified, Xiaonan rebelled and fled to Zhou.
entries.literal: Xiaonan in peril and fear then rebelled and entered Zhou.

entries.zh: 時論歸罪義雲，云其規報子瑞，事亦上聞。
entries.en: Public opinion blamed Yiyun for scheming revenge on Zirui, and word reached the throne.
entries.literal: Opinion of the time laid blame on Yi Yun, saying he had plotted retaliation against Zirui; the matter also reached the throne.

entries.zh: 爾前讌嘗，義雲常預，從此後集見稍疏，聲望大損。
entries.en: Before this he had always been at court feasts; afterward he was seen less often and his standing collapsed.
entries.literal: Before this at banquets and feasts Yi Yun was always present; from this time onward his appearances at gatherings grew somewhat sparse and his reputation greatly fell.

entries.zh: 邸珍，字寶安，本中山上曲陽人也。
entries.en: Di Zhen, style Bao'an, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Di Zhen, style Bao'an, was originally a man of Shangquyang in Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 從高祖起義，拜為長史。
entries.en: He followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army and was made chief clerk.
entries.literal: He followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army and was appointed chief clerk.

entries.zh: 性嚴暴，求取無厭。
entries.en: Stern and violent by nature, he sought and took without satiety.
entries.literal: His nature was stern and violent; in seeking and taking he knew no satiety.

entries.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射、大行臺，節度諸軍事。
entries.en: He later also served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner of the Traveling Court, directing military affairs.
entries.literal: Later he also held concurrent posts as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner with the Traveling Court, directing all military affairs.

entries.zh: 珍御下殘酷，衆士離心，為民所害。
entries.en: Zhen ruled subordinates with cruel severity; his officers lost heart and the people killed him.
entries.literal: Zhen ruled subordinates with cruel severity; the host of officers lost heart, and the people killed him.

entries.zh: 後贈定州刺史。
entries.en: He was later posthumously made inspector of Ding province.
entries.literal: Later he was posthumously given Ding province.

entries.zh: 宋遊道，廣平人，其先自燉煌徙焉。
entries.en: Song Youdao was from Guangping; his ancestors had moved there from Dunhuang.
entries.literal: Song Youdao was a man of Guangping; his ancestors had moved there from Dunhuang.

entries.zh: 父季預，為渤海太守。
entries.en: His father Jiyu was prefect of Bohai.
entries.literal: His father Jiyu was prefect of Bohai.

entries.zh: 遊道弱冠隨父在郡，父亡，吏人贈遺，一無所受。
entries.en: As a youth Youdao followed his father in the commandery; when his father died he accepted no gift from clerks or people.
entries.literal: In his weak-capping years Youdao followed his father in the commandery; when his father died, gifts from clerks and people he accepted not one.

entries.zh: 事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He served his mother and was known for filial piety.
entries.literal: He served his mother and was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 與叔父別居，叔父為奴誣以逆，遊道誘令返，雪而殺之。
entries.en: Living apart from an uncle whose slave falsely accused him of treason, Youdao lured the slave back, cleared the charge, and killed him.
entries.literal: He lived apart from his uncle; the uncle had a slave falsely accuse him of treason—Youdao lured the slave to return, cleared the charge, and killed him.

entries.zh: 魏廣陽王深北伐，請為鎧曹，及為定州刺史，又以為府佐。
entries.en: When the Wei Prince of Guangyang marched north, Youdao was requested as armor-cases staff; as inspector of Ding he again made Youdao a staff officer.
entries.literal: When Wei Prince of Guangyang campaigned north, Youdao was requested as armor-cases staff; when he became inspector of Ding province, Youdao was again made staff officer of his office.

entries.zh: 廣陽王為葛榮所殺，元徽誣其降賊，收錄妻子，遊道為訴得釋，與廣陽王子迎喪返葬。
entries.en: The Prince of Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong; Yuan Hui slandered him for surrendering to bandits and seized his family—Youdao pleaded and freed them and with the prince's son escorted the coffin home for burial.
entries.literal: The Prince of Guangyang was killed by Ge Rong; Yuan Hui slandered him as having surrendered to the bandits and seized his wife and children—Youdao pleaded and won their release, and with the prince's son escorted the coffin back for burial.

entries.zh: 中尉酈善長嘉其氣節，引為殿中侍御史，臺中語曰：「見賊能討宋遊道。」
entries.en: Commandant Li Shanchang admired his spirit and made him palace attendant censor; within the Terrace they said: "See a bandit and strike— that is Song Youdao."
entries.literal: Commandant Li Shanchang admired his integrity and spirit and brought him in as palace attendant censor; within the Terrace they said: "To see a bandit and be able to attack him—that is Song Youdao."

entries.zh: 遊道剛直，疾惡如讐，見人犯罪，皆欲致之極法。
entries.en: Youdao was rigidly upright and hated wrongdoing like an enemy; whenever he saw a crime he wanted the harshest penalty applied.
entries.literal: Youdao was upright and rigid, hating evil as though it were a foe; seeing anyone commit a crime, he wished to bring them to the utmost penalty.

entries.zh: 彈糾見事，又好察陰私。
entries.en: He impeached whatever came before him and loved to probe private conduct as well.
entries.literal: He impeached matters before his eyes and also loved to probe private affairs.

entries.zh: 問獄察情，捶撻嚴酷。
entries.en: In interrogation he read circumstances through beatings that were savage and cruel.
entries.literal: In questioning prisoners and examining circumstances, beating and flogging were severe and cruel.

entries.zh: 兗州刺史李子貞在州貪暴，遊道案之。
entries.en: Li Zizhen, inspector of Yanzhou, was greedy and brutal in his province; Youdao took up the case.
entries.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Li Zizhen was greedy and violent in the province; Youdao investigated him.

entries.zh: 文襄以貞預建義勳，意將含忍。
entries.en: Gao Cheng meant to show forbearance because Zizhen had helped in the founding struggle.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng, because Zizhen had shared in the merit of founding the righteous cause, intended to be forbearing.

entries.zh: 遊道疑陳元康為其內助，密啟云：「子貞、元康交遊，恐其別有請囑。」
entries.en: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang was backing him from within and secretly wrote, "Zizhen and Yuankang are close; I fear there are other private arrangements."
entries.literal: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang was his inside helper and secretly reported: "Zizhen and Yuankang associate; I fear they have other private requests."

entries.zh: 文襄怒，於尚書都堂集百僚，撲殺子貞。
entries.en: Gao Cheng flew into a rage, assembled the hundred officials in the main hall of the Masters of Writing, and beat Zizhen to death on the spot.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng in anger, at the Masters of Writing main hall assembled the hundred officials and beat Zizhen to death.

entries.zh: 又兗州人為遊道生立祠堂，像題曰「忠清君」。
entries.en: Men of Yanzhou also built him a living shrine, with an image inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."
entries.literal: Moreover, men of Yanzhou while he still lived built a shrine to Youdao, with his image inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."

entries.zh: 遊道別劾吉寧等五人同死，有欣悅色。
entries.en: Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others for the same death sentence, his face bright with satisfaction.
entries.literal: Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others to die together, with a look of pleasure.

entries.zh: 朝士甚鄙之。
entries.en: Court gentlemen despised him for it.
entries.literal: Court gentlemen greatly despised him for it.

entries.zh: 及文襄疑黃門郎溫子昇知元瑾之謀，繫之獄而餓之，食敝襦而死。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng suspected Wen Zisheng of Yuan Jin's plot, he bound and starved him—he ate his ragged coat and died.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng suspected Yellow Gate gentleman Wen Zisheng of knowing Yuan Jin's plot, he bound him in prison and starved him—he ate his ragged coat and died.

entries.zh: 棄屍路隅，遊道收而葬之。
entries.en: The corpse was cast by the road; Youdao collected and buried it.
entries.literal: The corpse was cast by the roadside; Youdao collected and buried it.

entries.zh: 文襄謂曰：「吾近書與京師諸貴，論及朝士，卿僻於朋黨，將為一病。
entries.en: Gao Cheng said: "I wrote the capital nobles on court gentlemen—you lean to factions; that is one sickness.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng said: "I recently wrote to the nobles of the capital discussing court gentlemen—you are partial to factions; that will be one sickness.

entries.zh: 今卿真是重舊節義人，此情不可奪。
entries.en: Now you truly weigh old ties and righteousness; that cannot be taken.
entries.literal: Now you are truly a man who weighs old ties and righteousness; that feeling cannot be taken away.

entries.zh: 子昇吾本不殺之，卿葬之何所憚。
entries.en: I would not have killed Zisheng—what fear in burying him?
entries.literal: I originally would not kill Zisheng—what do you fear in burying him?

entries.zh: 天下人代卿怖者，是不知吾心也。」
entries.en: Those who would replace you in fear do not know my heart."
entries.literal: Those in the world who would replace you in fear do not know my heart."

entries.zh: 尋除御史中尉。
entries.en: Soon he was made censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: Soon he was made censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 魏安平王坐事亡，章武二王及諸王妃、太妃是其近親者皆被徵責。
entries.en: When the Prince of Anping perished, Zhangwu's two princes and related consorts and grand consorts were all summoned to account.
entries.literal: When Prince of Anping Wang sat in a matter and perished, Zhangwu's two princes and the various princes' consorts and grand consorts who were his close kin were all summoned to account.

entries.zh: 都官郎中畢義雲主其事，有奏而禁，有不奏輒禁者。
entries.en: Bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun directed the matter—memorial or no, he forbade.
entries.literal: Bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun directed the matter; where there was a memorial he forbade, where there was none he still forbade.

entries.zh: 遊道判下廷尉科罪，高隆之不同，於是反誣遊道厲色挫辱己，遂枉考羣令史證成之，與僕射襄城王旭、尚書鄭述祖等上言曰：「飾偽亂真，國法所必去；
entries.en: Youdao sent the case to the Court of Justice; Gao Longzhi disagreed and slandered Youdao for stern insults, falsely examining clerks to prove it; with Vice Director Wang Xu of Xiangcheng, Director Zheng Suzu and others he memorialized: "Adorning falsehood and confusing truth—state law must remove it;
