entries.literal: Youdao judged and sent down to the Court of Justice for punishment; Gao Longzhi disagreed; thereupon in reverse he slandered Youdao for stern color and insulting himself, and falsely examined group clerks to prove it, and with Vice Director Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu, Director Zheng Suzu and others memorialized: "Adorning falsehood and confusing truth—what state law must remove;

entries.zh: 附下罔上，王政所不容。
entries.en: Winning over subordinates while deceiving superiors—royal governance cannot tolerate it.
entries.literal: Winning over subordinates while deceiving superiors—what royal governance cannot tolerate.

entries.zh: 謹案尚書左丞宋遊道名望本闕，功績何紀。
entries.en: We find Left Vice Director Song Youdao—fame deficient, merit unrecorded:
entries.literal: We respectfully find Left Vice Director Song Youdao—his fame and standing originally deficient, his merit and record—what tally?

entries.zh: 屬永安之始，朝士亡散，乏人之際，叨竊臺郎。
entries.en: at Yong'an's start, when court gentlemen fled, he stole a Terrace post in dearth of men.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, court gentlemen scattered in flight; in a time of dearth of men he stole the Terrace gentleman post.

entries.zh: 躁行諂言，肆其姦詐，罕識名義，不顧典文，人鄙其心，衆畏其口。
entries.en: Restless and fawning, full of treachery; heedless of canon; men despised him, crowds feared his mouth.
entries.literal: Restless conduct and fawning words, giving full play to his treachery; he rarely knew righteousness, heedless of canonical text; men despised his heart, the crowd feared his mouth.

entries.zh: 出州入省，歷忝清資，而長惡不悛，曾無忌諱，毀譽由己，憎惡任情。
entries.en: Out to provinces, in the Secretariat on pure posts, he long did evil unrepentant; praise and blame were his, hatred his whim.
entries.literal: Going out to provinces, entering the Secretariat, he repeatedly held pure posts, yet long did evil without repentance, never restrained; praise and blame were his own, hatred and favor at his whim.

entries.zh: 比因安平王事，遂肆其褊心，因公報隙，與郎中畢義雲遞相糾舉。
entries.en: Recently over the Prince of Anping he gave play to narrow heart, repaying grudges through office, mutually impeaching with Bi Yiyun.
entries.literal: Recently because of the Prince of Anping Wang matter he then gave full play to his narrow heart, using public business to repay a grudge, mutually impeaching with bureau gentleman Bi Yiyun.

entries.zh: 又左外兵郎中魏叔道牒云：『局內降人左澤等為京畿送省，令取保放出。』
entries.en: Also Wei Shudao of Left Outer Army Bureau wrote: 'Surrendered men Zuo Ze were sent to the capital with orders to release on guaranty.'
entries.literal: Also Left Outer Army Bureau gentleman Wei Shudao's document said: 'Within the bureau surrendered men Zuo Ze and others were sent to the capital by the capital region with orders to release on guaranty.'

entries.zh: 大將軍在省日，判『聽』。
entries.en: When the great general was in the province he judged 'allow.'
entries.literal: When the great general was in the province he judged 'hear and allow.'

entries.zh: 遊道發怒曰：『往日官府何物官府，將此為例！』
entries.en: Youdao raged: 'What sort of office was that, to take as precedent!'
entries.literal: Youdao grew angry and said: 'In past days what sort of office was that office, that you take this as precedent!'

entries.zh: 又云：『乘前旨格，成何物旨格！』
entries.en: Also: 'Riding a former edict—what edict is that!'
entries.literal: Also he said: 'Riding on a former edict pattern—what sort of edict pattern is that!'

entries.zh: 依事請問，遊道並皆承引。
entries.en: Questioned on the matter, Youdao acknowledged all.
entries.literal: Asked according to the matter, Youdao acknowledged all.

entries.zh: 案律：『對捍詔使，無人臣之禮，大不敬者死。』
entries.en: By code: 'Resisting an edict-bearing envoy without minister's rites—death for great irreverence.'
entries.literal: According to the code: 'Resisting and defying an edict-bearing envoy—without a minister's rites, great irreverence is death.'

entries.zh: 對捍使者尚得死坐，況遊道吐不臣之言，犯慢上之罪，口稱夷、齊，心懷盜跖，欺公賣法，受納苞苴，產隨官厚，財與位積，雖贓汚未露，而姦詐如是。
entries.en: Resisting an envoy earns death; how much more unministered words, slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harbors robbers, deceiving the public, taking bribes—wealth piled with rank though bribery was not yet exposed.
entries.literal: Resisting an envoy still earns death; how much more Youdao's unministered words, the crime of slighting superiors, mouth naming Yi and Qi while heart harboring robbers, deceiving the public and selling the law, receiving wrapped bribes—property following office thick, wealth with rank piled; though bribery was not yet exposed, treachery was such.

entries.zh: 舉此一隅，餘詐可驗。
entries.en: This one corner proves the rest.
entries.literal: Citing this one corner, the rest of the fraud can be verified.

entries.zh: 今依禮據律處遊道死罪。」
entries.en: Now by ritual and law we place Youdao in the death crime."
entries.literal: Now according to ritual and law we place Youdao in the death crime."

entries.zh: 是時朝士皆分為遊道不濟。
entries.en: Court gentlemen took sides, thinking Youdao would fail.
entries.literal: At the time court gentlemen all took sides, thinking Youdao would not succeed.

entries.zh: 而文襄聞其與隆之相抗之言，謂楊遵彥曰：「此真是鯁直大剛惡人。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng, hearing his clash with Longzhi, told Yang Zunyan: "This is truly a straight, hard, evil man."
entries.literal: Yet Gao Cheng, hearing his words contending with Longzhi, told Yang Zunyan: "This is truly a straight, great, hard evil man."

entries.zh: 遵彥曰：「譬之畜狗，本取其吠，今以數吠殺之，恐將來無復吠狗。」
entries.en: Zunyan said: "Like a dog kept for barking—kill it for barking too much and later none will bark."
entries.literal: Zunyan said: "It is like keeping a dog—you take it for its barking; now if you kill it for barking too much, I fear later there will be no dog to bark."

entries.zh: 詔付廷尉，遊道坐除名。
entries.en: An edict sent him to the Court of Justice; Youdao was removed from office.
entries.literal: An edict sent him to the Court of Justice; Youdao was sentenced to removal from name.

entries.zh: 文襄使元景康謂曰：「卿早逐我向幷州，不爾，他經略殺卿。」
entries.en: Gao Cheng sent Yuan Jingkang: "Follow me early to Bing—or others in strategy will kill you."
entries.literal: Gao Cheng sent Yuan Jingkang to tell him: "You early follow me to Bing province, or else others in strategy will kill you."

entries.zh: 遊道從至晉陽，以為大行臺吏部，又以為太原公開府諮議。
entries.en: Youdao followed to Jinyang as Traveling Court personnel director and advisory staff of the Taiyuan Duke's office.
entries.literal: Youdao followed to Jinyang and was made Traveling Court personnel director; also made advisory staff of Taiyuan Duke's opening office.

entries.zh: 及平陽公為中尉，遊道以諮議領書侍御史。
entries.en: When the Prince of Pingyang was commandant, Youdao as advisory staff held writing attendant censor.
entries.literal: When Prince of Pingyang was commandant, Youdao as advisory staff held the writing attendant censor post.

entries.zh: 尋以本官兼司徒左長史。
entries.en: Soon he concurrently held Secretariat Left chief administrator.
entries.literal: Soon with his original post he concurrently held Secretariat Left chief administrator.

entries.zh: 東萊王道習參御史選，限外投狀，道習與遊道有舊，使令史受之。
entries.en: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi joined censor selection and submitted beyond the limit; old friends with Youdao, he had the clerk receive it.
entries.literal: Prince of Donglai Dao Xi joined censor selection; beyond the limit he submitted a petition; Dao Xi was old friends with Youdao and had the clerk receive it.

entries.zh: 文襄怒，杖遊道而判之曰：「遊道稟性遒悍，是非肆口，吹毛洗垢，瘡疵人物。
entries.en: Gao Cheng flogged Youdao and judged: "Youdao is fierce; right and wrong pour from his mouth; he blows hairs to find dirt and scars men.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng was angry, flogged Youdao and judged: "Youdao's nature is fierce and tough; right and wrong pour from his mouth; he blows hairs to wash away dirt and scars men's persons.

entries.zh: 往與郎中蘭景雲忿競，列事十條。
entries.en: Formerly he quarreled with Lan Jingyun, listing ten items.
entries.literal: Formerly he quarreled with bureau gentleman Lan Jingyun, listing ten items.

entries.zh: 及加推窮，便是虛妄。
entries.en: Pushed and examined, they were false.
entries.literal: When pushed and examined, they were empty and false.

entries.zh: 方共道習淩侮朝典，法官而犯，特是難原，宜付省科。」
entries.en: Now with Dao Xi he insults court canon—a judge who violates it is hard to forgive; hand to the province."
entries.literal: Now together with Dao Xi he insults and violates the court canon—a judge who violates it is especially hard to forgive; he should be handed to the province for punishment."

entries.zh: 遊道被禁，獄吏欲為脫枷，遊道不肯曰：「此令命所著，不可輒脫。」
entries.en: Imprisoned, clerks wished to remove his cangue; Youdao refused: "Orders are written here—it cannot be removed."
entries.literal: Youdao was imprisoned; prison clerks wished to remove his cangue; Youdao would not: "This is where orders are written—it cannot be lightly removed."

entries.zh: 文襄聞而免之。
entries.en: Gao Cheng heard and pardoned him.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng heard and pardoned him.

entries.zh: 遊道抗志不改。
entries.en: Youdao's upright will did not change.
entries.literal: Youdao's upright will did not change.

entries.zh: 天保元年，以遊道兼太府卿，乃於少府覆檢主司盜截，得鉅萬計。
entries.en: In Tianbao's first year Youdao was made concurrent Grand Steward of the Palace; re-examining the chief office at the Lesser Treasury for theft, he uncovered a sum in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, Youdao was made concurrent Grand Steward of the Palace; he then at the Lesser Treasury re-examined the chief office theft and interception and obtained a huge sum.

entries.zh: 奸吏返誣奏之，下獄。
entries.en: Corrupt clerks turned on him with false accusations; he was thrown into prison.
entries.literal: Corrupt clerks in turn slandered and memorialized against him; he was cast into prison.

entries.zh: 尋得出，不歸家，徑之府理事。
entries.en: He was soon released, did not go home, and went straight to his office to work.
entries.literal: Soon he was released, did not return home, and went straight to the office to handle affairs.

entries.zh: 卒，遺令薄葬，不立碑表，不求贈諡。
entries.en: When he died he ordered a plain burial—no stele, no marker, no posthumous title sought.
entries.literal: At death he left instructions for a simple burial, no stele or tablet, and no request for a posthumous title.

entries.zh: 贈瓜州刺史。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Governor of Guazhou.
entries.literal: Posthumously made Governor of Guazhou.

entries.zh: 武平中以子士素久典機密，重贈儀同三司，諡曰貞惠。
entries.en: In the Wuping era, because his son Shisu had long handled state secrets, he was again posthumously made Pillar of State with the posthumous name Upright and Gracious.
entries.literal: In Wuping, because his son Shisu had long held confidential duties, he was again posthumously made Pillar of State, posthumous name Zhenhui.

entries.zh: 盧斐，字子章，范陽涿人也。
entries.en: Lu Fei, courtesy name Zizhang, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.
entries.literal: Lu Fei, styled Zizhang, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.

entries.zh: 父同，魏殿中尚書。
entries.en: His father Tong had been palace attendant master of writing under the Wei.
entries.literal: His father Tong was Wei Palace Attendant Master of Writing.

entries.zh: 斐性殘忍，以強斷知名。
entries.en: Fei was cruel by nature and famed for harsh, decisive rulings.
entries.literal: Fei's nature was cruel; he was known for forceful judgment.

entries.zh: 世宗引為相府刑獄參軍。
entries.en: Gao Cheng brought him in as legal-prison aide in the chancellor's office.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng summoned him as legal-prison aide in the chancellor's office.

entries.zh: 謂之云：「狂簡，斐然成章，非佳名字也。」
entries.en: He told him, "'Reckless and terse, yet splendor to completion'—not a flattering name."
entries.literal: He said to him: "Reckless and terse, yet splendor to completion—not a fine name."

entries.zh: 天保中，稍遷尚書左丞，別典京畿詔獄，酷濫非人情所為。
entries.en: In the Tianbao era he rose to left vice director of the masters of writing and separately ran capital-region imperial prison cases with cruelty beyond ordinary humanity.
entries.literal: In Tianbao he was gradually promoted to Master of Writing Left Vice Director, separately in charge of metropolitan-area imperial prison cases, cruel and excessive beyond what human feeling allows.

entries.zh: 無問事之大小，拷掠過度，於大棒車輻下死者非一。
entries.en: Regardless of the crime's scale, torture went too far; not a few died under the great rod or the chariot wheel.
entries.literal: Without regard to whether the matter was great or small, torture exceeded bounds; under the great rod and chariot wheel hub those who died were not one.

entries.zh: 或嚴冬至寒，置囚於冰雪之上；
entries.en: Sometimes in bitter midwinter he set prisoners on ice and snow;
entries.literal: Sometimes in severe winter's cold he placed prisoners on ice and snow;

entries.zh: 或盛夏酷熱，暴之日下。
entries.en: sometimes in blazing midsummer he left them in the open sun.
entries.literal: sometimes in midsummer's fierce heat he exposed them under the sun.

entries.zh: 枉陷人致死者，前後百數。
entries.en: Those he framed to death numbered in the hundreds.
entries.literal: Those wrongly framed and driven to death numbered in the hundreds before and after.

entries.zh: 又伺察官人罪失，動卽奏聞，朝士見之，莫不重跡屏氣，皆目之為盧校事。
entries.en: He also spied on officials' faults and reported every move; court gentlemen shortened their steps and held their breath at the sight of him, and all called him Investigator Lu.
entries.literal: He also watched officials' faults and at every move memorialized the throne; when court gentlemen saw him, none did not walk with shortened steps and held breath—all called him Investigator Lu.

entries.zh: 斐後以謗史，與李庶俱病鞭死獄中。
entries.en: Fei later slandered the history; he and Li Shu both died in prison of flogging wounds.
entries.literal: Fei later for slandering the history, together with Li Shu, died of flogging-wounds in prison.

entries.zh: 畢義雲，小字陀兒。
entries.en: Bi Yiyun's childhood name was Tuo'er.
entries.literal: Bi Yiyun, childhood name Tuo'er.

entries.zh: 少粗俠，家在兗州北境，常劫掠行旅，州里患之。
entries.en: Young, he was rough and swaggering; his family lived on Yanzhou's northern frontier and often robbed travelers, to the province's grief.
entries.literal: In youth he was rough and chivalric; his family was on Yanzhou's northern border and often robbed travelers—the province and district suffered from him.

entries.zh: 晚方折節從官。
entries.en: Only late in life did he reform and take office.
entries.literal: Only late did he restrain himself and enter office.

entries.zh: 累遷尚書都官郎中。
entries.en: He rose to director of the bureau of punishments in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Masters of Writing Director of the Bureau of Punishments.

entries.zh: 性嚴酷，事多幹了。
entries.en: He was severe and cruel, but in business he was sharp and effective.
entries.literal: His nature was severe and cruel, and in affairs he was largely capable and effective.

entries.zh: 齊文襄作相，以為稱職，令普勾偽官，專以車輻考掠，所獲甚多。
entries.en: When Gao Cheng was chancellor he judged him capable and ordered a sweep for false officials, relying chiefly on chariot-wheel torture; the haul was enormous.
entries.literal: When Gao Cheng was chancellor he found him fit for duty and ordered a universal investigation of false officials, using exclusively chariot-wheel torture; what was obtained was very great.

entries.zh: 然大起怨謗。
entries.en: Yet resentment and outcry rose everywhere.
entries.literal: Yet resentment and slander rose greatly.

entries.zh: 曾為司州吏所訟，云其有所減截，幷改換文書。
entries.en: A Si Province clerk once sued him, claiming he had skimmed funds and falsified documents.
entries.literal: He was once sued by a Si Province clerk who said he had skimmed funds and altered documents together.

entries.zh: 文襄以其推偽，衆人怨望，並無所問，乃拘吏數人而斬之。
entries.en: Gao Cheng, since Yiyun was exposing false officials and the crowd was bitter, ignored the charge and instead detained several clerks and beheaded them.
entries.literal: Gao Cheng, because he was pressing false officials and the crowd was resentful, questioned nothing of it; instead he detained several clerks and beheaded them.

entries.zh: 因此銳情訊鞠，威名日盛。
entries.en: After that his zeal for interrogation sharpened and his fearsome name spread.
entries.literal: From this his zeal for interrogation sharpened and his dread name grew daily.

entries.zh: 然重交遊，存然諾之分。
entries.en: Yet he prized friendship and kept his pledged word.
entries.literal: Yet he valued friendship and kept the bond of pledged word.

entries.zh: 歷官嚴整，而時大納賄，分及親故之艱匱者，其男女孤弱為嫁娶之，臨喪必哀，躬親襄事。
entries.en: In office he was stern and exacting, yet he also took heavy bribes and shared them with kin and friends in need; he arranged marriages for orphaned men and women, and at every funeral he mourned deeply and handled the rites himself.
entries.literal: Through his offices he was stern and orderly, yet at times took large bribes and distributed them to kin and friends in hardship and want; for orphaned men and women he arranged marriages, and at funerals he was always mournful and personally assisted in the rites.

entries.zh: 為司州綱紀與牧昌樂、西河二王乖忤，及二王薨，每事經恤之，與頓丘李獎一面，便定死交。
entries.en: As Si Province regulator he fell out with the Changlean and Xihe princes; when both died he still looked after their affairs. With Li Jiang of Dunqiu he met once and swore friendship unto death.
entries.literal: As Si Province regulator he clashed with the princes governing Changlean and Xihe; when the two princes died, he showed care in every matter concerning them. With Dunqiu Li Jiang, after one meeting they swore death friendship.

entries.zh: 獎曰：「我年位已高。
entries.en: Jiang said, "My years and rank are already high.
entries.literal: Jiang said: "My years and rank are already high.

entries.zh: 會用弟為佐史，令弟北面於我足矣。」
entries.en: When the time comes I will use my younger brother as aide; let him face north to me and that will do."
entries.literal: When the time comes I will employ my younger brother as aide; having him face north toward me is enough."

entries.zh: 遊道曰：「不能。」
entries.en: Youdao said, "I cannot."
entries.literal: Youdao said: "I cannot."

entries.zh: 旣而獎為河南尹，辟遊道為中正，使者相屬，以衣帢待之，握手歡謔。
entries.en: Soon Jiang became Intendant of Henan and appointed Youdao impartial judge; envoys came one after another, and he received him informally, clasping hands in easy jest.
entries.literal: Before long Jiang became Intendant of Henan and summoned Youdao as impartial judge; messengers came in succession, and he received him with headcloth, hand in hand in merry banter.

entries.zh: 元顥入洛，獎受其命，出使徐州，都督元孚與城人趙紹兵殺之。
entries.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his orders and went to Xuzhou on mission; Area Commander Yuan Fu and a townsman named Zhao Shao killed him with troops.
entries.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his commission and went out as envoy to Xuzhou; Area Commander Yuan Fu with the city man Zhao Shao killed him by force of arms.

entries.zh: 遊道為獎訟冤，得雪，又表為請贈，廻己考一泛階以益之。
entries.en: Youdao sued to clear Jiang's name and won, then memorialized for posthumous honors, deducting one grade from his own review to add to Jiang's.
entries.literal: Youdao pleaded Jiang's grievance and cleared his name, and also memorialized to request posthumous honors, turning back one grade from his own examination to add to Jiang's.

entries.zh: 又與劉廞結交，託廞弟粹於徐州殺趙紹。
entries.en: He also befriended Liu Yin and had Yin's younger brother Cui kill Zhao Shao at Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He also befriended Liu Yin and entrusted Yin's younger brother Cui at Xuzhou to kill Zhao Shao.

entries.zh: 後劉廞伏法於洛陽，粹以徐州叛，官軍討平之，梟粹首於鄴市。
entries.en: Later Liu Yin was executed at Luoyang; Cui rebelled in Xuzhou, government troops put him down, and his head was displayed in the Ye market.
entries.literal: Later Liu Yin was executed by law at Luoyang; Cui rebelled at Xuzhou, government troops suppressed him, and Cui's head was exposed at Ye market.

entries.zh: 孫騰使客告市司，得錢五百萬後聽收。
entries.en: Sun Teng sent an agent to the market office saying they could collect the head only after five million cash was paid.
entries.literal: Sun Teng sent a client to tell the market office that only after five million cash was received would they be allowed to take it down.

entries.zh: 遊道時為司州中從事，令家人作劉粹所親，於州陳訴，依律判「許」而奏之。
entries.en: Youdao was then Central Army aide in Si Province; he had his household pose as Liu Cui's relatives, sue in the province, obtain a legal ruling of "permitted," and memorialized it.
entries.literal: Youdao was then Central Army aide of Si Province; he had his household pose as Liu Cui's kin, filed suit in the province, and by law obtained a ruling of "permitted" and memorialized it.

entries.zh: 勑至，市司猶不許。
entries.en: When the edict arrived, the market office still refused.
entries.literal: When the edict arrived, the market office still would not allow it.

entries.zh: 遊道杖司，勒使速付。
entries.en: Youdao beat the market staff and forced them to surrender the head immediately.
entries.literal: Youdao flogged the office staff and compelled them to hand it over at once.

entries.zh: 騰聞大怒。
entries.en: Teng was furious when he heard.
entries.literal: When Teng heard of it he was greatly enraged.

entries.zh: 時李獎二子構、訓居貧，遊道後令其求三富人死事，判免之，凡得錢百五十萬，盡以入構、訓。
entries.en: Li Jiang's sons Gou and Xun were then poor; Youdao later had them find three wealthy men facing capital charges, win acquittals, and collect one million five hundred thousand cash, which he gave them in full.
entries.literal: At the time Li Jiang's two sons Gou and Xun lived in poverty; Youdao later had them seek three rich men on capital charges, obtain acquittal, and in all got one million five hundred thousand cash, which he gave entirely to Gou and Xun.

entries.zh: 其使氣黨俠如此。
entries.en: His swaggering, faction-bound chivalry was of this sort.
entries.literal: His bravado and chivalric partisanship were like this.

entries.zh: 時人語曰：「遊道獼猴面，陸操科斗形，意識不關貌，何謂醜者必無情。」
entries.en: A saying of the time ran, "Youdao has a monkey's face and Lu Cao a tadpole's body—mind has nothing to do with looks; why assume the ugly are heartless?"
entries.literal: People said at the time: "Youdao has a monkey's face, Lu Cao a tadpole's shape; awareness has nothing to do with looks—why say the ugly must be without feeling?"

entries.zh: 構嘗因遊道會客，因戲之曰：「賢從在門外，大好人，宜自迎接。」
entries.en: Once, while Gou was at Youdao's gathering of guests, he teased him: "Your excellent cousin is at the gate—a fine fellow; you ought to welcome him yourself."
entries.literal: Gou once at Youdao's reception for guests playfully said to him: "Your worthy cousin is outside the gate, a very fine man—you should go welcome him yourself."

entries.zh: 為通名稱「族弟遊山。」
entries.en: He sent word in under the name "clansman You Shan."
entries.literal: He had him announced under the name "clansman cousin You Shan."

entries.zh: 遊道出見之，乃獼猴衣帽也。
entries.en: Youdao went out to receive him and found monkey cap and clothes.
entries.literal: Youdao went out to see him—it was monkey cap and clothes.

entries.zh: 將與構絕，構謝之，豁然如舊。
entries.en: He was ready to break with Gou, but Gou apologized and they were suddenly close again.
entries.literal: He was about to break with Gou, but Gou apologized and they were suddenly as before.

entries.zh: 遊道死後，構為定州長史，遊道第三子士孫為墨曹、博陵王管記，與典籖共誣奏構。
entries.en: After Youdao's death, Gou became chief clerk of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shisun, registrar in the Ink Office and recorder to the Prince of Boling, joined the registry keeper in a false accusation against Gou.
entries.literal: After Youdao died, Gou became chief clerk of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shisun was Ink Office registrar and recorder for the Prince of Boling, and together with the registry keeper falsely memorialized against Gou.

entries.zh: 構於禁所祭遊道而訴焉。
entries.en: Imprisoned, Gou sacrificed to Youdao and pleaded to him.
entries.literal: Gou in the detention house offered sacrifice to Youdao and appealed to him.

entries.zh: 士遜晝臥如夢者，見遊道怒己曰：「我與構恩義，汝豈不知，何共小人謀陷清直之士！」
entries.en: Shixun napped by day as if dreaming and saw Youdao rebuke him: "Jiang and I were bound in grace and duty—do you not know it? How dare you join petty men to trap an upright man!"
entries.literal: Shixun by day lay asleep as in a dream and saw Youdao angrily addressing him: "Jiang and I had bond of grace and duty—do you not know it? How can you join petty men to plot against an upright man!"

entries.zh: 士遜驚跪曰：「不敢，不敢。」
entries.en: Shixun knelt in terror and said, "I dare not, I dare not."
entries.literal: Shixun in alarm knelt and said: "I dare not, I dare not."

entries.zh: 旬日而卒。
entries.en: Within ten days he was dead.
entries.literal: Within ten days he died.

entries.zh: 乾明初，子瑞遷御史中丞。
entries.en: Early in Qianming, Zirui became censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianming, Zirui was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 鄭子默正被任用，義雲之姑卽子默祖母，遂除度支尚書，攝左丞。
entries.en: Zheng Zimo was then in favor; Yiyun's aunt was Zimo's grandmother, so he was made minister of revenue and acting left vice director.
entries.literal: Zheng Zimo was then in active use; Yi Yun's paternal aunt was Zimo's grandmother, and he was therefore made Minister of Revenue and acting Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 子默誅後，左丞便解。
entries.en: After Zimo was killed, he gave up the acting left vice director post at once.
entries.literal: After Zimo was executed, the left vice director post was at once relinquished.

entries.zh: 孝昭赴晉陽，高元海留鄴，義雲深相依附。
entries.en: When Gao Yan went to Jinyang and Gao Yuanhai stayed at Ye, Yiyun attached himself to Yuanhai with deep reliance.
entries.literal: When Gao Yan went to Jinyang, Gao Yuanhai remained at Ye; Yi Yun clung to him in deep dependence.

entries.zh: 知其信向釋氏，常隨之聽講，為此款密，無所不至。
entries.en: Knowing Yuanhai was devoted to the Buddhist teaching, Yiyun often followed him to lectures; for that warm friendship he spared no effort.
entries.literal: Knowing that he was devoted to the Buddhist teaching, [Yiyun] often followed him to hear lectures; for this intimate friendship he went to every length.

entries.zh: 及孝昭大漸，顧命武成。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaozhao grew critically ill, he entrusted the succession to Gao Zhan.
entries.literal: When Xiaozhao grew critically ill, he entrusted the succession to Gao Zhan.

entries.zh: 高歸彥至都，武成猶致疑惑。
entries.en: When Gao Guiyan reached the capital, Gao Zhan still harbored doubts about him.
entries.literal: When Gao Guiyan reached the capital, Gao Zhan still harbored doubts about him.

entries.zh: 元海遣犢車迎義雲入北宮參審，遂與元海等勸進，仍從幸晉陽，參預時政。
entries.en: Yuanhai sent an ox cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace for the deliberations; he then joined Yuanhai and the others in urging Gao Zhan to the throne, followed the court to Jinyang, and took part in affairs of state.
entries.literal: Yuanhai sent an ox cart to bring Yiyun into the Northern Palace to take part in the deliberations; he then joined Yuanhai and the others in urging [Gao Zhan] to take the throne, followed the imperial progress to Jinyang, and joined in the government of the time.

entries.zh: 尋除兗州刺史，給後部鼓吹，卽本州也，軒昂自得，意望銓衡之舉。
entries.en: Soon he was made governor of Yan Province and given rear-guard musicians—it was his native province. He carried himself with lofty pride, his hopes set on a capital post in the personnel offices.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Province, given rear-guard musicians—it was his home province; he bore himself loftily and at ease, his ambition fixed on an appointment through the evaluation and selection offices.

entries.zh: 見諸人自陳，逆許引接。
entries.en: When petitioners came before him, he would assent against expectation and draw them in.
entries.literal: When he saw people presenting themselves, he would contrary to expectation assent and draw them in.

entries.zh: 又言離別暫時，非久在州。
entries.en: He also said his absence was only temporary and he would not long stay in the province.
entries.literal: He also said his leave was only temporary and he would not long remain in the province.

entries.zh: 先有鐃吹，至於案部行遊，遂兩部並用。
entries.en: He already had nao-and-blowing musicians; when he toured his jurisdiction, both bands went out together.
entries.literal: He already had nao-and-blowing musicians; when it came to touring his jurisdiction, both ensembles were used together.

entries.zh: 猶作書與元海，論敘時事。
entries.en: He still wrote Yuanhai a letter discussing affairs of the day.
entries.literal: He still wrote a letter to Yuanhai discussing affairs of the time.

entries.zh: 元海入內，不覺遺落，給事中李孝貞得而奏之，為此元海漸疏，孝貞因是兼中書舍人。
entries.en: Yuanhai entered the palace and dropped it without noticing; palace attendant Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized it. Yuanhai grew gradually estranged, and Xiaozhen was made concurrent secretariat drafting officer.
entries.literal: When Yuanhai entered the palace he inadvertently dropped it; Palace Attendant Li Xiaozhen found it and memorialized it—on this account Yuanhai grew gradually estranged, and Xiaozhen was made concurrent Secretariat Drafting Officer.

entries.zh: 又高歸彥起逆，義雲在州私集人馬，並聚甲仗，將以自防，實無他意。
entries.en: When Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Yiyun in his province privately gathered men and horses and stockpiled arms and armor for self-defense—he truly had no other design.
entries.literal: Moreover, when Gao Guiyan rose in rebellion, Yiyun in his province privately gathered men and horses and also stockpiled arms and armor, intending them for his own defense—he truly had no other intent.

entries.zh: 為人所啟，及歸彥被擒，又列其朋黨專擅，為此追還。
entries.en: Someone reported him; when Guiyan was taken, Yiyun was also named among his partisans who had monopolized power, and for that he was recalled.
entries.literal: Someone reported him; when Guiyan was captured, [Yiyun] was also listed among his partisans who monopolized power—for this he was recalled.

entries.zh: 武成猶錄其往誠，竟不加罪，除兼七兵尚書。
entries.en: Gao Zhan still credited his past loyalty, did not punish him in the end, and appointed him concurrent minister of the seven armies.
entries.literal: Gao Zhan still credited his past loyalty, in the end did not punish him, and appointed him concurrent Minister of the Seven Armies.

entries.zh: 義雲性豪縱，頗以施惠為心，累世本州刺史，家富於財，士之匱乏者，多有拯濟。
entries.en: Yiyun was bold and unrestrained by nature, and took pleasure in doing favors. For generations his family had held the governorship of this province; the house was rich, and many needy scholars he rescued.
entries.literal: Yiyun was by nature bold and unrestrained, taking pleasure in showing favor; for generations his family had been governors of this province, his house rich in goods, and many scholars in want he aided and rescued.

entries.zh: 及貴，恣情驕侈，營造第宅宏壯，未幾而成。
entries.en: Once he rose high, he gave free rein to pride and extravagance and built a mansion so grand it was finished almost at once.
entries.literal: Once he grew eminent, he indulged pride and extravagance, building a mansion grand and vast that was finished in no time.

entries.zh: 閨門穢雜，聲遍朝野。
entries.en: His inner quarters were foul and disorderly; the scandal ran through court and countryside.
entries.literal: His inner quarters were foul and disorderly; the scandal ran through court and countryside.

entries.zh: 為郎時，與左丞宋遊道因公事忿競，遊道廷辱之云：「《雄狐》之詩，千載為汝。」
entries.en: As a gentleman he had quarreled with left vice director Song Youdao over official business; Youdao publicly humiliated him, saying, "The poem 'The Male Fox'—a thousand years it has waited for you."
entries.literal: When he was a gentleman, over official business he quarreled with Left Vice Director Song Youdao; Youdao publicly humiliated him, saying: "The poem 'The Male Fox'—for a thousand years it has waited for you."

entries.zh: 義雲一無所答。
entries.en: Yiyun answered not a word.
entries.literal: Yiyun answered not a word.

entries.zh: 然酷暴殘忍，非人理所及。
entries.en: Yet he was cruel and violent beyond what human reason can compass.
entries.literal: Yet he was cruel and violent beyond what human reason can compass.

entries.zh: 為家尤甚，子孫仆隸，常瘡痍被體。
entries.en: At home it was worst of all—children, grandchildren, and servants were often covered in sores and wounds.
entries.literal: At home it was worst of all—children, grandchildren, and servants were often covered in sores and wounds.

entries.zh: 有孽子善昭，性至凶頑，與義雲侍婢姦通，搒掠無數，為其著籠頭，系之庭樹，食以芻秣，十餘日乃釋之。
entries.en: He had a bastard son, Shanzhao, vicious to the core; he lay with Yiyun's maidservant, and after countless beatings Yiyun put a cangue on him, tied him to a courtyard tree, fed him fodder, and only released him after more than ten days.
entries.literal: He had a bastard son, Shanzhao, vicious to the utmost; he fornicated with Yiyun's maidservant, and after countless beatings Yiyun had a cangue put on him, tied him to a tree in the courtyard, fed him fodder, and only released him after more than ten days.

entries.zh: 夜中義雲被賊害，卽善昭所佩刀也，遺之於義雲庭中。
entries.en: In the night Yiyun was murdered—it was the knife Shanzhao wore; it was left in Yiyun's courtyard.
entries.literal: In the night Yiyun was murdered by a thief—it was the knife Shanzhao carried; it was left in Yiyun's courtyard.

entries.zh: 善昭聞難奔哭，家人得佩刀，善昭怖，便走出，投平恩墅舍。
entries.en: Shanzhao heard of the calamity and ran to weep; when the household found the sword, Shanzhao was terrified and fled at once to the Ping'en villa estate.
entries.literal: Shanzhao heard of the calamity and ran to weep; when the household found the worn sword, Shanzhao was frightened and fled at once, taking refuge at the Ping'en villa estate.

entries.zh: 旦日，世祖令舍人蘭子暢就宅推之。
entries.en: The next day Emperor Xiaozong ordered gentleman-of-the-household Lan Zichang to go to the mansion and investigate.
entries.literal: Next day Emperor Xiaozong ordered Gentleman-of-the-Household Lan Zichang to go to the mansion and investigate.

entries.zh: 爾前，義雲新納少室范陽盧氏，有色貌。
entries.en: Not long before, Yiyun had newly married the Lady Lu of Fanyang from the Shaoshi quarter—she had beauty and charm.
entries.literal: Some time before, Yiyun had newly taken in marriage the Lady Lu of Fanyang from the Shaoshi quarter—she had beauty and charm.

entries.zh: 子暢疑盧姦人所為，將加拷掠，盧具列善昭云爾，乃收捕繫臨漳獄，將斬之。
entries.en: Zichang suspected Lady Lu of adultery and was about to torture her; Lu laid out in full what Shanzhao had done—they seized him, bound him in Linzhang jail, and were about to execute him.
entries.literal: Zichang suspected Lady Lu of having done it with an adulterer and was about to put her to torture; Lu set out in full the facts about Shanzhao as told above—they then seized him, imprisoned him in Linzhang jail, and were about to execute him.

entries.zh: 邢卲上言，此乃大逆，義雲又是朝貴，不可發。
entries.en: Xing Shao submitted a memorial: "This is great treason, and Yiyun was a court noble—the sentence must not be carried out in public."
entries.literal: Xing Shao submitted a memorial: "This is great treason; Yiyun was moreover a court noble—the execution must not be carried out in public."

entries.zh: 乃斬於獄，棄屍漳水。
entries.en: He was beheaded in prison and the corpse cast into the Zhang River.
entries.literal: He was beheaded in prison and the corpse cast into the Zhang River.

entries.zh: 邸珍 宋遊道 盧斐 畢義雲
entries.en: Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun
entries.literal: Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun

entries.zh: 趙猛，太安狄那人。
entries.en: Zhao Meng was from Di in Tai’an.
entries.literal: Zhao Meng was a native of Di in Tai’an.

entries.zh: 姊為文穆皇帝繼室，生趙郡王琛。
entries.en: His elder sister was Emperor Wenmu’s successor consort and bore Zhao Commandery Prince Chen.
entries.literal: His elder sister was the successor consort of Emperor Wenmu and bore Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen.

entries.zh: 猛性方直，頗有器幹。
entries.en: Meng was upright and capable.
entries.literal: Meng was upright by nature and possessed considerable ability.

entries.zh: 高祖舉義，遷南營州刺史，卒。
entries.en: When Gaozu rose in arms, Meng was made inspector of South Ying Province, where he died in office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozu raised the righteous standard, Meng was transferred to be Inspector of South Ying Province and died in office.

entries.zh: 婁叡，字佛仁，武明皇後兄子也。
entries.en: Lou Rui, styled Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.
entries.literal: Lou Rui, courtesy name Foren, was a nephew of Empress Wuming.

entries.zh: 父壯，魏南部尚書。
entries.en: His father Zhuang served Wei as Minister of the Southern Department.
entries.literal: His father Zhuang was Minister of the Southern Department in Wei.

entries.zh: 叡少好弓馬，有武幹，為高祖帳內都督。
entries.en: In youth Rui loved archery and horsemanship, showed martial talent, and served in Gaozu’s personal guard.
entries.literal: Rui in youth loved bow and horse, had martial ability, and served as a commander in Gaozu’s personal guard.

entries.zh: 從破尒朱於韓陵，累遷開府儀同、驃騎大將軍。
entries.en: He fought at Hanling in the defeat of the Erzhu and rose through the ranks to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.
entries.literal: He followed in the defeat of the Erzhu at Hanling and was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and General of Cavalry with Rapid Steeds.

entries.zh: 叡無器幹，唯以外戚貴幸，而縱情財色，為時論所鄙。
entries.en: Rui had little talent and owed his rank only to kinship with the throne; he squandered himself on wealth and women, and contemporaries held him in contempt.
entries.literal: Rui lacked ability and relied solely on his status as an imperial affine for favor; he indulged wealth and women and was despised by contemporary opinion.

entries.zh: 皇建初，封東安王。
entries.en: At the opening of Huangjian he was made Prince of Dong’an.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Huangjian era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dong’an.

entries.zh: 高歸彥反於冀州，詔叡往平之。
entries.en: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, Rui was ordered to suppress him.
entries.literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled in Ji Province, an edict ordered Rui to go and pacify him.

entries.zh: 還，拜司徒公。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed director of the Department of State.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed Director of the Department of State.

entries.zh: 周兵寇東關，叡率軍赴援，頻戰有功，擒周將楊檦等。
entries.en: When Zhou troops threatened the eastern passes, Rui marched to their relief, won repeated victories, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.
entries.literal: When Zhou forces raided the eastern passes, Rui led troops to relieve them, fought repeatedly with merit, and captured the Zhou general Yang Biao and others.

entries.zh: 進大司馬，出總偏師，赴懸瓠。
entries.en: Promoted to grand marshal, he took a detached command at Xuanhu.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Grand Marshal and went out to command a detached force at Xuanhu.

entries.zh: 叡在豫境，留停百餘日，侵削官私，專行非法，坐免官。
entries.en: Rui lingered in Yu more than a hundred days, plundering public and private goods and acting with impunity, until he was dismissed.
entries.literal: Rui remained in the Yu region more than a hundred days, encroaching on public and private property and acting lawlessly on his own authority; for this he was removed from office.

entries.zh: 尋授太尉。
entries.en: He was soon appointed grand commandant.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 薨。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 尒朱文暢，榮第四子也。
entries.en: Erzhu Wenchang was Erzhu Rong’s fourth son.
entries.literal: Erzhu Wenchang was the fourth son of Rong.

entries.zh: 初封昌樂王。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed prince of Changle.
entries.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

entries.zh: 其姊魏孝莊皇後，及四胡敗滅，高祖納之，待其家甚厚，文暢由是拜肆州刺史。
entries.en: His sister had been Empress Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the Erzhu were overthrown, Gaozu married her and treated her kin lavishly, and Wenchang became inspector of Si Province.
entries.literal: His elder sister was Empress of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei; after the four Erzhu were destroyed, Gaozu took her in marriage and treated her family very generously, and Wenchang was therefore appointed Inspector of Si Province.

entries.zh: 家富於財，招致賓客，既籍門地，窮極豪侈，與丞相司馬任胄、主簿李世林、都督鄭仲禮、房子遠等深相愛狎，外示杯酒之交，而潛謀逆亂。
entries.en: Rich and hospitable, he leaned on his birth to live in extreme splendor. With Ren Zhou, Li Shilin, Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he feigned convivial friendship while secretly plotting revolt.
entries.literal: His household was rich in wealth and he gathered guests; relying on his lineage, he pursued luxury to the utmost. With the chief minister’s aide Ren Zhou, registrar Li Shilin, commander Zheng Zhongli, and Fang Ziyuan he was deeply intimate—outwardly they showed the friendship of wine cups, yet secretly they plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 自魏氏舊俗，以正月十五日夜為打竹簇之戲，有能中者，即時賞帛。
entries.en: By Wei custom, on the fifteenth night of the first month people played at striking bamboo targets; a hit won silk on the spot.
entries.literal: By the old custom of Wei, on the night of the fifteenth day of the first month there was a game of striking bamboo clusters; whoever hit the mark received silk rewards on the spot.

entries.zh: 任胄令仲禮藏刀於袴中，因高祖臨觀，謀為竊發，事捷之後，共奉文暢為主。
entries.en: Ren Zhou hid a blade in Zhongli’s trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they meant to strike—and if they succeeded, to set Wenchang on the throne.
entries.literal: Ren Zhou had Zhongli hide a knife in his trousers; when Gaozu came to watch, they planned a sudden attack, and if the affair succeeded they would together install Wenchang as ruler.

entries.zh: 為任氏家客薛季孝告高祖，問皆具伏。
entries.en: Ren’s retainer Xue Jixiao exposed them to Gaozu, and under questioning all confessed.
entries.literal: A retainer of the Ren household, Xue Jixiao, informed Gaozu; on interrogation all confessed.

entries.zh: 以其姊寵故，止坐文暢一房。
entries.en: Thanks to his sister’s favor, only Wenchang’s own household was punished.
entries.literal: Because of his sister’s favor, punishment was limited to Wenchang’s household alone.

entries.zh: 弟文略，以兄文羅卒無後，襲梁郡王。
entries.en: Younger brother Wenlüe inherited the Liang Commandery princedom when Wenluo died heirless.
entries.literal: His younger brother Wenlüe, because his elder brother Wenluo died without heirs, inherited the title Prince of Liang Commandery.

entries.zh: 以文暢事，當從坐，高祖特加寬貸。
entries.en: He should have shared Wenchang’s guilt, but Gaozu spared him.
entries.literal: Because of Wenchang’s affair he should have been punished as an associate, but Gaozu specially granted him leniency.

entries.zh: 文略聰明儁爽，多所通習。
entries.en: Wenlüe was brilliant, quick-witted, and accomplished in many arts.
entries.literal: Wenlüe was clever, sharp, and widely accomplished in many arts.

entries.zh: 世宗嘗令章永興於馬上彈胡琵琶，奏十餘曲，試使文略寫之，遂得其八。
entries.en: Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the pipa on horseback through more than ten pieces and asked Wenlüe to write them down; he caught eight.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong once had Zhang Yongxing play the foreign pipa on horseback and perform more than ten pieces; he had Wenlüe transcribe them, and Wenlüe got eight correct.

entries.zh: 世宗戲之曰：「聰明人多不老壽，梁郡其慎之。」
entries.en: The emperor teased him: “Clever men seldom live long—take care, Prince of Liang.”
entries.literal: The emperor jested, “Clever men often do not live long; Prince of Liang, take care.”

entries.zh: 文略對曰：「命之修短，皆在明公。」
entries.en: Wenlüe answered, “Long life or short is entirely for Your Majesty to decide.”
entries.literal: Wenlüe replied, “Whether life is long or short is all in Your Majesty’s hands.”

entries.zh: 世宗愴然曰：「此不足慮也。」
entries.en: The emperor said, moved, “That is nothing to worry about.”
entries.literal: The emperor said sadly, “That is nothing to worry over.”

entries.zh: 初，高祖遺令恕文略十死，恃此益橫，多所淩忽。
entries.en: Gaozu’s will had granted Wenlüe ten stays of execution; emboldened, he grew ever more insolent.
entries.literal: Earlier, Gaozu’s testament had pardoned Wenlüe ten capital offenses; relying on this he grew ever more overbearing and often insulted others.

entries.zh: 平秦王有七百里馬，文略敵以好婢，賭而取之。
entries.en: Prince Pingqin owned a horse said to run seven hundred li in a day; Wenlüe wagered a fine maid against it and won.
entries.literal: The Prince of Pingqin owned a horse worth seven hundred li; Wenlüe matched it against a fine maidservant, gambled, and won it.

entries.zh: 明日，平秦致請，文略殺馬及婢，以二銀器盛婢頭馬肉而遺之。
entries.en: When Pingqin came to claim his stake, Wenlüe slaughtered horse and maid and sent back their flesh and her head in silver dishes.
entries.literal: The next day the Prince of Pingqin came to redeem the stake; Wenlüe killed the horse and the maid and sent him the maid’s head and the horse’s flesh in two silver vessels.

entries.zh: 平秦王訴之於文宣，系於京畿獄。
entries.en: Pingqin appealed to Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was thrown into the metropolitan prison.
entries.literal: The Prince of Pingqin complained to Emperor Wenxuan, and Wenlüe was imprisoned in the capital jail.

entries.zh: 文略彈琵琶，吹橫笛，謠詠，倦極便臥唱挽歌。
entries.en: In prison he played pipa and flute, sang songs, and when tired would lie down and chant dirges.
entries.literal: Wenlüe played pipa and blew the transverse flute, sang ballads, and when weary would lie down and intone dirges.

entries.zh: 居數月，奪防者弓矢以射人曰：「不然，天子不憶我。」
entries.en: After months in custody he seized his guards’ bow and shot at people, crying, “Otherwise the emperor would never think of me.”
entries.literal: After several months he seized his guards’ bow and arrows and shot at people, saying, “Otherwise the Son of Heaven would not remember me.”

entries.zh: 有司奏之，伏法。
entries.en: Officials reported him, and he was put to death.
entries.literal: The authorities reported this, and he was executed.

entries.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為其父作佳傳，收論尒朱榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。
entries.en: Wenlüe once paid Wei Shou heavily to glorify his father in print—hence Shou’s likening of Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang.
entries.literal: Wenlüe once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father; that Wei Shou compared Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was largely for this reason.

entries.zh: 鄭仲禮，滎陽開封人，魏鴻臚嚴庶子也。
entries.en: Zheng Zhongli was from Kaifeng in Xingyang, son of Yan, Wei’s director of ceremonial.
entries.literal: Zheng Zhongli was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang; he was the son of Yan, Director of Ceremonial of Wei.

entries.zh: 少輕險，有膂力，高祖嬖寵其姊，以親戚被昵，擢帳內都督。
entries.en: Young and reckless, strong of body, he rose through Gaozu’s fondness for his sister to a post in the personal guard.
entries.literal: In youth he was reckless and had physical strength; Gaozu favored his elder sister, and as a kinsman he was treated with intimacy and promoted to commander in the personal guard.

entries.zh: 嘗執高祖弓刀，出入隨從。
entries.en: He even bore Gaozu’s bow and sword and attended him everywhere.
entries.literal: He once carried Gaozu’s bow and blade and attended him in and out.

entries.zh: 任胄為好酒不憂公事，高祖責之，胄懼，謀為逆。
entries.en: Ren Zhou drank and neglected duty; rebuked by Gaozu, he turned to treason.
entries.literal: Ren Zhou loved wine and neglected official business; Gaozu reproved him, and in fear Zhou plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 賴武明婁後為請，故仲禮死，不及其家。
entries.en: Empress Wuming Lou pleaded for him, so only Zhongli died and his kin were spared.
entries.literal: Thanks to Empress Wuming Lou’s intercession, Zhongli alone was put to death and his family was not implicated.

entries.zh: 胡長仁，字孝隆，安定臨涇人，武成皇後之兄。
entries.en: Hu Changren, styled Xiaolong, was from Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Wucheng’s Empress Hu.
entries.literal: Hu Changren, courtesy name Xiaolong, was a native of Linjing in Anding and elder brother of Empress Hu of Emperor Wucheng.

entries.zh: 父延之，魏中書令。
entries.en: His father Yanzhi had been Wei’s secretariat director.
entries.literal: His father Yanzhi was Secretariat Director in Wei.

entries.zh: 長仁累遷右樸射及尚書令。
entries.en: Changren rose to right vice director of the Masters of Writing and director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Changren was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，預參朝政，封隴東王。
entries.en: At Shizu’s death he joined in governing and was made prince of Longdong.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu died, he took part in deliberating government and was enfeoffed Prince of Longdong.

entries.zh: 左丞鄒孝裕、郎中陸仁惠、盧元亮厚相結托。
entries.en: Left assistant Zou Xiaoyu and gentlemen Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang attached themselves to him.
entries.literal: Left Assistant Zou Xiaoyu and Gentlemen of the Palace Lu Renhui and Lu Yuanliang formed a close, trusting bond with him.

entries.zh: 長仁每上省，孝裕必方駕而來。
entries.en: Whenever Changren entered the provincial offices, Xiaoyu arrived in a matching carriage.
entries.literal: Whenever Changren went up to the provincial offices, Xiaoyu would certainly come in parallel carriages.

entries.zh: 省務既繁，簿案堆積，令史欲諮都座者日有百數。
entries.en: Paperwork overwhelmed the offices; a hundred clerks a day might seek the chief seat.
entries.literal: Provincial business was already heavy and documents piled up; clerks wishing to consult the chief seat numbered a hundred or more each day.

entries.zh: 孝裕屏人私話，朝退亦相隨，仁惠、元亮又伺間而往，停斷公事，時人號為三佞。
entries.en: Xiaoyu drew him aside for private talk and followed him from court; Renhui and Yuanliang slipped in between sessions and stalled the bureaucracy—contemporaries dubbed them the Three Flatterers.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu would dismiss others for private talk; after court he would follow along as well, and Renhui and Yuanliang would seize intervals to go too, halting public business—people of the time called them the Three Flatterers.

entries.zh: 長仁私遊密席，處處追尋。
entries.en: His secret feasts and private parties were notorious.
entries.literal: Changren’s private feasts and secret gatherings were pursued and tracked everywhere.

entries.zh: 孝裕勸其求進，和士開深疾之，於是奏除孝裕為章武郡守，元亮等皆出。
entries.en: Xiaoyu urged him to climb higher; He Shikai, loathing this, had Xiaoyu sent to Zhangwu and the others posted away.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu urged him to seek advancement; He Shikai deeply hated this, and therefore memorialized to appoint Xiaoyu as Administrator of Zhangwu Commandery and to send Yuanliang and the others out as well.

entries.zh: 孝裕又說長仁曰：「王陽臥疾，士開必來，因而殺之。
entries.en: Xiaoyu told Changren, “Feign illness—when Shikai comes, kill him.
entries.literal: Xiaoyu again said to Changren, “If the prince feigns illness, Shikai will certainly come, and you can kill him then.

entries.zh: 入見太后，不過百日失官，便代其處。」
entries.en: See the empress dowager; within a hundred days you lose your post, then you take his.”
entries.literal: Go in to see the empress dowager; within no more than a hundred days you will lose office, then take his place.”

entries.zh: 士開知謀，徙孝裕為北營州建德郡守。
entries.en: Shikai uncovered the plot and sent Xiaoyu to Jiande in North Ying Province.
entries.literal: Shikai learned of the plot and transferred Xiaoyu to be Administrator of Jiande Commandery in North Ying Province.

entries.zh: 後長仁倚親，驕豪無畏憚。
entries.en: Later, secure in his kinship, Changren grew arrogant and fearless.
entries.literal: Later Changren, relying on his kinship, was arrogant and feared nothing.

entries.zh: 士開出為齊州刺史。
entries.en: Shikai left the capital to be inspector of Qi Province.
entries.literal: Shikai went out to serve as Inspector of Qi Province.

entries.zh: 長仁怨憤，謀令剌士開，事覺，遂賜死。
entries.en: Changren, bitter, plotted assassination; discovered, he was ordered to take his own life.
entries.literal: Changren, resentful and angry, plotted to have Shikai assassinated; the affair was discovered and he was ordered to die.

entries.zh: 尋而後主納長仁女為后，重加贈謚，長仁弟等前後七人並賜王爵，合門貴盛。
entries.en: Soon the Later Lord married Changren’s daughter; honors were heaped on the dead, and seven brothers in all were made princes—the clan blazed with rank.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the Later Lord took Changren’s daughter as empress and richly added posthumous honors; Changren’s younger brothers and others, seven in all before and after, were granted princely titles, and the whole household flourished in glory.

entries.zh: 從祖兄長粲。
entries.en: His elder clan cousin was Changcan.
entries.literal: His elder clan cousin was Changcan.

entries.zh: 父僧敬，即魏孝靜帝之舅，位至司空。
entries.en: His father Sengjing was the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and rose to Minister of Works.
entries.literal: His father Sengjing was the maternal uncle of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei and rose in office to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 長粲少而敏悟，以外戚起家給事中，遷黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Changcan was quick and perceptive in youth. As an imperial in-law, he began his career as palace attendant and was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Changcan was quick and perceptive in youth; as an imperial in-law he began his career as palace attendant and was transferred to gentleman attendant at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 後主踐祚，長粲被勑與黃門馮子琮出入禁中，專典敷奏。
entries.en: When the Later Sovereign ascended, Changcan was ordered, together with Yellow Gate attendant Feng Zicong, to enter and leave the palace precincts and handle the presentation of memorials.
entries.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, Changcan was ordered, together with Yellow Gate attendant Feng Zicong, to enter and leave the forbidden precincts and exclusively manage the presentation of memorials.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，與領軍婁定遠、錄尚書趙彥深、和士開、高文遙、領軍綦連猛、高阿那肱、樸射唐邕同知朝政，時人號為八貴。
entries.en: When Shizu died, he jointly directed court government with Lou Dingyuan, Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, Gao Wenyao, Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and Vice Director Tang Yong. People of the time called them the Eight Nobles.
entries.literal: When Shizu died, he, together with army commander Lou Dingyuan, recorder of the Masters of Writing Zhao Yanshen, He Shikai, Gao Wenyao, army commander Qilian Meng, Gao Anagong, and vice director Tang Yong, jointly directed court government; people of the time called them the Eight Nobles.

entries.zh: 於後定遠、文遙並出，唐邕專典外兵，綦連猛、高阿那肱別總武任，長粲常在左右，兼宣詔令，從幸晉陽。
entries.en: Afterward Dingyuan and Wenyao were sent out, Tang Yong managed the external troops, Qilian Meng and Gao Anagong separately oversaw military duties, and Changcan remained constantly at the sovereign's side, proclaiming edicts and following him to Jinyang.
entries.literal: Afterward Dingyuan and Wenyao were both sent out, Tang Yong exclusively managed the external troops, Qilian Meng and Gao Anagong separately supervised military responsibilities, and Changcan was constantly at the sovereign's side, also proclaiming edicts and orders, and followed the imperial visit to Jinyang.

entries.zh: 後主即位，富於春秋，庶事皆歸委長粲，長粲盡心毗奉，甚得名譽。
entries.en: When the Later Sovereign took the throne, he was still young, so all affairs were entrusted to Changcan. Changcan devoted himself to supporting and serving him and gained a strong reputation.
entries.literal: When the Later Sovereign took the throne, he was young in years, and all affairs were entrusted to Changcan; Changcan devoted his heart to supporting and serving him and gained a great reputation.

entries.zh: 又為侍中。
entries.en: He also became palace attendant.
entries.literal: He also became palace attendant.

entries.zh: 長仁心欲入處機要之地，為執政不許，長仁疑長粲通謀，大以為恨。
entries.en: Changren wanted to enter the key councils, but those in power would not permit it. Suspecting that Changcan had conspired against him, Changren deeply resented him.
entries.literal: Changren wished in his heart to enter a place of vital importance, but those in power did not permit it; Changren suspected that Changcan had conspired in this and deeply resented him.

entries.zh: 遂言於太后，發其陰私，請出為州，後主不得已從焉。
entries.en: He then spoke to the empress dowager, exposed Changcan's private misconduct, and asked that he be sent out to a province; the Later Sovereign had no choice but to agree.
entries.literal: He then spoke to the empress dowager, exposed Changcan's private misconduct, and requested that he be sent out to a province; the Later Sovereign had no choice but to follow this.

entries.zh: 除趙州刺史。
entries.en: Changcan was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou.
entries.literal: Changcan was appointed inspector of Zhaozhou.

entries.zh: 及辭，長粲流涕，後主亦憫默。
entries.en: When Changcan took leave, he wept, and the Later Sovereign too fell silent in pity.
entries.literal: When he took leave, Changcan shed tears, and the Later Sovereign too was silent with pity.

entries.zh: 至州，因沐髮手不得舉，失音，卒。
entries.en: After arriving in the province, he was washing his hair when his hand would no longer lift; he lost his voice and died.
entries.literal: After arriving in the province, while washing his hair his hand could not be raised; he lost his voice and died.

entries.zh: 仁自兩漢以來，外戚之家罕有全者，其傾覆之跡，逆亂之機，皆詳諸前史。
entries.en: Since the Han dynasties, few consort clans have survived unscathed—their falls and the seeds of rebellion are fully recorded in earlier histories.
entries.literal: Since the Two Han dynasties, few households of imperial affines have been preserved intact; the traces of their ruin and the occasions of rebellion and disorder are all set forth in detail in the earlier histories.

entries.zh: 齊氏后妃之族，多自保全，唯胡長仁以譖訴貽禍，斛律光以地勢被戮，俱非女謁盛衰之所致也。
entries.en: Among Northern Qi empresses’ kin, many kept themselves safe; only Hu Changren fell to denunciation, and Hulu Guang was killed for his territorial power—neither owed simply to the waxing and waning of palace women.
entries.literal: Among the clans of Qi consorts and empresses, many preserved themselves; only Hu Changren suffered disaster through slander and accusation, and Hulu Guang was executed because of his territorial power—neither was caused by the rise and fall of women’s influence at court.

entries.zh: 今依前代史官，述《外戚》云爾。
entries.en: Following earlier historians, I here present the account of Imperial Affines.
entries.literal: Now, following the historians of former ages, I set forth the “Imperial Affines” as follows.

entries.zh: 王春，河東人，少好易占，明風角，遊於趙、魏之間，飛符上天。
entries.en: Wang Chun of Hedong loved the Changes in youth, read the winds, wandered Zhao and Wei, and was famed for sending talismans heavenward.
entries.literal: Wang Chun was a native of Hedong; in youth he loved Changes divination, understood wind angles, traveled between Zhao and Wei, and sent talismans flying to Heaven.

entries.zh: 高祖起於信都，引為館客。
entries.en: When Gaozu raised his banner at Xindu, Chun became his house diviner.
entries.literal: When Gaozu rose at Xindu, Chun was brought in as a house guest.

entries.zh: 韓陵之戰，四面受敵，從寅至午，三合三離。
entries.en: At Hanling they were surrounded; from dawn to noon they clashed three times and broke off three times.
entries.literal: At the battle of Hanling they were attacked on all sides; from the yin hour to the wu hour they joined battle three times and broke off three times.

entries.zh: 高祖將退軍，春叩馬諫曰：「比未時，必當大捷。」
entries.en: Gaozu meant to retreat; Chun caught his bridle: “Before mid-afternoon you will win decisively.”
entries.literal: Gaozu was about to withdraw; Chun seized his horse’s bridle and remonstrated, “By the wei hour there will certainly be a great victory.”

entries.zh: 遽縛其子詣王為質，不勝請斬之。
entries.en: He bound his son and offered him as a hostage, asking that the son be beheaded if his prediction proved wrong.
entries.literal: He immediately bound his son and brought him to the prince as a hostage, begging that if he was wrong his son be beheaded.

entries.zh: 俄而賊大敗。
entries.en: Soon the enemy was routed.
entries.literal: Before long the enemy was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 其後每從征討，其言多中，位徐州刺史，卒。
entries.en: On later campaigns his forecasts usually proved right; he became inspector of Xu Province and died in office.
entries.literal: Thereafter on every campaign his words mostly hit true; he rose to Inspector of Xu Province and died.

entries.zh: 綦母懷文，不知何郡人。
entries.en: Qimu Huaiwen’s home commandery was unknown.
entries.literal: Qimu Huaiwen—no one knew from what commandery he came.

entries.zh: 以道術事高祖。
entries.en: He served Gaozu with Daoist arts.
entries.literal: By Daoist arts he served Gaozu.

entries.zh: 武定初，官軍與周文戰於邙山。
entries.en: Early in Wuding the royal army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wuding, the government army fought Zhou Wen at Mount Mang.

entries.zh: 是時官軍旗幟盡赤，西軍盡黑，懷文言於高祖曰：「赤火色，黑水色，水能滅火，不宜以赤對黑。
entries.en: At this time the official army's banners were all red, and the western army's were all black. Huaiwen said to Gao Huan, "Red is the color of fire; black is the color of water. Water can extinguish fire. It is not fitting to set red against black.
entries.literal: At this time the official army's banners were all red, and the western army's were all black. Huaiwen said to Gao Huan, "Red is the color of fire; black is the color of water. Water can extinguish fire. It is not fitting to set red against black.

entries.zh: 土勝水，宜改為黃。」
entries.en: Earth conquers water—use yellow.”
entries.literal: Earth overcomes water; you should change to yellow.”

entries.zh: 高祖遂改為赭黃，所謂河陽幡者。
entries.en: Gaozu switched to ochre yellow—the Heyang banners.
entries.literal: Gaozu therefore changed to ochre yellow—the so-called Heyang banners.

entries.zh: 趙輔和，清都人。
entries.en: Zhao Fuhe was from Qingdu.
entries.literal: Zhao Fuhe was a native of Qingdu.

entries.zh: 少以明《易》善筮為館客。
entries.en: From youth he mastered the Changes and milfoil and served as a house diviner.
entries.literal: In youth, because he understood the Changes and was skilled at milfoil divination, he became a house guest.

entries.zh: 高祖崩於晉陽，葬有日矣，世宗書令顯祖親卜宅兆相於鄴西北漳水北原。
entries.en: After Gaozu died at Jinyang, Shizong ordered Xianzu to choose a tomb on the Zhang’s north bank west of Ye.
entries.literal: Gaozu died at Jinyang; the burial day was set, and Shizong wrote ordering Xianzu personally to divine a tomb site and geomantic aspect on the north bank of the Zhang west of Ye.

entries.zh: 顯祖與吳遵世擇地，頻卜不吉，又至一所，命遵世筮之，遇《革》，遵世等數十人咸云不可用。
entries.en: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi cast repeatedly with ill results; at one site Zunshi drew Ge, and dozens agreed it was unlucky.
entries.literal: Xianzu and Wu Zunshi chose ground; repeated divinations were unlucky. At another place he ordered Zunshi to divine and obtained Ge; Zunshi and several dozen others all said it could not be used.

entries.zh: 輔和少年，在衆人之後，進云：「《革卦》於天下人皆凶，唯王家用之大吉。
entries.en: Young Fuhe spoke last: “Ge bodes ill for commoners, but for a royal house it is excellent.
entries.literal: Fuhe was young and stood behind the crowd; he advanced and said, “The hexagram Ge is ill-omened for all under Heaven, but for a royal house to use it is greatly auspicious.

entries.zh: 《革彖辭》云：『湯武革命，應天順人。』」
entries.en: The Ge judgment says that Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and the people."
entries.literal: The Judgment of Ge says that Tang and Wu changed the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people."

entries.zh: 顯祖遽登車，顧云：「卽以此地為定。」
entries.en: Xianzu mounted at once and said, “This is the place.”
entries.literal: Xianzu immediately mounted his carriage, turned, and said, “Let this place be fixed.”

entries.zh: 卽義平陵也。
entries.en: That became Yiping Tomb.
entries.literal: This was Yiping Tomb.

entries.zh: 有一人父疾，是人詣館別托相知者筮之，遇《泰》，筮者云：「此卦甚吉，疾愈。」
entries.en: When a man’s father fell ill, a friend divined Tai for him and said, "This hexagram is very auspicious; the illness will heal."
entries.literal: A man’s father was ill; the man went to the lodge and had an acquaintance he entrusted elsewhere divine for him; he obtained Tai, and the diviner said, “This hexagram is very auspicious—the illness will heal.”

entries.zh: 是人喜。
entries.en: The man rejoiced.
entries.literal: The man was pleased.

entries.zh: 出後，和謂筮者云：「《泰卦》《乾》下《坤》上，然則入土矣，豈得言吉？」
entries.en: Fuhe told the diviner afterward, “Tai puts Qian under Kun—he goes into the earth; how is that auspicious?”
entries.literal: After he left, Fuhe said to the diviner, “In Tai, Qian is below and Kun above—thus one enters the earth; how can you call it auspicious?”

entries.zh: 果以凶問至。
entries.en: Soon came word of death.
entries.literal: Sure enough news of death arrived.

entries.zh: 和大寧、武平中筮後宮誕男女及時日多中，遂授通直常侍。
entries.en: In Daning and Wuping he divined palace births and dates with great success and was made regular attendant in direct communication.
entries.literal: In the Daning and Wuping eras Fuhe divined for the inner palace on the birth of sons and daughters and the times, and mostly hit true; he was therefore appointed Regular Attendant in Direct Communication.

entries.zh: 信都芳，河間人。
entries.en: Xindu Fang was from Hejian.
entries.literal: Xindu Fang was a native of Hejian.

entries.zh: 少明算術，為州裏所稱。
entries.en: From youth he excelled at mathematics and was praised locally.
entries.literal: In youth he was skilled in calculation and was praised in his district.

entries.zh: 有巧思，每精研究，忘寢與食，或墜坑坎。
entries.en: Ingenious and obsessive, he forgot food and sleep over his work and once fell into a ditch.
entries.literal: He had ingenious thought; whenever he studied closely he forgot sleep and food and sometimes fell into pits and ditches.

entries.zh: 嘗語人云：「算之妙，機巧精微，我每一沈思，不聞雷霆之聲也。」
entries.en: He said, “Calculation is so subtle that when I ponder it I hear no thunder.”
entries.literal: He once told someone, “The subtlety of calculation—its ingenuity and fineness—whenever I ponder deeply I do not hear the sound of thunder.”

entries.zh: 其用心如此。
entries.en: Such was his concentration.
entries.literal: Such was the concentration of his mind.

entries.zh: 以術數干高祖為館客，授參軍丞相倉曹。
entries.en: He offered his arts to Gaozu, became a house guest, and was made staff officer in the chancellor’s granary bureau.
entries.literal: By numerology he sought Gaozu and became a house guest, appointed Staff Officer in the Chancellor’s Granary Bureau.

entries.zh: 祖珽謂芳曰：「律管吹灰，術甚微妙，絕來旣久，吾思所不至，卿試思之。」
entries.en: Zu Ting said, “The pitch-pipe ash test is subtle and long lost—I cannot recover it; try.”
entries.literal: Zu Ting said to Fang, “Blowing ash through pitch-pipes is an extremely subtle art long lost; I cannot think it through—try to work it out.”

entries.zh: 芳遂留意，十數日，便云：「吾得矣，然終須河內葭莩灰。」
entries.en: Fang labored ten days and said, “I have it—but only with reed-ash from Henei.”
entries.literal: Fang then applied himself; in a dozen days he said, “I have it—but in the end we need reed-ash from Henei.”

entries.zh: 後得河內葭莩，用其術，應節便飛，餘灰卽不動也。
entries.en: With Henei reed-ash the ash leapt at each season’s turn; other ash stayed still.
entries.literal: Later they obtained Henei reed-ash; using his method, at the proper season it flew, while other ashes did not move.

entries.zh: 不為時所重，竟不行，故此法遂絕云。
entries.en: The court ignored him, the method was never used, and the art died out.
entries.literal: He was not valued by his time and the method was never put into practice, so the art died out.

entries.zh: 芳又撰次古來渾天、地動、欹器、漏刻諸巧事，並畫圖，名曰《器準》。
entries.en: He compiled ancient devices—armillary spheres, seismoscopes, tipping vessels, clepsydras—illustrated them in Standards of Instruments.
entries.literal: Fang also compiled ancient ingenious devices—the armillary sphere, earthquake indicator, tipping vessel, and clepsydra—illustrated them, and titled the work Standards of Instruments.

entries.zh: 又著《樂書》、《遁甲經》、《四術周髀宗》。
entries.en: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and Four Arts and the Gnomon of the Zhou.
entries.literal: He also wrote Books of Music, the Classic of Hidden Stem, and the Four Arts and Gnomon of the Zhou Tradition.

entries.zh: 芳又私撰歷書，名為《靈憲歷》，算月有頻大頻小，食必以朔，證據甚甄明，每云：「何承天亦為此法，不能精，靈憲若成，必當百代無異議。」
entries.en: His private Spiritual Constitution Calendar tracked the moon’s varying size and fixed eclipses at new moon with rare clarity. “He Chengtian tried this but lacked precision,” he said; “finish this calendar and posterity will not quarrel.”
entries.literal: Fang also privately drafted a calendar called the Spiritual Constitution Calendar, calculating that the moon is sometimes large and sometimes small and that eclipses must fall on new moon; the evidence was very clear. He often said, “He Chengtian also used this method but could not refine it; if the Spiritual Constitution is completed, for a hundred generations there will be no dispute.”

entries.zh: 書未就而卒。
entries.en: He died before the book was finished.
entries.literal: The book was unfinished when he died.

entries.zh: 許遵，高陽人。
entries.en: Xu Zun was from Gaoyang.
entries.literal: Xu Zun was a native of Gaoyang.

entries.zh: 明《易》，善筮，兼曉天文、風角、占相、逆刺，其驗若神。
entries.en: He mastered the Changes and milfoil, astronomy, wind lore, physiognomy, and geomantic needles—with uncanny accuracy.
entries.literal: He understood the Changes, was skilled at milfoil divination, and also knew astronomy, wind angles, physiognomy, and reverse needle techniques; his verification was like a spirit’s.

entries.zh: 高祖引為館客，自言祿命不富貴，不橫死，是以任性疏誕，多所犯忤，高祖常容惜之。
entries.en: Gaozu kept him as house diviner; Zun said his fate held neither riches nor violent death, so he spoke freely and often gave offense, yet Gaozu indulged him.
entries.literal: Gaozu brought him in as a house guest; Zun said himself that his allotted fate was not wealth and nobility and that he would not die a violent death, and therefore he was willful, unrestrained, and often offensive, yet Gaozu always indulged him.

entries.zh: 邙陰之役，遵謂李業興曰：「彼為火陣，我木陣，火勝木，我必敗。」
entries.en: At the Mang’s north bank he told Li Yexing, “Their formation is fire, ours wood—fire defeats wood; we will lose.”
entries.literal: In the campaign on the north bank of the Mang, Zun said to Li Yexing, “They have a fire formation and we a wood formation; fire overcomes wood—we are certain to lose.”

entries.zh: 果如其言。
entries.en: It happened as he said.
entries.literal: It turned out exactly as he said.

entries.zh: 清河王岳以遵為開府田曹記室。
entries.en: Prince Qinghe Yue made him recorder in his field bureau.
entries.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yue appointed Zun recorder in the opening staff’s field bureau.

entries.zh: 岳封王，以告遵，遵曰：「蜜蜂亦作王。」
entries.en: When Yue became a prince, Zun remarked, “Bees make kings too.”
entries.literal: When Yue was enfeoffed prince, he told Zun; Zun said, “Bees also make kings.”

entries.zh: 岳後將救江陵，遵曰：「此行必致後凶，宜辭疾勿去。」
entries.en: When Yue prepared to relieve Jiangling, Zun warned, “This march brings disaster—plead illness and stay.”
entries.literal: Later, when Yue was about to march to relieve Jiangling, Zun said, “This expedition will bring later calamity; you should plead illness and not go.”

entries.zh: 岳曰：「勢不免去，正當與君同行。」
entries.en: Yue said, “I cannot refuse—I ought to take you along.”
entries.literal: Yue said, “I cannot avoid going; I should go with you.”

entries.zh: 遵曰：「好與生人相隨，不欲共死人同路。」
entries.en: Zun said, “I keep company with the living—I will not share a road with the dead.”
entries.literal: Zun said, “I like to keep company with the living and do not wish to travel the same road as the dead.”

entries.zh: 還。
entries.en: He stayed behind.
entries.literal: He returned.

entries.zh: 岳至京尋喪。
entries.en: Yue reached the capital and soon died.
entries.literal: Yue reached the capital and soon died.

entries.zh: 顯祖無道日甚，遵語人曰：「多折算來，吾筮此狂夫何時當死。」
entries.en: As Xianzu grew more lawless, Zun said, “I keep casting when this madman will die.”
entries.literal: As Xianzu’s lawlessness grew daily, Zun told people, “I have calculated repeatedly when this madman will die.”

entries.zh: 遂布算滿床，大言曰：「不出冬初，我乃不見。」
entries.en: He spread rods across his bed and cried, “Before winter I shall not see him.”
entries.literal: He spread counting-rods over the bed and declared loudly, “Before the beginning of winter I shall not see him.”

entries.zh: 顯祖以十月崩，遵果以九月死。
entries.en: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun died in the ninth as he foretold.
entries.literal: Xianzu died in the tenth month; Zun indeed died in the ninth.

entries.zh: 又有荊次德，有術數，預知尒朱榮成敗，又言代魏者齊。
entries.en: Jing Cide, versed in numerology, foretold Erzhu Rong’s fall and declared that Qi would replace Wei.
entries.literal: There was also Jing Cide, skilled in numerology, who foretold the success or failure of Erzhu Rong and also said that Qi would replace Wei.

entries.zh: 葛榮聞之，故自號齊王。
entries.en: Ge Rong heard this and took the title King of Qi.
entries.literal: When Ge Rong heard this, he therefore styled himself King of Qi.

entries.zh: 待次德以殊禮，問其天人之事。
entries.en: Ge Rong honored him and asked about heaven and earth.
entries.literal: He treated Cide with exceptional courtesy and asked him about affairs of Heaven and man.

entries.zh: 對曰：「齊當興，東海出天子，今王據渤海，是齊地。
entries.en: Cide answered, “Qi will rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. You hold Bohai—that is Qi’s ground.
entries.literal: He replied, “Qi is about to rise; a Son of Heaven will come from the Eastern Sea. Your Majesty now holds Bohai—that is Qi territory.

entries.zh: 又太白與月幷，宜速用兵，遲則不吉。」
entries.en: Venus stands with the moon—strike at once; delay is ill-omened.”
entries.literal: Moreover Venus and the moon are together; you should use troops quickly—delay is unlucky.”

entries.zh: 榮不從也。
entries.en: Rong ignored him.
entries.literal: Rong did not follow this.

entries.zh: 吳遵世，字季緒，渤海人，少學《易》，入恒山從隱居道士遊處。
entries.en: Wu Zunshi, styled Jixu, was from Bohai; he studied the Changes in youth and lived with a hermit priest on Mount Heng.
entries.literal: Wu Zunshi, courtesy name Jixu, was a native of Bohai; in youth he studied the Changes and entered Mount Heng to wander with a reclusive Daoist priest.

entries.zh: 數年，忽見一老翁謂之云：「授君開心符。」
entries.en: After years an old man said, “I give you the Heart-Opening Talisman.”
entries.literal: After several years an old man suddenly said to him, “I give you the talisman that opens the heart.”

entries.zh: 遵世跪取吞之，遂明占候。
entries.en: Zunshi knelt, swallowed it, and became a master of divination.
entries.literal: Zunshi knelt, took it, and swallowed it; thereafter he was clear in prognostication.

entries.zh: 後出遊京洛，以《易》筮知名。
entries.en: In the capital he became famed for the Changes.
entries.literal: Later he traveled to the capital region and became famous for Changes divination.

entries.zh: 魏武帝之將卽位也，使遵世筮之，遇《明夷》之《賁》曰：「初登于天，後入于地。」
entries.en: Before Wei Wudi took the throne, Zunshi cast Mingyi changing to Bi: “First he rises to heaven, then he goes into the earth.”
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei was about to ascend the throne, he had Zunshi divine and obtained Mingyi changing to Bi, saying, “First he ascends to Heaven, afterward he enters the earth.”

entries.zh: 帝曰：「何謂也？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, “What does that mean?”
entries.literal: The emperor said, “What does that mean?”

entries.zh: 遵世曰：「初登于天，當作天子。
entries.en: Zunshi said, “Rising to heaven means he becomes Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Zunshi said, “First ascending to Heaven—he will become Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 後入于地，不得久也。」
entries.en: Entering the earth means his reign will not last.”
entries.literal: Entering the earth afterward—he will not long remain.”

entries.zh: 終如其言。
entries.en: It ended exactly as he said.
entries.literal: In the end it was as he said.

entries.zh: 世祖以丞相在京師居守，自致猜疑，甚懷憂懼，謀將起兵，每宿蓍令遵世筮之，遵世云：「不須起動，自有大慶。」
entries.en: Shizu, holding the capital as chief minister, feared suspicion and plotted revolt; nightly he had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “Do not move—great fortune will come unbidden.”
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu as chief minister kept watch in the capital, he brought suspicion on himself and was deeply fearful, planning to raise troops; each night he kept milfoil and had Zunshi divine. Zunshi said, “There is no need to move; great good fortune will come of itself.”

entries.zh: 俄而趙郡王奉太後令以遺詔追世祖。
entries.en: Soon the Prince of Zhao, by the empress dowager’s testament, recalled Shizu.
entries.literal: Before long the Prince of Zhao Commandery, acting on the empress dowager’s order and the testamentary edict, summoned Shizu back.

entries.zh: 及卽祚，授其中書舍人，固辭疾。
entries.en: On his accession he offered Zunshi a secretariat post; Zunshi pleaded illness and refused.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, he offered Zunshi the post of Palace Secretariat Draftsman, but Zunshi firmly pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 魏寧，鉅鹿人。
entries.en: Wei Ning was from Julu.
entries.literal: Wei Ning was a native of Julu.

entries.zh: 以善推祿命征為館客。
entries.en: Summoned as house guest for his skill in fate calculation.
entries.literal: Because he was skilled at calculating allotted fate he was summoned as a house guest.

entries.zh: 武成親試之，皆中。
entries.en: Wucheng tested him personally; he never missed.
entries.literal: Wucheng personally tested him, and all hit true.

entries.zh: 乃以己生年月託為異人而問之，寧曰：「極富貴，今年入墓。」
entries.en: Wucheng disguised his birth date; Ning said, “Supreme fortune—and the tomb this year.”
entries.literal: He then gave his own birth year and month, pretending to be another person and asking; Ning said, “Extremely rich and noble—this year he enters the tomb.”

entries.zh: 武成驚曰：「是我！」
entries.en: Wucheng cried, “That is me!”
entries.literal: Wucheng said in alarm, “That is me!”

entries.zh: 寧變辭曰：「若帝王，自有法。」
entries.en: Ning backtracked: “Emperors follow other rules.”
entries.literal: Ning changed his words and said, “If an emperor and king, he has his own method.”

entries.zh: 又有陽子術，語人曰：「謠言：『盧十六，雉十四，犍子拍頭三十二。』
entries.en: Master Yang cited a rhyme: “Lu sixteen, pheasant fourteen, the colt strikes his head at thirty-two.
entries.literal: There was also Master Yang’s technique; he told people, “A rhyme says: ‘Lu at sixteen, pheasant at fourteen, the colt beats his head at thirty-two.’

entries.zh: 且四八天之大數，太上之祚，恐不過此。」
entries.en: Four eights are heaven’s great number—the Grand Supreme’s reign will not pass it.”
entries.literal: Moreover four times eight is Heaven’s great number; the Grand Supreme’s reign, I fear, will not pass this.”

entries.zh: 旣而武成崩，年三十二也。
entries.en: Wucheng died at thirty-two, as he said.
entries.literal: Before long Wucheng died, aged thirty-two.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：定天下之吉兇，成天下之亹亹，莫善於蓍龜。
entries.en: The Book of Changes says: To discern fortune and ruin for the realm and to sustain its ceaseless work, nothing surpasses divination by milfoil and tortoise.
entries.literal: The Book of Changes says: To settle the auspice and bane of the realm and to accomplish the realm’s tireless striving, nothing is better than milfoil and tortoise.

entries.zh: 是故天生神物，聖人則之。
entries.en: Heaven produces sacred things, and the sage models himself upon them.
entries.literal: Therefore Heaven produces numinous things, and the sage takes them as his model.

entries.zh: 又神農、桐君論《本草》藥性，黃帝、岐伯說病候治方，皆聖人之所重也。
entries.en: Shennong and Lord Tong classified herbs in the Root Canon; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo set forth disease and cure—all arts the sages held dear.
entries.literal: Again, Shennong and Lord Tong discussed the properties of drugs in the Root Canon of Materia Medica; the Yellow Emperor and Qibo explained symptoms and healing prescriptions—all were prized by sages.

entries.zh: 故太史公著《龜策》、《日者》及《扁鵲倉公傳》，皆所以廣其聞見，昭示後昆。
entries.en: Hence Sima Qian’s treatises on tortoise divination, day-selection, and the physicians Bian Que and Lord Cang—all to widen what we know and guide posterity.
entries.literal: Thus Grand Historian Sima Qian wrote the “Treatises on Tortoises and Divination,” “The Day Diviners,” and the “Biographies of Bian Que and Lord Cang”—all to broaden knowledge and show the way to later generations.

entries.zh: 齊氏作霸以來，招引英俊，但有藝能，無不畢策，今並錄之以備《方伎》云。
entries.en: Since Qi began its rise, it has gathered talent; anyone with a craft was pressed into service. They are recorded here for the account of Arts and Techniques.
entries.literal: Since Qi rose to hegemony, it has recruited outstanding men; whoever had any skill was exhaustively enlisted. Now all are recorded here to complete the “Arts and Techniques.”

entries.zh: 甚哉齊末之嬖幸也，蓋書契以降未之有焉。
entries.en: Never in recorded history had a dynasty's closing years seen favorites like those of Qi.
entries.literal: How extreme were the favored minions at the end of Qi! Since the invention of writing, nothing like it had ever existed.

entries.zh: 心利錐刀，居台鼎之任；
entries.en: With hearts as keen as blades for profit, they occupied the highest offices of state;
