entries.literal: Hearts sharp as awls and knives, they held the posts of chief ministers;

entries.zh: 智昏菽麥，當機衡之重。
entries.en: yet with minds too dim to tell beans from wheat, they shouldered the empire's decisive authority.
entries.literal: minds confused about beans and wheat, they bore the weight of the empire's pivot.

entries.zh: 刑殘閹宦、蒼頭盧兒，西域醜胡、龜茲雜伎，封王者接武，開府者比肩。
entries.en: Castrated eunuchs, menial slaves, grotesque Western barbarians, and Kucha acrobats were enfeoffed as kings in succession and granted grand prefectures one beside another.
entries.literal: Mutilated eunuchs, house slaves and lackeys, ugly barbarians from the Western Regions and assorted Kucha performers—those enfeoffed as kings followed one after another, those granted grand prefectures stood shoulder to shoulder.

entries.zh: 非直獨守弄臣，且復多干朝政。
entries.en: They were not only imperial playthings but frequently meddled in government.
entries.literal: They were not merely kept as playthings of the ruler, but also often meddled in court affairs.

entries.zh: 賜予之費，帑藏以虛；
entries.en: Imperial largesse drained the state coffers bare;
entries.literal: The cost of gifts and grants emptied the treasury;

entries.zh: 杼軸之資，剝掠將盡。
entries.en: and the people's last resources were plundered nearly to nothing.
entries.literal: the resources of the loom and spindle were stripped almost clean.

entries.zh: 縱龜鼎之祚，卜世靈長，屬此淫昏，無不亡之理，齊運短促，固其宜哉。
entries.en: Though heaven's mandate might promise long life for a dynasty, under such depravity collapse was inevitable; that Qi's star burned so briefly was only fitting.
entries.literal: Even if the tortoise-and-cauldron mandate promised long-lasting reign, under such licentious folly there was no way the state would not perish—Qi's brief fortune was only what one should expect.

entries.zh: 高祖、世宗，情存庶政，文武任寄，多貞幹之臣，唯郭秀小人，有累明德。
entries.en: Under Gaozu and Shizong, government still had substance and upright men filled military and civil posts—only the petty Guo Xiu tarnished their good name.
entries.literal: Gaozu and Shizong still cared for common governance; in the civil and military posts they employed many upright, resolute ministers—only the petty man Guo Xiu marred their bright virtue.

entries.zh: 天保五年之後，雖罔念作狂，所幸之徒，唯左右驅馳，內外褻狎，其朝廷之事一不與聞。
entries.en: After Tianbao 5, though the emperor abandoned restraint, his favorites were merely runners and intimates who never heard a word of state business.
entries.literal: After the fifth year of Tianbao, though he forgot virtue and ran wild, those he favored were only attendants who raced to his side; intimate inside and out, they heard nothing at all of court affairs.

entries.zh: 大寧之後，姦佞浸繁，盛業鴻基，以之顛覆。
entries.en: After Daning, flatterers multiplied until they toppled the dynasty's great foundation.
entries.literal: After Daning, treacherous flatterers multiplied; the great enterprise and broad foundation were overturned by them.

entries.zh: 生民免夫被發左袵，非不幸也。
entries.en: That the people were spared barbarian subjugation was no calamity.
entries.literal: That the common people were spared the disheveled hair and left lapel—that was no misfortune.

entries.zh: 今緝諸凶族為《佞幸傳》云。
entries.en: I have now compiled their accounts into the Biographies of Favored Minions.
entries.literal: Now I have compiled these wicked clans into the "Biographies of Favored Minions."

entries.zh: 其宦者之徒，尤是亡齊之一物。
entries.en: The eunuchs were especially among the instruments of Qi's ruin.
entries.literal: As for the eunuchs among them, they were especially one cause of Qi's destruction.

entries.zh: 醜聲穢跡，千端萬緒，其事闕而不書，仍略存姓名，附之此《傳》之末。
entries.en: Their vile deeds were too numerous to record in full; I have listed only their names at the end of this biography.
entries.literal: Their foul reputations and filthy deeds were myriad; those affairs are omitted from writing, but names are briefly preserved and appended at the end of this biography.

entries.zh: 其帝家諸奴及胡人樂工，叨竊貴辛，今亦出焉。
entries.en: Imperial slaves and barbarian musicians who usurped high rank are included as well.
entries.literal: The various bondservants of the imperial house and foreign musicians who presumptuously seized noble rank are also included here.

entries.zh: 郭秀，范陽涿人。
entries.en: Guo Xiu was from Zhuo in Fanyang.
entries.literal: Guo Xiu was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.

entries.zh: 事高祖為行臺右丞，親寵日隆，多受賂遺。
entries.en: Serving Gaozu as Right Director of the Mobile Secretariat, he won ever greater personal favor and took bribes freely.
entries.literal: He served Gaozu as Right Director of the Mobile Secretariat; the emperor's personal favor for him grew daily, and he frequently accepted bribes.

entries.zh: 秀遇疾，高祖親臨視之，問所欲官。
entries.en: When Xiu fell ill, Gaozu visited him in person and asked what post he wanted.
entries.literal: When Xiu fell ill, Gaozu personally visited him and asked what office he desired.

entries.zh: 乃啟為七兵尚書，除書未至而卒。
entries.en: He asked to be made Director of the Seven Armies, but died before the appointment reached him.
entries.literal: He requested appointment as Director of the Seven Armies; the commission had not arrived before he died.

entries.zh: 家無成人子弟，高祖自至其宅，親使錄知其家資粟帛多少，然後去。
entries.en: The family had no grown sons; Gaozu went to the house himself, had its grain and silk inventoried, and only then departed.
entries.literal: His household had no adult sons or younger brothers; Gaozu went in person to his residence and had someone record how much grain, silk, and cloth the family possessed, and only then left.

entries.zh: 命其子孝義與太原公已下同學讀書。
entries.en: He had Xiu's son Xiaoyi study alongside the Prince of Taiyuan and his classmates.
entries.literal: He ordered Xiu's son Xiaoyi to study together with the Prince of Taiyuan and those below him.

entries.zh: 初，秀忌楊愔，誑脅令其逃亡。
entries.en: Earlier, Xiu had resented Yang Yin and tricked and intimidated him into fleeing.
entries.literal: Earlier, Xiu resented Yang Yin and deceived and threatened him into fleeing.

entries.zh: 秀死後，愔還，高祖追忿秀，卽日斥孝義，終身不齒。
entries.en: When Yin returned after Xiu's death, Gaozu, still angry at Xiu, that same day expelled Xiaoyi and never admitted him to polite society again.
entries.literal: After Xiu died, Yin returned; Gaozu, reflecting angrily on Xiu, that very day cast out Xiaoyi and for life counted him unworthy of company.

entries.zh: 和士開，字彥通，清都臨漳人也。
entries.en: He Shikai, styled Yantong, was from Linzhang in Qingdu.
entries.literal: He Shikai, courtesy name Yantong, was a native of Linzhang in Qingdu.

entries.zh: 其先西域商胡，本姓素和氏。
entries.en: His forebears were Western Region merchant aliens originally surnamed Suhe.
entries.literal: His ancestors were merchant barbarians from the Western Regions; their original surname was Suhe.

entries.zh: 父安，恭敏善事人，稍遷中書舍人。
entries.en: His father An was deferential, clever, and adept at winning favor, and rose eventually to Palace Secretariat Draftsman.
entries.literal: His father An was respectful, quick-witted, and skilled at pleasing people; he was gradually promoted to Palace Secretariat Draftsman.

entries.zh: 魏孝靜嘗夜中與朝賢講集，命安看斗柄所指，安答曰：「臣不識北斗。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei once met with court worthies at night and asked An to read the Dipper's handle. An answered, "I do not know the Northern Dipper."
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei once gathered with court worthies for discussion at night and ordered An to observe where the Dipper's handle pointed. An replied, "Your servant does not know the Northern Dipper."

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，以為淳直。
entries.en: Gaozu heard of it and took it for plain, honest speech.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard this, he regarded it as simple honesty.

entries.zh: 後為儀州刺史。
entries.en: He later became Inspector of Yizhou.
entries.literal: Later he served as Inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 高阿那肱，善無人也。
entries.en: Gao Anagujin was a native of Shanwu.
entries.literal: Gao Anagujin was a native of Shanwu.

entries.zh: 其父市貴，從高祖起義。
entries.en: His father Shigui had followed Gaozu in the founding uprising.
entries.literal: His father Shigui followed Gaozu in raising the righteous army.

entries.zh: 那肱為庫典，從征討，以功勤擢為武衛將軍。
entries.en: Anagujin began as a storehouse clerk, campaigned with the army, and rose to General of Martial Guards for his service.
entries.literal: Anagujin served as a storehouse clerk; he followed campaigns and, for meritorious exertion, was promoted to General of Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 肱妙於騎射，便僻善事人，每宴射之次，大為世祖所愛重。
entries.en: Expert at mounted archery and winning favor, he was a favorite at Shizu's hunts and banquets.
entries.literal: Anagujin was skilled at mounted archery and adept at pleasing people; at each banquet and archery contest he was greatly loved and esteemed by Shizu.

entries.zh: 又諂悅和士開，尤相褻狎，士開每為之言，彌見親待。
entries.en: He fawned on He Shikai and grew especially close; Shikai's patronage brought him ever greater favor.
entries.literal: He also fawned on He Shikai and was especially intimate with him; Shikai often spoke for him, and he grew all the more personally favored.

entries.zh: 後主卽位，累遷幷省尚書左僕射，封淮陰王，又除幷省尚書令。
entries.en: Under the Later Lord he rose to Left Vice Director and then Director of the Combined Provinces Department of State Affairs and Prince of Huaiyin.
entries.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, Anagujin was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Combined Provinces, enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyin, and then appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Combined Provinces.

entries.zh: 韓寶業、盧勒叉、齊紹，並高祖舊左右，唯門閹驅使，不被恩遇。
entries.en: Han Baoye, Lu Lecha, and Qi Shao had been Gaozu’s gate eunuchs, never favored.
entries.literal: Han Baoye, Lu Lecha, and Qi Shao were all old attendants of Gaozu, mere gate eunuchs for errands, unrewarded with favor.

entries.zh: 歷天保、皇建之朝，亦不至寵幸，但漸有職任。
entries.en: Through Tianbao and Huangjian they gained office but not favor.
entries.literal: Through the Tianbao and Huangjian reigns they still did not reach favor, but gradually gained offices.

entries.zh: 寶業至長秋卿，勒叉等或為中常侍。
entries.en: Baoye became director of the Long Autumn Palace; Lecha and others became palace attendants.
entries.literal: Baoye reached Director of the Long Autumn Palace; Lecha and others sometimes became palace regular attendants.

entries.zh: 世祖時有曹文摽、鄧長顒輩，亦有至儀同食幹者，唯長顒武平中任參宰相，干預朝權。
entries.en: Under Shizu, Cao Wenbiao and Deng Changyang rose high; only Changyang in Wuping shared in governing.
entries.literal: In Shizu’s time there were Cao Wenbiao, Deng Changyang, and others; some even reached provisioners of the same rank as the emperor’s meals; only Changyang in the Wuping era served as associate of the chancellor and meddled in court power.

entries.zh: 後寶業、勒叉、齊紹、子徵並封王，不過侵暴。
entries.en: Later Baoye, Lecha, Shao, and Zizheng were made princes and lived by plunder.
entries.literal: Later Baoye, Lecha, Shao, and Zizheng were all enfeoffed as princes—nothing more than violent oppression.

entries.zh: 於後主之朝，有陳德信等數十人，並肆其姦佞，敗政虐人，古今未有。
entries.en: Under the Later Lord, dozens like Chen Dexin ruined the state as never before.
entries.literal: In the Later Lord’s court dozens like Chen Dexin practiced flattery and wickedness, ruining government and tormenting the people—unprecedented in old or new times.

entries.zh: 多授開府，罕止儀同，亦有加光祿大夫，金章紫綬者。
entries.en: Most became directors of ceremonial parallels; some even grandees with golden seals.
entries.literal: Most were appointed directors of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels; few stopped at ceremonial peers; some were even advanced to Grand Master of Palace Leisure with golden seals and purple cords.

entries.zh: 多帶侍中、中常侍，此二職乃數十人，又皆封王、開府。
entries.en: Dozens held attendant posts—and every one was a prince or director of ceremonial parallels.
entries.literal: Many bore the posts of palace attendant or palace regular attendant—these two offices numbered dozens of men, and all were enfeoffed princes or directors of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels.

entries.zh: 恒出入門禁，往來園苑，趨侍左右，通宵累日。
entries.en: They haunted palace gates and gardens, attending the emperor day and night.
entries.literal: They constantly passed in and out of the palace gates, coming and going in the parks and gardens, hurrying to wait on the emperor’s left and right, all night and day without cease.

entries.zh: 承候顏色，競進諂諛，莫不發言動意，多會深旨。
entries.en: They read his mood and flattered him, almost always hitting his intent.
entries.literal: Receiving his expression, they vied in flattery; none failed to speak and act in ways that mostly matched his deepest intent.

entries.zh: 一戲之賞，動逾巨萬，丘山之積，貪吝無厭。
entries.en: One jest could bring tens of thousands; they hoarded without end.
entries.literal: A reward for one jest exceeded tens of thousands; mountains of wealth—and still they were greedy without end.

entries.zh: 猶以波斯狗為儀同、郡君，分其幹祿。
entries.en: They even ennobled a Persian dog as ceremonial peer and gave it a stipend.
entries.literal: They even made a Persian dog a ceremonial peer and commandery lady, sharing out its stipends.

entries.zh: 神獸門外有朝貴憩息之所，時人號為解卸廳。
entries.en: Outside the Divine Beast Gate was the courtiers’ rest hall, called the Hall of Unburdening.
entries.literal: Outside the Divine Beast Gate was a place where court nobles rested; people of the time called it the Hall of Unburdening.

entries.zh: 諸閹或在內多日，暫放歸休，所乘之馬牽至神獸門階，然後升騎，飛鞭競走，數十為羣，馬塵必坌。
entries.en: Eunuchs released from duty raced their horses from the Divine Beast Gate in dusty packs of dozens.
entries.literal: When eunuchs who had been inside many days were briefly released to rest, the horses they rode were led to the Divine Beast Gate steps; then they mounted, whipped their horses, and raced off in groups of dozens, raising clouds of dust.

entries.zh: 諸朝貴爰至唐、趙、韓、駱皆隱聽趨避，不敢為言。
entries.en: Even great clans hid and gave way, daring not protest.
entries.literal: Court nobles even of the Tang, Zhao, Han, and Luo clans would hide and listen and give way, not daring to speak.

entries.zh: 高祖時有蒼頭陳山提、蓋豐樂、劉桃枝等數十人，俱驅馳便僻，頗蒙恩遇。
entries.en: Gaozu favored dozens of runners like Chen Shanti, Gai Fengle, and Liu Taozhi.
entries.literal: In Gaozu’s time there were dozens of household slaves such as Chen Shanti, Gai Fengle, and Liu Taozhi—all nimble runners and flatterers who received considerable favor.

entries.zh: 天保、大寧之朝，漸以貴盛，至武平時皆以開府、封王，其不及武平者則追贈王爵。
entries.en: By Wuping they were all princes and directors of ceremonial parallels; the dead were posthumously ennobled.
entries.literal: In the Tianbao and Daning reigns they gradually grew exalted; by Wuping all were directors of the Bureau of Ceremonial Parallels and enfeoffed princes; those who did not reach Wuping were posthumously given princely titles.

entries.zh: 士開幼而聰慧，選為國子學生，解悟捷疾，為同業所尚。
entries.en: Shikai was bright from boyhood; chosen for the Imperial Academy, he grasped lessons swiftly and was admired by his peers.
entries.literal: Shikai was clever from childhood; selected as a student of the Imperial Academy, he was quick in comprehension and admired by his fellows.

entries.zh: 天保初，世祖封長廣王，辟士開府行參軍。
entries.en: Early in Tianbao, Shizu was made Prince of Changguang and took Shikai onto his staff as a traveling adjutant.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Shizu was enfeoffed as Prince of Changguang and recruited Shikai as a traveling adjutant in his princely staff.

entries.zh: 世祖性好握槊，士開善於此戲，由是遂有斯舉。
entries.en: Shizu loved polo, and Shikai's skill at the game opened the way to favor.
entries.literal: Shizu loved the game of polo; Shikai excelled at this sport, and from this arose his advancement.

entries.zh: 加以傾巧便僻，又能彈胡琵琶，因此親狎。
entries.en: His sly flattery and skill on the barbarian pipa drew him ever closer to the prince.
entries.literal: Add to this his sycophantic cleverness and deft flattery, and his ability to play the barbarian pipa—by these means he grew intimate with the prince.

entries.zh: 嘗謂王曰：「殿下非天人也，是天帝也。」
entries.en: He once told the prince, "Your Highness is no mortal—you are the Emperor of Heaven."
entries.literal: He once said to the prince, "Your Highness is not a man of Heaven—you are the Emperor of Heaven."

entries.zh: 王曰：「卿非世人也，是世神也。」
entries.en: The prince replied, "You are no ordinary man—you are a spirit of this age."
entries.literal: The prince said, "You are not a man of the world—you are a spirit of the world."

entries.zh: 其深相愛如此。
entries.en: Their mutual affection ran as deep as that.
entries.literal: They loved each other deeply in this fashion.

entries.zh: 顯祖知其輕薄，不令王與小人相親善，責其戲狎過度，徙長城。
entries.en: Xianzu saw his frivolity and forbade the prince such company; rebuking their excessive horseplay, he sent Shikai to the Great Wall.
entries.literal: Xianzu knew how frivolous he was and would not allow the prince to be friendly with such a petty man; rebuking him for excessive playful intimacy, he banished Shikai to the Great Wall garrison.

entries.zh: 後除京畿士曹參軍，長廣王請之也。
entries.en: He was later made Capital Region Personnel Adjutant at the Prince of Changguang's request.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Adjutant of the Capital Region Personnel Office at the Prince of Changguang's request.

entries.zh: 世祖踐祚，累除侍中，加開府。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, Shikai rose step by step to Attendant-in-Ordinary with the rank of Grand Prefect.
entries.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Shikai was repeatedly promoted, finally to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Prefect of the Palace.

entries.zh: 遭母劉氏憂，帝聞而悲惋，遣武衛將軍呂芬詣宅，晝夜扶侍，成服後方還。
entries.en: On mourning for his mother Lady Liu, the emperor grieved and sent General Lü Fen of the Martial Guards to wait on him day and night until the mourning period was complete.
entries.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, Lady Liu, the emperor heard and grieved; he sent General of Martial Guards Lü Fen to his house to attend him day and night, and Fen returned only after the mourning garments were completed.

entries.zh: 其日，帝又遣以犢車迎士開入內，帝見，親自握手，愴惻下泣，曉喻良久，然後遣還，幷諸弟四人並起復本官。
entries.en: That day he sent a calf carriage to bring Shikai inside; taking his hand, the emperor wept and comforted him at length before letting him go, and restored all four of Shikai's brothers to office as well.
entries.literal: That same day the emperor again sent a calf-drawn carriage to bring Shikai into the palace; upon seeing him, the emperor personally took his hand, wept in deep sorrow, and counseled him at length before sending him back—and all four of his younger brothers were also recalled and restored to their former offices.

entries.zh: 其見親重如此。
entries.en: Such was the depth of favor he enjoyed.
entries.literal: Such was the degree of his favor and esteem.

entries.zh: 除右僕射。
entries.en: He was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 帝先患氣疾，因飲酒輒大發動，士開每諫不從。
entries.en: The emperor had a chronic choleric illness that drinking always aggravated; Shikai remonstrated repeatedly, but the emperor refused to heed him.
entries.literal: The emperor had long suffered from a choleric complaint; drinking would always set off severe attacks. Shikai admonished him each time, but the emperor would not listen.

entries.zh: 屬帝氣疾發，又欲飲，士開淚下歔欷不能言。
entries.en: Once, as the illness flared and the emperor reached again for wine, Shikai wept silently and could not speak.
entries.literal: When the emperor's choleric illness flared and he wished to drink again, Shikai wept and sobbed, unable to speak.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿此是不言之諫。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "This is admonition without words."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "This is your admonition without words."

entries.zh: 因不復飲。
entries.en: He put the cup aside and drank no more.
entries.literal: And so he drank no more.

entries.zh: 言辭容止，極諸鄙褻，以夜繼晝，無復君臣之禮。
entries.en: His words and manners sank to the lowest vulgarity; day ran into night with no trace of the rites between ruler and minister.
entries.literal: In speech and bearing he was utterly base and indecent; night followed day without any observance of the rites between ruler and minister.

entries.zh: 至說世祖云：「自古帝王，盡為灰燼，堯、舜、桀、紂，竟復何異？
entries.en: He even told Shizu, "Every emperor since antiquity ends as ashes—what difference between Yao, Shun, Jie, and Zhou?
entries.literal: He even told Shizu, "Emperors from ancient times have all turned to ash—what difference in the end between Yao, Shun, Jie, and Zhou?

entries.zh: 陛下宜及少壯，恣意作樂，縱橫行之，卽是一日快活敵千年。
entries.en: While you are still young, indulge yourself without restraint—a single day of pleasure is worth a thousand years.
entries.literal: Your Majesty should while you are still young indulge in pleasure as you please, roaming at will—a single day's joy equals a thousand years.

entries.zh: 國事分付大臣，何慮不辦，無為自勤苦也。」
entries.en: Leave government to the great ministers; it will be managed. Do not wear yourself out with toil."
entries.literal: Leave state affairs to the great ministers—why worry they will not be handled? Do not torment yourself with labor."

entries.zh: 世祖大悅。
entries.en: Shizu was delighted.
entries.literal: Shizu was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 其年十二月，世祖寢疾於乾壽殿，士開入侍醫藥。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of that year Shizu took to his bed in Qianshou Hall, and Shikai attended him with medicine.
entries.literal: That December Shizu fell ill in Qianshou Hall; Shikai entered to attend him with medicine.

entries.zh: 世祖謂士開有伊、霍之才，殷勤屬以後事，臨崩，握士開之手曰：「勿負我也。」
entries.en: Shizu declared that Shikai had the gifts of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and earnestly entrusted the aftermath to him; dying, he clasped Shikai's hand and said, "Do not betray me."
entries.literal: Shizu said Shikai had the talent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and earnestly entrusted him with affairs after his death; on his deathbed he grasped Shikai's hand and said, "Do not fail me."

entries.zh: 仍絕於士開之手。
entries.en: He breathed his last still holding Shikai's hand.
entries.literal: He then expired with his hand still in Shikai's.

entries.zh: 後主以世祖顧托，深委仗之。
entries.en: The Later Lord, honoring Shizu's deathbed charge, placed deep trust in him.
entries.literal: The Later Lord, because of Shizu's deathbed trust, relied on him deeply.

entries.zh: 又先得幸於胡太后，是以彌見親密。
entries.en: He had already won Empress Dowager Hu's favor, and their intimacy only deepened.
entries.literal: He had also won favor with Empress Dowager Hu earlier, and so grew all the more intimate.

entries.zh: 趙郡王叡與婁定遠等謀出士開，引諸貴人共為計策。
entries.en: Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery, with Lou Dingyuan and others, plotted to oust Shikai and summoned the great nobles to counsel together.
entries.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui, together with Lou Dingyuan and others, plotted to remove Shikai and brought in the various nobles to plan together.

entries.zh: 屬太后觴朝貴於前殿，叡面陳士開罪失，云：「士開先帝弄臣，城狐社鼠，受納貨賄，穢亂宮掖，臣等義無杜口，冒死以陳。」
entries.en: As the empress dowager feasted the nobles in the front hall, Rui openly accused Shikai: "Shikai was the late emperor's favorite, a rat in the city wall—taking bribes and polluting the inner palace. We cannot in conscience stay silent and risk death to speak."
entries.literal: When the empress dowager entertained the court nobles with wine in the front hall, Rui openly stated Shikai's crimes and faults, saying, "Shikai was the late emperor's plaything, a rat nesting under the city wall—accepting bribes and defiling the inner palace. We are bound by duty not to hold our tongues and risk death to speak out."

entries.zh: 太后曰：「先帝在時，王等何不道？
entries.en: The empress dowager said, "When the late emperor lived, why did you not say this?
entries.literal: The empress dowager said, "When the late emperor was alive, why did Your Highnesses not speak?

entries.zh: 今日欲欺孤寡耶！
entries.en: Do you mean to bully a widow and a child today!
entries.literal: Do you wish to deceive a widow and orphan today!

entries.zh: 但飲酒，勿多言。」
entries.en: Drink your wine and say no more."
entries.literal: Just drink—do not say more."

entries.zh: 叡詞色愈厲。
entries.en: Rui's tone and bearing turned fiercer still.
entries.literal: Rui's words and expression grew harsher still.

entries.zh: 或曰：「不出士開，朝野不定。」
entries.en: Someone said, "Unless Shikai goes, court and realm will never be secure."
entries.literal: Someone said, "Unless Shikai is removed, court and country will not be settled."

entries.zh: 叡等或投冠於地，或拂衣而起，言詞咆勃，無所不至。
entries.en: Some threw down their caps, others stormed away; their words grew violent beyond measure.
entries.literal: Rui and the others either flung their caps to the ground or swept their robes and rose; their words were raging and unrestrained.

entries.zh: 明日，叡等共詣雲龍門，令文遙入奏之，太后不聽。
entries.en: The next day they went to the Cloud Dragon Gate and had Wen Yao submit a memorial; the empress dowager refused to hear it.
entries.literal: The next day Rui and the others went together to the Cloud Dragon Gate and had Wen Yao enter to memorialize; the empress dowager would not listen.

entries.zh: 段韶呼胡長粲傳言，太后曰：「梓宮在殯，事大拚速，欲王等更思量。」
entries.en: Duan Shao sent Hu Changcan with a message: the empress dowager said, "The late emperor's coffin is still in mourning—this is no time for rash action. I ask you to think again."
entries.literal: Duan Shao summoned Hu Changcan to convey a message; the empress dowager said, "The imperial coffin still lies in state—the matter is too urgent to be hasty. I wish Your Highnesses to reconsider."

entries.zh: 趙郡王等遂並拜謝，更無餘言。
entries.en: The Prince of Zhao and the rest bowed in apology and said nothing further.
entries.literal: The Prince of Zhao and the others then all bowed in thanks and said nothing more.

entries.zh: 太后及後主召見問士開，士開曰：「先帝群官之中，待臣最重，陛下諒暗始爾，大臣皆有覬覦心，若出臣，正是剪陛下羽翼。
entries.en: The empress dowager and Later Lord questioned Shikai. He said, "Of all the late emperor's officials, none was favored as I was. Your Majesty has only just entered mourning, and the great ministers already eye power hungrily. Remove me, and you clip Your Majesty's own wings.
entries.literal: The empress dowager and Later Lord summoned Shikai and questioned him. Shikai said, "Among all the late emperor's officials, none was treated more generously than I. Your Majesty has only just begun mourning, and the great ministers already harbor covetous designs. If you remove me, you will precisely be clipping the wings of Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 宜謂叡等云：『令士開為州，待過山陵，然後發遣。』
entries.en: Tell Rui and the others: 'Make Shikai a provincial inspector and send him off after the tomb rites.'
entries.literal: You should tell Rui and the others, 'Appoint Shikai to a provincial post; after the imperial burial, then send him away.'

entries.zh: 叡等謂臣真出，必心喜之。」
entries.en: They will think I am truly being sent away and rejoice."
entries.literal: Rui and the others, believing I am truly being sent out, will surely rejoice."

entries.zh: 後主及太后然之，告叡等如士開旨，以士開為兗州刺史。
entries.en: The Later Lord and empress dowager agreed, told Rui and the rest as Shikai advised, and made Shikai Inspector of Yan Province.
entries.literal: The Later Lord and empress dowager agreed and told Rui and the others as Shikai advised, appointing Shikai Inspector of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 山陵畢，叡等促士開就路。
entries.en: After the burial, Rui and the others pressed Shikai to set out for his post.
entries.literal: When the imperial tomb rites were complete, Rui and the others pressed Shikai to take up his post on the road.

entries.zh: 士開載美女珠簾及條諸寶玩以詣定遠，謝曰：「諸貴欲殺士開，蒙王特賜性命，用作方伯。
entries.en: Shikai loaded up women, pearl curtains, and other treasures and went to Dingyuan, saying, "The nobles meant to kill me; thanks to Your Highness sparing my life, I am made a regional governor.
entries.literal: Shikai loaded beautiful women, pearl curtains, and various precious playthings and went to Dingyuan, saying in thanks, "The nobles wished to kill Shikai; thanks to Your Highness's special gift of life, I am made a regional governor.

entries.zh: 今欲奉別，謹具上二女子、一珠簾。」
entries.en: As I take my leave, I respectfully offer two women and a pearl curtain."
entries.literal: Now wishing to take my leave, I respectfully present two women and one pearl curtain."

entries.zh: 定遠喜，謂士開曰：「欲得還入不？」
entries.en: Dingyuan was pleased and asked, "Do you want to go back inside?"
entries.literal: Dingyuan was pleased and said to Shikai, "Do you wish to return inside?"

entries.zh: 士開曰：「在內久，常不自安，令得出，實稱本意，不願更入，但乞王保護，長作大州刺史。
entries.en: Shikai said, "Inside the palace I have long felt unsafe. Going out suits me—I do not wish to return, but only beg Your Highness's protection as inspector of a great province.
entries.literal: Shikai said, "Within the palace I have long felt ill at ease. Now that I may leave, that truly suits my wish—I do not wish to return, but only beg Your Highness's protection that I may long serve as inspector of a great province.

entries.zh: 今日遠出，願得一辭觀二宮。」
entries.en: Before I depart, I ask only to bid farewell at the two palaces."
entries.literal: Setting out far today, I wish only to take leave and visit the two palaces."

entries.zh: 定遠許之。
entries.en: Dingyuan consented.
entries.literal: Dingyuan agreed.

entries.zh: 士開由是得見太后及後主，進說曰：「先帝一旦登遐，臣愧不能自死。
entries.en: Thus Shikai saw the empress dowager and Later Lord and pleaded, "When the late emperor died, I was ashamed that I did not die with him.
entries.literal: By this means Shikai gained audience with the empress dowager and Later Lord and pleaded, "When the late emperor suddenly ascended to the distant realms, I was ashamed that I could not die with him.

entries.zh: 觀朝貴勢欲陛下為幹明。
entries.en: I see the court nobles mean to rule through Your Majesty as a figurehead,
entries.literal: Seeing how the court nobles mean to make Your Majesty their puppet,

entries.zh: 臣出之後，必有大變，復何面見先帝於地下。」
entries.en: and once I am gone there will be grave turmoil—how could I face the late emperor in the grave?"
entries.literal: after I am sent out there will surely be great upheaval—how could I face the late emperor beneath the earth?"

entries.zh: 因慟哭。
entries.en: He burst into tears.
entries.literal: He then broke into anguished weeping.

entries.zh: 帝及太后皆泣，問計將安出。
entries.en: Emperor and empress dowager wept and asked what he would do.
entries.literal: The emperor and empress dowager both wept and asked what plan he proposed.

entries.zh: 士開曰：「臣已得入，復何所慮，正須數行詔書耳。」
entries.en: Shikai said, "Now that I am inside again, what is there to fear? A few lines of edict will suffice."
entries.literal: Shikai said, "Now that I am back inside, what is there to worry about? I need only a few lines of edict."

entries.zh: 於是詔出定遠青州刺史，責趙郡王叡以不臣之罪，召入而殺之。
entries.en: Edicts then sent Dingyuan to Qing Province, charged Prince Rui of Zhao with treason, summoned him in, and executed him.
entries.literal: An edict then sent Dingyuan out as Inspector of Qing Province, charged Prince of Zhao Rui with the crime of disloyalty, summoned him in, and killed him.

entries.zh: 復除士開侍中、右僕射。
entries.en: Shikai was restored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: Shikai was again appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 定遠歸士開所遺，加以餘珍賂之。
entries.en: Dingyuan returned Shikai's gifts and added more treasures to buy him off.
entries.literal: Dingyuan returned what Shikai had given him and added further precious gifts to bribe him.

entries.zh: 武平元年，封淮陽王，除尚書令、錄尚書事，復本官悉得如故。
entries.en: In Wuping 1 he was made Prince of Huaiyang, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Chief Recorder, with all former offices restored.
entries.literal: In Wuping 1 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang, appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs and Chief Recorder of the Department of State Affairs; all his former offices were restored as before.

entries.zh: 世祖時，恒令士開與太后握槊，又出入臥內無復期限，遂與太后為亂。
entries.en: Under Shizu, Shikai often played polo with the empress dowager and entered the inner quarters without restraint, eventually taking her as a lover.
entries.literal: During Shizu's reign, Shikai was regularly made to play polo with the empress dowager; he also came and went in the sleeping quarters without limit, and eventually had an illicit affair with the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 及世祖崩後，彌自放恣。
entries.en: After Shizu's death he abandoned all restraint.
entries.literal: After Shizu's death he grew ever more unrestrained.

entries.zh: 瑯邪王儼惡之，與領軍庫狄伏連、侍中馮子琮、禦史王子宜、武衛高舍洛等謀誅之。
entries.en: Prince Yan of Langye hated him and, with Army Director Kudie Fulian, Attendant Feng Zicong, Censor Wang Ziyi, Martial Guard Gao Shelou, and others, plotted his death.
entries.literal: Prince of Langye Yan hated him and, with Army Director Kudie Fulian, Attendant-in-Ordinary Feng Zicong, Censor Wang Ziyi, and Martial Guard Gao Shelou and others, plotted to kill him.

entries.zh: 伏連發京畿軍士，帖神武、千秋門外，並私約束，不聽士開入殿。
entries.en: Fulian deployed capital troops outside the Shenwu and Qianqiu gates with secret orders to keep Shikai from the hall.
entries.literal: Fulian mobilized capital-region troops and posted them outside the Shenwu and Qianqiu gates, with private orders not to let Shikai enter the hall.

entries.zh: 其年七月二十五日旦，士開依式早參，伏連前把士開手曰：「今有一大好事。」
entries.en: On the morning of the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month, Shikai came for the regular audience; Fulian seized his hand and said, "Today brings great good fortune."
entries.literal: On the morning of the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month that year, Shikai came for the regular early audience; Fulian stepped forward and took Shikai's hand, saying, "Today there is a great piece of good news."

entries.zh: 王子宜便授一函，云：「有勑令王向臺。」
entries.en: Wang Ziyi handed him a sealed message: "There is an edict summoning the prince to the tribunal."
entries.literal: Wang Ziyi at once handed him a packet, saying, "There is an edict ordering the prince to go to the tribunal."

entries.zh: 遣兵士防送，禁於治書侍御廳事。
entries.en: Soldiers escorted and detained him in the Supervising Censor's hall.
entries.literal: Soldiers were sent to escort and guard him, confining him in the hall of the Supervising Censor.

entries.zh: 儼遣都督馮永洛就臺斬之，時年四十八，簿錄其家口。
entries.en: Yan sent Commander Feng Yongluo to behead him at the tribunal; he was forty-eight, and his household was registered and seized.
entries.literal: Yan sent Commander Feng Yongluo to the tribunal to behead him; he was forty-eight years old, and his household register was seized for inventory.

entries.zh: 後誅儼等。
entries.en: Later Yan and his accomplices were put to death.
entries.literal: Later Yan and the others were executed.

entries.zh: 上哀悼，不視事數日，追憶不已。
entries.en: The emperor grieved for days without holding court, unable to put Shikai from his mind.
entries.literal: The emperor mourned, did not attend to affairs for several days, and could not cease remembering him.

entries.zh: 詔起復其子道盛為常侍，又勑其弟士休入內省參典機密，詔贈士開假黃鉞、十州諸軍事、左丞相、太宰如故。
entries.en: Edicts recalled Shikai's son Daosheng as Attendant-in-Ordinary, brought his brother Shi Xiu into the inner palace for state secrets, and posthumously invested Shikai with the yellow axe, ten-province military command, Left Chancellor, and Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: An edict recalled his son Daosheng from mourning as Attendant-in-Ordinary, ordered his brother Shi Xiu to enter the inner palace to participate in confidential affairs, and posthumously granted Shikai the yellow axe, command over ten provinces' military affairs, Left Chancellor, and Grand Preceptor as before.

entries.zh: 肱才伎庸劣，不涉文史，識用尤在士開之下，而姦巧計數亦不逮士開。
entries.en: Mediocre in talent and ignorant of letters, he was duller and less cunning even than Shikai.
entries.literal: Anagujin's talent and skill were mediocre and inferior; he did not touch literary or historical learning, and his discernment and ability were especially below Shikai's, while his cunning calculation also fell short of Shikai's.

entries.zh: 旣為世祖所幸，多令在東宮侍後主，所以大被寵遇。
entries.en: Shizu had favored him and kept him in the Eastern Palace with the young heir, which won him lasting preferment.
entries.literal: Because he had been favored by Shizu, he was often kept in the Eastern Palace attending the Later Lord, and for this reason was greatly favored.

entries.zh: 士開死後，後主謂其識度足繼士開，遂致位宰輔。
entries.en: After Shikai's death the Later Lord thought him Shikai's equal and made him chief minister.
entries.literal: After Shikai died, the Later Lord considered his discernment sufficient to succeed Shikai, and so raised him to chief minister.

entries.zh: 武平四年，令其錄尚書事，又總知外兵及內省機密。
entries.en: In Wuping 4 he became Chief Recorder, commanding external armies and inner-palace secrets.
entries.literal: In Wuping 4 he was ordered to serve as Chief Recorder of the Department of State Affairs and also to oversee external military affairs and inner-palace secrets.

entries.zh: 尚書郎中源師嘗諮肱云：「龍見，當雩。」
entries.en: Yuan Shi of the Department of State Affairs told Anagujin, "A dragon has appeared—we must perform a rain sacrifice."
entries.literal: Director of the Department of State Affairs Yuan Shi once consulted Anagujin, saying, "A dragon has appeared—we should perform a rain sacrifice."

entries.zh: 問師云：「何處龍見？
entries.en: Anagujin asked, "Where was it seen?
entries.literal: Anagujin asked, "Where did the dragon appear?

entries.zh: 作何物顏色？」
entries.en: What color was it?"
entries.literal: What did it look like?"

entries.zh: 師云：「此是龍星見，須雩祭，非是真龍見。」
entries.en: Shi said, "It is the dragon star, not a real dragon—we need a rain rite, not a dragon hunt."
entries.literal: Shi said, "This is the dragon star appearing—we must perform the rain sacrifice; it is not a real dragon appearing."

entries.zh: 肱云：「漢兒強知星宿！」
entries.en: Anagujin snapped, "Han dogs playing astronomer!"
entries.literal: Anagujin said, "These Han dogs pretend to know the stars!"

entries.zh: 其墻面如此。
entries.en: Such was his brazen ignorance.
entries.literal: His shamelessness was like this.

entries.zh: 又為右丞相，餘如故。
entries.en: He was also made Right Chancellor; his other posts remained unchanged.
entries.literal: He was also made Right Chancellor; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 韓鳳，字長鸞，昌黎人也。
entries.en: Han Feng, styled Changluan, was from Changli.
entries.literal: Han Feng, courtesy name Changluan, was a native of Changli.

entries.zh: 父永興，青州刺史。
entries.en: His father Yongxing had been Inspector of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: His father Yongxing was Inspector of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 鳳少而聰察，有膂力，善騎射。
entries.en: From youth Feng was sharp-eyed and strong, skilled at mounted archery.
entries.literal: Feng from youth was perceptive and keen, had physical strength, and was skilled at mounted archery.

entries.zh: 稍遷都督。
entries.en: He rose gradually to Area Commander.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Area Commander.

entries.zh: 後主居東宮，年幼稚，世祖簡都督二十人送令侍衛，鳳在其數。
entries.en: While the young Later Lord lived in the Eastern Palace, Shizu chose twenty area commanders to guard him; Feng was one.
entries.literal: When the Later Lord lived in the Eastern Palace and was still young, Shizu selected twenty area commanders and sent them to attend and guard him; Feng was among them.

entries.zh: 後主親就衆中牽鳳手曰：「都督看兒來。」
entries.en: The prince went among them, took Feng's hand, and said, "Commander, look after my boy."
entries.literal: The Later Lord personally went among the crowd, took Feng's hand, and said, "Area Commander, look at my boy."

entries.zh: 因此被識，數喚共戲。
entries.en: Feng was remembered and often called to play with him.
entries.literal: From this he came to be recognized and was repeatedly summoned to play together.

entries.zh: 後主走度太行，令那肱以數千人投濟州關，仍遣覘候。
entries.en: Crossing the Taihang, the Later Lord sent Anagujin with several thousand men to Jizhou Pass and ordered scouts ahead.
entries.literal: The Later Lord fled over the Taihang Mountains and ordered Anagujin to take several thousand men to Jizhou Pass, still sending scouts ahead.

entries.zh: 每奏：「周軍未至，且在青州集兵，未須南行。」
entries.en: Each report said, "Zhou troops are not yet here—raise men at Qingzhou; no need to flee south yet."
entries.literal: Each report said, "Zhou troops have not yet arrived; gather troops at Qingzhou first—there is no need to go south yet."

entries.zh: 及周將軍尉遲迥至關，肱遂降。
entries.en: When Zhou General Yuchi Jiong reached the pass, Anagujin surrendered.
entries.literal: When Zhou General Yuchi Jiong reached the pass, Anagujin surrendered.

entries.zh: 時人皆云肱表款周武，必仰生致齊主，故不速報兵至，使後主被擒。
entries.en: Contemporaries said Anagujin had pledged to Zhou and delayed reporting the enemy so the Qi ruler could be taken alive.
entries.literal: People of the time all said Anagujin had pledged himself to Emperor Wu of Zhou and surely hoped to deliver the Qi ruler alive, and so did not quickly report the enemy's arrival, causing the Later Lord to be captured.

entries.zh: 肱至長安，授大將軍，封郡公，為隆州刺史，誅。
entries.en: In Chang'an he was made Grand General and a commandery duke, then Governor of Longzhou—and executed.
entries.literal: Anagujin reached Chang'an, was appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery, made Governor of Longzhou, and was executed.

entries.zh: 初，天保中，顯祖自晉陽還鄴，陽愚僧阿禿師於路中大叫，呼顯祖姓名云：「阿那瓌終破你國。」
entries.en: In Tianbao, as Xianzu returned from Jinyang to Ye, the monk Atuo of Yangyu shouted his name on the road: "Anagujin will destroy your state."
entries.literal: Earlier, in Tianbao, Xianzu was returning from Jinyang to Ye when the monk Atuo of Yangyu shouted along the road, calling Xianzu by name and saying, "Anagujin will in the end destroy your state."

entries.zh: 是時茹茹主阿那瑰在塞北強盛，顯祖尤忌之，所以每歲討擊，後亡齊者遂屬阿那肱云。
entries.en: The Rouran ruler Anagujin then dominated the northern frontier and Xianzu feared him; years later Qi's destroyer proved to be Gao Anagujin.
entries.literal: At that time the Rouran ruler Anagujin was powerful north of the frontier and Xianzu especially feared him, and so every year launched punitive campaigns; later the destroyer of Qi turned out to be Anagujin, it is said.

entries.zh: 雖作「肱」字，世人皆稱為「瓌」音，斯固「亡秦者胡」，蓋懸定於窈冥也。
entries.en: Though written with the character for "gujin," all pronounced it like "gui"—as if fate had already whispered, "He who destroys Qin is the Hu."
entries.literal: Though the character is written "gujin," everyone pronounced it like "gui"; this is indeed like "the one who will destroy Qin is the Hu"—fixed in the dark beyond.

entries.zh: 郭秀 和士開 穆提婆 高阿那肱 韓鳳 韓寶業等
entries.en: Guo Xiu, He Shikai, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagujin, Han Feng, Han Baoye, and the like
entries.literal: Guo Xiu, He Shikai, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagujin, Han Feng, Han Baoye, and others

entries.zh: 文帝諱沙漠汗，以國太子留洛陽。
entries.en: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, stayed in Luoyang as hostage heir.
entries.literal: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, remained in Luoyang as the state's heir.

entries.zh: 後文帝以神元春秋已高，求歸。
entries.en: Later, seeing Shenyuan's great age, Shamohan asked leave to go home.
entries.literal: Later Wen Emperor, because Shenyuan's years were already advanced, requested to return.

entries.zh: 晉武帝具禮護送。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Jin honored him with full ceremony and sent him homeward under escort.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin treated him with full rites and escorted him on his way.

entries.zh: 五十六年，文帝復如晉，其冬還國。
entries.en: In the fifty-sixth year he visited Jin again and came back that winter.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Wen Emperor again went to Jin; that winter he returned to his state.

entries.zh: 晉征北將軍衛瓘以文帝雄異，恐為後患，請留不遣。
entries.en: Jin's north-pacifying general Wei Guan, fearing Shamohan's formidable talent, asked that he be kept and not released.
entries.literal: Wei Guan, General Who Subdues the North of Jin, because Wen Emperor was formidable and strange, feared he would be a later trouble and requested that he be detained and not sent back.

entries.zh: 復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙。
entries.en: He also proposed bribing the tribal great men with gold and brocade to set them at odds with one another.
entries.literal: He again requested that gold and brocade be used to bribe the great men of the state so as to sow divisions among them.

entries.zh: 五十八年方遣帝。
entries.en: Not until the fifty-eighth year was the heir allowed to depart.
entries.literal: Only in the fifty-eighth year was the Emperor sent off.

entries.zh: 神元使諸部大人詣陰館迎帝。
entries.en: Shenyuan ordered the tribal chiefs to Yinyuan to welcome the heir home.
entries.literal: Shenyuan had the great men of the tribes go to Yinyuan to welcome the Emperor.

entries.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，飛丸落之。
entries.en: Wine deep in the cup, the heir glanced up at a bird in flight and dropped it with a pellet.
entries.literal: As the wine went deep, the Emperor looked up at a flying bird and brought it down with a pellet.

entries.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾大驚，相謂曰：「太子被服同南夏，兼奇術絕人。
entries.en: The people knew no slingshot; everyone was shaken and murmured, "The heir wears southern dress and commands arts no one here can match.
entries.literal: At the time the nation's custom knew no slings; all were greatly alarmed and said to one another, "The heir dresses like the southern Xia and possesses wondrous arts beyond any man.

entries.zh: 若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志。」
entries.en: If he inherits the realm and changes our customs, we will never prosper again."
entries.literal: If he inherits the state and alters our old ways, we shall never have our will."

entries.zh: 乃謀危害帝，並先馳還，曰：「太子引空弓而落飛鳥，似得晉人異法。」
entries.en: They plotted against him and rode ahead with a story: "The heir shot an empty bow and felled a bird in flight, as if he had learned some Jin sorcery."
entries.literal: Thereupon they plotted to harm the Emperor, and first galloped back, saying, "The heir drew an empty bow yet brought down a flying bird, as though he had obtained some strange method of the Jin people."

entries.zh: 自帝在晉後，諸子愛寵，神元頗有所惑。
entries.en: During Shamohan's long stay in Jin, his younger brothers won favor, and Shenyuan grew uncertain.
entries.literal: After the Emperor had been in Jin, the other sons were favored and cherished, and Shenyuan was much perplexed.

entries.zh: 及聞諸大人請，因曰：「當便除之。」
entries.en: When the elders pressed their case, he said, "Then let him be killed at once."
entries.literal: On hearing the great men's request, he therefore said, "He should be removed at once."

entries.zh: 於是諸大人馳詣塞南，矯害帝。
entries.en: The great men raced south of the frontier passes and murdered the heir under a forged order.
entries.literal: Thereupon the great men galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the Emperor.

entries.zh: 其年，神元不豫。
entries.en: That same year Shenyuan fell ill.
entries.literal: In that year Shenyuan was unwell.

entries.zh: 烏丸王庫賢親近任勢。
entries.en: Kuxian, a Wuhuan king, stood close to the throne and held real power.
entries.literal: Kuxian, king of the Wuhuan, was close at hand and wielded power.

entries.zh: 先受衛瓘之貨，欲沮動諸部，因於庭中礪鉞斧，曰：「上恨汝曹讒殺太子，欲盡收諸大人長子殺之。」
entries.en: Having taken Wei Guan's bribes, he meant to panic the tribes; in the courtyard he sharpened axe and blade, crying, "The High One blames you for the heir's murder and will seize every chief's eldest son and kill him."
entries.literal: He had earlier accepted bribes from Wei Guan and wished to stir up the various tribes; therefore in the courtyard he sharpened axe and hatchet, saying, "The High One resents you all for slandering and killing the heir; he intends to seize every great man's eldest sons and put them to death."

entries.zh: 大人皆信，各各散走。
entries.en: The chiefs believed him and fled in every direction.
entries.literal: The great men all believed it; each scattered and fled.

entries.zh: 神元尋崩，凡饗國五十八年，年一百四歲。
entries.en: Shenyuan died soon after, having ruled fifty-eight years and lived to one hundred and four.
entries.literal: Shenyuan soon died; in all he had ruled the state fifty-eight years, and his years reached one hundred and four.

entries.zh: 道武即位，尊為始祖。
entries.en: When Daowu came to power he enshrined Shenyuan as the dynastic Progenitor.
entries.literal: When Daowu took the throne he honored him as Progenitor.

entries.zh: 子章皇帝悉鹿立，時諸部離叛。
entries.en: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded while the tribes were splintering away.
entries.literal: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded; at the time the tribes were breaking away.

entries.zh: 帝九年而崩。
entries.en: Silu reigned nine years and died.
entries.literal: The Emperor died in the ninth year.

entries.zh: 弟平皇帝綽立，七年而崩。
entries.en: His brother Ping Emperor Chuo ruled seven years and died.
entries.literal: His younger brother Ping Emperor Chuo succeeded; in seven years he died.

entries.zh: 文帝少子思皇帝立，思皇帝諱弗。
entries.en: Wen Emperor's youngest son, Si Emperor, came next; Si Emperor's taboo name was Fu.
entries.literal: The youngest son of Wen Emperor, Si Emperor, succeeded; Si Emperor, taboo name Fu.

entries.zh: 政崇寬簡，百姓懷服。
entries.en: He governed with leniency and ease, and the people gave him their hearts.
entries.literal: His government honored leniency and simplicity; the common people were attached and submitted.

entries.zh: 一年而崩。
entries.en: He died after a single year.
entries.literal: In one year he died.

entries.zh: 神元子昭帝祿官立。
entries.en: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan took the throne.
entries.literal: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan succeeded.

entries.zh: 帝元年，分國為三部：一居上穀北，濡源西，東接宇文部，自統之；
entries.en: In his first year Luguan split the realm in three: one branch lived north of Shanggu and west of Ruyuan, adjoining the Yuwen, under his own hand;
entries.literal: In the first year of the Emperor he divided the state into three parts: one group dwelt north of Shanggu, west of Ruyuan, bordering the Yuwen tribe, and he ruled them himself;

entries.zh: 一居代郡之參合陂北，使文帝長子桓帝諱猗厓統之；
entries.en: one camped north of Canhe Marsh in Dai commandery, ruled by Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu;
entries.literal: one dwelt north of Canhebo in Dai commandery, and he had Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu, rule them;

entries.zh: 一居定襄之盛樂故城，使桓帝弟穆帝猗盧統之。
entries.en: one occupied old Shengle in Dingxiang, ruled by Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu.
entries.literal: one dwelt at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang, and he had Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu rule them.

entries.zh: 三年，晉并州刺史劉琨遣子遵為質，乞師。
entries.en: In the third year Liu Kun of Bing province sent his son Zun as hostage and asked for military aid.
entries.literal: In the third year Liu Kun, Jin inspector of Bing province, sent his son Zun as hostage and begged for troops.

entries.zh: 帝使弟子平文皇帝助琨，破白部大人，次攻鐵弗劉武。
entries.en: The Emperor sent his nephew Pingwen Emperor to help Kun, routed the White Tribe chief, then marched against the Iron-Fu leader Liu Wu.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent his younger brother's son, Emperor Pingwen, to aid Kun, defeated the White Tribe great chief, and next attacked the Iron-Fu Liu Wu.

entries.zh: 晉懷帝進帝大單于，封代公。
entries.en: Jin's Emperor Huai promoted him to Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.
entries.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin advanced the Emperor to Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.

entries.zh: 帝以封邑去國縣遠，從琨求句注陘北地。
entries.en: His grant lay too far from the heartland, so he asked Kun for territory north of Gouzhu Pass.
entries.literal: Because his fief lay far from the state capital, the Emperor asked Kun for the lands north of Gouzhu Pass.

entries.zh: 琨大喜，乃徙馬邑、陰館、樓煩、繁畤、崞五縣人于陘南，更立城邑，盡獻其地。
entries.en: Kun gladly moved the populations of Mayi, Yinyuan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and ceded the vacated lands in full.
entries.literal: Kun was greatly pleased and therefore moved the people of Mayi, Yinyuan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo five commanderies south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and presented all the land.

entries.zh: 東接代郡，西連西河、朔方數百百。
entries.en: It reached east to Dai commandery and west through Xihe and Shuofang for several hundred li.
entries.literal: To the east it adjoined Dai commandery; to the west it linked with Xihe and Shuofang for several hundred li.

entries.zh: 帝乃徙十萬家以充之。
entries.en: He then settled a hundred thousand households there to people the land.
entries.literal: The Emperor then moved a hundred thousand households to fill it.

entries.zh: 平文皇帝諱郁律，姿質雄壯，甚有威略。
entries.en: Pingwen Emperor, taboo name Yulü, was powerfully built and commanded awe through force and guile.
entries.literal: Emperor Pingwen, taboo name Yulü, was of heroic and stalwart bearing and possessed great authority and strategy.

entries.zh: 元年，歲在丁丑。
entries.en: His first year was a dingchou year.
entries.literal: In the first year the year was dingchou.

entries.zh: 二年，劉武據朔方，來侵西部，帝大破之。
entries.en: In the second year Liu Wu, entrenched in Shuofang, invaded the west and was shattered.
entries.literal: In the second year Liu Wu held Shuofang, came to invade the western lands, and the Emperor routed him utterly.

entries.zh: 西兼烏孫故地，東吞勿吉以西，控弦上馬將百萬。
entries.en: He seized the old Wusun country in the west and swallowed everything west of the Wuji in the east; a million warriors stood ready at bow and saddle.
entries.literal: To the west he annexed the old lands of the Wusun; to the east he swallowed all west of the Wuji; bowmen and mounted warriors numbered a million.

entries.zh: 桓帝中子惠帝賀傉立，以五年為元年。
entries.en: Huan Emperor's second son Hui Emperor Helu took the throne, dating his reign from the fifth year.
entries.literal: Huan Emperor's second son, Emperor Hui Helu, succeeded and took the fifth year as his first.

entries.zh: 帝未親政事，太后臨朝。
entries.en: The young king did not yet rule; the empress dowager governed.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not yet handle government in person; the empress dowager held court.

entries.zh: 遣使與石勒通和，時人謂之女國使。
entries.en: She sent envoys to Shi Le, whom contemporaries nicknamed the ambassadors of the women's court.
entries.literal: She sent envoys to open relations with Shi Le, and people of the time called them the envoys of the women's state.

entries.zh: 四年，帝始臨朝，以諸部人情未悉款順，乃築城於東木根山，徙都之。
entries.en: In the fourth year he took the throne in person; doubting tribal loyalty, he built a fortress on East Mugen Mountain and moved the seat of rule there.
entries.literal: In the fourth year the Emperor first held court in person; because the hearts of the various tribes were not yet fully loyal, he walled a city on East Mugen Mountain and moved the capital there.

entries.zh: 五年，帝崩。
entries.en: He died in the fifth year.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor died.

entries.zh: 四年，築盛樂城于故城南八里。
entries.en: In the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old walls.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old city.

entries.zh: 皇后慕容氏崩。
entries.en: Empress Murong died.
entries.literal: Empress Murong died.

entries.zh: 十月，劉武寇西境，帝遣軍大破之。
entries.en: In the tenth month Liu Wu struck the western frontier; the Emperor's army crushed him.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Liu Wu raided the western border; the Emperor sent troops and routed him utterly.

entries.zh: 武死，子務桓立，始來歸順，帝以女妻之。
entries.en: Wu died and his son Wuhuan submitted; the Emperor gave him a princess in marriage.
entries.literal: Wu died; his son Wuhuan succeeded and first came to submit; the Emperor gave him a daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 十九年正月，劉務桓死，其弟閼頭立，潛謀反。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year's first month Liu Wuhuan died; his brother Kentou took power and plotted treason in secret.
entries.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year Liu Wuhuan died; his younger brother Kentou succeeded and secretly plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 二年春正月壬戌，帝引騎圍信都。
entries.en: On renxu day in the first month of the second year the Emperor led cavalry to besiege Xindu.
entries.literal: On day renxu in the first month of spring in the second year the Emperor led cavalry to besiege Xindu.

entries.zh: 其夜，寶冀州刺史、宜都王慕容鳳逾城奔中山。
entries.en: That night Murong Feng, Bao's governor of Jizhou and Prince of Yidu, climbed the wall and fled to Zhongshan.
entries.literal: That night Bao's Governor of Jizhou and Prince of Yidu, Murong Feng, climbed over the wall and fled to Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 癸亥，寶輔國將軍張驤、護軍將軍徐超舉城降。
entries.en: On guihai day Zhang Yang, Bao's Supporting-the-State General, and Xu Chao the Protecting-the-Army General surrendered the city.
entries.literal: On day guihai Bao's Supporting-the-State General Zhang Yang and Protecting-the-Army General Xu Chao surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 是月，鮮卑禿發烏孤私署大單于、西平王。
entries.en: That month the Xianbei chief Tufa Wuji took the titles Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.
entries.literal: That month the Xianbei Tufa Wuji privately styled himself Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.

entries.zh: 二月丁丑，帝軍于钜鹿之柏肆塢，臨滹沱水。
entries.en: On dingchou day in the second month the Emperor camped at Bozhi Hill in Julu, on the Hutuo River.
entries.literal: On day dingchou in the second month the Emperor encamped at Bozhi Hill in Julu, on the Hutuo River.

entries.zh: 其夜，寶悉眾犯營，燎及行宮，兵人駭散。
entries.en: That night Bao threw his whole army against the camp; flames reached the traveling palace and the troops broke in terror.
entries.literal: That night Bao mustered all his forces and struck the camp; fire reached the traveling palace and soldiers and men scattered in panic.

entries.zh: 帝驚起，不及衣冠，跣出擊鼓。
entries.en: The Emperor leapt up, seized neither robe nor cap, and ran out barefoot to beat the alarm drum.
entries.literal: The Emperor started up in alarm, had no time for robe or cap, and ran out barefoot to beat the drum.

entries.zh: 俄而，左右及中軍將士稍集。
entries.en: Soon his guards and the central army began to rally.
entries.literal: Before long the guards at hand and the central army officers and soldiers gradually gathered.

entries.zh: 帝設奇陣，列烽營外，縱騎沖之。
entries.en: He laid an ambush, set beacon fires beyond the camp, and sent cavalry to charge.
entries.literal: The Emperor set an ambush formation, lined beacon fires outside the camp, and sent cavalry to charge them.

entries.zh: 寶眾大敗，走還中山，獲其器械數十萬計。
entries.en: Bao's army was shattered and fled to Zhongshan; weapons taken numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: Bao's host was utterly defeated and fled back to Zhongshan; weapons and gear captured were reckoned in the hundreds of thousands.

entries.zh: 寶尚書閔亮、秘書監崔逞等降者相屬，賜拜職爵各有差。
entries.en: Min Liang of Bao's Masters of Writing, Cui Cheng the Secretariat Director, and others who surrendered were given offices and ranks according to merit.
entries.literal: Bao's Masters of Writing Min Liang, Secretariat Director Cui Cheng, and others who surrendered came one after another and were granted offices and ranks each according to merit.

entries.zh: 三月己酉，車駕次盧奴。
entries.en: On jiyou day in the third month the court camped at Lunu.
entries.literal: On day jiyou in the third month the imperial carriage halted at Lunu.

entries.zh: 寶求和，請送秦王觚，割常山以西奉魏，乞守中山以東。
entries.en: Bao sued for peace, offering to send Prince Gu of Qin, cede everything west of Changshan to Wei, and keep only the lands east of the mountains around Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Bao sued for peace, asking to send Prince Gu of Qin, to cede the lands west of Changshan to Wei, and to hold Zhongshan east of the mountains.

entries.zh: 帝許之。
entries.en: The Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor consented.

entries.zh: 已而寶背約。
entries.en: Soon Bao broke his word.
entries.literal: Before long Bao broke the agreement.

entries.zh: 辛亥，車駕次中山，命將圍之。
entries.en: On xinhai day the court came to Zhongshan and ordered a siege.
entries.literal: On day xinhai the imperial carriage halted at Zhongshan and ordered the generals to besiege it.

entries.zh: 是夜，寶弟賀驎將妻子走西山。
entries.en: That night Bao's brother He Lin fled west into the hills with his family.
entries.literal: That night Bao's younger brother He Lin led his wife and children to flee to the western hills.

entries.zh: 寶恐賀驎先據和龍，壬子夜，北遁。
entries.en: Fearing He Lin would take Helong first, Bao fled north on the night of renzi day.
entries.literal: Bao feared that He Lin would seize Helong first; on the night of day renzi he fled north.

entries.zh: 城內共立慕容普鄰為主。
entries.en: The city set up Murong Pulin as their lord.
entries.literal: Within the city they jointly set up Murong Pulin as ruler.

entries.zh: 夏四月，帝以軍糧不繼，詔東平公儀罷鄴圍，徙屯巨鹿。
entries.en: In the fourth month, with supplies failing, he ordered Duke Yi of Dongping to raise the siege of Ye and move to Julu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, because army grain could not keep up, he ordered Duke Yi of Dongping to lift the siege of Ye and move camp to Julu.

entries.zh: 五月庚子，帝以中山城內為普鄰所脅，乃招喻之。
entries.en: On gengzi day in the fifth month, seeing the city held hostage by Pulin, he sent envoys to win the people over.
entries.literal: On day gengzi in the fifth month, because those within Zhongshan were coerced by Pulin, he sent messages to win them over.

entries.zh: 甲辰，曜兵揚威，以示城內，命諸軍罷圍南徙，以待其變。
entries.en: On jiachen day he paraded his army before the walls, drew off the siege southward, and waited for the city to turn.
entries.literal: On day jiachen he displayed his troops to show might before the city, ordered the armies to lift the siege and move south, and waited for the city to change.

entries.zh: 甲寅，以東平公儀為左丞相，封衛王。
entries.en: On jiayin day he made Duke Yi of Dongping Left Chancellor and Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: On day jiayin he made Duke Yi of Dongping Left Chancellor and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 進襄城公題爵為王。
entries.en: He raised Duke Ti of Xiangcheng to prince.
entries.literal: He advanced Duke Ti of Xiangcheng to princely rank.

entries.zh: 秋七月，普鄰遣烏丸、張驤率五千餘人出城求食，寇靈壽。
entries.en: In the seventh month Pulin sent Zhang Yang the Wuhuan with five thousand men to forage and raid Linghou.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Pulin sent the Wuhuan Zhang Yang with more than five thousand men out of the city to forage and raid Linghou.

entries.zh: 賀驎自丁零中入軍，因其眾，復入中山，殺普鄰而自立。
entries.en: He Lin came in from the Dingling tribes, gathered their men, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulin, and made himself ruler.
entries.literal: He Lin entered the army from among the Dingling, rallied their forces, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulin, and set himself up as ruler.

entries.zh: 八月丙寅朔，帝進軍九門。
entries.en: On bingyin day, the new moon of the eighth month, the Emperor marched on Jiumen.
entries.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, day bingyin, the Emperor advanced the army to Jiumen.

entries.zh: 時大疫，人馬牛死者十五六，中山猶拒守，群下咸思北還。
entries.en: A great pestilence was abroad; men, horses, and cattle died by the tens of thousands, yet Zhongshan still held, and everyone below wanted to turn north.
entries.literal: At that time a great pestilence raged; fifteen or sixteen of every hundred men, horses, and cattle died, yet Zhongshan still held out, and all below wished to return north.

entries.zh: 帝知之，謂曰：「斯固天命，將若之何！
entries.en: Knowing their minds, the Emperor said, "This is Heaven's decree. What can we do!
entries.literal: The Emperor knew it and said: "This is truly Heaven's decree; what can be done!

entries.zh: 四海之人皆可與為國，在吾所以撫之耳，何恤乎無人！」
entries.en: Every man under heaven may be made a subject of the realm; it is only a matter of how I win them. Why fear there will be no people!"
entries.literal: All the people within the four seas may be made into a state; it lies in how I comfort them. Why fear that there will be no men!"

entries.zh: 群臣乃不敢言。
entries.en: The ministers dared not speak again.
entries.literal: The ministers then dared not speak.

entries.zh: 九月，賀驎饑窮，率三萬餘人寇新市。
entries.en: In the ninth month He Lin, starving and cornered, led more than thirty thousand men against Xinyi.
entries.literal: In the ninth month He Lin, hungry and desperate, led more than thirty thousand men to raid Xinyi.

entries.zh: 甲子晦，帝進軍討之。
entries.en: On jiazi day, the last day of the month, the Emperor marched out against him.
entries.literal: On the last day of the month, day jiazi, the Emperor advanced the army to attack him.

entries.zh: 太史令晁崇奏曰：「不吉。」
entries.en: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong said, "The day is ill-omened."
entries.literal: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong memorialized: "This is ill-omened."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「何也？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, "How so?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "How so?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「紂以甲子亡，兵家忌之。」
entries.en: He answered, "King Zhou of Shang fell on a jiazi day; soldiers dread it."
entries.literal: He replied: "Zhou fell on a jiazi day; military men hold it in dread."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「周武不以甲子勝乎？」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "Did not King Wu of Zhou win on a jiazi day?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Did not King Wu of Zhou win on a jiazi day?"

entries.zh: 崇無以對。
entries.en: Chong had nothing to say.
entries.literal: Chong had no reply.

entries.zh: 冬十月丙寅，帝進軍新市，賀驎退阻泒水，依漸洳澤以自固。
entries.en: On bingyin day in the tenth month the Emperor marched on Xinshi; He Lin fell back to the Gu River and dug in among the marshes of Jianru.
entries.literal: On day bingyin in the tenth month of winter the Emperor advanced the army to Xinshi; He Lin retreated to block the Gu River and relied on the Jianru Marsh to hold firm.

entries.zh: 甲戌，帝臨其營，戰於義台塢，大破之。
entries.en: On jiaxu day the Emperor faced their camp and fought at Eagle Terrace Hill; he crushed them.
entries.literal: On day jiaxu the Emperor came to their camp and fought at Yitai Walled Hill; he routed them utterly.

entries.zh: 賀驎單馬走鄴，慕容德殺之。
entries.en: He Lin fled alone on horseback toward Ye; Murong De killed him.
entries.literal: He Lin fled Ye on a single horse; Murong De killed him.

entries.zh: 甲申，賀驎所署公卿尚書將吏士卒降者二萬餘人。
entries.en: On jiashen day more than twenty thousand officers and men whom He Lin had appointed surrendered.
entries.literal: On day jiashen more than twenty thousand of the civil and military officers, Masters of Writing clerks, generals, and soldiers whom He Lin had appointed surrendered.

entries.zh: 其將張驤、李沈、慕容文等先來降，尋皆亡還，是日復獲之，皆赦而不問。
entries.en: Generals Zhang Rang, Li Shen, and Murong Wen had surrendered earlier, then fled back; captured again that day, they were all pardoned.
entries.literal: His generals Zhang Rang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others had come over first, then all fled back; that day they were captured again and all were pardoned without inquiry.

entries.zh: 獲其所傳皇帝璽綬、圖書、府庫珍寶。
entries.en: They took the imperial seal and regalia, the archives, and the palace treasures.
entries.literal: They seized the imperial seal and cord of investiture he had passed down, books and documents, and the treasures of the treasury.

entries.zh: 中山平。
entries.en: Zhongshan fell.
entries.literal: Zhongshan was pacified.

entries.zh: 乙酉，襄城王題薨。
entries.en: On yiyou day Prince Ti of Xiangcheng died.
entries.literal: On day yiyou Prince Ti of Xiangcheng died.

entries.zh: 太宗明元皇帝諱嗣，道武皇帝之長子也。
entries.en: Emperor Mingyuan, styled the Grand Ancestor, whose name was Si, was Dao Wu's eldest son.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Mingyuan, personal name Si, was the eldest son of Emperor Dao Wu.

entries.zh: 母曰劉貴人，登國七年，生於雲中宮。
entries.en: His mother was Honored Lady Liu; in Dengguo year seven he was born at the Cloud Palace.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Liu the Honored; in the seventh year of Dengguo he was born in the Cloud Palace.

entries.zh: 道武晚有男，聞而大悅，乃大赦。
entries.en: Dao Wu had long awaited a son; when he heard, he rejoiced and proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: Dao Wu had a son late in life; on hearing the news he rejoiced greatly and proclaimed a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 帝明睿寬毅，非禮不動。
entries.en: He was clear-minded, wise, magnanimous, and firm; nothing moved him outside the rites.
entries.literal: The Emperor was bright, wise, generous, and resolute; he would not act against propriety.

entries.zh: 天興六年，封齊王，拜相國。
entries.en: In Tianxing year six he was made Prince of Qi and Chancellor of State.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianxing he was enfeoffed Prince of Qi and appointed Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 初，帝母既賜死，道武召帝告曰：「昔漢武將立其子而殺其母，不令婦人與國政，汝當繼統，故吾遠同漢武。」
entries.en: When his mother had been put to death, Dao Wu called him in and said: "Emperor Wu of Han killed his son's mother before setting the boy on the throne, lest a woman hold the state. You will succeed me, so I have done as Han Wu did."
entries.literal: At the outset, after the Emperor's mother had been ordered to die, Dao Wu summoned the Emperor and said: "In old days Emperor Wu of Han was about to establish his son and therefore killed the mother, not allowing women a share in state affairs; you are to succeed to the throne, so I follow Han Wu in the distant past."

entries.zh: 帝素純孝，哀不自勝。
entries.en: The Emperor had always been devoted; grief overwhelmed him.
entries.literal: The Emperor had always been pure in filial piety; grief overwhelmed him beyond bearing.

entries.zh: 道武怒。
entries.en: Dao Wu grew angry.
entries.literal: Dao Wu was angry.

entries.zh: 帝還宮，哀不自止，道武知而又召帝。
entries.en: He went back to the palace still weeping; when Dao Wu heard, he summoned him again.
entries.literal: The Emperor returned to the palace; grief would not cease; Dao Wu learned of it and summoned him again.

entries.zh: 帝欲入，左右諫，請待和解而進，帝從之。
entries.en: He started to go in; his attendants urged him to wait until tempers had cooled; he listened.
entries.literal: The Emperor wished to enter; his attendants remonstrated, asking that he wait until feelings had eased before going in; the Emperor followed their advice.

entries.zh: 及元紹之逆，帝還而誅之。
entries.en: When Prince Shao rebelled, the Emperor came back and put him to death.
entries.literal: When Prince Shao's rebellion came, the Emperor returned and had him executed.

entries.zh: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝
entries.en: Emperor Daowu the Grand Progenitor; Emperor Mingyuan the Grand Successor.
entries.literal: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu; Grand Successor Emperor Mingyuan.

entries.zh: 三年春二月壬子，秦州沙門劉光秀謀反，州郡捕斬之。
entries.en: In the third year, in spring, in the second month, on the renzi day, Liu Guangxiu, a monk of Qin Province, plotted rebellion; provincial and commandery authorities captured and beheaded him.
entries.literal: In the third year, in spring, in the second month, on the renzi day, Liu Guangxiu, a monk of Qin Province, plotted rebellion, and the province and commandery authorities captured and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 癸亥，秦州隴西羌殺鎮將趙俊反，州軍討平之。
entries.en: On the guihai day, Qiang of Longxi in Qin Province killed the garrison commander Zhao Jun and rebelled; provincial troops attacked and pacified them.
entries.literal: On the guihai day, Qiang of Longxi in Qin Province killed the garrison commander Zhao Jun and rebelled; provincial troops attacked and pacified them.

entries.zh: 三月丙戌，皇子詡生，大赦。
entries.en: In the third month, on the bingxu day, the imperial son Xu was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the bingxu day, the imperial son Xu was born, and there was a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 夏四月，平陽郡之禽昌、襄陵二縣大疫，自正月至此月，死者二千七百三十人。
entries.en: In summer, in the fourth month, the two counties of Qinchang and Xiangling in Pingyang Commandery suffered a great epidemic; from the first month to this month, 2,730 people died.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, the two counties of Qinchang and Xiangling in Pingyang Commandery suffered a great epidemic; from the first month to this month, 2,730 people died.

entries.zh: 五月丁亥，冀、定二州旱儉，詔開倉振恤。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the dinghai day, Ji and Ding provinces suffered drought and shortage, and an edict ordered granaries opened for relief.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the dinghai day, Ji and Ding provinces suffered drought and shortage, and an edict ordered granaries opened to relieve them.

entries.zh: 六月甲寅，詔重求遺書於天下。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the jiayin day, an edict again sought lost books throughout the realm.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the jiayin day, an edict again sought lost books throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛卯，中山王英薨。
entries.en: In winter, in the tenth month, on the xinmao day, Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, died.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the xinmao day, Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, died.

entries.zh: 丙申，詔太常立館，使京畿內外疾病之徒，咸令居處。
entries.en: On the bingshen day, an edict ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to establish a hospice where the sick from inside and outside the capital region could all be housed.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day, an edict ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to establish a hospice and have all the sick inside and outside the capital region reside there.

entries.zh: 嚴敕醫署分師救療，考其能否而行賞罰。
entries.en: The Medical Office was strictly ordered to assign physicians for treatment, with rewards and punishments based on assessments of their effectiveness.
entries.literal: The Medical Office was strictly ordered to assign physicians to treat and rescue them, and their ability or inability was to be examined so rewards and punishments could be carried out.

entries.zh: 又令有司集諸醫工，惟簡精要，取三十卷以班九服。
entries.en: It was also ordered that the responsible officials gather the medical practitioners, select the essential material, and compile thirty juan for distribution throughout the realm.
entries.literal: It was also ordered that the responsible officials gather the medical practitioners, select only the essential material, and take thirty juan to distribute through the nine regions.

entries.zh: 十二月辛巳，江陽王繼坐事除名。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the xinsi day, Ji, Prince of Jiangyang, was stripped of office and title for an offense.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the xinsi day, Ji, Prince of Jiangyang, was stripped of his name for an offense.

entries.zh: 甲申，詔於青州立孝文皇帝廟。
entries.en: On the jiashen day, an edict ordered a temple for Emperor Xiaowen established in Qing Province.
entries.literal: On the jiashen day, an edict ordered a temple for Emperor Xiaowen established in Qing Province.

entries.zh: 殿中侍御史王敞謀反，伏誅。
entries.en: Wang Chang, Palace Attendant Censor, plotted rebellion and was executed.
entries.literal: Wang Chang, Palace Attendant Censor, plotted rebellion and submitted to execution.

entries.zh: 是歲，西域、東夷、北狄十六國並遣使朝貢。
entries.en: That year, sixteen states of the Western Regions, Eastern Yi, and Northern Di all sent envoys to court with tribute.
entries.literal: That year, sixteen states of the Western Regions, Eastern Yi, and Northern Di all sent envoys to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 四年春正月丁巳，汾州劉龍駒聚眾反，詔諫議大夫薛和討之。
entries.en: In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the dingsi day, Liu Longju of Fen Province gathered a crowd and rebelled; an edict ordered Remonstrance Grandee Xue He to attack him.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the dingsi day, Liu Longju of Fen Province gathered a crowd and rebelled; an edict ordered Remonstrance Grandee Xue He to attack him.

entries.zh: 二月壬午，青、齊、徐、兗四州人饑甚，遣使振恤。
entries.en: In the second month, on the renwu day, the people of Qing, Qi, Xu, and Yan provinces suffered severe famine, and envoys were sent to provide relief.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the renwu day, the people of Qing, Qi, Xu, and Yan provinces suffered severe famine, and envoys were sent to relieve them.

entries.zh: 三月壬戌，司徒、廣陽王嘉薨。
entries.en: In the third month, on the renxu day, Jia, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Guangyang, died.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the renxu day, Jia, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Guangyang, died.

entries.zh: 夏四月，梁遣其鎮北將軍張稷及馬仙琕寇朐山，詔徐州刺史盧昶率眾赴之。
entries.en: In summer, in the fourth month, Liang sent its General Who Guards the North Zhang Ji and Ma Xianbei to raid Qushan; an edict ordered Lu Chang, inspector of Xu Province, to lead troops there.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Liang sent its General Who Guards the North Zhang Ji and Ma Xianbei to raid Qushan; an edict ordered Lu Chang, inspector of Xu Province, to lead troops to go there.

entries.zh: 五月己亥，遷代京銅龍置天泉池西。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the jihai day, the bronze dragon from the old capital at Dai was moved and placed west of Tianquan Pool.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the jihai day, the bronze dragon from the old capital at Dai was moved and placed west of Tianquan Pool.

entries.zh: 丙辰，詔禁天文學。
entries.en: On the bingchen day, an edict prohibited the study of astronomy and astrology.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day, an edict prohibited the study of astronomy and astrology.

entries.zh: 冬十一月，朐山城陷，盧昶大敗而還。
entries.en: In winter, in the eleventh month, Qushan city fell, and Lu Chang returned after a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: In winter, in the eleventh month, Qushan city fell, and Lu Chang returned after a great defeat.

entries.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，日有蝕之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the renxu day, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the renxu day, the first day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 是歲，西域、東夷、北狄二十九國並遣使朝貢。
entries.en: That year, twenty-nine states of the Western Regions, Eastern Yi, and Northern Di all sent envoys to court with tribute.
entries.literal: That year, twenty-nine states of the Western Regions, Eastern Yi, and Northern Di all sent envoys to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 宜遵舊典，稱詔宇內，以副黎蒸元元之望。」
entries.en: We should follow precedent, proclaim the title throughout the realm, and answer the hopes of the common people."
entries.literal: It is fitting to follow the old precedents, proclaim the title throughout the realm, and answer the hopes of the black-haired common people."

entries.zh: 是月，改葬文昭皇太后高氏。
entries.en: That month, Empress Dowager Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.
entries.literal: That month, Empress Dowager Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.

entries.zh: 二月乙丑，齊郡王祐薨。
entries.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi Commandery, died.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi Commandery, died.

entries.zh: 庚午，羽林千餘人焚征西將軍張彝第，毆傷彝，燒殺其子始均。
entries.en: On the gengwu day, more than a thousand Feathered Forest guards burned the residence of Zhang Yi, General Who Conquers the West, beat and injured him, and burned his son Shijun to death.
entries.literal: On the gengwu day, more than a thousand Feathered Forest guards burned the residence of Zhang Yi, General Who Conquers the West, beat and injured Yi, and burned his son Shijun to death.

entries.zh: 乙亥，大赦。
entries.en: On the yihai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, there was a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 丁丑，詔求直言。
entries.en: On the dingchou day, an edict called for forthright criticism.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, an edict sought forthright speech.

entries.zh: 壬寅，詔以旱故，命依舊雩祈，察理冤獄，掩胔埋骼，振窮恤寡。
entries.en: On the renyin day, because of the drought, an edict ordered rain-prayers according to old practice, the review of wrongful imprisonments, the burial of exposed remains, and relief for the poor and widowed.
entries.literal: On the renyin day, because of the drought, an edict ordered rain-prayers according to old practice, the investigation and correction of unjust imprisonments, the covering of exposed corpses and burial of bones, and relief for the poor and aid for widows.

entries.zh: 三月甲辰，澍雨大洽。
entries.en: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell in great abundance.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell in great abundance.

entries.zh: 夏五月戊戌，以司空、任城王澄為司徒，京兆王繼為司空。
entries.en: In summer, in the fifth month, on the wuxu day, Cheng, Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng, was made Minister over the Masses, and Ji, Prince of Jingzhao, was made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, on the wuxu day, Cheng, Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng, was made Minister over the Masses, and Ji, Prince of Jingzhao, was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 秋八月乙未，御史中尉、東平王匡坐事削除官爵。
