entries.en: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the yiwei day, Kuang, Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Dongping, was stripped of office and noble rank for an offense.
entries.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the yiwei day, Kuang, Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Dongping, was implicated in an affair and stripped of office and noble rank.

entries.zh: 九月庚寅，皇太后幸嵩高山。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the gengyin day, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Songgao.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the gengyin day, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Songgao.

entries.zh: 癸巳，還宮。
entries.en: On the guisi day, she returned to the palace.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, she returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 冬十二月癸丑，司徒、任城王澄薨。
entries.en: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guichou day, Cheng, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Rencheng, died.
entries.literal: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guichou day, Cheng, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Rencheng, died.

entries.zh: 庚申，大赦。
entries.en: On the gengshen day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day, there was a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 詔除淫祀，焚諸雜神。
entries.en: An edict abolished improper cults and burned assorted cult images.
entries.literal: An edict abolished improper sacrifices and burned the various miscellaneous gods.

entries.zh: 是歲，吐谷渾、宕昌、嚈噠等國並遣使朝貢。
entries.en: That year, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, the Hephthalites, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.
entries.literal: That year, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, Hephthalites, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 世宗宣武帝
entries.en: Emperor Shizong Xuanwu.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong Xuanwu.

entries.zh: 魏氏王業之兆，雖始於神元，然自昭成之前，未具言六宮之典；
entries.en: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;
entries.literal: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;

entries.zh: 而章、平、思、昭、穆、惠、煬、烈八帝妃後無聞。
entries.en: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.
entries.literal: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.

entries.zh: 道武追尊祖妣，皆從帝諡為皇后。
entries.en: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.
entries.literal: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.

entries.zh: 始立中宮，餘妾或稱夫人，多少無限，然皆有品次。
entries.en: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.
entries.literal: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.

entries.zh: 太武稍增左右昭儀及貴人、椒房等，後庭漸已多矣。
entries.en: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi, noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.
entries.literal: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi and noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.

entries.zh: 又魏故事，將立皇后，必令手鑄金人，以成者為吉，不則不得立也。
entries.en: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.
entries.literal: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.

entries.zh: 又太武、文成，保母劬勞之恩，並極尊崇之義，雖事乖典禮，而觀過知仁。
entries.en: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.
entries.literal: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.

entries.zh: 孝文改定內官：左右昭儀位視大司馬，三夫人視三公，三嬪視三卿，六嬪視六卿，世婦視中大夫，御女視元士。
entries.en: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grandees; palace women with yuan shi.
entries.literal: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grand masters; palace women with yuan shi.

entries.zh: 後置女職，以典內司。
entries.en: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.
entries.literal: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.

entries.zh: 內司視尚書令、僕。
entries.en: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 作司、大監、女侍中三官視二品。
entries.en: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.
entries.literal: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.

entries.zh: 監、女尚書、美人，女史、女賢人、女書史、書女、小書女五官視三品。
entries.en: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.
entries.literal: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.

entries.zh: 中才人、供人、中使、女生才人、恭使宮人視四品。
entries.en: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.
entries.literal: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.

entries.zh: 青衣、女酒、女饗、女食、奚官女奴視五品。
entries.en: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.
entries.literal: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.

entries.zh: 及齊神武、文襄，俱未踐尊極。
entries.en: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.
entries.literal: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.

entries.zh: 神武嫡妻稱妃，其所娉蠕蠕女稱為蠕蠕公主。
entries.en: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.
entries.literal: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.

entries.zh: 文襄既尚魏朝公主，故無別號。
entries.en: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.
entries.literal: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.

entries.zh: 兩宮自余姬侍，並稱娘而已。
entries.en: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.
entries.literal: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.

entries.zh: 文宣後庭雖有夫人、嬪、御之稱，然未具員數。
entries.en: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.
entries.literal: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.

entries.zh: 孝昭內職甚少，唯楊嬪才貌兼美，復是貴家，襄城王母桑氏有德行，並蒙恩禮，其餘無聞焉。
entries.en: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.
entries.literal: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.

entries.zh: 魏神元皇后竇氏 文帝皇后封氏 桓皇后惟氏 平文皇后王氏 昭成皇后慕容氏 獻明皇后賀氏 道武皇后慕容氏 道武宣穆皇后劉氏 明元昭哀皇后姚氏 明元密皇后杜氏 太武皇后赫連氏 太武敬哀皇后賀氏 景穆恭皇后郁久閭氏 文成文明皇后馮氏 文成元皇后李氏 獻文思皇后李氏 孝文貞皇后林氏 孝文廢皇后馮氏 孝文幽皇后馮氏 孝文文昭皇后高氏 宣武順皇后于氏 宣武皇后高氏 宣武靈皇后胡氏 孝明皇后胡氏 孝武皇后高氏 文帝文皇后乙弗氏 文帝悼皇后郁久閭氏 廢帝皇后宇文氏 恭帝皇后若干氏 孝靜皇后高氏
entries.en: Empress Dowager Dou of Wei Shenyuan; Empress Feng of Wei Wendi; Empress Wei of Wei Huandi; Empress Wang of Wei Pingwen; Empress Murong of Wei Zhaocheng; Empress He of Wei Xianming; Empress Murong of Wei Daowu; Empress Liu, Xuanmu, of Wei Daowu; Empress Yao, Zhaoguai, of Wei Mingyuan; the secret empress Du of Wei Mingyuan; Empress Helian of Wei Taiwu; Empress He, Jing'ai, of Wei Taiwu; Empress Yujiulü, Gong, of Wei Jingmu; Empress Feng, Civilizing, of Wei Wencheng; Empress Li, Yuan, of Wei Wencheng; Empress Li, Si, of Wei Xianwen; Empress Lin, Zhen, of Wei Xiaowen; the deposed Empress Feng of Wei Xiaowen; Empress Feng, You, of Wei Xiaowen; Empress Gao, Wenzhao, of Wei Xiaowen; Empress Yu, Shun, of Wei Xuanwu; Empress Gao of Wei Xuanwu; Empress Hu, Ling, of Wei Xuanwu; Empress Hu of Wei Xiaoming; Empress Gao of Wei Xiaowu; Empress Yifu, Wen, of Wei Wendi; Empress Yujiulü, Dao, of Wei Wendi; Empress Yuwen of the deposed emperor; Empress Ruogan of Wei Gongdi; Empress Gao of Wei Xiaojing

entries.zh: 公孫表，字玄元，燕郡廣陽人也。
entries.en: Gong Sunbiao, styled Xuanyuan, was a native of Guangyang in Yan Commandery.
entries.literal: Gong Sunbiao, styled Xuanyuan, was a native of Guangyang in Yan Commandery.

entries.zh: 為慕容沖尚書郎。
entries.en: He served Murong Chong as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He served Murong Chong as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 慕容垂破長子，從入中山。
entries.en: When Murong Chui took Changzi, Biao followed him into Zhongshan.
entries.literal: When Murong Chui took Changzi, Biao followed him into Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 慕容寶走，乃歸，為博士。
entries.en: When Murong Bao fled, he submitted and was made a Erudite.
entries.literal: When Murong Bao fled, he submitted and was made a Erudite.

entries.zh: 初，道武以慕容垂諸子分據勢要，權柄推移，遂至亡滅，表詣闕上《韓非書》二十卷。
entries.en: Earlier, Daowu had seen how Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and power shifted until ruin came; Biao went to court and presented twenty scrolls of Han Feizi.
entries.literal: Earlier, Daowu had seen how Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and power shifted until ruin came; Biao went to court and presented twenty scrolls of Han Feizi.

entries.zh: 道武稱善。
entries.en: Daowu praised it.
entries.literal: Daowu praised it.

entries.zh: 明元初，賜爵固安子。
entries.en: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gu'an.

entries.zh: 河西饑胡劉武反於上黨，詔表討之。
entries.en: The starving Hu of Hexi, Liu Wu, rebelled at Shangdang; an edict ordered Biao to suppress him.
entries.literal: The starving Hu of Hexi, Liu Wu, rebelled at Shangdang; an edict ordered Biao to suppress him.

entries.zh: 為胡所敗，帝深銜之。
entries.en: He was defeated by the Hu; the emperor bore a deep grudge.
entries.literal: He was defeated by the Hu; the emperor bore a deep grudge.

entries.zh: 泰常七年，宋武帝殂。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Taichang, Emperor Wu of Song died.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang, Emperor Wu of Song died.

entries.zh: 時議取河南侵地，以奚斤為都督，以表為吳兵將軍、廣州刺史。
entries.en: At the time the court debated taking the invaded lands south of the Yellow River; Xi Jin was made supreme commander, and Biao was made General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: At the time the court debated taking the invaded lands south of the Yellow River; Xi Jin was made supreme commander, and Biao was made General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 表既克滑台，遂圍武牢。
entries.en: After Biao took Huatai, he then besieged Wulao.
entries.literal: After Biao took Huatai, he then besieged Wulao.

entries.zh: 車駕次汲郡。
entries.en: The imperial carriage halted at Ji Commandery.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Ji Commandery.

entries.zh: 始昌子蘇坦、太史令王亮奏表置軍武牢東，不得形便之地，故令賊不時滅。
entries.en: Shichangzi Su Tan and Grand Astrologer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Wulao, not on advantageous ground, and so the bandits were not destroyed in time.
entries.literal: Shichangzi Su Tan and Grand Astrologer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Wulao, not on advantageous ground, and so the bandits were not destroyed in time.

entries.zh: 明元雅好術數，又積前忿，及攻武牢，士卒多傷，乃使人夜就帳中縊殺之。
entries.en: Mingyuan was fond of numerology and divination and still harbored old resentment; when the assault on Wulao cost many wounded soldiers, he sent men at night into the tent to strangle Biao.
entries.literal: Mingyuan was fond of numerology and divination and still harbored old resentment; when the assault on Wulao cost many wounded soldiers, he sent men at night into the tent to strangle Biao.

entries.zh: 以賊未退，秘而不宣。
entries.en: Because the enemy had not yet withdrawn, it was kept secret.
entries.literal: Because the enemy had not yet withdrawn, it was kept secret.

entries.zh: 毛修之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。
entries.en: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, of Yangwu in Xingyang.
entries.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, native of Yangwu in Xingyang.

entries.zh: 世仕晉。
entries.en: His house served Jin for generations.
entries.literal: For generations the house served Jin.

entries.zh: 劉裕之平關中，留子義真鎮長安，以修之為司馬。
entries.en: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left son Yizhen at Chang'an with Xiuzhi as marshal.
entries.literal: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an, making Xiuzhi marshal.

entries.zh: 及義真敗，修之沒統萬。
entries.en: When Yizhen fell Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.
entries.literal: When Yizhen was defeated Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.

entries.zh: 太武平赫連昌，獲之。
entries.en: Taiwu pacified Helian Chang and took him.
entries.literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang he obtained him.

entries.zh: 使領吳兵，以功拜吳兵將軍。
entries.en: He was set to lead Wu troops and enfeoffed General of Wu Troops for merit.
entries.literal: He was made to lead Wu troops; for merit enfeoffed General of Wu Troops.

entries.zh: 修之能為南人飲食，手自煎調，多所適意。
entries.en: Xiuzhi could cook southern food and season it himself to please.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi could make southern food and personally season it, often to satisfaction.

entries.zh: 太武親待之，累遷尚書，賜爵南郡公，常在太官主進禦膳。
entries.en: Taiwu favored him, raised him to Vice Director, Duke of Nan, always in the Imperial Kitchen directing meals.
entries.literal: Taiwu personally favored him, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Masters of Writing, enfeoffed Duke of Nan commandery, constantly in the Imperial Kitchen directing imperial meals.

entries.zh: 從討和龍，時諸軍攻城，行宮人少，宋故將硃修之為雲中將軍，欲率吳兵為逆。
entries.en: Besieging Helong the camp had few men; Song's Zhu Xiuzhi, General of Yunzhong, wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.
entries.literal: On campaign against Helong, when the armies besieged the city the traveling palace had few men; Song's old general Zhu Xiuzhi was General of Yunzhong and wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.

entries.zh: 因入和龍，冀浮海南歸。
entries.en: He entered Helong hoping to sail south by sea.
entries.literal: He entered Helong hoping to float south by sea and return.

entries.zh: 以告修之，不聽，乃止。
entries.en: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi refused and he stopped.
entries.literal: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi would not listen and he stopped.

entries.zh: 是日無修之，大變幾作。
entries.en: That day without Xiuzhi a great disaster nearly came.
entries.literal: That day without Xiuzhi a great upheaval nearly happened.

entries.zh: 硃修之遂奔馮弘。
entries.en: Zhu Xiuzhi fled to Feng Hong.
entries.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi then fled to Feng Hong.

entries.zh: 修之又以軍功，遷特進、撫軍大將軍，位次崔浩下。
entries.en: Xiuzhi rose again for merit to Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, below Cui Hao.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi again for military merit was promoted Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, rank below Cui Hao.

entries.zh: 浩以其中國舊門，雖不博洽，猶涉獵書傳，與共論說之。
entries.en: Hao, because he was an old Chinese house, though not broad still read books and debated with him.
entries.literal: Hao because he was an old house of China, though not broadly versed still dipped into books and records, and debated with him.

entries.zh: 次及陳壽《三國志》，云「有古良史風，其所著述，文義典正，班史以來無及壽者」。
entries.en: They came to Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; Hao said it had the air of a good ancient historian, canonical since Ban Gu.
entries.literal: Next they reached Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; he said "it has the air of an ancient good historian; what he wrote is canonical in meaning — since Ban Gu none match Shou."

entries.zh: 修之曰：「昔在蜀中，聞長老言，壽曾為諸葛亮門下書佐，得撻百下，故其論武侯云：應變非其所長。」
entries.en: Xiuzhi said, "In Shu elders said Shou had been Zhuge Liang's clerk, was flogged a hundred times, so he wrote the Martial Lord was weak at adaptation."
entries.literal: Xiuzhi said: "In Shu I once heard elders say Shou had been a clerk under Zhuge Liang and was flogged a hundred strokes, so in judging the Martial Lord he wrote: adapting to change was not his strength.

entries.zh: 浩乃與論曰：「承祚之評亮，乃有故義過美之譽，非挾恨之言。
entries.en: Hao argued, "Shou's judgment of Liang was old obligation praising too much, not resentment.
entries.literal: Hao then argued: "Chen Shou's judgment of Liang was praise beyond measure from old obligation, not words of resentment.

entries.zh: 夫亮之相備，英雄奮發之時，君臣相得，魚水為喻。
entries.en: Liang serving Bei was hero and lord meeting, ruler and minister like fish and water.
entries.literal: Liang's serving Bei was the time when hero and lord met; ruler and minister matched, fish and water as metaphor.

entries.zh: 而不能與曹氏爭天下，委棄荊州，退入巴蜀，守窮崎嶇之地，僭號邊夷之間，此策之下者。
entries.en: Yet he could not fight Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated to Ba-Shu, held poor hills, styled himself emperor among barbarians—the lowest stratagem.
entries.literal: Yet he could not contend with Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated into Ba-Shu, held poor rugged ground, styled himself emperor among border barbarians — this is the lowest stratagem.

entries.zh: 可以趙佗為偶，而以管、蕭之亞匹，不亦過乎！
entries.en: He may match Zhao Tuo; to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He—is that not too much!
entries.literal: He may be paired with Zhao Tuo, yet to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He — is that not excessive!

entries.zh: 且亮既據蜀，弗量勢力，嚴威切法，控勒蜀人，欲以邊夷之眾，抗衡上國。
entries.en: Moreover Liang held Shu, misread strength, ruled Shu with harsh law, wished border tribes to resist the center.
entries.literal: Moreover Liang held Shu, did not measure strength, used harsh law to control Shu men, wished with border barbarians' masses to resist the central state.

entries.zh: 出兵隴右，再攻祁山，一攻陳倉，疏遲失會，摧衄而反。
entries.en: He marched from Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once Chencang, slow and late, broken and back.
entries.literal: He sent troops out Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once attacked Chencang, slow and missing the moment, broken and returned.

entries.zh: 後入秦川，更求野戰。
entries.en: Later he entered Qinchuan and again sought battle in the open.
entries.literal: Later he entered Qin River valley and again sought field battle.

entries.zh: 魏人知其意，以不戰屈之。
entries.en: Wei knew his mind and wore him down without fighting.
entries.literal: The Wei men knew his intent and wore him down without fighting.

entries.zh: 智窮勢盡，發病而死。
entries.en: Wits gone, power spent, he fell ill and died.
entries.literal: Wits exhausted, power spent, he fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 由是言之，豈合古之善將，見可知難乎？」
entries.en: By that measure, how is he an ancient good general who sees difficulty and stops?"
entries.literal: By this speaking, how does he fit an ancient good general who sees difficulty and knows when to stop?"

entries.zh: 修之謂浩言為然。
entries.en: Xiuzhi said Hao was right.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi said Hao's words were right.

entries.zh: 後卒於外都大官，諡恭公。
entries.en: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous Duke Gong.
entries.literal: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous name Duke Gong.

entries.zh: 修之在南有四子，唯子法仁入魏。
entries.en: In the south Xiuzhi had four sons; only Faren entered Wei.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi in the south had four sons; only son Faren entered Wei.

entries.zh: 文成初，為金部尚書，襲爵，轉殿中尚書。
entries.en: At Wencheng's start he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, then Director Within the Hall.
entries.literal: At the start of Wencheng he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, transferred to Director Within the Hall.

entries.zh: 法仁言聲壯大，至於軍旅田狩，唱呼處分，振於山谷。
entries.en: Faren's voice was huge; on campaign and hunt his commands shook the valleys.
entries.literal: Faren's voice was strong and large; in army camp and hunt his shouts directing ranks shook the valleys.

entries.zh: 卒，贈征東大將軍、南郡王，諡曰威。
entries.en: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan, posthumous name Martial.
entries.literal: At death posthumously General Who Pacifies the East, Prince of Nan commandery, posthumous name Wei (Martial).

entries.zh: 屈遵 張蒲 谷渾 公孫表 張濟 李先 賈彝 竇瑾 李訢 韓延之 袁式 毛脩之 唐和 寇讚 酈範 韓秀 堯暄 柳崇
entries.en: Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gong Sunbiao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Dou Jin, Li Xin, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan, and Liu Chong
entries.literal: Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gong Sunbiao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Dou Jin, Li Xin, Han Yanzhi, Yuan Shi, Mao Xiuzhi, Tang He, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan, Liu Chong

entries.zh: 臣聞為國之道，其要有五：一曰文德，二曰武功，三曰法度，四曰防固，五曰刑賞。
entries.en: I have heard that governing a state rests on five essentials: civil virtue, martial prowess, law and regulation, frontier defense, and the balance of punishment and reward.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the Way of governing a state has five essentials: first, civil virtue; second, martial achievement; third, laws and standards; fourth, defense and fortification; fifth, punishments and rewards.

entries.zh: 故遠人不服，則修文德以來之；
entries.en: When distant peoples refuse submission, cultivate civil virtue to win them over;
entries.literal: Thus when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in;

entries.zh: 荒狡放命，則播武功以威之；
entries.en: when savage and defiant enemies run riot, display martial might to overawe them;
entries.literal: when wild and cunning men defy orders, deploy martial achievement to awe them;

entries.zh: 人未知戰，則制法度以齊之；
entries.en: when the people are untrained for war, establish laws and standards to discipline them;
entries.literal: when men do not yet know warfare, establish laws and standards to bring them into order;

entries.zh: 暴敵輕侵，則設防固以禦之；
entries.en: when violent foes raid with impunity, build defenses to hold them off;
entries.literal: when violent enemies lightly invade, set up defenses and fortifications to repel them;

entries.zh: 臨事制勝，則明賞罰以勸之。
entries.en: when victory must be seized in the field, make rewards and punishments clear to spur men on.
entries.literal: when facing affairs and securing victory, clarify rewards and punishments to encourage them.

entries.zh: 用能辟國甯方，征伐四克。
entries.en: By such means a state may expand its borders, secure the realm, and prevail in every campaign.
entries.literal: By these means one can open the state and bring the realm to peace, and campaigns and punitive expeditions succeed on all sides.

entries.zh: 北狄悍愚，同於禽獸，所長者野戰，所短者攻城。
entries.en: The northern barbarians are brutal and simple, little better than animals; they excel at open battle but are weak at siege warfare.
entries.literal: The northern Di are fierce and stupid, like birds and beasts; what they excel at is fighting in the wild, what they are poor at is besieging cities.

entries.zh: 若以狄之所短，奪其所長，則雖眾不能成患，雖來不能內逼。
entries.en: If we exploit their weaknesses to neutralize their strengths, then even in great numbers they cannot threaten us, and even when they come they cannot press deep into our territory.
entries.literal: If one uses what the Di are poor at to overcome what they excel at, then though numerous they cannot become a calamity, and though they come they cannot press inward.

entries.zh: 又狄散居野澤，隨逐水草，戰則與室家並至，奔則與畜牧俱逃。
entries.en: Moreover they live scattered across marshes and wild country, moving with the pasturage; when they fight they bring their families with them, and when they flee they drive off their herds as well.
entries.literal: Moreover the Di live scattered in marshes and wilds, following after water and grass; when they fight they arrive together with their households, when they flee they escape together with their herds.

entries.zh: 是以古人伐北方，攘其侵掠而已。
entries.en: That is why the ancients, when they campaigned northward, contented themselves with repelling raids and incursions.
entries.literal: Therefore the ancients in campaigning against the north merely drove off their raids and invasions.

entries.zh: 歷代為邊患者，良以倏忽無常故也。
entries.en: Dynasty after dynasty suffered on the frontier chiefly because these enemies struck suddenly and without warning.
entries.literal: The reason successive dynasties suffered frontier troubles was truly because the barbarians were sudden and unpredictable.

entries.zh: 六鎮勢分，倍眾不鬥，互相圍逼，難以制之。
entries.en: The six frontier garrisons are scattered; even at double strength they hesitate to give battle, and when they hem one another in they become difficult to command.
entries.literal: The six garrisons are divided in strength; though twice the enemy in number they do not fight, and when they surround and press one another they are hard to control.

entries.zh: 昔周命南仲，城彼朔方，趙靈、秦始，長城是築；
entries.en: Long ago Zhou commissioned Nanzhong to fortify the northern frontier; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin raised the Long Wall;
entries.literal: Formerly Zhou appointed Nanzhong and walled that northern region; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;

entries.zh: 漢之孝武，踵其前事。
entries.en: and Emperor Wu of Han followed their example.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han followed their earlier deeds.

entries.zh: 此四代之君，皆帝王之雄傑，所以同此役者，非智術之不長，兵眾之不足，乃防狄之要事，理宜然也。
entries.en: These four rulers were all formidable sovereigns. They undertook the same labor not from lack of strategy or troops, but because guarding against the northern barbarians was essential—and rightly so.
entries.literal: These rulers of four dynasties were all heroic emperors and kings; the reason they all undertook this task was not that their wisdom and arts were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter and reason demanded it.

entries.zh: 魏初，博士清河張揖著《埤倉》、《廣雅》、《古今字詁》。
entries.en: Early in Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe composed the Etymological Storehouse, the Broad Lexicon, and the Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Erudite Zhang Yi of Qinghe wrote the *Etymological Storehouse*, the *Broad Lexicon*, and the *Glosses on Ancient and Modern Characters*.

entries.zh: 究諸《埤》、《廣》，綴拾遺漏，增長事類，抑亦于文為益者。
entries.en: In compiling the Storehouse and the Lexicon, he patched omissions and expanded the categories of terms—work that did some service to written learning.
entries.literal: Examining the *Storehouse* and the *Lexicon*, patching omissions and adding categories of things, this too was of some benefit to letters.

entries.zh: 然其《字詁》，方之許篇，古今體用，或得或失。
entries.en: Yet in his Character Glosses, measured against Xu's treatise, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes correct and sometimes mistaken.
entries.literal: Yet in his *Character Glosses*, compared with Xu's work, the ancient and modern forms and usages were sometimes right and sometimes wrong.

entries.zh: 陳留邯鄲淳亦與揖同，博開古藝，特善《倉》、《雅》。
entries.en: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's peer: broadly versed in ancient arts and especially masterful in the Cangjie and the Lexicon.
entries.literal: Handan Chun of Chenliu was Zhang Yi's equal, broadly versed in ancient arts and especially skilled in the *Cangjie* and the *Lexicon*.

entries.zh: 許氏字指、八體、六書，精究閑理，有名於揖。
entries.en: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he pursued the subtle logic to the full and outshone Zhang Yi in reputation.
entries.literal: In the Xu family's explanations of character purpose, the eight scripts, and the six principles, he thoroughly investigated subtle principles and was more renowned than Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 以書教諸皇子。
entries.en: He instructed the princes in writing.
entries.literal: He taught writing to the various princes.

entries.zh: 又建《三字石經》於漢碑西，其文蔚煥，三體復宣。
entries.en: He also set up the Three-Script Stone Classic west of the Han stele; its text shone with brilliance, and the three scripts were displayed once more.
entries.literal: He also erected the *Three-Script Stone Classic* west of the Han stele; its text was splendidly luminous, and the three scripts were again displayed.

entries.zh: 校之《說文》，篆、隸大同，而古字少異。
entries.en: Checked against the Explaining Graphs, the seal and clerical forms were largely identical, though a few ancient characters differed.
entries.literal: Compared with the *Explaining Graphs*, the seal and clerical forms were largely the same, though the ancient characters differed slightly.

entries.zh: 又有京兆韋誕、河東衛覬二家，並號能篆。
entries.en: Two other masters were famed for seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.
entries.literal: There were also two masters styled able in seal script: Wei Dan of Jingzhao and Wei Ji of Hedong.

entries.zh: 當時台觀榜題，寶器之銘，悉是誕書。
entries.en: In those days the inscriptions on palace towers and precious vessels were all written by Dan.
entries.literal: At the time the inscriptions on palace towers and the texts on precious vessels were all in Dan's hand.

entries.zh: 咸傳之子孫，世稱其妙。
entries.en: Their art passed to their descendants, and for generations their skill was hailed as exquisite.
entries.literal: All were handed down to their descendants, and generation after generation their skill was praised as marvelous.

entries.zh: 晉世義陽王典祠令任城呂忱表上《字林》六卷，尋其況趣，附托許慎《說文》，而按偶章句，隱別古籀奇惑之字，文得正隸，不差篆意也。
entries.en: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, director of sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, submitted the six scrolls of the Forest of Characters. In spirit it followed Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs, arranged entries in parallel phrases, and discreetly sorted out ancient Zhou forms, odd characters, and misleading variants, preserving correct clerical writing without abandoning seal-script meaning.
entries.literal: In Jin, Lü Chen of Rencheng, Director of Sacrifices under the Prince of Yiyang, memorialized and submitted the six scrolls of the *Forest of Characters*; tracing its intent, it leaned on Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, arranged parallel phrases, and discreetly distinguished ancient Zhou, odd, and misleading characters, so that the text kept correct clerical forms without losing seal intent.

entries.zh: 忱弟靜別放故左校令李登《聲類》之法，作《韻集》五卷，使宮、商、角、徵、羽各為一篇，而文字與兄便是魯、衛，音讀楚、夏，時有不同。
entries.en: Chen's younger brother Jing, adapting the method of Li Deng's Categories of Sounds, compiled the five scrolls of the Collection of Rhymes, with gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each forming one chapter. In script he and his brother were as close as Lu to Wei, yet in pronunciation they were as far apart as Chu from Xia—sometimes they did not agree.
entries.literal: Chen's younger brother Jing, separately following the method of the former Colonel Director of Works Li Deng's *Categories of Sounds*, composed the five scrolls of the *Collection of Rhymes*, making gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu each one chapter; yet in written characters he and his elder brother were like Lu and Wei, and in pronunciation Chu and Xia—at times they differed.

entries.zh: 皇魏承百王之季，紹五運之緒。
entries.en: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and carried forward the line of the five cycles.
entries.literal: Great Wei succeeded the last of the hundred kings and continued the thread of the five cycles.

entries.zh: 世易風移，文字改變，篆形謬錯，隸體失真。
entries.en: As times changed and customs shifted, the script altered too: seal forms grew corrupt and clerical writing lost its integrity.
entries.literal: As the age changed and customs shifted, writing altered; seal forms went awry and clerical bodies lost their truth.

entries.zh: 俗學鄙習，復加虛造。
entries.en: Shallow scholarship and vulgar habit piled invention upon invention.
entries.literal: Vulgar learning and base habit further added fictitious invention.

entries.zh: 巧談辯士，以意為疑，炫惑于時，難以厘改。
entries.en: Clever talkers and debaters, treating private fancy as grounds for doubt, dazzled their contemporaries and made correction nearly impossible.
entries.literal: Clever talkers and debaters, taking their own whims as grounds for doubt, dazzled and misled the age, and correction was hard to achieve.

entries.zh: 乃曰：追來為歸，巧言為辯，小免為< 需免>，神嵒為蠶。
entries.en: They would say that zhui (follow) stood for gui (return), qiaoyan (clever speech) for bian (debate), xiaomian (small hare) for xumian, and shenyan (divine cliff) for can (silkworm).
entries.literal: They would say: "follow" was written for "return," "clever speech" for "debate," "small hare" for "need hare," and "divine cliff" for "silkworm."

entries.zh: 如斯甚眾，皆不合孔氏古書、史籀《大篆》、許氏《說文》、《石經》三字也。
entries.en: Such cases were legion, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient texts, Scribe Zhou's Great Seal, Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs, or the three-script stone classic.
entries.literal: Cases like these were extremely numerous, and none accorded with the Kong family's ancient books, Scribe Zhou's *Great Seal*, Xu Shen's *Explaining Graphs*, or the three-script stone classic.

entries.zh: 凡所關古，莫不惆悵焉。
entries.en: Every matter touching the ancient script filled the heart with sorrow.
entries.literal: Everything touching antiquity filled one with sorrow.

entries.zh: 嗟夫！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 文字者六籍之宗，王教之始，前人所以垂今，今人所以識古。
entries.en: Writing is the root of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal instruction: through it the ancients handed down the past to the present, and the present learns to know antiquity.
entries.literal: Writing is the ancestor of the Six Classics and the beginning of royal teaching; by it the men of old handed down to the present, and the men of today recognize antiquity.

entries.zh: 游雅 高閭 趙逸 胡叟 胡方回 張湛 段承根 闞駰 劉延明 趙柔 索敞 宋繇 江式
entries.en: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, and Jiang Shi
entries.literal: You Ya, Gao Lu, Zhao Yi, Hu Sou, Hu Fanghui, Zhang Zhan, Duan Chenggen, Kang Yin, Liu Yanming, Zhao Rou, Sou Chang, Song Yao, Jiang Shi

entries.zh: 先是，齊寇數入，人廢耕桑，前後刺史，莫能防扞。
entries.en: Northern Qi raiders had repeatedly invaded the region, driving the people from their fields; none of Bao's predecessors had been able to stop them.
entries.literal: Before this, Qi raiders had repeatedly entered; the people abandoned farming and sericulture; successive governors could not defend against them.

entries.zh: 褒至，適會寇來，乃不下屬縣。
entries.en: Shortly after Bao took office, raiders struck again—but he did not warn the subordinate counties.
entries.literal: When Bao arrived, it happened that raiders came; he did not alert the subordinate counties.

entries.zh: 人既不備，以故多被抄掠。
entries.en: Caught unprepared, many were robbed.
entries.literal: Since the people were unprepared, for this reason many were plundered.

entries.zh: 齊人喜於不覺，以為州先未集兵，今還必不能追躡，由是益懈，不為營壘。
entries.en: The Qi troops, pleased that no alarm had been raised, assumed the province had no forces ready and that no pursuit would follow. They grew careless and made no fortified camp.
entries.literal: The Qi men were pleased at not being detected; they thought the province had not yet gathered troops before, and on returning now surely could not pursue—thereby they grew more slack and did not build camps.

entries.zh: 褒已先勒精銳，伏北山中，分據險阻，邀其歸路。
entries.en: Bao had already positioned his best troops in ambush in the northern mountains, holding the defiles along the raiders' line of retreat.
entries.literal: Bao had already beforehand mustered elite troops, hidden them in the northern mountains, divided and held the dangerous passes, and blocked their return route.

entries.zh: 乘其眾怠，縱伏擊之，盡獲其眾。
entries.en: When the enemy relaxed their guard, he sprang the ambush and captured the entire raiding party.
entries.literal: Taking advantage of their troops' slackness, he released the ambush and struck them, capturing their entire force.

entries.zh: 故事，獲生口者，並送京師，褒因是奏曰：「所獲賊眾，不足為多，俘而辱之，但益其忿耳。
entries.en: By custom all captives were sent to the capital. Bao memorialized the throne: "These prisoners are too few to matter; holding and humiliating them will only deepen their hatred.
entries.literal: By precedent, captives taken alive were all sent to the capital; Bao therefore memorialized: "The bandit force captured is not large enough to matter; to hold them captive and humiliate them only increases their rage.

entries.zh: 請一切放還，以德報怨。」
entries.en: I beg that they all be released, so that we may repay enmity with kindness."
entries.literal: I ask that they all be released and that enmity be answered with virtue."

entries.zh: 有詔許焉。
entries.en: The emperor approved his request.
entries.literal: An edict approved this.

entries.zh: 自此抄兵頗息，遷河州總管，仍轉鳳州刺史。
entries.en: Raids largely ceased after this. He was appointed commander of He Province and later transferred to governor of Feng.
entries.literal: From this raiding troops largely ceased; he was transferred to commander of He Province, then turned to governor of Feng Province.

entries.zh: 尋以年老請致事，詔許之。
entries.en: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of age, and the emperor granted his request.
entries.literal: Soon, on account of age, he requested retirement; an edict granted it.

entries.zh: 天和五年，拜少保。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Tianhe era he was appointed junior mentor to the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe he was appointed junior mentor.

entries.zh: 褒曆事三帝，以忠厚見知。
entries.en: Bao served three emperors and was esteemed for his loyalty and integrity.
entries.literal: Bao served through three emperors and was known for loyalty and honesty.

entries.zh: 武帝深相敬重，常以師道處之，每入朝見，必有詔令坐，然始論政事。
entries.en: Emperor Wu held him in the highest regard and always treated him as a teacher. Whenever Bao came to court, the emperor would order him seated before any business was discussed.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu deeply respected him, constantly treating him with the ceremony due a teacher; each time he entered court for audience there was always an edict ordering him to be seated before political matters were discussed.

entries.zh: 卒，贈涇、岐、燕三州刺史，諡曰貞。
entries.en: When he died, he was posthumously honored with the titles of governor of Jing, Qi, and Yan provinces, and given the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).
entries.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the three provincial governorships of Jing, Qi, and Yan; his posthumous name was Zhen.

entries.zh: 保定二年，為小吏部。
entries.en: In the second year of Baoding (562), he was made junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he served as junior director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 時益州殷阜，軍國所資，經途艱險，每苦劫盜。
entries.en: Yizhou was then rich and fertile—the source of supplies for army and state—but the transport routes were treacherous and brigands were a constant scourge.
entries.literal: At that time Yizhou was prosperous and fertile, providing resources for army and state; the routes were perilous, and banditry was a constant affliction.

entries.zh: 詔昂使于益、梁，軍人之務皆委決焉。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Ang to Yi and Liang provinces; all military matters there were placed entirely in his hands.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Ang to go as envoy to Yi and Liang; all military affairs were entrusted to his judgment.

entries.zh: 昂撫導荒梗，頗得寧靜。
entries.en: Ang soothed and guided the wild borderlands until a measure of peace was restored.
entries.literal: Ang pacified and guided the rugged frontier regions, achieving considerable tranquility.

entries.zh: 天和初，陸騰討信州蠻，詔昂便於通、渠等州運糧饋之。
entries.en: Early in the Tianhe era (566), when Lu Teng marched against the Xinxhou tribes, the court ordered Ang to haul grain from Tong, Qu, and neighboring provinces to feed the campaign.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, Lu Teng campaigned against the Man of Xinxhou; an edict ordered Ang to transport grain from Tong, Qu, and other provinces to supply him.

entries.zh: 時臨、信、楚、合等諸州人庶多從逆，昂諭以禍福，赴者如歸。
entries.en: Many people in Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces had joined the rebels, but when Ang reasoned with them about reward and ruin, they flocked to him as gladly as men returning home.
entries.literal: At that time the common people of Lin, Xin, Chu, He, and other provinces largely followed the rebels. Ang instructed them regarding fortune and disaster, and those who came to him did so as if returning home.

entries.zh: 乃令老弱負糧，壯夫拒戰，莫有怨者。
entries.en: He put the old and weak to carrying grain and the able-bodied men to fighting—and not one man murmured against it.
entries.literal: He then ordered the old and weak to carry grain and the strong men to resist in battle; none complained.

entries.zh: 使還，屬巴州萬榮郡人反叛，圍郡城，昂於是遂募通、開二州，得三千人，倍道兼行，出其不意。
entries.en: On his way back, the people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rose in revolt and besieged the commandery seat. Ang promptly raised three thousand men from Tong and Kai, forced a double-time march, and fell upon the rebels before they expected it.
entries.literal: When his mission ended and he was returning, people of Wanrong Commandery in Bazhou rebelled and besieged the commandery city. Ang thereupon recruited from Tong and Kai provinces, obtaining three thousand men, marched at double speed day and night, and struck unexpectedly.

entries.zh: 又令其眾皆作中國歌，直趣賊壘。
entries.en: He also had his men sing Chinese songs as they marched straight for the rebel stronghold.
entries.literal: He also ordered his troops all to sing songs of China and go straight toward the rebel camp.

entries.zh: 謂有大軍赴救，望風瓦解。
entries.en: Believing a large relief force was at hand, the rebels broke apart at the first sign of them.
entries.literal: Thinking a great army was coming to the rescue, the rebels dispersed at the mere sight of them.

entries.zh: 朝廷嘉其權以濟事，詔梁州總管、杞國公亮即於軍中賞昂奴婢二十口，繒彩四百匹。
entries.en: The court applauded his resourcefulness in bringing the affair to success and ordered Liangzhou's regional commander, Duke Liang of Qi, to reward Ang on the spot with twenty household slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: The court praised his expedient measures for achieving the task; an edict ordered Liang Province regional commander, Duke of Qi State Liang, to reward Ang in camp with twenty slaves and four hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 又以昂威信布于宕梁，遂表為渠州刺史。
entries.en: Since Ang's authority and credibility now reached throughout Dangliang, the court memorialized him for appointment as governor of Qu Province.
entries.literal: Because Ang's prestige and trust had spread through Dangliang, he was memorialized for appointment as governor of Qu Province.

entries.zh: 轉通州。
entries.en: He was transferred to Tong Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Tong Province.

entries.zh: 推誠布信，甚得夷獠歡心。
entries.en: By treating them with open sincerity and steadfast trust, he won the deep loyalty of the tribal peoples.
entries.literal: He extended sincerity and spread good faith, greatly winning the hearts of the Yi and Liao peoples.

entries.zh: 秩滿還京，首領皆隨昂詣闕朝覲。
entries.en: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs accompanied him to court for an imperial audience.
entries.literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, tribal chiefs all followed Ang to the palace to pay court audience.

entries.zh: 以昂化洽夷落，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: In recognition of his civilizing work among the frontier tribes, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with the privilege of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Because Ang's transforming influence had reached the barbarian settlements, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Commissioner with the Same Privileges as a Three-in-One Grand Officer.

entries.zh: 時晉公護執政，昂稍被護親待，武帝頗銜之。
entries.en: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held the reins of government, and Ang gradually won Hu's personal favor—a fact that Emperor Wu took rather badly.
entries.literal: At that time Duke of Jin Hu held power; Ang came gradually to enjoy Hu's intimate favor, and Emperor Wu harbored considerable resentment.

entries.zh: 及誅護，加之捶楚，因此遂卒。
entries.en: When Hu was put to death, Ang was beaten and flogged as well and died from it.
entries.literal: When Hu was executed, Ang was subjected to beating and torture and thereby died.

entries.zh: 初，陳文帝弟安成王頊為質于梁，及江陵平，頊隨例遷長安。
entries.en: Earlier, Chen Emperor Wen's younger brother, Prince Xu of Ancheng, had been held as a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was moved to Chang'an with the other captives.
entries.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen of Chen's younger brother, Prince An Cheng Xu, had been a hostage in Liang; when Jiangling fell, Xu was transferred to Chang'an along with the others.

entries.zh: 陳人請之，周文帝許而未遣。
entries.en: Chen asked for his return; Northern Zhou Emperor Wen agreed in principle but did not yet release him.
entries.literal: The Chen side requested his return; Emperor Wen of Zhou agreed but did not yet send him back.

entries.zh: 至是，帝欲歸之，命杲使焉。
entries.en: On this occasion the emperor decided to send Xu home and dispatched Guo as envoy.
entries.literal: At this time the emperor wished to return him and ordered Guo to go as envoy.

entries.zh: 陳文帝大悅，即遣使報聘，並賂黔中數州地，仍請畫野分疆，永敦鄰好。
entries.en: Chen Emperor Wen was delighted, promptly sent envoys in return, offered several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and asked that borders be drawn so that good relations might endure.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was greatly pleased, immediately sent envoys in return, ceded several prefectures in Qianzhong as a gift, and further requested demarcation of borders to cement neighborly friendship forever.

entries.zh: 以杲奉使稱旨，進授都督，行小禦伯，更往分界。
entries.en: Because Guo's embassy had fully satisfied the throne, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron and sent back to settle the frontier.
entries.literal: Because Guo's mission accorded with the imperial intent, he was promoted to regional commander and acting Junior Defender Baron, and sent again to demarcate the border.

entries.zh: 陳於是歸魯山郡。
entries.en: Chen thereupon restored Lushan Commandery.
entries.literal: Chen thereupon returned Lushan Commandery.

entries.zh: 帝乃拜頊柱國大將軍，詔杲送之還國。
entries.en: The Zhou emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him home.
entries.literal: The emperor then enfeoffed Xu as Pillar General and ordered Guo to escort him back to his country.

entries.zh: 陳文帝謂杲曰：「家弟今蒙禮遣，實是周朝之惠。
entries.en: Chen Emperor Wen said to Guo: "My brother has now been honorably sent home—a genuine kindness from your court.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen said to Guo: "My younger brother has now received the courtesy of being sent home—this is truly a kindness from the Zhou court.

entries.zh: 然不還魯山，亦恐未能及此。」
entries.en: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I doubt this would have been possible".
entries.literal: Yet had Lushan not been returned, I fear this might not have been possible."

entries.zh: 杲答曰：「安成之在關中，乃咸陽一布衣耳。
entries.en: Guo replied: "When Prince Xu of Ancheng was in Guanzhong, he was no more than a commoner of Xianyang in plain cloth.
entries.literal: Guo replied: "When Prince An Cheng was in the Guanzhong region, he was no more than a common cloth-clad man of Xianyang.

entries.zh: 然是陳之介弟，其價豈止一城？
entries.en: Yet he is Chen's own brother—is his worth no more than one walled town?
entries.literal: Yet he is Chen's honored younger brother—is his worth limited to a single city?

entries.zh: 本朝親睦九族，恕己及物，上遵太祖遺旨，下思繼好之義，所以發德音者，蓋為此也。
entries.en: Our court cherishes kinship through the nine degrees of relation, extends forbearance from oneself to others, honors above the founding emperor's testament and below the duty of lasting friendship—that is why this gracious decree was issued.
entries.literal: Our court cherishes the nine degrees of kinship, extends forbearance from oneself to others, above observes the founding emperor's testament, below honors the duty of continuing friendly relations—the reason for issuing this gracious decree is precisely this.

entries.zh: 若知止侔魯山，固當不貪一鎮。
entries.en: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not covet a single commandery.
entries.literal: If Prince Xu were worth no more than Lushan, we would certainly not be greedy for one commandery.

entries.zh: 況魯山梁之舊地，梁即本朝籓臣，若以始末言之，魯山自合歸國。
entries.en: Moreover Lushan was former Liang territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal; judged by the whole course of events, Lushan ought by rights to have returned to us.
entries.literal: Moreover Lushan was Liang's former territory, and Liang was itself our court's vassal—in light of the whole history, Lushan ought by rights to return to our state.

entries.zh: 雲以尋常之土，易已骨肉之親，使臣猶謂不可，何以聞諸朝廷！」
entries.en: To propose trading ordinary soil for one's own flesh and blood—even I find that impossible; how could I report such a thing to my court"!
entries.literal: To speak of trading ordinary land for one's own kin—even your envoy finds it impossible; how could I report such a thing to our court!"

entries.zh: 陳文帝慚恧久之，乃曰：「前言戲之耳！」
entries.en: Chen Emperor Wen was abashed for some time, then said: "What I said before was only in jest"!
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Chen was ashamed for a long while, then said: "My earlier words were spoken in jest!"

entries.zh: 自是接遇有加常禮。
entries.en: From then on he treated Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.
entries.literal: From then on he received Guo with honors beyond the usual protocol.

entries.zh: 及還，引升殿，親降御座，執手以別。
entries.en: When Guo was leaving, the emperor led him into the hall, came down from the throne in person, and clasped his hand in farewell.
entries.literal: When Guo was about to return, the emperor led him up to the hall, personally descended from the imperial seat, and clasped his hand in farewell.

entries.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授大都督、小載師下大夫，行小納言，復聘于陳。
entries.en: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, and acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another embassy to Chen.
entries.literal: The Zhou court commended him, appointing him Grand Regional Commander, junior grand master under the Master of Carriages, acting Junior Remonstrator, and sent him on another mission to Chen.

entries.zh: 及華皎來附，詔令衛公直、都督元定等援之。
entries.en: When Hua Jiao defected to Zhou, an edict ordered Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei, Regional Commander Yuan Ding, and others to go to his aid.
entries.literal: When Hua Jiao came over to submit, an edict ordered Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi, regional commander Yuan Ding, and others to support him.

entries.zh: 定等並沒。
entries.en: Ding and his men were wiped out.
entries.literal: Ding and the others were all lost.

entries.zh: 自是連兵不息，東南搔動。
entries.en: From then on the fighting never let up, and the southeast was in turmoil.
entries.literal: From then on fighting continued without pause and the southeast was unsettled.

entries.zh: 武帝授杲禦正中大夫，使陳，論保境息人之意。
entries.en: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to propose securing the borders and giving the people peace.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Guo Chief Straightening Grand Master and sent him to Chen to discuss the idea of securing borders and giving the people rest.

entries.zh: 陳宣帝遣其黃門侍郎徐陵謂杲曰：「兩國通好，彼朝受我叛人，何也？」
entries.en: Chen Emperor Xuan sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Xu Ling, to say to Guo: "Our two states are at peace—why does your court take in our deserters"?
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen sent his Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Xu Ling to say to Guo: "Our two states are on friendly terms—why does your court accept our defectors?"

entries.zh: 杲曰：「陳主昔在本朝，非慕義而至，主上授以柱國，位極人臣，子女玉帛，備禮將送，今主社稷，孰謂非恩？
entries.en: Guo said: "Your ruler once lived at our court—not because he admired our righteousness; our sovereign made him a Pillar of State, raised him to the highest rank, and sent him home with sons, daughters, jade, and silks in full ceremony. Now he sits upon the Chen throne—who would call that anything but grace?
entries.literal: Guo said: "The Chen ruler once dwelt in our court—not because he admired our righteousness did he come; our sovereign enfeoffed him as Pillar of State, raised him to the utmost rank, and sent him off with full ceremony of sons, daughters, jade, and silks. Now he rules his realm—who would say this is not grace?

entries.zh: 郝烈之徒，邊人狂狡，曾未報德，而先納之。
entries.en: Men like Hao Lie were wild, cunning border folk who had never repaid a kindness, yet you took them in first.
entries.literal: The likes of Hao Lie were wild and cunning border folk who had never repaid kindness, yet you took them in first.

entries.zh: 今受華氏，正是相報。
entries.en: Our acceptance of the Hua clan is simply repayment in kind.
entries.literal: Now that we accept the Hua clan, it is precisely repayment in kind.

entries.zh: 過自彼始，豈在本朝！」
entries.en: The offense began on your side—how can the fault be ours"!
entries.literal: The offense began on your side—how can it be laid at our court's door!"

entries.zh: 陵曰：「彼納華皎，志圖吞噬。
entries.en: Ling said: "In taking Hua Jiao, your court aims at swallowing us whole.
entries.literal: Ling said: "In accepting Hua Jiao, your side aims at swallowing us whole.

entries.zh: 此受郝烈。
entries.en: In this case we took in Hao Lie.
entries.literal: In this matter we accepted Hao Lie.

entries.zh: 容之而已。
entries.en: We merely gave him shelter—that is all.
entries.literal: We merely harbored him, that is all.

entries.zh: 且華皎方州列將。
entries.en: Moreover Hua Jiao was a frontier commander and a ranked general.
entries.literal: Moreover Hua Jiao was a regional commander and ranked general.

entries.zh: 竊邑叛亡。
entries.en: He seized his command and fled in rebellion.
entries.literal: He seized a city and rebelled in flight.

entries.zh: 郝烈一百許戶，脫身逃竄。
entries.en: Hao Lie was no more than a hundred-odd households who slipped away in flight.
entries.literal: Hao Lie was a mere hundred or so households who slipped away in escape.

entries.zh: 大小有異，豈得同年而語乎？」
entries.en: The cases differ in scale—how can they be mentioned in the same breath"?
entries.literal: The scale differs—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?"

entries.zh: 杲曰：「大小雖殊，受降一也。
entries.en: Guo said: "Great or small, the principle of accepting surrender is the same.
entries.literal: Guo said: "Though the scale differs, accepting surrender is the same principle.

entries.zh: 若論先後，本朝無失。」
entries.en: If we speak of who acted first, our court was not in the wrong".
entries.literal: If we speak of sequence, our court was not in the wrong."

entries.zh: 陵曰：「周朝送主上還國，既以為恩，衛公共元定度江，孰云非怨？
entries.en: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home and call that kindness; Duke Yuwen Zhi of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not cause for grievance?
entries.literal: Ling said: "Your Zhou court sent our ruler home—you call that kindness; Duke of Wei and Yuan Ding crossed the Yangtze—is that not grounds for grievance?

entries.zh: 計恩與怨，亦足相埒。」
entries.en: Set kindness against grievance, and the two are enough to cancel each other out".
entries.literal: Counting kindness against grievance, they are sufficient to balance each other."

entries.zh: 杲曰：「元定等軍敗身囚，其怨已滅。
entries.en: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and his men were defeated and taken prisoner—the grievance from that is already spent.
entries.literal: Guo said: "Yuan Ding and the others were defeated and taken captive—their grievance is already extinguished.

entries.zh: 陳主負扆馮玉，其恩猶在。
entries.en: Your ruler sits upon the throne with the jade screen before him—the grace you received still stands.
entries.literal: The Chen ruler sits upon the throne with jade before him—your grace still stands.

entries.zh: 且怨由彼國，恩起本朝，以怨酬恩，未之聞也。」
entries.en: Moreover the grievance came from your state and the grace from ours—to answer grace with grievance is something I have never heard of".
entries.literal: Moreover the grievance arose from your state and the grace from ours—to repay grace with grievance—is unheard of."

entries.zh: 陵笑而不答。
entries.en: Ling smiled and said nothing.
entries.literal: Ling smiled and did not reply.

entries.zh: 杲因陳和通之便，陵具以聞。
entries.en: Seizing the opening to discuss peace, Guo pressed his case, and Ling reported the whole exchange to his sovereign.
entries.literal: Guo took advantage of the opportunity to discuss peace, and Ling reported everything to his sovereign.

entries.zh: 陳宣許之，遂遣使來聘。
entries.en: Chen Emperor Xuan agreed and thereupon sent envoys on a formal visit.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen agreed and thereupon sent envoys to pay a court visit.

entries.zh: 劉璠，字寶義，沛人也。
entries.en: Liu Fan, whose style name was Baoyi, came from Pei.
entries.literal: Liu Fan, style name Baoyi, was a native of Pei.

entries.zh: 六世祖敏，以永嘉亂，徙居廣陵。
entries.en: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, fleeing the chaos of the Yongjia era, moved the family to Guangling.
entries.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Min, because of the Yongjia chaos, moved to settle in Guangling.

entries.zh: 父臧，性方正，篤志好學，居家以孝聞。
entries.en: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted to learning, and renowned at home for filial conduct.
entries.literal: His father Zang was upright in character, devoted in will and fond of learning, and at home was known for filial conduct.

entries.zh: 仕梁，為著作郎。
entries.en: Under Liang he served as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He served Liang as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 璠九歲而孤，居喪合禮。
entries.en: Fan lost his father at nine and observed mourning in full accordance with ritual.
entries.literal: Fan at nine years lost his father and observed mourning in accordance with ritual.

entries.zh: 少好讀書，兼善文筆。
entries.en: From youth he loved books and was also skilled with the brush.
entries.literal: In youth he loved reading and was also skilled in literary composition.

entries.zh: 十七，為上黃侯蕭曄所器重。
entries.en: At seventeen he won the deep esteem of the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.
entries.literal: At seventeen he was deeply valued by the Marquis of Shanghuang, Xiao Ye.

entries.zh: 范陽張綰，梁之外戚，才高口辯，見推於世。
entries.en: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, a Liang imperial in-law, was talented and eloquent and widely admired.
entries.literal: Zhang Wan of Fanyang, an in-law of Liang, was talented and eloquent and was praised by the age.

entries.zh: 以曄懿貴，亦假借之。
entries.en: Because Ye was of high rank and noble birth, Wan also relied on his patronage.
entries.literal: Because Ye was honored and noble, Wan also leaned on him.

entries.zh: 璠年少未仕，而負才使氣，不為之屈。
entries.en: Fan was still young and had not yet entered office, yet trusting in his talent and proud in spirit, he would not defer to Wan.
entries.literal: Fan was young and had not yet taken office, yet relied on his talent and was proud in spirit, and would not yield to Wan.

entries.zh: 綰嘗于新渝侯宅，因酒後詬京兆杜杲曰：「寒士不遜。」
entries.en: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after drinking, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao: "A poor scholar knows no deference".
entries.literal: Once at the residence of the Marquis of Xinyu, Wan, after wine, reviled Du Gao of Jingzhao, saying: "A poor scholar shows no deference".

entries.zh: 璠厲色曰：「此坐誰非寒士？」
entries.en: Fan said sharply, "Who at this table is not a poor scholar?"
entries.literal: Fan said sternly: "Who at this gathering is not a poor scholar?"

entries.zh: 璠本意在綰，而曄以為屬己，辭色不平。
entries.en: Fan's remark was really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought it was meant for him and showed his displeasure.
entries.literal: Fan's words were really aimed at Wan, but Ye thought they were directed at himself and showed displeasure in face and speech.

entries.zh: 璠曰：「何王之門不可曳長裾也！」
entries.en: Fan said, "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!
entries.literal: Fan said: "Under whose gate may one not trail a long robe"!

entries.zh: 遂拂衣而去。
entries.en: With that he shook out his robes and walked away.
entries.literal: Then he shook out his robes and left.

entries.zh: 曄謝之，乃止。
entries.en: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan relent.
entries.literal: Ye apologized, and only then did Fan stop.

entries.zh: 後隨曄在淮南。
entries.en: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.
entries.literal: Later he followed Ye to Huainan.

entries.zh: 璠母在建康遘疾，璠弗之知。
entries.en: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, but Fan knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Fan's mother fell ill in Jiankang, and Fan did not know of it.

entries.zh: 嘗忽一日舉身楚痛，尋而家信至，雲其母病。
entries.en: One day his whole body was suddenly racked with pain; soon afterward a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.
entries.literal: Suddenly one day his whole body was racked with pain; soon a letter from home arrived saying his mother was ill.

entries.zh: 璠即號泣戒道，絕而又蘇。
entries.en: Fan at once wailed and set out on the road; he stopped breathing and revived.
entries.literal: Fan at once wailed and prepared to travel; he stopped breathing and revived.

entries.zh: 當身痛之辰，即母死之日。
entries.en: The day his body was racked with pain was exactly the day his mother died.
entries.literal: The day his body was in pain was exactly the day his mother died.

entries.zh: 居喪毀瘠，遂感風氣，服闋後一年，猶杖而後起。
entries.en: In mourning he wasted away and then contracted a wind ailment; even a year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff to rise.
entries.literal: In mourning he wasted away; he then contracted wind illness, and a full year after the mourning period ended he still needed a staff before he could rise.

entries.zh: 及曄終於毗陵，故吏多分散，璠獨奉曄喪還都，墳成乃退。
entries.en: When Ye died at Piling, many of his former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted the coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was finished.
entries.literal: When Ye died at Piling, many former subordinates scattered, but Fan alone escorted Ye's coffin back to the capital and withdrew only after the tomb was completed.

entries.zh: 梁簡文暼寺在東宮，遇曄素重，諸不送者多被劾責，唯璠獨被優嘗賞。
entries.en: When Jianwen of Liang was crown prince at the Eastern Palace, Ye had long been held in high esteem, and many who failed to attend his funeral were impeached and punished; Fan alone received special commendation and reward.
entries.literal: When Jianwen of Liang was at the Eastern Palace, since Ye had long been held in esteem, many who did not attend the funeral were impeached and punished, but Fan alone received special commendation and reward.

entries.zh: 解褐王國常侍，非其好也。
entries.en: On first taking office he became Regular Attendant of a princely domain, a post that did not suit him.
entries.literal: On first appointment he became Regular Attendant of the princely domain, which was not to his liking.

entries.zh: 璠少慷慨，好功名，志欲立事邊城，不樂隨牒平進。
entries.en: From youth Fan was generous and hungered for fame and achievement; he wished to make his mark on the frontier and took no pleasure in routine promotion.
entries.literal: Fan from youth was generous and fond of fame and merit, resolved to achieve deeds on the frontier, and did not delight in advancing step by step through routine appointments.

entries.zh: 曾宜豐侯蕭脩出為北徐州刺史，即請為其輕車府主簿，兼記室參軍。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, was appointed Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.
entries.literal: Once when the Marquis of Yifeng, Xiao Xiu, went out as Governor of Northern Xu Province, Fan at once asked to serve as Master of Records in his Light Chariot Office and concurrently as Recording Army Adjutant.

entries.zh: 脩為梁州，又板為中記室，補華陽太守。
entries.en: When Xiu became Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and made Administrator of Huayang.
entries.literal: When Xiu was made Governor of Liang Province, Fan was again appointed by written commission as Senior Master of Records and supplemented as Administrator of Huayang.

entries.zh: 屬侯景度江，梁室大亂，脩以璠有才略，甚親委之。
entries.en: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into chaos, Xiu, recognizing Fan's talent and strategic mind, entrusted him with great confidence.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze and the Liang court fell into great disorder, Xiu, because Fan had talent and strategy, entrusted him with great intimacy.

entries.zh: 時寇難繁興，未有所定，璠乃喟然賦詩以見志。
entries.en: Raids and troubles arose on every side and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to declare his resolve.
entries.literal: At that time raids and troubles arose in profusion and nothing was settled; Fan sighed and composed a poem to express his resolve.

entries.zh: 其末章曰：「隨會平王室，夷吾匡霸功。
entries.en: Its final stanza reads: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.
entries.literal: Its final stanza says: "Sui Hui stabilized the royal house; Guan Zhong restored hegemony.

entries.zh: 虛薄而時用，徒然慕昔風。」
entries.en: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the heroes of old".
entries.literal: I am slight in talent yet used by the times; in vain I admire the winds of old".

entries.zh: 脩開府，置佐史，以璠為諮議參軍，仍領記室。
entries.en: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and appointed aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.
entries.literal: When Xiu opened a princely headquarters and established aides and clerks, he made Fan Consulting Army Adjutant and still head of the secretariat.

entries.zh: 梁元帝承制，授樹功將軍、鎮西府諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional authority, Fan was appointed General Who Establishes Merit and Consulting Army Adjutant of the Pacifying West Headquarters.

entries.zh: 賜書曰：「鄧禹文學，尚或執戈；
entries.en: An imperial letter said, "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;
entries.literal: An imperial letter said: "Deng Yu was a man of letters, yet still took up arms;

entries.zh: 葛洪書生，且雲破賊。
entries.en: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.
entries.literal: Ge Hong was a scholar, and yet it is said he broke bandits.

entries.zh: 前修無遠，屬望良深。」
entries.en: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you run very deep".
entries.literal: The ancients are not far off; my hopes for you are deep indeed".

entries.zh: 元帝尋以脩紹鄱陽之封，且為雍州刺史，復以璠為為脩平北府司馬。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan soon had Xiu succeed to the fief of Poyang and also made him Governor of Yong Province, and again appointed Fan as Chief of Staff of Xiu's Pacifying North Headquarters.

entries.zh: 及武陵王紀稱制於蜀，以璠為中書侍郎。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, declared himself emperor in Shu, he made Fan Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 遣召璠，使者八反，乃至蜀。
entries.en: Ji sent to summon Fan; the envoy returned eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.
entries.literal: He sent to summon Fan; the envoy came back eight times before Fan finally reached Shu.

entries.zh: 又以為黃門侍郎，令長史劉孝勝深布心腹，使工畫《陳平度河歸漢圖》以遺之。
entries.en: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted agents deeply; he also had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" and sent it to Fan as a gift.
entries.literal: He again made Fan Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and ordered Chief Clerk Liu Xiaosheng to plant trusted men deeply and had an artist paint "Chen Ping Crossing the River to Return to Han" as a gift to him.

entries.zh: 璠苦求還，中記室韋登私曰：「殿下忍而蓄憾，足下不留，將致大禍。
entries.en: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately, "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will follow. If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine?
entries.literal: Fan bitterly begged to return. Senior Master of Records Wei Deng said privately: "The Prince broods and harbors resentment; if you do not stay, great disaster will come. If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished. Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine?

entries.zh: 脫使盜遮於葭萌，則卿殆矣。
entries.en: If robbers waylay you at Jiameng, you are finished.
entries.literal: If bandits waylay you at Jiameng, you will be finished.

entries.zh: 孰若共構大廈，使身名俱美哉！」
entries.en: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let your person and your name both shine"?
entries.literal: Would it not be better to build the great house together and let body and name both shine"?

entries.zh: 璠正色曰：「卿欲緩頰於我邪？
entries.en: Fan said sternly, "Do you wish to soften my resolve?
entries.literal: Fan said sternly: "Do you wish to soften my resolve?

entries.zh: 我與府侯分義已定，豈以寵辱夷險易其心乎！
entries.en: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?
entries.literal: My bond with the Prince is already fixed in duty; how could favor and disgrace, ease and danger, change my heart?

entries.zh: 丈夫立志，當死生以之耳。
entries.en: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.
entries.literal: A man who sets his will should hold to it through life and death.

entries.zh: 殿下方布大義於天下，終不逞志於一人。」
entries.en: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."
entries.literal: Your Highness is now spreading great righteousness throughout the realm; in the end he will not indulge his whim against one man."

entries.zh: 紀知不為己用，乃厚贈而遣之。
entries.en: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.
entries.literal: Ji knew Fan would not serve his purposes, so he gave him rich gifts and sent him away.

entries.zh: 臨別，紀又解其佩刀贈璠曰：「想見物思人。」
entries.en: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying, "When you see this object, think of the man".
entries.literal: At parting Ji again unfastened his girdle knife and gave it to Fan, saying: "When you see this object, think of the man".

entries.zh: 璠曰：「敢不奉揚威靈，克翦奸宄。」
entries.en: Fan said, "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"
entries.literal: Fan said: "How dare I fail to carry forth your authority and cut down traitors and rebels?"

entries.zh: 紀於是遣使拜脩為益州刺史，封隨郡王，以璠為府長史，加蜀郡太守。
entries.en: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.
entries.literal: Ji thereupon sent an envoy to appoint Xiu Governor of Yi Province, enfeoff him as Prince of Suichun, and make Fan Chief of Staff and concurrently Administrator of Shu Commandery.

entries.zh: 還至白馬西，屬達奚武軍已至南鄭，璠不得入城，遂降武。
entries.en: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng; Fan could not enter the city and surrendered to Wu.
entries.literal: On returning west to White Horse, Daxi Wu's army had already reached Nanzheng, and Fan could not enter the city, so he surrendered to Wu.

entries.zh: 周文帝素聞其名，先戒武曰：「勿使劉璠死。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu: "Do not let Liu Fan die".
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou had long heard Fan's name and beforehand warned Wu, saying: "Do not let Liu Fan die".

entries.zh: 故武先令璠赴闕。
entries.en: Therefore Wu first sent Fan to the capital.
entries.literal: Therefore Wu first had Fan go to the capital.

entries.zh: 周文見之如舊，謂僕射申徽曰：「劉璠佳士，古人何以過之！」
entries.en: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui, "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!
entries.literal: Emperor Wen received him as of old and said to Vice Director Shen Hui: "Liu Fan is an excellent man—how did the ancients surpass him"!

entries.zh: 徽曰：「晉人滅吳，利在二陸。
entries.en: Hui said, "When the Jin destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.
entries.literal: Hui said: "When the Jin people destroyed Wu, the profit lay in the two Lus.

entries.zh: 明公今平梁漢，得劉璠也。」
entries.en: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."
entries.literal: Your lordship now pacifies Liang and Han and has gained Liu Fan."

entries.zh: 時南鄭尚拒守，達奚武請屠之，周文將許焉，唯令全脩一家而已。
entries.en: Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu asked to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.
entries.literal: At that time Nanzheng still held out in defense. Daxi Wu requested to slaughter the city; Emperor Wen was about to consent, ordering only that Xiu's household be spared.

entries.zh: 璠乃請之于朝，周文怒而不許也。
entries.en: Fan then pleaded at court, but Emperor Wen was angry and refused.
entries.literal: Fan then pleaded at court; Emperor Wen was angry and would not consent.

entries.zh: 璠泣而固請，移時不退。
entries.en: Fan wept and pleaded firmly, and for a long time would not withdraw.
entries.literal: Fan wept and firmly pleaded, and for a long time would not withdraw.

entries.zh: 柳仲禮侍側，曰：「此烈士也。」
entries.en: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said, "This is a man of heroic resolve".
entries.literal: Liu Zhongli, attending at his side, said: "This is a man of heroic resolve".

entries.zh: 周文既納蕭脩降，又許其反國。
entries.en: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen both accepted Xiao Xiu's surrender and promised that he might return to his state.

entries.zh: 脩至長安累月，未之遣也。
entries.en: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.
entries.literal: Xiu reached Chang'an and for months was not sent back.

entries.zh: 璠因侍宴，周文曰：「我于古誰比？」
entries.en: While attending a banquet, Fan was asked by Emperor Wen, "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?
entries.literal: Fan, while attending a banquet, was asked by Emperor Wen: "Among the ancients, to whom do you compare me"?

entries.zh: 曰：「常以公命世英主，湯、武莫逮。
entries.en: He said, "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.
entries.literal: He said: "I have always regarded Your Lordship as a hero of the age; even Tang and Wu could not match you.

entries.zh: 今日所見，曾是齊桓、晉文之不若。」
entries.en: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."
entries.literal: What I see today falls short even of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin."

entries.zh: 周文曰：「我不得比湯、武，望與伊、周為匹，何桓、文之不若乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to stand equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why should I fall short of Huan and Wen?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "I cannot compare with Tang and Wu; I hope to be the equal of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—why fall short of Huan and Wen?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「齊桓存三亡國，晉文不失信于伐原。」
entries.en: He replied, "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."
entries.literal: He replied: "Duke Huan of Qi preserved three extinguished states; Duke Wen of Jin did not break faith in the campaign against Yuan."

entries.zh: 語未終，周文撫掌曰：「我解爾意，欲激我耳。」
entries.en: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said, "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."
entries.literal: Before he finished speaking, Emperor Wen clapped his hands and said: "I understand your meaning—you wish to spur me on."

entries.zh: 即命遣脩。
entries.en: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.
entries.literal: He at once ordered Xiu sent back.

entries.zh: 脩請與璠俱還，周文不許。
entries.en: Xiu asked to return together with Fan, but Emperor Wen refused.
entries.literal: Xiu asked to return together with Fan; Emperor Wen would not consent.

entries.zh: 以璠為中外府記室，遷黃門侍郎、儀同三司。
entries.en: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.
entries.literal: Fan was made Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters, then promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate with the third rank of ceremonial parity.

entries.zh: 嘗臥疾居家，對雪興感，乃作《雪賦》以遂志焉。
entries.en: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.
entries.literal: Once, ill at home, he was moved by the sight of snow and composed the "Rhapsody on Snow" to express his resolve.

entries.zh: 初，蕭脩在漢中與蕭紀箋，及答西魏書、移襄陽文，皆璠辭也。
entries.en: When Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji, his replies to Western Wei, and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all written by Fan.
entries.literal: At first, when Xiao Xiu was in Hanzhong, his letters to Xiao Ji and his replies to Western Wei's letters and his proclamation to Xiangyang were all Fan's compositions.

entries.zh: 祥字休徵。
entries.en: Xiang, whose style name was Xiuzheng.
entries.literal: Xiang, style name Xiuzheng.

entries.zh: 幼聰慧，賓客見者皆號神童。
entries.en: From childhood he was clever and bright; every guest who saw him called him a prodigy.
entries.literal: From childhood he was clever and intelligent; all guests who saw him called him a divine child.

entries.zh: 事嫡母以至孝聞。
entries.en: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.
entries.literal: In serving his stepmother he was known for utmost filial devotion.

entries.zh: 其伯父黃門郎璆，有名江左，在嶺南，聞而奇之，乃令名祥字休徵。
entries.en: His father's elder brother Qiu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of the boy in Lingnan, he marveled and had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.
entries.literal: His father's elder brother, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Qiu, was famous east of the Yangtze; hearing of him in Lingnan, he marveled and therefore had him named Xiang with the style Xiuzheng.

entries.zh: 後以字行於世。
entries.en: Later he was known in the world by his style name.
entries.literal: Later he was known in the world by his style name.

entries.zh: 十歲能屬文，十二通《五經》。
entries.en: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he had mastered the Five Classics.
entries.literal: At ten he could compose prose; at twelve he mastered the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 仕梁，為宜豐侯記室參軍。
entries.en: Under Liang he served as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.
entries.literal: He served Liang as Recording Army Adjutant to the Marquis of Yifeng.

entries.zh: 江陵平，隨例入關中。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass with the other captives.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, he entered the pass according to precedent.

entries.zh: 齊公憲召為記室，府中書記皆令掌之。
entries.en: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.
entries.literal: Duke Yuwen Xian summoned him as Master of Records, and all documents in the princely headquarters were put under his charge.

entries.zh: 封漢安縣子。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Han'an.
