entries.zh: 憲進爵為王，以休徵為王友。
entries.en: When Xian was raised to princely rank, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.
entries.literal: When Xian advanced in rank to prince, Xiuzheng was made Friend of the Prince.

entries.zh: 俄除內史上士。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Senior Clerk of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 武帝東征，休徵陪侍帷幄，平齊露布即休徵文也。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was written by Xiuzheng.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned east, Xiuzheng attended him in the command tent; the victory bulletin on the pacification of Qi was Xiuzheng's composition.

entries.zh: 累遷車騎大將軍、儀同大將軍。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand General with the great rank of ceremonial parity.

entries.zh: 曆長安、萬年二縣令，頗獲時譽。
entries.en: He served in succession as magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.
entries.literal: He successively served as Magistrate of Chang'an and Wannian counties and won considerable praise in his time.

entries.zh: 卒於官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 初，璠所選《梁典》始就，未及刊定而卒，臨終謂休徵曰：「能成我志，其在此書乎！」
entries.en: The Liang Canon that Fan had compiled was just finished but not yet edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng, "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!
entries.literal: At first the Liang Canon that Fan compiled was just finished but had not yet been edited and published when he died; on his deathbed he told Xiuzheng: "To fulfill my wish—will it not lie in this book"!

entries.zh: 休徵修定繕寫。
entries.en: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.
entries.literal: Xiuzheng edited, corrected, and copied it.

entries.zh: 勒成一家，行於世。
entries.en: He brought it to completion as a work in its own right, and it circulated in his day.
entries.literal: He completed it as a work in its own right, and it circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 行本，璠兄子也。
entries.en: Xingben was the son of Fan's elder brother.
entries.literal: Xingben was Fan's elder brother's son.

entries.zh: 父環，仕梁，曆職清顯。
entries.en: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.
entries.literal: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.

entries.zh: 行本起家梁武陵王國常侍。
entries.en: Xingben first entered office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.
entries.literal: Xingben first took office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.

entries.zh: 遇蕭脩以梁州北附，遂與叔父璠歸周，寓居新豐。
entries.en: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and made his home in Xinfeng.
entries.literal: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he then returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and lodged in Xinfeng.

entries.zh: 每以諷讀為事，精力忘疲，雖衣食乏絕，晏如也。
entries.en: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, driving himself without fatigue; though food and clothing ran short, he remained perfectly at ease.
entries.literal: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, forgetting fatigue in his energy; though food and clothing were exhausted, he was perfectly at ease.

entries.zh: 性剛烈，有不可奪之志。
entries.en: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.
entries.literal: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.

entries.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室。
entries.en: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.
entries.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.

entries.zh: 武帝親總萬機，轉禦正中士，兼領起居注。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.

entries.zh: 累遷掌朝下大夫。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.

entries.zh: 周代故事，天子臨軒，掌朝典筆硯，持至御坐，則承禦大夫取進之。
entries.en: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, on reaching the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.
entries.literal: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, when he reached the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.

entries.zh: 及行本為掌朝，將進筆於帝，承禦復欲取之。
entries.en: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again tried to take it.
entries.literal: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again wished to take it.

entries.zh: 行本抗聲曰：「筆不可得。」
entries.en: Xingben said loudly, "The brush cannot be taken".
entries.literal: Xingben said loudly: "The brush cannot be taken".

entries.zh: 帝驚視問之，行本曰：「臣聞設官分職，各有司存。
entries.en: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said, "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.
entries.literal: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said: "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.

entries.zh: 臣既不得佩承禦刀，承禦亦焉得取臣筆？」
entries.en: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"
entries.literal: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「然。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "So it is."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is."

entries.zh: 因令二司各行所職。
entries.en: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.
entries.literal: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.

entries.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，多失德，行本切諫忤旨，出為河內太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.

entries.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，攻懷州，行本率吏人拒之，拜儀同，賜爵文安縣子。
entries.en: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was granted ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.
entries.literal: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was appointed with ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.

entries.zh: 拜太子左庶子，領書侍御史如故。
entries.en: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 皇太子虛襟敬憚。
entries.en: The Crown Prince treated him with open respect and restraint.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince opened his breast to him in respect and fear.

entries.zh: 時唐令則為左庶子，太子昵狎之，每令以弦歌教內人。
entries.en: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.
entries.literal: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.

entries.zh: 行本責之曰：「庶子當匡太子以正道，何嬖昵房帷之間哉！」
entries.en: Xingben reproached him, saying, "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!
entries.literal: Xingben reproached him, saying: "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!

entries.zh: 令則甚慚而不能改。
entries.en: Lingze was deeply ashamed but could not change.
entries.literal: Lingze was greatly ashamed but could not change.

entries.zh: 時沛國劉臻、平原明克讓、河南陸爽等並以文學為太子所親。
entries.en: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.

entries.zh: 行本怒其不能調護，每謂三人曰：「卿等正解讀書耳。」
entries.en: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect the prince, and often said to the three, "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".
entries.literal: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect him, and often said to the three: "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".

entries.zh: 時左術率長史夏侯福為太子所昵，嘗於閤內與太子戲。
entries.en: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.
entries.literal: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.

entries.zh: 福大笑，聲聞於外。
entries.en: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.
entries.literal: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.

entries.zh: 行本時在閤下聞之，待其出，數之曰：「汝何小人，敢為褻慢！」
entries.en: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he rebuked him, saying, "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!
entries.literal: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he counted his faults, saying: "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!

entries.zh: 因付執法者推之。
entries.en: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.
entries.literal: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.

entries.zh: 太子為請，乃釋之。
entries.en: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.

entries.zh: 太子嘗得良馬，令福乘而觀之。
entries.en: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.

entries.zh: 太子甚悅，因欲令行本復乘。
entries.en: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it as well.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it again.

entries.zh: 行本正色曰：「至尊置臣於庶子位，欲輔導殿下以正道，非為殿下作弄臣。」
entries.en: Xingben said sternly, "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".
entries.literal: Xingben said sternly: "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".

entries.zh: 太子慚而止。
entries.en: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.
entries.literal: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.

entries.zh: 復以本官領大興令，權貴憚其方正，無敢至其門者。
entries.en: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.
entries.literal: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.

entries.zh: 由是請托路絕，吏人懷之。
entries.en: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and commoners cherished him.
entries.literal: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and people cherished him.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒於官，上甚傷惜之。
entries.en: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned his loss.
entries.literal: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned and regretted it.

entries.zh: 及太子廢，上曰：「嗟乎！
entries.en: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said, "Alas!
entries.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said: "Alas!

entries.zh: 若使劉行本在，勇當不及此乎！」
entries.en: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!
entries.literal: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!

entries.zh: 行本無子。
entries.en: Xingben had no son.
entries.literal: Xingben had no son.

entries.zh: 韓襃 趙肅 張軌 李彥 郭彥 梁昕 皇甫璠 辛慶之 王子直 杜杲 呂思禮 徐招 檀翥 孟信 宗懍 劉璠 柳遐
entries.en: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, and Liu Xia
entries.literal: Han Bao, Zhao Su, Zhang Gui, Li Yan, Guo Yan, Liang Xin, Huang Fufan, Xing Qingzhi, Wang Zizhi, Du Gao, Lu Sili, Xu Zhao, Tan Zhu, Meng Xin, Zong Lin, Liu Fan, Liu Xia

entries.zh: 孫惠蔚，武邑武遂人也。
entries.en: Sun Huiwei was from Wusui in Wuyi.
entries.literal: Sun Huiwei was a man of Wusui in Wuyi.

entries.zh: 年十五，粗通《詩》、《書》及《孝經》、《論語》。
entries.en: At fifteen he had roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.
entries.literal: At fifteen he roughly mastered the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.

entries.zh: 十八，師董道季講《易》。
entries.en: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.
entries.literal: At eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji.

entries.zh: 十九，師程玄讀《禮經》及《春秋三傳》。
entries.en: At nineteen he studied the Rites and the three Spring and Autumn commentaries under Cheng Xuan.
entries.literal: At nineteen he studied the Book of Rites and the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn under Cheng Xuan.

entries.zh: 周流儒肆，有名于冀方。
entries.en: He traveled among Confucian schools and was renowned in Ji.
entries.literal: He traveled through Confucian academies and was famous in the Ji region.

entries.zh: 太和初，郡舉孝廉，對策於中書省。
entries.en: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he took the policy examination at the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In early Taihe his commandery recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he answered policy questions at the Directorate of Archives.

entries.zh: 時中書監高閭因相談薦，俄為中書博士，轉皇宗博士。
entries.en: Director Gao Lu recommended him after conversation; he soon became Secretariat Doctor, then Imperial Clan Doctor.
entries.literal: At that time Director Gao Lu because of conversation recommended him; soon he became Secretariat Doctor and was transferred to Imperial Clan Doctor.

entries.zh: 閭被敕理定雅樂，惠蔚參其事。
entries.en: Lu was ordered to arrange court music; Huiwei assisted.
entries.literal: Lu received an edict to arrange the elegant music; Huiwei participated in the affair.

entries.zh: 及樂成，閭上疏請集朝士于太樂，共研是非。
entries.en: When the music was finished, Lu asked court gentlemen to review it at the Grand Music Office.
entries.literal: When the music was completed, Lu submitted a memorial requesting court gentlemen assemble at the Grand Music Office to jointly investigate right and wrong.

entries.zh: 秘書令李彪，自以才辯，立難於其前。
entries.en: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his eloquence, challenged him.
entries.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his talent and eloquence, raised difficulties before him.

entries.zh: 閭命惠蔚與彪抗論，彪不能屈。
entries.en: Lu had Huiwei debate Biao, who could not prevail.
entries.literal: Lu ordered Huiwei to debate with Biao; Biao could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 黃門侍郎張彝，常與遊處，每表疏論事，多參訪焉。
entries.en: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often consulted him on memorials.
entries.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Yi often associated with him; whenever memorials discussed affairs, he often consulted him.

entries.zh: 十七年，孝文南征，上議告類之禮。
entries.en: In year seventeen, during Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, he memorialized on reporting rites to ancestors.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, when Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he submitted a memorial on the ceremony of reporting to the ancestors.

entries.zh: 及太師馮熙薨，惠蔚監其喪禮。
entries.en: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised the mourning rites.
entries.literal: When Grand Tutor Feng Xi died, Huiwei supervised his mourning rites.

entries.zh: 上書，令熙未冠之子，皆服成人服。
entries.en: He memorialized that Xi's uncapped sons should wear adult mourning.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial that Xi's sons who had not yet capped should all wear adult mourning garments.

entries.zh: 惠蔚與李彪以儒學相知，及彪位至尚書，惠蔚仍太廟令。
entries.en: Huiwei and Li Biao were friends in scholarship; when Biao became Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: Huiwei and Li Biao knew each other through Confucian learning; when Biao reached Minister, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 孝文曾從容言曰：「道固既登龍門，而孫蔚猶沈涓澮，朕常以為負矣。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen once said: "Dao Gu has crossed the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei remains in the mud—I have always regretted this."
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once said at leisure: "Dao Gu has ascended the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still sinks in a muddy ford—I have always felt this a burden."

entries.zh: 雖久滯小官，深體通塞，無孜孜之望，儒者以是尚焉。
entries.en: Though long in minor posts, he understood fortune and setback without ambition; scholars esteemed him.
entries.literal: Though long stuck in minor office, he deeply understood fortune and obstruction and had no eager hopes; Confucians therefore esteemed him.

entries.zh: 二十二年，侍讀東宮。
entries.en: In year twenty-two he lectured in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 先是，七廟以平文為太祖。
entries.en: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.
entries.literal: Earlier the seven temples took Emperor Pingwen as Founder.

entries.zh: 孝文議定祖宗，以道武為太祖。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen fixed Emperor Daowu as Founder.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deliberated fixing the ancestors and took Emperor Daowu as Founder.

entries.zh: 祖宗雖定，然昭穆未改。
entries.en: Though ancestors were fixed, the zhao-mu order was unchanged.
entries.literal: Though the ancestors were fixed, the zhao and mu order was not yet changed.

entries.zh: 及孝文崩，將祔神主於廟。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be installed in the temple.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, spirit tablets were to be enshrined in the temple.

entries.zh: 侍中崔光兼太常卿，以太祖既改，昭穆以次而易。
entries.en: Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that with the Founder changed, zhao-mu should shift accordingly.
entries.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, also Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, held that since the Founder was changed, zhao and mu should change in sequence accordingly.

entries.zh: 兼御史中尉、黃門侍郎邢巒，以為太祖雖改，昭穆仍不應易，乃立彈草，欲按奏光。
entries.en: Xing Luan held that zhao-mu should not change despite the new Founder and drafted impeachment against Guang.
entries.literal: Concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Yellow Gate Gentleman Xing Luan held that though the Founder was changed, zhao and mu still should not change; he drafted an impeachment to report Guang.

entries.zh: 光謂惠蔚曰：「此乃禮也，而執法欲見彈劾，思獲助於碩學。」
entries.en: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual, yet legal officers wish to impeach me—I need your help."
entries.literal: Guang told Huiwei: "This is ritual law, yet the law officers wish to impeach me—I seek help from a great scholar."

entries.zh: 惠蔚曰：「此深得禮變。」
entries.en: Huiwei said: "This accords with proper ritual change."
entries.literal: Huiwei said: "This deeply obtains the ritual change."

entries.zh: 尋為書以與光，贊明其事。
entries.en: He soon wrote supporting Guang's position.
entries.literal: Soon he wrote a letter for Guang clarifying the matter.

entries.zh: 光以惠蔚書呈宰輔，乃召惠蔚與巒庭議得失。
entries.en: Guang presented the letter and summoned Huiwei and Luan to debate at court.
entries.literal: Guang presented Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers and summoned Huiwei and Luan to court to debate gains and losses.

entries.zh: 尚書令王肅又助巒，而巒理終屈，彈事遂寢。
entries.en: Minister Wang Su aided Luan, but Luan lost the debate and the impeachment was dropped.
entries.literal: Minister Wang Su again aided Luan, but Luan's reasoning was ultimately defeated and the impeachment was shelved.

entries.zh: 天平四年，與兼散騎常侍李諧、兼吏部郎盧元明使梁。
entries.en: In Tianping year four he was envoy to Liang with Li Xie and Lu Yuanming.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping, together with Concurrent Regular Attendant Li Xie and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Yuanming he was envoy to Liang.

entries.zh: 梁散騎常侍硃異問業興曰：「魏洛中委粟山是南郊邪？
entries.en: Liang Regular Attendant Zhu Yi asked Yexing: "Is Wei's Luoyang Mount Weisu the southern suburb?
entries.literal: Liang Regular Attendant Zhu Yi asked Yexing: "Is Wei's Luoyang Mount Weisu the southern suburb?

entries.zh: 圓丘邪？」
entries.en: Or the round mound?"
entries.literal: Or the round mound?"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「委粟是圓丘，非南郊。」
entries.en: Yexing said: "Weisu is the round mound, not the southern suburb."
entries.literal: Yexing said: "Weisu is the round mound, not the southern suburb."

entries.zh: 異曰：「比聞郊、丘異所，是用鄭義。
entries.en: Yi said: "Recently I heard the suburban altar and mound differ in place—this uses the Zheng interpretation.
entries.literal: Yi said: "Recently I heard the suburban altar and mound differ in place—this uses the Zheng interpretation.

entries.zh: 我此中用王義。」
entries.en: We here use Wang's interpretation."
entries.literal: We here use Wang's interpretation."

entries.zh: 業興曰：「然。
entries.en: Yexing said: "So it is.
entries.literal: Yexing said: "So it is.

entries.zh: 洛京郊丘之處，用鄭解。」
entries.en: The place of suburban altar and mound in Luoyang uses Zheng's explanation."
entries.literal: The place of suburban altar and mound in Luoyang uses Zheng's explanation."

entries.zh: 異曰：「若然，女子逆降傍親，亦從鄭以不？」
entries.en: Yi said: "If so, when women marry down to collateral kin, do you also follow Zheng?"
entries.literal: Yi said: "If so, when women marry down to collateral kin, do you also follow Zheng?"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「此之一事，亦不專從。
entries.en: Yexing said: "In this one matter we do not exclusively follow.
entries.literal: Yexing said: "In this one matter we do not exclusively follow.

entries.zh: 若卿此間用王義，除禫應用二十五月，何以王儉《喪禮》，禫用二十七月也？」
entries.en: If your side uses Wang, for removing mourning should you use twenty-five months—why does Wang Jian's Mourning Rites use twenty-seven for the final mourning period?"
entries.literal: If your side uses Wang, for removing mourning should you use twenty-five months—why does Wang Jian's Mourning Rites use twenty-seven for the final mourning period?"

entries.zh: 異遂不答。
entries.en: Yi fell silent.
entries.literal: Yi then did not answer.

entries.zh: 業興曰：「我昨見明堂，四柱方屋，都無五九之室，當是裴頠所制。
entries.en: Yexing said: "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—four pillars and a square house, entirely without the five-by-nine chambers; it must be Pei Yan's design.
entries.literal: Yexing said: "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—four pillars and a square house, entirely without the five-by-nine chambers; it must be Pei Yan's design.

entries.zh: 明堂上圓下方，裴唯除室耳，今此上不圓，何也？」
entries.en: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers—yet this top is not round; why?"
entries.literal: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers—yet this top is not round; why?"

entries.zh: 異曰：「圓方俗說，經典無文，何怪于方。」
entries.en: Yi said: "Round and square are vulgar sayings; the classics have no text—why wonder at square?"
entries.literal: Yi said: "Round and square are vulgar sayings; the classics have no text—why wonder at square?"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「圓方之言，出處甚明，卿自不見。
entries.en: Yexing said: "The words round and square have very clear origins—you yourself do not see them.
entries.literal: Yexing said: "The words round and square have very clear origins—you yourself do not see them.

entries.zh: 見卿錄梁主《孝經義》亦云'上圓下方'，卿言豈非自相矛盾？」
entries.en: I see your recorded Liang ruler's Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety also says 'round above, square below'—are your words not self-contradictory?"
entries.literal: I see your recorded Liang ruler's Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety also says 'round above, square below'—are your words not self-contradictory?"

entries.zh: 異曰：「若然，圓方竟出何經？」
entries.en: Yi said: "If so, from what classic do round and square ultimately come?"
entries.literal: Yi said: "If so, from what classic do round and square ultimately come?"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「出《孝經援神契》。」
entries.en: Yexing said: "From the Classic of Filial Piety Apocryphal Divine Contract."
entries.literal: Yexing said: "From the Classic of Filial Piety Apocryphal Divine Contract."

entries.zh: 異曰：「緯候之書，何可信也！」
entries.en: Yi said: "Weft and omen books—how can they be trusted!"
entries.literal: Yi said: "Weft and omen books—how can they be trusted!"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「卿若不信，《靈威仰》、《葉光紀》之類，經典亦無出者，卿復信不？」
entries.en: Yexing said: "If you do not believe them, books like Spiritual Majesty and Leaf Light Annals also have no classical source—do you believe those?"
entries.literal: Yexing said: "If you do not believe them, books like Spiritual Majesty and Leaf Light Annals also have no classical source—do you believe those?"

entries.zh: 異不答。
entries.en: Yi again was silent.
entries.literal: Yi did not answer.

entries.zh: 梁武問業興：「《詩·周南》，王者之風，系之周公；
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Yexing: "In the Odes, Zhou South is the king's wind, attached to the Duke of Zhou;
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked Yexing: "In the Odes, Zhou South is the king's wind, attached to the Duke of Zhou;

entries.zh: 《召南》，仁賢之風，系之召公。
entries.en: Shao South is the humane and worthy wind, attached to the Duke of Shao.
entries.literal: Shao South is the humane and worthy wind, attached to the Duke of Shao.

entries.zh: 何名為系？」
entries.en: What is meant by 'attached'?"
entries.literal: What is meant by 'attached'?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「鄭注《儀禮》云：昔太王、王季居於岐陽，躬行《召南》之教以興王業。
entries.en: Yexing replied: "Zheng's note on the Ceremonial says: Formerly Grandfather Tai and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally practiced Shao South's teaching to raise the royal enterprise.
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "Zheng's note on the Ceremonial says: Formerly Grandfather Tai and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally practiced Shao South's teaching to raise the royal enterprise.

entries.zh: 及文王行今《周南》之教以受命，作邑於酆。
entries.en: When King Wen practiced present Zhou South's teaching to receive the Mandate, he made his seat at Feng.
entries.literal: When King Wen practiced present Zhou South's teaching to receive the Mandate, he made his seat at Feng.

entries.zh: 文王為諸侯之地所化之國，今既登九五之尊，不可復守諸侯之地，故分封二公，名為系。」
entries.en: Wen was lord of the lands transformed by feudal states; now having ascended to the nine-five dignity he could not again keep feudal lands—therefore he enfeoffed the two dukes, named 'attached.'"
entries.literal: Wen was lord of the lands transformed by feudal states; now having ascended to the nine-five dignity he could not again keep feudal lands—therefore he enfeoffed the two dukes, named 'attached.'

entries.zh: 梁武又問：「《尚書》'正月上日，受終文祖'，此時何正？」
entries.en: The Liang ruler also asked: "In the Documents 'first month, first day, received the end from the culture-ancestor'—what calendar month was this?"
entries.literal: The Liang ruler also asked: "In the Documents 'first month, first day, received the end from the culture-ancestor'—what calendar month was this?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「此夏正月。」
entries.en: Yexing replied: "This is the first month of summer."
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "This is the first month of summer."

entries.zh: 梁武言：「何以得知？」
entries.en: Emperor Wu said: "How do you know?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said: "How do you know?"

entries.zh: 業興曰：「案《尚書中候運衡篇》雲'日月營始'，故知夏正。」
entries.en: Yexing said: "According to the Documents apocryphon Transport Balance it says 'sun and moon begin their circuit'—thus I know it is summer's first month."
entries.literal: Yexing said: "According to the Documents apocryphon Transport Balance it says 'sun and moon begin their circuit'—thus I know it is summer's first month."

entries.zh: 又問：「堯時以前，何月為正？」
entries.en: He also asked: "Before Yao, what month was taken as first?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "Before Yao, what month was taken as first?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「自堯以上，書典不載，實所不知。」
entries.en: Yexing replied: "From above Yao, books and canons are not recorded—I truly do not know."
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "From above Yao, books and canons are not recorded—I truly do not know."

entries.zh: 梁武又云：「'寅賓出日'，是正月，'日中星鳥，以殷仲春'，即是二月。
entries.en: The Liang ruler also said: "'Guest at sunrise' is the first month; 'sun at mid-day, stars like birds, marking mid-spring of Yin' is the second month.
entries.literal: The Liang ruler also said: "'Guest at sunrise' is the first month; 'sun at mid-day, stars like birds, marking mid-spring of Yin' is the second month.

entries.zh: 此出《堯典》，何得雲堯時不知用何正？」
entries.en: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say Yao's time did not know what calendar was used?"
entries.literal: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say Yao's time did not know what calendar was used?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「雖三正不同，言時節者，皆據夏時正月。
entries.en: Yexing replied: "Though the three calendars differ, when speaking of seasons all rely on summer's first month.
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "Though the three calendars differ, when speaking of seasons all rely on summer's first month.

entries.zh: 《周禮》：'仲春二月，會男女之無夫家者。
entries.en: He cited the Zhou Rites.
entries.literal: The Offices of Zhou: 'mid-spring second month, gather men and women without spouses.'

entries.zh: '雖自周書，月亦夏時。
entries.en: Even Zhou texts used Xia months.
entries.literal: Though from Zhou's book, the month is also summer time.

entries.zh: 堯之日月，亦當如此。
entries.en: Yao's calendar should be the same.
entries.literal: Yao's sun and moon should be the same.

entries.zh: 但所見不深，無以辯析明問。」
entries.en: But what I have seen is not deep enough to analyze your clear questions."
entries.literal: But what I have seen is not deep enough to analyze your clear questions."

entries.zh: 梁武又曰：「《禮》：原壤母死，叩木而歌。
entries.en: The Liang ruler also said: "In the Rites, when Yuan Rang's mother died, he knocked wood and sang.
entries.literal: The Liang ruler also said: "In the Rites, when Yuan Rang's mother died, he knocked wood and sang.

entries.zh: 孔子聖人，而與壤為友？」
entries.en: Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Rang?"
entries.literal: Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Rang?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「孔即自解，言親者不失其親，故者不失其故。」
entries.en: Yexing replied: "Confucius himself explained: those close do not lose the close; the old do not lose the old."
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "Confucius himself explained: those close do not lose the close; the old do not lose the old."

entries.zh: 又問：「壤何處人？」
entries.en: He also asked: "What place was Rang from?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "What place was Rang from?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「《注》云：原壤，孔子幼之舊故。
entries.en: He replied: "The note says Yuan Rang was Confucius's childhood old acquaintance.
entries.literal: He replied: "The note says Yuan Rang was Confucius's childhood old acquaintance.

entries.zh: 是魯人。」
entries.en: He was a man of Lu."
entries.literal: He was a man of Lu."

entries.zh: 又問：「原壤不孝，有逆人倫，何以存故舊之小節，廢不孝之大罪？」
entries.en: He also asked: "Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why keep a small tie of old acquaintance and abandon the great crime of unfiliality?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why keep a small tie of old acquaintance and abandon the great crime of unfiliality?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「原壤所行，事自彰著，幼少之交，非是今始。
entries.en: He replied: "Yuan Rang's conduct was self-evident; the childhood tie was not begun now.
entries.literal: He replied: "Yuan Rang's conduct was self-evident; the childhood tie was not begun now.

entries.zh: 既無大故，何容棄之？」
entries.en: Since there was no great breach, how could he be cast off?"
entries.literal: Since there was no great breach, how could he be cast off?"

entries.zh: 又問：「孔子聖人，何以書原壤之事，垂法萬代？」
entries.en: He also asked: "Confucius was a sage—why record Yuan Rang's affair to set law for ten thousand generations?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "Confucius was a sage—why record Yuan Rang's affair to set law for ten thousand generations?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「此是後人所錄，非孔子自製，猶合葬於防。
entries.en: Yexing replied: "This was recorded by later men, not made by Confucius himself—like joint burial at Fang.
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "This was recorded by later men, not made by Confucius himself—like joint burial at Fang.

entries.zh: 如此 之比，《禮記》之中，動有百數。」
entries.en: Matters like this in the Book of Rites number in the hundreds."
entries.literal: Matters like this in the Book of Rites number in the hundreds."

entries.zh: 又問：「《易》有太極，極是有無？」
entries.en: He also asked: "The Changes has the Supreme Ultimate—is the ultimate being or non-being?"
entries.literal: He also asked: "The Changes has the Supreme Ultimate—is the ultimate being or non-being?"

entries.zh: 業興對曰：「所傳太極是有。」
entries.en: Yexing replied: "The transmitted Supreme Ultimate is being."
entries.literal: Yexing replied: "The transmitted Supreme Ultimate is being."

entries.zh: 還，兼散騎常侍，加中軍大將軍。
entries.en: On return he was Concurrent Regular Attendant and Central Army general.
entries.literal: Returning, he was Concurrent Regular Attendant and made Grand General of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 儒林上
entries.en: Confucian Scholars, Part 1
entries.literal: Confucian Forest, Upper

entries.zh: 臣聞成湯遭旱，以六事自陳。
entries.en: I have heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed his faults in six matters.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed himself in six matters.

entries.zh: 宣王太甚，而圭璧斯竭。
entries.en: When King Xuan of Zhou went too far, even jade offerings were exhausted.
entries.literal: When King Xuan went too far, jade disks and bi were exhausted.

entries.zh: 豈非遠慮元元，俯哀黎庶。
entries.en: Surely that was because he looked to the welfare of the people and pitied the masses.
entries.literal: Was this not because he looked far to the common people and bowed in pity to the masses?

entries.zh: 今農要之月，時雨猶愆，率土之心，有懷渴仰。
entries.en: Now in the month when agriculture matters most, timely rain is still lacking, and the whole realm looks up in thirst.
entries.literal: Now in the month when agriculture is vital, timely rain is still lacking; the heart of all within the realm thirsts and looks up.

entries.zh: 陛下垂情萬類，子愛群生，覲禮百神，猶未豐洽。
entries.en: Your Majesty cares for all living things and loves the people as his children; you perform rites to the spirits, yet blessings are not yet complete.
entries.literal: Your Majesty extends affection to the ten thousand kinds and loves the multitude as children; you observe rites toward the hundred spirits, yet abundance is not yet full.

entries.zh: 豈或作事不節，有違時令，舉措失中，當邀斯旱。
entries.en: Could it be that undertakings are ill timed, the seasons violated, or measures misplaced, and so this drought has been invited?
entries.literal: Could it be that works are not regulated, the seasons are violated, or measures are misplaced, perchance inviting this drought?

entries.zh: 臣聞寬大所以兼覆，慈愛所以懷眾。
entries.en: I have heard that breadth enables covering all, and kindness enables embracing the multitude.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that breadth and largeness are what enable covering all; kindness and love are what enable embracing the multitude.

entries.zh: 故天地稱其高厚者，萬物得其容養焉；
entries.en: Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive shelter and nurture from them;
entries.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive their shelter and nurture;

entries.zh: 四時著其寒暑者，庶類資其忠信焉。
entries.en: the four seasons show cold and heat because all living kinds rely on their constancy and good faith.
entries.literal: the four seasons display their cold and heat because the myriad kinds rely on their constancy and trust.

entries.zh: 是以帝王者，寬大象天地，忠信則四時。
entries.en: Thus emperors and kings model themselves on the breadth of Heaven and Earth and the good faith of the four seasons.
entries.literal: Thus emperors and kings take Heaven and Earth as their model of breadth, and the four seasons as their constancy and trust.

entries.zh: 招搖東指，天下識其春；
entries.en: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows spring has come;
entries.literal: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows it is spring;

entries.zh: 人君布德，率土懷其惠。
entries.en: when a ruler spreads virtue, the realm cherishes his grace.
entries.literal: when a ruler spreads virtue, all within the realm cherishes his grace.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下，資乾禦宇，品物咸亨，時乘六龍，自強不息，好問受規，天下幸甚。
entries.en: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs all things in prosperity, rides the six dragons without cease, and loves to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.
entries.literal: Bow low: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs the universe; all things flourish. You ride the six dragons, strengthen yourself without cease, love to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.

entries.zh: 自古至道之君，亦皆廣延博訪，詢采皞蕘，置鼓樹木，以求其過。
entries.en: Since antiquity rulers of utmost virtue have sought counsel widely, even from the humblest, and welcomed criticism to learn their faults.
entries.literal: From antiquity the rulers of utmost Way have all broadly extended invitations and sought counsel, gathering even the words of grass cutters, setting up drums and trees to welcome criticism, to seek out their faults.

entries.zh: 頃者亢旱逾時，人懷望歲，陛下爰發明詔，廣求六瘼，同禹、湯之罪己，高宋景之守正，澍雨應時，年穀斯稔。
entries.en: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season and the people hoped for rain. Your Majesty issued a brilliant edict seeking the people's afflictions, matching Yu and Tang in blaming yourself and Duke Jing of Song in holding to the upright; timely rain came and the year's grain ripened.
entries.literal: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season; people harbored hope for the year's harvest. Your Majesty then issued a brilliant edict, broadly seeking the six afflictions of the people, matching Yu and Tang in blaming themselves and rising to Duke Jing of Song in holding to the upright; timely rain responded, and the year's grain ripened.

entries.zh: 克己節用，慕質去華，此則尚矣。
entries.en: You restrained yourself and economized, admired simplicity and detested extravagance—this is already lofty.
entries.literal: Restraining oneself and economizing, admiring simplicity and detesting splendor—this is already lofty.

entries.zh: 然而硃紫仍耀于衢路，綺縠猶侈于豪富，短褐未充於細人，糟糠未厭於編戶。
entries.en: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, fine silks still adorn wealthy houses, coarse cloth does not clothe the common people, and coarse grain does not fill their bowls.
entries.literal: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, and fine silks are still extravagant in wealthy houses; coarse cloth does not fill the common people, and chaff and husks do not satisfy registered households.

entries.zh: 此則勸導之理，有所未周故也。
entries.en: This shows that guidance and persuasion have not yet reached everywhere.
entries.literal: This is because the principle of guidance and leading has not yet been fully applied.

entries.zh: 今雖導之以禮，齊之以刑，風俗固難以一矣。
entries.en: Though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to unify at once.
entries.literal: Now though you guide them with ritual and align them with punishments, custom is hard to make one.

entries.zh: 昔漢文帝集上書之囊，以作帷帳；
entries.en: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered memorial bags to make curtains;
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered the bags of memorials to make curtains;

entries.zh: 惜十家之產，不造露臺。
entries.en: he would not build a terrace that cost the wealth of ten households;
entries.literal: he prized the wealth of ten households and would not build the open terrace;

entries.zh: 後宮所幸，衣不曳地，方之今日富室之飾，嘗不如婢隸之服。
entries.en: palace women wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with rich houses today, even servants dress more lavishly.
entries.literal: those favored in the rear palace wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with the adornment of rich houses today, they were not even like servants' dress.

entries.zh: 然而以身率下，國富刑清，廟稱太宗，良有以也。
entries.en: By leading through his own example the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple honors him as Emperor Taizong, and rightly so.
entries.literal: Yet by taking the body to lead those below, the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple calls him Emperor Taizong—and rightly so.

entries.zh: 臣聞聖人久于其道而天下化成。
entries.en: When the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.

entries.zh: 今承魏氏衰亂之後，貞信未興。
entries.en: Now, after the disorders of Wei, constancy and trust have not yet been restored.
entries.literal: Now, inheriting the age after Wei's disorders, constancy and trust have not yet arisen.

entries.zh: 宜先尊五美，屏四惡，革浮華之俗，抑流競之風，察鴻都之小藝，焚雉頭之異服，無益之貨勿重于時，虧德之器勿陳於側，則人知德矣。
entries.en: First follow the five beauties and banish the four evils: reform empty display, restrain reckless competition, examine minor arts, burn outlandish dress, let useless goods not be prized, and harmful luxuries not be displayed—then the people will know virtue.
entries.literal: One should first follow the five beauties and banish the four evils, reform the custom of empty show, restrain the wind of reckless competition, examine the minor arts of Hongdu, burn the strange garments of pheasant-head style, let goods of no benefit not be prized in the age, and vessels that harm virtue not be displayed at the side—then the people will know virtue.

entries.zh: 帝覽而嘉之。
entries.en: The emperor read the memorial and commended him.
entries.literal: The emperor read it and commended him.

entries.zh: 保定三年，盛營宮室。
entries.en: In the third year of Baoding palace construction was carried out on a grand scale.
entries.literal: In the third year of Baoding, palace buildings were constructed on a grand scale.

entries.zh: 春夏大旱，詔公卿百僚，極言得失。
entries.en: Spring and summer brought severe drought; the throne ordered ministers and officials to speak freely on what was going wrong.
entries.literal: In spring and summer there was great drought; an edict ordered the high ministers and the hundred officials to speak to the utmost on gains and losses.

entries.zh: 季明上封事曰：
entries.en: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial:
entries.literal: Jiming submitted a sealed memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 《春秋》，君舉必書，動為典禮。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every act of a ruler; conduct is canon and ritual.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that a ruler's every act must be written; movement is canon and ritual.

entries.zh: 水旱陰陽，莫不應行而至。
entries.en: Flood, drought, and the balance of yin and yang all respond to how a ruler behaves.
entries.literal: Flood, drought, yin and yang—none fail to respond to conduct and arrive.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「言行，君子之所以動天地，可不慎乎！」
entries.en: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?"
entries.literal: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?"

entries.zh: 《春秋》莊公三十一年冬，不雨，《五行傳》以為是歲一年而三築台，奢侈不恤人也。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, winter, there was no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year three platforms were built in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang year 31 winter: no rain. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year platforms were built three times in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.

entries.zh: 僖公二十一年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為時作南門，勞人興役。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year of Duke Xi of Lu, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was under construction, exhausting the people with labor.
entries.literal: Duke Xi year 21 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was being built, laboring the people with corvée.

entries.zh: 漢惠帝二年夏，大旱，五年夏，大旱，江河水少，溪澗水絕，《五行傳》以為先是發十四萬六千人城長安。
entries.en: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, summer, there was great drought. In the fifth year, summer, there was great drought; the great rivers ran low and streams dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui of Han year 2 summer: great drought. Year 5 summer: great drought; the Yangtze and Yellow rivers had little water, and streams and brooks dried up. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.

entries.zh: 漢武帝元狩三年夏，大旱，《五行傳》以為是歲發天下故吏，穿昆明池。
entries.en: In the third year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu of Han, summer, there was great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year former officials throughout the realm were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, Yuanshou year 3 summer: great drought. The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year men throughout the realm who had formerly held office were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.

entries.zh: 然則土木之功，動人興役，天輒應之以異。
entries.en: Thus whenever earth and wood works mobilize the people, Heaven responds with anomalies.
entries.literal: Thus works of earth and wood, moving the people with corvée—Heaven always responds with anomalies.

entries.zh: 典籍作誡，倘或可思，上天譴告，改之則善。
entries.en: The warnings of the classics are perhaps worth pondering; Heaven's reproof, if heeded, leads to good.
entries.literal: The admonitions of the classics—perhaps they may be pondered; Heaven's reproof—if changed, then good.

entries.zh: 今若息人省役，以答天譴，庶靈澤時降，嘉谷有時，則年登可覬，子來非晚。
entries.en: If Your Majesty now rests the people and reduces corvée to answer Heaven's reproof, timely rain may fall, grain ripen, and the people come gladly—not too late.
entries.literal: If now the people are rested and corvée reduced, to answer Heaven's reproof, then perhaps timely blessings will descend, fine grain will ripen in season, the year's harvest may be hoped for, and the people will come as children—not late.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：「人亦勞止，迄可小康，惠此中國，以綏四方。」
entries.en: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."
entries.literal: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease; show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."

entries.zh: 或恐極陽生陰，秋多雨水，年復不登，人將無覬。
entries.en: Or perhaps when yang reaches its extreme, yin will arise; autumn may bring heavy rain, the harvest may fail again, and the people will have nothing to hope for.
entries.literal: Or perhaps one fears that when yang reaches its extreme yin is born, and in autumn there will be much rain; the year again will not yield, and the people will have nothing to hope for.

entries.zh: 如又薦饑，為慮更甚。
entries.en: If famine follows as well, the danger is even greater.
entries.literal: If famine is added on top, the concern is even greater.

entries.zh: 時外史廨宇屢移，未有定所。
entries.en: At that time the outer historians’ offices were repeatedly relocated and had no fixed site.
entries.literal: At that time the offices of the outer historians were repeatedly moved and had no fixed site.

entries.zh: 季明又上言曰：「外史之職，漢之東觀，帝王所寶，此焉攸在。
entries.en: Jiming submitted another memorial: “The office of outer historian corresponds to the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is kept here.
entries.literal: Jiming again submitted a memorial, saying, “The office of outer historian is the Eastern Pavilion of Han—what emperors treasure is preserved here.

entries.zh: 自魏及周，公館不立，臣雖愚瞽，猶知其非。
entries.en: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.
entries.literal: From Wei through Zhou no public hall was established; though I am foolish and blind, I still know this was wrong.

entries.zh: 是以去年十一月中，敢冒奏陳，特降中旨，即遣修營。
entries.en: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.
entries.literal: Therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared to memorialize, and a special edict descended ordering construction at once.

entries.zh: 荏苒一周，未知功力。
entries.en: A full year has passed and the progress of the work is still unknown.
entries.literal: A year has passed and the work accomplished is still unknown.

entries.zh: 臣職思其憂，敢不重請。」
entries.en: The duties of my office weigh upon my mind; I dare press the request again."
entries.literal: My office weighs upon my mind; I dare again to press the request."

entries.zh: 帝納焉，於是廨宇方立。
entries.en: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.
entries.literal: The emperor accepted it, and only then were the offices established.

entries.zh: 天和二年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Director with powers equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 後以疾卒。
entries.en: He later died of illness.
entries.literal: Later he died of illness.

entries.zh: 何妥，字棲風，西城人也。
entries.en: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, came from Xicheng.
entries.literal: He Tuo, styled Qifeng, was a native of Xicheng.

entries.zh: 父細腳胡，通商入蜀，遂家郫縣。
entries.en: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.
entries.literal: His father was a Sogdian merchant who traded into Shu and then made his home in Pixian.

entries.zh: 事梁武陵王紀，主知金帛，因致巨富，號為西州大賈。
entries.en: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.
entries.literal: He served the Liang Prince of Wuling, Xiao Ji, as overseer of gold and silk, and thereby amassed great wealth, being called the greatest merchant of the Western Provinces.

entries.zh: 妥少機警，八歲游國子學，助教顧良戲之曰：「汝姓何，是荷葉之荷？
entries.en: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and Assistant Instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?
entries.literal: Tuo was clever from youth; at eight he entered the Imperial Academy, and the assistant instructor Gu Liang teased him, saying, “Your surname He—is it the he of lotus leaf?

entries.zh: 為河水之河？」
entries.en: Or the he of river water?"
entries.literal: Or the he of river water?"

entries.zh: 妥應聲答曰：「先生姓顧，是眷顧之顧？
entries.en: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?
entries.literal: Tuo answered at once, “Sir, your surname Gu—is it the gu of regard?

entries.zh: 為新故之故？」
entries.en: Or the gu of old and new?"
entries.literal: Or the gu of old and new?"

entries.zh: 眾咸異之。
entries.en: The crowd all marveled at him.
entries.literal: The crowd all marveled at him.

entries.zh: 十七，以伎巧事湘東王。
entries.en: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.
entries.literal: At seventeen he served the Prince of Xiangdong with skill in craft.

entries.zh: 後知其聰明，召為誦書左右。
entries.en: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.
entries.literal: Later, knowing his intelligence, the prince summoned him as a recitation attendant at his side.

entries.zh: 時蘭陵蕭翽，亦有俊才，住青楊巷，妥住白楊頭。
entries.en: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo at White Poplar Head.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao Xu of Lanling also had outstanding talent; Xu lived on Green Poplar Lane and Tuo lived at White Poplar Head.

entries.zh: 時人為之語曰：「世有兩俊，白楊何妥，青楊蕭翽。」
entries.en: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar."
entries.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: “In the age there are two outstanding men—He Tuo of White Poplar and Xiao Xu of Green Poplar."

entries.zh: 其見美如此。
entries.en: Thus was he admired.
entries.literal: Thus was he admired.

entries.zh: 儒林下
entries.en: Confucian Scholars, Part Two
entries.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.

entries.zh: 公孫景茂，字元蔚，河間阜城人也。
entries.en: Gongsun Jingmao, courtesy name Yuanwei, was a native of Fucheng in Hejian.
entries.literal: Gongsun Jingmao, styled Yuanwei, was a man of Fucheng in Hejian.

entries.zh: 容貌魁梧，少好學，博涉經史。
entries.en: Tall and imposing, in youth he loved learning and read widely in the classics.
entries.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing; in youth he loved learning and broadly traversed the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 在魏，察孝廉，射策甲科。
entries.en: In Wei he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and ranked first in the archery examination.
entries.literal: In Wei he was examined as Filial and Incorrupt and in archery examination ranked first class.

entries.zh: 稍遷太常博士，多所損益，時人稱為書庫。
entries.en: Promoted to doctor of the grand sacrifices, he made many improvements; contemporaries called him a walking library.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, making many improvements; people of the time called him a library of books.

entries.zh: 曆高唐令、大理正，俱有能名。
entries.en: He served as magistrate of Gaotang and director of justice, famed for ability in both.
entries.literal: He served successively as Magistrate of Gaotang and Director of Justice, both with reputations for ability.

entries.zh: 齊滅，周武帝聞而召見，與語器之，授濟北太守。
entries.en: After Qi's fall, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him, valued his talent, and made him prefect of Jibei.
entries.literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard and summoned him, spoke with him and valued his capacity, and appointed him Administrator of Jibei.

entries.zh: 以母憂去職。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.

entries.zh: 開皇初，召拜汝南太守。
entries.en: Early in Kaihuang he was appointed prefect of Runan.
entries.literal: In the founding of Kaihuang he was summoned and appointed Administrator of Runan.

entries.zh: 郡廢，為曹州司馬，遷息州刺史。
entries.en: When the commandery was abolished he became Cao province marshal, then governor of Xi.
entries.literal: When the commandery was abolished he became Marshal of Cao Province and was transferred to Governor of Xi Province.

entries.zh: 法令清靜，德化大行。
entries.en: His laws were quiet; moral transformation flourished.
entries.literal: Laws and orders were pure and quiet; transforming virtue was greatly practiced.

entries.zh: 屬平陳之役，征人在路病者，景茂減俸祿為饘粥湯藥，多方振濟之，賴全活者千數。
entries.en: During the Chen campaign he used his salary for gruel, medicine, and relief for sick conscripts, saving thousands.
entries.literal: During the campaign to pacify Chen, conscripts on the road who fell ill—Jingmao reduced his salary to provide gruel, soup, and medicine and in many ways relieved them; those who lived thanks to this numbered in the thousands.

entries.zh: 上聞嘉之，詔宣示天下。
entries.en: The emperor commended him and proclaimed it throughout the realm.
entries.literal: The emperor heard and commended this; an edict proclaimed it to the realm.

entries.zh: 十五年，上幸洛陽，景茂謁見。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang and received Jingmao.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor visited Luoyang; Jingmao had an audience.

entries.zh: 時七十七，上命升殿坐。
entries.en: At seventy-seven he was seated in the hall by imperial order.
entries.literal: He was then seventy-seven; the emperor ordered him to ascend the hall and be seated.

entries.zh: 問其年，哀其老，嗟歎久之。
entries.en: Asked his age, the emperor pitied his age and sighed long.
entries.literal: Asked his age, the emperor pitied his old age and sighed long.

entries.zh: 景茂再拜曰：「呂望八十而遇文王，臣逾七十而逢陛下。」
entries.en: Jingmao said: "Lü Wang met King Wen at eighty; I pass seventy and meet Your Majesty."
entries.literal: Jingmao bowed again and said: "Lü Wang met King Wen at eighty; your servant passes seventy and meets Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 上甚悅，下詔褒美之，加上儀同三司，伊州刺史。
entries.en: The emperor praised him, advanced him to upper palace guard of the third order, and made him governor of Yi.
entries.literal: The emperor was very pleased, issued an edict praising him, and advanced him to Upper Palace Guard of the Third Order and Governor of Yi Province.

entries.zh: 明年，以疾征，吏人號泣於道。
entries.en: Recalled for illness, officials and people wailed along the road.
entries.literal: The next year, recalled for illness, officials and people wailed on the road.

entries.zh: 及疾愈，復乞骸骨，又不許。
entries.en: When healed he begged to retire again; again refused.
entries.literal: When his illness healed he again begged to retire; again it was not permitted.

entries.zh: 轉道州刺史。
entries.en: Transferred to governor of Dao province.
entries.literal: Transferred to Governor of Dao Province.

entries.zh: 悉以秩俸買牛犢雞豬，散惠孤弱不自存者。
entries.en: He spent his salary on livestock and gave them to orphans and the destitute.
entries.literal: He used all his salary to buy oxen, calves, chickens, and pigs and distributed them to the orphaned and weak who could not support themselves.

entries.zh: 好單騎巡人，家至戶入，閱視百姓產業。
entries.en: He patrolled alone, entering homes to inspect livelihoods.
entries.literal: He liked to patrol alone on horseback, entering every home, inspecting the people's livelihoods.

entries.zh: 有修理者，于都會時，乃褒揚稱述；
entries.en: Those who improved their affairs he praised at the great assembly;
entries.literal: Those who had improved their affairs—at the time of the great assembly he praised and proclaimed them;

entries.zh: 如有過惡，隨即訓導，而不彰也。
entries.en: those at fault he guided privately without exposing them.
entries.literal: if there were faults and evils, he immediately instructed and guided without exposing them.

entries.zh: 由是人行義讓，有無均通。
entries.en: People practiced righteousness; resources were shared.
entries.literal: Hence people practiced righteousness and yielding; having or lacking was mutually shared.

entries.zh: 男子相助耕耘，婦女相從紡織，大村或數百戶，皆如一家之務。
entries.en: Men helped plow; women spun together; large villages worked as one family.
entries.literal: Men helped one another in plowing; women followed one another in spinning; large villages of several hundred households all worked like one family.

entries.zh: 其後請致仕，上優詔聽之。
entries.en: He retired on an gracious imperial edict.
entries.literal: Later he requested retirement; the emperor graciously assented by edict.

entries.zh: 仁壽中，上明公楊紀出使河北，見景茂神力不衰，還以狀奏。
entries.en: In Renshou Duke Yang Ji saw Jingmao's vigor undiminished and reported it.
entries.literal: In Renshou, Duke Yang Ji of Shangming went on mission to Hebei, saw Jingmao's strength had not declined, and on return memorialized the fact.

entries.zh: 於是就拜淄州刺史，賜以馬輦，便道之官。
entries.en: He was appointed governor of Zi, granted a carriage, and sent directly to office.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was appointed on the spot Governor of Zi Province, granted a carriage, and went to office by expedited route.

entries.zh: 前後曆職，皆有德政，論者稱為良牧。
entries.en: Every post showed virtuous rule; critics called him a good shepherd.
entries.literal: In every office before and after he had virtuous government; discussants called him a good shepherd.

entries.zh: 大業初，卒官。
entries.en: Early in Daye he died in office.
entries.literal: In the early Daye period he died in office.

entries.zh: 年八十七，諡曰康。
entries.en: He was eighty-seven; posthumous title Kang.
entries.literal: Age eighty-seven; posthumous title Kang.

entries.zh: 身死之日，諸州人吏赴喪者數千人。
entries.en: Thousands came to his funeral.
entries.literal: On the day of his death several thousand officials and people from the provinces came to the funeral.

entries.zh: 或不及葬，皆望墳慟哭，野祭而去。
entries.en: Some could not attend burial; mourners wailed at his mound and left wild offerings.
entries.literal: Some could not reach the burial; all gazed at the mound and wailed, making wild sacrifices and leaving.

entries.zh: 辛公義，隴西狄道人也。
entries.en: Xin Gongyi was from Didao in Longxi.
entries.literal: Xin Gongyi was a man of Didao in Longxi.

entries.zh: 祖徽，魏徐州刺史。
entries.en: His grandfather Hui was Wei Inspector of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hui was Wei Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 父季慶，青州刺史。
entries.en: His father Jiqing was Inspector of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: His father Jiqing was Inspector of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 公義早孤，爲母氏所養，親授《書》、《傳》。
entries.en: Gongyi was orphaned young and raised by his mother’s family, who personally taught him the Documents and the commentaries.
entries.literal: Gongyi was orphaned early and was raised by his mother’s family; they personally taught him the Documents and the Commentaries.

entries.zh: 周天和中，選良家子任太學生。
entries.en: During the Zhou Tianhe era, he was selected from the sons of respectable families to become a student at the Imperial University.
entries.literal: During the Tianhe era of Zhou, he was selected as a son of a good family to serve as an Imperial University student.

entries.zh: 武帝時，召入露門學，令受道義，毎月集御前，令與大儒講論。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu, he was summoned to the Lumen School to study moral principles. Each month he assembled before the emperor and debated with great scholars.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, he was summoned into the Lumen School and ordered to receive instruction in principles and right conduct; each month he assembled before the emperor and was ordered to debate with great scholars.

entries.zh: 上數嗟異，時輩慕之。
entries.en: The emperor often sighed in admiration, and his contemporaries looked up to him.
entries.literal: The emperor repeatedly sighed in admiration, and his contemporaries admired him.

entries.zh: 建德初，授宣納中士。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Middle Clerk of Proclamation and Reception.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he was appointed Middle Clerk of Proclamation and Reception.

entries.zh: 從平齊，累遷掌治上士、掃寇將軍。
entries.en: He took part in the pacification of Qi and rose through successive promotions to Senior Clerk in Charge of Administration and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.
entries.literal: He followed in the pacification of Qi, and through successive promotions became Senior Clerk in Charge of Administration and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits.

entries.zh: 隋文帝作相，授內史上士，參掌機要。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Gongyi was appointed Senior Clerk of the Secretariat and helped manage confidential affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as chief minister, Gongyi was appointed Senior Clerk of the Secretariat and participated in handling confidential affairs.

entries.zh: 開皇元年，除主客侍郎，攝內史舍人，賜爵安陽縣男。
entries.en: In 581, he was appointed Gentleman Attendant of Guests, acted as Secretariat Drafter, and was granted the title Baron of Anyang County.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Gentleman Attendant of Guests, acted as Secretariat Drafter, and was granted the title Baron of Anyang County.

entries.zh: 轉駕部侍郎，使勾檢諸馬牧，所獲十餘萬匹。
entries.en: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Chariot Bureau and sent to audit the horse pastures, recovering more than a hundred thousand horses.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Chariot Bureau and sent to inspect the horse pastures, where he obtained more than a hundred thousand horses.

entries.zh: 上喜曰：「唯我公義，奉國罄心。」
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and said, “Only my Gongyi devotes his whole heart to serving the state.”
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and said, “Only my Gongyi serves the state with all his heart.”

entries.zh: 先王疆理天下，司牧黎元，刑法以禁其奸，禮教以防其欲，雖為政以德，理實殊塗，百慮一致，在斯而已。
entries.en: The ancient kings divided the land and ruled the world, caring for the common people. They employed criminal law to curb wrongdoing and ritual teaching to restrain excess desire. Though they governed through virtue, the practical means differed; yet every policy aimed at the same end—nothing more.
entries.literal: The ancient kings demarcated and governed the realm, tended and shepherded the common people, used penal law to restrain their wickedness, and used ritual instruction to guard against their desires. Though governing by virtue, the principles in truth followed different paths; a hundred considerations converged on one point—that was all.

entries.zh: 《書》云「知人則哲」，又云「無曠庶官」，言非其人為空官也。
entries.en: The Book of Documents states, "Knowing men is wisdom," and also warns, "Do not leave the offices vacant"—which is to say, an office held by the wrong man is no office at all.
entries.literal: The Book of Documents says, "He who knows men is wise," and also says, "Do not let the multitude of offices go vacant"—meaning that when the wrong person holds a post, it is an empty office.

entries.zh: 睿哲之後，必致清明之臣；
entries.en: Under a wise and perceptive sovereign, clear-minded and upright ministers inevitably appear;
entries.literal: After a sagacious and wise ruler, there will surely appear clear and upright ministers;

entries.zh: 昏亂之朝，多有貪殘之吏。
entries.en: A corrupt and chaotic court breeds greedy and brutal officials in abundance.
entries.literal: In a benighted and disorderly court, there are many greedy and cruel officials.

entries.zh: 嗜欲所召，影響從之。
entries.en: Whatever a ruler's appetites call forth, imitators trail in their wake.
entries.literal: What appetites summon, shadows and echoes follow.

entries.zh: 故五帝三王，不易人而化，皆在所由化之而已。
entries.en: The Five Emperors and Three Kings transformed people without replacing them; everything hinged on who did the transforming.
entries.literal: Thus the Five Emperors and Three Kings did not change men yet achieved transformation—all depended on whom they had to transform them.

entries.zh: 蓋有無能之吏，無不可禦之人焉。
entries.en: There may be incompetent officials, but there is no one beyond the reach of good governance.
entries.literal: For there are incapable officials, but there are no people who cannot be governed.

entries.zh: 自罷侯置守，歷年永久，統以方牧，仍世相循，所以寬猛為用，庇人調俗。
entries.en: Ever since feudal domains were abolished and prefectural governors installed, the system of regional oversight has endured for generations, alternating severity and leniency to protect the people and shape local custom.
entries.literal: Since the abolition of feudal lords and the establishment of commanderies, years have passed in long succession; governing through regional inspectors continued generation after generation—thus leniency and severity were employed to shelter the people and harmonize custom.

entries.zh: 但廉平常跡，聲有難高；
entries.en: Yet modest integrity wins little acclaim;
entries.literal: But honest and ordinary conduct—its reputation is hard to raise high;

entries.zh: 適時應務，招響必速。
entries.en: while timely boldness brings instant recognition.
entries.literal: Adapting to the times and responding to affairs—its summons and echo come swiftly.

entries.zh: 是故搏擊為侯，起不旋踵；
entries.en: Hence the forceful rose to noble rank overnight;
entries.literal: Therefore those who strike hard become marquises, rising without turning the heel;

entries.zh: 懦弱貽咎，錄用無時。
entries.en: the timid were blamed and passed over when offices were filled.
entries.literal: The weak and timid incur blame, and when recorded for appointment, there is no timely selection.

entries.zh: 此則已然於前世矣！
entries.en: Such was the pattern long before our own day!
entries.literal: This was already manifest in former ages!

entries.zh: 後之為吏，與世沈浮，叔季澆漓，奸巧多緒，居官蒞職，道各不同，故往籍述其賢能，以彰懲勸之道。
entries.en: Later generations of officials rode the currents of their times; as the age declined, customs grew shallow and cunning multiplied. Men in office pursued divergent paths. That is why earlier annals recorded the worthy and capable—to illustrate how reward and punishment should work.
entries.literal: Later officials drifted with the age; in the declining season customs ran thin and deceitful schemes multiplied. Holding office and exercising duty—each followed a different path. Therefore past records set forth the worthy and capable to make manifest the way of reward and punishment.

entries.zh: 案魏立《良吏傳》有張恂、鹿生、張膺、宋世景、路邕、閻慶胤、明亮、杜纂、裴佗、竇瑗、羊敦、蘇淑。
entries.en: Wei compiled a Biography of Good Officials including Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, and Su Shu.
entries.literal: Examining Wei: they established the "Biography of Good Officials" with Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Zhang Ying, Song Shijing, Lu Yong, Yan Qingyin, Ming Liang, Du Zuan, Pei Tuo, Dou Yuan, Yang Dun, and Su Shu.

entries.zh: 齊立《循吏傳》有張華原、宋世良、郎基、孟業、崔伯謙、蘇瓊、房豹、路去病。
entries.en: Qi compiled a Biography of Virtuous Officials including Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing.
entries.literal: Qi established the "Biography of Virtuous Officials" with Zhang Huayuan, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Meng Ye, Cui Boqian, Su Qiong, Fang Bao, and Lu Qubing.

entries.zh: 《周書》不立此篇。
entries.en: The History of Zhou includes no such chapter.
entries.literal: The Zhou History does not establish this chapter.

entries.zh: 隋《循吏傳》有梁彥光、樊叔略、趙軌、房恭懿、公孫景茂、辛公義、柳儉、劉曠、王伽、魏德深。
entries.en: The Sui Biography of Virtuous Officials lists Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Zhao Gui, Fang Gongyi, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, and Wei Deshen.
entries.literal: The Sui "Biography of Virtuous Officials" has Liang Yanguang, Fan Shulüe, Zhao Gui, Fang Gongyi, Gongsun Jingmao, Xin Gongyi, Liu Jian, Liu Kuang, Wang Jia, and Wei Deshen.

entries.zh: 其張恂、鹿生、宋世景、裴佗、羊敦、宋世良、郎基、崔伯謙、房豹、趙軌、房恭懿，各附其家傳，其餘皆依時代編緝，以備《循吏篇》云。
entries.en: Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Song Shijing, Pei Tuo, Yang Dun, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Cui Boqian, Fang Bao, Zhao Gui, and Fang Gongyi each appear in their family biographies; the remainder are arranged by period here to complete the chapter on virtuous officials.
entries.literal: As for Zhang Xun, Lu Sheng, Song Shijing, Pei Tuo, Yang Dun, Song Shiliang, Lang Ji, Cui Boqian, Fang Bao, Zhao Gui, and Fang Gongyi—each is appended to his family biography; the rest are compiled by era to complete the chapter on virtuous officials.

entries.zh: 邸珍，字安寶，本中山上曲陽人也，魏太和中，徙居武州鎮。
entries.en: Di Zhen, courtesy name Anbao, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan. During the Wei Taihe era his family moved to Wuzhou Garrison.
entries.literal: Di Zhen, style name Anbao, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan; in the Taihe era of Wei he moved to Wuzhou garrison.

entries.zh: 孝昌中，六鎮兵起，珍遂從杜洛周賊。
entries.en: During the Xiaochang era, when the Six Garrisons rebelled, Zhen joined the rebel Du Luozhou.
entries.literal: In the Xiaochang era the Six Garrisons rose in arms; Zhen thereupon followed the rebel Du Luozhou.

entries.zh: 洛周為葛榮所吞，珍入榮軍。
entries.en: When Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong, Zhen entered Ge Rong's army.
entries.literal: Luozhou was swallowed up by Ge Rong, and Zhen entered Rong's army.

entries.zh: 榮為爾硃榮所破，珍與其餘黨，俱徙并州。
entries.en: When Ge Rong was defeated by Erzhu Rong, Zhen and the remaining rebels were relocated to Bing Province.
entries.literal: Rong was defeated by Erzhu Rong; Zhen and the remaining partisans were all moved to Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 從齊神武出山東。
entries.en: He followed Northern Qi's Shenwu in his campaign east of the mountains.
entries.literal: He followed Qi Shenwu in emerging to Shandong.

entries.zh: 神武起義信都，拜珍長史，封上曲縣侯，除殷州刺史。
entries.en: When Shenwu raised his army at Xindu he appointed Zhen chief clerk, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangqu County, and made him governor of Yin Province.
entries.literal: When Shenwu raised the righteous army at Xindu he appointed Zhen Chief Clerk, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangqu County, and made him governor of Yinzhou.

entries.zh: 珍求取無厭，大為州人所疾苦。
entries.en: Zhen's greed was insatiable, and the people of the province suffered greatly.
entries.literal: Zhen's demands were insatiable, and the people of the province suffered greatly from him.

entries.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射、大行台，節度諸軍事，擊梁州將成景攜等，解東行圍，回軍彭城。
entries.en: Later he served concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner, directing military affairs. He attacked Liang generals including Cheng Jingxie, lifted the siege of Dongxing, and returned to Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Later he concurrently served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner, directing all military affairs; he attacked Liang generals Cheng Jingxie and others, lifted the siege of Dongxing, and returned the army to Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 珍禦下殘酷，士眾離心，至於土人豪族，遇之無禮，遂為州人所害。
entries.en: Zhen ruled his subordinates with cruelty, alienating soldiers and civilians alike, and treated local gentry without courtesy. He was eventually killed by men of the province.
entries.literal: Zhen was cruel in governing subordinates; soldiers and masses lost heart; as for local gentry and powerful clans, he treated them without propriety—therefore he was killed by men of the province.

entries.zh: 後贈定州刺史、司空公。
entries.en: He was later posthumously honored as governor of Ding Province and Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Later he was posthumously granted governor of Dingzhou and Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 子神 張赦提 趙霸 崔暹 邸珍 田式 燕榮 元弘嗣 王文同
entries.en: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong
entries.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, Wang Wentong

entries.zh: 蓋兼濟獨善，顯晦之殊，其事不同，由來久矣。
entries.en: The choice between benefiting the world and perfecting oneself alone, between serving in the open and withdrawing into obscurity—these paths have differed from the earliest times.
entries.literal: For benefiting all and cultivating oneself alone, the difference between public service and withdrawal—their affairs are not the same, and this has been so from long ago.

entries.zh: 昔夷、齊獲全于周武，華矞不容于太公，何哉？
entries.en: Long ago Boyi and Shuqi were spared by King Wu of Zhou, yet Hua Yu found no place with the Grand Duke Jiang—why was that?
entries.literal: In former times Boyi and Shuqi were preserved whole by King Wu of Zhou, while Hua Yu was not tolerated by Grand Duke Jiang—why?

entries.zh: 求其心者，許以激貪之用；
entries.en: Those who looked to their inner purpose hailed them as a check on greed;
entries.literal: Those who sought their hearts praised them as useful for restraining greed;

entries.zh: 督其跡者，矯以教義之風。
entries.en: those who judged them by their deeds took them as a corrective wind of moral instruction.
entries.literal: those who scrutinized their conduct corrected by them with a wind of teaching righteousness.

entries.zh: 而肥遁不歸，代有其人矣。
entries.en: Yet in every generation there have been men who withdrew deep into hiding and never came back.
entries.literal: Yet those who concealed themselves and did not return—each age has had such men.

entries.zh: 故《易》稱「遁世無悶」，「不事王侯」。
entries.en: Hence the Book of Changes speaks of one who 'leaves the world behind without distress' and 'serves neither kings nor lords.'
entries.literal: Thus the Book of Changes says, 'One who withdraws from the world is without vexation' and 'does not serve kings and lords.'

entries.zh: 《詩》云「皎皎白駒，在彼空谷」。
entries.en: The Odes has it: 'Bright is the white colt, there in the empty valley.'
entries.literal: The Odes says, 'The bright white colt is there in that empty valley.'

entries.zh: 《禮》云「儒有上不臣天子，下不事諸侯」。
entries.en: The Book of Rites declares that some scholars 'will not bow to the Son of Heaven above, nor serve the feudal lords below.'
entries.literal: The Rituals says, 'There are scholars who above do not serve the Son of Heaven as subjects, and below do not serve feudal lords.'

entries.zh: 《語》曰「舉逸民，天下之人歸心焉」。
entries.en: The Analects says that when reclusive worthies are brought forward, 'the hearts of the people throughout the realm will incline toward you.'
entries.literal: The Analects says, 'Raise up reclusive subjects, and the people throughout the realm will turn their hearts to you.'

entries.zh: 雖出處殊途，語默異用，各言其志，皆君子之道也。
entries.en: Though whether to enter public life or withdraw, to speak or keep silent, follows different courses, each man declares his own intent—and all alike belong to the way of the gentleman.
entries.literal: Though whether to serve or withdraw follows different paths, and speech and silence serve different ends, each expresses his purpose—all are the way of the gentleman.

entries.zh: 初在縉雲山，太極真人徐君降之曰：「汝年出八十，當為王者師，然後得道也。」
entries.en: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected One of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: 'When your years pass eighty you will become teacher to a king, and only then attain the Way.'
entries.literal: When he was first on Mount Jinyun, the Perfected One of the Grand Ultimate, Lord Xu, descended to him and said: 'When your years pass eighty you will become teacher to a king, and only then attain the Way.'

entries.zh: 晉王廣鎮揚州，聞其名，手書召之曰：「夫道得眾妙，法體自然，包涵二儀，混成萬物，人能弘道，道不虛行。
entries.en: Prince of Jin Yang Guang held Yangzhou and, hearing his name, personally wrote to summon him: 'The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature, embraces the two principles, and blends to form the ten thousand things. Man can expand the Way, and the Way does not move in vain.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang held Yangzhou and, hearing his name, personally wrote to summon him: 'The Way obtains the myriad subtleties; its law embodies nature, embraces the two principles, and blends to form the ten thousand things. Man can expand the Way, and the Way does not move in vain.

entries.zh: 先生履德養空，宗玄齊物，深曉義理，頗味法門。
entries.en: You, sir, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the dark as your standard and align with things, deeply understand principle and reason, and have tasted the gates of the Law.
entries.literal: You, sir, tread virtue and nurture emptiness, take the dark as your standard and align with things, deeply understand principle and reason, and have tasted the gates of the Law.

entries.zh: 悅性沖玄，恬神虛白，餐松餌術，棲息煙霞。
entries.en: Your nature delights in pure mystery, your spirit is tranquil and empty-white; you dine on pine and take elixirs, dwelling amid mist and rosy clouds.
entries.literal: Your nature delights in pure mystery, your spirit is tranquil and empty-white; you dine on pine and take elixirs, dwelling amid mist and rosy clouds.

entries.zh: 望赤城而待風雲，遊玉堂而駕龍鳳。
entries.en: Gazing toward Red Wall to await wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall and driving dragon and phoenix.
entries.literal: Gazing toward Red Wall to await wind and clouds, roaming the Jade Hall and driving dragon and phoenix.

entries.zh: 雖復藏名台嶽，猶且騰實江、淮。
entries.en: Though you again conceal your name on terrace and peak, your substance still rises along the Yangtze and Huai.
