entries.literal: Though you again conceal your name on terrace and peak, your substance still rises along the Yangtze and Huai.

entries.zh: 藉甚嘉猷，有勞寤寐。
entries.en: Your excellent counsel is greatly renowned and has long occupied my waking and sleeping thoughts.
entries.literal: Your excellent counsel is greatly renowned and has long occupied my waking and sleeping thoughts.

entries.zh: 欽承素道，久積虛襟，側席幽人，夢想岩穴。
entries.en: I respectfully receive your pure Way, long held in my open heart; I sit askance for the recluse and dream of mountain caves.
entries.literal: I respectfully receive your pure Way, long accumulated in my empty breast; I sit askance for the recluse and dream of mountain caves.

entries.zh: 霜風已冷，海氣將寒，偃息茂林，道體休悆。
entries.en: The frost wind is already cold and the sea air will soon turn chill; rest at ease in the lush forest and let your Way-body find repose.
entries.literal: The frost wind is already cold and the sea air will soon turn chill; rest at ease in the lush forest and let your Way-body find repose.

entries.zh: 昔商山四皓，輕舉漢庭；
entries.en: In former times the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly entered the Han court;
entries.literal: In former times the Four Hoary Heads of Mount Shang lightly entered the Han court;

entries.zh: 淮南八公，來儀籓邸。
entries.en: the Eight Worthies of Huainan came as guests to a princely residence.
entries.literal: the Eight Worthies of Huainan came as guests to a princely residence.

entries.zh: 古今雖異，山谷不殊。
entries.en: Though ancient and modern differ, mountains and valleys are not unlike.
entries.literal: Though ancient and modern differ, mountains and valleys are not unlike.

entries.zh: 市朝之隱，前賢已說。
entries.en: Reclusion within the marketplace and court—former worthies have already spoken of it.
entries.literal: Reclusion within the marketplace and court—former worthies have already spoken of it.

entries.zh: 導凡述聖。
entries.en: To guide the common and expound the sage—
entries.literal: To guide the common and expound the sage—

entries.zh: 非先生而誰？
entries.en: if not you, sir, then who?
entries.literal: if not you, sir, then who?

entries.zh: 故遣使人，往彼延請，想無勞東帛，賁然來思，不待蒲輪，去彼空穀。
entries.en: Therefore I send an envoy to invite you; I trust you need not be urged with silk gifts but will come with radiant intent, and need not wait for rush-wheeled carriages to leave that empty valley.
entries.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to go there and invite you; I trust you need not be urged with silk gifts but will come with radiant intent, and need not wait for rush-wheeled carriages to leave that empty valley.

entries.zh: 希能屈己，佇望披云。」
entries.en: I hope you can humble yourself; I wait in expectation to part the clouds.'
entries.literal: I hope you can humble yourself; I wait in expectation to part the clouds.'

entries.zh: 則謂門人曰：「吾今年八十一，王來召我，徐君之旨，信而不征。」
entries.en: Ze said to his disciples: 'I am eighty-one this year; the prince has come to summon me—Lord Xu's prophecy is trustworthy and not false.'
entries.literal: Ze said to his disciples: 'I am eighty-one this year; the prince has come to summon me—Lord Xu's prophecy is trustworthy and not false.'

entries.zh: 於是遂詣揚州。
entries.en: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon he went to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 晉王將請受道法，則辭以時日不便。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way, but Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin was about to request instruction in the Way, but Ze declined on the grounds that the time was not suitable.

entries.zh: 其後夕中，命待者取香火，如平常朝禮之儀，至於五更而死。
entries.en: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and perform the usual morning ritual; by the fifth watch he was dead.
entries.literal: That evening he ordered his attendants to fetch incense and fire and perform the usual morning ritual; by the fifth watch he was dead.

entries.zh: 支體柔弱如生，停留數旬，顏色不變。
entries.en: His limbs were soft as in life; he remained for several tens of days and his complexion did not change.
entries.literal: His limbs were soft as in life; he remained for several tens of days and his complexion did not change.

entries.zh: 晉王下書曰：「天台真隱東海徐先生，虛確居宗，沖玄成德，齊物處外，檢行安身。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin issued a letter: 'The true recluse of Mount Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, takes emptiness and certainty as his standard, forms virtue through pure mystery, aligns with things while standing apart, and restrains conduct to secure his person.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin issued a letter: 'The true recluse of Mount Tiantai, Master Xu of Donghai, takes emptiness and certainty as his standard, forms virtue through pure mystery, aligns with things while standing apart, and restrains conduct to secure his person.

entries.zh: 草褐蒲衣，餐松餌朮，棲隱靈岳，五十餘年。
entries.en: In hemp robe and rush garment he dined on pine and took atractylodes, dwelling in seclusion on the numinous peak for more than fifty years.
entries.literal: In hemp robe and rush garment he dined on pine and took atractylodes, dwelling in seclusion on the numinous peak for more than fifty years.

entries.zh: 卓矣仙才，飄然騰氣，千尋萬頃，莫測其涯。
entries.en: Transcendent was his immortal talent, soaring and ethereal; a thousand fathoms and ten thousand acres—none could measure his bounds.
entries.literal: Transcendent was his immortal talent, soaring and ethereal; a thousand fathoms and ten thousand acres—none could measure his bounds.

entries.zh: 寡人欽承道風，久餐德素，頻遣使乎，遠此延屈，冀得虔受上法，式建良緣。
entries.en: I have long admired his Way-wind and nourished myself on his pure virtue, repeatedly sending envoys to invite him from afar, hoping to receive the higher Law devoutly and establish a fine bond.
entries.literal: I have long admired his Way-wind and nourished myself on his pure virtue, repeatedly sending envoys to invite him from afar, hoping to receive the higher Law devoutly and establish a fine bond.

entries.zh: 至止甫爾，未淹旬日，厭塵羽化，反真靈府。
entries.en: He had just arrived and not yet passed ten days when, weary of the dust, he transformed by feather and returned to the numinous realm.
entries.literal: He had just arrived and not yet passed ten days when, weary of the dust, he transformed by feather and returned to the numinous realm.

entries.zh: 身體柔軟，顏色不變，經方所謂屍解地仙者哉。
entries.en: His body was soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the scriptures call a corpse-dissolving earthly immortal?
entries.literal: His body was soft and his complexion unchanged—is this not what the scriptures call a corpse-dissolving earthly immortal?

entries.zh: 誠復師禮未申，而心許有在，雖忘怛化，猶愴於懷。
entries.en: Truly the rites of master and disciple were not yet performed, yet a promise of the heart remained; though he forgot sorrow in transformation, grief still lodges in my breast.
entries.literal: Truly the rites of master and disciple were not yet performed, yet a promise of the heart remained; though he forgot sorrow in transformation, grief still lodges in my breast.

entries.zh: 喪事所資，隨須供給。
entries.en: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.
entries.literal: Whatever the funeral requires shall be supplied as needed.

entries.zh: 霓裳羽蓋，既且騰雲；
entries.en: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies have already risen on clouds;
entries.literal: Rainbow robes and feathered canopies have already risen on clouds;

entries.zh: 空槨餘衣，詎藉墳壟？
entries.en: an empty coffin and leftover garments—why rely on mound and tomb?
entries.literal: an empty coffin and leftover garments—why rely on mound and tomb?

entries.zh: 但杖舄在爾，可同俗法。
entries.en: Only the staff and shoes remain with you; you may follow the common custom.
entries.literal: Only the staff and shoes remain with you; you may follow the common custom.

entries.zh: 宜遣使人，送還天台定葬。」
entries.en: You should send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for burial.'
entries.literal: You should send envoys to return him to Mount Tiantai for burial.'

entries.zh: 子賾，字祖浚，七歲能屬文。
entries.en: His son Ze, styled Zujun, could compose literary pieces at the age of seven.
entries.literal: His son Ze, styled Zujun, at seven could compose literary pieces.

entries.zh: 容貌短小，有口辯。
entries.en: He was short in stature but gifted in debate.
entries.literal: His appearance was short and small, but he had eloquence in speech.

entries.zh: 開皇初，秦孝王薦之，射策高第。
entries.en: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him, and he placed at the top in the policy examination.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Prince Xiao of Qin recommended him and he placed at the top in the archery-and-policy examination.

entries.zh: 詔與諸儒定樂，授校書郎，轉協律郎。
entries.en: An edict ordered him, together with various Confucian scholars, to fix the court music; he was appointed Collator and later promoted to Director of Harmonization.
entries.literal: An edict ordered him together with various Confucian scholars to fix the music; he was appointed Collator and later transferred to Director of Harmonization.

entries.zh: 太常卿蘇威雅重之。
entries.en: Director of Ceremonies Su Wei held him in high esteem.
entries.literal: Director of Ceremonies Su Wei held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 母憂去職，性至孝，水漿不入口者五日。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his mother; deeply filial by nature, he took neither water nor food for five days.
entries.literal: He left office on his mother's death; his nature was deeply filial, and for five days he took neither water nor food.

entries.zh: 後徵為河南、豫章二王侍讀，每更日來往二王之第。
entries.en: Later he was summoned to serve as Lecturer to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, alternating each day between their two residences.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned to serve as Lecturer to the Princes of Henan and Yuzhang, each day alternating between the two princes' residences.

entries.zh: 及河南為晉王，轉記室參軍，自此去豫章。
entries.en: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin, Ze was transferred to Recorder of the Headquarters and thereafter left Yuzhang.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Henan became Prince of Jin he was transferred to Recorder of the Headquarters and from then on left Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 王重之不已，遺賾書曰：
entries.en: The prince valued him without cease and sent Ze a letter that read:
entries.literal: The prince valued him without cease and sent Ze a letter saying:

entries.zh: 是時，自江都至天台，在道多見則徒步，云得放還。
entries.en: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, many on the road saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.
entries.literal: At that time, from Jiangdu to Mount Tiantai, many on the road saw Ze walking on foot, saying he had been released to return.

entries.zh: 至其舊居，取經書道法，分遣弟子，仍令淨掃一房，曰：「若有客至，宜延之於此。」
entries.en: When he reached his old dwelling he took out scriptures and Daoist methods, distributed them among his disciples, and ordered a room swept clean, saying: 'If guests come, they should be received here.'
entries.literal: When he reached his old dwelling he took out scriptures and Daoist methods, distributed them among his disciples, and ordered a room swept clean, saying: 'If guests come, they should be received here.'

entries.zh: 然後跨石梁而去，不知所之。
entries.en: Then he crossed the stone bridge and departed, and no one knew where he went.
entries.literal: Then he crossed the stone bridge and departed, and no one knew where he went.

entries.zh: 須臾屍柩至，知其靈化，時年八十二。
entries.en: Shortly afterward the coffin arrived; they knew he had undergone spiritual transformation; he was then eighty-two.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward the coffin arrived; they knew he had undergone spiritual transformation; he was then eighty-two.

entries.zh: 晉王聞而益異之，賵物千段，遣畫工圖其狀，令柳{巧言}為之贊。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Bi to compose a eulogy.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin, hearing this, was all the more astonished; he sent a thousand bolts of funeral goods, dispatched a painter to depict his likeness, and ordered Liu Yan to compose a eulogy.

entries.zh: 時有建安宋玉泉、會稽孔道茂、丹陽王遠知等，亦行辟穀道，以松水自給，皆為煬帝所重。
entries.en: At that time there were also Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, and Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, who likewise practiced the Way of grain abstinence and sustained themselves on pine water—all were esteemed by Emperor Yang.
entries.literal: At that time there were also Song Yuquan of Jian'an, Kong Daomao of Kuaiji, and Wang Yuanzhi of Danyang, who likewise practiced the Way of grain abstinence and sustained themselves on pine water—all were esteemed by Emperor Yang.

entries.zh: 大業四年，從駕汾陽宮，次河陽鎮。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial procession to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial procession to Fenyang Palace and halted at Heyang garrison.

entries.zh: 藍田令王曇于藍田山得一玉人，長三四寸，著大領衣，冠幘。
entries.en: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three or four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a cap with headwrap.
entries.literal: Wang Tan, magistrate of Lantian, obtained a jade figure on Mount Lantian, three or four inches tall, wearing a broad-collared robe and a cap with headwrap.

entries.zh: 奏之。
entries.en: He reported it to the throne.
entries.literal: He memorialized it.

entries.zh: 詔問群臣，莫有識者。
entries.en: An edict asked the assembled ministers, but none could identify it.
entries.literal: An edict asked the assembled ministers, but none recognized it.

entries.zh: 賾答曰：「謹案：漢文帝已前，未有冠幘，即是文帝以來所制也。
entries.en: Ze replied: 'I respectfully consider: before Emperor Wen of Han there were no caps with headwraps; this must have been made from Emperor Wen's time onward.
entries.literal: Ze replied: 'I respectfully consider: before Emperor Wen of Han there were no caps with headwraps; this must have been made from Emperor Wen's time onward.

entries.zh: 臣見魏大司農盧元明撰《嵩高山廟記》云：『有神人，以玉為形，像長數寸，或出或隱，出則令世延長。』
entries.en: Your subject has seen the Record of the Song Mountain Temple written by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, which says: "There is a divine being in the form of jade, a figure several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears the age is prolonged."
entries.literal: Your subject has seen the Record of the Song Mountain Temple written by Lu Yuanming, Grand Minister of Agriculture of Wei, which says: "There is a divine being in the form of jade, a figure several inches long, who sometimes appears and sometimes hides; when he appears the age is prolonged."

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下，應天順人，定鼎嵩、雒，嶽神自見，臣敢稱慶。」
entries.en: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and following the people, has fixed the tripod at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself, and your subject dares to offer congratulations.'
entries.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Majesty, responding to Heaven and following the people, has fixed the tripod at Song and Luo; the mountain god has revealed himself, and your subject dares to offer congratulations.'

entries.zh: 因再拜，百官畢賀。
entries.en: Thereupon he bowed twice, and all the officials offered congratulations.
entries.literal: Thereupon he bowed twice, and all the officials offered congratulations.

entries.zh: 天子大悅，賜縑二百匹。
entries.en: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted him two hundred bolts of silk.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and granted two hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 從駕往太山，詔問賾曰：「何處有羊腸阪？」
entries.en: Accompanying the procession to Mount Tai, the emperor asked Ze: 'Where is Yangchang Slope?'
entries.literal: Accompanying the procession to Mount Tai, an edict asked Ze: 'Where is Yangchang Slope?'

entries.zh: 賾答曰：「臣案《漢書·地理志》，上党壺關縣有羊腸阪。」
entries.en: Ze replied: 'Your subject finds in the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han that Yangchang Slope is in Huguan County, Shangdang.'
entries.literal: Ze replied: 'Your subject finds in the Geography Monograph of the Book of Han that Yangchang Slope is in Huguan County, Shangdang.'

entries.zh: 帝曰：「不是。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'That is not it.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'That is not it.'

entries.zh: 又答曰：「臣案皇甫士安撰《地書》，云太原北九十里，有羊腸阪。」
entries.en: He replied again: 'Your subject finds in the Geography written by Huangfu Shi'an that ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Yangchang Slope.'
entries.literal: He replied again: 'Your subject finds in the Geography written by Huangfu Shi'an that ninety li north of Taiyuan there is a Yangchang Slope.'

entries.zh: 帝曰：「是也。」
entries.en: The emperor said: 'That is it.'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'That is it.'

entries.zh: 因謂牛弘曰：「崔祖浚所謂問一知二。」
entries.en: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'
entries.literal: Thereupon he said to Niu Hong: 'This is what Cui Zujun means by asking one and knowing two.'

entries.zh: 五年，受詔與諸儒撰《區宇圖志》二百五十卷，奏之。
entries.en: In the fifth year he received an edict to compile, with various Confucian scholars, the Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes, and submitted it.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he received an edict to compile with various Confucian scholars the Gazetteer of the Realm in two hundred fifty volumes, and submitted it.

entries.zh: 帝不善之，更令虞世基、許善心演為六百卷。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased with it and ordered Yu Shiji and Xu Shanxin to expand it into six hundred volumes.

entries.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his father, but was soon recalled and ordered to resume his duties.
entries.literal: He left office on his father's death, but soon was recalled and ordered to resume his duties.

entries.zh: 遼東之役，授鷹揚長史。
entries.en: During the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Soaring Hawk Command.
entries.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Soaring Hawk Command.

entries.zh: 置遼東郡縣名，皆賾之議也。
entries.en: The names of the commanderies and counties established in Liaodong were all Ze's proposals.
entries.literal: The names of the commanderies and counties established in Liaodong were all Ze's proposals.

entries.zh: 奉詔作《東征記》。
entries.en: He received an edict to compose the Record of the Eastern Expedition.
entries.literal: He received an edict to compose the Record of the Eastern Expedition.

entries.zh: 九年，除越王長史。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yue.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yue.

entries.zh: 于時山東盜賊蜂起，帝令撫慰高陽、襄國，歸首者八百餘人。
entries.en: At that time bandits rose like bees in the eastern provinces; the emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred surrendered.
entries.literal: At that time bandits rose like bees in the eastern provinces; the emperor ordered him to pacify Gaoyang and Xiangguo, and more than eight hundred surrendered.

entries.zh: 十二年，從駕江都。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Jiangdu.

entries.zh: 宇文化及之弑帝也，引為著作郎，稱疾不起。
entries.en: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the emperor, Ze was appointed Compiler, but he pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
entries.literal: When Yuwen Huaji assassinated the emperor he was appointed Compiler, but Ze pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 在路發疾，卒于彭城，年六十九。
entries.en: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.
entries.literal: On the road he fell ill and died at Pengcheng at the age of sixty-nine.

entries.zh: 一昨伏奉教書，榮貺非恆，心靈自失。
entries.en: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit was overwhelmed.
entries.literal: Yesterday I respectfully received your instructive letter; the honor bestowed was beyond the ordinary, and my spirit lost itself.

entries.zh: 若乃理高《象系》，管輅思而不解；
entries.en: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;
entries.literal: As for reasoning that surpasses the Image and Attachment of the Changes, even Guan Lu would ponder without understanding;

entries.zh: 事富《山海》，郭璞注而未詳。
entries.en: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated them yet could not exhaust them.
entries.literal: matters rich as the Classic of Mountains and Seas—Guo Pu annotated yet could not exhaust them.

entries.zh: 至於五色相宣，八音繁會，鳳鳴不足喻，龍章莫之比。
entries.en: As for the five colors harmonizing and the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, and dragon pattern has no equal.
entries.literal: As for the five colors harmonizing, the eight tones gathering in abundance—phoenix song is insufficient as a metaphor, dragon pattern has no equal.

entries.zh: 吳劄之論《周頌》，詎盡揄揚；
entries.en: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;
entries.literal: Wu Zha's discourse on the Zhou Eulogies—how could it fully praise you;

entries.zh: 郢客之奏《陽春》，誰能赴節？
entries.en: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?
entries.literal: the Ying guest's performance of 'Spring Sun'—who could match the measure?

entries.zh: 伏惟令王殿下，稟潤天潢，承輝日觀，雅道邁于東平，文藝高於北海。
entries.en: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.
entries.literal: I respectfully consider that Your Highness the Prince, endowed with the moisture of the Heavenly Ford and inheriting radiance from Sun-View Peak, surpasses the Prince of Dongping in refined learning and rises above the Prince of Beihai in literary art.

entries.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。
entries.en: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
entries.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

entries.zh: 雞樹騰聲，鵷池播美，望我清塵，悠然路絕。
entries.en: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my humble dust, the path between us is far and still.
entries.literal: Your fame rises at the Rooster Tree, your beauty spreads at the Egret Pool; gazing at my clear dust, the path between us is far and still.

entries.zh: 祖浚燕南贅客，河朔惰游，本無意于希顏，豈有心于慕藺。
entries.en: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer of the northern Yellow River region; I never intended to emulate Yan Hui, nor had any mind to admire Lin Xiangru.
entries.literal: Zujun is a superfluous guest south of Yan, an idle wanderer of the northern Yellow River region; I never intended to emulate Yan Hui, nor had any mind to admire Lin Xiangru.

entries.zh: 未嘗聚螢映雪，懸頭刺股。
entries.en: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snowlight, nor hung my head and pricked my thigh in study.
entries.literal: I have never gathered fireflies to read by snowlight, nor hung my head and pricked my thigh in study.

entries.zh: 讀《論》唯取一篇，披《莊》不過盈尺。
entries.en: Reading the Analects I take only one chapter; opening the Zhuangzi I read no more than a foot's length.
entries.literal: Reading the Analects I take only one chapter; opening the Zhuangzi I read no more than a foot's length.

entries.zh: 況復桑榆漸暮，藜藿屢空，舉燭無成，穿楊盡棄。
entries.en: Moreover my mulberry-and-elm years draw toward evening, my wild greens are often empty, raising the candle yields no success, and shooting through the willow is wholly abandoned.
entries.literal: Moreover my mulberry and elm years draw toward evening, my wild greens are often empty, raising the candle yields no success, and shooting through the willow is wholly abandoned.

entries.zh: 但以燕求馬首，薛養雞鳴，謬齒鴻儀，虛班驥ＩＺ。
entries.en: Yet like Yan seeking the horse's head, or Xue raising the cock's crow, I wrongly take rank among the grand rites and falsely occupy a place among fine steeds.
entries.literal: Yet like Yan seeking the horse's head, or Xue raising the cock's crow, I wrongly take rank among the grand rites and falsely occupy a place among fine steeds.

entries.zh: 挾太山而超海，比報德而非難；
entries.en: To clasp Mount Tai and leap over the sea—compared with repaying your kindness this would not be hard;
entries.literal: To clasp Mount Tai and leap over the sea—compared with repaying your kindness this would not be hard;

entries.zh: 堙昆侖以為池，匹酬恩而反易。
entries.en: to dam Mount Kunlun and make it a pool—matching your grace in return would instead be easy.
entries.literal: to dam Mount Kunlun and make it a pool—matching your grace in return would instead be easy.

entries.zh: 張文詡，河東人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenxu was a man of Hedong.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenxu was a man of Hedong.

entries.zh: 父琚，開皇中，為洹水令，以清正聞。
entries.en: His father Ju, during Kaihuang, served as magistrate of Huanshui and was known for integrity and uprightness.
entries.literal: His father Ju, during Kaihuang, served as magistrate of Huanshui and was known for integrity and uprightness.

entries.zh: 文詡博覽群書，特精《三禮》。
entries.en: Wenxu read broadly in all books and was especially expert in the Three Rituals.
entries.literal: Wenxu read broadly in all books and was especially expert in the Three Rituals.

entries.zh: 隋文帝方引天下名儒碩學之士，文詡時游太學，博士房暉遠等莫不推伏之。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Sui was then gathering renowned Confucian scholars and eminent learned men from throughout the realm; Wenxu was studying at the Imperial Academy, and Erudites such as Fang Huiyuan all deferred to him.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui was then gathering renowned Confucian scholars and eminent learned men from throughout the realm; Wenxu was then studying at the Imperial Academy, and Erudites such as Fang Huiyuan all deferred to him.

entries.zh: 書侍御史皇甫誕，一時朝彥，恆執弟子之禮，以所乘馬就學邀屈。
entries.en: Palace Attendant Censor Huangfu Dan, a leading figure of the court, always performed the rites of a disciple and used the horse he rode to invite Wenxu to study.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Huangfu Dan, a leading figure of the court, always performed the rites of a disciple and used the horse he rode to invite Wenxu to study.

entries.zh: 文詡遂每牽馬步進，意在不因人自致也。
entries.en: Wenxu therefore each time led the horse and walked on foot, intending not to advance himself through others.
entries.literal: Wenxu therefore each time led the horse and walked on foot, intending not to advance himself through others.

entries.zh: 右僕射蘇威聞而召之，與語大悅，勸令從官，文詡固辭。
entries.en: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard of him and summoned him; after conversing he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenxu firmly declined.
entries.literal: Right Vice Director Su Wei heard of him and summoned him; after conversing he was greatly pleased and urged him to take office, but Wenxu firmly declined.

entries.zh: 仁壽末，學廢，文詡策杖而歸，灌園為業。
entries.en: At the end of Renshou the academy was abolished; Wenxu returned leaning on a staff and made watering gardens his occupation.
entries.literal: At the end of Renshou the academy was abolished; Wenxu returned leaning on a staff and made watering gardens his occupation.

entries.zh: 州郡頻舉，皆不應命。
entries.en: Prefectures and commanderies repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered the summons.
entries.literal: Prefectures and commanderies repeatedly recommended him, but he never answered the summons.

entries.zh: 事母以孝聞。
entries.en: He was known for filial devotion to his mother.
entries.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother.

entries.zh: 每以德化人，鄉黨頗移風俗。
entries.en: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and neighborhood gradually changed their customs.
entries.literal: He always transformed people through virtue, and the village and neighborhood gradually changed their customs.

entries.zh: 嘗有人夜中竊刈其麥者，見而避之。
entries.en: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and stepped aside.
entries.literal: Once someone stole and reaped his wheat at night; Wenxu saw him and stepped aside.

entries.zh: 盜因感悟，棄麥而謝。
entries.en: The thief was moved by this, abandoned the wheat, and apologized.
entries.literal: The thief was moved by this, abandoned the wheat, and apologized.

entries.zh: 文詡慰諭之，自誓不言，固令持去。
entries.en: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore he would not speak of it, and firmly told him to take the wheat away.
entries.literal: Wenxu comforted and instructed him, swore he would not speak of it, and firmly told him to take the wheat away.

entries.zh: 經數年，盜者向鄉人說之，始為遠近所悉。
entries.en: After several years the thief told fellow villagers, and only then did those near and far come to know of it.
entries.literal: After several years the thief told fellow villagers, and only then did those near and far come to know of it.

entries.zh: 鄰家築牆，心有不直，文詡因毀舊堵以應之。
entries.en: When a neighbor built a wall that encroached inward, Wenxu tore down his old wall to accommodate him.
entries.literal: When a neighbor built a wall that was not straight, Wenxu therefore tore down his old wall to accommodate him.

entries.zh: 文詡常有腰疾，會醫者自言善禁，文詡令禁之，遂為刀所傷，至於頓伏床枕。
entries.en: Wenxu often suffered from a waist ailment; once a physician claimed skill in incantation-healing, and Wenxu had him perform it, but was wounded by a knife and collapsed on bed and pillow.
entries.literal: Wenxu often suffered from a waist ailment; once a physician claimed skill in incantation-healing, and Wenxu had him perform it, but was wounded by a knife and collapsed on bed and pillow.

entries.zh: 醫者叩頭請罪。
entries.en: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.
entries.literal: The physician kowtowed and begged forgiveness.

entries.zh: 文詡遽遣之，因為隱，謂妻子曰：「吾昨風眩，落坑所致。」
entries.en: Wenxu at once sent him away and concealed the matter, telling his wife and children: 'I had a dizzy spell yesterday and fell into a pit.'
entries.literal: Wenxu at once sent him away and concealed the matter, telling his wife and children: 'I had a dizzy spell yesterday and fell into a pit.'

entries.zh: 其掩人短，皆此類也。
entries.en: His way of concealing others' faults was all of this kind.
entries.literal: His concealing others' faults was all of this kind.

entries.zh: 州縣以其貧素，將加賑恤，輒辭不受。
entries.en: Because he was poor and plain, prefectures and counties were about to grant relief, but he always declined and would not accept.
entries.literal: Because he was poor and plain, prefectures and counties were about to grant relief, but he always declined and would not accept.

entries.zh: 嘗閒居無事，從容歎曰：「老冉冉而將至，恐修名之不立！」
entries.en: Once, idle at home with nothing to do, he sighed at ease and said: 'Old age slowly approaches—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!'
entries.literal: Once, idle at home with nothing to do, he sighed at ease and said: 'Old age slowly approaches—I fear a cultivated name will not be established!'

entries.zh: 以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。
entries.en: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
entries.literal: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

entries.zh: 終於家，鄉人為立碑頌，號曰張先生。
entries.en: He died at home; fellow villagers erected a stele in his praise and called him Master Zhang.
entries.literal: He died at home; fellow villagers erected a stele in his praise and called him Master Zhang.

entries.zh: 眭誇 馮亮 鄭修 崔廓 子賾 徐則 張文詡
entries.en: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, Cui Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu
entries.literal: Suikua, Feng Liang, Zheng Xiu, Cui Kuo, his son Ze, Xu Ze, and Zhang Wenxu

entries.zh: 成死，子湯立。
entries.en: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded him.
entries.literal: When Cheng died, his son Tang succeeded.

entries.zh: 乾明元年，齊廢帝以湯爲使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianming the Deposed Emperor of Qi invested Tang as holder of the staff of authority, colonel of the Eastern Yi, duke of Liaodong commandery, and king of Goguryeo.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianming, the Deposed Emperor of Qi made Tang Holder of the Staff, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.

entries.zh: 周建德六年，湯遣使至周，武帝以湯爲上開府儀同大將軍、遼東郡公、遼東王。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou, and Emperor Wu of Zhou invested him as Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Liaodong.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou; Emperor Wu of Zhou made Tang Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Liaodong.

entries.zh: 隋文帝受禪，湯遣使詣闕，進授大將軍，改封高麗王。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Tang sent envoys to court, was promoted to Grand General, and was re-invested as King of Goguryeo.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Tang sent envoys to the court; he was promoted to Grand General and re-invested as King of Goguryeo.

entries.zh: 自是，歲遣使朝貢不絕。
entries.en: From then on tribute envoys came every year without fail.
entries.literal: From this onward, tribute envoys were sent every year without interruption.

entries.zh: 高麗 百濟 新羅 勿吉 奚 契丹 室韋 豆莫婁 地豆幹 烏洛侯 流求 倭
entries.en: Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Wuji, Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didougan, Wuluohou, Liuqiu, and Japan
entries.literal: Goryeo, Baekje, Silla, Wuji, Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, Doumolou, Didougan, Wuluohou, Liuqiu, Japan

entries.zh: 高祖下
entries.en: The Founder, Part Two
entries.literal: The Founder (Part Two)

entries.zh: 永定元年冬十月乙亥，高祖即皇帝位于南郊，柴燎告天曰：「皇帝臣霸先，敢用玄牡昭告于皇皇后帝：梁氏以圮剝荐臻，歷運有極，欽若天應，以命于霸先。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding (557), on yihai day, the Founder took the throne at the Southern Suburb. He kindled the firewood offering and addressed Heaven: "Your subject Baxian, now Emperor, ventures to sacrifice a black bull and declare to the August Empress and August Emperor: The Liang dynasty lies in ruins, disaster heaped upon disaster, its mandate spent—yet Heaven's answer has come, and the charge is laid upon Baxian.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding, on yihai day, the Founder assumed the imperial dignity at the Southern Suburb. With firewood piled for the burnt offering he announced to Heaven: "The Emperor, your subject Baxian, dares to use a black bull to proclaim clearly to the August Empress and August Emperor: The House of Liang, its edifice crumbling, calamity piled upon calamity, its allotted span exhausted—reverently in accord with Heaven's response, the mandate was given to Baxian.

entries.zh: 夫肇有烝民，乃樹司牧，選賢與能，未常厥姓。
entries.en: When the people first arose, rulers were appointed over them; worth and ability, not bloodline alone, decided who would lead.
entries.literal: From the beginning there have been the multitude of people; therefore rulers were set over them, choosing the worthy and able—never always of one surname.

entries.zh: 放勛、重華之世，咸無意於受終，當塗、典午之君，雖有心於揖讓，皆以英才處萬乘，高勳御四海，故能大庇黔首，光宅區縣。
entries.en: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.
entries.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.

entries.zh: 有梁末運，仍葉遘屯，獯醜憑陵，久移神器，承聖在外，非能祀夏，天未悔禍，復罹寇逆，嫡嗣廢黜，宗枝僭詐，天地蕩覆，紀綱泯絕。
entries.en: In Liang's last days disaster followed disaster. Barbarian armies trampled the borders and the imperial regalia passed from hand to hand. Emperor Chengsheng languished in exile, unable to keep the altars of state; Heaven had not yet lifted the scourge, and rebels struck again. The rightful heir was cast aside; kinsmen seized power by deceit. Heaven and earth were overturned; law and order perished.
entries.literal: In the final fortune of Liang, misfortune still followed misfortune; savage foes leaned upon the borders, and for long the sacred vessel shifted. Emperor Chengsheng was abroad and could not sacrifice to Xia; Heaven had not yet repented the calamity, and again they suffered bandit invasions. The legitimate heir was deposed and discarded; collateral branches usurped by fraud. Heaven and earth were overturned; statutes and norms were extinguished.

entries.zh: 霸先爰初投袂，大拯橫流，重舉義兵，實戡多難，廢王立帝，寔有厥功，安國定社，用盡其力。
entries.en: The Founder first flung aside his robe and plunged into the flood to save the realm; again he raised righteous armies and truly cut through countless perils. He deposed one ruler and set up another—merit undeniable—and gave all his strength to secure the nation and its altars.
entries.literal: Baxian at the first cast aside his sleeve and greatly rescued the crosscurrent; again he raised the righteous army and truly conquered many hardships; deposing a king and establishing an emperor, he truly had merit therein; settling the state and fixing the altars, he exhausted his strength.

entries.zh: 是謂小康，方期大道。
entries.en: This was modest order; the Great Way still lay ahead.
entries.literal: This is called modest prosperity; one looks toward the Great Way.

entries.zh: 既而煙雲表色，日月呈瑞，緯聚東井，龍見譙邦，除舊布新，既彰玄象，遷虞事夏，且協謳訟，[2]九域八荒，同布衷款，百神群祀，皆有誠願。
entries.en: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.
entries.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.

entries.zh: 梁帝高謝萬邦，授以大寶，霸先自惟菲薄，讓德不嗣，至于再三，辭弗獲許。
entries.en: The Liang emperor abdicated with lofty grace and handed over the great seal. The Founder, judging himself unworthy, declined again and again; a third time he refused, yet consent was denied him.
entries.literal: The Liang Emperor, with lofty yielding, surrendered the myriad states and conferred the great treasure. Baxian, considering himself slight, yielded virtue and would not succeed; even to a third time, his refusal could not obtain consent.

entries.zh: 僉以百姓須主，萬機難曠，皇靈眷命，非可謙拒。
entries.en: All agreed that the people needed a ruler and the myriad affairs of state could not stand idle; Heaven's favor rested on him—humility was not permitted.
entries.literal: All said that the hundred surnames needed a lord and the myriad affairs could not be left vacant; the imperial numen favored the mandate—it could not be modestly refused.

entries.zh: 畏天之威，用膺嘉祚，永言夙志，能無慚德。
entries.en: In awe of Heaven's majesty he accepted the glorious mandate; yet remembering his lifelong modesty, how could he be free of shame?
entries.literal: In awe of Heaven's majesty, he received the fine fortune; ever mindful of long-held resolve, how could he be without shame in virtue?

entries.zh: 敬簡元辰，升壇受禪，告類上帝，用答民心，永保于我有陳。
entries.en: He reverently chose the auspicious day, ascended the altar, and received the abdication, reporting to the Supreme Lord to answer the people's hearts—may Chen endure forever.
entries.literal: Reverently selecting the first day, he ascended the altar and received the abdication, announcing his category to the August Lord, to answer the people's heart—forever to preserve our Chen.

entries.zh: 惟明靈是饗！」
entries.en: May the bright spirits accept this offering!"
entries.literal: May the bright spirits partake!"

entries.zh: 先是氛霧，晝夜晦冥，至于是日，景氣清晏，識者知有天道焉。
entries.en: Before this, miasma and fog had shrouded the land in unbroken gloom. On that day the air cleared and grew serene; the discerning knew Heaven's Way was at work.
entries.literal: Earlier there had been miasma and fog; day and night were dim and dark. On this day the atmosphere was clear and calm; those who knew recognized that Heaven's Way was at work.

entries.zh: 禮畢，輿駕還宮，臨太極前殿。
entries.en: When the rites were finished, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and halted before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and proceeded to the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「五德更運，帝王所以御天，三正相因，夏、殷所以宰世，雖色分辭翰，時異文質，揖讓征伐，迄用參差，而育德振民，義歸一揆。
entries.en: An edict declared: "The Five Virtues succeed one another, and thus emperors and kings hold Heaven's mandate. The Three Rectifications follow in turn, and thus Xia and Yin governed the world. Though ritual color and written style changed with the age, and abdication gave way to conquest as times required, the aim was always one: to nurture virtue and lift up the people.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The Five Virtues rotate in succession—therefore emperors and kings rule Heaven. The Three Rectifications follow one another—therefore Xia and Yin govern the age. Though colors differed in written edicts and times differed in pattern and substance, yielding and warfare, expeditions and punishments, were used in varying measure; yet to nurture virtue and stir the people, the principle returns to one standard.

entries.zh: 朕以寡昧，時屬艱危，國步屢屯，天維三絕，肆勤先后，拯厥橫流，藉將帥之功，兼猛士之力，一匡天下，再造黔黎。
entries.en: We, unworthy and obscure, came to power in grievous times. The throne stumbled again and again; Heaven's bonds were thrice severed. We labored for our ancestors' sake to stem the flood, leaning on our commanders' deeds and our warriors' might—once to restore the realm and again to remake the people.
entries.literal: We, slight and dim, at the time met with hardship and peril; the state's steps repeatedly met distress; Heaven's cords thrice snapped. Diligently we toiled for our forebears and rescued that crosscurrent, relying on our generals' merit and joining the fierce warriors' strength—once to set the realm right and twice to remake the black-haired people.

entries.zh: 梁氏以天祿永終，歷數攸在，遵與能之典，集大命于朕躬。
entries.en: The House of Liang, its heavenly mandate exhausted, its turn complete, followed the ancient canon of yielding to the worthy and laid the great charge upon Our person.
entries.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing ended forever, its sequence where it belonged, followed the canon of yielding to the able and gathered the great mandate upon Our person.

entries.zh: 顧惟菲德，辭不獲亮，式從天睠，俯協民心，受終文祖，升禋上帝，繼跡百王，君臨萬宇，若涉川水，罔知攸濟。
entries.en: Reflecting on Our meager worth, We could not refuse with honor; bowing to Heaven's favor and the people's will, We received the mandate from the culture-ancestor, ascended to worship the Supreme Lord, and took up the hundred kings' legacy to rule the world—like a man fording a river without knowing the far shore.
entries.literal: Looking back on Our slight virtue, Our refusal could not obtain clarity; following Heaven's favor, We bow to match the people's heart, receiving the end from the Culture Ancestor, ascending to offer to the August Lord, continuing the traces of the hundred kings, ruling over the ten thousand realms—like crossing river water, We know not where to ford.

entries.zh: 寶業初建，皇祚惟新，思俾惠澤，覃被億兆。
entries.en: Our dynasty is newly founded, Our fortune freshly renewed; We mean to spread gracious bounty to the hundred millions.
entries.literal: The precious enterprise newly founded, the imperial fortune newly renewed—We think to extend gracious favor and spread it over the hundred millions.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下，改梁太平二年為永定元年。
entries.en: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm, and let Liang's second year of Taiping be renamed the first year of Yongding.
entries.literal: Let there be a great amnesty for all under Heaven; change Liang's second year of Taiping to the first year of Yongding.

entries.zh: 賜民爵二級，文武二等。
entries.en: Grant the people two ranks of nobility and civil and military officials two grades of promotion.
entries.literal: Bestow on the people two ranks of nobility; on civil and military officials, two grades.

entries.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者人穀五斛。
entries.en: Give five hu of grain to each widower, widow, orphan, or solitary who cannot support himself.
entries.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves—five hu of grain per person.

entries.zh: 逋租宿債，皆勿復收。
entries.en: Overdue rents and old debts shall not be collected again.
entries.literal: Overdue rents and old debts—all shall not again be collected.

entries.zh: 其有犯鄉里清議贓汙淫盜者，皆洗除先注，與之更始。
entries.en: Those guilty of village scandal, corruption, debauchery, or theft shall have prior records erased and begin anew.
entries.literal: Those who have violated village pure criticism, corruption, lewdness, or theft—all shall wash away prior entries and be given a fresh start.

entries.zh: 長徒敕繫，特皆原之。
entries.en: Long-term prisoners held under imperial order are specially pardoned.
entries.literal: Long-term convicts under edict imprisonment—all are specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 亡官失爵，禁錮奪勞，一依舊典。」
entries.en: Loss of office, forfeiture of rank, and penalties of disgrace and barred honors shall follow the former statutes."
entries.literal: Loss of office and forfeiture of rank, prohibition and deprivation of honors—all follow the old statutes."

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「禮陳杞、宋，詩詠二客，弗臣之重，歷代斯敦。
entries.en: A second edict read: "The Rites enshrine the houses of Qi and Song; the Odes praise the two guest-lords—the ancient honor of not treating them as mere subjects, which every age has upheld.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "The Rites set forth Qi and Song; the Odes sing of the two guests—the weight of not treating them as subjects, each generation has honored this.

entries.zh: 梁氏欽若人祇，憲章在昔，濟河沈璧，高謝萬邦，茅賦所加，宜遵舊典。
entries.en: The House of Liang, reverent toward Heaven and the people, took its model from antiquity; crossing the river and casting the jade disk into the stream, it abdicated with lofty grace and surrendered the realm. The tribute of thatch we now confer shall follow the old precedent.
entries.literal: The House of Liang, reverently in accord with the people's lord, took its model from the past; crossing the river and sinking the jade disk, with lofty yielding it surrendered the myriad states—the thatch tribute conferred should follow the old canon.

entries.zh: 其以江陰郡奉梁主為江陰王，行梁正朔，車旗服色，一依前準，宮館資待，務盡優隆。」
entries.en: Let Jiangyin commandery be conferred to enfeoff the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, keeping Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and regalia as before; his palaces and stipends shall be maintained in full honor."
entries.literal: Let Jiangyin commandery be used to enfeoff the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, observing Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and dress all according to former standards; palace quarters and stipends shall be maintained with full generous elevation."

entries.zh: 又詔梁皇太后為江陰國太妃，皇后為江陰國妃。
entries.en: Another edict named the Liang empress dowager Grand Consort of the State of Jiangyin and the empress consort Consort of the State of Jiangyin.
entries.literal: Another edict made the Liang Empress Dowager Grand Princess of the State of Jiangyin and the Empress Consort Princess of Jiangyin.

entries.zh: 又詔百司依位攝職。
entries.en: Another edict ordered all offices to resume their duties according to rank.
entries.literal: Another edict ordered the hundred offices to assume their duties according to rank.

entries.zh: 庚辰，詔出佛牙於杜姥宅，集四部設無遮大會，高祖親出闕前禮拜。
entries.en: On gengchen day an edict brought the Buddha's tooth forth from the Du family's old residence. The four assemblies were gathered for a boundless great assembly, and the Founder came in person before the palace gate to bow in worship.
entries.literal: On gengchen day an edict ordered the Buddha's tooth brought forth from the Du family's old residence; the four assemblies were gathered for an unbounded great assembly, and the Founder personally came forth before the palace gate to bow in worship.

entries.zh: 初，齊故僧統法獻於烏纏國得之，常在定林上寺，梁天監末，為攝山慶雲寺沙門慧興保藏，慧興將終，以屬弟慧志，承聖末，慧志密送于高祖，至是乃出。
entries.en: Long before, Fazian, former Buddhist superintendent of Qi, had obtained it in Wuchan; it had remained at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian reign the monk Huixing of Qingyun Monastery on She Mountain kept it safe. On his deathbed Huixing entrusted it to his brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it displayed.
entries.literal: Earlier, Qi former Buddhist superintendent Fazian had obtained it in the Wuchan state; it had long been at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian era, Shramana Huixing of Sheshan Qingyun Monastery kept it in safekeeping. When Huixing was near death he entrusted it to his younger brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it brought forth.

entries.zh: 景子，輿駕幸鍾山祠蔣帝廟。
entries.en: On jingzi day the emperor visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.
entries.literal: On jingzi day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.

entries.zh: 戊寅，輿駕幸華林園，親覽詞訟，臨赦囚徒。
entries.en: On wuyin day the emperor went to Hualin Park, personally heard lawsuits, and pardoned prisoners on the spot.
entries.literal: On wuyin day the imperial carriage visited the Hualin Park, personally reviewing lawsuits and pardoning prisoners on the spot.

entries.zh: 己卯，分遣大使宣勞四方，下璽書敕州郡曰：「夫四王革代，商、周所以應天，五勝相推，軒、羲所以當運。
entries.en: On jimao day he sent great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters, issuing sealed letters of instruction to the provinces and commanderies: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thus answered Heaven; the Five Agents succeeded one another—Xuanyuan and Fuxi thus met their destined turn.
entries.literal: On jimao day he dispatched great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters and sent down imperial-seal letters instructing the provinces and commanderies, saying: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thereby answered Heaven; the Five Victories succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thereby met their fortune.

entries.zh: 梁德不造，喪亂積年，東夏崩騰，西都蕩覆。
entries.en: Liang's mandate failed; mourning and chaos lasted for years. The east erupted in rebellion; the western capital was overrun.
entries.literal: Liang's virtue was unmade; mourning and disorder piled up for years. The eastern domains collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was swept away.

entries.zh: 蕭勃干紀，非唯趙倫，侯景滔天，踰於劉載。
entries.en: Xiao Bo rebelled against the throne—his crime outdid Zhao Lun's. Hou Jing's outrage touched Heaven—it exceeded Liu Zai's.
entries.literal: Xiao Bo defied the statutes—he was not merely Zhao Lun. Hou Jing reached to Heaven—he surpassed Liu Zai.

entries.zh: 貞陽反篡，賊約連兵，江左累屬於鮮卑，金陵久非於梁國。
entries.en: Zhenyang seized the throne by treachery; rebels joined forces in league. The lands east of the Yangtze fell under Xianbei rule; Jinling for long was no longer Liang's.
entries.literal: Zhenyang turned traitor and usurped; the bandits' pact linked armies. The lands east of the Yangtze long belonged to the Xianbei; Jinling for long was no longer the land of Liang.

entries.zh: 有自氤氳混沌之世，[3]龍圖鳳紀之前，東漢興平之初，西朝永嘉之亂，天下分崩，未有若於梁朝者也。
entries.en: From the age of primordial chaos, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix annals, from Eastern Han's Xingping through Western Jin's Yongjia disaster—the realm has fractured, but never as ruinously as under Liang.
entries.literal: From the age of swirling chaos since primordial mist, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix record, from the beginning of Eastern Han's Xingping, through Western Jin's Yongjia turmoil—the realm split apart, never as in the Liang dynasty.

entries.zh: 朕以虛薄，屬當興運，自昔登庸，首清諸越，徐門浪泊，靡不征行，浮海乘山，所在戡定。
entries.en: We, unworthy and slight, came to power at a time of renewal. From our first rise we cleared the Yue lands; at Xumen and Langbo we left no foe unbeaten. Crossing seas and climbing mountains, we pacified wherever we marched.
entries.literal: We, empty and slight, met with the rising fortune. From old upon taking office We first cleared the Yue regions; Xumen and Langbo—none went unmarched upon. Crossing seas and scaling mountains, wherever We went was pacified.

entries.zh: 冒愬風塵，騁馳師旅，六延梁祀，十翦彊寇，豈曰人謀，皆由天啟。
entries.en: We braved dust and hardship and drove our armies hard—six times we prolonged Liang's rites, ten times we struck down mighty rebels. This was not human planning alone; Heaven opened the way.
entries.literal: Braving complaint and wind-blown dust, galloping with the army—we extended Liang's sacrifices six times and cut down powerful bandits tenfold. How could one call it human counsel alone? All was opened by Heaven.

entries.zh: 梁氏以天祿斯改，期運永終，欽若唐、虞，推其鼎玉，朕東西退讓，拜手陳辭，避舜子於箕山之陽，求支伯於滄洲之野，而公卿敦逼，率土翹惶，天命難稽，遂享嘉祚。
entries.en: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne.
entries.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.

entries.zh: 今月乙亥，升禮太壇，言念遷
entries.en: This month, on yihai, We performed the rites at the Great Altar, mindful of the transfer
entries.literal: This month on yihai We ascended the rites at the Great Altar, thinking of the transfer

entries.en: (jiong)
entries.literal: (jiong)

entries.zh: 桐，[4]但有慚德。
entries.en: Tong, [4] yet We are ashamed of Our meager worth.
entries.literal: Tong, [4] yet We have shame in virtue.

entries.zh: 自梁氏將末，頻月亢陽，火運斯終，秋霖奄降。
entries.en: As Liang neared its end, drought blazed for months; the fire cycle closed, and autumn rains burst forth.
entries.literal: From the time Liang neared its end, for months the sun stood drought-strong; the fire cycle ended, and autumn rains suddenly fell.

entries.zh: 翌日成禮，圓丘宿設，埃雲晚霽，星象夜張。
entries.en: On the morrow the rites were complete. The round altar had been prepared overnight; evening dust clouds cleared and the stars shone forth.
entries.literal: The next day the rites were completed; the round mound was set overnight. Dust clouds cleared at evening; the stars spread at night.

entries.zh: 朝景重輪，泫三危之膏露，晨光合璧，帶五色之卿雲。
entries.en: At dawn the sun showed a double halo, dripping the sacred dew of Mount Sanwei; morning light joined like paired jades, trailing five-colored auspicious clouds.
entries.literal: The morning scene showed a doubled sun-disk; it dripped the fat dew of Mount Sanwei. The morning light joined jade disks; it bore five-colored minister-clouds.

entries.zh: 顧惟寡薄，彌慚休祉，昧旦丕顯，方思至治。
entries.en: Reflecting on Our slight worth, We are the more ashamed of such blessing. From cockcrow We labor for good government and now ponder how best to rule.
entries.literal: Looking back on Our slightness, We are the more ashamed of this fine blessing. From cockcrow We strive for greatness; We now think of utmost governance.

entries.zh: 卿等擁旄方岳，相任股肱，剖符名守，[5]方寄恤隱。
entries.en: You who bear command in the provinces are Our arms and thighs; you who hold the tallies as governors [5] are charged with pity for the people.
entries.literal: You, bearing halberds in the border provinces, share in responsibility as Our arms and thighs; with divided tallies as famed administrators, [5] We entrust you with compassionate care for the people.

entries.zh: 王曆惟新，念有欣慶，想深求民瘼，務在廉平，愛惠以撫孤貧，威刑以御彊猾。
entries.en: The calendar is newly renewed—share in the people's joy. Probe deeply for their hardships; keep government honest and fair. Show kindness to orphans and the poor; use stern law against the violent and cunning.
entries.literal: The imperial calendar is newly renewed—think of the people's joy. Deeply seek the people's afflictions; strive for integrity and fairness. Cherish and favor to comfort the orphaned and poor; authority and punishment to restrain the violent and cunning.

entries.zh: 若有萑蒲之盜，[6]或犯戎商，山谷之酋，擅彊幽險，皆從肆赦，咸使知聞。
entries.en: Reed-marsh bandits [6] who break martial law, mountain chiefs who lord over hidden passes—all are included in the amnesty; make this known everywhere.
entries.literal: If there are reed-marsh bandits, [6] or offenders against military law, chieftains of mountain valleys who tyrannize in hidden defiles—all are within the general pardon; let all know this.

entries.zh: 如或迷途，俾在無貸。
entries.en: Those who still stray from the path shall receive no mercy.
entries.literal: If any still lose the way, they shall have no pardon.

entries.zh: 今遣使人具宣往旨，念思善政，副此虛懷。」
entries.en: We now send envoys to proclaim Our intent in full. Devise good government and answer Our earnest hope."
entries.literal: Now We send envoys to proclaim fully the former intent. Think on good government and answer this empty heart."

entries.zh: 辛巳，追尊皇考曰景皇帝，廟號太祖；
entries.en: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, with temple name Taizu;
entries.literal: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, temple name Taizu;

entries.zh: 皇妣董太夫人曰安皇后。
entries.en: and the Founder's late mother, Lady Dong, as Empress An.
entries.literal: the Founder's late mother Lady Dong as Empress An.

entries.zh: 追謚前夫人錢氏號為昭皇后，世子克為孝懷太子。
entries.en: The former primary consort of the Qian clan was posthumously titled Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was named Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.
entries.literal: The former primary consort, Lady Qian, was given the posthumous title Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was titled Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 立夫人章氏為皇后。
entries.en: Lady Zhang was installed as empress.
entries.literal: Lady Zhang was established as Empress.

entries.zh: 癸未，尊景帝陵曰瑞陵，昭皇后陵曰嘉陵，依梁初園陵故事。
entries.en: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was styled Ruiling and Empress Zhao's tomb Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.
entries.literal: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was honored as Ruiling and Empress Zhao's tomb as Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.

entries.zh: 立刪定郎，治定律令。
entries.en: Officers for revision and codification were appointed to compile laws and ordinances.
entries.literal: Revision and codification officers were established to compile and fix laws and ordinances.

entries.zh: 戊子，遷景皇帝神主祔于太廟。
entries.en: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was enshrined in the Grand Temple.
entries.literal: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was moved to take its place in the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 辛卯，以中權將軍、開府儀同三司、丹陽尹王沖為左光祿大夫。
entries.en: On xinmao day Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and Danyang intendant, was made left grand master of the palace.
entries.literal: On xinmao day the Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Danyang Intendant Wang Chong was made Left Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 癸巳，追贈皇兄梁故散騎常侍、平北將軍、兗州刺史[7]長城縣公道譚驃騎大將軍、太尉，封始興郡王；
entries.en: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, the late Liang scattered-cavalry palace attendant, general who pacifies the north, and Yanzhou inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously made grand general of agile cavalry and grand tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;
entries.literal: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, Liang former Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Yanzhou Inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously honored as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;

entries.zh: 弟梁故侍中、驃騎將軍、南徐州刺史武康縣侯[8]休先車騎大將軍、司徒，封南康郡王。
entries.en: his younger brother, the late Liang palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and South Xuzhou inspector [8] Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county, was posthumously made grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.
entries.literal: his younger brother, Liang former Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and South Xuzhou Inspector Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county [8] was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.

entries.zh: 二年春正月乙未，詔曰：「夫設官分職，因事重輕，羽儀車馬，隨時隆替，晉之五校，鳴笳啟途，漢之九卿，傳呼並迾，虞官夏禮，豈曰同科，殷朴周文，固無恆格。
entries.en: In spring of the second year, on yiwei day of the first month, an edict declared: "Offices and duties are weighed by the business at hand; ceremonial escorts rise and fall with the age. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-pipe to clear the road; Han's nine ministers had heralds cry out as they passed—Yu and Xia rites were not one model; Yin austerity and Zhou ornament had no fixed pattern.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on yiwei day, an edict said: "Setting offices and dividing duties follows the weight of affairs; feathered banners and chariots and horses rise and fall with the times. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-whistle to open the road; Han's Nine Ministers had runners call out together as they passed—rites of Yu and Xia, how could they be one standard? Yin simplicity and Zhou pattern surely have no fixed rule.

entries.zh: 朕膺茲寶歷，代是天工，留念官方，庶允時衷。
entries.en: We have received the sacred succession and take up Heaven's task; We mean to restore official ranks to suit the present need.
entries.literal: We have received this precious succession, replacing Heaven's work; We keep in mind the official ranks, that they may match the time's core.

entries.zh: 梁天監中，左右驍騎領朱衣直閤，並給儀從，北徐州刺史
entries.en: Under Liang's Tianjian reign, the left and right valiant cavalry led the vermilion-robed direct attendants and were both granted ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou inspector
entries.literal: In Liang's Tianjian era, the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry led the Vermilion-Robed Direct Attendants and were both given ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou Inspector

entries.en: (chang)
entries.literal: (chang)

entries.zh: 昌義之
entries.en: Chang Yizhi
entries.literal: Chang Yizhi

entries.en: (chu)
entries.literal: (chu)

entries.zh: 首為此職。
entries.en: was the first to hold this office.
entries.literal: was the first to hold this office.

entries.zh: [10]亂離歲久，朝典不存，後生年少，希聞舊則。
entries.en: [10] Years of chaos have effaced the court's precedents; the young scarcely know the old rules.
entries.literal: [10] Disorder and separation for years on end—the court canon did not survive. The young of later generations scarcely heard the old rules.

entries.zh: 今去左右驍騎，宜通文武，文官則用腹心，武官則用功臣，所給儀從，同太子二衛率。
entries.en: We now abolish the left and right valiant cavalry and make the post serve both civil and military ranks—civil officials drawn from trusted intimates, military from meritorious commanders—with escorts equal to the crown prince's two guard commanders.
entries.literal: Now abolishing the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, they should unite civil and military; for civil officials use trusted intimates, for military officials use meritorious ministers. The ceremonial escort granted shall match the crown prince's two guard commanders.

entries.zh: 此外眾官，尚書詳為條制。」
entries.en: For all other offices the Masters of Writing shall draft detailed regulations."
entries.literal: For other offices as well, the Masters of Writing shall draw up detailed regulations.

entries.zh: 車騎將軍、開府儀同三司侯瑱進位司空，中權將軍、開府儀同三司、新除左光祿大夫王沖為太子少傅。
entries.en: Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, was promoted to minister of works; Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and newly appointed left grand master of the palace, became junior tutor of the crown prince.
entries.literal: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Tian advanced in rank to Minister of Works; Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and newly appointed Left Grand Master of the Palace Wang Chong became Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 左衛將軍徐世譜為護軍將軍，南兗州刺史吳明徹進號安南將軍，衡州刺史歐陽頠進號鎮南將軍。
entries.en: Xu Shipu, left guard general, became general who protects the army; Wu Mingche, South Yanzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Ouyang Wei, Hengzhou inspector, was promoted to general who garrisons the south.
entries.literal: Left Guard General Xu Shipu became General Who Protects the Army; South Yanzhou Inspector Wu Mingche advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South; Hengzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 辛丑，輿駕親祠南郊。
entries.en: On xinchou day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Southern Suburb.
entries.literal: On xinchou day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕受命君臨，初移星琯，孟陬嘉月，備禮泰壇，景候昭華，人祗允慶，思令億兆，咸與惟新。
entries.en: An edict declared: "We received the mandate and now rule the realm; the calendar has newly turned. In the auspicious first month We completed the rites at the Great Altar. The seasons showed bright signs; Heaven and the people rejoiced together. We mean for the hundred millions to share in this renewal.
entries.literal: An edict said: "We received the mandate and rule as lord; the stars have newly shifted. In the first month of auspicious spring the full rites were performed at the Great Altar. The seasonal signs were bright and splendid; the people's lord approved the celebration. We think to make the hundred millions all share in renewal.

entries.zh: 且往代祅氛，于今猶梗，軍機未息，徵賦咸繁，事不獲已，久知下弊，言念黔黎，無忘寢食。
entries.en: Yet the evil vapors of former days still linger; armies have not rested; levies remain heavy. Necessity alone drove this—we have long known the people's hardship. When We think of the common folk, We cannot sleep in peace.
entries.literal: Moreover, demonic vapors of former ages still obstruct today; military affairs have not ceased; levies and corvée are all heavy. Affairs could not be otherwise—we have long known the harm below. Speaking of the black-haired people, We cannot forget them even in sleep.

entries.zh: 夫罪無輕重，已發覺未發覺，在今昧爽以前，皆赦除之。
entries.en: Crimes light or heavy, discovered or not—before dawn today all are pardoned.
entries.literal: Crimes, whether light or heavy, already discovered or not yet discovered—before dawn today all are pardoned and removed.

entries.zh: 西寇自王琳以下，並許返迷，一無所問。
entries.en: Western rebels from Wang Lin downward may return to the fold without question.
entries.literal: Western bandits from Wang Lin downward—all are permitted to return from error; nothing shall be questioned.

entries.zh: 近所募義軍，本擬西寇，並宜解遣，留家附業。
entries.en: Volunteer armies lately raised against the western foe shall be disbanded and sent home to their fields.
entries.literal: Recently recruited righteous armies, originally intended for the western bandits, should all be dismissed and sent home to their occupations.

entries.zh: 晚訂軍資未送者並停，元年軍糧逋餘者原其半。
entries.en: Military supplies still undelivered are cancelled; half the surplus grain levied in the first year is forgiven.
entries.literal: Military supplies ordered late and not yet delivered—all are halted. Surplus grain levied in the first year—half is remitted.

entries.zh: 州郡縣軍戍並不得輒遣使民閒，務存優養。
entries.en: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrisons must not send agents among the people without authorization; they shall treat the people with care.
entries.literal: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrison troops must not on their own dispatch envoys among the people; they shall strive to preserve generous care.

entries.zh: 若有侵擾，嚴為法制。」
entries.en: Whoever harasses the people shall be punished under strict law."
entries.literal: If there is harassment, the law shall be sternly enforced."

entries.zh: 乙巳，輿駕親祠北郊。
entries.en: On yisi day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
entries.literal: On yisi day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.

entries.zh: 甲辰，振遠將軍、梁州刺史張立表稱去乙亥歲八月，[11]丹徒、蘭陵二縣界遺山側，一旦因濤水涌生，沙漲，周旋千餘頃，並膏腴，堪墾植。
entries.en: On jiachen day Zhang Li, general who quells the distance and Liangzhou inspector, reported that in the eighth month of the past yihai year, [11] beside a remnant hill on the border of Dantu and Lanling, tidal flood had suddenly thrown up sand over a thousand qing of rich soil fit for cultivation.
entries.literal: On jiachen day, General Who Quells the Distance and Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Li memorialized that in the eighth month of the year before last, yihai, [11] on the flank of a remnant mountain at the border of Dantu and Lanling commanderies, all at once because of surging tide-waters sand piled up, circling more than a thousand qing, all fertile and fit for opening to cultivation.

entries.zh: 戊午，輿駕親祠明堂。
entries.en: On wuwu day the emperor personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
entries.literal: On wuwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

entries.zh: 十一月景申，詔曰：「東都齊國，義乃親賢，西漢城陽，事兼功烈。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict declared: "The eastern capital honored Qi for kinship and worth together; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang joined merit with family bond.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict said: "The eastern capital's State of Qi honored kinship as worthy; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang combined merit with affection.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍、使持節、都督會稽等十郡諸軍事、宣毅將軍、會稽太守長城縣侯蒨，學尚清優，神宇凝正，文參禮樂，武定妖氛，心力謀猷，為家治國，擁旄作守，期月有成，辟彼關河，[9]功踰蕭、寇，萑蒲之盜，自反耕農，篁竹之豪，用稟聲朔。
entries.en: Scattered-cavalry palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies, general who proclaims martial valor, and Kuaiji administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng—his learning is pure and refined, his bearing grave and correct. In civil affairs he upholds ritual and music; in war he quells rebellion. With heart and stratagem he has ordered home and state alike. As territorial defender, within a month he brought order. On the frontier passes [9] his merit outdid Xiao He and Kou Xun; marsh bandits returned to the plow; mountain lords accepted Our calendar.
entries.literal: Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies' military affairs, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, and Kuaiji Administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng county—his learning esteems pure refinement; his spirit and bearing are concentrated and correct. In letters he joins ritual and music; in arms he settles demonic vapors. With heart-strength and stratagems he governs the family and orders the state. Bearing the halberd as defender, within a month he had achievement. Opening those border passes, [9] his merit surpassed Xiao and Kou; reed-marsh bandits returned of themselves to farming; bamboo-grove magnates submitted to Our sound and calendar.

entries.zh: 朕以虛寡，屬當興運，提彼三尺，賓于四門，王業艱難，賴乎此子，宜隆上爵，稱是元功。
entries.en: We, unworthy and alone, came to power in a time of renewal. With sword in hand We opened the four gates to talent. The founding of the dynasty was arduous—we lean on this son. Let him receive exalted rank worthy of his foremost merit.
entries.literal: We, empty and few, met the rising fortune. Taking up the three-foot [sword] We received guests at the four gates. The royal enterprise was hard and perilous—we rely on this son. Let him receive lofty rank fitting this primary merit.

entries.zh: 可封臨川郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: Let him be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: He may be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan, fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 兄子梁中書侍郎頊襲封始興王，弟子梁中書侍郎曇朗襲封南康王，禮秩一同正王。」
entries.en: His nephew Xu, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; his younger brother's son Tanlang, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited as King of Nankang—their ritual standing equal to that of reigning kings."
entries.literal: The elder brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Xu, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; the younger brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Tanlang, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Nankang—their ritual ranks the same as full kings.

entries.zh: 己亥，甘露降于鍾山松林，彌滿巖谷。
entries.en: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan until cliffs and valleys were full.
entries.literal: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan, filling the cliffs and valleys.

entries.zh: 庚子，開善寺沙門採之以獻，敕頒賜群臣。
entries.en: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed among the ministers.
entries.literal: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed to the ministers.

entries.zh: 景辰，以鎮西將軍、南豫州刺史徐度為鎮右將軍、領軍將軍。
entries.en: On jingchen day Xu Du, general who pacifies the west and South Yuzhou inspector, was made general who pacifies the right and commander of the palace guards.
entries.literal: On jingchen day the General Who Pacifies the West and South Yuzhou Inspector Xu Du was made General Who Pacifies the Right and Commander of the Palace Guards.

entries.zh: 庚申，京師大火。
entries.en: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.
entries.literal: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.

entries.zh: 十二月庚辰，皇后謁太廟。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the empress visited the Grand Temple.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the Empress visited the Grand Temple.

entries.zh: 三月甲午，詔曰：「罰不及嗣，自古通典，罪疑惟輕，布在方策。
entries.en: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict declared: "Punishment does not fall on heirs—so the ancients taught; when guilt is in doubt, favor mercy—so the law books say.
entries.literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict said: "Punishment does not reach the sons—this is an ancient universal canon; when guilt is doubtful, lean toward leniency—it is set forth in the statutes.

entries.zh: 沈泰反覆無行，遐邇所知，昔有微功，仍荷朝寄，剖符名郡，推轂累藩，漢口班師，還居方岳，良田有逾於四百，食客不止於三千，富貴顯榮，政當如此。
entries.en: Shen Tai was treacherous and faithless, known throughout the realm. He had once done minor service and still held the court's trust; enfeoffed in a great commandery, promoted through many frontier posts. After the Hankou campaign he returned to provincial command. His estates ran to four hundred fields; his retainers to three thousand—such were the rewards of his rank.
entries.literal: Shen Tai was fickle and without conduct, known far and near. In the past he had slight merit and still bore the court's trust; with divided tally he held a famed commandery, with chariot-shaft he was pushed up through many border posts. When the army withdrew from Hankou he returned to a territorial post. Good fields exceeded four hundred; retainers numbered no fewer than three thousand—wealth, honor, and glory ought indeed to be thus.

entries.zh: 鬼害其盈，天奪之魄，無故猖狂，自投獯醜。
entries.en: His pride invited ruin; Heaven withdrew his wits. Without provocation he rebelled and cast himself among the barbarians.
entries.literal: Ghosts harmed his fullness; Heaven took his soul. Without cause he ran wild and threw himself among the savage foes.

entries.zh: 雖復知人則哲，惟帝其難，光武有蔽於龐萌，魏武不知於于禁，但令朝廷無我負人。
entries.en: Even the wise err in judging men—only an emperor finds it hardest. Guangwu was deceived by Pang Meng; Cao Cao misread Yu Jin. Let the court never say We wronged Our servants.
entries.literal: Though again to know men is wise and only the emperor finds it hard—Guangwu was blinded regarding Pang Meng; Weiwu did not know Yu Jin—only let the court have no case of Our failing others.

entries.zh: 其部曲妻兒各令復業，所在及軍人若有恐脅侵掠者，皆以劫論。
entries.en: His soldiers' families shall return to their trades. Any trooper who threatens or loots the people shall be punished as a brigand.
entries.literal: His troops' wives and children are each ordered to resume their occupations. Wherever soldiers have intimidated or plundered, all are to be prosecuted as bandits.

entries.zh: 若有男女口為人所藏，並許詣臺申訴。
entries.en: Anyone held in secret bondage may appeal at court.
entries.literal: If any men or women are hidden by others, all are permitted to come to the capital to appeal.

entries.zh: 若樂隨臨川王及節將立效者，悉皆聽許。」
entries.en: Those who wish to serve the King of Linchuan or other commanders in earning merit may do so."
entries.literal: If any wish to follow the King of Linchuan and the commanders bearing staffs to render merit, all are permitted."

entries.zh: 乙卯，高祖幸後堂聽訟，還於橋上觀山水，賦詩示群臣。
entries.en: On yimao day the Founder heard cases in the rear hall; on his way back he paused on the bridge to take in the landscape and wrote a poem for his ministers.
entries.literal: On yimao day the Founder visited the rear hall to hear lawsuits; returning, on the bridge he viewed mountains and waters and composed a poem to show the assembled ministers.

entries.zh: 是月，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊于郢州。
entries.en: That month Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang, Prince of Yongjia of Liang, at Yingzhou.
entries.literal: That month Wang Lin installed Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, at Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 八月景寅，以廣梁郡為陳留郡。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was renamed Chenliu.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was made Chenliu commandery.

entries.zh: 辛未，詔臨川王蒨西討，[13]以舟師五萬發自京師，輿駕幸冶城寺親送焉。
entries.en: On xinwei day an edict sent the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign. [13] With fifty thousand sailors he sailed from the capital, and the emperor went in person to Ye City Monastery to see him off.
entries.literal: On xinwei day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign; [13] with a fleet of fifty thousand he set out from the capital, and the imperial carriage went to Ye City Monastery to see him off in person.

entries.zh: 前開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史周文育，前鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史、新除開府儀同三司侯安都等於王琳所逃歸，自劾廷尉，即日引見，並宥之。
entries.en: Zhou Wenyü, former grand mentor with staff and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Hou Andu, former general who pacifies the north, inspector of South Xuzhou, and newly made grand mentor with staff, who had escaped Wang Lin, presented themselves to the court of punishments to confess fault; that day they were received and pardoned.
