entries.literal: Former Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and South Yuzhou Inspector Zhou Wenyü, and former General Who Pacifies the North, South Xuzhou Inspector, and newly appointed Grand Mentor with Staff Hou Andu, who had escaped from Wang Lin's custody, impeached themselves before the Court for Punishments; that same day they were received in audience and all were pardoned.

entries.zh: 戊寅，詔復文育等本官。
entries.en: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former posts.
entries.literal: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former offices.

entries.zh: 壬午，追封皇子立為豫章王，諡曰獻；
entries.en: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;
entries.literal: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;

entries.zh: 權為長沙王，諡曰思；
entries.en: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;
entries.literal: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;

entries.zh: 長女為永世公主，諡曰懿。
entries.en: and the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.
entries.literal: the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.

entries.zh: 謝哲反命，王琳請還鎮湘川，詔追眾軍緩其伐。
entries.en: Xie Zhe returned from his mission. Wang Lin asked to go back and hold the Xiang River region; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.
entries.literal: Xie Zhe returned with a contrary mandate. Wang Lin asked to return and hold Xiang River; an edict recalled the armies and suspended the campaign.

entries.zh: 癸未，西討眾軍至自大雷。
entries.en: On guiwei day the western expedition reached Great Thunder.
entries.literal: On guiwei day the western campaign armies arrived from Great Thunder.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以信威將軍、江州刺史周迪為開府儀同三司，進號平南將軍。
entries.en: On dinghai day Zhou Di, trustworthy and martial general and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes and promoted to general who pacifies the south.
entries.literal: On dinghai day the Trustworthy and Martial General and Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 改南徐州所領南蘭陵郡復為東海郡。
entries.en: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was restored as Donghai.
entries.literal: South Lanling commandery under South Xuzhou was again made Donghai commandery.

entries.zh: 夏四月甲子，輿駕親祠太廟。
entries.en: On jiazi in the fourth month of summer, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiazi, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 乙丑，江陰王薨，詔遣太宰弔祭，司空監護喪事，凶禮所須，隨由備辦。
entries.en: On yichou, the Prince of Jiangyin died. An edict sent the Grand Steward to offer condolences and sacrifices, placed the Minister of Works in charge of the funeral, and ordered that everything required for the mourning rites be supplied as needed.
entries.literal: On yichou, the Prince of Jiangyin died; an edict sent the Grand Steward to offer condolences and sacrifices, had the Minister of Works supervise the funeral affairs, and ordered that whatever the mourning rites required be supplied according to need.

entries.zh: 以梁武林侯蕭諮息季卿嗣為江陰王。
entries.en: Jiqing, son of Xiao Zhi (Liang Marquis of Wulin), was made successor as Prince of Jiangyin.
entries.literal: Xiao Zhi's son Jiqing, of the Liang Marquis of Wulin, was made to succeed as Prince of Jiangyin.

entries.zh: 景寅，輿駕幸石頭，餞司空侯瑱。
entries.en: On bingyin, the emperor visited Shitou and gave a farewell banquet for Hou Tian, the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: On bingyin, the imperial carriage visited Shitou and held a farewell banquet for Hou Tian, Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 戊辰，重雲殿東鴟尾有紫煙屬天。
entries.en: On wuchen, purple smoke rose to the sky from the eastern chiwei roof ornament of Chongyun Hall.
entries.literal: On wuchen, from the eastern chiwei roof ornament of Chongyun Hall, purple smoke reached up to the sky.

entries.zh: 五月乙未，京師地震。
entries.en: On yiwei in the fifth month, an earthquake struck the capital.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on yiwei, the capital had an earthquake.

entries.zh: 癸丑，齊廣陵南城主張顯和、長史張僧那各率其所部入附。
entries.en: On guichou, Zhang Xianhe, commander of Qi's Southern Guangling city, and the chief secretary Zhang Sengna each led his command in submission.
entries.literal: On guichou, Zhang Xianhe, commander of Qi's Southern Guangling city, and Zhang Sengna, the chief secretary, each led the troops under his command and came over in submission.

entries.zh: 辛酉，輿駕幸大莊嚴寺捨身。
entries.en: On xinyou, the emperor visited Dazhuangyan Monastery and performed the Buddhist rite of offering himself.
entries.literal: On xinyou, the imperial carriage visited Dazhuangyan Monastery and offered his body.

entries.zh: 壬戌，群臣表請還宮。
entries.en: On renxu, the assembled ministers submitted a memorial asking him to return to the palace.
entries.literal: On renxu, the assembled ministers memorialized requesting that he return to the palace.

entries.zh: 秋七月戊戌，輿駕幸石頭，親送填等。
entries.en: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the emperor went to Stone City and personally saw off Hou Tian and the commanders.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the imperial carriage went to Stone City and personally sent off Tian and the others.

entries.zh: 己亥，江州刺史周迪擒王琳將李孝欽、樊猛、余孝頃于工塘。
entries.en: On jihai day Zhou Di, inspector of Jiangzhou, took Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing at Gongtang.
entries.literal: On jihai day Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di captured Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing at Gongtang.

entries.zh: 甲辰，遣吏部尚書謝哲諭王琳。
entries.en: On jiachen day Xie Zhe, minister of personnel, was dispatched to address Wang Lin.
entries.literal: On jiachen day the Minister of Personnel Xie Zhe was sent to instruct Wang Lin.

entries.zh: 甲寅，嘉禾一穗六岐生五城。
entries.en: On jiayin day a six-tined ear of grain appeared at Wucheng.
entries.literal: On jiayin day at Wucheng a single stalk of grain with six tines grew.

entries.zh: 初，侯景之平也，火焚太極殿，承聖中議欲營之，獨闕一柱，至是有樟木大十八圍，長四丈五尺，流泊陶家後渚，監軍鄒子度以聞。
entries.en: When Hou Jing fell, fire had destroyed the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. Under Emperor Chengsheng the court planned to rebuild it but lacked a single pillar. Now a camphor eighteen spans around and four zhang five chi long drifted to the Tao family's rear landing; the supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Hou Jing was pacified, fire had burned the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate. In the Chengsheng era deliberation wished to rebuild it, but alone one pillar was lacking. Now there was a camphor tree eighteen arm-spans around and four zhang five chi long, drifting to moor at the rear ford of the Tao household. Supervising general Zou Zidu reported it.

entries.zh: 詔中書令沈眾兼起部尚書，少府卿蔡儔兼將作大匠，起太極殿。
entries.en: An edict named Shen Zhong, director of the central secretariat, concurrent director of the ministry that raises works, and Cai Chou, junior chamberlain for the palace treasury, concurrent director of works, to rebuild the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Central Secretariat Director Shen Zhong also to serve as Director of the Ministry that Raises Works, and Junior Chamberlain for the Palace Treasury Cai Chou also to serve as Director of Works, to raise the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 冬十月庚午，遣鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司周文育都督眾軍出豫章，討余孝勱。
entries.en: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Zhou Wenyü, pacifying south general and grand mentor with staff, was sent from Yuzhang at the head of the armies against Yu Xiaoqing.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Pacifying South General and Grand Mentor with Staff Zhou Wenyü was sent as commander-in-chief of the armies to march out of Yuzhang to attack Yu Xiaoqing.

entries.zh: 乙亥，輿駕幸莊嚴寺，發金光明經題。
entries.en: On yihai day the emperor went to Zhuangyan Monastery to inaugurate the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.
entries.literal: On yihai day the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery and opened the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以仁威將軍、高州刺史黃法𣰋為開府儀同三司，[14]進號鎮南將軍。
entries.en: On dingyou day Huang Fa Tu, benevolent and martial general and inspector of Gaozhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes [14] and promoted to general who guards the south.
entries.literal: On dingyou day the Benevolent and Martial General and Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fa Tu was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes [14] and promoted to General Who Guards the South.

entries.zh: [15]甲寅，太極殿成，匠各給復。
entries.en: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was finished; every craftsman was granted tax and labor exemption.
entries.literal: [15] On jiayin day the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate was completed; each craftsman was given exemption from corvée.

entries.zh: 六月己巳，詔司空侯瑱、領軍將軍徐度率舟師為前軍，以討王琳。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Hou Tian, minister of works, and Xu Du, palace bulwark general, to lead the fleet as vanguard against Wang Lin.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Minister of Works Hou Tian and Palace Bulwark General Xu Du to lead the fleet as the vanguard army to attack Wang Lin.

entries.zh: 十二月庚申，侍中、安東將軍臨川王蒨率百僚朝前殿，拜上牛酒。
entries.en: On gengshen day Qian, king of Linchuan, palace attendant and pacifying east general, led the hundred offices to the front hall to offer oxen and wine.
entries.literal: On gengshen day the Palace Attendant and Pacifying East General, the King of Linchuan Qian, led the hundred offices to the front hall of the palace to bow and present oxen and wine.

entries.zh: 甲子，輿駕幸大莊嚴寺，設無遮大會，捨乘輿法物。
entries.en: On jiazi day the emperor went to the Great Zhuangyan Monastery for a boundless great assembly and gave up the imperial carriage and ritual regalia.
entries.literal: On jiazi day the imperial carriage visited the Great Zhuangyan Monastery and held an unbounded great assembly, donating the imperial carriage and ritual objects.

entries.zh: 群臣備法駕奉迎，即日輿駕還宮。
entries.en: Ministers with full ceremonial escort came to welcome him; that day the emperor returned to the palace.
entries.literal: The assembled ministers with full ritual carriages came to welcome him; that same day the imperial carriage returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 景寅，高祖於太極殿東堂宴群臣，設金石之樂，以路寢告成也。
entries.en: On jingyin day the Founder feasted his ministers in the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate with full orchestra, celebrating completion of the inner palace.
entries.literal: On yingyin day the Founder at the eastern hall of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate feasted the assembled ministers and set out metal and stone music, because the inner chamber dwelling was reported complete.

entries.zh: 壬申，割吳郡鹽官、海鹽、前京三縣置海寧郡，屬揚州。
entries.en: On renshen day Haining commandery was carved from Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing in Wu commandery and placed under Yangzhou.
entries.literal: On renshen day from Wu commandery's Yanguan, Haiyan, and Qianjing counties Haining commandery was established, subordinate to Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 以安成所部廣興六洞置安樂郡。
entries.en: From the six caves of Guangxing in Ancheng, Anle commandery was established.
entries.literal: From Ancheng's six caves of Guangxing, Anle commandery was established.

entries.zh: 景戌，以寧遠將軍、北江州刺史熊曇朗為開府儀同三司，進號平西將軍。
entries.en: On jingxu day Xiong Tanlang, general who pacifies the distant and inspector of North Jiangzhou, was granted the right to open a staff with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to general who pacifies the west.
entries.literal: On jingxu day the Pacifying Distance General and North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「梁時舊仕，亂離播越，始還朝廷，多未銓序。
entries.en: On dinghai day an edict declared: "Former officials of Liang, scattered by the troubles, have only now returned to court and for the most part await appointment.
entries.literal: On dinghai day an edict said: "Former Liang officials, scattered by disorder, have only lately returned to court and for the most part have not yet been ranked.

entries.zh: 又起兵已來，軍勳甚眾。
entries.en: Since the armies were raised, military merit has been abundant.
entries.literal: Since the raising of armies, military merit has been very numerous.

entries.zh: 選曹即條文武簿及節將應九流者，量其所擬。」
entries.en: The Selection Office shall at once compile rolls of civil and military men and of commanders with staffs eligible for the nine ranks, and assign posts as their talents warrant."
entries.literal: The Selection Office is immediately to list civil and military registers and commanders bearing staffs who fit the nine ranks, and weigh what posts suit them."

entries.zh: 於是隨材擢用者五十餘人。
entries.en: More than fifty men were then promoted according to ability.
entries.literal: Thereupon more than fifty men were promoted according to ability.

entries.zh: 六月戊子，儀同侯安都敗眾愛等於左里，獲琳從弟襲、主帥羊暕等三十餘人，眾愛遁走，庚寅，廬山民斬之，傳首京師。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Hou Andu, bearer of staff equal to the three dukes, routed Zhong'ai at Zuoli and took Wang Lin's cousin Xi, the commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan killed him and sent his head to the capital.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Andu defeated Zhong'ai and the others at Zuoli, capturing Wang Lin's younger cousin Xi, chief commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

entries.zh: 甲午，眾師凱歸。
entries.en: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.
entries.literal: On jiawu day the armies returned in triumph.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「曇朗噬逆，罪不容誅，分命眾軍，仍事掩討，方加梟磔，以明刑憲。」
entries.en: An edict declared: "Tanlang has turned traitor and murderer; his crime admits no pardon. The armies are already hunting him; when he is taken, the law will be made plain."
entries.literal: An edict said: "Tanlang devoured and rebelled; even execution cannot contain his crime. We ordered the armies to continue the concealed attack; when he is exposed to the halter and cleaver, the penal statutes will be made clear."

entries.zh: 徵臨川王蒨往皖口置城柵，以錢道戢守焉。
entries.en: The King of Linchuan, Qian, was called to Wan Estuary to build fortifications, with Qian Daozai left to hold them.
entries.literal: The King of Linchuan, Qian, was summoned to Wan Estuary to set up stockades and palisades; Qian Daozai was left to defend them.

entries.zh: 丁酉，高祖不豫，遣兼太宰、尚書左僕射王通以疾告太廟，兼太宰、中書令謝哲告大社、南北郊。
entries.en: On dingyou day the Founder fell ill. He sent Wang Tong, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and left vice director of the secretariat, to announce his illness at the Grand Temple, and Xie Zhe, concurrent grand minister of sacrifices and director of the central secretariat, to announce it at the Grand Altar and the suburban altars.
entries.literal: On dingyou day the Founder was unwell. He sent Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Tong to report the illness to the Grand Temple, and Concurrent Grand Minister of Sacrifices and Central Secretariat Director Xie Zhe to report to the Grand Altar and the southern and northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 辛丑，高祖疾小瘳。
entries.en: On xinchou day the Founder's illness eased slightly.
entries.literal: On xinchou day the Founder's illness slightly improved.

entries.zh: 故司空周文育之柩至自建昌。
entries.en: The coffin of the late Zhou Wenyü, minister of works, arrived from Jianchang.
entries.literal: The coffin of the late Minister of Works Zhou Wenyü arrived from Jianchang.

entries.zh: 壬寅，高祖素服哭于東堂，哀甚。
entries.en: On renyin day the Founder, in plain mourning dress, wept in the eastern hall with deepest grief.
entries.literal: On renyin day the Founder in plain robes wept in the eastern hall, grief extreme.

entries.zh: 癸卯，高祖臨訊獄
entries.en: On guimao day the Founder personally heard prison cases.
entries.literal: On guimao day the Founder personally inspected and questioned at the pris

entries.en: (omitted)
entries.literal: (omitted)

entries.zh: 訟。
entries.en: ons.
entries.literal: ons.

entries.zh: [20]是夜，熒惑在天尊。
entries.en: [20] That night Mars stood at the Celestial Honored One.
entries.literal: [20] That night the Sparkling Deluder was at the Celestial Honored One.

entries.zh: 高祖疾又甚。
entries.en: The Founder's illness worsened again.
entries.literal: The Founder's illness again grew severe.

entries.zh: [21]景午，崩于璿璣殿，時年五十七。
entries.en: [21] On jingwu day he died in the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.
entries.literal: [21] On jingwu day he died at the Hall of the Rotating Pearl, aged fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 遺詔追臨川王蒨入纂。
entries.en: His testament summoned the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed him.
entries.literal: The testamentary edict recalled the King of Linchuan, Qian, to succeed.

entries.zh: 甲寅，大行皇帝遷殯于太極殿西階。
entries.en: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was placed in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: On jiayin day the late emperor's coffin was moved to lie in state at the western steps of the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 夏閏四月庚寅，詔曰：「開廩賑絕，育民之大惠，巡方恤患，前王之令典。
entries.en: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict declared: "Opening the granaries to save the starving is the great act of nurturing the people; touring the realm to ease suffering is the ancient kings' law.
entries.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of summer, on gengyin day, an edict said: "Opening granaries to relieve the destitute is the great bounty for nurturing the people; touring the regions to pity the afflicted is the former kings' established canon.

entries.zh: 朕當斯季俗，膺此樂推，君德未孚，民瘼猶甚，重茲多壘，彌疚納隍。
entries.en: We came to power in a fallen age and accepted the people's acclaim, yet Our virtue has not won their hearts and their suffering remains deep. Fortress upon fortress of trouble fills Us with shame.
entries.literal: We meet this declining age and receive this joyful succession; Our lordly virtue is not yet trusted, the people's afflictions are still severe. Heaping ramparts upon ramparts, We are the more ashamed to stand at the brink.

entries.zh: 良由四聰弗達，[17]千里勿應。
entries.en: Truly the four keen listeners were not heard, [17] and no voice answered from a thousand li.
entries.literal: Truly because the four keen listeners were not reached, [17] a thousand li gave no response.

entries.zh: [18]博施之仁，何其或爽？
entries.en: [18] How could the grace of broad giving ever be wanting?
entries.literal: [18] The benevolence of broad giving—how could it ever fail?

entries.zh: 殘弊之軌，致此未康。
entries.en: Yet the road of ruin and exhaustion has not yet led to peace.
entries.literal: The track of ruin and exhaustion brought this not yet to peace.

entries.zh: 吳州、縉州去歲蝗旱，郢田雖呪，[19]鄭渠終涸，室靡盈積之望，家有填壑之嗟。
entries.en: Wu and Jing provinces suffered locusts and drought last year. Though the fields of Ying were blessed, [19] the Zheng Canal ran dry at last. No household could hope for a full granary; many faced starvation.
entries.literal: Wu and Jing provinces last year suffered locusts and drought. Though the fields of Ying were charmed, [19] the Zheng Canal in the end dried up. Houses had no hope of full stores; families had the lament of filling gullies.

entries.zh: 百姓不足，兆民何賴？
entries.en: When the people lack food, what can the realm depend upon?
entries.literal: If the hundred surnames are not sufficient, on what do the myriad people rely?

entries.zh: 近已遣中書舍人江德藻銜命東陽，與令長二千石問民疾苦，仍以入臺倉見米分恤。
entries.en: We have lately sent Jiang Dezao, drafter of the Central Secretariat, to Dongyang with Our mandate to inquire into the people's hardships with the local magistrates, and to distribute grain from the capital granaries in relief.
entries.literal: Recently We have sent Palace Attendant Jiang Dezao bearing Our mandate to Dongyang to question the people and officials of two thousand piculs rank about their hardships, and likewise to divide and comfort them with rice from the capital granary on hand.

entries.zh: 雖德非既飽，庶微慰阻飢。」
entries.en: Our virtue is not yet enough to fill every belly, yet We hope in some measure to ease those who starve."
entries.literal: Though Our virtue is not yet that of full satiety, We hope in small measure to comfort those who block hunger."

entries.zh: 甲午，詔依前代置西省學士，兼以伎術者預焉。
entries.en: On jiawu day an edict, following earlier dynasties, established scholars of the Western Secretariat, including men skilled in arts and techniques.
entries.literal: On jiawu day an edict ordered, following former dynasties, Western Secretariat scholars established, and moreover those skilled in arts and techniques to be included.

entries.zh: 丁酉，遣鎮北將軍徐度率眾城南皖口。
entries.en: On dingyou day Xu Du, pacifying north general, led the armies south to Wan Estuary.
entries.literal: On dingyou day Pacifying North General Xu Du led the armies south to Wan Estuary.

entries.zh: 是時久不雨，景午，輿駕幸鍾山祠蔣帝廟，是日降雨，迄于月晦。
entries.en: Rain had long been absent. On jingwu day the emperor sacrificed at Emperor Jiang's temple on Zhongshan; rain fell that day and lasted to month's end.
entries.literal: At this time rain had long been lacking. On jingwu day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang; that day rain fell, continuing until the month's end.

entries.zh: 三年春正月己丑，青龍見于東方。
entries.en: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon was seen in the east.
entries.literal: In the third year, first month, on jichou day, a green dragon appeared in the east.

entries.zh: 丁酉，以鎮南將軍、廣州刺史歐陽頠即本號開府儀同三司。
entries.en: On dingyou day Ouyang Wei, general who guards the south and inspector of Guangzhou, was confirmed as grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes.
entries.literal: On dingyou day the General Who Guards the South and Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei was given his present title as Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 是夜大雪，及旦，太極殿前有龍跡見。
entries.en: That night heavy snow fell; by dawn dragon tracks appeared before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: That night great snow fell, and at dawn dragon tracks were seen before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 甲午，廣州刺史歐陽頠表稱白龍見于州江南岸，[16]長數十丈，大可八九圍，歷州城西道入天井崗。
entries.en: On jiawu day Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, reported a white dragon on the south bank of the Jiang in the province, [16] tens of zhang in length and eight or nine spans around, which passed west along the provincial city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.
entries.literal: On jiawu day Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon appeared on the south bank south of the province, [16] several tens of zhang long and eight or nine arm-spans around, passing west along the provincial city road into Heavenly Well Ridge.

entries.zh: 仙人見于羅浮山寺小石樓，長三丈所，通身潔白，衣服楚麗。
entries.en: An immortal was seen at the small stone tower on Luofu Mountain, some three zhang tall, wholly white, dressed in splendid Chu fashion.
entries.literal: An immortal appeared at the small stone tower of Luofu Mountain Monastery, about three zhang tall, all body pure white, garments splendid in Chu style.

entries.zh: 辛丑，詔曰：「南康、始興王諸妹，已有封爵，依禮止是藩主。
entries.en: On xinchou day an edict declared: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already hold titles; by ritual they should rank only as feudal princesses.
entries.literal: On xinchou day an edict said: "The younger sisters of the kings of Nankang and Shixing already have enfeoffments; by ritual they should only be feudal ladies.

entries.zh: 此二王者，有殊恆情，宜隆禮數。
entries.en: These two kings stand in a special bond; their sisters deserve higher honor.
entries.literal: These two kings have a special constant feeling; ritual measure ought to be exalted.

entries.zh: 諸主儀秩及尚主，可並同皇女。」
entries.en: Let the princesses' ceremonial standing and their husbands' ranks equal those of the emperor's own daughters."
entries.literal: The princesses' ritual ranks and those who marry them may both be the same as imperial daughters."

entries.zh: 戊申，詔臨川王蒨省揚、徐二州辭訟。
entries.en: On wushen day an edict charged the King of Linchuan, Qian, with hearing appeals from Yang and Xu provinces.
entries.literal: On wushen day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, to review lawsuits of Yang and Xu provinces.

entries.zh: 五月景辰朔，日有食之，有司奏：舊儀，御前殿，服朱紗袍、通天冠。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices reported the old rite: at the front hall the emperor should wear the vermilion gauze robe and penetrating-heaven crown.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jingchen, there was a solar eclipse. The relevant offices memorialized: According to old ritual, at the front hall one wears the vermilion gauze robe and the penetrating-heaven crown.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「此乃前代承用，意有未同。
entries.en: An edict replied: "Former generations followed this practice, but the meaning is not the same.
entries.literal: An edict said: "This is what former generations used in succession; the intent is not the same.

entries.zh: 合朔仰助太陽，宜備袞冕之服。
entries.en: At the conjunction one assists the sun; full imperial regalia should be worn.
entries.literal: At the conjunction one looks up to aid the sun; one ought to prepare the robes of the full regalia.

entries.zh: 自今已去，永可為准。」
entries.en: Henceforth this shall be the permanent rule."
entries.literal: From now onward this shall forever be the standard."

entries.zh: 景寅，扶南國遣使獻方物。
entries.en: On jingyin day Funan sent envoys with tribute.
entries.literal: On yingyin day Funan sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 乙酉，北江州刺史熊曇朗殺都督周文育于軍，舉兵反。
entries.en: On yiyou day Xiong Tanlang, inspector of North Jiangzhou, murdered the commander Zhou Wenyü in camp and rebelled.
entries.literal: On yiyou day North Jiangzhou Inspector Xiong Tanlang killed Commander-in-Chief Zhou Wenyü in the army and raised troops in rebellion.

entries.zh: 王琳遣其將常眾愛、曹慶率兵援余孝勱。
entries.en: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing with troops to support Yu Xiaoqing.
entries.literal: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing leading troops to aid Yu Xiaoqing.

entries.zh: 二月辛酉，以平西將軍、桂州刺史淳于量為開府儀同三司，進號鎮西大將軍。
entries.en: In the second month, on xinyou day, Chunyu Liang, general who pacifies the west and inspector of Guizhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to grand general who guards the west.
entries.literal: In the second month, on xinyou day, the General Who Pacifies the West and Guizhou Inspector Chunyu Liang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to Grand General Who Guards the West.

entries.zh: 壬午，司空侯瑱督眾軍自江入合州，焚齊舟艦。
entries.en: On renwu day Hou Tian, minister of works, led the armies from the Yangtze into Hefei and burned Qi's fleet.
entries.literal: On renwu day Minister of Works Hou Tian commanded the armies from the river into Hefei and burned Qi's boats.

entries.zh: 三月景申，侯瑱至自合肥，眾軍獻捷。
entries.en: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei and the armies reported victory.
entries.literal: In the third month, on jingshen day, Hou Tian returned from Hefei; the armies presented the spoils.

entries.zh: 皇帝臣霸先 「霸先」二字原作「諱」，蓋仍姚察舊文，姚察為梁、陳之史官，例避陳諱也。
entries.en: On "your subject Baxian": the text originally read "taboo name," preserving Yao Cha's wording; as a Liang and Chen historian he avoided the imperial name.
entries.literal: The Emperor, your subject Baxian: the two characters "Baxian" originally read "taboo name"—this preserves Yao Cha's old text; as an official historian of Liang and Chen, he observed the Chen taboo.

entries.zh: 北監本、汲本、殿本並已改「諱」為「霸先」，今從之。
entries.en: The Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions all changed "taboo name" to "Baxian"; we follow them.
entries.literal: The Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions have all changed "taboo name" to "Baxian"; the present text follows them.

entries.zh: 後同。
entries.en: The same applies below.
entries.literal: The same hereafter.

entries.zh: 秋八月甲午，群臣上諡曰武皇帝，廟號高祖。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Wu and the temple name Founder.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu day, the assembled ministers posthumously titled him Emperor Wu, temple name Founder.

entries.zh: 景申，葬萬安陵。
entries.en: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.
entries.literal: On jingshen day he was buried at Wan'an Tomb.

entries.zh: 高祖智以綏物，武以寧亂，英謀獨運，人皆莫及，故能征伐四克，靜難夷凶。
entries.en: The Founder pacified the realm through wisdom and quelled chaos through arms; his strategy was his alone, and none could rival it. Thus he conquered in every direction and stilled rebellion and slaughter.
entries.literal: The Founder with wisdom pacified things, with martial prowess settled disorder; his heroic stratagem worked alone—none could match him. Therefore he could conquer on campaign in four directions and quiet hardship and level the fierce.

entries.zh: 至升大麓之日，居阿衡之任，恆崇寬政，愛育為本。
entries.en: When he was raised to the great foothills, he occupied the office of Aheng; he always favored lenient rule and made cherishing the people his foundation.
entries.literal: When he ascended the great footstool's day he occupied the office of Aheng; he constantly honored lenient government and took cherishing nurture as the root.

entries.zh: 有須發調軍儲，皆出於事不可息。
entries.en: Whenever he levied grain for the armies, it was only because necessity would not allow rest.
entries.literal: Whenever it was necessary to issue levies for army stores, all arose from affairs that could not rest.

entries.zh: 加以儉素自率，常膳不過數品，私饗曲宴，皆瓦器蚌盤，肴核庶羞，裁令充足而已，不為虛費。
entries.en: He was frugal in his own habits: daily meals were only a few courses; private feasts used pottery and clam shells, with food no more than enough—never spent on display.
entries.literal: Moreover he led by frugal simplicity himself; ordinary meals were no more than a few dishes. Private feasts and informal banquets all used earthenware and clam shells for dishes; meat and vegetables were only enough to suffice—not for empty waste.

entries.zh: 初平侯景，及立紹泰，子女玉帛，皆班將士。
entries.en: After he first subdued Hou Jing and again when he set up the Shaotai regime, sons and daughters, jade, and silks were all shared out among his officers and soldiers.
entries.literal: When he first pacified Hou Jing, and when he established Shaotai, children, jade, and silks were all distributed to officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 其充闈房者，衣不重綵，飾無金翠，哥鍾女樂，不列於前。
entries.en: Those in the inner quarters wore no doubled brocade; ornaments bore no gold or kingfisher feather; bells and female musicians were not set before him.
entries.literal: Those who filled the inner quarters wore no double brocade; ornaments had no gold or kingfisher; song-bells and female musicians were not arrayed before him.

entries.zh: 及乎踐祚，彌厲恭儉。
entries.en: Once he took the throne, he was stricter still in modest frugality.
entries.literal: When he ascended the throne, he was even stricter in respectful frugality.

entries.zh: 故隆功茂德，光有天下焉。
entries.en: Thus his towering merit and rich virtue held sway over the realm.
entries.literal: Therefore his lofty merit and abundant virtue shone over all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：高祖英略大度，應變無方，蓋漢高、魏武之亞矣。
entries.en: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The Founder's genius was vast and his bearing magnanimous; he met every turn without a set plan—he was next only to Han Gaozu and Cao Cao.
entries.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: The Founder's heroic strategy was broad and magnanimous; in meeting change he had no fixed method—he was next only to Han Gaozu and Wei Wu.

entries.zh: 及西都盪覆，誠貫天人。
entries.en: When the western capital fell, his loyalty ran through Heaven and earth.
entries.literal: When the western capital was overthrown, his sincerity pierced Heaven and man.

entries.zh: 王僧辯闕伊尹之才，空結桐宮之憤，貞陽假秦兵之送，不思穆嬴之泣。
entries.en: Wang Sengbian lacked the gift of an Yiyin yet brooded on the wrong of the Tong Palace; Zhenyang leaned on northern troops yet never remembered Mu Ying's tears.
entries.literal: Wang Sengbian lacked Yiyin's talent yet vainly nursed the grievance of the Tung Palace; Zhenyang borrowed the escort of Qin troops yet did not think of Mu Ying's weeping.

entries.zh: 高祖乃蹈玄機而撫末運，乘勢隙而拯橫流，王跡所基，始自於此，何至戡黎升陑之捷而已焉。
entries.en: The Founder then walked the hidden Way to steady a dying age, caught the breach in the flood to save the realm—the throne's roots began here; it was far more than the triumph at Li and the ascent of Mount Yang.
entries.literal: The Founder then trod the dark mystery to comfort the declining age, seized the gap in the tide to rescue the crosscurrent—the royal foundations began here; how could it be only the victory of defeating the Li people and ascending Yang?

entries.zh: 故於慎徽時序之世，變聲改物之辰，兆庶歸以謳歌，炎靈去如釋負，方之前代，何其美乎！
entries.en: In that age of careful ritual and renewed order, when music and customs were remade, the people sang him home and the old mandate slipped away like a load set down—set beside earlier dynasties, how fine a founding it was!
entries.literal: Therefore in the age of careful compliance with the seasons and proper sequence, at the time of changing sounds and altering things, the myriad people returned in song; the blazing spirit departed as if a burden were lifted—compared with former ages, how beautiful!

entries.zh: 言念遷
entries.en: Speaking of the transfer
entries.literal: Speaking of the transfer

entries.en: (jiong)
entries.literal: (jiong)

entries.zh: 桐據各本及《元龜》二一三改。
entries.en: Tong—corrected per all editions and Yuan Gui 213.
entries.literal: Tong—corrected according to all editions and Yuan Gui 213.

entries.zh: 按此用伊尹放太甲於桐故事，坰與桐形近而訛。
entries.en: Note: the passage uses Yiyin's exile of Tai Jia to Tong; jiong is a graphic slip for tong.
entries.literal: Comment: this alludes to Yiyin's placing Tai Jia at Tong; jiong and tong are graphically close and the former is a corruption.

entries.zh: 詔臨川王蒨西討 「蒨」字原作「諱」，姚察原文如此，今依北監本、汲本、殿本改。
entries.en: On "Prince of Linchuan Qian, western campaign": the text originally read taboo name, as in Yao Cha; restored to Qian per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.
entries.literal: Edict to Prince of Linchuan Qian for the western campaign: the character "Qian" originally read "taboo name"—so in Yao Cha's original text; now changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.

entries.zh: 後如此不悉出校記。
entries.en: Similar cases below are not all annotated.
entries.literal: Later cases of the same kind are not all given collation notes.

entries.zh: 高祖臨訊獄
entries.en: The Founder personally heard lawsuits
entries.literal: The Founder personally examined lawsuits

entries.en: (omitted)
entries.literal: (omitted)

entries.zh: 訟 據北監本、汲本、殿本及《南史·陳武帝紀》刪。
entries.en: lawsuits—deleted per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions and the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: lawsuits—deleted according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions and the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

entries.zh: 高祖疾又甚 按北監本、汲本、殿本無「又」字。
entries.en: On "the Founder's illness again grew severe": the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions omit again.
entries.literal: The Founder's illness again grew severe—comment: the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions lack the character "again."

entries.zh: 甲午廣州刺史歐陽頠表稱白龍見于州江南岸 「甲午」《南史·陳武帝紀》作「甲子」。
entries.en: On "jiawu day, Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon was seen on the south bank of the river at the prefecture": the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties read jiazi.
entries.literal: On jiawu day Guangzhou Inspector Ouyang Wei memorialized that a white dragon was seen on the south bank south of the province: "jiawu"—the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "jiazi."

entries.zh: 殿本考證云：「按上文書丁酉夜大雪，則甲午為前二日，不應顛倒在後。
entries.en: The Hall edition notes: "The text above has heavy snow on dingyou night, so jiawu would be two days earlier and cannot come after.
entries.literal: The Hall edition's textual verification says: "According to the text above, on dingyou night there was great snow; then jiawu is two days earlier and should not be placed after.

entries.zh: 若《南史》稱甲子，則以下文辛丑考之，又不相合。
entries.en: If the Southern Dynasties read jiazi, the xinchou that follows still will not align.
entries.literal: If the Southern Dynasties reads jiazi, checked against xinchou below, it again does not agree.

entries.zh: 不可考矣。」
entries.en: The date cannot be settled."
entries.literal: It cannot be determined."

entries.zh: 陳書卷二
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 2
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 2

entries.zh: 廢帝諱伯宗，字奉業，小字藥王，世祖嫡長子也。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor, taboo name Bozong, styled Fengye and in youth called Yaowang, was the legitimate eldest son of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: The Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Bozong, style name Fengye, childhood name Yaowang; he was Emperor Wen's legitimate eldest son.

entries.zh: 梁承聖三年五月庚寅生。
entries.en: He was born on gengyin day in the fifth month of the third year of Liang's Chengsheng era (554).
entries.literal: He was born on gengyin day of the fifth month in the third year of Liang's Chengsheng era.

entries.zh: 永定二年二月戊辰，拜臨川王世子。
entries.en: In Yongding year 2, on wuchen day of the second month, he was named heir of the Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: On wuchen day of the second month in the second year of Yongding, he was appointed heir of the Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 三年，世祖嗣位，八月庚戌，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In year 3, when Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made crown prince on gengxu day of the eighth month.
entries.literal: In year three Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne; on gengxu day of the eighth month he was established as crown prince.

entries.zh: [1]自梁室亂離，東宮焚燼，太子居于永福省。
entries.en: After the Liang court was torn apart, the eastern palace lay in ashes, and the crown prince lived in Yongfu Province.
entries.literal: Since the Liang house fell into chaos and separation, the eastern palace was burned to ashes, and the crown prince dwelt in Yongfu Province.

entries.zh: 天康元年四月癸酉，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位于太極前殿，詔曰：「上天降禍，大行皇帝奄棄萬國，攀號靡及，五內崩殞。
entries.en: On guiyou day of the fourth month in Tiankang year 1, Emperor Wen died. That same day the crown prince ascended the throne in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate and proclaimed: "Heaven has sent calamity; the late emperor has left the realm. We cannot reach him with our laments; Our inmost being is broken.
entries.literal: On guiyou day of the fourth month in the first year of Tiankang, Emperor Wen died; that same day the crown prince took the throne in the Hall before the Supreme Ultimate and issued an edict: "Heaven has sent down calamity; the late emperor has suddenly abandoned the myriad realms. We cannot reach him with our cries; Our five viscera are shattered.

entries.zh: 朕以寡德，嗣膺寶命，掼掼在疚，懼甚綴旒，方賴宰輔匡其不逮。
entries.en: We, of little merit, have received the sacred charge; day and night in mourning We fear for the realm as for loose cap-strings, and now depend on our ministers to mend what We lack.
entries.literal: We, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the precious mandate; night and day in grief We fear greatly for the jade beads of the cap, and just now rely on the chief ministers to correct Our shortcomings.

entries.zh: 可大赦天下。」
entries.en: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
entries.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."

entries.zh: 又詔內外文武，各復其職，遠方悉停奔赴。
entries.en: A further edict ordered civil and military officers at court and in the provinces to return to their posts, and forbade distant regions to hurry envoys to the capital.
entries.literal: Another edict ordered all civil and military officials within and without to resume their offices, and all distant regions to cease rushing to court.

entries.zh: 中軍儀同、鎮北儀同、鎮右將軍、護軍將軍、八座卿士：昔梁運季末，[11]海內沸騰，天下蒼生，殆無遺唣。
entries.en: To the central army commander with staff equal to the three dukes, the garrisoning north commander with equal honors, the garrisoning right general, the protector general, and the eight chief ministers: In the closing years of Liang, the empire boiled over and the common people were all but destroyed.
entries.literal: Central Army with staff equal to the three dukes, Garrisoning North with staff equal to the three dukes, Garrisoning Right General, Protector General, and the eight chief ministers: In the last days of Liang's mandate, the realm seethed; the black-haired people were nearly wiped out.

entries.zh: 高祖武皇帝撥亂反正，膺圖御籙，重懸三象，還補二儀；
entries.en: The Founder put rebellion down and righted the realm, took the mandate and ruled by the tally, restored heaven's lights, and repaired earth's order;
entries.literal: The Founder, Martial Emperor, put down disorder and restored the right, received the chart and held the tally, rehung the three luminaries, and mended the two principles;

entries.zh: 世祖文皇帝克嗣洪基，光宣寶業，惠養中國，綏寧外荒；
entries.en: Emperor Wen carried on the great foundation, enlarged the royal work, nourished the heartland, and pacified the frontier;
entries.literal: Emperor Wen, Literary Emperor, succeeded the great foundation, spread the precious enterprise, nurtured the central lands, and quieted the outer wilds;

entries.zh: 並戰戰兢兢，劬勞締構，庶幾鼎運，方隆殷、夏。
entries.en: both labored in fear and sweat to build the state, hoping the dynasty might flourish like Yin and Xia.
entries.literal: both trembled in caution and toiled in founding, hoping that the bronze vessel's fortune might rise like Yin and Xia.

entries.zh: 帝仁弱無人君之器，世祖每慮不堪繼業，既居冢嫡，廢立事重，是以依違積載。
entries.en: The emperor was mild and feeble and lacked a ruler's stature; Emperor Wen long feared he could not bear the inheritance. Because he was the principal legitimate heir, replacing him was grave, and for years Emperor Wen could not decide.
entries.literal: The emperor was gentle and weak and lacked the capacity of a ruler; Emperor Wen always feared he could not sustain the succession. Since he occupied the place of principal legitimate heir, deposition and enthronement were weighty matters, and so Emperor Wen hesitated for years.

entries.zh: 及疾將大漸，召高宗謂曰「吾欲遵太伯之事」，高宗初未達旨，後寤，乃拜伏涕泣，固辭。
entries.en: As his illness deepened he called Emperor Xuan and said, "I mean to follow the Duke of Wu's example of yielding the throne." At first Emperor Xuan did not understand; when he did, he prostrated himself, wept, and refused.
entries.literal: When his illness was about to reach its crisis, he summoned Emperor Xuan and said, "I wish to follow the affair of Duke Tai," Emperor Xuan at first did not grasp his meaning; afterward he understood, then bowed prostrate, wept, and firmly declined.

entries.zh: 其後宣太后依詔廢帝焉。
entries.en: Later Dowager Empress Xuan carried out the will and deposed him.
entries.literal: Afterward Dowager Empress Xuan carried out the edict and deposed the emperor.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：臨海雖繼體之重，仁厚儒弱，[13]混一是非，不驚得喪，蓋帝摯、漢惠之流也。
entries.en: The historian writes: Though Linhai held the heir's place, he was gentle, mild, and timid in the Confucian way; he blurred right and wrong and was unmoved by gain or loss—in the line of Emperor Zhi and Emperor Hui of Han.
entries.literal: The historian says: Though Linhai bore the weight of succession, he was benevolent, mild, and Confucian-weak; blending right and wrong, undisturbed by gain or loss—he was of the sort of Emperor Zhi and Emperor Hui of Han.

entries.zh: 世祖知神器之重，諒難負荷，深鑒堯旨，弗傳寶祚焉。
entries.en: Emperor Wen knew how heavy the throne was and that this son could not carry it; reading Yao's intent, he did not hand him the mandate.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen knew the weight of the sacred vessel and that it was hard to bear; deeply discerning Yao's intent, he did not pass on the precious throne.

entries.zh: 太傅安成王固天生德，齊聖廣深，二后鍾心，三靈佇眷。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, is virtuous by nature, sage and far-reaching; both empresses trust him, and heaven and earth mark him out.
entries.literal: The Grand Tutor, Prince of Ancheng, Xu, by nature possesses virtue; sagely and broad, the two empresses set their hearts on him, and the three spirits look to him in hope.

entries.zh: 自前朝不悆，任總邦家，威惠相宣，刑禮兼設，指揮嘯咊，湘、郢廓清，辟地開疆，荊、益風靡，若太戊之承殷歷，中都之奉漢家，校以功名，曾何髣屉。
entries.en: Since the last reign's troubles he has governed the realm; power and grace went together, law and ritual alike; at his word Xiang and Ying were pacified, and in opening lands Jing and Yi submitted—like Taiwu carrying on Yin, or Zhongdu upholding Han; beside his merit and fame, who else even comes close?
entries.literal: Since the previous reign's discontent he has held overall charge of the state; authority and kindness were proclaimed together, punishments and ritual alike established; at his command Xiang and Ying were cleared, and opening territory and expanding borders, Jing and Yi bowed to the wind—like Taiwu continuing Yin, or Zhongdu serving the house of Han; compared for merit and fame, how could the rest even be glimpsed?

entries.zh: 且地彰靈璽，天表長彗，布新除舊，禎祥咸顯。
entries.en: The earth has shown a sacred seal and heaven a long comet; omens of renewal have all appeared.
entries.literal: Moreover the earth revealed a spirit seal and heaven showed a long comet; removing the old and establishing the new, auspicious signs all appeared.

entries.zh: 文皇知子之鑒，事甚帝堯，傳弟之懷，又符太伯。
entries.en: Emperor Wen knew which son could bear the charge, as Yao did; his wish to pass the throne to his younger brother matched the Duke of Wu.
entries.literal: The Literary Emperor knew his son's measure, a matter like Emperor Yao's; his wish to pass the throne to his younger brother also matched Duke Tai of Wu.

entries.zh: 今可還申曩志，崇立賢君，方固宗祧，載貞辰象。
entries.en: Let his former intent now be fulfilled: raise the worthy prince and secure the temple, that the throne and the heavens may stand firm.
entries.literal: Now his former intent may again be carried out; establish the worthy ruler and exalt the sage lord, that the ancestral temple may be secured and the stars held firm.

entries.zh: 中外宜依舊典，奉迎輿駕。
entries.en: Court and command should follow the old rites and welcome the new emperor.
entries.literal: Within and without should follow the old statutes and welcome the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 五月
entries.en: Fifth month
entries.literal: Fifth month

entries.en: yi
entries.literal: (yi)

entries.zh: [己]卯，[2]尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。
entries.en: On jimao day the empress dowager was raised to grand empress dowager and the empress to empress dowager.
entries.literal: On jimao day the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager, and the empress as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 庚寅，以驃騎將軍、司空、揚州刺史、新除尚書令安成王頊為驃騎大將軍，進位司徒、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事。
entries.en: On gengyin day Xu, Prince of Ancheng—cavalry general, minister of works, inspector of Yangzhou, and newly appointed director of the Masters of Writing—was made grand general of agile cavalry, promoted to minister over the masses and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and given overall command of armies at court and in the field.
entries.literal: On gengyin day the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, bearer of the staff, minister of works, inspector of Yangzhou, and newly appointed director of the Masters of Writing, was made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, advanced to grand mentor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and area commander over all armies within and without.

entries.zh: 丁酉，中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司徐度進位司空；
entries.en: On dingyou day Xu Du, central army general and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, was promoted to minister of works;
entries.literal: On dingyou day Central Army General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Xu Du was advanced to minister of works;

entries.zh: 鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史章昭達為侍中，進號征南將軍；
entries.en: Zhang Zhaoda, garrisoning south general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Jiangzhou, became palace attendant and was promoted to general who campaigns south;
entries.literal: Garrisoning South General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda became palace attendant and was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns South;

entries.zh: 鎮東將軍、東揚州刺史始興王伯茂進號征東將軍、開府儀同三司；
entries.en: Bomao, Prince of Shixing, garrisoning east general and inspector of East Yangzhou, was promoted to general who campaigns east with a mansion equal to the three dukes;
entries.literal: Garrisoning East General and Inspector of East Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing, Bomao, was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns East and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;

entries.zh: 平北將軍、南徐州刺史鄱陽王伯山進號鎮北將軍；
entries.en: Boshan, Prince of Poyang, pacifying north general and inspector of South Xuzhou, was promoted to general who garrisons the north;
entries.literal: Pacifying North General and Inspector of South Xuzhou, the Prince of Poyang, Boshan, was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the North;

entries.zh: 吏部尚書袁樞為尚書左僕射；
entries.en: Yuan Shu, minister of personnel, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing;
entries.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

entries.zh: 雲麾將軍、吳興太守沈欽為尚書右僕射；
entries.en: Shen Qin, cloud-banner general and administrator of Wuxing, became right vice director of the Masters of Writing;
entries.literal: Cloud-Banner General and Administrator of Wuxing Shen Qin became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

entries.zh: 新除中領軍吳明徹為領軍將軍；
entries.en: Wu Mingche, newly appointed central palace guard general, was made general of the palace guards;
entries.literal: the newly appointed Central Palace Guard General Wu Mingche became General of the Palace Guards;

entries.zh: 新除中護軍沈恪為護軍將軍；
entries.en: Shen Ke, newly appointed central protector general, was made protector general;
entries.literal: the newly appointed Central Protector General Shen Ke became Protector General;

entries.zh: [3]平南將軍、湘州刺史華皎進號安南將軍；
entries.en: Hua Jiao, pacifying south general and inspector of Xiangzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the south;
entries.literal: Pacifying South General and Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South;

entries.zh: 散騎常侍、御史中丞徐陵為吏部尚書。
entries.en: Xu Ling, regular attendant and censor-in-chief, became minister of personnel.
entries.literal: Regular Attendant and Censor-in-Chief Xu Ling became Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 八月庚戌立為皇太子 按「八月庚戌」
entries.en: On "eighth month, gengxu day, established as crown prince"—note:
entries.literal: On gengxu day of the eighth month he was established as crown prince—comment: "eighth month, gengxu day"

entries.zh: 〈世祖紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉

entries.zh: 作「九月辛酉」。
entries.en: reads "ninth month, xinyou day."
entries.literal: reads "ninth month, xinyou day."

entries.zh: 以征東將軍開府儀同三司東揚州刺史始興王伯茂為中纫大將軍 「征東將軍」
entries.en: On "Prince of Shixing Bomao, general who campaigns east, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, inspector of East Yangzhou, made central army general"—note on general who campaigns east:
entries.literal: the Prince of Shixing, Bomao, General Who Campaigns East, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, was made Central Army General—"General Who Campaigns East"

entries.zh: 〈世祖紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉

entries.zh: 天嘉三年作「鎮東將軍」，本傳同。
entries.en: Tianjia year 3 reads "general who garrisons the east," matching his biography.
entries.literal: in the third year of Tianjia reads "General Who Garrisons the East," the same as the main biography.

entries.zh: 「中纫大將軍」本傳作「中纫將軍」。
entries.en: "Central army general" in his biography reads "central commander general."
entries.literal: "Central Army General" in the main biography reads "Central Commander General."

entries.zh: 二年春正月己亥，侍中、都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司徒、錄尚書、揚州刺史安成王頊進位太傅，領司徒，加殊禮，闰履上殿；
entries.en: On jihai day in the first month of year 2 Xu, Prince of Ancheng—palace attendant, commander of all armies, grand general of agile cavalry, minister over the masses, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yangzhou—was promoted to grand tutor, retained the post of minister over the masses, received extraordinary honors, and was allowed to wear shoes in the audience hall;
entries.literal: On jihai day of the first month, spring, in year two, the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over all armies within and without, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Mentor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou, was advanced to Grand Tutor, retained the post of grand mentor, was granted extraordinary honors, and wore shoes in the hall;

entries.zh: 侍中、征南將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史章昭達進號征南大將軍；
entries.en: Zhang Zhaoda, palace attendant, general who campaigns south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Jiangzhou, was promoted to grand general who campaigns south;
entries.literal: Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda was advanced in title to Grand General Who Campaigns South;

entries.zh: 中撫大將軍、新除征南大將軍淳于量為侍中、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司；
entries.en: Chunyu Liang, central pacifying general and newly named general who campaigns south, became palace attendant, central army general, and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;
entries.literal: Central Pacifying General and newly appointed General Who Campaigns South Chunyu Liang became Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;

entries.zh: 安南將軍、湘州刺史吳明徹即本號開府儀同三司，進號鎮南將軍；
entries.en: Wu Mingche, general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, received a mansion equal to the three dukes on his current rank and was promoted to general who garrisons the south;
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche, on his present title, became opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South;

entries.zh: [10]雲麾將軍、郢州刺史程靈洗進號安西將軍。
entries.en: Cheng Lingxi, cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the west.
entries.literal: Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou Cheng Lingxi was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 庚子，詔討華皎軍人死王事者並給棺槥，送還本鄉，仍復其家。
entries.en: On gengzi day an edict directed that troops who died fighting Hua Jiao receive coffins and be sent home, and their families restored to standing.
entries.literal: On gengzi day an edict ordered that soldiers who died in the campaign against Hua Jiao all be given coffins and sent back to their native districts, and their households restored.

entries.zh: 甲子，罷吳州，以鄱陽郡還屬江州。
entries.en: On jiazi day Wu Province was abolished and Poyang commandery was placed back under Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: On jiazi day Wu Province was abolished and Poyang commandery was returned to Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 侍中、司空、車騎將軍徐度薨。
entries.en: Xu Du, palace attendant, minister of works, and general of chariots and cavalry, died.
entries.literal: Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and General of Chariots and Cavalry Xu Du died.

entries.zh: 五月景辰，太傅安成王頊獻玉璽一。
entries.en: On jingchen day of the fifth month Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, presented a jade seal.
entries.literal: On jingchen day of the fifth month, Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, presented one jade seal.

entries.zh: 安南將軍湘州刺史吳明徹即本號開府儀同三司進號鎮南將軍 按
entries.en: On "Wu Mingche, general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, on his present title made opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and advanced to general who garrisons the south"—note:
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche, on his present title, became opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South—comment:

entries.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

entries.zh: 太建元年又有「新除安南將軍、開府儀同三司、湘州刺史吳明徹進號鎮南將軍」之文，本傳亦云「太建元年授鎮南將軍」，疑此衍「進號鎮南將軍」六字。
entries.en: Taijian year 1 again has the passage "newly appointed general who pacifies the south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche, promoted in title to general who garrisons the south"; his biography also says "in Taijian year 1 appointed general who garrisons the south." The six characters "promoted in title to general who garrisons the south" here are probably intrusive.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian there is again the passage "the newly appointed General Who Pacifies the South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South"; the main biography also says "in the first year of Taijian he was appointed General Who Garrisons the South"—it is suspected that the six characters "was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South" here are intrusive.

entries.zh: 伯宗昔在儲宮，本無令問，及居崇極，遂騁凶淫。
entries.en: Bozong had no good name as heir apparent; once he took the throne he abandoned himself to cruelty and debauchery.
entries.literal: Bozong, when in the eastern palace, had no fair reputation; once he ascended the supreme height, he gave free rein to wickedness and lust.

entries.zh: 居處諒闇，固不哀慼，嬪嬙弗隔，就館相仍，豈但衣車所納，是譏宗正，衰絰生子，得誚右師。
entries.en: In the mourning lodge he showed no grief; he would not stay from the inner consorts, and one visiting bed followed another—not only the garments and carriages he took in, which the director of the imperial clan censured, but children born while he wore mourning, which made a mockery of the right mentor.
entries.literal: Dwelling in the mourning hut, he was by no means sorrowful; he did not keep apart from the inner consorts, and visiting lodges followed one after another—was it only the clothes and carts he admitted, for which the Director of the Imperial Clan reproved him, or children born in deep mourning, for which the Right Mentor was mocked?

entries.zh: 七百之祚何憑，三千之罪為大。
entries.en: How could he sustain a reign like Zhou's seven hundred years? His offenses were greater still.
entries.literal: On what could the seven hundred years of Zhou depend? His three thousand offenses were great indeed.

entries.zh: 且費引金帛，令充椒閫，內府中藏，軍備國儲，未盈硋稔，皆已空竭。
entries.en: He poured out gold and silk to stock the inner quarters; palace treasuries, armories, and state reserves were drained before the bins were full.
entries.literal: Moreover he squandered gold and silk to fill the pepper chambers; the inner treasury and the arsenals, the stores of the state—before the granaries were full, all were already emptied.

entries.zh: 太傅親承顧託，鎮守宮闈，遺誥綢繆，義深垣屏，而欑塗未御，翌日無淹，仍遣劉師知、殷不佞等顯言排斥。
entries.en: The Grand Tutor had been entrusted in person to guard the palace; the late emperor's will bound him like a wall—yet the emperor never came to him on the first day of mourning, and on the very next day sent Liu Shizhi, Yin Buxin, and others to push him aside.
entries.literal: The Grand Tutor personally received the entrustment and guarded the palace gates; the late emperor's testament was close-woven in meaning, deep as a rampart wall—yet the ceremonial road was not yet driven, and not even a day passed before he still sent Liu Shizhi, Yin Buxin, and others to speak openly of driving him out.

entries.zh: 韓子高小豎輕佻，推心委仗，陰謀禍亂，決起蕭牆。
entries.en: Han Ziga, a low creature, was light and reckless; the emperor trusted him with his heart, and treason brewed inside the palace.
entries.literal: Han Ziga, a petty fellow, was frivolous and rash; the emperor gave him his inmost trust and relied on him, and secret plots for calamity rose within the palace walls.

entries.zh: 元相雖持，但除君側。
entries.en: Though the chief minister still held office, the emperor only removed those at the ruler's side.
entries.literal: Though the chief minister held office, the emperor only removed those at the ruler's side.

entries.zh: 又以余孝頃密邇京師，便相徵召，殃慝之咎，凶徒自擒，宗社之靈，祅氛是滅。
entries.en: Because Yu Xiaoqing lay near the capital he was called in; the guilty destroyed themselves, and the spirits of the state swept away the foul air.
entries.literal: Moreover, because Yu Xiaoqing was close to the capital, he was summoned; the penalty of disaster fell on the wicked band themselves, and the numen of the altars destroyed the evil vapors.

entries.zh: 於是密詔華皎，稱兵上流，國祚憂惶，幾移醜類。
entries.en: Then he secretly instructed Hua Jiao to take up arms on the upper Yangtze; the realm trembled and the throne nearly fell to a usurper's line.
entries.literal: Then he secretly ordered Hua Jiao to raise troops upriver; the fate of the dynasty was in peril, and the throne nearly passed to an ugly breed.

entries.zh: 乃至要招遠近，叝力巴、湘，支黨縱橫，寇擾黟、歙。
entries.en: He even rallied allies far and near, gathered force in Ba and Xiang, and sent his factions to ravage Yi and She.
entries.literal: He even called in distant and near, mustered strength in Ba and Xiang, and his partisans ranged abroad, plundering Yi and She.

entries.zh: 又別队歐陽紇等攻逼衡州，嶺表紛紜，殊淹弦望。
entries.en: Another column under Ouyang He and others besieged Hengzhou; the south of the mountains was in turmoil for many months.
entries.literal: Moreover a separate column under Ouyang He and others pressed Hengzhou; south of the ranges all was turmoil, and the months dragged on.

entries.zh: 豈止罪浮於昌邑，非唯聲醜於太和。
entries.en: His crimes outdid the deposed Prince of Changyi; his name was fouler than Emperor Taihe's.
entries.literal: His guilt exceeded that of the Prince of Changyi; his infamy was worse than that of Emperor Taihe.

entries.zh: 但賊豎皆亡，祅徒已散，日望懲改，猶加掩抑，而悖禮忘德，情性不悛，樂禍思亂，犷慝無已。
entries.en: Though the ringleaders were dead and their gangs broken up, We still waited for him to mend his ways, but he only hid his faults; scorning ritual and virtue, he would not change—he loved trouble and schemed rebellion, fierce and unrepentant.
entries.literal: Yet though the wicked leaders were dead and the evil bands scattered, day by day We looked for reform, yet he only concealed it the more; defying ritual and forgetting virtue, his nature would not mend—he delighted in calamity and plotted disorder, savage and stubborn without end.

entries.zh: 張安國蕞爾凶狡，窮為小盜，仍遣使人蔣裕鉤出上京，即置行臺，分選凶黨。
entries.en: Zhang Anguo, mean, violent, and sly, had shrunk to a petty robber, yet still sent Jiang Yu to draw men from the capital, set up a field headquarters, and pick out hardened criminals.
entries.literal: Zhang Anguo, petty, fierce, and cunning, was reduced to a small bandit, yet still sent his man Jiang Yu to lure men out of the upper capital, set up a mobile headquarters, and choose vicious accomplices.

entries.zh: 賊皎妻呂，舂徒為戮，納自奚
entries.en: Jiao's wife Lu, sentenced to labor at the mortar, was received from the
entries.literal: Jiao's wife Lu, condemned to pounding as punishment, was taken in from the

entries.en: (palace)
entries.literal: (gong)

entries.zh: [官]，[12]藏諸永巷，使其結引親舊，規圖戕禍。
entries.en: palace offices and hidden in the Everlasting Lane to win over kin and friends and plot murder.
entries.literal: offices and hidden in the Everlasting Lane, that she might win over kin and friends and plot deadly harm.

entries.zh: 盪主侯法喜等，太傅麾下，恆遊府朝，啗以深利，謀興肘腋。
entries.en: The steward Hou Faxi and others, who served in the Grand Tutor's household and frequented the court, were bought with heavy bribes to strike at close range.
entries.literal: The steward Hou Faxi and others, under the Grand Tutor's command, constantly moved in and out of the princely mansion; fed with deep profit, they plotted trouble at the armpit.

entries.zh: 適又盪主孫泰等潛相連結，大有交通，兵力殊彊，指期挻亂。
entries.en: Then the steward Sun Tai and others secretly joined them; their traffic was heavy and their forces strong, and they set a day for revolt.
entries.literal: Then again the steward Sun Tai and others secretly linked together, with great traffic between them; their military strength was very strong, and they fixed a date to raise disorder.

entries.zh: 皇家有慶，歷數遐長，天誘其衷，同然開發。
entries.en: The dynasty is blessed with long fortune; Heaven moved their hearts, and the plot came to light together.
entries.literal: The royal house has fortune; its span is far; Heaven guided their hearts, and all alike were exposed.

entries.zh: 此諸文纹，今以相示，是而可忍，誰則不容？
entries.en: We now show you these documents—if this can be tolerated, who could bear it?
entries.literal: These documents We now show you—if this can be borne, who could endure it?

entries.zh: 祖宗基業，將懼傾霣，豈可復肅恭禋祀，臨御兆民？
entries.en: The ancestral foundation would totter—how could We still perform the great sacrifices and rule the people?
entries.literal: The ancestral foundation will fear collapse and ruin—how can We again perform the solemn suburban sacrifices and face the myriad people?

entries.zh: 式稽故實，宜在流放，今可特降為臨海郡王，送還藩邸。
entries.en: By ancient precedent he belongs in exile; let him therefore be demoted to Prince of Linhai and sent to his fief.
entries.literal: Following precedent, he should be sent into exile; now let him be specially demoted to Prince of Linhai and sent back to his princely residence.

entries.zh: 九月乙巳，詔曰：「逆賊華皎，極惡窮凶，遂樹立蕭巋，謀危社稷。
entries.en: An edict declared: "The traitor Hua Jiao, steeped in evil, has enthroned Xiao Kui and menaced the dynasty.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The rebel Hua Jiao, utterly wicked and utterly cruel, has set up Xiao Kui and plotted against the altars of state.

entries.zh: 棄親即讎，人神憤惋，王師電邁，水陸爭前，梟剪之期，匪朝伊暮。
entries.en: He has abandoned his own house for the foe; heaven and earth are angered. Our armies rush forward by land and sea, and his end is near.
entries.literal: Casting off kin for the enemy, men and spirits alike are outraged; the royal army advances like lightning by land and water, and the day of decapitation is not far off.

entries.zh: 其家口在北里尚方，宜從誅戮，用明國憲。」
entries.en: His family held in the Northern Ward of the Palace Workshop are to be executed, that the nation's law may be plain."
entries.literal: His household in the Northern Ward of the Palace Workshop should be put to death, to make clear the law of the state."

entries.zh: 景辰，百濟國遣使獻方物。
entries.en: On jingchen day envoys from Baekje presented tribute.
entries.literal: On jingchen day, Baekje sent envoys presenting local products.

entries.zh: 是月，周將長胡公拓跋定率步騎二萬入郢州，與華皎水陸俱進，都督淳于量、吳明徹等與戰，大破之。
entries.en: That month Northern Zhou's general Tuoba Ding, Duke of Chang, entered Yingzhou with twenty thousand foot and horse and joined Hua Jiao on land and water; Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others fought them and won a great victory.
entries.literal: That month Zhou's general the Duke of Chang, Tuoba Ding, led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry into Yingzhou and advanced with Hua Jiao by land and water; Area Commander Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others gave battle and inflicted a great defeat.

entries.zh: 皎單舸奔江陵，擒拓跋定，俘獲萬餘人，馬四千餘匹，送京師。
entries.en: Jiao fled alone by boat to Jiangling; Tuoba Ding was captured, and more than ten thousand prisoners and four thousand horses were sent to the capital.
entries.literal: Jiao fled alone in a single boat to Jiangling; Tuoba Ding was captured, and more than ten thousand were taken prisoner, with over four thousand horses, and sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛巳，赦湘、巴二
entries.en: On xinsi day in the tenth month of winter a pardon was granted to Xiang and Ba
entries.literal: On xinsi day of the tenth month, winter, a pardon was granted to Xiang and Ba

entries.en: (commandery)
entries.literal: (jun)

entries.zh: [州]為皎所詿誤者。
entries.en: [province] for those misled by Jiao.
entries.literal: [zhou] for those misled by Jiao.

entries.zh: [9]甲申，輿駕親祠太廟。
entries.en: On jiashen day the emperor offered sacrifice in person at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: On jiashen day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.

entries.zh: 陳書卷四
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 4
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 4

entries.zh: 高祖章皇后 世祖沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 高宗柳皇后
entries.en: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu
entries.literal: Founder Empress Zhang; Emperor Wen Empress Shen; Deposed Emperor Empress Wang; Emperor Xuan Empress Liu

entries.zh: 周禮，王者立后，六宮，三夫人，九嬪，二十七世婦，八十一御妻，以聽天下之內治。
entries.en: The Rites of Zhou say that a king establishes a queen, the Six Palaces, three chief consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendant wives to govern the inner realm.
entries.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the king establishes a queen, the Six Palaces, three consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendant wives to hear and govern inner affairs throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 然受命繼體之主，非獨外相佐也，蓋亦有內德助焉。
entries.en: Yet rulers who receive the Mandate and succeed to the throne are aided not only by ministers without, but also by virtue within.
entries.literal: Yet rulers who receive the Mandate and succeed to the line are aided not only by ministers without; surely inner virtue assists as well.

entries.zh: 漢魏已來，六宮之職，因襲增置，代不同矣。
entries.en: From Han and Wei onward the offices of the Six Palaces were carried on and expanded, and no two dynasties were alike.
entries.literal: From Han and Wei onward the offices of the Six Palaces were inherited and increased, and each age differed.

entries.zh: 高祖承微接亂，光膺天歷，以朴素自處，故後宮員位多闕。
entries.en: The Founder took the throne amid turmoil and lived plainly, so many posts in the inner palace went unfilled.
entries.literal: The Founder received the succession amid turmoil and disorder and brightly bore Heaven's calendar; because he kept himself in plain simplicity, many posts in the inner palace stood vacant.

entries.zh: 世祖天嘉初，詔立後宮員數，始置貴妃、貴嬪、貴姬三人，以擬古之三夫人。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) Emperor Wen fixed the number of inner-palace posts and for the first time created three offices—noble consort, noble concubine, and noble lady—to match the ancient three chief consorts.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia under Emperor Wen, an edict fixed the number of inner-palace posts; for the first time three offices were established—noble consort, noble concubine, and noble lady—to match the ancient three consorts.

entries.zh: 又置淑媛、淑儀、淑容、昭華、昭容、昭儀、[1]脩華、脩儀、脩容九人，以擬古之九嬪。
entries.en: He also appointed nine women—Shuyuan, Shuyi, Shurong, Zhaohua, Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, [1] Xiuhua, Xiuyi, and Xiurong—to match the ancient nine concubines.
entries.literal: There were also established nine persons: Shuyuan, Shuyi, Shurong, Zhaohua, Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, Xiuhua, Xiuyi, and Xiurong, to match the ancient nine concubines.

entries.zh: 又置婕妤、容華、充華、承徽、烈榮五人，謂之五職，亞於九嬪。
entries.en: He also created five offices—Jieyu, Ronghua, Chonghua, Chenghui, and Lierong—the Five Duties, ranking below the nine concubines.
entries.literal: There were also established five offices—Jieyu, Ronghua, Chonghua, Chenghui, and Lierong—called the Five Duties, ranking below the nine concubines.

entries.zh: 又置美人、才人、良人三職，其職無員數，號為散位。
entries.en: He also created three offices—Beauty, Talent, and Good Wife—with no fixed quota; they were called scattered ranks.
entries.literal: There were also established three offices—Beauty, Talent, and Good Wife—with no fixed quota for their posts; they were called scattered ranks.

entries.zh: 世祖性恭儉，而嬪嬙多闕，高宗、後主內職無所改作。
entries.en: Emperor Wen was respectful and frugal, and many concubines' posts still went unfilled; Emperor Xuan and the Last Emperor changed nothing in the inner offices.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature respectful and frugal, yet many concubines' posts still stood vacant; Emperor Xuan and the Last Emperor made no changes to the inner offices.

entries.en: (order)
entries.literal: (order)

entries.zh: [今]之所綴，[2]略備此篇。
entries.en: [Now] what is compiled here [2] briefly supplies this chapter.
entries.literal: [Now] what is compiled here, briefly supplies this chapter.

entries.zh: 高祖宣皇后章氏，諱要兒，吳興烏程人也。
entries.en: Lady Xuan, empress of the Founder, of the Zhang clan, was named Yao'er and came from Wucheng in Wuxing.
entries.literal: The Founder's Empress Xuan, of the Zhang clan, personal name Yao'er, was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 本姓鈕，父景明為章氏所養，因改焉。
entries.en: Her family had borne the surname Niu; her father Jingming was adopted by the Zhang clan and took their name.
entries.literal: Her original surname was Niu; her father Jingming was adopted by the Zhang clan and therefore changed it.

entries.zh: 景明，梁代官至散騎侍郎。
entries.en: Jingming had served Liang as scattered-cavalry gentleman.
entries.literal: Jingming under Liang reached the office of scattered-cavalry gentleman.

entries.zh: 后母蘇，嘗遇道士以小龜遺己，光采五色，曰：「三年有徵。」
entries.en: The empress's mother Su once met a Daoist who gave her a small turtle glowing in five colors and said, "In three years there will be a sign."
entries.literal: The empress's mother Su once met a Daoist who gave her a small turtle with a five-colored radiance, saying, "In three years there will be a sign."

entries.zh: 及期，后生而紫光照室，因失龜所在。
entries.en: When the time came, the empress was born and purple light filled the room; the turtle was nowhere to be found.
entries.literal: When the term arrived, the empress was born and purple light filled the chamber; the turtle's whereabouts were then lost.

entries.zh: 少聰慧，美容儀，手爪長五寸，色嵭紅白，每有硋功之服，則一爪先折。
entries.en: As a girl she was clever and beautiful; her fingernails were five inches long, reddish white, and whenever she wore mourning garments that got in the way, one nail would snap first.
entries.literal: In youth she was clever and quick, with a beautiful bearing; her fingernails were five inches long, reddish and white in color, and whenever there were mourning garments that hindered work, one nail would break first.

entries.zh: 高祖先娶同郡錢仲方女，早卒，後乃聘后。
entries.en: The Founder had first married a daughter of Qian Zhongfang of the same commandery, who died young; only then did he betroth the empress.
entries.literal: The Founder first married a daughter of Qian Zhongfang of the same commandery, who died early; afterward he betrothed the empress.

entries.zh: 后善書計，能誦詩及楚辭。
entries.en: The empress was skilled at writing and reckoning and could recite the Odes and the Songs of Chu.
entries.literal: The empress was skilled at writing and reckoning and could recite the Odes and the Songs of Chu.

entries.zh: 高祖自廣州南征交阯，命后與衡陽王昌隨世祖由海道歸于長城。
entries.en: When the Founder marched from Guangzhou against Jiaozhi, he sent the empress with Prince of Hengyang Chang and Emperor Wen home by sea to Changcheng.
entries.literal: When the Founder from Guangzhou campaigned south against Jiaozhi, he ordered the empress to follow Prince of Hengyang Chang with Emperor Wen by the sea route back to Changcheng.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖下至豫章，后為景所囚。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder went down to Yuzhang, and the empress was taken prisoner by Jing.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder went down to Yuzhang; the empress was imprisoned by Jing.

entries.zh: 景平，而高祖為長城縣公，后拜夫人。
entries.en: After Jing fell and the Founder became Duke of Changcheng, the empress was made his lady.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified and the Founder became Duke of Changcheng county, the empress was invested as Lady.

entries.zh: 及高祖踐祚，永定元年立為皇后。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, in Yongding year 1 (557) she was made empress.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, in the first year of Yongding she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 追贈后父景明特進、金紫光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，拜后母蘇安吉縣君。
entries.en: The empress's father Jingming was posthumously made special grand master and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon; her mother Su was made Lady of Anji county.
entries.literal: The empress's father Jingming was posthumously promoted to special grand master and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, with a golden seal and purple cord added; the empress's mother Su was invested as Lady of Anji county.

entries.zh: 二年，安吉君卒，與后父合葬吳興。
entries.en: In the second year the Lady of Anji died and was buried with the empress's father in Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the second year the Lady of Anji died and was buried with the empress's father in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 明年，追封后父為廣德縣侯，邑五百戶，謚曰溫。
entries.en: The next year her father was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde with five hundred households; his posthumous title was Wen.
entries.literal: The next year the empress's father was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde county with a fief of five hundred households; his posthumous title was Wen.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，后與中書舍人蔡景歷定計，祕不發喪，召世祖入纂，事在蔡景歷及侯安都傳。
entries.en: When the Founder died, the empress and masters of writing attendant Cai Jingli laid their plans, kept the death secret, and summoned Emperor Wen to succeed; the affair is told in the biographies of Cai Jingli and Hou Andu.
entries.literal: When the Founder died, the empress with Masters of Writing Attendant Cai Jingli settled the plan, kept the death secret, and summoned Emperor Wen to succeed; the matter is in the biographies of Cai Jingli and Hou Andu.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰慈訓。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Cixun.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Cixun.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，尊后為太皇太后。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, she was honored as grand empress dowager.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the empress was honored as grand empress dowager.

entries.zh: 光大二年，后下令黜廢帝為臨海王，命高宗嗣位。
entries.en: In Guangda year 2 (568) she issued an order deposing the Deposed Emperor as Prince of Linhai and installing Emperor Xuan in his place.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangda the empress issued an order deposing the Deposed Emperor as Prince of Linhai and appointing Emperor Xuan to succeed.

entries.zh: 太建元年，尊后為皇太后。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian (569) she was again honored as empress dowager.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian she was again honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 二年三月景申，崩于紫極殿，時年六十五。
entries.en: In the third month of Taijian year 2 (570), on day bingshen, she died in the Hall of Purple Apex at sixty-five.
entries.literal: In the second year, third month, day bingshen, she died in the Hall of Purple Apex at age sixty-five.

entries.zh: 遺令喪事所須，並從儉約，諸有饋奠，不得用牲牢。
entries.en: Her last command was that the funeral be kept frugal and that no offerings of oxen or sheep be used.
entries.literal: Her final command was that all funeral needs be kept frugal and simple, and that offerings presented at the mourning must not use oxen or sheep.

entries.zh: 其年四月，羣臣上謚曰宣太后，祔葬萬安陵。
entries.en: That fourth month the ministers gave her the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuan; she was buried with the Founder at Wan'an Mausoleum.
entries.literal: That year, fourth month, the ministers submitted the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuan; she was buried with the Founder at Wan'an Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 後主沈皇后諱婺華，儀同三司望蔡貞憲侯君理女也。
entries.en: Empress Shen of the Last Emperor, personal name Wuhua, was the daughter of Junli, Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Marquis Zhenxian of Wangcai.
