entries.literal: Empress Shen of the Last Emperor, personal name Wuhua, was the daughter of Junli, Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Marquis Zhenxian of Wangcai.

entries.zh: 母即高祖女會稽穆公主。
entries.en: Her mother was Princess Mu of Kuaiji, a daughter of the Founder.
entries.literal: Her mother was Princess Mu of Kuaiji, a daughter of the Founder.

entries.zh: 主早亡，時后尚幼，而毀瘠過甚。
entries.en: The princess died early. The empress was still young, yet she wasted herself with grief beyond measure.
entries.literal: The princess died early; the empress was still young at the time, yet her mourning emaciation was excessive.

entries.zh: 及服畢，每至歲時朔望，恆獨坐涕泣，哀動左右，內外咸敬異焉。
entries.en: Even after mourning ended, whenever seasonal rites, new moons, or full moons came, she sat alone and wept. Her grief moved those around her, and everyone inside and outside the palace honored her as extraordinary.
entries.literal: After mourning dress ended, whenever the seasonal rites, new moons, or full moons arrived, she always sat alone weeping, and her sorrow moved those around her; inside and outside all respected and marveled at her.

entries.zh: 太建三年納為皇太子妃。
entries.en: In Taijian year 3 (571), she was taken as the crown prince's consort.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 3, she was taken in as the crown prince's consort.

entries.zh: [6]後主即位，立為皇后。
entries.en: [6] When the Last Emperor came to the throne, she was made empress.
entries.literal: [6] When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 高祖皇后章要兒
entries.en: Founder Empress Zhang Yao'er
entries.literal: Founder Empress Zhang Yao'er

entries.zh: 世祖沈皇后諱妙容，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Emperor Wen's empress Shen, named Miaorong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen's Empress Shen, personal name Miaorong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 父法深，梁安前中錄事參軍。
entries.en: Her father Fashen had served Liang as recorder of the Prince of An's front headquarters.
entries.literal: Her father Fashen under Liang was recorder of the Prince of An's front headquarters.

entries.zh: 后年十餘歲，以梁大同中歸于世祖。
entries.en: When she was barely ten, in the Datong era of Liang she was married to Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: When the empress was a little more than ten years old, in the Datong era of Liang she was married to Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 高祖之討侯景，世祖時在吳興，景遣使收世祖及后。
entries.en: When the Founder moved against Hou Jing, Emperor Wen was in Wuxing; Jing sent men to seize him and the empress.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing, Emperor Wen was then in Wuxing; Jing sent envoys to seize Emperor Wen and the empress.

entries.zh: 景平，乃獲免。
entries.en: After Jing fell they were freed.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, they were then released.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，永定元年，后為臨川王妃。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, in Yongding year 1 (557) she became Princess of Linchuan.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, in the first year of Yongding the empress became Princess of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，為皇后。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, she was made empress.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, she became empress.

entries.zh: 追贈后父法深光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，封建
entries.en: Her father Fashen was posthumously made grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian
entries.literal: The empress's father Fashen was posthumously promoted to grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian

entries.en: (success)
entries.literal: (success)

entries.zh: [城]縣侯，[3]邑五百戶，謚曰恭，追贈后母高綏安縣君，謚曰定。
entries.en: [cheng] county, [3] with a fief of five hundred households and posthumous title Gong; her mother Gao was posthumously made Lady of Sui'an county with posthumous title Ding.
entries.literal: [cheng] county, [3] fief five hundred households, posthumous title Gong; the empress's mother Gao was posthumously invested as Lady of Sui'an county, posthumous title Ding.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰安德。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, she was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Ande.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, the empress was honored as empress dowager; her palace was called Ande.

entries.zh: 弟盼，太建中尚世祖女富陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: Her younger brother Pan in the Taijian era married Emperor Wen's daughter, Princess of Fuyang, and was made commandant of the emperor's son-in-law.
entries.literal: Her younger brother Pan in the Taijian era married Emperor Wen's daughter Princess of Fuyang and was appointed commandant of the emperor's son-in-law.

entries.zh: 後主即位，以帝舅加散騎常侍。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, as the emperor's uncle by marriage he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, as the emperor's maternal uncle he was promoted to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 盼性愚戇，使酒，常因醉乘馬入殿門，為有司所劾，坐免官，卒於家。
entries.en: Pan was dull and fond of drink; drunk, he often rode through the palace gate, was impeached, dismissed, and died at home.
entries.literal: Pan was dull and foolish, fond of wine; he often rode his horse drunk through the palace gate and was impeached by the responsible offices, stripped of office, and died at home.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、中護軍。
entries.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant and central guard commander.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given palace attendant and central guard commander.

entries.zh: 世祖皇后沈妙容
entries.en: Emperor Wen Empress Shen Miaorong
entries.literal: Emperor Wen Empress Shen Miaorong

entries.zh: 后兄欽，隨世祖征伐，以功至貞威將軍、安州刺史。
entries.en: The empress's elder brother Qin followed Emperor Wen on campaign and for merit rose to steadfast-prestige general and inspector of Anzhou.
entries.literal: The empress's elder brother Qin followed Emperor Wen on campaign and for merit reached the post of steadfast-prestige general and Inspector of Anzhou.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，襲爵建城侯，加通直散騎常侍、持節、會稽等九郡諸軍事、明威將軍、會稽太守，入為侍中、左纫將軍、纫尉卿。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Qin inherited the marquisate of Jiancheng, was made supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication with credentials, area commander of nine commanderies including Kuaiji, bright-prestige general, and Kuaiji administrator, then entered court as palace attendant, left guard general, and guard commandant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, [Qin] inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Jiancheng, was promoted to supernumerary regular attendant for direct communication, given credentials, made area commander of the nine commanderies including Kuaiji, bright-prestige general, and Kuaiji Administrator; he entered court as palace attendant, left guard general, and guard commandant.

entries.zh: 光大中，為尚書右僕射，尋遷左僕射。
entries.en: In the Guangda era he was right vice director of the masters of writing, then left vice director.
entries.literal: In the Guangda era he was right vice director of the masters of writing; soon he was transferred to left vice director.

entries.zh: 欽素無技能，奉己而已。
entries.en: Qin had no talent and cared only for his own ease.
entries.literal: Qin by nature had no skill; he looked only to his own comfort.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，出為雲麾將軍、義興太守，秩中二千石。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Qin went out as cloud-banner general and administrator of Yixing at two thousand shi of the middle rank.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Qin] went out as cloud-banner general and Administrator of Yixing, salary at two thousand shi of the middle rank.

entries.zh: 太建元年卒，時年六十七，贈侍中、特進、翊左將軍，謚曰成。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian (569) he died at sixty-seven; he was posthumously made palace attendant, special grand master, and left assistant general, with posthumous title Cheng.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian he died at age sixty-seven; he was posthumously given palace attendant, special grand master, and left assistant general, posthumous title Cheng.

entries.zh: 時高宗與僕射到仲舉、舍人劉師知等並受遺輔政，師知與仲舉恆居禁中參決红事，而高宗為揚州刺史，與左右三百人入居尚書省。
entries.en: At that time Emperor Xuan, with vice director Dao Zhongju, attendant Liu Shizhi, and others, shared the testament and governed; Shizhi and Zhongju lived in the inner palace and decided affairs of state, while Emperor Xuan was inspector of Yangzhou and lodged in the masters of writing office with three hundred men.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan, together with Vice Director Dao Zhongju, Attendant Liu Shizhi, and others, all received the testament and assisted in government; Shizhi and Zhongju constantly dwelt within the forbidden quarters deciding military affairs, while Emperor Xuan was Inspector of Yangzhou and entered the Masters of Writing office with three hundred followers.

entries.zh: 師知見高宗權重，陰忌之，乃矯队謂高宗曰：「今四方無事，王可還東府，經理州務。」
entries.en: Shizhi saw Emperor Xuan's power growing and secretly feared him; he forged an order saying, "The realm is at peace; you may return to the Eastern Mansion and mind the prefecture."
entries.literal: Shizhi saw Emperor Xuan's power growing and secretly resented him; he therefore forged an order and told Emperor Xuan, "Now the four quarters are at peace; Your Highness may return to the Eastern Mansion and manage the prefecture's affairs."

entries.zh: 高宗將出，而諮議毛喜止之曰：「今若出外，便受制於人，譬如曹爽，願作富家翁不可得也。」
entries.en: Emperor Xuan was about to leave when adviser Mao Xi stopped him and said, "Go out now and you fall under another's hand—as with Cao Shuang, you may wish only to be a rich man and cannot even have that."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to go out when Adviser Mao Xi stopped him and said, "If you go out now you will be subject to others—as with Cao Shuang, you may wish to be a rich householder yet cannot obtain it."

entries.zh: 高宗乃稱疾，召師知留之與語，使毛喜先入言之於后。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan then feigned illness, summoned Shizhi and kept him talking, and sent Mao Xi ahead to speak to the empress.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan then claimed illness, summoned Shizhi and detained him to talk, and sent Mao Xi in first to speak to the empress.

entries.zh: 后曰：「今伯宗年幼，政事並委二郎，此非我意。」
entries.en: The empress said, "Bozong is still young; to put all government in the Second Lord's hands is not my wish."
entries.literal: The empress said, "Now Bozong is young; all government is entrusted to the Second Lord—this is not my wish."

entries.zh: 喜又言於廢帝，帝曰：「此自師知等所為，非朕意也。」
entries.en: Xi also spoke to the Deposed Emperor, who said, "That was Shizhi and his party—not my wish."
entries.literal: Xi also spoke to the Deposed Emperor; the emperor said, "This was done by Shizhi and the others alone; it is not my wish."

entries.zh: 喜出以報高宗，高宗因囚師知，自入見后及帝，極陳師知之短，仍自草敕請畫，以師知付廷尉治罪。
entries.en: Xi came out and told Emperor Xuan, who then seized Shizhi, went in to see the empress and the emperor, laid out Shizhi's crimes, drafted the edict himself, and sent Shizhi to the court of trials.
entries.literal: Xi went out and reported to Emperor Xuan; Emperor Xuan therefore imprisoned Shizhi, entered in person to see the empress and the emperor, set forth Shizhi's faults at length, himself drafted the edict and requested the seal, and handed Shizhi over to the Court of Trials for punishment.

entries.zh: 其夜，於獄中賜死。
entries.en: That night he was granted death in prison.
entries.literal: That night he was granted death in prison.

entries.zh: 自是政無大小，盡歸高宗。
entries.en: From then on, great and small alike, all power passed to Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: From then on, whether affairs were great or small, all fell to Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 后憂悶計無所出，乃密賂宦者蔣裕，令誘建安人張安國，使據郡反，冀因此以圖高宗。
entries.en: The empress, anxious and at her wits' end, secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to stir Zhang Anguo of Jian'an into holding the commandery in rebellion, hoping thus to move against Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: The empress, worried and distressed with no plan, secretly bribed the eunuch Jiang Yu to induce Zhang Anguo of Jian'an to hold the commandery in rebellion, hoping thereby to strike at Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 安國事覺，並為高宗所誅。
entries.en: When Anguo's plot was discovered, Emperor Xuan had them all executed.
entries.literal: When Anguo's affair was discovered, all were executed by Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 時后左右近侍頗知其事，后恐連逮黨與，並殺之。
entries.en: Her close attendants largely knew of the plot; fearing they would be seized with their associates, she had them all killed.
entries.literal: At that time the empress's close attendants largely knew of the affair; fearing that their associates would be seized together, she had them all killed.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，以后為文皇后。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, the empress was titled Empress Wen.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, the empress was made Empress Wen.

entries.zh: 陳亡入隋，大業初，自長安歸于江南，頃之，卒。
entries.en: When Chen fell to Sui, in the early Daye era she returned from Chang'an to the south; soon she died.
entries.literal: When Chen fell and entered Sui, in the early Daye era she returned from Chang'an to the southland; before long she died.

entries.zh: 高宗柳皇后諱敬言，河東解人也。
entries.en: Empress Liu of Emperor Xuan, personal name Jingyan, came from Xie in Hedong.
entries.literal: Empress Liu of Emperor Xuan, personal name Jingyan, was from Xie in Hedong.

entries.zh: 曾祖世隆，齊侍中、司空、尚書令、貞陽忠武公。
entries.en: Her great-grandfather Shilong served Qi as palace attendant, minister of works, director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke Zhongwu of Zhenyang.
entries.literal: Her great-grandfather Shilong was palace attendant, minister of works, director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke Zhongwu of Zhenyang under Qi.

entries.zh: 祖惲，有重名於梁代，官至祕書監，贈侍中、中護軍。
entries.en: Her grandfather Yun had a weighty reputation under Liang, rose to director of the Palace Library, and was posthumously made palace attendant and central guard commander.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Yun had a weighty reputation in Liang times, rose to director of the Palace Library, and was posthumously presented as palace attendant and central guard commander.

entries.zh: 父偃，尚梁武帝女長城公主，拜駙馬都尉，大寶中，為鄱陽太守，卒官。
entries.en: Her father Yan married Princess Changcheng, daughter of Emperor Wu of Liang, and was made commandant of imperial sons-in-law. During Dabao he served as administrator of Poyang and died in office.
entries.literal: Her father Yan married Princess Changcheng, daughter of Emperor Wu of Liang, was appointed commandant of imperial sons-in-law, and during Dabao became administrator of Poyang, dying in office.

entries.zh: 后時年九歲，幹理家事，有若成人。
entries.en: The empress was nine at the time, yet she managed household affairs as if she were grown.
entries.literal: The empress was then nine years old, but managed household affairs as if she were an adult.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，后與弟盼往江陵依梁元帝，元帝以長城公主之故，待遇甚厚。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, the empress and her younger brother Pan went to Jiangling to seek refuge with Emperor Yuan of Liang. Because of Princess Changcheng, Emperor Yuan treated them with great favor.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, the empress and her younger brother Pan went to Jiangling to rely on Emperor Yuan of Liang; because of Princess Changcheng, Emperor Yuan treated them very generously.

entries.zh: 及高宗赴江陵，元帝以后配焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan came to Jiangling, Emperor Yuan gave the empress to him in marriage.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan went to Jiangling, Emperor Yuan matched the empress to him.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，后生後主於江陵。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year 2 (553), the empress gave birth to the Last Emperor at Jiangling.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year 2, the empress gave birth to the Last Emperor at Jiangling.

entries.zh: 明年，江陵陷，高宗遷于關右，后與後主俱留穰城。
entries.en: The next year Jiangling fell and Emperor Xuan was moved west of the passes, while the empress and the Last Emperor remained at Rangcheng.
entries.literal: The next year Jiangling fell, and Emperor Xuan was moved to the lands west of the passes; the empress and the Last Emperor both remained at Rangcheng.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，與後主還朝，后為安成王妃。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 2 (561), she returned to court with the Last Emperor and became Princess of Ancheng.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 2, she and the Last Emperor returned to court, and the empress became Princess of Ancheng.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，立為皇后。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, she was made empress.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 后美姿容，身長七尺二寸，手垂過膝。
entries.en: The empress had beautiful bearing, stood seven feet two inches tall, and her hands hung below her knees.
entries.literal: The empress had beautiful bearing, was seven feet two inches tall, and her hands hung below her knees.

entries.zh: 初，高宗居鄉里，先娶吳興錢氏女，及即位，拜為貴妃，甚有寵，后傾心下之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Emperor Xuan was living at home, he had first married a woman of the Qian clan of Wuxing. After he came to the throne he made her honored consort and favored her greatly, while the empress humbled herself before her with complete sincerity.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xuan was living in his home district, he had first married a woman of the Qian clan of Wuxing; when he ascended the throne, he appointed her honored consort and favored her greatly, while the empress lowered herself to her wholeheartedly.

entries.zh: 每尚方供奉之物，其上者皆推於貴妃，而己御其次焉。
entries.en: Whenever the imperial workshops supplied goods, she always yielded the finest to the honored consort and used the lesser ones herself.
entries.literal: Whenever objects were supplied by the imperial workshops, she always yielded the finest to the honored consort and used the lesser ones herself.

entries.zh: 高宗崩，始興王叔陵為亂，後主賴后與樂安君吳氏救而獲免，事在叔陵傳。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan died, Prince Shuling of Shixing rebelled. The Last Emperor escaped only because the empress and Lady Wu of Le'an rescued him; the affair is told in Shuling's biography.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Prince Shuling of Shixing made disorder; the Last Emperor escaped only through rescue by the empress and Lady Wu of Le'an. The affair is in Shuling's biography.

entries.zh: 後主即位，尊后為皇太后，宮曰弘範。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, he honored the empress as empress dowager; her palace was called Hongfan.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, he honored the empress as empress dowager, and her palace was called Hongfan.

entries.zh: 當是之時，新失淮南之地，隋師臨江，又國遭大喪，後主病瘡不能聽政，其誅叔陵、供大行喪事、邊境防守及百司红務，雖假以後主之命，實皆決之於后。
entries.en: At the time Huainan had just been lost, Sui forces were on the Yangzi, and the state was in mourning. The Last Emperor was ill with sores and could not hear government, so the execution of Shuling, the late emperor's funeral, frontier defense, and all the business of the offices were formally done in the Last Emperor's name but in fact decided by the empress.
entries.literal: At this time the Huainan lands had newly been lost, the Sui army stood on the Yangzi, and the state had suffered a great mourning; the Last Emperor was ill with sores and could not hear government, so the execution of Shuling, the funeral affairs for the deceased ruler, frontier defenses, and the many offices of government, though carried out in the Last Emperor's name, were all in fact decided by the empress.

entries.zh: 後主瘡愈，乃歸政焉。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor recovered, she returned the government to him.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor recovered from his sores, she then returned government to him.

entries.zh: 陳亡入長安，大業十一年薨於東都，[4]年八十三，葬洛陽之邙山。
entries.en: When Chen fell, she was taken to Chang'an. In Daye year 11 (615) she died at the Eastern Capital, [4] aged eighty-three, and was buried on Mang Mountain at Luoyang.
entries.literal: When Chen fell, she entered Chang'an; in Daye year 11 she died at the Eastern Capital, [4] aged eighty-three, and was buried on Mang Mountain at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 高宗柳皇后
entries.en: Emperor Xuan Empress Liu
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan Empress Liu

entries.zh: 昭容昭儀 北監本、汲本、殿本「昭儀」在「昭容」上。
entries.en: On "Zhaorong, Zhaoyi": Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions place Zhaoyi above Zhaorong.
entries.literal: Fair Lady Zhaorong / Lady Zhaoyi: in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Palace editions "Zhaoyi" stands above "Zhaorong."

entries.zh: 按《南史·后妃傳》序，梁武帝所制九嬪之序，「昭儀」在「昭容」上，陳制多襲梁，當以作「昭儀、昭容」為是。
entries.en: The Southern Dynasties preface to the consorts' biographies lists Liang's nine ranks with "Zhaoyi" above "Zhaorong"; Chen largely followed Liang, so "Zhaoyi, Zhaorong" is correct.
entries.literal: Note: the preface to the "Biographies of Empresses and Consorts" in the History of the Southern Dynasties, on the nine consort ranks instituted by Emperor Wu of Liang, places "Zhaoyi" above "Zhaorong"; Chen institutions mostly followed Liang—the order "Zhaoyi, Zhaorong" is correct.

entries.zh: 后叔君公，自梁元帝敗後，常在江陵。
entries.en: Her uncle Jun Gong, after Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated, stayed at Jiangling.
entries.literal: The empress's uncle Jun Gong, after Emperor Yuan of Liang was defeated, remained constantly at Jiangling.

entries.zh: 禎明中，與蕭瓛、蕭巖率红叛隋歸朝，後主擢為太子詹事。
entries.en: In the Zhenming era he and Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan led their men in defecting from Sui back to Chen; the Last Emperor made him grand mentor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the Zhenming era, together with Xiao Kan and Xiao Yan he led their followers in defecting from Sui and returning to court; the Last Emperor promoted him to grand mentor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 君公博學有才辯，善談論，後主深器之。
entries.en: Jun Gong was learned, eloquent, and skilled in debate; the Last Emperor prized him highly.
entries.literal: Jun Gong was broadly learned, talented in debate, and skilled at discussion; the Last Emperor valued him deeply.

entries.zh: 陳亡，隋文帝以其叛己，命斬于建康。
entries.en: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui had him beheaded at Jiankang for rebelling against Sui.
entries.literal: When Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui, because he had rebelled against Sui, ordered him beheaded at Jiankang.

entries.zh: 后性端靜，寡嗜慾，聰敏彊記，涉獵經史，工書翰。
entries.en: The empress was upright and quiet by nature, with few desires. She was intelligent, had a strong memory, read widely in the classics and histories, and was skilled with the brush.
entries.literal: The empress was upright and quiet by nature, with few desires; she was intelligent, had a strong memory, read in the classics and histories, and was skilled at writing.

entries.zh: 初，後主在東宮，而后父君理卒，后居憂，處於別殿，哀毀逾禮。
entries.en: Earlier, while the Last Emperor was still in the Eastern Palace, the empress's father Junli died. She observed mourning in a separate hall and wasted herself with grief beyond the rites.
entries.literal: Earlier, while the Last Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, the empress's father Junli died; the empress observed mourning and stayed in a separate hall, wasting herself with grief beyond the rites.

entries.zh: 後主遇后既薄，而張貴妃寵傾後宮，後宮之政嵭歸之，后澹然未嘗有所忌怨。
entries.en: The Last Emperor treated the empress coldly, while Noble Consort Zhang dominated the harem in favor and all inner-palace affairs passed to her. The empress remained calm and never showed jealousy or resentment.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor treated the empress coldly, while Noble Consort Zhang's favor dominated the rear palace and all inner-palace government went to her; the empress remained calm and never showed jealousy or resentment.

entries.zh: 而居處儉約，衣服無錦繡之飾，左右近侍纔百許人，唯尋閱圖史、誦佛經為事。
entries.en: She lived frugally, wore no brocade or embroidery, kept only about a hundred close attendants, and spent her time reading books and histories and reciting Buddhist scriptures.
entries.literal: Her living was frugal, her clothing had no brocade or embroidery, her close attendants numbered only about a hundred, and her only occupations were reading illustrated histories and reciting Buddhist scriptures.

entries.zh: 陳亡，與後主俱入長安。
entries.en: When Chen fell, she was taken to Chang'an with the Last Emperor.
entries.literal: When Chen fell, she and the Last Emperor both entered Chang'an.

entries.zh: 及後主薨，后自為哀辭，文甚酸切。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor died, the empress herself composed a lament, deeply sorrowful in its wording.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor died, the empress herself composed a lament, and the writing was deeply sorrowful.

entries.zh: 隋煬帝每所巡幸，恆令從駕。
entries.en: Whenever Emperor Yang of Sui went on tour, he always ordered her to accompany the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: Whenever Emperor Yang of Sui made an inspection tour, he always ordered her to accompany his carriage.

entries.zh: 及煬帝為宇文化及所害，后自廣陵過江還鄉里，不知所終。
entries.en: After Emperor Yang was killed by Yuwen Huaji, the empress crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and returned to her home district. Her end is unknown.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang was killed by Yuwen Huaji, the empress crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and returned to her home district; her end is unknown.

entries.zh: 後主張貴妃名麗華，兵家女也。
entries.en: Noble Consort Zhang of the Last Emperor, named Lihua, was the daughter of a military household.
entries.literal: Noble Consort Zhang of the Last Emperor, named Lihua, was the daughter of a military household.

entries.zh: 家貧，父兄以織席為事。
entries.en: Her family was poor, and her father and elder brothers made a living weaving mats.
entries.literal: Her family was poor, and her father and elder brothers made a living weaving mats.

entries.zh: 後主為太子，以選入宮。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor was crown prince, she was selected to enter the palace.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor was crown prince, she was selected to enter the palace.

entries.zh: 是時龔貴嬪為良娣，貴妃年十歲，為之給使，後主見而說焉，因得幸，遂有娠，生太子深。
entries.en: At the time Honored Consort Gong was liangdi, and the noble consort, then ten, served her. The Last Emperor saw and liked her, so she gained his favor, became pregnant, and gave birth to Crown Prince Shen.
entries.literal: At this time Honored Consort Gong was liangdi, and the noble consort, aged ten, served her; the Last Emperor saw her and liked her, so she gained favor, became pregnant, and gave birth to Crown Prince Shen.

entries.zh: 後主即位，拜為貴妃。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor came to the throne, she was appointed noble consort.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, she was appointed noble consort.

entries.zh: 性聰惠，甚被寵遇。
entries.en: She was intelligent and clever by nature and was greatly favored.
entries.literal: She was intelligent and clever by nature and was very much favored.

entries.zh: 後主每引貴妃與賓客遊宴，貴妃薦諸宮女預焉，後宮等咸德之，競言貴妃之善，由是愛傾後宮。
entries.en: Whenever the Last Emperor brought the noble consort to feasts with guests, she recommended other palace women to take part. The women of the harem were all grateful and competed to praise her goodness, so affection throughout the harem turned toward her.
entries.literal: Whenever the Last Emperor brought the noble consort to roam and feast with guests, she recommended palace women to take part; the women of the rear palace were all grateful and vied in speaking of the noble consort's goodness, so affection in the rear palace leaned wholly to her.

entries.zh: 又好厭魅之術，假鬼道以惑後主，置淫祀於宮中，聚諸妖巫使之鼓舞，因參訪外事，人閒有一言一事，妃必先知之，以白後主，由是益重妃，內外宗族，多被引用。
entries.en: She also delighted in spells and enchantment, using ghostly arts to delude the Last Emperor. She set up illicit sacrifices in the palace, gathered shamans and witches to drum and dance, and used them to inquire into outside affairs. Whenever some word or event arose among the people, the consort always knew it first and reported it to the Last Emperor. Because of this he valued her still more, and many of her relatives inside and outside the palace were brought into office.
entries.literal: She also liked arts of spells and enchantment, borrowed ghost ways to delude the Last Emperor, set up illicit sacrifices in the palace, gathered shamans and witches and had them drum and dance, and through them investigated outside affairs; if among the people there was a word or an event, the consort always knew it first and reported it to the Last Emperor. Because of this he valued her still more, and many of her kin inside and outside were brought into office.

entries.zh: 及隋軍陷臺城，妃與後主俱入于井，隋軍出之，晉王廣命斬貴妃，牓於青溪中橋。
entries.en: When the Sui army took Taicheng, the consort and the Last Emperor hid together in a well. Sui soldiers brought them out, and Guang, Prince of Jin, ordered the noble consort beheaded and displayed at the middle bridge over Qingxi.
entries.literal: When the Sui army took Taicheng, the consort and the Last Emperor both entered a well; Sui soldiers brought them out, and Guang, Prince of Jin, ordered the noble consort beheaded and displayed at the middle bridge over Qingxi.

entries.zh: 封建
entries.en: On "fengjian (establish-fief)"
entries.literal: "establish-fief" (fengjian)

entries.en: (cheng)
entries.literal: (cheng)

entries.zh: [城]縣侯 據《南史》改。
entries.en: On "[cheng] county marquis": emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.
entries.literal: [cheng] county marquis—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.

entries.zh: 按建城縣，漢侯邑。
entries.en: Jiancheng county was a Han enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Note: Jiancheng county was a Han marquisate.

entries.zh: 《太平寰宇記》引雷次宗《豫章記》云：「漢高帝置。
entries.en: The Universal Gazetteer quotes Lei Cizong's Record of Yuzhang: "Emperor Gaodi of Han established it.
entries.literal: The Universal Gazetteer cites Lei Cizong's Record of Yuzhang: "Emperor Gaodi of Han established it.

entries.zh: 以其創建城邑，故曰建城。」
entries.en: Because he founded the settlement, it was called Jiancheng."
entries.literal: Because he founded the city-settlement, it is called Jiancheng."

entries.zh: 今漢志、表作「建成」，後漢志以下皆作「建城」。
entries.en: The Han Treatise and tables read "Jiancheng" (built-complete); from the Later Han Treatise on all read "Jiancheng" (establish-city).
entries.literal: In the present Han Treatise and tables it reads "Jiancheng" (built-complete); from the Later Han Treatise onward all read "Jiancheng" (establish-city).

entries.zh: 後文后兄欽襲爵建城侯，亦作「建城」。
entries.en: Later Empress Wen's brother Qin inherited as Marquis of Jiancheng, likewise written "Jiancheng."
entries.literal: Later the younger brother of Empress Wen, Qin, inherited as Marquis of Jiancheng—there too it reads "Jiancheng."

entries.zh: 太建三年納為皇太子妃 按「太建三年」當依
entries.en: On "taken as crown prince's consort in Taijian year three": Taijian year three should follow
entries.literal: "In the third year of Taijian taken in as crown prince's consort"—note: on "third year of Taijian" one should follow

entries.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

entries.zh: 作「太建元年」。
entries.en: which reads "first year of Taijian."
entries.literal: which reads "first year of Taijian."

entries.zh: 〈沈君理傳〉
entries.en: 〈Biography of Shen Junli〉
entries.literal: 〈Biography of Shen Junli〉

entries.zh: 云太建二年高宗以君理女為皇太子妃，亦訛。
entries.en: says the High Ancestor made Junli's daughter crown prince's consort in Taijian year two—that too is wrong.
entries.literal: says that in Taijian year two the High Ancestor made Junli's daughter crown prince's consort—this too is erroneous.

entries.zh: 陳書卷七
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 7
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 7

entries.zh: 周鐵虎，不知何許人也，梁世南渡。
entries.en: Zhou Tiehu came from no known place. Under Liang he crossed south with the migration.
entries.literal: Zhou Tiehu—no one knew where he was from; in the Liang era he crossed south.

entries.zh: 語音傖重，膂力過人，便馬槊，事梁河東王蕭譽，以勇敢聞，譽板為府中兵參軍。
entries.en: He spoke with a heavy northern accent, had uncommon strength, and fought well from horseback with the spear. He served Liang's Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, and won a name for bravery. Yu commissioned him military adjutant in the princely staff.
entries.literal: His speech was thick with a northern accent; his physical strength surpassed other men; he was skilled with horse and spear; he served Liang's Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, and was known for courage; Yu appointed him by commission as military adjutant in the prince's establishment.

entries.zh: 譽為廣州刺史，以鐵虎為興寧令。
entries.en: When Yu became inspector of Guangzhou, he made Tiehu magistrate of Xingning.
entries.literal: When Yu became Inspector of Guangzhou, he made Tiehu magistrate of Xingning.

entries.zh: 譽遷湘州，又為臨蒸令。
entries.en: When Yu moved to Xiangzhou, Tiehu was again made magistrate of Linzheng.
entries.literal: When Yu was transferred to Xiangzhou, Tiehu was again made magistrate of Linzheng.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝於荊州遣世子方等代譽，且以兵臨之。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou sent his heir Fangdeng to replace Yu and marched troops against him.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan at Jingzhou sent the heir Fangdeng to replace Yu and also advanced troops against him.

entries.zh: 譽拒戰，大捷，方等死，鐵虎功最，譽委遇甚重。
entries.en: Yu fought back and won a crushing victory. Fangdeng was killed. Tiehu's merit stood first, and Yu relied on him ever more heavily.
entries.literal: Yu resisted in battle and won a great victory; Fangdeng died; Tiehu's merit was foremost; Yu entrusted and favored him heavily.

entries.zh: 及王僧辯討譽，於陣獲鐵虎，僧辯命烹之，鐵虎呼曰：「侯景未滅，柰何殺壯士。」
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yu, he took Tiehu on the field. Sengbian ordered him boiled alive. Tiehu shouted, "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—why kill a fighting man?"
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Yu, he captured Tiehu in the battle line; Sengbian ordered him boiled alive; Tiehu cried out: "Hou Jing is not yet destroyed—how can you kill a stalwart?"

entries.zh: 僧辯奇其言，乃宥之，還其麾下。
entries.en: Sengbian was struck by his words, spared him, and returned him to his troops.
entries.literal: Sengbian marveled at his words, then pardoned him and returned him to his command.

entries.zh: 及侯景西上，鐵虎從僧辯克任約，獲宋子仙，每戰皆有功。
entries.en: When Hou Jing marched west, Tiehu followed Sengbian against Ren Yue, took Song Zixian prisoner, and earned merit in every fight.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing marched west, Tiehu followed Sengbian in defeating Ren Yue, captured Song Zixian, and in every battle had merit.

entries.zh: 元帝承制授仁威將軍、潼州刺史，封沌陽縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan's provisional commission he was made general of benevolent prestige and inspector of Tongzhou, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Dunyang with three hundred households.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Yuan's provisional mandate he was made General of Benevolent Prestige and Inspector of Tongzhou, enfeoffed as Viscount of Dunyang county with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 又從僧辯克定京邑，降謝答仁，平陸納於湘州。
entries.en: He again followed Sengbian in recovering the capital, took Xie Daren's surrender, and pacified Lu Na in Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: He again followed Sengbian in recovering the capital, received the surrender of Xie Daren, and pacified Lu Na in Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，以前後戰功，進爵為侯，增邑赠前五百戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Chengsheng (553), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, for his successive battle merits he was advanced to marquis, his fief increased together with the previous to five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍為散騎常侍，領信義太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was then made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and concurrently administrator of Xinyi, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He was then made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, concurrently Administrator of Xinyi, general as before.

entries.zh: 高祖誅僧辯，鐵虎率所部降，因復其本職。
entries.en: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Tiehu surrendered with his command and was restored to his former post.
entries.literal: The Founder executed Sengbian; Tiehu led his command in surrender and thereby recovered his former post.

entries.zh: 時有盱眙馬明，字世朗，梁世事鄱陽嗣王蕭範。
entries.en: At that time Ma Ming of Xuyi, styled Shilang, had served under Liang the Prince of Poyang, Xiao Fan.
entries.literal: At that time there was Ma Ming of Xuyi, styled Shilang, who under Liang served the Prince of Poyang, Xiao Fan.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，據廬江之東界，拒賊臨城柵。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he held Lujiang's eastern border and held the rebels at bay at the Lincheng stockade.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he held the eastern border of Lujiang and resisted the rebels at the Lincheng stockade.

entries.zh: 元帝授散騎常侍、平北將軍、北论州刺史，領廬江太守。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan made him scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who pacifies the north, inspector of Beixi, and concurrently administrator of Lujiang.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Beixi province, and concurrently Administrator of Lujiang.

entries.zh: 荊州陷沒，歸于高祖。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell he submitted to the Founder.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou fell, he came over to the Founder.

entries.zh: 紹泰中，復官位，封西華縣侯，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the Shaotai era his offices were restored and he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xihua with two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the Shaotai era his offices were restored; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xihua county with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 亦隨文育西征王琳，於沌口軍敗，明力戰死之，贈使持節、征西將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: He too followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken; Ming fought to the death. He was posthumously given the staff of authority, made general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: He too followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin; at Dankou the army was defeated; Ming fought fiercely and died; he was posthumously given the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，靈洗聚徒據黟、歙以拒景。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lingxi gathered followers and held Yi and She against Jing.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lingxi gathered followers and held Yi and She to resist Jing.

entries.zh: 景軍據有新安，新安太守湘西鄉侯蕭隱奔依靈洗，靈洗奉以主盟。
entries.en: Jing's army held Xin'an. The administrator, Marquis of Xiangxi village Xiao Yin, fled to Lingxi, who took him as head of the alliance.
entries.literal: Jing's army held Xin'an; the Administrator of Xin'an, Marquis of Xiangxi village, Xiao Yin, fled to rely on Lingxi; Lingxi received him as alliance chief.

entries.zh: 梁元帝於荊州承制，又遣使間道奉表。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou took provisional authority; Lingxi also sent envoys by secret paths to present memorials.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou assumed provisional authority; he also sent envoys by hidden routes to present memorials.

entries.zh: 劉神茂自東陽建義拒賊，靈洗攻下新安，與神茂相應。
entries.en: Liu Shenmao raised arms at Dongyang against the rebels. Lingxi took Xin'an and acted in concert with him.
entries.literal: Liu Shenmao raised righteous arms at Dongyang to resist the rebels; Lingxi took Xin'an and coordinated with Shenmao.

entries.zh: 元帝授持節、通直散騎常侍、都督新安郡諸軍事、雲麾將軍、譙州刺史資，領新安太守，封巴丘縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan gave him the staff, made him regular attendant of direct communication and commander of all forces in Xin'an, cloud-banner general and inspector of Qiao with credentials, administrator of Xin'an, and Marquis of Baqiu with five hundred households.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Xin'an commandery, Cloud-Banner General, Inspector of Qiao province with credentials, concurrently Administrator of Xin'an, and enfeoffed Marquis of Baqiu county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 神茂為景所破，景偏帥呂子榮進攻新安，靈洗退保黟、歙。
entries.en: Shenmao was defeated by Jing. Jing's lieutenant Lü Zirong pressed Xin'an; Lingxi fell back to Yi and She.
entries.literal: Shenmao was broken by Jing; Jing's lieutenant Lü Zirong advanced against Xin'an; Lingxi withdrew to hold Yi and She.

entries.zh: 及景敗，子榮退走，靈洗復據新安。
entries.en: When Jing fell, Zirong withdrew and Lingxi recovered Xin'an.
entries.literal: When Jing was defeated, Zirong withdrew; Lingxi again held Xin'an.

entries.zh: 進軍建德，擒賊帥趙桑乾。
entries.en: He advanced on Jiande and captured the rebel chief Zhao Sanggan.
entries.literal: He advanced on Jiande and captured the rebel chief Zhao Sanggan.

entries.zh: 以功授持節、散騎常侍、都督青冀二州諸軍事、青州刺史，增邑赠前一千戶，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: For merit he received the staff, was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Qing and Ji, and inspector of Qing; his fief rose to one thousand households in all; he kept his general's rank and the administration.
entries.literal: For his merit he was given the Staff, made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qing and Ji provinces, and Inspector of Qing province; his fief was increased together with the previous to one thousand households; general and administrator as before.

entries.zh: 又隨文育西征王琳，於沌口敗績，鐵虎與文育、侯安都嵭為琳所擒。
entries.en: He marched west again with Wenyü against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken, and Tiehu, Wenyü, and Hou Andu were all captured.
entries.literal: He again followed Wenyü west against Wang Lin; at Dankou they were defeated; Tiehu, with Wenyü and Hou Andu, were all taken by Lin.

entries.zh: 琳引見諸將，與之語，唯鐵虎辭氣不屈，故琳盡宥文育之徒，獨鐵虎見害，時年四十九。
entries.en: Lin called the generals before him. Only Tiehu answered without bending. Lin spared Wenyü and the rest but put Tiehu to death. He was forty-nine.
entries.literal: Lin summoned the generals to audience and spoke with them; only Tiehu's words and bearing were unyielding; therefore Lin pardoned all Wenyü's party but Tiehu alone was killed; he was forty-nine.

entries.zh: 高祖聞之，下詔曰：「天地之寶，所貴曰生，形魄之徒，所重唯命。
entries.en: When the Founder heard, he issued an edict: "Heaven and earth treasure life above all; among mortal men nothing weighs like a single fate.
entries.literal: When the Founder heard of it, he issued an edict saying: "The treasure of Heaven and Earth is life itself; among embodied souls nothing is heavier than fate.

entries.zh: 至如捐生立節，刋命酬恩，追遠懷昔，信宜加等。
entries.en: To throw away life for principle and spend one's last breath repaying grace—when the court looks back on such men, honor must rise by degrees.
entries.literal: As for giving life to establish integrity and laying down life to repay kindness—when one looks back on the distant past and cherishes the former age, honor should indeed be raised by degrees.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍、嚴威將軍、太子左衛率、潼州刺史、領信義太守沌陽縣開國侯鐵虎，器局沈厚，風力勇壯，北討南征，竭忠盡力。
entries.en: Scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, left defender of the heir, inspector of Tongzhou, administrator of Xinyi, and Marquis of Dunyang, Tiehu—deep of bearing, fierce in the field—fought north and south until loyalty and strength were spent.
entries.literal: Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Stern Prestige General, Left Defender of the Heir Apparent, Inspector of Tongzhou, Administrator of Xinyi, and Marquis of Dunyang county Tiehu—his bearing was deep and weighty, his martial spirit brave and strong; north and south he campaigned, exhausting loyalty and strength.

entries.zh: 推鋒江夏，致陷凶徒，神氣彌雄，肆言無撓。
entries.en: He led the charge at Jiangxia and fell into the rebels' hands. His spirit only hardened; he spoke plainly and would not yield.
entries.literal: He drove the van at Jiangxia and fell among the rebels; his spirit grew only sterner; he spoke freely and would not bend.

entries.zh: 豈直溫序見害，方其理鬚，龐德臨危，猶能瞋目。
entries.en: Was this not Wen Xu at his death, stroking his beard, or Pang De at the end still glaring in wrath?
entries.literal: Was this not like Wen Xu meeting death and stroking his beard, or Pang De at the last hour still glaring with anger?

entries.zh: 忠貞如此，惻愴兼深，可贈侍中、護軍將軍、青冀二州刺史，加封一千戶，赠給鼓吹一部，侯如故。」
entries.en: Constancy such as this stirs the deepest grief. Let him be posthumously palace attendant, general who protects the army, and inspector of Qing and Ji; add one thousand households to his fief; grant a suite of war drums; let his marquisate stand as before."
entries.literal: Loyalty and constancy such as this move pity to the depths; he may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Protects the Army, and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; his fief is increased by one thousand households; a suite of war drums is granted; his marquisate is unchanged."

entries.zh: 天嘉五年，世祖又詔曰：「漢室功臣，形寫宮觀，魏朝猛將，名配宗祧，功烈所以長存，世代因之不朽。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianjia (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjia, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.

entries.zh: 故侍中、護軍將軍、青冀二州刺史沌陽縣開國侯鐵虎，誠節梗亮，力用雄敢，王業初基，行閒累及，垂翅賊壘，正色寇庭，古之遺烈，有識同壯。
entries.en: The late palace attendant, general who protects the army, inspector of Qing and Ji, and Marquis of Dunyang, Tiehu—upright in loyalty, bold in battle—was caught when the dynasty was young, yet in the rebels' camp he kept his color before the foe, a hero of old days whom all who knew him admired.
entries.literal: The late Palace Attendant, General Who Protects the Army, Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, and Marquis of Dunyang county Tiehu—his loyalty was upright and bright, his strength bold; when the royal enterprise was first founded he was caught in the course of events; wings folded in the rebel camp, he kept his color in the enemy's court—an ancient hero; the discerning share his awe.

entries.zh: 隕身不屈，雖隆榮等，營魂易遠，言追嘉惜。
entries.en: He died unbowed. Though honors were piled on him, his spirit is far; the court speaks only praise and regret.
entries.literal: He fell without yielding; though glory was heaped on him, the returning soul is far; words of praise and regret follow.

entries.zh: 宜仰陪壖寢，恭頒饗奠，可配食高祖廟庭。」
entries.en: Let him attend the Founder's mound and receive sacrifice with reverence, and share offerings in the Founder's temple."
entries.literal: He should attend the Founder's tomb mound and receive sacrificial offerings with reverence; he may share offerings in the Founder's temple hall."

entries.zh: 子瑜嗣。
entries.en: His son Yu succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Yu succeeded.

entries.zh: 隨周文育西討王琳，於沌口敗績，為琳所拘。
entries.en: He followed Zhou Wenyü west against Wang Lin. At Dankou the army was broken and Lin held him prisoner.
entries.literal: He followed Zhou Wenyü west to attack Wang Lin; at Dankou they were defeated and he was detained by Lin.

entries.zh: 明年，與侯安都等逃歸。
entries.en: The next year he escaped back with Hou Andu and the rest.
entries.literal: The next year he escaped back with Hou Andu and others.

entries.zh: 兼丹陽尹，出為高唐、太原二郡太守，仍鎮南陵。
entries.en: He was concurrently administrator of Danyang, then went out as administrator of Gaotang and Taiyuan and still held Nanling.
entries.literal: He was concurrently Administrator of Danyang; he went out as Administrator of Gaotang and Taiyuan commanderies and still garrisoned Nanling.

entries.zh: 遷太子左衛率。
entries.en: He was transferred to left defender of the heir.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Defender of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，王琳前軍東下，靈洗於南陵破之，虜其兵士，并獲青龍十餘乘。
entries.en: When the Founder died, Wang Lin's vanguard marched east. Lingxi broke it at Nanling, took its troops prisoner, and seized more than ten green-dragon coaches.
entries.literal: When the Founder died, Wang Lin's vanguard marched east; Lingxi defeated it at Nanling, captured its soldiers, and also seized more than ten green-dragon coaches.

entries.zh: 以功授持節、都督南豫州緣江諸軍事、信武將軍、南豫州刺史。
entries.en: For merit he received the staff and was made commander of South Yuzhou's river frontier forces, trustworthy-martial general, and inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: For his merit he was given the Staff, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs along the Yangzi frontier in South Yuzhou, Trustworthy Martial General, and Inspector of South Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 侯瑱等敗王琳于柵口，靈洗乘勝逐北，據有魯山。
entries.en: Hou Tian and others defeated Wang Lin at Zhakou. Lingxi pressed the rout and took Lushan.
entries.literal: Hou Tian and others defeated Wang Lin at Zhakou; Lingxi pursued the victory north and held Lushan.

entries.zh: 徵為左衛將軍，[2]餘如故。
entries.en: He was recalled as left guard general; [2] all else unchanged.
entries.literal: He was summoned to be Left Guard General; the rest as before.

entries.zh: 仍令靈洗率所部下揚州，助王僧辯鎮防。
entries.en: He was then ordered to lead his command to Yangzhou to help Wang Sengbian hold the garrison.
entries.literal: He was then ordered to lead his command down to Yangzhou to assist Wang Sengbian in garrison defense.

entries.zh: 遷吳興太守，未行，僧辯命靈洗從侯瑱西援荊州。
entries.en: He was named administrator of Wuxing, but before he went Sengbian sent him with Hou Tian west to relieve Jingzhou.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing; before he took up the post Sengbian ordered Lingxi to follow Hou Tian west to relieve Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，還都。
entries.en: Jingzhou fell and he returned to the capital.
entries.literal: Jingzhou fell; he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖誅僧辯，靈洗率所領來援，其徒力戰於石頭西門，[1]軍不利，遣使招諭，久之乃降，高祖深義之。
entries.en: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Lingxi marched to his aid. His men fought hard at Shitou's western gate. [1] The battle went against them. Messengers were sent to summon and persuade him; only after long delay did he yield. The Founder held his conduct in high esteem.
entries.literal: The Founder executed Sengbian; Lingxi led his command to come to the rescue; his troops fought fiercely at Shitou's western gate; the army fared ill; envoys were sent to summon and instruct him; only after a long time did he surrender; the Founder deeply approved his conduct.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，授使持節、信武將軍、蘭陵太守，常侍如故，助防京口。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he received the staff, was made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Lanling, retaining his attendant post, to help defend Jingkou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was given the Staff of Authority, made Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Lanling, regular attendant as before, to assist in defending Jingkou.

entries.zh: 及平徐嗣徽，靈洗有功，除南丹陽太守，封遂安縣侯，增邑并前一千五百戶，仍鎮採石。
entries.en: When Xu Sihui was suppressed Lingxi earned merit. He was made administrator of South Danyang, enfeoffed Marquis of Suian, his fief brought to one thousand five hundred households in all, and continued to hold Caishi.
entries.literal: When Xu Sihui was pacified Lingxi had merit; he was made Administrator of South Danyang, enfeoffed Marquis of Suian county, his fief increased together with the previous to one thousand five hundred households; he still garrisoned Caishi.

entries.zh: 靈洗性嚴急，御下甚苛刻，士卒有小罪，必以軍法誅之，造次之閒，便加捶撻，而號令分明，與士卒同甘苦，红亦以此依附。
entries.en: Lingxi was harsh by nature and ruled his men with iron severity. Small faults brought military execution; idle moments brought the lash. Yet his orders were clear, he shared hardship with the ranks, and the troops clung to him for it.
entries.literal: Lingxi's nature was stern and harsh; in commanding subordinates he was very severe; for small offenses among the soldiers he invariably executed them by military law; in idle moments he would add beatings; yet his orders were clear, he shared hardship and comfort with the soldiers, and the troops for that reason attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 性好播植，躬勤耕稼，至於水陸所宜，刈穫早晚，雖老農不能及也。
entries.en: He loved to plant and worked the fields himself. What suited wet land or dry, when to cut and when to gather—veteran farmers could not match him.
entries.literal: By nature he loved planting; he personally labored at tillage; as to what suited land and water, when to reap and harvest—though old farmers could not match him.

entries.zh: 伎妾無游手，嵭督之紡績。
entries.en: His concubines had no idle hands; all were set to spin and weave.
entries.literal: His concubines had no idle hands; all were pressed to spin and weave.

entries.zh: 至於散用貲財，亦弗儉吝。
entries.en: When he spent, he did not count small coins.
entries.literal: As for distributing wealth in expenditure, he was not stingy.

entries.zh: 光大二年，卒於州，時年五十五。
entries.en: In the second year of Guangda (568) he died in office, aged fifty-five.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangda he died in his province, aged fifty-five.

entries.zh: 贈鎮西將軍、開府儀同三司，謚曰忠壯。
entries.en: He was posthumously made garrisoning-west general and opener of an office equal to the three dukes, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Garrisoning-West General and Opener of an Office Equal to the Three Dukes; posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

entries.zh: 太建四年，詔配享高祖廟庭。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Taijian (572) an edict ordered him to share offerings in the Founder's temple.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian an edict ordered him to share offerings in the Founder's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子文季嗣。
entries.en: His son Wenji succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Wenji succeeded.

entries.zh: 文季字少卿。
entries.en: Wenji, styled Shaoqing.
entries.literal: Wenji, styled Shaoqing.

entries.zh: 幼習騎射，多幹略，果決有父風。
entries.en: From boyhood he trained in riding and archery, had his father's resource, and was resolute in his father's mold.
entries.literal: From childhood he practiced riding and archery; he had much resourcefulness; he was resolute and had his father's manner.

entries.zh: 弱冠從靈洗征討，必前登陷陣。
entries.en: At twenty he followed Lingxi on campaign and was always first over the wall and into the breach.
entries.literal: At twenty he followed Lingxi on campaigns and always was first to scale the ramparts and break the line.

entries.zh: 靈洗與周文育、侯安都等敗於沌口，為王琳所執，高祖召陷賊諸將子弟厚遇之，文季最有禮容，深為高祖所賞。
entries.en: When Lingxi, Wenyü, and Hou Andu were beaten at Dankou and held by Wang Lin, the Founder summoned the sons of captured generals and treated them well. Wenji bore himself best and won the Founder's deep regard.
entries.literal: When Lingxi, with Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu, were defeated at Dankou and taken by Wang Lin, the Founder summoned the sons of generals who had fallen into the enemy and treated them generously; Wenji had the finest bearing and was deeply prized by the Founder.

entries.zh: 永定中，累遷通直散騎侍郎、句容令。
entries.en: In the Yongding era he rose through regular attendant of direct communication to magistrate of Jurong.
entries.literal: In the Yongding era he was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and magistrate of Jurong.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，除宣惠始興王府限內中直兵參軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was made central straight military adjutant in the establishment of the Manifest Favor Prince of Shixing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he was made Central Straight Military Adjutant within the limits of the Manifest Favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.

entries.zh: 是時王為揚州刺史，鎮冶城，府中軍事，悉以委之。
entries.en: The prince was then inspector of Yangzhou, holding Yecheng; all military business of the staff was placed in Wenji's hands.
entries.literal: At that time the prince was Inspector of Yangzhou and garrisoned Yecheng; all military affairs of the establishment were entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，除貞毅將軍、新安太守，仍隨侯安都東討留異。
entries.en: In the second year of Tianjia (561) he was made steadfast-resolution general and administrator of Xin'an, and marched east with Hou Andu against Liu Yi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjia he was made Steadfast Resolution General and Administrator of Xin'an, and still followed Hou Andu east against Liu Yi.

entries.zh: 異黨向文政據有新安，文季率精甲三百，輕往攻之。
entries.en: Yi's man Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an. Wenji took three hundred picked armored men and struck lightly.
entries.literal: Yi's partisan Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an; Wenji led three hundred picked armored men and went lightly to attack him.

entries.zh: 文政遣其兄子瓚來拒，文季與戰，大破瓚軍，文政乃降。
entries.en: Wenzheng sent his brother's son Zan to meet him. Wenji routed Zan's force and Wenzheng surrendered.
entries.literal: Wenzheng sent his elder brother's son Zan to resist; Wenji fought him, broke Zan's army completely, and Wenzheng then surrendered.

entries.zh: 四年，陳寶應與留異連結，又遣兵隨周迪更出臨川，世祖遣信義太守余孝頃自海道襲晉安，文季為之前軍，所向克捷。
entries.en: In the fourth year Chen Baoying allied with Liu Yi and sent troops with Zhou Di against Linchuan again. Emperor Wen sent Yu Xiaoqing, administrator of Xinyi, by sea against Jin'an with Wenji as vanguard. Everywhere they went they prevailed.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Chen Baoying joined with Liu Yi; he also sent troops with Zhou Di to come out again at Linchuan; Emperor Wen sent the Administrator of Xinyi, Yu Xiaoqing, by the sea route to strike Jin'an; Wenji served as his vanguard; wherever he went he won.

entries.zh: 陳寶應平，文季戰功居多，還，轉府諮議參軍，領中直兵。
entries.en: When Baoying was suppressed Wenji's battle merit stood first. On return he was made advisory military adjutant of the staff, still commanding the central straight guard.
entries.literal: When Chen Baoying was pacified Wenji's battle merit was greatest; on return he was transferred to advisory military adjutant of the establishment, concurrently commanding the central straight guard.

entries.zh: 出為臨海太守。
entries.en: He went out as administrator of Linhai.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Linhai.

entries.zh: 尋乘金翅助父鎮郢城。
entries.en: Before long he sailed a golden-wing warship to help his father hold Yingcheng.
entries.literal: Soon he took the golden-wing [vessel] to help his father garrison Yingcheng.

entries.zh: 華皎平，靈洗及文季嵭有扞禦之功。
entries.en: After Hua Jiao was suppressed, both Lingxi and Wenji were credited with defensive merit.
entries.literal: When Hua Jiao was pacified, Lingxi and Wenji both had merit in defense.

entries.zh: 及靈洗卒，文季盡領其红，起為超武將軍，仍助防郢州。
entries.en: When Lingxi died, Wenji assumed command of all his troops, was made super-martial general, and continued to help defend Yingzhou.
entries.literal: When Lingxi died, Wenji took full command of his troops; he was raised as Super Martial General and still helped defend Ying prefecture.

entries.zh: 文季性至孝，雖軍旅奪禮，而毀瘠甚至。
entries.en: Wenji was deeply filial; though active service set mourning aside, he grew emaciated with grief.
entries.literal: Wenji was by nature extremely filial; though campaigns set aside mourning rites, he wasted away from grief to an extreme degree.

entries.zh: 太建二年，為豫章內史，將軍如故。
entries.en: In Taijian year two he was appointed interior secretary of Yuzhang, keeping his general's rank.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taijian he was made Interior Secretary of Yuzhang; his general's rank was unchanged.

entries.zh: 服闋，襲封重安縣公。
entries.en: When mourning ended he inherited the dukedom of Chong'an county.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Chong'an county.

entries.zh: 隨都督章昭達率軍往荊州征蕭巋。
entries.en: He followed Zhang Zhaoda, area commander, who led an army to Jingzhou against Xiao Kui.
entries.literal: He followed Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda leading troops to Jingzhou to campaign against Xiao Kui.

entries.zh: 巋與周軍多造舟艦，置于青泥水中。
entries.en: Kui and the Northern Zhou forces built many warships and anchored them in the Qingni channel.
entries.literal: Kui and the Zhou army built many ships and placed them in the Qingni waters.

entries.zh: 時水長漂疾，昭達乃遣文季共錢道戢輕舟襲之，盡焚其舟艦。
entries.en: With the river swollen and swift, Zhaoda sent Wenji and Qian Daozhi in light craft to strike and burn the entire fleet.
entries.literal: When the river was high and flowing fast, Zhaoda sent Wenji together with Qian Daozhi in light boats to attack, and they burned all the ships.

entries.zh: 昭達因蕭巋等兵稍怠，又遣文季夜入其外城，殺傷甚红。
entries.en: As Xiao Kui's men slackened, Zhaoda sent Wenji again by night into the outer city, killing many.
entries.literal: Zhaoda took advantage of Xiao Kui's troops growing slack and again sent Wenji by night into the outer city, inflicting very many casualties.

entries.zh: 既而周兵大出，巴陵內史雷道勤拒戰死之，文季僅以身免。
entries.en: Northern Zhou then brought up its main force; Lei Daoqin, interior secretary of Baling, died fighting; Wenji barely escaped alive.
entries.literal: Soon the Zhou army came out in force; Lei Daoqin, Interior Secretary of Baling, fought to the death in resistance; Wenji barely escaped with his life.

entries.zh: 以功加通直散騎常侍、安遠將軍，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made supernumerary regular attendant and distant-pacifying general, with five hundred added households.
entries.literal: For merit he was given Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Distant-Pacifying General, fief increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 10
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 10

entries.zh: 黃法抃字仲昭，巴山新建人也。
entries.en: Huang Faqu, styled Zhongzhao, came from Xinjian in Bashan.
entries.literal: Huang Faqu, styled Zhongzhao, was a native of Xinjian in Bashan.

entries.zh: 少勁捷有膽力，步行日三百里，距躍三丈。
entries.en: As a young man he was quick and fearless, could march three hundred li in a day on foot, and leap three zhang in a bound.
entries.literal: In youth he was vigorous and swift, brave and strong; on foot he could cover three hundred li in a day and leap three zhang.

entries.zh: 頗便書疏，閑明簿領，出入郡中，為鄉閭所憚。
entries.en: He wrote well and kept accounts with ease. Moving through the commandery, he was feared in every village.
entries.literal: He was quite skilled at letters and memorials, clear and adept in registers and accounts; moving in and out of the commandery, the township and hamlets feared him.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，於鄉里合徒眾。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled he raised a band in his home district.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered followers in his native place.

entries.zh: 太守賀詡下江州，法抃監知郡事。
entries.en: When Administrator He Xu went downriver to Jiangzhou, Faqu took charge of the commandery.
entries.literal: The Administrator He Xu went down to Jiangzhou; Faqu supervised and managed commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖將踰嶺入援建業，李遷仕作梗中途，高祖命周文育屯于西昌，法抃遣兵助文育。
entries.en: The Founder was about to cross the mountains to relieve Jianye, but Li Qianshi blocked the road. He ordered Zhou Wenyü to camp at Xichang, and Faqu sent troops to join him.
entries.literal: The Founder was about to cross the mountains to enter and relieve Jianye; Li Qianshi obstructed him midway; the Founder ordered Zhou Wenyü to encamp at Xichang; Faqu sent troops to aid Wenyü.

entries.zh: 時法抃出頓新淦縣，景遣行臺于慶至豫章，慶分兵來襲新淦，法抃拒戰，敗之。
entries.en: Faqu was then encamped at Xingan. Jing's touring commissioner Yu Qing reached Yuzhang and sent a detachment against Xingan. Faqu met them in battle and drove them off.
entries.literal: At that time Faqu had gone out to garrison Xingan county; Jing sent touring commissioner Yu Qing to Yuzhang; Qing divided his troops to strike at Xingan; Faqu resisted in battle and defeated them.

entries.zh: 高祖亦遣文育進軍討慶，文育疑慶兵彊，未敢進，法抃率眾會之，因進克笙屯，俘獲甚眾。
entries.en: The Founder also sent Wenyü against Qing, but Wenyü feared Qing's strength and held back. Faqu brought his men to join him, then they advanced together, took Sheng tun, and captured a great host of prisoners and plunder.
entries.literal: The Founder also sent Wenyü to advance and campaign against Qing; Wenyü doubted Qing's troops were strong and dared not advance; Faqu led his masses to join him, then advanced and captured Sheng tun, taking captives and booty in great number.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝凡遣五軍入援京邑，量預其一。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang sent five armies to aid the capital, and Chunyu Liang served in one of them.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang sent five armies in all to aid the capital, and Liang was among them.

entries.zh: 臺城陷，量還荊州。
entries.en: When Taicheng fell, Liang returned to Jingzhou.
entries.literal: When Taicheng fell, Liang returned to Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 元帝承制以量為假節、通直散騎常侍、都督巴州諸軍事、信威將軍、巴州刺史。
entries.en: Acting by delegated authority, Emperor Yuan appointed Liang as Acting with the Tally, Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, commander of all military affairs in Bazhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Inspector of Bazhou.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting by delegated authority, made Liang Acting with the Tally, Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, Commander-in-chief of the military affairs of Bazhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Inspector of Bazhou.

entries.zh: 侯景西上攻巴州，元帝使都督王僧辯入據巴陵。
entries.en: When Hou Jing advanced west to attack Bazhou, Emperor Yuan sent the commander Wang Sengbian to occupy Baling.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing advanced west and attacked Bazhou, Emperor Yuan sent the commander Wang Sengbian to enter and occupy Baling.

entries.zh: 量與僧辯并力拒景，大敗景軍，擒其將任約。
entries.en: Liang joined forces with Sengbian to resist Jing, badly defeated Jing's army, and captured his general Ren Yue.
entries.literal: Liang joined strength with Sengbian to resist Jing, greatly defeated Jing's army, and captured his general Ren Yue.

entries.zh: 進攻郢州，獲宋子仙。
entries.en: They advanced on Yingzhou and captured Song Zixian.
entries.literal: They advanced to attack Yingzhou and captured Song Zixian.

entries.zh: 仍隨僧辯克平侯景，
entries.en: He then followed Sengbian in defeating and pacifying Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He then followed Sengbian in defeating and pacifying Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 承聖元年，以功授左衛將軍，封謝沐縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Chengsheng, for this merit he was appointed Left Guard General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiemu County, with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chengsheng, for this merit he was appointed Left Guard General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiemu County with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋出為持節、都督桂定東西寧等四州諸軍事、信威將軍、安遠護軍、桂州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was sent out as Envoy Holding the Tally, commander of all military affairs in the four provinces of Gui, Ding, East Ning, and West Ning, General of Trustworthy Might, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Distant, and Inspector of Guizhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent out as Envoy Holding the Tally, Commander-in-chief of the military affairs of the four provinces Gui, Ding, East Ning, and West Ning, General of Trustworthy Might, Protector-general Who Pacifies the Distant, and Inspector of Guizhou.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，量保據桂州。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell, Liang held Guizhou.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou fell, Liang held and defended Guizhou.

entries.zh: 王琳擁割湘、郢，累遣召量，量外雖與琳往來，而別遣使從閒道歸於高祖。
entries.en: Wang Lin held Xiang and Ying and repeatedly summoned Liang. Outwardly Liang dealt with Lin, but in secret he sent envoys by hidden paths to the Founder.
entries.literal: Wang Lin held and carved up Xiang and Ying; he repeatedly sent summonses to Liang; outwardly Liang kept dealings with Lin, but separately he sent emissaries by a bypath to return to the Founder.

entries.zh: 高祖受襌，授持節、散騎常侍、平西大將軍，給鼓吹一部，都督、刺史並如故。
entries.en: When the Founder received the abdication, Liang was made credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, with pipes and drums and his command and inspectorship unchanged.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was appointed credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and pacify-west grand general, given one set of pipes and drums, area commander and inspector as before.

entries.zh: 尋進號鎮南將軍。
entries.en: Soon his title was raised to secure-the-south general.
entries.literal: Soon his designation was advanced to secure-the-south general.

entries.zh: 仍授都督、鎮西大將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: He was then made area commander, secure-the-west grand general, and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: He was then appointed area commander, secure-the-west grand general, and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，進號征南大將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, his title was raised to campaign-south grand general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, his designation was advanced to campaign-south grand general.

entries.zh: 梁元帝承制授超猛將軍、交州刺史資，領新淦縣令，封巴山縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting under the provisional mandate, made him supernumerary fierce general with credentials as inspector of Jiaozhou, gave him Xingan as magistrate, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Bashan with three hundred households.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang under the provisional mandate appointed him supernumerary fierce general, credentials as Inspector of Jiaozhou, concurrent magistrate of Xingan, enfeoffed as Viscount of Bashan county with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 承聖三年，除明威將軍、游騎將軍，進爵為侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year 3 (554) he was made bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, raised to marquis with five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Chengsheng he was appointed bright-prestige general and roaming-cavalry general, advanced in rank to marquis with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，除左驍騎將軍。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, he was made left nimble-cavalry general.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, he was made left nimble-cavalry general.

entries.zh: 敬帝即位，改封新建縣侯，邑如前。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne his title was changed to Marquis of Xinjian, with the same fief as before.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Xinjian county, fief as before.

entries.zh: 量少善自居處，偉姿容，有幹略，便弓馬。
entries.en: In youth Liang carried himself well, had a commanding presence, showed judgment and resolve, and fought well from horseback.
entries.literal: In youth Liang was good at deporting himself, of imposing looks, possessed of capacity and strategy, skilled at bow and horse.

entries.zh: 梁元帝為荊州刺史，文成分量人馬，令往事焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jingzhou, Wencheng gave Liang troops and horses and sent him to serve there.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was Inspector of Jingzhou, Wencheng assigned Liang men and horses and ordered him to serve there.

entries.zh: 起家湘東王國常侍，兼西中郎府中兵參軍。
entries.en: He entered service as regular attendant of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom and middle-arms adjutant in the western center-general's office.
entries.literal: He began his career as regular attendant of the Kingdom of the Prince of Xiangdong, and concurrently middle-arms adjutant in the Western Center-General's office.

entries.zh: 累遷府佐、常兼中兵、直兵者十餘載，兵甲士卒，盛於府中。
entries.en: He rose through staff posts, often holding middle-arms and direct-arms duties together for more than ten years, until armored soldiers filled the prince's household.
entries.literal: He rose through the ranks to staff offices, often holding concurrently middle-arms and direct-arms posts for more than ten years; armor-bearing soldiers filled the prince's establishment.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，進號安南將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Faqu's title was raised to secure-south general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, his designation was advanced to pacify-south general.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，周迪反，法抃率兵會都督吳明徹，討迪於工塘。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 2 (561) Zhou Di rebelled. Faqu led his men to join area commander Wu Mingche and fought Di at Gongtang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, Zhou Di rebelled; Faqu led troops to join area commander Wu Mingche and campaigned against Di at Gongtang.

entries.zh: 迪平，法抃功居多。
entries.en: When Di fell, Faqu's merit stood first.
entries.literal: When Di was pacified, Faqu's merit was foremost.

entries.zh: 徵為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南徐州諸軍事、鎮北大將軍、南徐州刺史，儀同、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: He was summoned as credential-holder and scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of South Xuzhou armies, secure-the-north grand general, and inspector of South Xuzhou, with grand-master rank and pipes and drums unchanged.
entries.literal: He was summoned as credential-holder, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, area commander of South Xuzhou military affairs, secure-the-north grand general, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, grand-master status and pipes and drums as before.

entries.zh: 未拜，尋又改授都督江吳二州諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: Before he could take office he was reassigned to command the armies of Jiang and Wu, made secure-the-south grand general, and named inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment, soon he was reassigned as area commander of Jiang and Wu commanderies' military affairs, secure-the-south grand general, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 六年，徵為中衛大將軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was recalled as central guard grand general.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as central guard grand general.

entries.zh: 王琳平後，頻請入朝，天嘉五年，徵為中撫大將軍，[2]常侍、儀同、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: After Wang Lin fell he repeatedly asked to come to court. In Tianjia year 5 (564) he was recalled as central pacification grand general, [2] with regular attendant rank, grand-master status, and pipes and drums unchanged.
entries.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified he repeatedly requested to come to court; in the fifth year of Tianjia he was summoned as central pacification grand general, regular attendant, grand-master status, and pipes and drums as before.

entries.zh: 量所部將帥，多戀本土，[3]並欲逃入山谷，不願入朝。
entries.en: Most of the generals under Liang longed for home. [3] They meant to flee into the hills rather than go to court.
entries.literal: The generals under Liang's command for the most part longed for their native lands, and all wished to flee into mountain valleys and would not come to court.

entries.zh: 世祖使湘州刺史華皎征衡州界黃洞，且以兵迎量。
entries.en: Emperor Wen sent Hua Jiao, inspector of Xiangzhou, to campaign against the Huang caves on Hengzhou's border and also to bring troops to escort Liang in.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen sent Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao to campaign against the Huang cave-folk on the borders of Hengzhou and also to bring troops to receive Liang.

entries.zh: 天康元年，至都，以在道淹留，為有司所奏，免儀同，餘並如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he reached the capital. Because he had lingered on the road the authorities impeached him and stripped his grand-master rank, leaving the rest unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he reached the capital; because of delay on the road he was impeached by the relevant office, stripped of grand-master status, the rest as before.

entries.zh: 光大元年，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda (567) he was given a set of pipes and drums.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda one set of pipes and drums was granted.

entries.zh: 華皎構逆，以量為使持節、征南大將軍、西討大都督，總率大艦，自郢州樊浦拒之。
entries.en: When Hua Jiao rebelled, Liang was made credential-holder, campaign-south grand general, and grand commander of the western expedition, leading great ships from Ezhou's Fan Ford against him.
entries.literal: Hua Jiao plotted treason; Liang was made credential-holder, campaign-south grand general, and grand commander of the western expedition, in overall command of great ships from Ezhou's Fan Ford to resist him.

entries.zh: 皎平，并降周將長胡公拓跋定等。
entries.en: When Jiao fell he also forced the surrender of the Zhou general Senior Duke Tuoba Ding and his men.
entries.literal: When Jiao was pacified, he also reduced Zhou general the Senior Duke Tuoba Ding and others.

entries.zh: 以功授侍中、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司，進封醴陵縣公，增邑一千戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made palace attendant, central army grand general, and grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon, and raised to Duke of Liling with one thousand households added to his fief.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed palace attendant, central army grand general, and grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Liling county with fief increased by one thousand households.

entries.zh: 未拜，出為使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史，侍中、儀同、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: Before he could take office he went out as credential-holder, commander of South Xuzhou armies, secure-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou, retaining palace attendant rank, grand-master status, and pipes and drums.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment he went out as credential-holder, area commander of South Xuzhou military affairs, secure-the-north general, and Inspector of South Xuzhou; palace attendant, grand-master status, and pipes and drums as before.

entries.zh: 昭達性倜儻，輕財尚氣。
entries.en: Zhaoda was free-spirited by nature, cared little for money, and prized boldness.
entries.literal: Zhaoda by nature was unconventional, lightly valued wealth and prized bold spirit.

entries.zh: 少時，嘗遇相者，謂昭達曰：「卿容貌甚善，須小虧損，則當富貴。」
entries.en: In youth he met a physiognomist who told him, "Your face is too perfect. You need a small flaw, and then you will rise to wealth and rank."
entries.literal: In youth he once met a physiognomist who said to Zhaoda: "Your countenance is very fine; you need but a small blemish, and then you will be rich and noble."

entries.zh: 梁大同中，昭達為東宮直後，因醉墜馬，鬢角小傷，昭達喜之，相者曰「未也」。
entries.en: Under Liang's Datong reign he was direct attendant to the Eastern Palace. Drunk, he fell from his horse and cut his temple. Zhaoda was pleased. The physiognomist said, "Not yet."
entries.literal: In the Datong era of Liang, Zhaoda was direct attendant behind the Eastern Palace; drunk he fell from a horse and received a small wound at the temple; Zhaoda was pleased at this; the physiognomist said, "Not yet."

entries.zh: 及侯景之亂，昭達率募鄉人援臺城，為流矢所中，眇其一目，相者見之，曰：「卿相善矣，不久當貴。」
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he led home recruits to relieve the Terrace City. A stray arrow blinded one eye. The physiognomist saw him and said, "Now your fate is set. You will soon be ennobled."
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhaoda led recruits from his native place to relieve the Terrace City; he was struck by a stray arrow and lost sight in one eye; the physiognomist saw him and said, "Your physiognomy is now excellent; before long you will be ennobled."

entries.zh: 京城陷，昭達還鄉里，與世祖遊，因結君臣之分。
entries.en: When the capital fell he went home and fell in with Emperor Wen, and from that day they were lord and minister.
entries.literal: When the capital fell Zhaoda returned to his native place and associated with Emperor Wen; thereby they formed the distinction of lord and minister.

entries.zh: 侯景平，世祖為吳興太守，昭達杖策來謁世祖。
entries.en: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wuxing. Zhaoda came leaning on his staff to pay his respects.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing; Zhaoda came leaning on his staff to call on Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 世祖見之大喜，因委以將帥，恩寵優渥，超於儕等。
entries.en: Emperor Wen was delighted and put him in command of troops, favoring him above his peers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen saw him he was greatly pleased and therefore entrusted him with command of troops, favor and grace surpassing his peers.

entries.zh: 及高祖討王僧辯，令世祖還長城招聚兵眾，以備杜龕，頻使昭達往京口，稟承計畫。
entries.en: When the Founder moved against Wang Sengbian he sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to raise men and stores against Du Kan and repeatedly sent Zhaoda to Jingkou to carry his orders.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Wang Sengbian he ordered Emperor Wen to return to Changcheng to gather troops and supplies against Du Kan, and repeatedly sent Zhaoda to Jingkou to receive and carry out plans.

entries.zh: 僧辯誅後，龕遣其將杜泰來攻長城，世祖拒之，命昭達總知城內兵事。
entries.en: After Sengbian was killed, Kan sent Du Tai against Changcheng. Emperor Wen held the city and put Zhaoda in charge of the garrison.
