entries.literal: After Sengbian was executed Kan sent his general Du Tai to attack Changcheng; Emperor Wen resisted him and ordered Zhaoda to take overall charge of troops within the city.

entries.zh: 及杜泰退走，因從世祖東進，軍吳興，以討杜龕。
entries.en: When Du Tai withdrew, he followed Emperor Wen east. The army camped at Wuxing to attack Du Kan.
entries.literal: When Du Tai withdrew, he followed Emperor Wen eastward; the army was at Wuxing to campaign against Du Kan.

entries.zh: 龕平，又從世祖東討張彪於會稽，克之。
entries.en: When Kan fell he marched east again with Emperor Wen against Zhang Biao at Kuaiji and took the city.
entries.literal: When Kan was pacified he again followed Emperor Wen east to campaign against Zhang Biao at Kuaiji and captured it.

entries.zh: 累功除明威將軍、定州刺史。
entries.en: For accumulated merit he was made bright-prestige general and inspector of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: For accumulated merit he was appointed bright-prestige general and Inspector of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 是時留異擁據東陽，私署守宰，高祖患之，乃使昭達為長山縣令，居其心腹。
entries.en: At that time Liu Yi held Dongyang, appointing his own officials; the Founder, troubled by this, made Zhaoda magistrate of Changshan county to plant him in Yi's heartland.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Yi held Dongyang in his grip, privately appointing prefectural and county officials; the Founder was troubled by it and therefore made Zhaoda magistrate of Changshan county, placing him in Yi's heartland.

entries.zh: 永定二年，除武康令。
entries.en: In Yongding year two he was made magistrate of Wukang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was made magistrate of Wukang.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，除員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Zhaoda was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, [Zhaoda] was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，追論長城之功，封欣樂縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year one, for merit at Changcheng he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinle county with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, for merit at the defense of Changcheng he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinle county, fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 初，世祖嘗夢昭達升於台鉉，及旦，以夢告之。
entries.en: Earlier Emperor Wen had dreamed that Zhaoda climbed a platform beam; at dawn he told him the dream.
entries.literal: Earlier Emperor Wen had once dreamed that Zhaoda ascended a platform beam; at dawn he told him the dream.

entries.zh: 至是侍醼，世祖顧昭達曰：「卿憶夢不？
entries.en: At a banquet Emperor Wen turned to Zhaoda and said, "Do you remember the dream?
entries.literal: On this occasion, while attending a banquet, Emperor Wen turned to Zhaoda and said, "Do you remember the dream?

entries.zh: 何以償夢？」
entries.en: How will you repay it?"
entries.literal: How will you repay the dream?"

entries.zh: 昭達對曰：「當效犬馬之用，以盡臣節，自餘無以奉償。」
entries.en: Zhaoda answered, "I shall serve like a dog or horse and fulfill my duty as a minister; beyond that I have nothing to offer in repayment."
entries.literal: Zhaoda replied, "I shall exert myself like a dog or horse to fulfill my minister's duty; beyond that I have nothing with which to repay you."

entries.zh: 尋又出為使持節、都督江郢吳三州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、江州刺史，常侍、儀同、鼓吹如故。
entries.en: Soon he was sent out again as bearer of the staff, commander of armies in Jiang, E, and Wu prefectures, general who garrisons the south, and inspector of Jiang prefecture, with his regular attendant rank, mansion equal to the three dukes, and martial music unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he was again sent out as bearer of the staff, area commander over military affairs in the three prefectures of Jiang, E, and Wu, general who garrisons the south, and inspector of Jiang prefecture; his regular attendant status, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and martial music were unchanged.

entries.zh: 周迪據臨川反，詔令昭達便道征之。
entries.en: Zhou Di rebelled in Linchuan; an edict sent Zhaoda against him by the direct route.
entries.literal: Zhou Di held Linchuan in rebellion; an edict ordered Zhaoda to campaign against him by convenient route.

entries.zh: 及迪敗走，徵為護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部，改封邵武縣侯，增邑并前二千戶，常侍如故。
entries.en: When Di was beaten and fled, Zhaoda was recalled as protector general and given a troupe of martial music; he was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Shaowu county with two thousand households in all, keeping his regular attendant rank.
entries.literal: When Di was defeated and fled, [Zhaoda] was summoned as protector general and granted a troupe of martial music; he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Shaowu county, his fief increased to two thousand households in all; his regular attendant status was unchanged.

entries.zh: 四年，陳寶應納周迪，復共寇臨川，又以昭達為都督討迪。
entries.en: In year four Chen Baoying sheltered Zhou Di and they raided Linchuan again; Zhaoda was again made area commander against Di.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Chen Baoying took Zhou Di in and together they raided Linchuan again; Zhaoda was again made area commander to campaign against Di.

entries.zh: 至東興嶺，而迪又退走。
entries.en: At Dongxing Ridge, Di again withdrew and fled.
entries.literal: When he reached Dongxing Ridge, Di again withdrew and fled.

entries.zh: 昭達仍踰嶺，頓于建安，以討陳寶應。
entries.en: Zhaoda then crossed the mountains, camped at Jian'an, and marched against Chen Baoying.
entries.literal: Zhaoda then crossed the ranges, halted at Jian'an, and campaigned against Chen Baoying.

entries.zh: 寶應據建安、晉安二郡之界，水陸為柵，以拒官軍。
entries.en: Baoying held the border of Jian'an and Jin'an commanderies with stockades on land and water against the imperial army.
entries.literal: Baoying held the border between Jian'an and Jin'an commanderies, building stockades on land and water to resist the imperial army.

entries.zh: 昭達與戰不利，因據其上流，命軍士伐木帶枝葉為筏，施拍於其上，綴以大索，相次列營，夾于兩岸。
entries.en: Zhaoda fought without success, then held the upper river, had his men cut trees with branches for rafts, mounted pounders on them, linked them with great ropes, and lined camps along both banks.
entries.literal: Zhaoda fought without success; he therefore held the upper reaches of the river, ordered the soldiers to cut trees with branches and leaves to make rafts, mounted pounders on them, linked them with great ropes, and set camps in succession lining both banks.

entries.zh: 寶應數挑戰，昭達按甲不動。
entries.en: Baoying repeatedly challenged him to battle; Zhaoda held his troops still.
entries.literal: Baoying repeatedly offered battle; Zhaoda kept his armor on and did not move.

entries.zh: 俄而暴雨，江水大長，昭達放筏衝突寶應水柵，水柵盡破。
entries.en: Soon a violent storm swelled the river; Zhaoda sent the rafts to smash Baoying's water stockades and broke them all.
entries.literal: Before long a violent rainstorm came; the river rose greatly; Zhaoda released the rafts to crash into Baoying's water stockades, and the water stockades were all broken.

entries.zh: 又出兵攻其步軍。
entries.en: He also sent troops to attack Baoying's infantry.
entries.literal: He also sent troops out to attack Baoying's infantry.

entries.zh: 方大合戰，會世祖遣余孝頃出自海道。
entries.en: As the great battle was joining, Emperor Wen sent Yu Xiaoqing by sea.
entries.literal: Just as the great battle was joining, Emperor Wen sent Yu Xiaoqing out by the sea route.

entries.zh: 適至，因并力乘之，寶應大潰，遂克定閩中，盡擒留異、寶應等。
entries.en: He arrived in time; together they pressed the attack; Baoying was routed; they pacified Minzhong and seized Liu Yi, Baoying, and the rest.
entries.literal: He arrived at the right moment; they therefore joined forces and pressed the attack; Baoying was routed in great disorder; they thereupon pacified Minzhong, capturing Liu Yi, Baoying, and the rest.

entries.zh: 以功授鎮前將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: For merit he was made general who guards the van and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed general who guards the van and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes.

entries.zh: 昭達性嚴刻，每奉命出征，必晝夜倍道；
entries.en: Zhaoda was stern and harsh; whenever he took the field he marched day and night by forced stages;
entries.literal: Zhaoda's nature was stern and harsh; whenever he received orders to campaign he always traveled day and night by double stages;

entries.zh: 然有所克捷，必推功將帥，廚膳飲食，並同於群下，將士亦以此附之。
entries.en: yet whenever he won he pushed the credit to his generals, ate and drank as his men did, and the troops for that reason gave him their loyalty.
entries.literal: yet whenever he won a victory he always pushed the merit onto his generals; kitchen fare and drink were the same as those of the rank and file, and the officers and soldiers for this reason attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 每飲會，必盛設女伎雜樂，備盡羌胡之聲，音律姿容，並一時之妙，雖臨對寇敵，旗鼓相望，弗之廢也。
entries.en: At every feast he set out female performers and every sort of music, Qiang and Hu sounds, melody and bearing the finest of the age; even with enemy banners and drums in sight he would not give it up.
entries.literal: At every drinking gathering he always set out female performers and mixed music to the full, with every sound of the Qiang and Hu, melody and bearing all the finest of the age; even when facing the enemy with banners and drums confronting one another, he did not abandon it.

entries.zh: 四年，配享世祖廟庭。
entries.en: In year four he was granted shared offerings in Emperor Wen's temple.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was granted shared offerings in Emperor Wen's temple hall.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：黃法抃、淳于量值梁末喪亂，劉、項未分，其有辯明暗見是非者蓋鮮，二公達向背之理，位至鼎司，亦其智也。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Huang Faqu and Chunyu Liang lived through the chaos at the end of Liang, when the realm had not yet chosen between rival founders; men who could tell right from wrong were few. Both understood which side to take and rose to the highest offices—that was their wisdom.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Huang Faqu and Chunyu Liang, meeting the disorders at the end of Liang when Liu and Xiang had not yet been decided, were among the very few who could distinguish light from dark and see right from wrong; the two lords understood the principle of which side to follow and rose to the chief minister's tripod—this too was their wisdom.

entries.zh: 昭達與世祖鄉壤惟舊，義等鄧、蕭，世祖纂曆，委任隆重，至於戰勝攻取，累平寇難，斯亦良臣良將，一代之吳、耿矣。
entries.en: Zhaoda and Emperor Wen were old friends from the same country; their bond was like that of Deng Yu and Xiao He. When Wen took the throne he gave Zhaoda great trust; in battle and siege he again and again crushed rebellion—a worthy minister and general, a Wu Han and Geng Yan for his age.
entries.literal: Zhaoda and Emperor Wen were old friends from the same native place; their bond was like that of Deng and Xiao; when Emperor Wen took the succession he entrusted Zhaoda with weighty responsibility; as for victory in battle and success in attack, repeatedly pacifying rebellions—he too was a worthy minister and worthy general, a Wu and Geng of his generation.

entries.zh: 徵為中撫大將軍 「中撫大將軍」
entries.en: On "summoned as grand general who pacifies the center":
entries.literal: Summoned as grand general who pacifies the center—"grand general who pacifies the center"

entries.zh: 〈世祖紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉

entries.zh: 作「中撫軍大將軍」，《南史》亦作「中撫軍大將軍」。
entries.en: reads "grand general who pacifies the army," and the History of the Southern Dynasties also reads "grand general who pacifies the army."
entries.literal: reads "grand general who pacifies the army," and the History of the Southern Dynasties also reads "grand general who pacifies the army."

entries.zh: 按「中撫」各書或作「中撫軍」。
entries.en: Note: in various books "pacifies the center" is sometimes written "pacifies the army."
entries.literal: Comment: in various books "pacifies the center" is sometimes written "pacifies the army."

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，遷侍中、征南將軍，改封邵陵郡公。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhaoda became palace attendant and general who campaigns south and was re-enfeoffed as duke of Shaoling commandery.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, [Zhaoda] was transferred to palace attendant and general who campaigns south, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shaoling commandery.

entries.zh: 華皎之反也，其移書文檄，並假以昭達為辭，又頻遣使招之，昭達盡執其使，送于京師。
entries.en: When Hua Jiao rebelled, his manifestos all invoked Zhaoda's name, and he repeatedly sent envoys to win him over; Zhaoda seized every envoy and sent them to the capital.
entries.literal: When Hua Jiao rebelled, his letters and proclamations all borrowed Zhaoda's name as their pretext, and he repeatedly sent envoys to win him over; Zhaoda seized all his envoys and sent them to the capital.

entries.zh: 皎平，進號征南大將軍，增邑并前二千五百戶。
entries.en: When Jiao was suppressed, Zhaoda was promoted to grand general who campaigns south, with his fief raised to two thousand five hundred households in all.
entries.literal: When Jiao was pacified, [Zhaoda's] title was advanced to grand general who campaigns south, and his fief was increased to two thousand five hundred households in all.

entries.zh: 秩滿，徵為中撫大將軍，侍中、儀同、鼓吹如故。
entries.en: When his term expired he was recalled as grand general who pacifies the center, keeping his palace attendant rank, mansion equal to the three dukes, and martial music.
entries.literal: When his term expired, he was summoned as grand general who pacifies the center; his palace attendant status, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and martial music were unchanged.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，進號車騎大將軍，以還朝遲留，為有司所劾，降號車騎將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Zhaoda was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry; because he lingered on the road, the responsible offices impeached him and his title was reduced to general of chariots and cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Zhaoda's] title was advanced to grand general of chariots and cavalry; because his return to court was delayed, the responsible offices impeached him, and his title was reduced to general of chariots and cavalry.

entries.zh: 太建二年，率師征蕭巋于江陵。
entries.en: In Taijian year two he led an army against Xiao Kui at Jiangling.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taijian he led an army to campaign against Xiao Kui at Jiangling.

entries.zh: 時蕭巋與周軍大蓄舟艦於青泥中，昭達分遣偏將錢道戢、程文季等，乘輕舟襲之，焚其舟艦。
entries.en: Kui and the Northern Zhou forces had massed many ships in the Qingni channel; Zhaoda detached Qian Daozhi, Cheng Wenji, and others in light craft to strike and burn the fleet.
entries.literal: At that time Kui and the Zhou army had stored many ships in great numbers in the Qingni channel; Zhaoda separately sent the subordinate generals Qian Daozhi, Cheng Wenji, and others in light boats to strike them and burn the ships.

entries.zh: 周兵又於峽下南岸築壘，[6]名曰安蜀城，於江上橫引大索，編𥯤為橋，[7]以度軍糧。
entries.en: The Zhou troops also built a fort on the south bank below the gorge [6] called Anshu City, stretched a great rope across the river, and wove rushes into a bridge [7] to move army grain.
entries.literal: The Zhou troops also built a fort on the south bank below the gorge; it was named Anshu City; they stretched a great rope across the river and wove rushes into a bridge; to convey army grain.

entries.zh: 昭達乃命軍士為長戟，施於樓船之上，仰割其索，索斷糧絕，因縱兵以攻其城，降之。
entries.en: Zhaoda had his men make long halberds on tower ships and cut the rope from below; when it parted the grain supply failed; he then attacked the fort and it surrendered.
entries.literal: Zhaoda thereupon ordered the soldiers to make long halberds, mount them on tower ships, and cut the rope from below; when the rope was severed the grain supply was cut off; he then sent the troops out to attack the fort and it surrendered.

entries.zh: 齊遣其歷陽王步騎五萬來援 按
entries.en: On "Qi sent its Prince of Liyang with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve them":
entries.literal: Qi sent its Prince of Liyang with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve them—comment:

entries.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

entries.zh: 云「齊遣兵十萬援歷陽」，此云「五萬」，與紀異。
entries.en: reads "Qi sent one hundred thousand troops to relieve Liyang," while this reads fifty thousand, differing from the annals.
entries.literal: says "Qi sent one hundred thousand troops to relieve Liyang," while this says "fifty thousand," differing from the annals.

entries.zh: 徵為中護大將軍 「中護大將軍」
entries.en: On "summoned as grand general who guards the center":
entries.literal: Summoned as grand general who guards the center—"grand general who guards the center"

entries.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉
entries.en: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
entries.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

entries.zh: 太建五年、六年並作「中權大將軍」，徐陵傳作「中權將軍」。
entries.en: in Taijian years five and six both read "grand general of the central guard," and the biography of Xu Ling reads "general of the central guard."
entries.literal: in Taijian years five and six both read "grand general of the central guard," and the biography of Xu Ling reads "general of the central guard."

entries.zh: 陳書卷十一
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 11
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 11

entries.zh: 胡穎 徐度 子敬成 杜稜 沈恪
entries.en: Hu Ying; Xu Du; son Jingcheng; Du Leng; Shen Ke
entries.literal: Hu Ying; Xu Du; son Jingcheng; Du Leng; Shen Ke

entries.zh: 胡穎字方秀，吳興東遷人也。
entries.en: Hu Ying, styled Fangxiu, came from Dongqian in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Hu Ying, styled Fangxiu, was a native of Dongqian in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 其先寓居吳興，土斷為民。
entries.en: His family had long lived in Wuxing as sojourners; after the register was broken off they were reckoned natives of the place.
entries.literal: His forebears had sojourned in Wuxing; when the native register was discontinued they were accounted local people.

entries.zh: 穎偉姿容，性寬厚。
entries.en: Ying was tall and striking, with an open, generous nature.
entries.literal: Ying had a grand bearing and handsome looks, and a generous disposition.

entries.zh: 梁世仕至武陵國侍郎，東宮直前。
entries.en: Under Liang he served as vice-minister in the state of Wuling and direct attendant before the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Under Liang he rose to Vice-Minister in the state of Wuling and Direct Attendant Before the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 出番禺，征討俚洞，廣州西江督護高祖在廣州，穎仍自結高祖，高祖與其同郡，接遇甚隆。
entries.en: Posted from Panyu against the Li caves, he held the West River defense command at Guangzhou. When the Founder was there, Ying sought him out on his own. They shared a home commandery, and the Founder treated him with exceptional warmth.
entries.literal: He went out from Panyu to campaign against the Li cave settlements. As West River defense commander of Guangzhou, when the Founder was at Guangzhou Ying attached himself to him of his own accord; the Founder was from the same commandery and received him with great favor.

entries.zh: 及南征交趾，穎從行役，餘諸將帥皆出其下。
entries.en: On the march to Jiaozhi he went with the army, and the other commanders stood beneath him in rank.
entries.literal: When the southern campaign against Jiaozhi was launched, Ying followed on campaign; the other generals all ranked below him.

entries.zh: 及平李賁，高祖旋師，穎隸在西江，出兵多以穎留守。
entries.en: After Li Ben fell the Founder turned homeward. Ying stayed on the West River, and in most campaigns he was left behind to guard the base.
entries.literal: When Li Ben was pacified the Founder withdrew his army; Ying remained subordinate on the West River, and whenever troops marched out Ying was often left to hold the rear.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，兼左衛將軍，餘如故。
entries.en: When the Founder accepted the abdication, Ying also became left guard general, retaining his other posts.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Ying concurrently became Left Guard General; his other posts remained as before.

entries.zh: 永定三年，隨侯安都征王琳，於宮亭破賊帥常眾愛等。
entries.en: In Yongding year 3, he followed Hou Andu against Wang Lin and defeated the rebel commanders Chang Zhongai and others at Gongting.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongding, he followed Hou Andu in campaigning against Wang Lin and defeated the rebel commanders Chang Zhongai and others at Gongting.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，除侍中、都督吳州諸軍事、宣惠將軍、吳州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ying was made palace attendant, commander of Wuzhou military affairs, general who spreads grace, and inspector of Wuzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ying was appointed Palace Attendant, Area Commander over military affairs in Wuzhou, General Who Spreads Grace, and Inspector of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 不行，尋為義興太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He did not go to the post and was soon made administrator of Yixing, keeping his general rank.
entries.literal: He did not take up the post, and soon became Administrator of Yixing, retaining his generalship as before.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，除散騎常侍、吳興太守。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 其年六月卒，時年五十四。
entries.en: He died that sixth month, aged fifty-four.
entries.literal: He died in the sixth month of that year, aged fifty-four.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、中護軍，諡曰壯。
entries.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant and central protector of the army and given the posthumous name Valiant.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Palace Attendant and Central Protector of the Army, with the posthumous name Valiant.

entries.zh: 二年，配享高祖廟庭。
entries.en: In the second year, he was given a place in the Founder's temple.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was enshrined in the Founder's temple court.

entries.zh: 子六同嗣。
entries.en: His son Liutong inherited the line.
entries.literal: His son Liutong succeeded.

entries.zh: 梁承聖初，元帝授穎假節、鐵騎將軍、羅州刺史，封漢陽縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: At the beginning of Liang Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan gave Ying acting credentials, made him iron cavalry general and inspector of Luo, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hanyang with five hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Liang Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan granted Ying acting credentials, made him Iron Cavalry General and Inspector of Luo, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Hanyang county with five hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋除豫章內史，隨高祖鎮京口。
entries.en: Soon he became interior minister of Yuzhang and followed the Founder to Jingkou.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Interior Minister of Yuzhang and followed the Founder to garrison Jingkou.

entries.zh: 齊遣郭元建出關，都督侯瑱率師禦之。
entries.en: Qi sent Guo Yuanjian through the pass; Hou Tian led an army to meet him.
entries.literal: Qi sent Guo Yuanjian out through the pass, and Area Commander Hou Tian led troops to resist him.

entries.zh: 高祖選府內驍勇三千人配穎，令隨瑱，於東關大破之（元建）。[1]
entries.en: The Founder picked three thousand brave men from his staff troops and assigned them to Ying under Tian. At Dongguan they routed Yuanjian.
entries.literal: The Founder selected three thousand brave men from his headquarters and assigned them to Ying, ordering him to follow Tian; at Dongguan they greatly defeated him, Yuanjian.

entries.zh: 三年，高祖圍廣陵，齊人東方光據宿預請降，[2]以穎為五原太守，隨杜僧明援光，不克，退還，除曲阿令。
entries.en: In the third year, the Founder besieged Guangling. Dongfang Guang of Qi held Suyu and asked to surrender; Ying was made administrator of Wuyuan and sent with Du Sengming to aid him. They failed, withdrew, and Ying was made magistrate of Qu'e.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Founder besieged Guangling. The Qi man Dongfang Guang held Suyu and asked to surrender; Ying was made Administrator of Wuyuan and followed Du Sengming to aid Guang, but they could not prevail, withdrew, and he was made Magistrate of Qu'e.

entries.zh: 尋領馬軍，從高祖襲王僧辯。
entries.en: Soon he took command of cavalry and followed the Founder against Wang Sengbian.
entries.literal: Soon he commanded cavalry and followed the Founder in the attack on Wang Sengbian.

entries.zh: 又隨周文育於吳興討杜龕。
entries.en: He also followed Zhou Wenyu against Du Kan at Wuxing.
entries.literal: He also followed Zhou Wenyu in campaigning against Du Kan at Wuxing.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，除假節、都督南豫州諸軍事、輕車將軍、南豫州刺史。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 1, he received acting credentials and was made commander of South Yuzhou military affairs, light chariot general, and inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai, he was appointed acting with credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in South Yuzhou, Light Chariot General, and Inspector of South Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 太平元年，除持節、散騎常侍、仁威將軍。
entries.en: In Taiping year 1, he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and benevolent-power general.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, and Benevolent-Power General.

entries.zh: 尋兼丹陽尹。
entries.en: Soon he also served as intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖克元景仲，仍渡嶺援臺，平蔡路養、李遷仕，穎皆有功。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder took Yuan Jingzhong, crossed the mountains to relieve the capital, and crushed Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi. Ying earned merit in every fight.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder captured Yuan Jingzhong, then crossed the ranges to relieve the Terrace City, and pacified Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi; Ying had merit in all of this.

entries.zh: 歷平固、遂興二縣令。
entries.en: He served in turn as magistrate of Pinggu and Suixing.
entries.literal: He served successively as magistrate of the two counties of Pinggu and Suixing.

entries.zh: 高祖進軍頓西昌，以穎為巴丘縣令，鎮大皋，督糧運。
entries.en: When the Founder marched and camped at Xichang, he made Ying magistrate of Baqiu, posted him at Dago, and put him in charge of grain convoys.
entries.literal: When the Founder advanced his army and halted at Xichang, he made Ying magistrate of Baqiu, garrisoned Dago, and supervised grain transport.

entries.zh: 下至豫章，以穎監豫章郡。
entries.en: Moving downriver to Yuzhang, he appointed Ying overseer of the commandery.
entries.literal: Descending to Yuzhang, he made Ying overseer of Yuzhang commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖率眾與王僧辯會於白茅灣，同討侯景，以穎知留府事。
entries.en: The Founder took his army to Baimao Bay to join Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing and left Ying to manage headquarters.
entries.literal: The Founder led his host to meet Wang Sengbian at Baimao Bay to campaign jointly against Hou Jing, and put Ying in charge of affairs left at headquarters.

entries.zh: 穎弟鑠，亦隨穎將軍。
entries.en: Ying's younger brother Shuo followed him into the ranks as a general.
entries.literal: Ying's younger brother Shuo also followed Ying as a general.

entries.zh: 穎卒，鑠統其眾。
entries.en: When Ying died, Shuo inherited his command.
entries.literal: When Ying died, Shuo took command of his troops.

entries.zh: 歷東海、豫章二郡守，遷員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He governed Donghai and Yuzhang in turn, then rose to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: He served successively as administrator of the two commanderies of Donghai and Yuzhang, and was promoted to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 隨章昭達南平歐陽紇，[3]為廣州東江督護。
entries.en: He marched south with Zhang Zhaoda to crush Ouyang He [3] and was made East River defense commander of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: He followed Zhang Zhaoda in the southern pacification of Ouyang He, and was made East River defense commander of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 還預北伐，除雄信將軍、歷陽太守。
entries.en: Back from the south he joined the northern campaign and was appointed trustworthy-faith general and administrator of Liyang.
entries.literal: Returning, he took part in the northern campaign and was made Trustworthy-Faith General and Administrator of Liyang.

entries.zh: 太建六年卒，贈桂州刺史。
entries.en: He died in Taijian year 6 (574) and was posthumously made inspector of Gui.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taijian he died; posthumously he was given Inspector of Gui.

entries.zh: 徐度字孝節，安陸人也。
entries.en: Xu Du, styled Xiaojie, came from Anlu.
entries.literal: Xu Du, styled Xiaojie, was a native of Anlu.

entries.zh: 世居京師。
entries.en: His family had lived in the capital for generations.
entries.literal: For generations his family dwelt in the capital.

entries.zh: 少倜儻，不拘小節。
entries.en: As a youth he was reckless and bold, careless of petty rules.
entries.literal: In youth he was bold and free, heedless of small proprieties.

entries.zh: 及長，姿貌瑰偉，嗜酒好博，恆使僮僕屠酤為事。
entries.en: Grown to manhood he was imposing in bearing, fond of wine and dice, and kept servants busy slaughtering and brewing for his table.
entries.literal: When grown, his looks were magnificent; he loved wine and gambling and constantly set his servants to butchering and brewing for his pleasure.

entries.zh: 梁始興內史蕭介之郡，度從之，將領士卒，征諸山洞，以驍勇聞。
entries.en: When Liang's interior minister of Shixing, Xiao Jie, took up his post, Du went with him, commanding men against the hill tribes, and became known for daring.
entries.literal: When Xiao Jie of Liang was interior minister of Shixing and went to his commandery, Du followed him, leading troops in campaigns against the mountain caves, and won a name for fierce courage.

entries.zh: 高祖征交趾，厚禮招之，度乃委質。
entries.en: On the Jiaozhi campaign the Founder courted him with rich gifts; Du at last pledged himself.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Jiaozhi he treated Du with generous courtesy to win him; Du then offered his allegiance.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，高祖克定廣州，平蔡路養，破李遷仕，計畫多出於度。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rising the Founder held Guangzhou, crushed Cai Luyang, and routed Li Qianshi. Du supplied much of the strategy.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder secured Guangzhou, pacified Cai Luyang, and broke Li Qianshi; much of the planning came from Du.

entries.zh: 兼統兵甲，每戰有功。
entries.en: He also commanded troops and arms and fought with merit in every engagement.
entries.literal: He also took overall command of armor and weapons; in every battle he had merit.

entries.zh: 歸至白茅灣，梁元帝授寧朔將軍、合州刺史。
entries.en: Back at Baimao Bay, Emperor Yuan of Liang made him pacifying-the-north general and inspector of He.
entries.literal: Returning to Baimao Bay, Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him Pacifying-the-North General and Inspector of He.

entries.zh: 侯景平後，追錄前後戰功，加通直散騎常侍，封廣德縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: Once Hou Jing fell, past and recent victories were tallied. He was raised to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde with five hundred households.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, his earlier and later battle achievements were entered in the record; he was promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was transferred to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮朱方，除信武將軍、蘭陵太守。
entries.en: When the Founder held Zhufang, Du was made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Lanling.
entries.literal: When the Founder garrisoned Zhufang, Du was appointed Trustworthy-Martial General and Administrator of Lanling.

entries.zh: 高祖遣衡陽獻王平荊州，度率所領從焉。
entries.en: The Founder sent Prince Xian of Hengyang to pacify Jingzhou, and Du went with him at the head of his troops.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Prince Xian of Hengyang to pacify Jingzhou, and Du led his own command in following him.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，閒行東歸。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, he slipped back east by hidden paths.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, he traveled secretly back east.

entries.zh: 高祖平王僧辯，度與侯安都為水軍。
entries.en: When the Founder struck Wang Sengbian, Du and Hou Andu commanded the river forces.
entries.literal: When the Founder pacified Wang Sengbian, Du and Hou Andu served as the naval force.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，高祖東討杜龕，奉敬帝幸京口，以度領宿衛，并知留府事。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 1, the Founder marched east against Du Kan and escorted Emperor Jing to Jingkou; Du was put over the palace guard and left in charge of headquarters affairs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai, when the Founder went east to campaign against Du Kan, he escorted Emperor Jing to Jingkou and had Du command the palace guard and manage affairs left at headquarters.

entries.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等來寇，高祖與敬帝還都。
entries.en: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others struck at the capital. The Founder and Emperor Jing came back to defend it.
entries.literal: Xu Siwei, Ren Yue, and others came to raid; the Founder and Emperor Jing returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 時賊已據石頭城，市鄽居民，並在南路，去臺遙遠，恐為賊所乘，乃使度將兵鎮于冶城寺，築壘以斷之。
entries.en: The rebels already held Shitou. Markets and towns on the southern road lay far from the palace, open to being overrun, so Du was sent with troops to Yecheng Temple to build a wall and block the approach.
entries.literal: At that time the rebels already held Shitou citadel; market towns and residents along the southern road lay far from the Terrace City, and there was fear they would be seized by the rebels; Du was therefore sent with troops to garrison Yecheng Temple and build a stockade to cut them off.

entries.zh: 賊悉眾來攻，不能克。
entries.en: The rebels threw their whole force against him and failed to break through.
entries.literal: The rebels mustered their full strength to attack but could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 高祖尋亦救之，大敗約等。
entries.en: The Founder soon arrived in relief and routed Ren Yue and his allies.
entries.literal: The Founder soon came to the rescue as well and inflicted a great defeat on Ren Yue and the others.

entries.zh: 明年，嗣徽等又引齊寇濟江，度隨眾軍破之於北郊壇。
entries.en: The next year Siwei again drew Qi troops across the Yangzi. Du marched with the main host and beat them at the North Suburbs altar.
entries.literal: The next year Siwei and the others again brought Northern Qi raiders across the river; Du followed the mass of armies and defeated them at the North Suburbs altar.

entries.zh: 以功除信威將軍、郢州刺史，兼領吳興太守。
entries.en: For merit he was made trustworthy-power general and inspector of Ying, and also administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: For merit he was made Trustworthy-Power General and Inspector of Ying, and concurrently Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 尋遷鎮右將軍、領軍將軍、徐州緣江諸軍事、[4]鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was soon made suppressing-the-right general, commandant of the guards, commander along the Yangzi frontier of Xuzhou, [4] suppressing-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou, with a full set of pipes and drums.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Suppressing-the-Right General, Commandant of the Guards, Commander of Military Affairs along the Yangzi bank of Xuzhou, Suppressing-the-North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, and was given one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，度預顧命，以甲仗五十人入殿省。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died, Du was named in the deathbed testament. Fifty armed guards were posted in the palace offices.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Du was named in the final testament; fifty men with arms and armor entered the palace offices.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，進位司空。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Du was promoted to minister of works.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Du was advanced to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 華皎據湘州反，引周兵下至沌口，與王師相持，乃加度使持節、車騎將軍，總督步軍，自安成郡由嶺路出于湘東，以襲湘州，盡獲其所留軍人家口以歸。
entries.en: Hua Jiao rebelled in Xiangzhou and drew Zhou armies to Chun Ford, where they locked with the imperial host. Du was given credentials as chariots-and-cavalry general and made commander of all foot troops. He marched from Ancheng over the ridges into eastern Xiang, raided Xiangzhou, and carried off every soldier's family Jiao had left there.
entries.literal: Hua Jiao held Xiangzhou in rebellion and brought Zhou troops down to Chun Ford, where they faced the royal army in stalemate; Du was then given credentials, made Chariots-and-Cavalry General, and put in overall command of the infantry. From Ancheng commandery he took the ridge route out into eastern Xiang to strike Xiangzhou and brought back all the army households and dependents Jiao had left behind.

entries.zh: 光大二年薨，時年六十。
entries.en: He died in Guangda year 2 (568), aged sixty.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangda he died, aged sixty.

entries.zh: 贈太尉，給班劍二十人，諡曰忠肅。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand commandant, granted twenty ritual swords, and given the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Commandant, twenty ritual swords, and the posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.

entries.zh: 太建四年，配享高祖廟庭。
entries.en: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was enshrined in the Founder's temple.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was given a place in the Founder's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子敬成嗣。
entries.en: His son Jingcheng inherited the line.
entries.literal: His son Jingcheng succeeded.

entries.zh: 周文育、侯安都等西討王琳，敗績，為琳所拘，乃以度為前軍都督，鎮于南陵。
entries.en: Zhou Wenyu, Hou Andu, and the others marched west against Wang Lin, were defeated, and were held by him. Du was therefore made vanguard commander and posted at Nanling.
entries.literal: When Zhou Wenyu, Hou Andu, and the others campaigned west against Wang Lin, they were defeated and detained by Lin, so Du was made Commander of the Vanguard Army and stationed at Nanling.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，遷侍中、中撫軍將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Du became palace attendant, central pacifying general, and holder of office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and his noble rank was advanced to duke.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Du was transferred to Palace Attendant, Central Pacifying General, and office holder with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and his title was advanced to duke.

entries.zh: 未拜，出為使持節、散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、吳郡太守。
entries.en: Before formal installation, he was sent out with credentials as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general who guards the east, and administrator of Wu.
entries.literal: Before he was formally installed, he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑千戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, one thousand households were added to his fief.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his fief was increased by one thousand households.

entries.zh: 以平王琳功，改封湘東郡公，邑四千戶。
entries.en: For helping pacify Wang Lin, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangdong commandery with four thousand households.
entries.literal: For his merit in pacifying Wang Lin, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangdong commandery with a fief of four thousand households.

entries.zh: 秩滿，為侍中、中軍將軍。
entries.en: At the end of his term, he became palace attendant and general of the central army.
entries.literal: When his term was complete, he became Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 出為使持節、都督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安新寧信安晉安建安九郡諸軍事、鎮東將軍、會稽太守。
entries.en: He was then sent out with credentials as commander of the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xīn'an, Xinning, Xìn'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, general who guards the east, and administrator of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in the nine commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xīn'an, Xinning, Xìn'an, Jin'an, and Jian'an, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 未行而太尉侯瑱薨于湘州，乃以度代瑱為都督湘沅武巴郢桂六州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: Before he could leave, Grand Commandant Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou. Du replaced him as commander of Xiang, Yuan, Wu, Ba, Ying, and Gui, general who guards the south, and inspector of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Before he departed, Grand Commandant Hou Tian died in Xiangzhou, so Du was sent in Tian's place as Area Commander over military affairs in the six provinces of Xiang, Yuan, Wu, Ba, Ying, and Gui, General Who Guards the South, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 秩滿，為侍中、中軍大將軍，儀同、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: At the end of his term, he became palace attendant and grand general of the central army, retaining his equal-ceremony honors and pipes and drums.
entries.literal: When his term was complete, he became Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army; his equal-ceremony rank and pipes and drums remained as before.

entries.zh: 杜稜字雄盛，吳郡錢塘人也。
entries.en: Du Leng, styled Xiongsheng, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Du Leng, styled Xiongsheng, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 世為縣大姓。
entries.en: For generations his clan was one of the county's great families.
entries.literal: For generations his clan was a great surname of the county.

entries.zh: 稜頗涉書傳，少落泊，不為當世所知。
entries.en: Leng had read widely, but in youth he drifted without notice.
entries.literal: Leng had dipped into books and records; in youth he was adrift and unknown to his age.

entries.zh: 遂遊嶺南，事梁廣州刺史新渝侯蕭映。
entries.en: He went south to Lingnan and entered the service of Liang's inspector of Guangzhou, the Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.
entries.literal: He then traveled to Lingnan and served Liang's Inspector of Guangzhou, the Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying.

entries.zh: 映卒，從高祖，恆典書記。
entries.en: When Ying died he followed the Founder and served constantly as his secretary.
entries.literal: When Ying died he followed the Founder and constantly kept the written records.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，命稜將領，平蔡路養、李遷仕皆有功。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was put in command. He helped crush Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi and won merit in both campaigns.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was ordered to take command; pacifying Cai Luyang and Li Qianshi, he had merit in both.

entries.zh: 軍至豫章，梁元帝承制授稜仁威將軍、石州刺史，上陌縣侯，邑八百戶。
entries.en: At Yuzhang, Emperor Yuan of Liang, exercising regency powers, made Leng benevolent-power general and inspector of Shi, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangmo with eight hundred households.
entries.literal: When the army reached Yuzhang, Emperor Yuan of Liang, acting on the regency commission, appointed Leng Benevolent-Power General and Inspector of Shi, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangmo county with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 三年，高祖崩，世祖在南皖。
entries.en: In the third year, the Founder died with Emperor Wen away at Southern Wan.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Founder died while Emperor Wen was at Southern Wan.

entries.zh: 時內無嫡嗣，外有彊敵，侯瑱、侯安都、徐度等並在軍中，朝廷宿將，唯稜在都，獨典禁兵，乃與蔡景歷等祕不發喪，奉迎世祖，事見景歷傳。
entries.en: There was no direct heir in the capital and strong enemies outside. Hou Tian, Hou Andu, Xu Du, and the rest were all in the field; of the court's old generals, only Leng was in the capital, commanding the guards. He and Cai Jingli kept the death secret and brought Emperor Wen in, as told in Jingli's biography.
entries.literal: At the time there was no legitimate heir inside the capital and powerful enemies outside; Hou Tian, Hou Andu, Xu Du, and the others were all with the armies, and among the court's veteran generals only Leng was in the capital, where he alone commanded the palace guards. He therefore joined Cai Jingli and the others in keeping the death secret and welcoming Emperor Wen; the matter is seen in Jingli's biography.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，遷領軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Leng became commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Leng was transferred to Commandant of the Guards.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，以預建立之功，改封永城縣侯，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, for helping establish the new reign, he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng with five hundred additional households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, for his merit in taking part in the enthronement, he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng county and his fief was increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 出為雲麾將軍，晉陵太守，加秩中二千石。
entries.en: He was sent out as cloud-standard general and administrator of Jinling, with middle two-thousand-dan rank.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Cloud-Standard General and Administrator of Jinling, with his salary raised to middle two thousand dan.

entries.zh: 二年，徵為侍中、領軍將軍。
entries.en: In the second year, he was recalled as palace attendant and commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Commandant of the Guards.

entries.zh: 尋遷翊左將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: Soon he became general who assists the left and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Assists the Left and Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 侯景圍臺城，恪率所領入臺，隨例加右軍將軍。
entries.en: When Hou Jing besieged the capital, Ke brought his men inside the walls and, by precedent, was made right army general.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Ke led his command into the city and, by precedent, was promoted to Right Army General.

entries.zh: 賊起東西二土山以逼城，城內亦作土山以應之，恪為東土山主，晝夜拒戰。
entries.en: The rebels piled earthen mounts east and west against the walls; the defenders raised mounts of their own. Ke held the eastern mound and fought day and night.
entries.literal: The rebels raised eastern and western earthen hills to press the walls; within the city earthen hills were also built in answer; Ke was master of the eastern hill and fought off attacks day and night.

entries.zh: 以功封東興縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with five hundred households.
entries.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 京城陷，恪閒行歸鄉里。
entries.en: When the capital fell, Ke stole home by back roads.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, Ke slipped away by hidden paths and returned to his home district.

entries.zh: 高祖之討侯景，遣使報恪，乃於東起兵相應。
entries.en: The Founder sent word when he marched against Hou Jing; Ke raised men in the east to join him.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing he sent envoys to notify Ke; Ke then raised troops in the east in response.

entries.zh: 賊平，恪謁高祖於京口，即日授都軍副。
entries.en: After the rebels fell, Ke met the Founder at Jingkou and was named deputy commander of the capital army that same day.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Ke called on the Founder at Jingkou and that same day was appointed deputy commander of the capital army.

entries.zh: 尋為（君）府司馬。[8]
entries.en: Soon he was made marshal of the commander's office.
entries.literal: Soon he became marshal of the commander's office.

entries.zh: 及高祖謀討王僧辯，恪預其謀。
entries.en: When the Founder planned his move against Wang Sengbian, Ke was in the councils.
entries.literal: When the Founder planned to campaign against Wang Sengbian, Ke took part in the planning.

entries.zh: 時僧辯女婿杜龕鎮吳興，高祖乃使世祖還長城，立柵備龕，又使恪還武康，招集兵眾。
entries.en: Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan then held Wuxing. The Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to build defenses against him and sent Ke back to Wukang to raise men.
entries.literal: At the time Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan garrisoned Wuxing, so the Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to set up palisades against Kan, and also sent Ke back to Wukang to gather troops.

entries.zh: 及僧辯誅，龕果遣副將杜泰率眾襲世祖於長城。
entries.en: After Sengbian was killed, Kan sent his deputy Du Tai to attack Emperor Wen at Changcheng.
entries.literal: When Sengbian was killed, Kan indeed sent his deputy Du Tai to lead troops in attacking Emperor Wen at Changcheng.

entries.zh: 恪時已率兵士出縣誅龕黨與，高祖尋遣周文育來援長城，文育至，泰乃遁走。
entries.en: Ke had already marched out to kill Kan's partisans. The Founder sent Zhou Wenyu to reinforce Changcheng, and once Wenyu arrived, Tai fled.
entries.literal: Ke had already led soldiers out of the county to punish Kan's followers; the Founder soon sent Zhou Wenyu to reinforce Changcheng, and when Wenyu arrived, Tai fled.

entries.zh: 世祖仍與文育進軍出郡，恪軍亦至，屯于郡南。
entries.en: Emperor Wen and Wenyu advanced out of the commandery; Ke's army arrived as well and camped to the south.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen then advanced out of the commandery with Wenyu, and Ke's army also arrived and camped south of the commandery seat.

entries.zh: 及龕平，世祖襲東揚州刺史張彪，以恪監吳興郡。
entries.en: After Kan was defeated, Emperor Wen struck Zhang Biao, inspector of East Yangzhou, and left Ke over Wuxing.
entries.literal: After Kan was pacified, Emperor Wen attacked Zhang Biao, Inspector of East Yangzhou, and had Ke supervise Wuxing commandery.

entries.zh: 太平元年，除宣猛將軍、交州刺史。
entries.en: In Taiping year 1, Ke was made fierce-proclaiming general and inspector of Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Ke was appointed Fierce-Proclaiming General and Inspector of Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 其年遷永嘉太守。
entries.en: That same year he was transferred to Yongjia.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Administrator of Yongjia.

entries.zh: 不拜，復令監吳興郡。
entries.en: He did not take up the appointment and was again ordered to supervise Wuxing.
entries.literal: He was not installed, and was again ordered to supervise Wuxing commandery.

entries.zh: 自吳興入朝。
entries.en: From Wuxing he came to court.
entries.literal: From Wuxing he entered court.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，使中書舍人劉師知引恪，令勒兵入辭，[9]因衛敬帝如別宮。
entries.en: When the Founder accepted the abdication, he had Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi bring Ke in and ordered Ke to lead troops in for the farewell audience, then escort Emperor Jing to a separate palace.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he had Secretariat Drafter Liu Shizhi bring Ke in and ordered him to lead troops in to take leave, then escort Emperor Jing to a separate palace.

entries.zh: 恪乃排闥入見高祖，叩頭謝曰：「恪身經事蕭家來，今日不忍見許事，分受死耳，決不奉命。」
entries.en: Ke forced his way in to the Founder, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "I have served the Xiao house with this body. I cannot bear to see this done today. I am ready to die, but I will not obey."
entries.literal: Ke pushed through the door to see the Founder, knocked his head to the ground, and apologized, saying, "This body of mine has served the Xiao house; today I cannot bear to see such a thing. I am prepared to accept death, but I will not obey the order."

entries.zh: 高祖嘉其意，乃不復逼，更以盪主王僧志代之。
entries.en: The Founder admired his loyalty and did not press him further, replacing him with the assault leader Wang Sengzhi.
entries.literal: The Founder admired his intent and no longer pressed him, instead replacing him with assault leader Wang Sengzhi.

entries.zh: 侯景平，高祖鎮朱方，稜監義興、琅邪二郡。
entries.en: After Hou Jing fell and the Founder held Zhufang, Leng was put over Yixing and Langya.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified and the Founder garrisoned Zhufang, Leng supervised the two commanderies of Yixing and Langya.

entries.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，[6]引稜與侯安都等共議，稜難之。
entries.en: When the Founder prepared to kill Wang Sengbian, he brought Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into council; Leng resisted the plan.
entries.literal: When the Founder prepared to kill Wang Sengbian, he drew Leng, Hou Andu, and the others into the planning, but Leng objected.

entries.zh: 高祖懼其泄己，乃以手巾絞稜，稜悶絕于地，因閉於別室。
entries.en: Fearing Leng would leak the plan, the Founder strangled him with a hand towel. Leng collapsed unconscious and was locked in another room.
entries.literal: The Founder feared he would reveal the matter, so he strangled Leng with a hand towel; Leng lost consciousness on the floor and was then shut in a separate room.

entries.zh: 軍發，召與同行。
entries.en: When the army marched, he summoned Leng to accompany it.
entries.literal: When the army set out, he summoned Leng to go with it.

entries.zh: 及僧辯平後，高祖東征杜龕等，留稜與安都居守。
entries.en: After Sengbian was defeated, the Founder marched east against Du Kan and left Leng and Andu to guard the base.
entries.literal: After Sengbian was pacified, the Founder campaigned east against Du Kan and the others, leaving Leng and Andu to hold the base.

entries.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約引齊寇濟江，攻臺城，安都與稜隨方抗拒，稜晝夜巡警，綏撫士卒，未常解帶。
entries.en: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue led Qi raiders across the river against the capital. Andu and Leng met them on every side; Leng patrolled day and night, steadied the men, and never once loosened his belt.
entries.literal: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi raiders across the river and attacked the Terrace City. Andu and Leng resisted them wherever needed; Leng patrolled day and night, soothed and encouraged the soldiers, and never even took off his belt.

entries.zh: 賊平，以功除通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: After the rebels were crushed, his merit brought him appointment as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, right guard general, and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and Intendant of Danyang for his merit.

entries.zh: 永定元年，加侍中、忠武將軍。
entries.en: In Yongding year 1, he was also made palace attendant and loyal-martial general.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongding, he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Loyal-Martial General.

entries.zh: 尋遷中領軍，侍中，將軍如故。
entries.en: Soon he became central commandant of the guards, retaining palace attendant and his general rank.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Central Commandant of the Guards, with Palace Attendant and his generalship as before.

entries.zh: 沈恪字子恭，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Shen Ke, styled Zigong, came from Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Shen Ke, styled Zigong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 深沈有幹局。
entries.en: He was reserved and steady, with a gift for command.
entries.literal: He was deep and steady, with administrative capacity.

entries.zh: 梁新渝侯蕭映為郡將，召為主簿。
entries.en: When Liang's Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, held a commandery, Ke was called up as chief clerk.
entries.literal: When Liang's Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, was commandery general, Ke was summoned as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 映遷北徐州，恪隨映之鎮。
entries.en: When Ying moved to North Xuzhou, Ke went with him to the post.
entries.literal: When Ying was transferred to North Xuzhou, Ke followed Ying to his garrison.

entries.zh: 映遷廣州，以恪兼府中兵參軍，常領兵討伐俚洞。
entries.en: When Ying went to Guangzhou, Ke was made concurrent military adjutant in the princely staff and often led troops against the Li caves.
entries.literal: When Ying was transferred to Guangzhou, Ke was made concurrent military adjutant in the establishment and constantly led troops to campaign against the Li cave settlements.

entries.zh: 盧子略之反也，恪拒戰有功，除中兵參軍。
entries.en: When Lu Zilüe rose, Ke fought him off with merit and was made middle military adjutant.
entries.literal: When Lu Zilüe rebelled, Ke resisted in battle and had merit; he was made middle military adjutant.

entries.zh: 高祖與恪同郡，情好甚暱，蕭映卒後，高祖南討李賁，仍遣妻子附恪還鄉。
entries.en: The Founder shared Ke's home commandery and liked him well. After Xiao Ying died, on the march against Li Ben he sent his family home under Ke's escort.
entries.literal: The Founder was from the same commandery and was on very close terms with Ke; after Xiao Ying died the Founder campaigned south against Li Ben and sent his wife and children home with Ke to their native place.

entries.zh: 尋補東宮直後，以嶺南勳除員外散騎侍郎，仍令招集宗從子弟。[7]
entries.en: He was soon made direct attendant after the Eastern Palace, then brevetted scattered-cavalry attendant gentleman for his southern service and told to rally his clan.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Direct Attendant After the Eastern Palace; for his merit in Lingnan he was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry attendant gentleman and was further ordered to gather kinsmen and clan youths.

entries.zh: 稜歷事三帝，並見恩寵。
entries.en: Leng served three emperors and won favor under each.
entries.literal: Leng served three emperors and in each was shown favor.

entries.zh: 末年不預征役，優遊京師，賞賜優洽。
entries.en: In his last years he stayed out of the field, idling in the capital while honors and gifts flowed freely.
entries.literal: In his last years he took no part in campaigns; he lived at ease in the capital, and gifts and rewards were generous.

entries.zh: 頃之卒于官，時年七十。
entries.en: He soon died in office, aged seventy.
entries.literal: Before long he died in office, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，喪事所須，並令資給，諡曰成。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand master for splendid happiness with three-excellency honors; the court paid for the funeral and gave him the posthumous name Accomplished.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies; all funeral needs were ordered supplied, and his posthumous title was Accomplished.

entries.zh: 其年配享高祖廟庭。
entries.en: That year he was enshrined in the Founder's temple.
entries.literal: That year he was given a place in the Founder's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子安世嗣。
entries.en: His son Anshi succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Anshi succeeded.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，除吳興太守。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Ke was made administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, [Ke] was appointed Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 永定二年，徙監會稽郡。
entries.en: In Yongding year two he was transferred to oversee Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was transferred to supervise Kuaiji commandery.

entries.zh: 會余孝頃謀應王琳，出兵臨川攻周迪，以恪為壯武將軍，率兵踰嶺以救迪。
entries.en: When Yu Xiaoqing plotted to side with Wang Lin and marched from Linchuan against Zhou Di, Ke was made stalwart-martial general and led an army over the mountains to relieve Di.
entries.literal: When Yu Xiaoqing plotted to join Wang Lin, he sent troops from Linchuan to attack Zhou Di; Ke was made Stalwart-Martial General and led troops across the ranges to rescue Di.

entries.zh: 余孝頃聞恪至，退走。
entries.en: When Yu Xiaoqing learned Ke was coming, he retreated.
entries.literal: When Yu Xiaoqing heard Ke had arrived, he withdrew.

entries.zh: 三年，遷使持節、通直散騎常侍、智武將軍、吳州刺史，便道之鄱陽。
entries.en: In year three he was made bearer of the staff, courier scattered-cavalry regular attendant, intelligent-martial general, and inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.
entries.literal: In year three he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Courier Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Intelligent-Martial General, and Inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.

entries.zh: 尋有詔追還，行會稽郡事。
entries.en: Before long an edict recalled him, and he administered Kuaiji commandery affairs.
entries.literal: Soon there was an edict recalling him; he acted in Kuaiji commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 其年，除散騎常侍、忠武將軍、會稽太守。
entries.en: That year he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, loyal-martial general, and administrator of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: That year he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Loyal-Martial General, and Administrator of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，進督會稽、東陽、新安、臨海、永嘉、建安、晉安、新寧、信安九郡諸軍事，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ke was promoted to command the nine commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, Yongjia, Jian'an, Jin'an, Xinning, and Xin'an, while keeping his general and administrator posts.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ke was advanced to command military affairs in the nine commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, Yongjia, Jian'an, Jin'an, Xinning, and Xin'an; his generalship and administrator post remained as before.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, five hundred households were added to his fief.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his fief was increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 二年，徵為左衛將軍。
entries.en: In the second year, he was recalled as left guard general.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was summoned as Left Guard General.

entries.zh: 俄出為都督郢武巴定四州諸軍事、軍師將軍、郢州刺史。
entries.en: Soon he was sent out as commander of Ying, Wu, Ba, and Ding, army adviser general, and inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent out as Area Commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Ying, Wu, Ba, and Ding, Army Adviser General, and Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 六年，徵為中護軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was recalled as central protector of the army.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned as Central Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 尋遷護軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he became protector general.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Protector General.

entries.zh: 光大二年，遷使持節、都督荊武祐三州諸軍事、平西將軍、荊州刺史。
entries.en: In Guangda year 2, he was made bearer of the staff with credentials, commander of Jing, Wu, and You, general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangda, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff with Credentials, Area Commander over military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Wu, and You, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 未之鎮，改為護軍將軍。[10]
entries.en: Before he left for the post, he was reassigned as protector general.
entries.literal: Before he went to the garrison, he was changed to Protector General.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，加散騎常侍、都督廣衡東衡交越成定新合羅愛德宜黃利安石雙等十八州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ke was further made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in eighteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, general who guards the south, Gentleman-General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Ke] was additionally made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, General Who Guards the South, Gentleman-General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 恪未至嶺，前刺史歐陽紇舉兵拒險，恪不得進，朝廷遣司空章昭達督眾軍討紇，紇平，乃得入州。
entries.en: Before Ke crossed the mountains, the former inspector Ouyang He held the passes with an army and blocked him. The court sent Zhang Zhaoda, minister of works, to lead the armies against He; only after He was suppressed could Ke enter the province.
entries.literal: Before Ke reached the ranges, the former inspector Ouyang He raised troops blocking the passes; Ke could not advance. The court sent Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to command the armies to campaign against He; when He was pacified, [Ke] was able to enter the prefecture.

entries.zh: 州罹兵荒，所在殘毀，恪綏懷安緝，被以恩惠，嶺表賴之。
entries.en: The province had been ravaged by war and lay in ruins. Ke comforted and settled the people, treating them with kindness, and the far south came to rely on him.
entries.literal: The prefecture had suffered war and devastation; everywhere was ruined. Ke soothed and settled the people, covering them with kindness; the region beyond the ranges relied on him.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：胡穎、徐度、杜稜、沈恪並附騏驥而騰躍，依日月之光輝，始覯王佐之才，方悟公輔之量，生則肉食，終以配饗。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all rode swift steeds to rise, drew on the light of sun and moon, first saw the gifts of royal counselors, then grasped the stature of chief ministers; in life they feasted at court, in death they shared offerings in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all attached to swift steeds and leaped upward, relied on the brilliance of sun and moon, first beheld the talent of royal assistants, then understood the measure of chief ministers; in life they ate at meat tables, in death they were granted temple shares.

entries.zh: 盛矣哉！
entries.en: How splendid!
entries.literal: Magnificent indeed!

entries.zh: 太建四年，徵為領軍將軍。
entries.en: In Taijian year 4, he was recalled as commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian, he was summoned as Commandant of the Guards.

entries.zh: 及代還，以途遠不時至，為有司所奏免。
entries.en: When his successor arrived and he returned, the long road delayed him. Officials impeached him for not arriving on time, and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: When his replacement arrived and he returned, because the road was distant and he did not arrive on time, the responsible officials memorialized against him and he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 十一年，起為散騎常侍、衛尉卿。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, he was brought back as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and chamberlain for the guards.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he was restored as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Chamberlain for the Guards.

entries.zh: 其年授平北將軍、假節，監南兗州。
entries.en: That same year he was made general who pacifies the north, received acting credentials, and was put over South Yanzhou.
entries.literal: That year he was granted General Who Pacifies the North, acting credentials, and supervision of South Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 十二年，改授散騎常侍、翊右將軍，監南徐州。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, he was reassigned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and general who assists the right, supervising South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, he was reassigned as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and General Who Assists the Right, supervising South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 又遣電威將軍裴子烈領馬五百匹，助恪緣江防戍。
entries.en: The court also sent Pei Zilie, lightning-might general, with five hundred horses to help Ke defend the river line.
entries.literal: The court also sent Lightning-Might General Pei Zilie with five hundred horses to assist Ke in the defenses and garrisons along the river.

entries.zh: 明年，入為衛尉卿，常侍、將軍如故。
entries.en: The next year, he returned to court as chamberlain for the guards, keeping regular attendant and his general rank.
entries.literal: The next year, he entered court as Chamberlain for the Guards, with Regular Attendant and generalship as before.

entries.zh: 尋加侍中，遷護軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was made palace attendant and promoted to protector general.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to Protector General.

entries.zh: 後主即位，以疾改授散騎常侍、特進、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the Later Lord succeeded, Ke was ill, so he was reassigned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant, special grandee, and grandee of splendid happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: When the Later Lord took the throne, because of illness Ke was reassigned as Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Special Grandee, and Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 其年卒，時年七十四。
entries.en: He died that year at seventy-four.
entries.literal: He died that year, aged seventy-four.

entries.zh: 贈翊左將軍，詔給東園祕器，仍出舉哀，喪事所須，並令資給，諡曰元。
entries.en: He was posthumously made general who assists the left. The court supplied an Eastern Park coffin, held public mourning, paid all funeral costs, and gave him the posthumous name Primal.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Assists the Left; an edict supplied a coffin from the Eastern Park imperial workshop, went out to hold mourning, and ordered all funeral needs funded; his posthumous name was Primal.

entries.zh: 子法興嗣。
entries.en: His son Faxing inherited the line.
entries.literal: His son Faxing succeeded.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十二
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 12
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 12

entries.zh: 徐世譜字興宗，巴東魚復人也。
entries.en: Xu Shipu, styled Xingzong, came from Yufu in Badong.
entries.literal: Xu Shipu, styled Xingzong, was a native of Yufu in Badong.

entries.zh: 世居荊州，為主帥，征伐蠻、蜒。
entries.en: His clan had long held Jingzhou as local commanders, campaigning against the Man and Yi peoples.
entries.literal: For generations the family dwelt in Jingzhou as a territorial commander, campaigning against the Man and the Yi.

entries.zh: 至世譜，尤敢勇有膂力，善水戰。
entries.en: Shipu was bolder and stronger than his forebears and excelled at river fighting.
entries.literal: By Shipu's time he was especially daring and brave, with great physical strength, and skilled in naval warfare.

entries.zh: 梁元帝之為荊州刺史，世譜將領鄉人事焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang governed Jingzhou, Shipu led the district commanders and village heads in his service.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was governor of Jingzhou, Shipu led the local commanders and village heads in serving him.

entries.zh: 西魏來寇荊州，世譜鎮馬頭岸，據有龍
entries.en: When Western Wei raided Jingzhou, Shipu held Matou Bank and occupied Long
entries.literal: Western Wei came to raid Jingzhou; Shipu garrisoned Matou Bank and held Long

entries.en: (zhou)
entries.literal: (zhou)

entries.zh: 洲，[3]元帝授侍中、使持節、都督江南諸軍事、鎮南將軍、護軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: Islet. [3] Emperor Yuan made him palace attendant, credential-holder, commander of all armies south of the Yangzi, general who guards the south, and protector-general, with one set of pipes and drums.
entries.literal: Islet, Emperor Yuan appointed him palace attendant, credential-holder, area commander of all armies south of the Yangzi, general who guards the south, protector-general, and gave him one set of pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 江陵陷沒，世譜東下依侯瑱。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Shipu went east and joined Hou Tian.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Shipu went east and attached himself to Hou Tian.

entries.zh: 悉達幼以孝聞，起家為梁南平嗣王中兵參軍。
entries.en: From boyhood Xida was known for filial piety. He first entered service as army supervisor in the establishment of Liang's heir Prince of Nanping.
entries.literal: From youth Xida was famed for filial piety; he first took office as army supervisor in the establishment of Liang's heir Prince of Nanping.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，悉達糾合鄉人，保新蔡，力田蓄穀。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion Xida rallied his neighbors to hold Xincai, farmed hard, and stored grain.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Xida gathered fellow-townsmen to hold Xincai, farming diligently and storing grain.

entries.zh: 時兵荒饑饉，京都及上川餓死者十八九，有得存者，皆攜老幼以歸焉。
entries.en: In the war and famine, eight or nine of ten in the capital and upper Yangzi died of hunger. Those who lived came back with the old and young in tow.
entries.literal: In that time of military chaos and famine, nine or ten in the capital and upper Yangzi valley died of hunger; those who survived all brought the aged and young back with them.

entries.zh: 悉達分給糧廩，其所濟活者甚眾，仍於新蔡置頓以居之。
entries.en: Xida opened his granaries. The people he kept alive were countless, and he set a camp at Xincai to shelter them.
entries.literal: Xida distributed grain from his granaries; those he saved were very many, and he then established a camp at Xincai to house them.

entries.zh: 招集晉熙等五郡，盡有其地。
entries.en: He drew in five commanderies, including Jinxi, and held all their lands.
entries.literal: He recruited the five commanderies including Jinxi and held all their territory.

entries.zh: 使其弟廣達領兵隨王僧辯討侯景。
entries.en: He sent his younger brother Guangda with troops to follow Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He had his younger brother Guangda lead troops to follow Wang Sengbian in suppressing Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 景平，梁元帝授持節、仁威將軍、散騎常侍、北江州刺史。
entries.en: When Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang made him credential-holder, benevolent-prestige general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him credential-holder, benevolent-prestige general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 俄而續部下將帥爭權，復反，殺續以降周迪。
entries.en: Soon Xu's officers fought for power, rebelled again, killed Xu, and submitted to Zhou Di.
entries.literal: Before long Xu's subordinate commanders vied for power, rebelled again, killed Xu, and surrendered to Zhou Di.

entries.zh: 迪素無簿閥，恐失眾心，倚敷族望，深求交結。
entries.en: Di had no pedigree in the registers and feared losing the crowd. He leaned on Fu's family standing and courted him hard.
entries.literal: Di by nature had no register of lineage and feared losing the hearts of the masses; relying on Fu's clan prestige he sought his friendship deeply.

entries.zh: 敷未能自固，事迪甚恭，迪大憑仗之，漸有兵眾。
entries.en: Fu could not yet stand alone and served Di with deep deference. Di relied on him heavily and slowly built an army.
entries.literal: Fu could not yet secure himself and served Di with great deference; Di leaned heavily on him and gradually had troops and horses.

entries.zh: 迪據臨川之工塘，敷鎮臨川故郡。
entries.en: Di held Gongtang in Linchuan; Fu held the old commandery seat.
entries.literal: Di held Gongtang in Linchuan; Fu garrisoned the old commandery seat of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝授敷使持節、通直散騎常侍、信武將軍、寧州刺史，封西豐縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: When Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang made Fu credential-holder, regular attendant for direct communication, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Ningzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng with one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Fu credential-holder, regular attendant for direct communication, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Ningzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 朗少慷慨，有將帥大略，起家梁廬陵王行參軍。
entries.en: From youth Lang was open-handed and bold, with a commander's breadth of plan. He first served as traveling attendant in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Luling.
entries.literal: From youth Lang was generous and bold, with the grand strategy of a commander; he first took office as traveling attendant in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Luling.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，朗招率徒旅，據巢湖閒，無所屬。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lang gathered followers, held the country about Chaohu Lake, and owed allegiance to no one.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Lang gathered a following, held the lands about Chaohu Lake, and belonged to no one.

entries.zh: 臺城陷後，簡文帝密詔授朗雲麾將軍、豫州刺史，令與外藩討景。
entries.en: After the capital fell, Emperor Jianwen of Liang secretly made him cloud-banner general and inspector of Yu and ordered him, with the outer provinces, to crush Jing.
entries.literal: After the Terrace City fell Emperor Jianwen of Liang sent a secret edict appointing Lang cloud-banner general and inspector of Yu and ordering him with outer provinces to suppress Jing.

entries.zh: 景使儀同宋子仙、任約等頻往征之，朗據山立砦自守，子仙不能克。
entries.en: Jing sent his comrades Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others against him again and again. Lang held mountain forts and Zixian could not take him.
entries.literal: Jing sent comrades-in-arms Song Zixian, Ren Yue, and others repeatedly to campaign against him; Lang held mountain stockades in defense and Zixian could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 時京師大饑，百姓皆於江外就食，朗更招致部曲，解衣推食，以相賑贍，眾至數萬人。
entries.en: The capital was starving. People crossed the Yangzi to find food. Lang gathered more men, stripped off his own clothes to feed them, and built a following of tens of thousands.
entries.literal: At that time the capital had great famine; commoners all went south of the Yangzi to seek food; Lang further recruited followers, doffed his own garments and shared food, giving mutual relief, until his following reached tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 侯景敗於巴陵，朗出自濡須截景，破其後軍。
entries.en: When Hou Jing was beaten at Baling, Lang came out from Ruru Ford, cut Jing off, and smashed his rearguard.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was defeated at Baling Lang came out from Ruru Ford to intercept Jing and broke his rearguard.

entries.zh: 王僧辯東討，朗遣其將范寶勝及弟曉領兵二千助之。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian marched east, Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao, with two thousand men, to help.
entries.literal: Wang Sengbian campaigned east; Lang sent his general Fan Baosheng and his younger brother Xiao each to lead two thousand troops to assist.

entries.zh: 侯景平後，又別破齊將郭元建於踟躕山。
entries.en: After Hou Jing fell he again defeated Qi general Guo Yuanjian at Chichu Mountain.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified he again separately defeated Qi general Guo Yuanjian at Chichu Mountain.

entries.zh: 梁承聖二年，率部曲萬餘家濟江，入宣城郡界立頓。
entries.en: In Liang Chengsheng year two, Lang led more than ten thousand follower households across the Yangzi, entered Xuancheng commandery, and set up camp.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng of Liang, [Lang] led more than ten thousand households of his following across the Yangzi, entered Xuancheng commandery territory, and established a camp.

entries.zh: 梁元帝授朗持節、通直散騎常侍、安南將軍、都督南兗州諸軍事、南兗州刺史。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang made Lang bearer of the staff, courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-south general, commander of South Yanzhou armies, and inspector of the province.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Lang Bearer of the Staff, Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-South General, Area Commander over Military Affairs in South Yanzhou, and Inspector of South Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 未行而荊州陷。
entries.en: Before he could take up the post, Jingzhou fell.
entries.literal: Before he took up the post, Jingzhou fell.

entries.zh: 炅少豪俠任氣，有將帥才。
entries.en: From youth Jiong was bold, chivalrous, and spirited, with the talent of a commander.
entries.literal: Jiong from youth was bold, chivalrous, and willful, with the talent of a commander.

entries.zh: 梁大同中為通直散騎侍郎、朱衣直閤。
entries.en: During Liang Datong he served as direct-communication scattered-cavalry gentleman and red-robed palace attendant.
entries.literal: During Liang Datong he served as direct-communication scattered-cavalry gentleman and red-robed palace attendant.

entries.zh: 太清元年，出為弋陽太守。
entries.en: In Taiqing year 1 (547), he was sent out as administrator of Yiyang.
entries.literal: In Taiqing year 1, he went out as administrator of Yiyang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝承制改授西陽太守，封西陵縣伯。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan, acting on provisional authority, changed his appointment to administrator of Xiyang and enfeoffed him as earl of Xiling county.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan, acting on provisional authority, changed his appointment to administrator of Xiyang and enfeoffed him as earl of Xiling county.

entries.zh: 景遣兄子思穆據守齊安，炅率驍勇襲破思穆，擒斬之。
entries.en: Jing sent his nephew Simu to occupy and guard Qi'an. Jiong led picked brave men in a raid, defeated Simu, captured him, and beheaded him.
entries.literal: Jing sent his nephew Simu to occupy and guard Qi'an; Jiong led picked brave men in a raid, defeated Simu, captured him, and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 以功授持節、高州刺史。
entries.en: For his merit he was made credential-holder and inspector of Gaozhou.
entries.literal: For his merit he was appointed credential-holder and inspector of Gaozhou.

entries.zh: 是時炅據武昌、西陽二郡，招聚卒徒，甲兵甚盛。
entries.en: At this time Jiong held Wuchang and Xiyang commanderies, gathered soldiers and followers, and had a very strong force.
entries.literal: At this time Jiong held Wuchang and Xiyang commanderies, gathered soldiers and followers, and had very strong troops and armor.

entries.zh: 景將任約來據樊山，炅與寧州長史徐文盛擊約，斬其部將叱羅子通、趙迦婁等。
entries.en: Jing's general Ren Yue came to occupy Fanshan. Jiong and Xu Wensheng, chief clerk of Ningzhou, attacked Yue and killed his subordinate commanders Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Jialou, and others.
entries.literal: Jing's general Ren Yue came to occupy Fanshan; Jiong and Xu Wensheng, chief clerk of Ningzhou, attacked Yue and killed his subordinate commanders Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Jialou, and others.

entries.zh: 因乘勝追之，頻克，約眾殆盡。
entries.en: He followed up the victory in pursuit, won repeatedly, and nearly wiped out Yue's force.
entries.literal: Then he followed up the victory and pursued them, winning repeatedly, until Yue's forces were almost exhausted.

entries.zh: 承聖元年，遷使持節、都督江定二州諸軍事、戎昭將軍、江州刺史，進爵為侯，邑五百戶。
