entries.en: In Chengsheng year 1 (552), he was transferred to credential-holder, director-general of all military affairs in Jiang and Ding provinces, martial-illustrious general, and inspector of Jiangzhou. His title was raised to marquis, with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year 1, he was transferred to credential-holder, director-general of all military affairs in Jiang and Ding provinces, martial-illustrious general, and inspector of Jiangzhou; his title was advanced to marquis, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，因預征討，累遷至員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he joined the punitive armies and rose step by step to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he took part in the punitive campaigns and rose in succession to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 尋領水軍，從司徒陸法和討景，與景戰於赤亭湖。
entries.en: Soon he commanded the navy and, under Minister of Education Lu Fahe, marched against Jing and fought him at Red Pavilion Lake.
entries.literal: Soon he took command of the navy and, following Minister of Education Lu Fahe, campaigned against Jing, fighting him at Red Pavilion Lake.

entries.zh: 時景軍甚盛，世譜乃別造樓船、拍艦、火舫、水車以益軍勢。
entries.en: Jing's army was then overwhelming. Shipu had new tower ships, rams, fire-boats, and water-engines built to swell his fleet.
entries.literal: At that time Jing's army was very strong; Shipu thereupon had tower ships, battering ships, fire vessels, and water-wheels built separately to strengthen the fleet.

entries.zh: 將戰，又乘大艦居前，大敗景軍，生擒景將任約，景退走。
entries.en: When battle came he again put a great ship in the van, crushed Jing's army, took Jing's general Ren Yue alive, and drove Jing off.
entries.literal: As battle was joined he again took a great war-ship to the fore, inflicted a great defeat on Jing's army, captured Jing's general Ren Yue alive, and Jing fled.

entries.zh: 因隨王僧辯攻郢州，世譜復乘大艦臨其倉門，賊將宋子仙據城降。
entries.en: He followed Wang Sengbian against Yingzhou. Shipu again brought a great ship under the granary gate, and the rebel Song Zixian surrendered the city.
entries.literal: He then followed Wang Sengbian in attacking Yingzhou; Shipu again took a great war-ship up to the granary gate, and the rebel general Song Zixian surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 以功除使持節、信武將軍、信州刺史，封魚復縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made credential-holder, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Xinzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu with five hundred households.
entries.literal: For merit he was appointed holder of credentials, trustworthy-faith general, and inspector of Xinzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yufu county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍隨僧辯東下，恆為軍鋒。
entries.en: He still marched east with Sengbian and was always the army's vanguard.
entries.literal: He still followed Sengbian eastward, always serving as the army's vanguard.

entries.zh: 又破景將侯子鑒於湖熟。
entries.en: He again broke Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu.
entries.literal: He again defeated Jing's general Hou Zijian at Hushu.

entries.zh: [1]侯景平後，以功除通直散騎常侍、衡州刺史資，
entries.en: [1] After Hou Jing fell, for merit he was made regular attendant for direct communication and given credentials as inspector of Hengzhou,
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, for merit he was appointed regular attendant for direct communication, with credentials as inspector of Hengzhou,

entries.en: (garrison)
entries.literal: (garrison)

entries.zh: 領河東太守，[2]增邑并前一千戶。
entries.en: garrison administrator of Hedong, [2] with his fief raised to one thousand households in all.
entries.literal: garrison Administrator of Hedong, fief increased to one thousand households combined with the former.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，鄉人周續合徒眾以討賊為名，梁內史始興藩王蕭毅以郡讓續，[6]續所部內有欲侵掠於毅，敷擁護之，親率其黨捍衛，送至豫章。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion the townsman Zhou Xu raised men in the name of punishing rebels. Liang's interior secretary, Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi, yielded the commandery to Xu. [6] Some of Xu's men meant to plunder Yi. Fu shielded him, led his own band in defense, and saw him safely to Yuzhang.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the townsman Zhou Xu gathered a host under the name of suppressing bandits; Liang's interior secretary the Prince of Shixing Xiao Yi made over the commandery to Xu, and within Xu's command some wished to plunder Yi; Fu guarded him, personally leading his faction to defend and escort him to Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 時觀寧侯蕭永、長樂侯蕭基、豐城侯蕭泰避難流寓，聞敷信義，皆往依之。
entries.en: The Marquis of Guanning Xiao Yong, the Marquis of Changle Xiao Ji, and the Marquis of Fengcheng Xiao Tai were then refugees. Hearing of Fu's faith and honor, they all came to him.
entries.literal: At that time the Marquis of Guanning Xiao Yong, the Marquis of Changle Xiao Ji, and the Marquis of Fengcheng Xiao Tai were refugees in flight; hearing of Fu's trustworthiness and righteousness they all went to rely on him.

entries.zh: 敷愍其危懼，屈體崇敬，厚加給卹，送之西上。
entries.en: Fu pitied their fear, treated them with humble courtesy, gave them generous aid, and sent them west upriver.
entries.literal: Fu pitied their peril and fear, bowed his body in reverence, gave them generous relief, and sent them upriver west.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，徵為侍中、左衛將軍。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 1 (555), Shipu was summoned as palace attendant and left guard general.
entries.literal: In Shaotai year 1, he was summoned as palace attendant and left guard general.

entries.zh: 高祖之拒王琳，其水戰之具，悉委世譜。
entries.en: When the Founder opposed Wang Lin, he entrusted all the equipment for naval warfare to Shipu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu resisted Wang Lin, he entrusted all the equipment for water warfare to Shipu.

entries.zh: 世譜性機巧，諳解舊法，所造器械，並隨機損益，妙思出人。
entries.en: Shipu was naturally ingenious and knew the old methods well. Every device he made was adapted to the situation, and his clever designs surpassed other men.
entries.literal: Shipu was ingenious by nature and understood old methods; the equipment he made was always adjusted according to circumstance, and his clever ideas surpassed other men.

entries.zh: 敬帝即位，王琳據有上流，留異、余孝頃、周迪等所在鋒起，悉達撫綏五郡，甚得民和，士卒皆樂為之用。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Wang Lin controlled the upper Yangzi, and Liu Yi, Yu Xiaoqing, Zhou Di, and others rose in arms everywhere. Xida pacified the five commanderies, won the people over, and his soldiers were all glad to serve him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, Wang Lin held the upper reaches, while Liu Yi, Yu Xiaoqing, Zhou Di, and others rose sharply everywhere; Xida pacified the five commanderies, greatly won the people, and the soldiers were all glad to serve him.

entries.zh: 琳授悉達鎮北將軍，高祖亦遣趙知禮授征西將軍、江州刺史，各送鼓吹女樂，悉達兩受之，遷延顧望，皆不就。
entries.en: Wang Lin appointed Xida general who guards the north, while the Founder sent Zhao Zhili to appoint him general who campaigns west and inspector of Jiangzhou. Both sides sent pipes and drums and female musicians; Xida accepted both gifts, delayed and watched, and took up neither appointment.
entries.literal: Lin appointed Xida general who guards the north; Gaozu also sent Zhao Zhili to appoint him general who campaigns west and inspector of Jiangzhou. Each sent pipes and drums and female musicians; Xida accepted both, delayed and watched, and took up neither.

entries.zh: 高祖遣安西將軍沈泰潛師襲之，不能克。
entries.en: The Founder sent Shen Tai, general who secures the west, to attack him by stealth, but Shen Tai could not defeat him.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Shen Tai, general who secures the west, to make a hidden attack on him, but Shen Tai could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 齊遣行臺慕容紹宗以眾三萬來攻鬱口諸鎮，兵甲甚盛，悉達與戰，敗齊軍，紹宗僅以身免。
entries.en: Qi sent Murong Shaozong of the mobile secretariat with thirty thousand troops to attack the Yukou garrisons. Their force was powerful, but Xida fought them, defeated the Qi army, and Shaozong barely escaped with his life.
entries.literal: Qi sent Murong Shaozong of the mobile secretariat with thirty thousand troops to attack the various garrisons at Yukou; their soldiers and armor were very strong, but Xida fought them, defeated the Qi army, and Shaozong barely escaped with his life.

entries.zh: 王琳欲圖東下，以悉達制其中流，恐為己患，頻遣使招誘，悉達終不從。
entries.en: Wang Lin wanted to move east, but Xida controlled the midstream and Lin feared he would become a threat. Lin repeatedly sent envoys to lure him over, but Xida never followed him.
entries.literal: Wang Lin wanted to plan an eastern descent, but because Xida controlled the middle current, he feared Xida would become a problem for him and repeatedly sent envoys to entice him; Xida never followed him.

entries.zh: 琳不得下，乃連結於齊，共為表裏，齊遣清河王高岳助之。
entries.en: Unable to move downriver, Lin allied with Qi so they could support each other from inside and outside; Qi sent Gao Yue, Prince of Qinghe, to help him.
entries.literal: Lin could not descend, so he joined with Qi and made an inside-and-outside alliance; Qi sent Gao Yue, Prince of Qinghe, to help him.

entries.zh: 相持歲餘，會裨將梅天養等懼罪，乃引齊軍入城。
entries.en: The standoff lasted more than a year, until the junior general Mei Tianyang and others, fearing punishment, led the Qi army into the city.
entries.literal: They held each other off for more than a year, until junior general Mei Tianyang and others, fearing punishment, led the Qi army into the city.

entries.zh: 悉達勒麾下數千人，濟江而歸高祖。
entries.en: Xida mustered several thousand of his men, crossed the Yangzi, and submitted to the Founder.
entries.literal: Xida mustered several thousand men under his command, crossed the Yangzi, and submitted to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖見之，甚喜，曰：「來何遲也？」
entries.en: When the Founder saw him, he was delighted and said, "Why have you come so late?"
entries.literal: Gaozu saw him and was very pleased, saying, "Why did you come so late?"

entries.zh: 悉達對曰：「臣鎮撫上流，願為蕃屏，陛下授臣以官，恩至厚矣，沈泰襲臣，威亦深矣，然臣所以自歸於陛下者，誠以陛下豁達大度，同符漢祖故也。」
entries.en: Xida replied, "I guarded and pacified the upper reaches and wished to serve as a shield. Your Majesty granted me office, and the favor was generous indeed; Shen Tai attacked me, and the show of force was also severe. Yet I submitted myself to Your Majesty because Your Majesty is open-hearted and magnanimous, matching the Founder of Han."
entries.literal: Xida replied, "I guarded and pacified the upper reaches and wished to be a fence and screen. Your Majesty gave me office, and the favor was most generous; Shen Tai attacked me, and the awe was also deep. Yet the reason I submitted myself to Your Majesty is truly that Your Majesty is open-hearted and magnanimous, matching the Founder of Han."

entries.zh: 高祖嘆曰：「卿言得之矣。」
entries.en: The Founder sighed and said, "You have said it exactly."
entries.literal: Gaozu sighed and said, "Your words have it."

entries.zh: 授平南將軍、散騎常侍、北江州刺史，封彭澤縣侯。
entries.en: He was appointed general who pacifies the south, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Pengze county.
entries.literal: He was appointed general who pacifies the south, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and inspector of North Jiangzhou, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Pengze county.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，進號安左將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Xida was promoted to general who secures the left.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, his title was advanced to general who secures the left.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳據有上流，余孝頃與琳黨李
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Yu Xiaoqing with Lin's ally Li
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Yu Xiaoqing with Lin's partisan Li

entries.en: (Xi)
entries.literal: (Xi)

entries.zh: 孝欽等共圍周迪，[7]敷大致人馬以助於迪。
entries.en: Xiao Qin and others besieged Zhou Di together. [7] Fu mustered a great body of men and horses to help Di.
entries.literal: Xiao Qin and others jointly besieged Zhou Di, and Fu gathered a great force of men and horses to aid Di.

entries.zh: 迪擒孝頃等，敷功居多。
entries.en: Di took Xiaoqing and his fellows prisoner. Fu's share of the merit was greatest.
entries.literal: Di captured Xiaoqing and the others; Fu's merit was greatest.

entries.zh: 高祖入輔，齊遣蕭軌、東方老等來寇，據石頭城。
entries.en: When the Founder entered to support the government, Qi sent Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others to raid the state and occupy Shitou city.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered as regent, Qi sent Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others to raid and occupy Shitou city.

entries.zh: 朗自宣城來赴，因與侯安都等大破齊軍。
entries.en: Lang came from Xuancheng to answer the call and, with Hou Andu and others, routed the Qi army.
entries.literal: Lang came from Xuancheng to answer the call and then, with Hou Andu and others, greatly defeated the Qi army.

entries.zh: 永定元年，賜爵興寧縣侯，邑二千戶，以朗兄昂為左衛將軍，弟晷為太子右衛率。
entries.en: In Yongding year 1 (557), Lang was granted the title marquis of Xingning county with two thousand households. His elder brother Ang was made left guard general, and his younger brother Gui right guard commandant to the crown prince.
entries.literal: In Yongding year 1, he was granted the title marquis of Xingning county with a fief of two thousand households; Lang's elder brother Ang was made left guard general, and his younger brother Gui was made right guard commandant to the crown prince.

entries.zh: 尋遣朗隨世祖拒王琳於南皖。
entries.en: Soon Lang was sent to follow Emperor Wen against Wang Lin at Nanwan.
entries.literal: Soon Lang was sent to follow Emperor Wen in resisting Wang Lin at Nanwan.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，宣太后與舍人蔡景歷祕不發喪，朗弟曉在都微知之，乃謀率其家兵襲臺。
entries.en: When the Founder died, Empress Dowager Xuan and the secretary Cai Jingli kept the death secret and did not announce mourning. Lang's younger brother Xiao, who was in the capital, learned a little of it and plotted to lead his household troops in an attack on the palace.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, Empress Dowager Xuan and secretary Cai Jingli kept the death secret and did not announce mourning; Lang's younger brother Xiao was in the capital and faintly learned of it, then plotted to lead his household troops in an attack on the palace.

entries.zh: 事覺，景歷殺曉，仍繫其兄弟。
entries.en: The plot was discovered; Jingli killed Xiao and imprisoned his brothers.
entries.literal: The affair was discovered; Jingli killed Xiao and then imprisoned his brothers.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，並釋之。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, he released them all.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he released them all.

entries.zh: 因厚撫慰朗，令與侯安都等共拒王琳。
entries.en: He then generously reassured Lang and ordered him to join Hou Andu and the others against Wang Lin.
entries.literal: He then generously soothed and reassured Lang, ordering him with Hou Andu and others to resist Wang Lin together.

entries.zh: 琳平，遷使持節、安北將軍、散騎常侍、都督霍晉合三州諸軍事、合州刺史。
entries.en: After Lin was pacified, Lang was transferred to credential-holder, general who secures the north, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, director-general of all military affairs in Huo, Jin, and He provinces, and inspector of Hezhou.
entries.literal: When Lin was pacified, Lang was transferred to credential-holder, general who secures the north, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, director-general of all military affairs in Huo, Jin, and He provinces, and inspector of Hezhou.

entries.zh: 天嘉六年卒，時年四十八。
entries.en: He died in Tianjia year 6 (565), aged forty-eight.
entries.literal: He died in Tianjia year 6, aged forty-eight.

entries.zh: 贈南豫州刺史，諡曰壯。
entries.en: He was posthumously made inspector of Southern Yuzhou and given the posthumous name Zhuang.
entries.literal: He was posthumously presented as inspector of Southern Yuzhou and given the title Zhuang.

entries.zh: 子法尚嗣。
entries.en: His son Fashang succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Fashang succeeded.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，王琳擁據上流，炅以州從之。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi, and Jiong brought his province to his side.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Jiong followed him with his prefecture.

entries.zh: 及王琳遣其將曹慶等攻周迪，仍使炅將兵掎角而進，為侯安都所敗，擒炅送都。
entries.en: When Wang Lin sent Cao Qing and others against Zhou Di, he also ordered Jiong to advance in concert; Hou Andu defeated him, took him prisoner, and sent him to court.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin sent his generals Cao Qing and others to attack Zhou Di, he also had Jiong lead troops in pincer advance; [Jiong] was defeated by Hou Andu, captured, and sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 世祖釋炅，授戎威將軍、定州刺史，帶西陽、武昌二郡太守。
entries.en: Emperor Wen freed Jiong and made him martial-power general and inspector of Dingzhou, with concurrent charge of Xiyang and Wuchang.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen released Jiong and appointed him Martial-Power General and Inspector of Dingzhou, concurrently Administrator of the two commanderies Xiyang and Wuchang.

entries.zh: 永定二年，遷護軍將軍。
entries.en: In Yongding year 2 (558) he was made protector-general.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was transferred to protector-general.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，加特進，進號安右將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was given special advance and promoted to secure-the-right general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, he was given special advance and promoted to secure-the-right general.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1 (560), his fief grew by five hundred households.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 1, his fief was increased by five hundred households.

entries.zh: 二年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督宣城郡諸軍事、安西將軍、宣城太守，秩中二千石。
entries.en: In the second year he went out as credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in Xuancheng, secure-the-west general, and administrator of Xuancheng at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
entries.literal: In the second year he went out with credentials as supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, area commander of all military affairs in Xuancheng prefecture, secure-the-west general, and administrator of Xuancheng, salary at the two-thousand-bushel level.

entries.zh: 還為安前將軍、右光祿大夫。
entries.en: Back at court he was made secure-the-front general and Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness.
entries.literal: Returning, he was made secure-the-front general and Right Grand Master with Splendid Happiness.

entries.zh: 尋以疾失明，謝病不朝。
entries.en: Soon illness blinded him, and he begged leave from court.
entries.literal: Soon he went blind from illness and excused himself from court on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 四年卒，時年五十五。
entries.en: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-five.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-five.

entries.zh: 贈本官，諡曰桓侯。
entries.en: He was posthumously given his former offices, with the posthumous name Marquis Huan.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given his former offices; posthumous name Marquis Huan.

entries.zh: 五年，迪又收合餘眾，還襲東興。
entries.en: In the fifth year Di rallied his remnants and struck Dongxing again.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Di again gathered remnant masses and returned to raid Dongxing.

entries.zh: 世祖遣都督章昭達征迪，敷又從軍。
entries.en: Emperor Wen sent area commander Zhang Zhaoda against Di, and Fu marched again.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen sent Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against Di; Fu again followed the army.

entries.zh: 至定川縣，與迪相對。
entries.en: At Dingchuan county he faced Di across the line.
entries.literal: Reaching Dingchuan county, he faced Di across the line.

entries.zh: 迪紿敷曰：「吾昔與弟戮力同心，宗從匪他，豈規相害。
entries.en: Di tricked Fu, saying: "Once we fought side by side, you and I, as kin and not strangers. How could I mean you harm?
entries.literal: Di deceived Fu, saying: "Formerly I and you, my younger brother, strove together with one heart; we are clan kin and no others—how could I scheme to harm you?

entries.zh: 今願伏罪還朝，因弟披露心腑，先乞挺身共立盟誓。」
entries.en: Now I wish to confess and return to court. Through you, younger brother, I lay bare my heart. First let us stand together and swear an oath."
entries.literal: Now I wish to confess guilt and return to court; through you, younger brother, I disclose my inmost heart; first I beg to bare my body and stand together to swear an oath."

entries.zh: 敷許之，方登壇，為迪所害，時年三十五。
entries.en: Fu agreed. As he climbed the altar, Di killed him. He was thirty-five.
entries.literal: Fu agreed; as he was mounting the altar he was killed by Di, aged thirty-five.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「使持節、散騎常侍、都督南豫州緣江諸軍事、鎮南將軍、南豫州刺史西豐縣開國侯敷，受任遐征，淹時違律，虛衿姦詭，遂貽喪仆。
entries.en: An edict said: "Fu, credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies along the South Yu Yangzi bank, general who guards the south, inspector of South Yu, and Opening Marquis of Xifeng—sent on a distant campaign, he long broke discipline, opened his heart to treachery, and so met death in the field.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, area commander of all armies along the Yangzi bank of South Yu, general who guards the south, inspector of South Yu, Opening Marquis of Xifeng county Fu—charged with a distant expedition, he long disobeyed regulations, held an empty breast toward treacherous deceit, and so met death and fell.

entries.zh: [9]但夙著勤誠，亟勞戎旅，猶深惻愴，愍悼于懷。
entries.en: [9] Yet he had long shown loyal service and toil on campaign. We are still deeply moved and grieve in Our heart.
entries.literal: Yet from of old he showed loyal earnestness and repeatedly labored on campaign; We are still deeply moved to compassion and grieve in Our heart.

entries.zh: 可存其茅賦，量所賻卹，還葬京邑。」
entries.en: Let his fief be kept. Give funeral gifts as fitting and bring his body back for burial in the capital."
entries.literal: His feudal income may be preserved; measure out funeral gifts as due and return his body for burial in the capital."

entries.zh: 諡曰脫。
entries.en: Posthumous name Tuo.
entries.literal: Posthumous name Tuo.

entries.zh: 子智安嗣。
entries.en: His son Zhian succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Zhian succeeded.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，留異據東陽反，世祖召炅還都，欲令討異。
entries.en: In Tianjia year two Liu Yi rebelled at Dongyang; Emperor Wen recalled Jiong to the capital to lead the campaign against him.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, Liu Yi held Dongyang in rebellion; Emperor Wen summoned Jiong back to the capital, intending to have him campaign against Yi.

entries.zh: 未至而異平，炅還本鎮。
entries.en: Before he arrived, Yi had been suppressed, and Jiong returned to his post.
entries.literal: Before he arrived, Yi was pacified; Jiong returned to his original command.

entries.zh: 天康元年，預平華皎之功，授員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Tiankang year one he shared credit for suppressing Hua Jiao and was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he shared in the merit of pacifying Hua Jiao and was given Supernumerary Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 太建元年，遷持節、龍驤將軍、通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Taijian year one he was made bearer of the staff, dragon-prancing general, and courier direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Dragon-Prancing General, and Courier Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十三
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 13
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 13

entries.zh: 衡陽獻王昌字敬業，高祖第六子也。
entries.en: Chen Chang, Prince Xian of Hengyang, styled Jingye, was the Founder's sixth son.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang, courtesy name Jingye, was the Founder's sixth son.

entries.zh: 梁太清末，高祖南征李賁，命昌與宣后隨沈恪還吳興。
entries.en: In the last years of Liang's Taiqing era, Gaozu marched south against Li Ben and sent Chang and Empress Xuan back to Wuxing with Shen Ke.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era, Gaozu campaigned south against Li Ben and ordered Chang and Empress Xuan to return to Wuxing with Shen Ke.

entries.zh: 及高祖東討侯景，昌與宣后、世祖並為景所囚。
entries.en: When the Founder turned east against Hou Jing, Chang, Lady Xuan, and Emperor Wen were all taken prisoner by Jing.
entries.literal: When the Founder marched east against Hou Jing, Chang, Lady Xuan, and Emperor Wen were all imprisoned by Jing.

entries.zh: 景平，拜長城國世子、吳興太守，時年十六。
entries.en: After Jing's defeat he was made heir of the princedom of Changcheng and administrator of Wuxing, at age sixteen.
entries.literal: When Jing was suppressed, Chang was appointed Heir of the Princedom of Changcheng and Administrator of Wuxing, aged sixteen.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，頻遣使請高宗及昌，周人許之而未遣，及高祖崩，乃遣之。
entries.en: After Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly sent envoys asking Zhou to return Gaozong and Chang. Zhou agreed but held them back, sending them only after Gaozu died.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he repeatedly sent envoys requesting the return of Gaozong and Chang; the Zhou agreed but did not send them, and only after Gaozu died did they send them.

entries.zh: 是時王琳梗於中流，昌未得還，居于安陸。
entries.en: At the time Wang Lin blocked the river's middle course, so Chang could not return and remained at Anlu.
entries.literal: At this time Wang Lin obstructed the midstream, so Chang could not yet return and stayed at Anlu.

entries.zh: 王琳平後，天嘉元年二月，昌發自安陸，由魯山濟江，而巴陵王蕭沇等率百僚上表曰：
entries.en: After Wang Lin was defeated, in the second month of Tianjia year 1, Chang left Anlu and crossed the Yangzi by way of Lushan. Prince Xiao Yan of Baling and the officials then submitted this memorial:
entries.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, in the second month of Tianjia year 1, Chang set out from Anlu and crossed the river by way of Lushan, whereupon Prince Xiao Yan of Baling and the hundred officials led a memorial saying:

entries.zh: 昌容貌偉麗，神情秀朗，雅性聰辯，明習政事。
entries.en: Chang was tall and handsome, with a clear, spirited face; he was quick-witted and articulate and knew government affairs well.
entries.literal: Chang's appearance was grand and handsome, his bearing bright and open; by nature he was clever and eloquent and well versed in administration.

entries.zh: 高祖遣陳郡謝哲、濟陽蔡景歷輔昌為郡，又遣吳郡杜之偉授昌以經書。
entries.en: The Founder sent Xie Zhe of Chen and Cai Jingli of Jiyang to help him govern the commandery, and Du Zhiwei of Wu to teach him the classics.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Xie Zhe of Chen commandery and Cai Jingli of Jiyang to assist Chang in the commandery, and Du Zhiwei of Wu commandery to instruct him in the classics.

entries.zh: 昌讀書一覽便誦，明於義理，剖析如流。
entries.en: He could read a passage once and recite it from memory, grasp doctrine clearly, and argue through a point without hesitation.
entries.literal: Chang read a text once and could recite it; he understood principles clearly and reasoned with fluent penetration.

entries.zh: 尋與高宗俱往荊州，梁元帝除員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: He soon went to Jingzhou with Emperor Xuan; Emperor Yuan of Liang made him external regular attendant of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Soon he went to Jingzhou with Emperor Xuan; Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him External Regular Attendant of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，又與高宗俱遷關右，西魏以高祖故，甚禮之。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell he was moved with Emperor Xuan to the northwest; Western Wei honored him greatly for the Founder's sake.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou fell, he again moved with Emperor Xuan to the region west of the Pass; Western Wei treated him with great honor on the Founder's account.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下神猷光大，聖德欽明，道高日月，德侔造化。
entries.en: Your Majesty's divine plan shines far; your sacred virtue is revered and clear; your Way rises above sun and moon; your virtue equals heaven and earth.
entries.literal: We bow that Your Majesty's divine counsel shines broad, sacred virtue revered and bright, the Way towers above sun and moon, and virtue matches creation.

entries.zh: 往者王業惟始，天步方艱，參奉權謨，匡合義烈，威略外舉，神武內定，故以再康禹跡，大庇生民者矣。
entries.en: When the throne was first being won and the realm was still in peril, you shared in strategy and rallied men of honor; your power reached beyond the borders and your strength secured the court—so you twice restored the ancient order and sheltered the people.
entries.literal: In the past, when the royal enterprise had only begun and Heaven's course was still hard, you took part in counsel and joined righteous heroes; your martial prestige was shown abroad and divine might settled within—thus you twice restored Yu's traces and greatly sheltered the living people.

entries.zh: 及聖武升遐，王師遠次，皇嗣敻隔，繼業靡歸，宗祧危殆，綴旒非喻。
entries.en: When the sage martial emperor passed away, the royal army was far away; the heir was cut off and the succession unsettled; the ancestral temple trembled and the throne seemed all but lost.
entries.literal: When the Sage Martial ascended far away, the royal army halted in the distance; the imperial heir was cut off afar and succession had no home; the ancestral temple was in peril and the jade beads hung loose beyond compare.

entries.zh: 既而傳車言反，公卿定策，纂我洪基，光昭景運，民心有奉，園寢克寧，后來其蘇，復在茲日，物情天意，皎然可求。
entries.en: Then word came that the heir was returning, the ministers settled the succession, you took up the great foundation, and the bright age began; the people had a ruler, the tombs were safe, and renewal came on that day—men's hearts and Heaven's will alike were clear.
entries.literal: Then the relay carriage announced return, the ministers fixed the plan, you took our great foundation, and the bright fortune shone forth; the people's hearts had a lord, the imperial tombs were secure, and renewal came on this day—human feeling and Heaven's intent were plainly to be sought.

entries.zh: 王琳逆命，逋誅歲久，今者連結犬羊，乘流縱釁，舟旗野陣，綿江蔽陸，兵疲民弊，杼軸用空，中外騷然，蕃籬罔固。
entries.en: Wang Lin had long rebelled and escaped justice; now he joined with barbarian allies and struck along the rivers—fleets and banners filled the land, the Yangzi hidden and the shores covered; armies were exhausted, the people drained, and the realm was in uproar while the borders gave way.
entries.literal: Wang Lin defied the mandate and long evaded punishment; now he has joined with dogs and sheep, riding the current to loose calamity—boats and banners in wild array, the river covered and the land hidden; troops weary and the people spent, the loom shuttles empty; within and without in turmoil, the frontier screens had no hold.

entries.zh: 乃旰食當朝，憑流授律，蒼兕既馳，長蛇自翦，廓清四表，澄滌八紘，雄圖遐舉，仁聲遠暢，德化所覃，風行草偃，故以功深於微禹，道大於惟堯，豈直社稷用寧，斯乃黔黎是賴。
entries.en: You labored at court and sent armies down the rivers; once your forces moved, the rebel host collapsed; you cleared the four quarters and pacified the realm, your design reaching far and your kindness heard abroad; where your rule reached, men yielded like grass in wind—your merit outshone the saviors of old and your Way surpassed the sage kings; it was not only the state that was saved—the people leaned on you.
entries.literal: You then ate late at court and issued orders upon the current; the azure rhinoceros banner had already galloped forth and the long serpent cut itself down; the four quarters were cleared and the eight cords washed clean; your great design was raised afar and benevolent fame carried far; where virtue and transformation reached, the wind blew and grass bent—thus your merit was deeper than slight Yu's and your Way greater than sole Yao's; how could it be only the altars of soil and grain that were settled? The black-haired people likewise relied on you.

entries.zh: 南康愍王曇朗，高祖母弟忠壯王休先之子也。
entries.en: Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.
entries.literal: Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.

entries.zh: 休先少倜儻有大志，梁簡文之在東宮，深被知遇。
entries.en: Xiuxian was daring and ambitious in youth; when Emperor Jianwen of Liang was crown prince he won deep favor.
entries.literal: Xiuxian in youth was bold and free with great ambition; when Emperor Jianwen of Liang was in the eastern palace he was deeply favored.

entries.zh: 太清中既納侯景，有事北方，乃使休先召募得千餘人，授文德主帥，頃之卒。
entries.en: In the Taqing era, after Hou Jing was admitted and war moved north, he had Xiuxian raise more than a thousand men and made him commander of Wende; he died soon after.
entries.literal: In Taqing, after welcoming Hou Jing, with affairs in the north he had Xiuxian recruit over a thousand men and appointed him Commander of Wende; soon he died.

entries.zh: 高祖之有天下也，每稱休先曰：「此弟若存，河洛不足定也。」
entries.en: Once the Founder held the realm, he often said of Xiuxian: "If this brother had lived, the Yellow and Luo would not have been hard to recover."
entries.literal: When the Founder had the realm, he often said of Xiuxian: "If this younger brother had lived, settling the Yellow and Luo would not have been hard."

entries.zh: 梁敬帝即位，追贈侍中、使持節、驃騎將軍、南徐州刺史，封武康縣公，邑一千戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing of Liang came to the throne, Xiuxian was posthumously made palace attendant, bearer of the staff, general of agile cavalry, and inspector of South Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang with one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing of Liang took the throne, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wukang county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，追贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司徒，封南康郡王，邑二千戶，諡曰忠壯。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, he was posthumously made palace attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and grand tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang with two thousand households, and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
entries.literal: When the Founder accepted the abdication, he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery with two thousand households, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.

entries.zh: 齊果背約，復遣蕭軌等隨嗣徽渡江，高祖與戰，大破之，虜蕭軌、東方老等。
entries.en: Qi broke the treaty and sent Xiao Gui and others with Siwei across the Yangzi; the Founder defeated them heavily and took Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others prisoner.
entries.literal: Qi indeed broke the pact and again sent Xiao Gui and others to follow Siwei across the river; the Founder fought them and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, and others.

entries.zh: 齊人請割地并入馬牛以贖之，高祖不許。
entries.en: Qi offered to cede land and send horses and cattle as ransom; the Founder refused.
entries.literal: The Qi asked to cede territory and present horses and cattle to ransom them; the Founder would not agree.

entries.zh: 及軌等誅，齊人亦害曇朗于晉陽，時年二十八。
entries.en: When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight.
entries.literal: When Gui and the others were executed, the Qi also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; at the time year twenty-eight.

entries.zh: [3]是時既與齊絕，弗之知也。
entries.en: The court had already broken with Qi and did not yet know.
entries.literal: At the time, already broken with Qi, they did not know of it.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，猶以曇朗襲封南康郡王，奉忠壯王祀，禮秩一同皇子。
entries.en: When the Founder became emperor, he still had Tanlang recorded as Prince of Nankang to maintain Prince Zhongzhuang's sacrifices, with honors equal to an imperial prince.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he still had Tanlang succeed as Prince of Nankang commandery to maintain the sacrifices to Prince Zhongzhuang, his ritual rank the same as an imperial prince.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，齊人結好，方始知之。
entries.en: In Tianjia year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjia, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.

entries.zh: 世祖詔曰：「夫追遠慎終，抑聞前誥。
entries.en: Emperor Wen issued an edict: "To honor the dead and observe the last rites is an ancient teaching.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen issued an edict: "To honor the distant dead and be careful in the final rites—this we have heard in former instructions.

entries.zh: 南康王曇朗，明哲懋親，蕃維是屬，入質北齊，用紓時難。
entries.en: Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang was a worthy kinsman and a pillar of the realm; he went as hostage to Northern Qi to ease the crisis.
entries.literal: Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, wise and bright in his kinship, was the pillar of the frontier screens; he went as hostage to Northern Qi to ease the time's hardship.

entries.zh: 皇運兆興，未獲旋反，永言跂予，日夜不忘。
entries.en: The dynasty was rising and he had not returned; we longed for him day and night.
entries.literal: The imperial fortune was just rising and he did not yet return; we long looked for him day and night without forgetting.

entries.zh: 齊使始至，凶問奄及，追懷痛悼，兼倍常情，宜隆寵數，以光恆序。
entries.en: When Qi's envoys first came, word of his death arrived; our grief was beyond measure; let honors be raised to mark his place.
entries.literal: When Qi's envoys first arrived, the grievous news came suddenly; in recalling him our grief doubled beyond the common measure; grand favor should be raised to brighten the constant order.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、安東將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史，諡曰愍。」
entries.en: Posthumously appoint him palace attendant, general who pacifies the east, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of South Xuzhou; posthumous title Min."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of South Xuzhou; posthumous title Min."

entries.zh: 乃遣兼郎中令隨聘使江德藻、劉師知迎曇朗喪柩，以三年春至都。
entries.en: He sent the acting director of the palace secretariat, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi, with the embassy to bring Tanlang's coffin home; it reached the capital in spring of year three.
entries.literal: Then he dispatched the acting director of the palace secretariat, together with the envoys on the mission, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi, to meet Tanlang's bier; in spring of year three it reached the capital.

entries.zh: 二年，徐嗣徽、任約引齊寇攻逼京邑，尋而請和，求高祖子姪為質。
entries.en: In year two, Xu Siwei and Ren Yue brought Qi armies against the capital; they then sought peace and demanded the Founder's sons and nephews as hostages.
entries.literal: In year two, Xu Siwei and Ren Yue led Qi invaders to press the capital; they soon sued for peace and asked for the Founder's sons and nephews as hostages.

entries.zh: 時四方州郡並多未賓，京都虛弱，糧運不斷，在朝文武咸願與齊和親，高祖難之，而重違眾議，乃言於朝曰：「孤謬輔王室，而使蠻夷猾夏，不能戡殄，何所逃責。
entries.en: Many provinces had not yet submitted, the capital was weak, and grain transport remained open; court officials all favored peace with Qi, and the Founder was torn—but he could not easily defy them. He told the assembly: "I have poorly served the dynasty and let barbarians ravage the realm without destroying them—how can I escape blame?
entries.literal: At the time many commanderies and districts had not yet submitted, the capital was weak, and grain transport had not been cut off; civil and military officials at court all wished to make peace with Qi, and the Founder found it hard—but he also could not lightly go against the assembly; he then spoke in court, saying: "I wrongly aided the royal house and let barbarians run riot in Xia, unable to destroy them—where can I escape blame?

entries.zh: 今在位諸賢，且欲息肩偃武，與齊和好，以靜邊疆，若違眾議，必謂孤惜子姪，今決遣曇朗，棄之寇庭。
entries.en: You wish to rest and make peace with Qi to quiet the borders; if I refuse, you will say I spare my kin—today I will send Tanlang and abandon him to the enemy.
entries.literal: Now the worthies in office wish to rest shoulders and lay down arms, make peace with Qi, and quiet the frontier; if I go against the assembly, they will surely say I spare my sons and nephews—today I resolve to send Tanlang and abandon him in the enemy court.

entries.zh: 且齊人無信，窺窬不已，謂我浸弱，必當背盟。
entries.en: The Qi are faithless and will not stop their scheming; seeing us weaken, they will surely break the treaty.
entries.literal: Moreover the Qi are faithless and their coveting does not cease; seeing us weaken day by day, they will surely break the pact.

entries.zh: 齊寇若來，諸君須為孤力鬥也。」
entries.en: If the Qi attack again, you must fight for me with all your strength."
entries.literal: If Qi invaders come, you gentlemen must fight hard for me."

entries.zh: 高祖慮曇朗憚行，或奔竄東道，乃自率步騎往京口迎之，以曇朗還京師，仍使為質於齊。
entries.en: The Founder feared Tanlang would refuse or flee east; he went in person with troops to Jingkou to fetch him, brought him back to the capital, and then sent him to Qi as a hostage.
entries.literal: The Founder feared Tanlang would dread the journey or flee east along the road; he himself led foot and horse to Jingkou to meet him, brought Tanlang back to the capital, and then sent him as hostage to Qi.

entries.zh: 曇朗少孤，尤為高祖所愛，寵踰諸子。
entries.en: Tanlang was orphaned young, and Gaozu loved him especially, favoring him even more than his own sons.
entries.literal: Tanlang lost his father young, was especially loved by Gaozu, and was favored beyond the other sons.

entries.zh: 有膽力，善綏御。
entries.en: He was brave and forceful, and good at calming and directing men.
entries.literal: He had courage and strength, and was good at pacifying and managing people.

entries.zh: 侯景平後，起家為著作佐郎。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was defeated, he entered service as assistant editorial director.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, he began his career as assistant editorial director.

entries.zh: 高祖北濟江，圍廣陵，宿預人東方光據鄉建義，乃遣曇朗與杜僧明自淮入泗應赴之。
entries.en: When Gaozu crossed north of the Yangzi and besieged Guangling, Dongfang Guang of Suyu raised a loyal force in his home district. Gaozu sent Tanlang and Du Sengming from the Huai into the Si River region to support him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu crossed north over the river and besieged Guangling, Dongfang Guang of Suyu occupied his home district and raised a righteous force, so Gaozu sent Tanlang and Du Sengming from the Huai into the Si to respond to him.

entries.zh: 齊援大至，曇朗與僧明築壘抗禦。
entries.en: When Qi reinforcements arrived in force, Tanlang and Sengming built forts and held them off.
entries.literal: Qi reinforcements arrived in great numbers, and Tanlang and Sengming built fortifications and resisted them.

entries.zh: 尋奉命班師，以宿預義軍三萬家濟江。
entries.en: Soon ordered to withdraw, he brought thirty thousand Suyu loyalist households across the Yangzi.
entries.literal: Soon he received orders to withdraw the army and brought thirty thousand households of the Suyu loyalist army across the river.

entries.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，留曇朗鎮京口，知留府事。
entries.en: After Gaozu killed Wang Sengbian, he left Tanlang at Jingkou to command the garrison and manage the rear headquarters.
entries.literal: When Gaozu executed Wang Sengbian, he left Tanlang to garrison Jingkou and oversee the affairs of the remaining headquarters.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，除中書侍郎，監南徐州。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 1 he was made attendant in the Secretariat and put in charge of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In Shaotai year 1, he was appointed Secretariat attendant and supervisor of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 四月庚寅，喪柩至京師，上親出臨哭。
entries.en: On gengyin day in the fourth month the coffin reached the capital; the emperor went out in person to mourn.
entries.literal: On gengyin day of the fourth month the bier reached the capital; the emperor went out in person to mourn and weep.

entries.zh: 乃下詔曰：「夫寵章所以嘉德，禮數所以崇親，乃歷代之通規，固前王之令典。
entries.en: An edict followed: "Honors reward virtue, and ritual exalts kin—this has been the rule of every age and the law of former kings.
entries.literal: Then an edict was issued: "Favor and insignia are meant to honor virtue, and ritual is meant to exalt kin—these are the constant rules of successive ages and the fixed statutes of former kings.

entries.zh: 新除使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、湘州牧衡陽王昌，明哲在躬，珪璋早秀，孝敬內湛，聰睿外宣。
entries.en: Chen Chang, newly made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of armies in Xiangzhou, general of agile cavalry, and governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Hengyang, was wise in himself and gifted from youth, inwardly filial and outwardly sharp.
entries.literal: The newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Xiangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Xiangzhou, Prince of Hengyang Chen Chang, had wisdom present in his person and jade and regalia early in bloom; filial reverence steeped within, keen insight shown without.

entries.zh: 梁季艱虞，宗社顛墜，西京淪覆，陷身關隴。
entries.en: In Liang's troubled years the dynasty fell; the western capital was lost and he was held captive in the northwest.
entries.literal: In Liang's years of hardship the altars toppled; the western capital was lost and he was trapped in the passes of Guan and Long.

entries.zh: 及鼎業初基，外蕃逆命，聘問斯阻，音介莫通，睠彼機橋，將鄰烏白。
entries.en: When the Chen house first rose, the frontiers were closed to us; no envoy could reach him and no word come through; we thought of him far away, almost beyond return.
entries.literal: When the great enterprise was first founded, outer regions defied the mandate; envoys were blocked and messages could not pass; we looked on that distant bridge, nearly bordering the crows of dusk.

entries.zh: 今者群公戮力，多難廓清，輕傳入郛，無勞假道。
entries.en: Now that the ministers have joined their strength and the realm is pacified, he could come home without asking leave of any foe.
entries.literal: Now the ministers have joined their strength and many hardships are cleared; light carriages enter the walls without need to borrow a road.

entries.zh: 周朝敦其繼好，驂駕歸來，欣此朝聞，庶歡昏定。
entries.en: Zhou once welcomed a kinsman home from captivity; we rejoiced to hear he was coming and hoped at last to see him again.
entries.literal: The Zhou court honored renewed kinship and the paired horses returned; we rejoice at this morning's news and hope for the evening's comfort of his presence.

entries.zh: 報施徒語，曾莫輔仁，人之云亡，殄悴斯在，奄焉薨殞，倍增傷悼。
entries.en: Heaven repaid him only with words, not with years; now he is gone and our grief is doubled.
entries.literal: Repayment of kindness was only words—he never aided our virtue; when a man is gone, the wasting grief is here; suddenly he died and our mourning redoubled.

entries.zh: 津門之慟空在，恆岫之切不追，靜言念之，心焉如割。
entries.en: We grieve at the river where he died, but cannot follow him to his grave; to think of it is to feel the heart torn.
entries.literal: The grief at the ford gate is empty; the longing for Mount Heng cannot be pursued; speaking of it in silence, the heart is as if cut apart.

entries.zh: 宜隆懋典，以協徽猷。
entries.en: Let great honors be granted to match his worth.
entries.literal: Grand honors should be raised to match his bright merit.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、太宰、揚州牧。
entries.en: Posthumously appoint him palace attendant, grant the yellow battle-axe, make him commander of all armies at court and in the field, grand tutor, and governor of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, given the yellow battle-axe, made Area Commander over All Military Affairs within and without, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 給東園溫明祕器，九旒鑾輅，黃屋左纛，武賁班劍百人，[2]轀輬車，前後部羽葆鼓吹。
entries.en: Grant the Eastern Garden burial regalia, the nine-tasseled carriage and imperial equipage, a hundred halberd guards, [2] the funeral carriage, and front and rear guards with drums and pipes.
entries.literal: Grant the warm-bright secret vessels of the Eastern Garden, the nine tassels and imperial carriage, the yellow canopy and left banner, a hundred tiger-guard halberd-bearers, [2] the encoffining carriage, and front and rear guards with feather fans, drums, and pipes.

entries.zh: 葬送之儀，一依漢東平憲王、齊豫章文獻王故事。
entries.en: Burial and escort shall follow the precedents of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping and the Qi Prince Wen of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: The rites of burial and escort shall wholly follow the precedents of the Han Prince Xian of Dongping and the Qi Prince Wen of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 仍遣大司空持節迎護喪事，大鴻臚副其羽衛，殯送所須，隨由備辦。」
entries.en: Send the grand minister of works with the staff to receive the coffin; let the grand herald assist with the guard; provide everything needed for the funeral along the route."
entries.literal: Still dispatch the Grand Minister of Works, bearer of the staff, to meet and escort the funeral; the Grand Herald shall assist with the guard of feathers; whatever the bier and escort require shall be fully provided along the way."

entries.zh: 諡曰獻。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Xian.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Xian.

entries.zh: 無子，世祖以第七皇子伯信為嗣。
entries.en: He left no sons; Emperor Wen made his seventh son Boxin his heir.
entries.literal: He had no sons; Emperor Wen made his seventh son Boxin heir.

entries.zh: 方泰少麤獷，與諸惡少年群聚，遊逸無度，世祖以南康王故，特寬貰之。
entries.en: Fangtai was coarse and unruly from youth, running with bad company and living without restraint; because of Prince Tanlang of Nankang, Emperor Wen especially spared him.
entries.literal: Fangtai in youth was rough and reckless; he gathered with wicked young men and roamed without limit; because of the Prince of Nankang, Emperor Wen especially indulged him.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，詔曰：「南康王曇朗，出隔齊庭，反身莫測，國廟方修，奠饗須主，可以長男方泰為南康世子，嗣南康王。」
entries.en: In Tianjia year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."

entries.zh: 後聞曇朗薨，於是襲爵南康嗣王。
entries.en: When word came that Tanlang had died, Fangtai succeeded as Prince of Nankang.
entries.literal: Later they heard Tanlang had died; thereupon he succeeded to the title of Prince of Nankang.

entries.zh: 尋為仁威將軍、丹陽尹，置佐史。
entries.en: He was soon made general of benevolent might and administrator of Danyang, with a full staff.
entries.literal: Soon he was made General of Benevolent Might and Administrator of Danyang, with staff officers appointed.

entries.zh: 太建四年，遷使持節、都督廣衡交越成定明新合羅德宜黃利安建石崖十九州諸軍事、[4]平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: In Taijian year four he was made bearer of the staff and commander of armies in nineteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, and Shiya, [4] general who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff and Area Commander over Military Affairs in the nineteen provinces of Guang, Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Ming, Xin, He, Luo, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Jian, Shiya, and others, [4] General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 為政殘暴，為有司所奏，免官。
entries.en: He governed with cruelty; the authorities reported him and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: His government was cruel and violent; the responsible offices memorialized against him and he was removed from office.

entries.zh: 尋起為仁威將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: He was soon restored as general of benevolent might with a staff.
entries.literal: Soon he was reappointed General of Benevolent Might, with staff officers appointed.

entries.zh: 六年，授持節、都督豫章郡諸軍事、豫章內史。
entries.en: In year six he received the staff and was made commander of armies in Yuzhang and interior magistrate of the commandery.
entries.literal: In year six he was given the staff and made Area Commander over Military Affairs in Yuzhang commandery and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 在郡不修民事，秩滿之際，屢放部曲為劫，又縱火延燒邑居，因行暴掠，驅錄富人，徵求財賄。
entries.en: In office he neglected the people; as his term ended he sent retainers to rob, set fires that burned towns, and plundered openly, seizing the wealthy and extorting bribes.
entries.literal: In the commandery he did not attend to the people's affairs; as his term neared its end he repeatedly sent his retainers out to rob, and also set fires that spread through the towns, then went about violent plunder, seizing and registering the rich and extorting wealth.

entries.zh: 代至，又淹留不還。
entries.en: When his successor arrived he lingered and would not leave.
entries.literal: When his replacement arrived, he still detained himself and would not return.

entries.zh: 至都，詔以為宗正卿，將軍、佐史如故。
entries.en: At the capital an edict made him director of the imperial clan, keeping his general's rank and staff.
entries.literal: On reaching the capital, an edict made him Director of the Imperial Clan, his general's title and staff unchanged.

entries.zh: 未拜，為御史中丞宗元饒所劾，免官，以王還第。
entries.en: Before he took office the censor-in-chief Zong Yuanrao impeached him; he was dismissed and sent back to his princely residence.
entries.literal: Before he took up the post, he was impeached by the censor-in-chief Zong Yuanrao, removed from office, and sent to his princely residence as a prince only.

entries.zh: 臣聞宗子維城，隆周之懋軌，封建藩屏，有漢之弘規，是以卜世斯永，寔資邢、衛，[1]鼎命靈長，實賴河、楚。
entries.en: We have heard that kinsmen of the royal house buttress the state, as in glorious Zhou, and that enfeoffing princes to guard the borders was Han's great design; lasting rule truly drew on domains such as Xing and Wei, [1] and the mandate's endurance truly rested on great regions such as the He River lands and Chu.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that imperial sons shore up the realm—the glorious standard of elevated Zhou—and that enfeoffed domains as screens was Han's grand rule; thus the dynasty's endurance truly relied on Xing and Wei, [1] and the sacred mandate's longevity truly depended on the lands of the He and Chu.

entries.zh: 第六皇弟昌，近以妙年出質，提契寇手，偏隔關徼，旋踵末由。
entries.en: Your sixth brother Chang was sent north as a hostage while still young; he fell into enemy hands and was cut off beyond the passes, unable to come home.
entries.literal: The sixth imperial younger brother Chang, recently sent as hostage in his prime years, fell into the enemy's grasp, cut off beyond the frontier passes, unable to return in a turn of the heel.

entries.zh: 陛下天倫之愛既深，克讓之懷常切。
entries.en: Your love for your kin runs deep, and you have long wished to yield your own desire.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's love within the heavenly bonds is already deep, and your constant thought is yielding virtue.

entries.zh: 伏以大德無私，至公有在，豈得徇匹夫之恆情，忘王業之大計。
entries.en: Great virtue knows no private favor, and supreme justice must prevail—how can private feeling outweigh the needs of the throne?
entries.literal: We submit that great virtue is without selfishness and supreme fairness is ever present—how can one indulge a common man's constant feelings and forget the royal enterprise's great plan?

entries.zh: 憲章故實，式遵典禮，欽若姬、漢，建樹賢戚。
entries.en: Follow ancient precedent, observe the rites, and as Zhou and Han did, enfeoff worthy kinsmen.
entries.literal: Take the old precedents as law, follow the ritual canon in form, emulate Zhou and Han, and establish worthy kin.

entries.zh: 湘中地維形勝，控帶川阜，扞城之寄，匪親勿居，宜啟服衡疑，兼崇徽飾。
entries.en: Xiang province is a strategic land of rivers and hills; only a kinsman should hold its defense; let him take Hengyang and receive the honors due a prince.
entries.literal: The Xiang region's terrain is strategically vital and commands rivers and hills; the charge of guarding the wall none but kin should hold; he should open his fief at Heng and Yi and likewise receive lofty insignia.

entries.zh: 臣等參議，以昌為使持節、散騎常侍、都督湘州諸軍事、驃騎將軍、湘州牧，封衡陽郡王，邑五千戶，加給皁輪三望車，後部鼓吹一部，班劍二十人。
entries.en: We propose that Chang be made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander of armies in Xiangzhou, general of agile cavalry, and governor of Xiangzhou; that he be enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang with five thousand households; and that he receive a black carriage with triple canopy, a guard of drums and pipes, and twenty halberd escorts.
entries.literal: We your servants jointly propose that Chang be made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in Xiangzhou, General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Xiangzhou; that he be enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang commandery with a fief of five thousand households; and that there be added a black-wheeled carriage with three canopy poles, a rear guard of drums and pipes, and twenty halberd-bearers.

entries.zh: 啟可奉行。
entries.en: Let this memorial be carried out.
entries.literal: The memorial may be executed.

entries.zh: 禎明三年，隋師濟江，東衡州刺史王勇遣高州刺史戴智烈將五百騎迎方慶，[8]欲令承制總督征討諸軍事。
entries.en: In Zhenming year three, as Sui crossed the Yangzi, Eastern Hengzhou inspector Wang Yong sent Gaozhou inspector Dai Zhilie with five hundred horsemen to fetch Fangqing, [8] planning to put him at the head of all southern armies.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, Sui forces crossed the Yangzi; Eastern Hengzhou Inspector Wang Yong sent Dai Zhilie, Inspector of Gaozhou, with five hundred cavalry to welcome Fangqing, [8] intending to have him take emergency command as overall commander of the armies for suppression and attack.

entries.zh: 是時隋行軍總管韋洸帥兵度嶺，宣隋文帝敕云：「若嶺南平定，留勇與豐州刺史鄭萬頃且依舊職。」
entries.en: Sui commander Wei Guang then crossed the mountains and proclaimed an edict from Emperor Wen of Sui: "If Lingnan is pacified, Yong and Fengzhou inspector Zheng Wanqing shall remain in their former posts."
entries.literal: At that time Sui's campaign commander Wei Guang led troops across the ranges and proclaimed an edict of Emperor Wen of Sui, saying: "If Lingnan is pacified, Yong and Zheng Wanqing, Inspector of Fengzhou, are to remain in their former posts."

entries.zh: 方慶聞之，恐勇賣己，乃不從，率兵以拒智烈。
entries.en: Fangqing feared Yong meant to betray him, refused, and marched against Zhilie.
entries.literal: When Fangqing heard this, he feared Yong would sell him out; he would not obey and led troops to resist Zhilie.

entries.zh: 智烈與戰，敗之，斬方慶於廣州，虜其妻子。
entries.en: Zhilie defeated him, killed Fangqing at Guangzhou, and took his family prisoner.
entries.literal: Zhilie fought him, defeated him, beheaded Fangqing at Guangzhou, and captured his wife and children.

entries.zh: 初，萬頃之在周，深被隋文帝知遇，及隋文踐祚，常思還北。
entries.en: In Zhou he had been close to the future Sui founder; once Sui was founded he often wished to return north.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wanqing was in Zhou, he was deeply favored by Emperor Wen of Sui; when Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he often thought of returning north.

entries.zh: 及王勇之殺方慶，萬頃乃率州兵拒勇，遣使由間道降于隋軍。
entries.en: After Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing marched against him and sent envoys by a hidden route to surrender to Sui.
entries.literal: When Yong killed Fangqing, Wanqing thereupon led the provincial troops to resist Yong and sent envoys by a secret route to surrender to the Sui army.

entries.zh: 拜上儀同，尋卒。
entries.en: Sui made him a senior dignitary of the first rank; he died soon after.
entries.literal: He was appointed Senior Dignitary of the First Rank; soon he died.

entries.zh: 鄭萬頃，滎陽人，梁司州刺史紹叔之族子也。
entries.en: Zheng Wanqing of Xingyang was a kinsman of Liang's Sizhou inspector Zheng Shaoshu.
entries.literal: Zheng Wanqing was a man of Xingyang, a clansman of Zheng Shaoshu, Inspector of Sizhou in Liang.

entries.zh: 父旻，梁末入魏。
entries.en: His father Min went over to Northern Wei at the end of Liang.
entries.literal: His father Min entered Wei at the end of Liang.

entries.zh: 萬頃通達有材幹，周武帝時為司城大夫，出為溫州刺史。
entries.en: Wanqing was talented and capable; under Zhou Emperor Wu he was metropolitan construction officer and later inspector of Wenzhou.
entries.literal: Wanqing was penetrating and capable; under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Metropolitan Construction Officer and went out as Inspector of Wenzhou.

entries.zh: 至德中，與司馬消難來奔。
entries.en: In the Zhide era he defected to Chen with Sima Xiaonan.
entries.literal: In the Zhide era he came to Chen together with Sima Xiaonan.

entries.zh: 尋拜散騎常侍、昭武將軍、豐州刺史。
entries.en: He was soon made regular attendant, general who manifests martiality, and inspector of Fengzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, General Who Manifests Martiality, and Inspector of Fengzhou.

entries.zh: 在州甚有惠政，吏民表請立碑，詔許焉。
entries.en: He governed Fengzhou with real kindness; the people petitioned for a commemorative stele and the court agreed.
entries.literal: In the province he had very benevolent government; officials and people memorialized requesting a stele, and an edict approved it.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十四
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 14
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 14

entries.zh: 陳擬字公正，高祖疏屬也。
entries.en: Chen Ni, whose style name was Gongzheng, belonged to the Founder's collateral line.
entries.literal: Chen Ni, styled Gongzheng, was a distant kinsman of the Founder.

entries.zh: 少孤貧，性質直彊記。
entries.en: He lost his parents early and grew up in poverty, yet he was upright by nature and possessed an exceptional memory.
entries.literal: Orphaned young and poor, by nature he was upright and had a powerful memory.

entries.zh: 高祖南征交趾，擬從焉。
entries.en: When the Founder marched south against Jiaozhi, Ni accompanied the expedition.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned south against Jiaozhi, Ni followed him.

entries.zh: 又進討侯景，至豫章，以擬為羅州刺史，與胡穎共知後事，並應接軍糧。
entries.en: On the later campaign against Hou Jing, when the army reached Yuzhang, the Founder made Ni prefect of Luozhou and paired him with Hu Ying to handle rear-area administration and the supply of grain to the troops.
entries.literal: Again he advanced to attack Hou Jing; reaching Yuzhang, he appointed Ni Prefect of Luozhou, together with Hu Ying to manage rear affairs and likewise to provision the army.

entries.zh: 高祖作鎮朱方，擬除步兵校尉、曲阿令。
entries.en: After the Founder established his headquarters at Zhufang, Ni was appointed commandant of footsoldiers and magistrate of Qu'e.
entries.literal: When the Founder established his base at Zhufang, Ni was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and Magistrate of Qu'e.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，授貞威將軍、義興太守。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai he received the rank of General of Upright Prestige and was made administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai, he was granted the title General of Upright Prestige and appointed Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 二年，入知衛尉事，除員外散騎常侍、明威將軍、雍州刺史，資監南徐州。
entries.en: In the second year he took charge of affairs in the Ministry of Guards and was appointed supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, general of illustrious prestige, and prefect of Yongzhou, with supervisory authority over Southern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year, he entered service managing the Ministry of Guards; he was appointed Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Illustrious Prestige, and Prefect of Yongzhou, with supervisory duties over Southern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，詔曰：「維城宗子，實固有周，盤石懿親，用隆大漢，故會盟則異姓為後，啟土則非劉勿王，所以糾合枝幹，廣樹蕃屏，前王懋典，列代恆規。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, an edict declared: 'Royal kinsmen who buttress the realm were the true foundation of Zhou; steadfast, rock-like relatives were what raised Han to greatness. At covenant assemblies collateral houses took second place; when fiefs were opened, none but the house of Liu could be made kings. By such means trunk and branch were bound together and a broad screen of feudal lords set up—an earnest canon of former kings and a constant rule of every age.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, an edict said: 'Kinsmen who hold the realm are the true foundation of Zhou; staunch stone kinsmen raised Han on high. Therefore at covenant assemblies collateral lineages stood second, and when lands were granted, only Liu could be enfeoffed. Thus branches and trunks were joined, and broad screens of feudatories erected—an ancient king's solemn canon, a constant rule of every age.

entries.zh: 從子持節、員外散騎常侍、明威將軍、雍州刺史、監南徐州擬，持節、通直散騎侍郎、貞威將軍、北徐州刺史褒，從子晃、炅，從孫假節、員外散騎常侍、明威將軍訬，假節、信威將軍、北徐州刺史吉陽縣開國侯諠，假節、通直散騎侍郎、信武將軍祏，[1]假節、散騎侍郎、雄信將軍、青州刺史、廣梁太守詳，貞威將軍、通直散騎侍郎慧紀，從孫敬雅、敬泰，並枝戚密近，劬勞王室，宜列河山，以光利建。
entries.en: His nephew Ni, holder of the staff, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, general of illustrious prestige, prefect of Yongzhou, and supervisor of Southern Xuzhou; Bao, holder of the staff, palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, general of upright prestige, and prefect of Northern Xuzhou; the nephews Huang and Jiong; the great-nephew Xu, acting holder of the staff, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, and general of illustrious prestige; Xuan, acting holder of the staff, general of trustworthy prestige, prefect of Northern Xuzhou, and marquis of Jiyang county; Zhi, acting holder of the staff, palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, and general of trustworthy martiality;[1] Xiang, acting holder of the staff, palace gentleman of the scattered cavalry, general of majestic trust, prefect of Qingzhou, and administrator of Guangliang; Huiji, general of upright prestige and palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry; and the great-nephews Jingya and Jingtai—all close collateral kin who have labored for the royal house—should be granted domains upon the rivers and mountains to honor the founding of the dynasty.
entries.literal: The Founder's nephew, Holder of the Staff, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Illustrious Prestige, Prefect of Yongzhou, and Supervisor of Southern Xuzhou, Ni; the Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Upright Prestige, and Prefect of Northern Xuzhou, Bao; the nephews Huang and Jiong; the great-nephew, Acting Holder of the Staff, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and General of Illustrious Prestige, Xu; the Acting Holder of the Staff, General of Trustworthy Prestige, Prefect of Northern Xuzhou, and Marquis of Jiyang County, Xuan; the Acting Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, and General of Trustworthy Martiality, Zhi;[1] the Acting Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Majestic Trust, Prefect of Qingzhou, and Administrator of Guangliang, Xiang; General of Upright Prestige and Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, Huiji; and the great-nephews Jingya and Jingtai—all collateral kin of close degree who have toiled for the royal house—ought to be arrayed among the rivers and mountains to brighten the founding of the state.

entries.zh: 擬可永脩縣開國侯，褒鍾陵縣開國侯，晃建城縣開國侯，炅上饒縣開國侯，訬虔化縣開國侯，諠仍前封，祏豫章縣開國侯，[2]詳遂興縣開國侯，慧紀宜黃縣開國侯，敬雅寧都縣開國侯，敬泰平固縣開國侯，各邑五百戶。」
entries.en: Ni was to be made marquis of Yongxiu county; Bao, marquis of Zhongling county; Huang, marquis of Jiancheng county; Jiong, marquis of Shangrao county; Xu, marquis of Qianhua county; Xuan was to retain his previous title; Zhi, marquis of Yuzhang county;[2] Xiang, marquis of Suixing county; Huiji, marquis of Yihuang county; Jingya, marquis of Ningdu county; and Jingtai, marquis of Pinggu county—each with a fief of five hundred households.'
entries.literal: Ni may be made Marquis of Yongxiu County; Bao, Marquis of Zhongling County; Huang, Marquis of Jiancheng County; Jiong, Marquis of Shangrao County; Xu, Marquis of Qianhua County; Xuan, his former enfeoffment to remain; Zhi, Marquis of Yuzhang County;[2] Xiang, Marquis of Suixing County; Huiji, Marquis of Yihuang County; Jingya, Marquis of Ningdu County; Jingtai, Marquis of Pinggu County—each with a fief of five hundred households.'

entries.zh: 擬尋除輕車將軍，兼南徐州刺史，常侍如故。
entries.en: Shortly afterward Ni was appointed general of the light chariots and concurrently prefect of Southern Xuzhou, while retaining his attendant post.
entries.literal: Ni was soon appointed General of the Light Chariots and concurrently Prefect of Southern Xuzhou, his attendant post remaining as before.

entries.zh: 其年，授通直散騎常侍、中領軍。
entries.en: That same year he received the rank of attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry and was made central commander of the army.
entries.literal: That year he was granted the title Attendant-in-Ordinary of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Central Commander of the Army.

entries.zh: 三年，復以本官監南徐州。
entries.en: In the third year he again exercised supervisory authority over Southern Xuzhou in his existing capacity.
entries.literal: In the third year, he again supervised Southern Xuzhou in his former capacity.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，除丹陽尹，常侍如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Ni was appointed intendant of Danyang while retaining his attendant rank.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Ni was appointed Intendant of Danyang, his attendant post remaining as before.

entries.zh: 坐事，又以白衣知郡，尋復本職。
entries.en: After an offense he was stripped of rank yet continued to administer the commandery as a commoner; before long he was restored to his former office.
entries.literal: Because of an offense he was again made to administer the commandery in commoner's dress; before long he was restored to his former post.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年卒，時年五十八。
entries.en: He died in the first year of Tianjia, at the age of fifty-eight.
entries.literal: He died in the first year of Tianjia, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 贈領軍將軍，凶事所須，並官資給。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as general of the palace guard, and all expenses of the funeral were met from official funds.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the title General of the Palace Guard; all requirements of the funeral were supplied by the state.

entries.zh: 諡曰定。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Ding.
entries.literal: His posthumous name was Ding.

entries.zh: 二年，配享高祖廟廷。
entries.en: In the second year he was granted a place of sacrifice in the Founder's ancestral temple.
entries.literal: In the second year he was given a place in the Founder's temple hall.

entries.zh: 子黨嗣。
entries.en: His son Dang succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Dang succeeded.

entries.zh: 陳詳字文幾，少出家為桑門。
entries.en: Chen Xiang, whose style name was Wenji, entered the Buddhist clergy in his youth.
entries.literal: Chen Xiang, styled Wenji, left home young and became a Buddhist monk.

entries.zh: 善書記，談論清雅。
entries.en: He was adept at record-keeping and spoke with refined, elegant ease.
entries.literal: He was skilled at clerical work and his conversation was refined and elegant.

entries.zh: 高祖討侯景，召詳，令反初服，配以兵馬，從定京邑。
entries.en: When the Founder marched against Hou Jing, he summoned Xiang, had him lay aside his monastic robes, supplied him with troops and horses, and Xiang followed the campaign that pacified the capital.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Hou Jing, he summoned Xiang, ordered him to return to secular dress, furnished him with troops and horses, and he followed in pacifying the capital region.

entries.zh: 高祖東征杜龕，詳別下安吉、原鄉、故鄣三縣。
entries.en: On the Founder's eastern campaign against Du Kan, Xiang detached a force and reduced the three counties of Anji, Yuanxiang, and Gucheng.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned east against Du Kan, Xiang separately subdued the three counties of Anji, Yuanxiang, and Gucheng.

entries.zh: 龕平，以功授散騎侍郎、假節、雄信將軍、青州刺史，資割故鄣、廣德置廣梁郡，以詳為太守。
entries.en: After Kan's defeat, Xiang was rewarded with the posts of palace gentleman of the scattered cavalry, acting holder of the staff, general of majestic trust, and prefect of Qingzhou; the districts of Gucheng and Guangde were detached to form Guangliang commandery, of which he was made administrator.
entries.literal: When Kan was pacified, for his merit he was granted the title Palace Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, Acting Holder of the Staff, General of Majestic Trust, and Prefect of Qingzhou; Gucheng and Guangde were carved off to establish Guangliang Commandery, and Xiang was made its Administrator.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，改廣梁為陳留，又以為陳留太守。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Guangliang was renamed Chenliu, and Xiang continued as administrator of Chenliu.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, Guangliang was renamed Chenliu, and Xiang was again made Administrator of Chenliu.

entries.zh: 永定二年，封遂興縣侯，食邑五百戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongding he was enfeoffed as marquis of Suixing county with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Suixing County with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 其年除明威將軍、通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: That same year he was appointed general of illustrious prestige and attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: That year he was appointed General of Illustrious Prestige and Attendant-in-Ordinary of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 三年，隨侯安都破王琳將常眾愛於宮亭湖。
entries.en: In the third year he followed Hou Andu in defeating Wang Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai at Gongting Lake.
entries.literal: In the third year he followed Hou Andu in defeating Wang Lin's general Chang Zhong'ai at Gongting Lake.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，除宣城太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Xiang was made administrator of Xuancheng while retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Xiang was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng, his general's rank remaining as before.

entries.zh: 王琳下據柵口，詳隨吳明徹襲湓城，取琳家口，不克，因入南湖，自鄱陽步道而歸。
entries.en: When Wang Lin moved downriver and seized Zhakou, Xiang followed Wu Mingche in a surprise attack on Pencheng to capture Lin's family, but the assault failed; he then entered South Lake and made his way back overland from Poyang.
entries.literal: Wang Lin descended and held Zhakou; Xiang followed Wu Mingche in a raid on Pencheng to seize Lin's family dependents, but did not succeed; he therefore entered South Lake and returned by the land route from Poyang.

entries.zh: 琳平，詳與明徹並無功。
entries.en: When Lin was finally defeated, neither Xiang nor Mingche received credit for the victory.
entries.literal: When Lin was pacified, neither Xiang nor Mingche received merit.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，隨例增邑并前一千五百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia his fief was enlarged by precedent, bringing the total to one thousand five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, following precedent his fief was increased, bringing the total to one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍除通直散騎常侍，兼右衛將軍。
entries.en: He was then appointed attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry and concurrently general of the right guard.
entries.literal: He was then appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 三年，出為假節、都督吳州諸軍事、仁威將軍、吳州刺史。
entries.en: In the third year he was sent out as acting holder of the staff, commander-in-chief of all military affairs of Wuzhou, general of humane prestige, and prefect of Wuzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year he went out as Acting Holder of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Wuzhou, General of Humane Prestige, and Prefect of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 陳慧紀字元方，高祖之從孫也。
entries.en: Chen Huiji, whose style name was Yuanfang, was a grandnephew of the Founder on the collateral line.
entries.literal: Chen Huiji, styled Yuanfang, was a great-grandson of the Founder on the collateral line.

entries.zh: 涉獵書史，負才任氣。
entries.en: He read widely in the histories and relied on his talents with a proud, headstrong temper.
entries.literal: He ranged widely through books and histories and relied on his talent with an arrogant spirit.

entries.zh: 高祖平侯景，慧紀從焉。
entries.en: When the Founder defeated Hou Jing, Huiji accompanied the campaign.
entries.literal: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing, Huiji followed him.

entries.zh: 尋配以兵馬。
entries.en: Before long he was given troops and horses of his own.
entries.literal: Before long he was furnished with troops and horses.

entries.zh: 景平，從征杜龕。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was defeated, he took part in the campaign against Du Kan.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, he followed the campaign against Du Kan.

entries.zh: 除貞威將軍、通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: He was appointed general of upright prestige and attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: He was appointed General of Upright Prestige and Attendant-in-Ordinary of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 高祖踐祚，封宜黃縣侯，邑五百戶，除黃門侍郎。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Huiji was enfeoffed as marquis of Yihuang county with a fief of five hundred households and appointed gentleman at the yellow gate.
entries.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, Huiji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yihuang County with a fief of five hundred households and appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，出為安吉縣令。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Huiji was posted as magistrate of Anji county.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Wen took the throne, Huiji was sent out as Magistrate of Anji County.

entries.zh: 遷明威將軍軍副。
entries.en: He was promoted to deputy commander under a general of illustrious prestige.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Deputy of the Army of the General of Illustrious Prestige.

entries.zh: 司空章昭達征安蜀城，慧紀為水軍都督，於荊州燒青泥船艫。
entries.en: On Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda's campaign against Ancheng, Huiji served as naval commander and at Jingzhou burned the Qingni war fleet.
entries.literal: When the Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda campaigned against Ancheng, Huiji served as Commander of the Naval Forces and at Jingzhou burned the Qingni war vessels.

entries.zh: 光大元年，以功除持節、通直散騎常侍、宣遠將軍、豐州刺史，增邑并前一千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda he was rewarded with the posts of holder of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, general of far-reaching prestige, and prefect of Fengzhou, and his fief was enlarged to one thousand households in all.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda, for his merit he was appointed Holder of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Far-reaching Prestige, and Prefect of Fengzhou; his fief was increased, bringing the total to one thousand households.

entries.zh: 太建十年，吳明徹北討敗績，以慧紀為持節、智武將軍、緣江都督、兗州刺史，增邑并前二千戶，餘如故。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Taijian, after Wu Mingche's northern campaign ended in defeat, Huiji was appointed holder of the staff, general of sagacious martiality, commander along the Yangzi, and prefect of Yanzhou, with his fief raised to two thousand households in all; his other honors remained unchanged.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Taijian, when Wu Mingche's northern campaign met defeat, Huiji was appointed Holder of the Staff, General of Sagacious Martiality, Commander along the River, and Prefect of Yanzhou; his fief was increased, bringing the total to two thousand households; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 周軍乘勝據有淮南，江外騷擾，慧紀收集士卒，自海道還都。
entries.en: As the Northern Zhou army pressed its victory and seized Huainan, turmoil spread along the southern bank; Huiji gathered his troops and returned to the capital by sea.
entries.literal: The Zhou army, pressing its victory, seized Huainan; disturbances spread beyond the river; Huiji gathered troops and returned to the capital by sea.

entries.zh: 尋除使持節、散騎常侍、宣毅將軍、都督郢巴二州諸軍事、郢州刺史，增邑并前二千五百戶。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, general of resolute prestige, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ying and Ba, and prefect of Yingzhou, with his fief raised to two thousand five hundred households in all.
