entries.literal: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Resolute Prestige, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the two prefectures of Ying and Ba, and Prefect of Yingzhou; his fief was increased, bringing the total to two thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 至德二年，遷使持節、散騎常侍、雲麾將軍、都督荊信二州諸軍事、荊州刺史，賜女伎一部，增邑并前三千戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhide he was transferred as bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, general of the cloud banner, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Jing and Xin, and prefect of Jingzhou; he was granted a company of female musicians, and his fief was raised to three thousand households in all.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was transferred as Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Cloud Banner, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the two prefectures of Jing and Xin, and Prefect of Jingzhou; he was granted a troupe of female performers, and his fief was increased, bringing the total to three thousand households.

entries.zh: 禎明元年，蕭琮尚書左僕射安平王蕭巖、晉熙王蕭瓛等，[3]率其部眾男女二萬餘口，詣慧紀請降，慧紀以兵迎之。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhenming, Xiao Yan, prince of Anping and left vice director of the masters of writing under Xiao Cong, Xiao Huan, prince of Jinxi, and others[3] led more than twenty thousand followers, men and women together, to offer surrender to Huiji, who marched out with troops to receive them.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, Xiao Cong's Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Ping'an Xiao Yan, the Prince of Jinxi Xiao Fan, and others,[3] leading more than twenty thousand men and women of their following, came to Huiji to surrender; Huiji went forth with troops to receive them.

entries.zh: 其年，以應接之功，加侍中、金紫光祿大夫、開府儀同三司、征西將軍，增邑并前六千戶，餘如故。
entries.en: That same year, for his service in receiving the defectors, he was promoted to palace attendant, grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon, general-in-chief with the ceremonial equipage of a three-division commandery, and general who conquers the west, with his fief raised to six thousand households in all; his other honors remained unchanged.
entries.literal: That year, for his merit in receiving them, he was promoted to Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, General-in-Chief with the Ceremonial Equipage of a Three-Division Commandery, and General Who Conquers the West; his fief was increased, bringing the total to six thousand households; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十五
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 15
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 15

entries.zh: 知禮涉獵文史，善隸書。
entries.en: Zhili read widely in literature and history and wrote a fine clerical hand.
entries.literal: Zhili ranged through literature and history and was skilled at clerical script.

entries.zh: 高祖之討元景仲也，或薦之，引為記室參軍。
entries.en: When the Founder marched against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was made record-office aide.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yuan Jingzhong, someone recommended him and he was brought in as record-office aide.

entries.zh: 知禮為文贍速，每占授軍書，下筆便就，率皆稱旨。
entries.en: Zhili wrote copiously and fast. Dictated army papers left his brush finished in one pass, and almost all pleased the Founder.
entries.literal: Zhili's writing was ample and swift; whenever he took dictation for military documents, his brush finished at once and nearly all pleased the ruler.

entries.zh: 由是恆侍左右，深被委任，當時計畫，莫不預焉。[1]
entries.en: From then on he was always at the Founder's side, deeply trusted, and party to every plan of the day. [1]
entries.literal: From this he constantly attended at the ruler's side and was deeply entrusted; of the plans of the time none in which he did not take part therein. [1]

entries.zh: 知禮亦多所獻替。
entries.en: He also offered much counsel on policy.
entries.literal: Zhili also offered much counsel for correction and replacement.

entries.zh: 高祖平侯景，軍至白茅灣，上表於梁元帝及與王僧辯論述軍事，其文並知禮所製。
entries.en: When the Founder crushed Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the letters to Wang Sengbian on military affairs were all Zhili's work.
entries.literal: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing and the army reached Baimao Bay, the memorials to Emperor Yuan of Liang and the missives with Wang Sengbian discussing military affairs were all composed by Zhili.

entries.zh: 侯景平，授中書侍郎，封始平縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was pacified, Zhili was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping with three hundred households.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, Zhili was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiping county with three hundred households.

entries.zh: 高祖為司空，以為從事中郎。
entries.en: When the Founder became minister of works, he made Zhili gentleman attendant on his staff.
entries.literal: When the Founder became Minister of Works, he made Zhili Gentleman Attendant on his staff.

entries.zh: 高祖入輔，遷給事黃門侍郎，兼衛尉卿。
entries.en: When the Founder entered court as regent, Zhili was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chamberlain for the Guards.
entries.literal: When the Founder entered to assist the government, Zhili was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Chamberlain for the Guards.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，遷通直散騎常侍，直殿省。
entries.en: When the Founder received the mandate, Zhili became direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and served in the palace offices.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, Zhili was transferred to Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and served on duty in the palace offices.

entries.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍，守太府卿，權知領軍事。
entries.en: Soon he became scattered-cavalry regular attendant, acting chamberlain of the treasury, and temporary manager of the guards.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, acted as Chamberlain of the Treasury, and provisionally managed the affairs of the guards.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，進爵為伯，增邑通前七百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, he was advanced to count, with his fief increased to seven hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, his noble rank was advanced to count, and his fief was increased to seven hundred households in all.

entries.zh: 王琳平，授持節、督吳州諸軍事、明威將軍、吳州刺史。
entries.en: After Wang Lin was pacified, he was made bearer of the staff, supervisor of Wuzhou military affairs, manifest-might general, and inspector of Wuzhou.
entries.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Wuzhou, Manifest-Might General, and Inspector of Wuzhou.

entries.zh: 衡陽獻王昌時為吳興郡，昌年尚少，[3]吳興王之鄉里，父老故人，尊卑有數，高祖恐昌年少，接對乖禮，乃遣景歷輔之。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang was administering Wuxing. [3] He was still young. Wuxing was his home commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority. The Founder feared the prince was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and sent Jingli to assist him.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang was then administrator of Wuxing; Chang was still young, Wuxing was the prince's native commandery; elders and old friends observed rank by seniority; the Founder feared Chang was young and might receive them with improper courtesy, and so sent Jingli to assist him.

entries.zh: 承聖中，授通直散騎侍郎，還掌府記室。
entries.en: In the Chengsheng era he was made regular attendant for direct communication and again ran the establishment record office.
entries.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was appointed Regular Attendant for Direct Communication and again managed the establishment record office.

entries.zh: 高祖將討王僧辯，獨與侯安都等數人謀之，景歷弗之知也。
entries.en: When the Founder was about to strike Wang Sengbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: When the Founder was about to campaign against Wang Sengbian he plotted alone with Hou Andu and a few others; Jingli did not know of it.

entries.zh: 部分既畢，召令草檄，景歷援筆立成，辭義感激，事皆稱旨。
entries.en: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation. Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the Founder.
entries.literal: When dispositions were complete he summoned him to draft the proclamation; Jingli took brush and finished at once; the wording was moving and all pleased the ruler.

entries.zh: 僧辯誅，高祖輔政，除從事中郎，掌記室如故。
entries.en: When Sengbian was killed the Founder assisted the government and made Jingli attendant of the masters of writing, still managing the record office.
entries.literal: When Sengbian was executed the Founder assisted the government and appointed Jingli Attendant of the Masters of Writing, still managing the record office as before.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，遷給事黃門侍郎，兼掌相府記室。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai (555), he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and also managed the chancellor's record office.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently managed the chancellor's record office.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，遷祕書監，中書通事舍人，掌詔誥。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne he was made director of the secretariat, secretariat communicating affairs attendant, and manager of edicts.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant, and managed edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 永定二年，坐妻弟劉淹詐受周寶安餉馬，為御史中丞沈炯所劾，降為中書侍郎，舍人如故。
entries.en: In Yongding year 2 (558) his wife's younger brother Liu Yan was found to have fraudulently accepted horses from Zhou Bao'an; Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong impeached him and he was demoted to secretariat gentleman, keeping his post as attendant.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding, because his wife's younger brother Liu Yan fraudulently accepted horses presented by Zhou Bao'an, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiong and demoted to Secretariat Gentleman, his post as attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 三年，高祖崩，時外有彊寇，世祖鎮于南皖，朝無重臣，宣后呼景歷及江大權、杜稜定議，乃祕不發喪，疾召世祖。
entries.en: In the third year, the Founder died. Strong enemies stood outside, Emperor Wen was away at Southern Wan, and the court had no senior minister. Empress Xuan called Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng to decide matters, kept the death secret, and hurriedly summoned Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: In the third year, the Founder died. At the time powerful enemies were outside, Emperor Wen was garrisoned at Southern Wan, and the court had no weighty ministers. Empress Xuan summoned Jingli, Jiang Daquan, and Du Leng to settle the plan; they then kept the death secret and urgently summoned Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 景歷躬共宦者及內人，密營斂服。
entries.en: Jingli himself worked with the eunuchs and palace women to prepare the burial garments in secret.
entries.literal: Jingli personally worked with the eunuchs and palace women to prepare the shrouding and garments in secret.

entries.zh: 時既暑熱，須治梓宮，恐斤斧之聲或聞于外，仍以蠟為祕器。
entries.en: It was high summer, and the coffin had to be prepared; fearing the sound of tools would carry outside, they made the secret coffin of wax.
entries.literal: Because the weather was hot, they had to prepare the coffin, but feared the sound of axes and adzes might be heard outside, so they used wax for the hidden coffin.

entries.zh: 文書詔誥，依舊宣行。
entries.en: Documents and edicts continued to go out as usual.
entries.literal: Documents, edicts, and proclamations continued to be issued as before.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，復為祕書監，舍人如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Jingli returned as director of the secretariat, retaining his attendant post.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Jingli was restored as Director of the Secretariat, with his attendant post as before.

entries.zh: 以定策功，封新豐縣子，邑四百戶。
entries.en: For helping settle the succession, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinfeng with four hundred households.
entries.literal: For his merit in settling the succession plan, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinfeng county with four hundred households.

entries.zh: 累遷散騎常侍。
entries.en: After several promotions, he became scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: After repeated promotions, he became Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖誅侯安都，景歷勸成其事。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen moved against Hou Andu, Jingli urged him to carry it through.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen executed Hou Andu, Jingli urged the matter to completion.

entries.zh: 天嘉三年，以功遷太子左衛率，進爵為侯，增邑百戶，常侍、舍人如故。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 3, for this service he became left guard commander of the crown prince, was advanced to marquis, and received one hundred more households, retaining regular attendant and attendant posts.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianjia, for this merit he was transferred to Left Guard Commander of the Crown Prince, his noble rank was advanced to marquis, and his fief was increased by one hundred households, while Regular Attendant and Attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 六年，坐妻兄劉洽依倚景歷權勢，前後姦訛，并受歐陽武威餉絹百匹，[4]免官。
entries.en: In the sixth year, his wife's elder brother Liu Qia used Jingli's power for repeated fraud and accepted one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei; Jingli was dismissed from office. [4]
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was implicated when his wife's elder brother Liu Qia relied on Jingli's power and influence to commit repeated frauds and accepted a gift of one hundred bolts of silk from Ouyang Wuwei; Jingli was dismissed from office. [4]

entries.zh: 景歷少俊爽，有孝行。
entries.en: Jingli in youth was bright and open, and known for filial piety.
entries.literal: Jingli in youth was handsome and alert and showed filial conduct.

entries.zh: 家貧好學，善尺牘，工草隸。
entries.en: Though poor he loved learning, wrote excellent letters, and excelled at cursive and clerical script.
entries.literal: His family was poor yet he loved learning; he was skilled at letters and excelled at cursive and clerical script.

entries.zh: 解褐諸王府佐，出為海陽令，為政有能名。
entries.en: He entered service as a princely aide, then became magistrate of Haiyang, where his rule won a name for competence.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as aide in princely establishments, went out as magistrate of Haiyang, and his governance won a name for ability.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，梁簡文帝為景所幽，景歷與南康嗣王蕭會理謀，欲挾簡文出奔，事泄見執，賊黨王偉保護之，獲免。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen was held by Jing. Jingli and the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to carry the emperor off, but the plot was discovered and he was arrested. The rebel Wang Wei shielded him and he survived.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Jianwen of Liang was imprisoned by Jing; Jingli with the heir of Nankang, Xiao Huili, plotted to seize the emperor and flee, but the affair leaked and he was seized; the rebel partisan Wang Wei protected him and he escaped death.

entries.zh: 因客遊京口。
entries.en: He then wandered as a guest to Jingkou.
entries.literal: He then traveled as a guest to Jingkou.

entries.zh: 侯景平，高祖鎮朱方，素聞其名，以書要之。
entries.en: After Hou Jing fell the Founder held Zhufang, had long heard of him, and summoned him by letter.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified the Founder garrisoned Zhufang and, having long heard his name, summoned him by letter.

entries.zh: 景歷對使人答書，筆不停綴，文不重改。
entries.en: Jingli answered the envoy's letter without lifting his brush and without a single revision.
entries.literal: Jingli replied to the envoy's letter; his brush never paused and the text needed no revision.

entries.zh: 曰：
entries.en: He wrote:
entries.literal: He said:

entries.zh: 高祖得書，甚加欽賞。
entries.en: The Founder received the letter and admired it greatly.
entries.literal: The Founder received the letter and greatly admired it.

entries.zh: 仍更賜書報答，即日板征北府中記室參軍，仍領記室。
entries.en: He sent another letter in reply and the same day appointed him record-office aide in the northern expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.
entries.literal: He again sent a letter in reply and the same day appointed him by provisional commission Record-Office Aide in the Northern Expedition headquarters, still heading the record office.

entries.zh: 師知好學，有當世才。
entries.en: Shizhi was studious and had real talent for his day.
entries.literal: Shizhi loved learning and had talent for his age.

entries.zh: 博涉書史，工文筆，善儀體，臺閣故事，多所詳悉。
entries.en: He read widely in history, wrote well, understood ceremony, and knew secretariat precedent in detail.
entries.literal: He ranged widely through books and histories, was skilled at literary composition, good at ritual forms, and knew many details of secretariat precedent.

entries.zh: 梁世歷王府參軍。
entries.en: Under Liang he served in several princes’ households as staff officer.
entries.literal: Under Liang he successively served as staff officer in princely households.

entries.zh: 紹泰初，高祖入輔，以師知為中書舍人，掌詔誥。
entries.en: When Shaotai began the Founder took power as regent and made Shizhi a palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary in charge of edicts.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai the Founder entered to assist the government and appointed Shizhi Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary, in charge of edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 是時兵亂之後，禮儀多闕，高祖為丞相及加九錫并受禪，其儀注並師知所定焉。
entries.en: After the wars ritual was largely lost; Shizhi drew up the protocols for the Founder’s regency, the Nine Bestowals, and the abdication.
entries.literal: At that time, after the military disorders, ritual observances were largely missing; when the Founder was Chancellor and received the Nine Bestowals and then the abdication, all the ritual protocols were set by Shizhi.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，仍為舍人。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne Shizhi kept his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate he remained Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 性疏簡，與物多忤，雖位宦不遷，而委任甚重，其所獻替，皆有弘益。
entries.en: He was blunt and often clashed with others; though his rank scarcely rose, his trust was great and his counsel was always useful.
entries.literal: By nature he was blunt and simple and often at odds with others; though his official rank did not advance, his commission was very weighty, and the proposals he offered all had broad benefit.

entries.zh: 及高祖崩，六日成服，朝臣共議大行皇帝靈座俠御人所服衣服吉凶之制，博士沈文阿議，宜服吉服。
entries.en: When the Founder died, on the sixth day mourning dress was completed. The court debated whether attendants at the late emperor’s spirit seat should wear auspicious or mourning dress. Academician Shen Wen’a argued for auspicious dress.
entries.literal: When the Founder died, on the sixth day they completed mourning dress; the court ministers together discussed whether the attendants at the late emperor’s spirit seat should wear auspicious or inauspicious garments. Academician Shen Wen’a argued that they should wear auspicious dress.

entries.zh: 師知議云：「既稱成服，本備喪禮，靈筵服物，皆悉縞素。
entries.en: Shizhi argued: "Completing mourning dress means preparing the full mourning rite. Everything at the spirit couch should be plain white.
entries.literal: Shizhi argued: "Since it is called completing mourning dress, it is fundamentally to prepare the mourning rites; all garments and objects at the spirit couch should be entirely plain white.

entries.zh: 今雖無大行俠御官事，按梁昭明太子薨，成服俠侍之官，悉著縗斬，唯著鎧不異，此即可擬。
entries.en: There is no formal office of spirit-seat attendants now, but when Liang’s Crown Prince Zhaoming died his attendants at the completion of mourning all wore the coarsest hemp, except that they still wore armor. That is our model.
entries.literal: Though today there is no office of attendants for the late emperor’s spirit seat, according to when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, at the completion of mourning dress the attendant officers all wore the coarsest hemp, differing only in that they still wore armor—this may serve as a model.

entries.zh: 愚謂六日成服，俠靈座須服縗絰。」
entries.en: On the sixth day, when mourning dress is completed, attendants at the spirit seat should wear hemp mourning."
entries.literal: I hold that on the sixth day, when mourning dress is completed, those attending the spirit seat must wear hemp mourning."

entries.zh: 中書舍人蔡景歷亦云：「雖不悉準，按山陵有凶吉羽儀，成服唯凶無吉，文武俠御，不容獨鳴玉珥貂，情禮二三，理宜縗斬。」
entries.en: Cai Jingli, palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary, also said: "The tomb procession has both auspicious and mourning regalia, but completion of mourning dress is mourning only. Civil and military attendants cannot alone wear jade and sable. In ritual feeling they should wear coarse hemp."
entries.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Jingli also said: "Though it does not fully accord, according to the fact that for the imperial tomb there are auspicious and inauspicious regalia, and completion of mourning dress has only the inauspicious and not the auspicious, civil and military attendants cannot alone wear jade pendants and sable tails; in feeling and ritual there are two or three points, and they ought to wear coarse hemp."

entries.zh: 中書舍人江德藻、謝岐等並同師知議。
entries.en: Palace secretariat attendants Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others all sided with Shizhi.
entries.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendants Jiang Dezao, Xie Qi, and others all agreed with Shizhi’s view.

entries.zh: 文阿重議云：「檢晉、宋山陵儀：『靈輿梓宮降殿，各侍中奏。』
entries.en: Wen’a replied: "The Jin and Song tomb protocols say: ‘When the spirit carriage and inner coffin descend to the hall, each attendant-in-ordinary reports.’
entries.literal: Wen’a argued again: "Checking the Jin and Song tomb protocols: ‘When the spirit carriage and inner coffin descend to the hall, each attendant-in-ordinary reports.’

entries.zh: 又成服儀稱：『靈輿梓宮容俠御官及香橙。』
entries.en: The protocol for completing mourning dress also says: ‘The spirit carriage and inner coffin accommodate attendant officers, incense, and oranges.’
entries.literal: The protocol for completing mourning dress also says: ‘The spirit carriage and inner coffin accommodate attendant officers and incense and oranges.’

entries.zh: 又檢靈輿梓宮進止儀稱：『直靈俠御吉服，在吉鹵簿中。』
entries.en: The protocol for the spirit carriage’s advance and halt says: ‘Direct attendants at the spirit seat wear auspicious dress and stand in the auspicious guard of honor.’
entries.literal: Checking again the protocol for the spirit carriage and inner coffin’s advance and halt, it says: ‘Direct attendants at the spirit seat wear auspicious dress and are in the auspicious guard of honor.’

entries.zh: 又云：『梓宮俠御縗服，在凶鹵簿中。』
entries.en: It also says: ‘Attendants at the inner coffin wear hemp mourning and stand in the inauspicious guard of honor.’
entries.literal: It also says: ‘Attendants at the inner coffin wear hemp mourning and are in the inauspicious guard of honor.’

entries.zh: 是則在殿吉凶兩俠御也。」
entries.en: So in the hall there are both auspicious and mourning attendants."
entries.literal: Thus in the hall there are both auspicious and inauspicious attendants.

entries.zh: 時以二議不同，乃啟取左丞徐陵決斷。
entries.en: Because the two sides disagreed, they asked left vice director Xu Ling to decide.
entries.literal: At the time, because the two arguments differed, they submitted a memorial asking Left Vice Director Xu Ling to decide.

entries.zh: 陵云：「梓宮祔山陵，靈筵祔宗廟，有此分判，便驗吉凶。
entries.en: Ling said: "The inner coffin goes to the tomb and the spirit couch to the ancestral temple. That division itself shows what is auspicious and what is mourning.
entries.literal: Ling said: "The inner coffin is lodged at the mountain tomb and the spirit couch at the ancestral temple—there is this division, and from it auspicious and inauspicious are verified.

entries.zh: 按山陵鹵簿吉部
entries.en: In the auspicious section of the tomb guard of honor
entries.literal: According to the auspicious section of the tomb guard of honor

entries.en: (office)
entries.literal: (office)

entries.zh: 伍中，[8]公卿以下導引者，爰及武賁、鼓吹、執蓋、奉車，[9]並是吉服，豈容俠御獨為縗絰邪？
entries.en: [8] in the fifth rank, from dukes and ministers down through guides, tiger guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants—all wear auspicious dress. How could spirit-seat attendants alone wear hemp mourning?
entries.literal: [8] in the five ranks, from the dukes and ministers down through those who lead the procession, as well as the tiger guards, musicians, canopy bearers, and chariot attendants—all wear auspicious dress. How could the spirit-seat attendants alone wear hemp mourning?

entries.zh: 斷可知矣。
entries.en: The answer is plain.
entries.literal: The conclusion is clear.

entries.zh: 若言公卿胥吏並服縗苴，此與梓宮部伍有何差別？
entries.en: If dukes, ministers, clerks, and attendants all wore hemp, how would they differ from the inner-coffin guard?
entries.literal: If one says that dukes, ministers, clerks, and attendants all wear hemp cloth, what difference is there between them and the inner-coffin guard?

entries.zh: 若言文物並吉，司事者凶，豈容
entries.en: If ritual objects are auspicious but those who manage affairs are in mourning, how could one
entries.literal: If one says that ritual objects are all auspicious but those who manage affairs are inauspicious, how could one

entries.en: (lapel)
entries.literal: (lapel)

entries.zh: 衽絰而奉華蓋，[10]縗衣而升玉輅邪？
entries.en: [10] wear hemp at the lapels yet hold the state canopy, or wear mourning robes yet mount the jade chariot?
entries.literal: [10] lapels wear hemp at the lapels yet hold the state canopy, or wear mourning robes yet mount the jade chariot?

entries.zh: 同博士議。」
entries.en: I agree with the academician."
entries.literal: I agree with the academician’s view.

entries.zh: 師知又議曰：「左丞引梓宮祔山陵，靈筵祔宗廟，必有吉凶二部，成服不容上凶，博士猶執前斷，終是山陵之禮。
entries.en: Shizhi argued again: "The left vice director says the inner coffin goes to the tomb and the spirit couch to the temple, so there must be auspicious and mourning sections, and completion of mourning dress cannot have mourning above. The academician still holds to the tomb rite.
entries.literal: Shizhi argued again: "The left vice director cites the inner coffin lodged at the mountain tomb and the spirit couch at the ancestral temple, saying there must be auspicious and inauspicious sections; completion of mourning dress cannot have the upper part inauspicious. The academician still holds to his former decision, which is ultimately the tomb protocol.

entries.zh: 若龍駕啟殯，鑾輿兼設，吉凶之儀，由來本備，準之成服，愚有未安。
entries.en: When the imperial carriage begins the funeral both regalia are already in place. Measured against completion of mourning dress, I am still uneasy.
entries.literal: If when the imperial carriage begins the funeral procession both regalia are set out together, auspicious and inauspicious protocols have from the outset been complete—measured against completion of mourning dress, I am still uneasy.

entries.zh: 夫喪禮之制，自天子達。
entries.en: Mourning regulations extend from the Son of Heaven downward.
entries.literal: The regulations of mourning rites extend from the Son of Heaven down.

entries.zh: 按王文憲喪服明記云：『官品第三，侍靈人二十。
entries.en: Wang Wenhien’s Explanations of Mourning Dress says: ‘For officials of the third rank, twenty persons attend the spirit.
entries.literal: According to Wang Wenhien’s Explanations of Mourning Dress it states: ‘For officials of the third rank, twenty persons attend the spirit.

entries.zh: 官品第四，下達士禮，侍靈之數，並有十人。
entries.en: From the fourth rank down to the scholar’s rite, ten attend the spirit in each case.
entries.literal: For the fourth rank down to the scholar’s rites, the number attending the spirit is ten in each case.

entries.zh: 皆白布袴褶，著白絹帽。
entries.en: All wear white-cloth trousers and jackets and white-silk caps.
entries.literal: All wear white-cloth trousers and jackets and white-silk caps.

entries.zh: 內喪女侍數如外，而著齊縗。
entries.en: For inner mourning the women attendants match the men in number but wear second-grade hemp.
entries.literal: For inner mourning, female attendants are as numerous as the outer, but they wear the second-grade hemp.

entries.zh: 或問內外侍靈是同，何忽縗服有異？
entries.en: Someone asked: if inner and outer attendants are the same, why is mourning dress different?
entries.literal: Someone asked: if inner and outer attendants to the spirit are the same, why suddenly is mourning dress different?

entries.zh: 答云，若依君臣之禮，則外侍斬，內侍齊。
entries.en: The answer was: by ruler-and-minister rites the outer attendants wear the coarsest cut and the inner the second grade.
entries.literal: The answer was: if one follows the rites of ruler and minister, then the outer attendants wear the coarsest cut and the inner the second grade.

entries.zh: 頃世多故，禮隨事省。
entries.en: Recent ages have seen many troubles, and rites were cut to fit the times.
entries.literal: In recent generations there have been many troubles, and rites have been reduced as affairs required.

entries.zh: 諸侯以下，臣吏蓋微，至於侍奉，多出義附，君臣之節不全，縗冠之費實闕，所以因其常服，止變帽而已。
entries.en: Below feudal lords, officials were humble and attendants mostly volunteers. Ruler-minister form was incomplete and hemp caps too costly, so they kept ordinary dress and only changed the cap.
entries.literal: Below the rank of feudal lord, ministers and clerks were slight; as for attendance, most came from voluntary attachment. The relation of ruler and minister was not complete, and the expense of hemp caps was in fact lacking; therefore they kept their ordinary dress and only changed the cap.

entries.zh: 婦人侍者，皆是卑隸，君妾之道既純，服章所以備矣。』
entries.en: Women attendants were low servants; lord and concubine stood apart, so their dress was complete.’
entries.literal: Women who attended were all low servants; the way of lord and concubine was pure, and therefore their dress and insignia were complete.

entries.zh: 皇朝之典，猶自不然，以此而推，是知服斬。
entries.en: Our dynasty’s code is not like that. From this one infers coarse hemp.
entries.literal: The statutes of our dynasty are still not so; from this one infers that the coarsest hemp should be worn.

entries.zh: 彼有侍靈，則猶俠御，既著白帽，理無彤服。
entries.en: Spirit attendants are like seat attendants; in white caps they cannot wear colored dress.
entries.literal: Where there are attendants to the spirit, it is like attendants at the seat; once they wear the white cap, by principle there can be no colored dress.

entries.zh: 且梁昭明儀注，今則見存，二文顯證，差為成準。
entries.en: Liang’s protocols for Crown Prince Zhaoming still survive. Those two texts are clear proof and a settled standard.
entries.literal: Moreover the Liang protocols for Crown Prince Zhaoming still exist today; these two texts are clear evidence and may serve as a settled standard.

entries.zh: 且禮出人情，可得消息。
entries.en: Rites arise from feeling and may be adjusted in practice.
entries.literal: Moreover rites arise from human feeling and may be adjusted in message.

entries.zh: 凡人有喪，既陳筵机，繐帷靈屏，[11]變其常儀，蘆箔草廬，即其凶禮。
entries.en: When anyone mourns, once the spirit couch and tables are set out and curtains hung, ordinary life changes; reed mats and grass huts are the mourning rite.
entries.literal: Whenever anyone has a bereavement, once the spirit couch and offering tables are set out, curtains and spirit screens are hung, [11] ordinary observances are changed, and reed mats and grass huts are the inauspicious rite.

entries.zh: 堂室之內，親賓具來，齊斬麻緦，差池哭次，玄冠不弔，莫非素服。
entries.en: Within the hall kin and guests gather in hemp of every grade, weeping in ranks. Black caps do not call—all wear plain dress.
entries.literal: Within the hall, kin and guests all come; in coarse hemp of various grades they take their places weeping in ranks; black caps do not pay condolence calls—all are plain dress.

entries.zh: 豈見門生故吏，綃縠間趨，左姬右姜，紅紫相糅？
entries.en: Who could see students and retainers rushing about in silk, with concubines in red and purple at their sides?
entries.literal: How could one see students and old retainers hurrying in silk and gauze, with concubines left and right in red and purple mingled?

entries.zh: 況四海遏密，率土之情是同，三軍縞素，為服之制斯壹。
entries.en: How much more when the realm is in deep mourning and all under Heaven feels as one, and the three armies wear plain white in a single regulation of dress.
entries.literal: How much more when the realm is in deep mourning and feeling under Heaven is one; the three armies in plain white—the regulation of dress is uniform.

entries.zh: 遂使千門旦啟，非塗堊於彤闈，百僚戾止，變服麤於朱韍，而耀金在列，鳴玉節行，求之懷抱，固為未愜，準以禮經，彌無前事。
entries.en: Yet a thousand gates open at dawn without whitewash on the vermilion gate; the hundred officials arrive in coarse dress instead of vermilion sashes, while gold gleams in the ranks and jade sounds in procession. In the heart it cannot satisfy; by the ritual canon there is no precedent.
entries.literal: Thus a thousand gates open at dawn—not whitewash on the vermilion gate; the hundred officials arrive and stop—coarse dress replaces the vermilion sash; yet gleaming gold stands in the ranks and sounding jade marks the procession. Sought in the heart, it is plainly unsatisfying; measured against the ritual canon, there is even less precedent.

entries.zh: 豈可成服之儀，譬以山陵之禮？
entries.en: How can completion of mourning dress be likened to the tomb rites?
entries.literal: How can the rites of completing mourning dress be likened to the tomb protocol?

entries.zh: 葬既始終已畢，故有吉凶之儀，所謂成服，本成喪禮，百司外內，皆變吉容，俠御獨不，何謂成服？
entries.en: When burial is finished there are auspicious and mourning protocols. Completing mourning dress means completing the mourning rite. All offices inside and out change to auspicious dress—if spirit-seat attendants alone do not, what is completion of mourning?
entries.literal: When burial has begun and ended, there are therefore auspicious and inauspicious protocols—what is called completing mourning dress is fundamentally completing the mourning rite. Inside and outside, the hundred offices all change to auspicious appearance; if the spirit-seat attendants alone do not, what is called completing mourning dress?

entries.zh: 若靈無俠御則已，有則必應縗服。」
entries.en: If there are no spirit-seat attendants, so be it; if there are, they must wear hemp mourning."
entries.literal: If there are no spirit-seat attendants, so be it; if there are, they must wear hemp mourning.

entries.zh: 謝岐議曰：「靈筵祔宗廟，梓宮祔山陵，實如左丞議。
entries.en: Xie Qi argued: "The spirit couch goes to the temple and the inner coffin to the tomb, as the left vice director said.
entries.literal: Xie Qi argued: "The spirit couch is lodged at the ancestral temple and the inner coffin at the mountain tomb—this is truly as the left vice director said.

entries.zh: 但山陵鹵簿，備有吉凶，從靈輿者儀服無變，從梓宮者皆服苴縗。
entries.en: But the tomb guard has both auspicious and mourning sections. Those who follow the spirit carriage keep their dress; those who follow the inner coffin all wear hemp.
entries.literal: But in the tomb guard of honor auspicious and inauspicious are both provided; those who follow the spirit carriage do not change dress, while those who follow the inner coffin all wear hemp cloth.

entries.zh: 爰至士禮，悉同此制，此自是山陵之儀，非關成服。
entries.en: Down to the scholar’s rite the rule is the same. That is the tomb rite, not completion of mourning dress.
entries.literal: Down to the scholar’s rites all follow this regulation—this is itself the tomb protocol and does not concern completion of mourning dress.

entries.zh: 今謂梓宮靈扆，共在西階，稱為成服，亦無鹵簿，直是爰自胥吏，上至王公，四海之內，必備縗絰。
entries.en: Now the inner coffin and spirit screen both stand on the western steps and we call it completing mourning dress, yet there is no guard of honor—only that from clerks to dukes, throughout the realm, all must wear hemp.
entries.literal: Now we call the inner coffin and spirit screen both on the western steps ‘completing mourning dress,’ yet there is no guard of honor—only from clerks and attendants up to dukes and ministers, within the four seas, all must wear hemp mourning.

entries.zh: 案梁昭明太子薨，略是成例，豈容凡百士庶，悉皆服重，而侍中至於武衛，最是近官，反鳴玉紆青，與平吉不異？
entries.en: When Liang’s Crown Prince Zhaoming died is the established example. How could every commoner wear the heavy grade while attendants-in-ordinary down to the martial guards—the nearest officers—wore jade and azure no differently from an ordinary auspicious day?
entries.literal: According to when Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died, which is roughly the established example—how could common scholars and people all wear the heavy grade, while attendants-in-ordinary down to the martial guards, who are the nearest officers, on the contrary sound jade and twist azure, no different from ordinary auspicious days?

entries.zh: 左丞既推以山陵事，愚意或謂與成服有殊。
entries.en: The left vice director treats it as a tomb matter; I think that may differ from completion of mourning dress.
entries.literal: The left vice director, pushing the matter of the tomb, in my humble view perhaps differs from completion of mourning dress.

entries.zh: 若爾日俠御，文武不異，維侍靈之人，主書、宣傳、齊幹、應敕，悉應不改。」
entries.en: If on that day spirit-seat attendants, civil and military alike, were unchanged, then chief clerks, heralds, runners, and responders to edicts who attend the spirit should likewise not change."
entries.literal: If on that day the spirit-seat attendants, civil and military, were not different, then those who attend the spirit—the chief clerks, heralds, runners, and responders to edicts—should all likewise not change.

entries.zh: 蔡景歷又議云：「俠御之官，本出五百，爾日備服居廬，仍於本省，引上登殿，豈應變服貂玉？
entries.en: Cai Jingli argued again: "Spirit-seat attendants came from the five hundred. That day they wore mourning dress and dwelt in the mourning hut but still belonged to their offices and were led up to the hall—how could they change to sable and jade?
entries.literal: Cai Jingli argued again: "The office of spirit-seat attendants originally came from the five hundred; on that day, though they wore mourning dress and dwelt in the mourning hut, they were still in their original department and were led up to ascend the hall—how could they change to sable and jade?

entries.zh: 若別攝餘官，以充簪珥，則爾日便有不成服者。
entries.en: If other officers were drafted to fill the insignia ranks, then on that day some would not have completed mourning dress.
entries.literal: If other officials were specially assigned to fill the ranks of insignia, then on that day there would be some who had not completed mourning dress.

entries.zh: 山陵自有吉凶二議，成服凶而不吉，猶依前議，同劉舍人。」
entries.en: The tomb has its own auspicious-and-mourning debate. Completion of mourning dress is mourning, not auspicious. I still follow the former view and agree with Attendant Liu."
entries.literal: The tomb has its own debate on auspicious and inauspicious; completion of mourning dress is inauspicious and not auspicious—still following the former view, I agree with Attendant Liu.

entries.zh: 德藻又議云：「愚謂祖葬之辰，始終永畢，達官有追贈，須表恩榮，有吉鹵簿，恐由此義，私家放效，因以成俗。
entries.en: Dezao argued again: "On the day of ancestral burial, when the rite is forever complete, high officials receive posthumous honors and display grace. The auspicious guard may come from that. Private families imitated it and it became custom.
entries.literal: Dezao argued again: "I hold that on the day of the ancestral burial, when beginning and end are forever complete, high officials receive posthumous honors and must display grace and glory; there is an auspicious guard of honor, and I fear the meaning lies here. Private families imitated it, and thus it became custom.

entries.zh: 上服本變吉為凶，理不應猶襲紈綺。
entries.en: Upper dress should change from auspicious to mourning; by principle one should not still wear silk gauze.
entries.literal: Upper dress fundamentally changes from auspicious to inauspicious; by principle one should not still wear silk gauze.

entries.zh: 劉舍人引王衛軍喪儀及檢梁昭明故事，此明據已審，博士、左丞乃各盡事衷，既未取證，須更詢詳，宜諮八座、詹事、太常、中丞
entries.en: Attendant Liu cited General Wang’s mourning protocol and the Liang Zhaoming precedent—clear proof already in hand. The academician and left vice director each stated his view; since no decision was reached, inquiry should go further—to the eight ministers, the heir apparent’s tutor, the minister of rites, the censor-in-chief
entries.literal: Attendant Liu cited General Wang’s mourning protocol and checked the Liang Zhaoming precedent—this clear evidence is already established. The academician and left vice director each exhausted their views; since no proof was taken, inquiry must go further. It should be put to the eight ministers, the household tutor of the heir apparent, the minister of rites, the censor-in-chief

entries.en: (Kong)
entries.literal: (Kong)

entries.zh: 及中庶諸通袁樞、張種、周弘正、弘讓、沈炯、孔奐[12]。」
entries.en: [12] and the household tutors and general attendants Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan."
entries.literal: [12] and the household tutors and general attendants Yuan Shu, Zhang Zhong, Zhou Hongzheng, Hongrang, Shen Jiong, and Kong Huan.

entries.zh: 時八座以下，並請：「案群議，斟酌舊儀，梁昭明太子喪成服儀注，明文見存，足為準的。
entries.en: The eight ministers and below all submitted: "Weighing the discussions and old protocol, Liang’s protocols for completing mourning dress at Crown Prince Zhaoming’s death survive in clear text and suffice as standard.
entries.literal: At that time the eight ministers and below all requested: "Considering the group discussions and weighing old protocol, the Liang protocols for completing mourning dress at Crown Prince Zhaoming’s death exist in clear text today and suffice as a standard.

entries.zh: 成服日，侍官理不容猶從吉禮。
entries.en: On the day of completing mourning dress, attendant officers cannot follow auspicious rites.
entries.literal: On the day of completing mourning dress, attendant officers by principle cannot still follow auspicious rites.

entries.zh: 其葬禮分吉，自是山陵之時，非關成服之日。
entries.en: Burial rites divide into auspicious sections at the tomb; that does not concern the day of completing mourning dress.
entries.literal: That burial rites are divided into auspicious sections is a matter of the time of the mountain tomb and does not concern the day of completing mourning dress.

entries.zh: 愚謂劉舍人議於事為允。」
entries.en: We hold that Attendant Liu’s view is acceptable."
entries.literal: I hold that Attendant Liu’s view is acceptable in the matter.

entries.zh: 陵重答云：「老病屬纊，不能多說，古人爭議，多成怨府，傅玄見尤於晉代，王商取陷於漢朝，謹自三緘，敬同高命。
entries.en: Ling answered again: "Old and ill, I can say little. Men of old who disputed often bred resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in Jin and Wang Shang fell in Han. I seal my lips thrice and honor your command.
entries.literal: Ling answered again: "Old and ill, I lie with the coverlet up to my chin and cannot say much. Men of old who disputed often became objects of resentment; Fu Xuan was blamed in the Jin age and Wang Shang fell into trouble in Han—I respectfully seal my lips thrice and honor your high command.

entries.zh: 若萬一不死，猶得展言，庶與朝賢更申揚搉。」
entries.en: If by chance I do not die, I may yet speak and discuss the matter again with the court."
entries.literal: If by any chance I do not die, I may yet speak further and, with the court worthies, discuss again in detail.

entries.zh: 文阿猶執所見，眾議不能決，乃具錄二議奏聞，從師知議。
entries.en: Wen’a still held to his view. The assembly could not decide, recorded both arguments, submitted them, and followed Shizhi’s view.
entries.literal: Wen’a still held to his view; the assembly could not decide, so they fully recorded both arguments and submitted them, following Shizhi’s view.

entries.zh: 岐少機警，好學，見稱於梁世。
entries.en: Qi was quick-witted as a youth, loved learning, and won praise under Liang.
entries.literal: Qi in youth was quick-witted, loved learning, and was praised in the Liang age.

entries.zh: 為尚書金部郎，山陰令。
entries.en: He was a revenue clerk in the masters of writing and magistrate of Shanyin.
entries.literal: He was Lang of the Ministry of Revenue in the Masters of Writing and Magistrate of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，岐流寓東陽。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, Qi took refuge in Dongyang.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Qi wandered in Dongyang.

entries.zh: 景平，依于張彪。
entries.en: After Jing was suppressed he joined Zhang Biao.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, he attached himself to Zhang Biao.

entries.zh: 彪在吳郡及會稽，庶事一以委之。
entries.en: When Biao held Wu and Kuaiji he entrusted all routine affairs to Qi.
entries.literal: When Biao was in Wu commandery and Kuaiji, he entrusted all miscellaneous affairs to Qi.

entries.zh: 彪每征討，恆留岐監郡，知後事。
entries.en: Whenever Biao campaigned he left Qi to supervise the commandery and handle affairs behind him.
entries.literal: Whenever Biao went on campaign, he always left Qi to supervise the commandery and manage subsequent affairs.

entries.zh: 彪敗，高祖引岐參預機密，以為兼尚書右丞。
entries.en: When Biao was defeated the Founder drew Qi into confidential planning and made him acting right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: When Biao was defeated, the Founder drew Qi into confidential planning and made him Acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 時軍旅屢興，糧儲多闕，岐所在幹理，深被知遇。
entries.en: Campaigns were frequent and grain stores often empty; wherever Qi managed affairs he won deep trust.
entries.literal: At that time campaigns were frequent and grain stores often lacked; wherever Qi took charge of affairs he was deeply known and favored.

entries.zh: 永定元年，為給事黃門侍郎、中書舍人，兼右丞如故。
entries.en: In Yongding year one he was made attendant of the yellow gate and palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary, still acting right vice director.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongding he was made Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary, still acting right vice director as before.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年卒，贈通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Tianjia year two he died and was posthumously made regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianjia he died; he was posthumously made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：高祖開基創業，剋定禍亂，武猛固其立功，文翰亦乃展力。[13]
entries.en: The historian says: When the Founder raised the dynasty and quelled chaos, martial prowess won his achievement, but literary men also played their part. [13]
entries.literal: The historian says: When the Founder opened the foundation and created the enterprise, quelling disaster and disorder, martial fierceness indeed established his achievement, but literary writing also displayed its power. [13]

entries.zh: 趙知禮、蔡景歷早識攀附，預締構之臣焉。
entries.en: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli recognized him early and helped build the state.
entries.literal: Zhao Zhili and Cai Jingli early recognized and attached themselves to him; they were ministers in the founding structure.

entries.zh: 劉師知博涉多通，而闇於機變，雖欲存乎節義，終陷極刑，斯不智矣。
entries.en: Liu Shizhi was broadly learned but blind to the moment; though he wished to keep his integrity, he ended on the execution ground—this was folly.
entries.literal: Liu Shizhi ranged widely and knew much, yet was dark about timely change; though he wished to preserve integrity and righteousness, in the end he fell to extreme punishment—this was lack of wisdom.

entries.zh: 知禮沈靜有謀謨，每軍國大事，世祖輒令璽書問之。
entries.en: Zhili was quiet and shrewd. On every grave matter of state or army, Emperor Wen sent sealed letters to ask his view.
entries.literal: Zhili was calm and possessed of stratagem; whenever there were great affairs of state and army, Emperor Wen would send sealed letters to ask him.

entries.zh: 秩滿，為明威將軍、太子右衛率。
entries.en: When his term ended he was made General of Manifest Prestige and right commandant of the heir apparent's guard.
entries.literal: When his term expired he was made General of Manifest Prestige and Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 遷右衛將軍，領前軍將軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to right guard general and also front army general.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Right Guard General and concurrently Front Army General.

entries.zh: 六年卒，時年四十七。
entries.en: In the sixth year he died, at forty-seven.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged forty-seven.

entries.zh: 詔贈侍中，諡曰忠。
entries.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant with the posthumous name Loyal.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant, posthumous title Loyal.

entries.zh: 子允恭嗣。[2]
entries.en: His son Yungong succeeded him. [2]
entries.literal: His son Yungong succeeded. [2]

entries.zh: 尋遷鴻臚卿，舍人如故。
entries.en: Soon he was made minister herald, keeping his post as attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister Herald, his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary unchanged.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，坐事免。
entries.en: In Tianjia year one he was dismissed for an offense.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was dismissed for an offense.

entries.zh: 初，世祖敕師知撰《起居注》，自永定二年秋至天嘉元年冬，為十卷。
entries.en: Earlier Emperor Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the imperial diary from autumn of Yongding year two through winter of Tianjia year one—ten scrolls.
entries.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen had ordered Shizhi to compile the imperial diary from the autumn of Yongding year two to the winter of Tianjia year one, ten scrolls.

entries.zh: 起為中書舍人，復掌詔誥。
entries.en: He was recalled as palace secretariat attendant-in-ordinary and again put in charge of edicts.
entries.literal: He was raised as Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary and again put in charge of edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 天康元年，世祖不豫，師知與尚書僕射到仲舉等入侍醫藥。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiankang, when Emperor Wen fell ill, Shizhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju, and others entered to tend him with medicine.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, when Emperor Wen was ill, Shizhi together with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju and others entered to attend with medicine.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，預受顧命。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died, Shizhi had already received the deathbed charge.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, he received the testamentary charge in advance.

entries.zh: 及高宗為尚書令，入輔，光大元年，師知與仲舉等遣舍人殷不佞矯詔令高宗還東府，事覺，於北獄賜死。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was Director of the Masters of Writing and regent, in the first year of Guangda, Shizhi, Zhongju, and the others sent Attendant Yin Buniu with a forged order telling Emperor Xuan to return to the Eastern Mansion. The plot was exposed, and Shizhi was ordered to die in the northern prison.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Director of the Masters of Writing and entered to assist the government, in the first year of Guangda, Shizhi together with Zhongju and others sent Attendant Yin Buniu with a forged order telling Emperor Xuan to return to the Eastern Mansion; the affair was discovered and at the northern prison he was granted death.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，遷宣惠豫章王長史，帶會稽郡守，行東揚州府事。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jingli became chief administrator to the Prince of Yuzhang, general who spreads grace, concurrently governor of Kuaiji, and acting head of the East Yangzhou administration.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jingli was transferred to Chief Administrator for the Prince of Yuzhang, General Who Spreads Grace, concurrently held the governorship of Kuaiji commandery, and acted in the affairs of the East Yangzhou administration.

entries.zh: 秩滿，遷戎昭將軍、宣毅長沙王長史、[6]尋陽太守，行江州府事，以疾辭，遂不行。
entries.en: At the end of his term, he became martial-illustrious general, chief administrator to the Prince of Changsha, general who proclaims resolve, and administrator of Xunyang, acting over Jiangzhou; he pleaded illness and did not take up the post. [6]
entries.literal: When his term was complete, he was transferred to Martial-Illustrious General, Chief Administrator for the Prince of Changsha, General Who Proclaims Resolve, and Administrator of Xunyang, acting in the affairs of the Jiangzhou administration; because of illness he declined and therefore did not go.

entries.zh: 入為通直散騎常侍、中書通事舍人，掌詔誥，仍復封邑。
entries.en: Back at court, he became direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and secretariat communicating affairs attendant, managed edicts, and had his fief restored.
entries.literal: Entering court, he became Direct-Communication Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant, managing edicts and proclamations, and his fief was restored.

entries.zh: 遷太子左衛率，常侍、舍人如故。
entries.en: He became left guard commander of the crown prince, retaining regular attendant and attendant posts.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Guard Commander of the Crown Prince, with Regular Attendant and Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 太建五年，都督吳明徹北伐，所向克捷，與周將梁士彥戰於呂梁，大破之，斬獲萬計，方欲進圖彭城。
entries.en: In Taijian year 5 (573) Commander Wu Mingche marched north and won wherever he went; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, shattered him, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance on Pengcheng.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian, as commander Wu Mingche marched north in expedition, wherever he went he won; he fought the Zhou general Liang Shiyan at Luliang, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded and captured tens of thousands; he was about to advance and take Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 是時高宗銳意河南，以為指麾可定，景歷諫稱師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated that the army was weary and the generals proud and that the distant strategy should not be pressed too far.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was keen on the lands south of the Yellow River and thought command alone could settle them; Jingli remonstrated, saying the army was weary and the generals proud and that one should not press the distant strategy too far.

entries.zh: 高宗惡其沮眾，大怒，猶以朝廷舊臣，不深罪責，出為宣遠將軍、豫章內史。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit and was furious, yet because he was an old court minister did not punish him deeply and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and interior magistrate of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan hated his damping the men's spirit, was greatly angered, yet because he was an old minister of the court did not deeply punish him and sent him out as General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 未行，為飛章所劾，以在省之日，贓汙狼藉，帝令有司按問，[7]景歷但承其半。
entries.en: Before he could leave he was impeached by flying memorial; his corruption in the capital was notorious and the emperor ordered investigation. [7] Jingli admitted only half.
entries.literal: Before he departed he was impeached by flying memorial; because in his days at the capital his corruption was notorious, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate, and Jingli admitted only half.

entries.zh: 於是御史中丞宗元饒奏曰：「臣聞士之行己，忠以事上，廉以持身，苟違斯道，刑茲罔赦。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao then memorialized: "I have heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.
entries.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Zong Yuanrao memorialized, saying: "Your servant has heard that in a gentleman's conduct loyalty serves his superiors and integrity holds his person; if he violates this way, punishment knows no pardon.

entries.zh: 謹按宣遠將軍、豫章內史新豐縣開國侯景歷，因藉多幸，豫奉興王，皇運權輿，頗參締構。
entries.en: I respectfully accuse General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.
entries.literal: Your servant respectfully accuses General of Far Illumination and Interior Magistrate of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xinfeng, Jingli: by many strokes of fortune he was early favored at the founding king's side; when the imperial fortune was lifting he took part in the founding structure.

entries.zh: 天嘉之世，贓賄狼藉，聖恩錄用，許以更鳴，裂壤崇階，不遠斯復。
entries.en: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.
entries.literal: In the Tianjia era his bribes were notorious; by imperial grace he was recorded for use and allowed to sound again; fief land and lofty rank were not long in returning.

entries.zh: 不能改節自勵，以報曲成，遂乃專擅貪汙，彰於遠近，一則已甚，其可再乎？
entries.en: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?
entries.literal: He could not change his ways and encourage himself to repay partial formation; he then monopolized greed and corruption, manifest near and far—once was already too much; how could there be a second?

entries.zh: 宜寘刑書，以明秋憲。
entries.en: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.
entries.literal: He should be placed in the penal code to clarify autumn law.

entries.zh: 臣等參議，以見事免景歷所居官，下鴻臚削爵土。
entries.en: We jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief.
entries.literal: Your servants jointly propose that, on the matter before us, Jingli be removed from the office he holds and the Court of Imperial Entertainments be directed to strip his fief land.

entries.zh: 謹奉白簡以聞。」
entries.en: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."
entries.literal: Respectfully presenting the white bamboo to inform."

entries.zh: 詔曰「可」。
entries.en: An edict said, "Approved."
entries.literal: An edict said, "Approved."

entries.zh: 於是徙居會稽。
entries.en: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was moved to live in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 及吳明徹敗，帝思景歷前言，即日追還，復以為征南鄱陽王諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.
entries.literal: When Wu Mingche was defeated the emperor recalled Jingli's former words and the same day recalled him, again making him Adviser to the Prince of Poyang, Campaign South.

entries.zh: 數日，遷員外散騎常侍，兼御史中丞，復本封爵，入守度支尚書。
entries.en: Within several days he was made extraordinary attendant of scattered cavalry and concurrently censor-in-chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of minister of revenue.
entries.literal: Within several days he was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, restored to his original enfeoffment, and entered to hold the post of Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 舊式拜官在午後，景歷拜日，適值輿駕幸玄武觀，在位皆侍宴，帝恐景歷不豫，特令早拜，其見重如此。
entries.en: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office the imperial carriage happened to visit the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were at the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.
entries.literal: By old form, receiving office was in the afternoon; on the day Jingli took office it happened that the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Observatory; all in office were attending the feast; the emperor feared Jingli would not be at ease and specially ordered early investiture—such was the regard for him.

entries.zh: 劉師知，沛國相人也。
entries.en: Liu Shizhi came from Xiang in Pei.
entries.literal: Liu Shizhi was a native of Xiang in Pei.

entries.zh: 家世素族。
entries.en: His family for generations had been a plain clan.
entries.literal: His family for generations was a plain clan.

entries.zh: 祖奚之，齊晉安王諮議參軍，淮南太守，有能政，齊武帝手詔頻褒賞。
entries.en: His grandfather Xi Zhi had been aide to Qi’s prince of Jin’an and administrator of Huainan, a capable magistrate whom Emperor Wu of Qi repeatedly praised in his own hand.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xi Zhi was Aide-de-Camp to the Prince of Jin'an of Qi and Administrator of Huainan; he had able administration, and Emperor Wu of Qi repeatedly praised and rewarded him in handwritten edicts.

entries.zh: 父景彥，梁尚書左丞、司農卿。
entries.en: His father Jingyan had been Liang’s left vice director of the masters of writing and minister of agriculture.
entries.literal: His father Jingyan was Liang Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十六
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 16
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 16

entries.zh: 王沖字長深，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
entries.literal: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

entries.zh: 祖僧衍，齊侍中。
entries.en: His grandfather Sengyan had been palace attendant of Qi.
entries.literal: His grandfather Sengyan was Palace Attendant of Qi.

entries.zh: 父茂璋，梁給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: His father Maozhang was an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate under Liang.
entries.literal: His father Maozhang was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in Liang.

entries.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
entries.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
entries.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

entries.zh: 年十八，起家梁祕書郎。
entries.en: At eighteen he entered service as a secretary of Liang.
entries.literal: At eighteen he began his career as Secretary of Liang.

entries.zh: 尋為永嘉太守。
entries.en: He was soon made administrator of Yongjia.
entries.literal: Soon he became Administrator of Yongjia.

entries.zh: 入為太子舍人，以父憂去職。
entries.en: He returned to court as mentor to the heir apparent and resigned when his father died.
entries.literal: He entered court as Mentor to the Heir Apparent and left office on his father's death.

entries.zh: 服闋，除太尉臨川王府外兵參軍、東宮領直。
entries.en: After mourning he was named external military aide on the Prince of Linchuan's staff in the Grand Marshal's office and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed External Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Grand Marshal's office and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 累遷太子洗馬、中舍人。
entries.en: He rose to be grand mentor to the heir apparent and attendant to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He rose through Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 出為招遠將軍、衡陽內史。
entries.en: He was posted as General Who Recruits the Distant and interior magistrate of Hengyang.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Recruits the Distant and Interior Magistrate of Hengyang.

entries.zh: 遷武威將軍、安成嗣王長史、長沙內史，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, chief clerk to the heir of Ancheng, and interior magistrate of Changsha, retaining his general's title.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Heir of the Princedom of Ancheng, and Interior Magistrate of Changsha, his rank as general unchanged.

entries.zh: 王薨於湘州，仍以沖監湘州事。
entries.en: When the prince died at Xiangzhou, Chong was left to govern the province.
entries.literal: When the prince died in Xiangzhou, Chong was left to oversee Xiangzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 入為太子庶子。
entries.en: He returned to court as household supporter of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He entered court as Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 大同三年，以帝甥賜爵安東亭侯，[1]邑一百五十戶。
entries.en: In the third year of Datong (537), as kin of the imperial house he was made Marquis of Andong, [1] with a fief of one hundred fifty households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Datong, as the emperor's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Andong ting, with a fief of one hundred fifty households.

entries.zh: 歷明威將軍、南郡太守、太子中庶子、侍中。
entries.en: He held the posts of General of Manifest Prestige, administrator of Nan commandery, household supporter of the heir apparent, and palace attendant.
entries.literal: He served as General of Manifest Prestige, Administrator of Nan commandery, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, and Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 出監吳郡，滿歲即真。
entries.en: He was sent to oversee Wu commandery and, when his term ended, received the substantive appointment.
entries.literal: He went out to oversee Wu commandery; when his term ended he received the actual appointment.

entries.zh: 徵為通直散騎常侍，兼左民尚書。
entries.en: He was recalled as regular attendant of the Secretariat and made concurrent master of the left for the people.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Master of the Left for the People.

entries.zh: 出為明威將軍、輕車當陽公府長史、江夏太守，行郢州事。
entries.en: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, chief clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, administrator of Jiangxia, and acting governor of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, Administrator of Jiangxia, conducting office in Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 遷平西邵陵王長史。
entries.en: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 轉驃騎廬陵王長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling, grand general of cavalry, and administrator of Nan commandery.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, and Administrator of Nan commandery.

entries.zh: 王薨，行州府事。
entries.en: When the prince died, he ran the prefecture and the princely establishment.
entries.literal: When the prince died, he conducted the prefecture and princely establishment affairs.

entries.zh: 梁元帝鎮荊州，為鎮西長史，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he became chief clerk to the establishment pacifying the west, keeping his general's title and his post as administrator.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he was Chief Clerk to the Establishment Pacifying the West, general and administrator unchanged.

entries.zh: 沖性和順，事上謹肅，習於法令，政在平理，佐藩两人，鮮有失德，雖無赫赫之譽，久而見思，由是推重，累居二千石。
entries.en: Chong was mild and obliging, reverent toward his superiors, and skilled in law; his rule was even-handed. Twice he served as an aide to princely establishments and scarcely stained his name. He won no dazzling fame, yet men remembered him long after—so he was held in esteem and repeatedly held governorships.
entries.literal: Chong's nature was gentle and compliant; in serving superiors he was reverent; versed in statutes, his governance fair and orderly; as aide in two princely establishments he rarely failed in virtue; though he won no brilliant renown, over time men came to miss him—thus he was esteemed and repeatedly held office at the two-thousand-shi level.

entries.zh: 又曉音樂，習歌舞，善與人交，貴游之中，聲名藉甚。
entries.en: He also knew music, excelled at song and dance, and made friends easily; among the great families his name rang far.
entries.literal: He also understood music, was skilled in song and dance, and good at friendship; among the noble wanderers his fame was very great.

entries.zh: 梁
entries.en: Liang
entries.literal: Liang

entries.en: (zhi)
entries.literal: (zhi)

entries.zh: [文]帝女新安穆公主早薨 據《南史》改。
entries.en: On "[Wen] Emperor's daughter Princess Xin'an Mu died early": emended per the Southern Dynasties history.
entries.literal: [Wen] Emperor's daughter, Princess Xin'an Mu, died early—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.

entries.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
entries.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
entries.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
entries.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

entries.zh: 作「文」是。
entries.en: "Wen" is the correct reading.
entries.literal: To write "Wen" is correct.

entries.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
entries.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
entries.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

entries.zh: 王通字公達，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
entries.literal: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

entries.zh: 祖份，梁左光祿大夫。
entries.en: His grandfather Fen had been left grand master of the golden sigil under Liang.
entries.literal: His grandfather Fen was Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil of Liang.

entries.zh: 父琳，司徒左長史。
entries.en: His father Lin was left chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: His father Lin was Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
entries.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
entries.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

entries.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
entries.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
entries.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

entries.zh: 又從登北顧樓，賦詩，辭義清典，帝甚嘉之。
entries.en: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose verse; the language was clear and classical, and the emperor praised him warmly.
entries.literal: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose poetry; the diction was clear and canonical; the Emperor greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，梁元帝於荊州承制，沖求解南郡，以讓王僧辯，并獻女妓十人，以助軍賞。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, when Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regime at Jingzhou, Chong asked to give up Nan commandery for Wang Sengbian and sent ten female entertainers as a gift toward the army's expenses.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou assumed the provisional regime; Chong asked to be relieved of Nan commandery to yield it to Wang Sengbian, and also presented ten female entertainers as military reward.

entries.zh: 元帝授持節、督衡桂成合四州諸軍事、雲麾將軍、衡州刺史。
entries.en: Yuan made him bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs over Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and inspector of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: Yuan appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs over the four prefectures Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and Inspector of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 元帝第四子元良為湘州刺史，仍以沖行州事，領長沙內史。
entries.en: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again governed the province while serving as interior magistrate of Changsha.
entries.literal: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was Inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again conducted the province, concurrently Interior Magistrate of Changsha.

entries.zh: 侯景平，授翊左將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: After Jing was suppressed, he was made General Who Assists the Left and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed General Who Assists the Left and Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，奔于江陵，元帝以為散騎常侍，遷守太常卿。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him regular attendant of the Secretariat and then minister of ceremonials.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him Regular Attendant of the Secretariat and promoted him to Minister of Ceremonials.

entries.zh: 自侯景亂後，臺內宮室，嵭皆焚燼，以通兼起部尚書，歸于京師，專掌繕造。
entries.en: After Jing's rebellion the palaces within the capital had all been burned to ash; Tong was made concurrent master of works for construction, returned to the capital, and alone directed the rebuilding.
entries.literal: After Jing's rebellion the palace halls within the capital were all burned to ashes; Tong was made concurrent Master of Works in charge of construction, returned to the capital, and solely managed repairs.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，西奔江陵，元帝承制以為太子中庶子，掌相府管記。
entries.en: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; under Emperor Yuan's provisional regime he was household supporter of the heir apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan's provisional regime made him Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.

entries.zh: 出為寧遠將軍、晉陵太守。
entries.en: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 時兵饑之後，郡中凋弊，勱為政清簡，吏民便安之。
entries.en: After war and famine the commandery lay in ruins; Mo governed plainly and simply, and officials and people alike were at ease.
entries.literal: After troops and famine the commandery was wasted; Mo's government was pure and simple, and officials and people found ease.

entries.zh: 徵為侍中，遷五兵尚書。
entries.en: He was recalled as palace attendant and promoted to minister of war.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and promoted to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 及西魏寇江陵，元帝徵湘州刺史宜豐侯蕭循入援，以勱監湘州。
entries.en: When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned Xiao Xun, Marquis of Yifeng and inspector of Xiangzhou, to reinforce him; Mo was left to oversee the province.
entries.literal: When Western Wei raided Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun, to aid; Mo was left to oversee Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝承制以為中書令。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年加侍中。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai he was added palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 高祖為司空，以勱兼司空長史。
entries.en: When the Founder was minister of works, Mo was concurrently his chief clerk.
entries.literal: When the Founder was Minister of Works, Mo was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 高祖為丞相，
entries.en: When the Founder was chancellor,
entries.literal: When the Founder was Chancellor,

entries.en: (as)
entries.literal: (as)

entries.zh: [勱]兼丞相長史，[5]侍中、中書令嵭如故。
entries.en: Mo was concurrently chief clerk to the chancellor, [5] retaining palace attendant and director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: [Mo] was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Chancellor, Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat unchanged.

entries.zh: 時吳中遭亂，民多乏絕，乃以勱監吳興郡。
entries.en: Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wuxing commandery.
entries.literal: At the time Wu suffered disorder and the people were much in want; Mo was made overseer of Wu commandery of Xing.

entries.zh: 及蕭勃平後，又以勱舊在嶺表，早有政勣，乃授使持節、都督廣州等二十州諸軍事、平南將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: After Xiao Bo was subdued, because Mo had long served in Lingnan with a record of good rule, he was given the staff, command over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, the titles General Who Pacifies the South and General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and the post of inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: After Xiao Bo was pacified, because Mo had long been in Lingnan with earlier administrative merit, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 未行，改為衡州刺史，持節、都督嵭如故。
entries.en: Before he could take up the post he was reassigned to inspector of Hengzhou, with staff and command unchanged.
entries.literal: Before he set out, he was changed to Inspector of Hengzhou, staff and command unchanged.

entries.zh: 王琳據有上流，衡、廣攜貳，勱不得之鎮，留于大庾嶺。
entries.en: Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Heng and Guang were divided in loyalty; Mo could not reach his command and stayed at Dayu Ridge.
entries.literal: Wang Lin held the upper reaches; Heng and Guang wavered; Mo could not reach his post and remained at Dayu Ridge.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，徵為侍中、都官尚書，未拜，復為中書令。
entries.en: In Tianjia year one he was called up as attendant-in-ordinary and minister of capital offenses, but before he took up the post he was again made director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Masters of Writing for Capital Offenses, but before taking office he was again made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 遷太子詹事，行東宮事，侍中嵭如故。
entries.en: He was made tutor to the crown prince and acting head of the eastern palace, keeping his attendant-in-ordinary rank.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting administrator of the Eastern Palace, his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary unchanged.

entries.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫，領度支尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to grandee with the golden horse seal and also directed the revenue office.
entries.literal: He was given the rank of Grandee with the Golden Horse and Grand Seal and concurrently held the post of Director of Revenue.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant as well.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given the additional title of Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 太建元年，遷尚書右僕射。
entries.en: In Taijian year one he was made right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right).

entries.zh: 時東境大水，百姓饑饉，以勱為仁武將軍、晉陵太守。
entries.en: The east was then stricken by flood and famine, and Mo was sent out as benevolent-martial general and administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: At that time the eastern regions suffered great floods and the people were in famine; Mo was made General of Benevolent Martial Might and Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 在郡甚有威惠，郡人表請立碑，頌勱政績，詔許之。
entries.en: He governed Jinling with real authority and kindness; the people petitioned for a stele to his record and the court agreed.
entries.literal: In the commandery he had great authority and kindness; the people of the commandery memorialized requesting a stele to praise Mo's achievements, and an edict approved it.

entries.zh: 徵為中書監，重授尚書右僕射，領右軍將軍。
entries.en: He was recalled as supervisor of the secretariat, again made right vice director of the masters of writing, and given the right army generalship.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Supervisor of the Secretariat, again appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right), and concurrently Right Army General.

entries.zh: 四年五月卒，時年六十七。
entries.en: He died in the fifth month of year four, at sixty-seven.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he died, aged sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、中書監，諡曰溫。
