entries.en: Posthumously he was made attendant-in-ordinary and supervisor of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wen.

entries.zh: 樞字踐言，梁吳郡太守君正之子也。
entries.en: Shu, styled Jianyan, was the son of Junzheng, Liang's administrator of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Shu, courtesy name Jianyan, was the son of Junzheng, Administrator of Wu commandery under Liang.

entries.zh: 美容儀，性沈靜，好讀書，手不釋卷。
entries.en: He was handsome and reserved, loved books, and always had one in hand.
entries.literal: He had fine looks and a calm disposition, loved reading, and never put down his books.

entries.zh: 家世顯貴，貲產充積，而樞獨居處率素，傍無交往，端坐一室，非公事未嘗出遊，榮利之懷淡如也。
entries.en: Though his house was great and rich, Shu lived simply alone, kept no company, and sat in one room; he went out only on duty and cared nothing for rank or gain.
entries.literal: His family for generations had been illustrious and wealthy, yet Shu alone lived plainly; he had no companions at his side, sat upright in a single room, and unless on public business never went abroad—his heart toward glory and profit was utterly indifferent.

entries.zh: 起家梁祕書郎，歷太子舍人，輕車河東王主簿，安前邵陵王、中軍宣
entries.en: He began as a Liang secretariat gentleman, then served as crown prince aide, registrar to the prince of Hedong of the light chariots, and merit clerk in the households of the former prince of Shaoling and the central army prince Xuan
entries.literal: He first entered office as a Liang Secretariat Gentleman, then served as Aide to the Crown Prince, Registrar to the Prince of Hedong of the Light Chariots, and Merit Clerk in the two prefectures of the preceding Prince of Shaoling and the Central Army Prince Xuan

entries.en: (Cheng)
entries.literal: (Cheng)

entries.zh: [城]王二府功曹史。
entries.en: merit clerk in the two establishments of the Prince of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: [City] Wang.

entries.zh: [6]侯景之亂，樞往吳郡省父，因丁父憂。
entries.en: [6] In Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu commandery to see his father and then mourned his father's death.
entries.literal: [6] During Hou Jing's rebellion Shu went to Wu commandery to visit his father and thereupon entered mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 時四方擾亂，人求苟免，樞居喪以至孝聞。
entries.en: The realm was in chaos and men sought only to save themselves, but Shu's mourning won fame for deep filial piety.
entries.literal: At the time the four quarters were in turmoil and men sought only to escape harm; Shu's conduct in mourning became known for supreme filial piety.

entries.zh: 王僧辯平侯景，鎮京城，衣冠爭往造請，樞獨杜門靜居，不求聞達。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian took the capital after defeating Hou Jing, the elite flocked to him; Shu stayed indoors and sought no advancement.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian pacified Hou Jing and held the capital, the gentry all rushed to call on him; Shu alone shut his doors and lived quietly, seeking no fame.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝為太宰，承制以沖為左長史。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang, acting as grand preceptor under the provisional regime, made Chong his left chief clerk.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang as Grand Preceptor assumed the provisional regime and made Chong left chief clerk.

entries.zh: 紹泰中，累遷左光祿大夫、尚書右僕射。
entries.en: In the Shaotai era he rose from left grand master of the golden sigil to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: In the Shaotai era he rose through Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.

entries.zh: 遷左僕射、開府儀同三司，侍中、將軍如故。
entries.en: He was made left vice director and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, retaining palace attendant and his general's title.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant and general unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋復領丹陽尹、南徐州大中正，給扶。
entries.en: Soon he again headed Danyang as intendant and served as grand arbiter of South Xuzhou, with aides granted to support him.
entries.literal: Soon he again headed Danyang as Intendant and Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou, with support staff granted.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，敬帝承制以通為吏部尚書。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong director of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，加侍中，尚書如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he was added palace attendant while keeping the directorship.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant, Director unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋為尚書右僕射，吏部如故。
entries.en: Soon he was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing, still heading personnel.
entries.literal: Soon he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Personnel unchanged.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，遷左僕射，侍中如故。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, he was transferred to left vice director, retaining palace attendant.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was transferred to Left Vice Director, Palace Attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，領太子少傅。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 天康元年，為翊右將軍、右光祿大夫，量置佐史。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he was made General Who Assists the Right and right grand master of the golden sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was General Who Assists the Right and Right Grand Master of the Golden Sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，號安右將軍，又領南徐州大中正。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed grand arbiter of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 太建元年，遷左光祿大夫。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian (569) he was transferred to left grand master of the golden sigil.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.

entries.zh: 六年，加特進，侍中、將軍、光祿、佐史嵭如故。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was given supernumerary privilege; palace attendant, general, grand master, and aides all remained as before.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was given Supernumerary Privilege; Palace Attendant, general, Grand Master, and aides unchanged.

entries.zh: 未拜卒，時年七十二。
entries.en: Before he could enter the new office he died, aged seventy-two.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment he died, aged seventy-two.

entries.zh: 詔贈本官，諡曰成，葬日給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: An edict restored his offices posthumously, gave him the posthumous name Cheng, and granted one set of martial music on the day of burial.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously restored his offices, posthumous name Cheng, and on the burial day granted one set of martial music.

entries.zh: 弟質、弟固各有傳。
entries.en: His younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.
entries.literal: Younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，解尹，以本官領左光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, he left the intendant's post and, in his former rank, headed the left grand master of the golden sigil.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was relieved as Intendant; in his former office he headed Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.

entries.zh: 未拜，改領太子少傅。
entries.en: Before he entered that office he was reassigned to head tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment, he was changed to head Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，解少傅，加特進、左光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as junior tutor and given supernumerary privilege together with the left grand master of the golden sigil.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as Junior Tutor and given Supernumerary Privilege and Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.

entries.zh: 尋又以本官領丹陽尹，參撰律令。
entries.en: Soon, in his former capacity, he again headed Danyang as intendant and took part in compiling statutes and ordinances.
entries.literal: Soon in his former office he again headed Danyang as Intendant and joined in compiling statutes and ordinances.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，給親信十人。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, he was granted ten trusted attendants.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given ten trusted attendants.

entries.zh: 初，高祖以沖前代舊臣，特申長幼之敬。
entries.en: At first the Founder, treating Chong as a veteran of the old court, paid him the special courtesy owed between elder and younger.
entries.literal: At first the Founder, because Chong was an old minister of the previous dynasty, specially showed him the respect due elder and younger.

entries.zh: 文帝即位，益加尊重，嘗從文帝幸司空徐度宅，宴筵之上，賜以几。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the honor grew; once, accompanying the emperor to Minister of Works Xu Du's house, he was given an armrest at the banquet.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, respect increased; once he followed Emperor Wen on a visit to Minister of Works Xu Du's residence, and at the banquet the Emperor gave him an armrest.

entries.zh: 其見重如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Such was the honor shown him.

entries.zh: 光大元年薨，時年七十六。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda (567) he died, aged seventy-six.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda he died, aged seventy-six.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、司空，諡曰元簡。
entries.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuanjian.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, posthumous name Yuancian.

entries.zh: 敬純孝有風格，幼便篤學，老而無倦。
entries.en: Jing was deeply filial and had real bearing. He loved study from childhood and never wearied of it even in old age.
entries.literal: Jing was pure in filial devotion and had character; from childhood he studied earnestly, and in old age he never tired.

entries.zh: 釋褐祕書郎，累遷太子舍人、洗馬、中舍人。
entries.en: He entered office as a secretary gentleman and rose through the posts of crown prince retainer, xima, and central retainer.
entries.literal: He left common dress as a secretary gentleman and rose successively to crown prince retainer, xima, and central retainer.

entries.zh: 江陵淪覆，流寓嶺表。
entries.en: After Jiangling fell, he lived as a refugee beyond the southern passes.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, he drifted into exile beyond the mountains.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，敬在廣州，依歐陽頠。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Jing was in Guangzhou under Ouyang Wei.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Jing was in Guangzhou and attached himself to Ouyang Wei.

entries.zh: 及頠卒，其子紇據州，將有異志，敬累諫紇，為陳逆順之理，言甚切至，紇終不從。
entries.en: After Wei died, his son He held the province and began to think of rebellion. Jing repeatedly remonstrated with him, laying out the case for loyalty to Chen with great urgency, but He refused to listen.
entries.literal: When Wei died, his son He occupied the province and began to harbor rebellious intentions; Jing repeatedly remonstrated with He, explaining the principles of rebellion and obedience toward Chen in extremely urgent words, but He would not listen.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，遣章昭達率眾討紇，紇將敗之時，恨不納敬言。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he sent Zhang Zhaoda with an army against He. As defeat closed in, He regretted not having listened to Jing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he sent Zhang Zhaoda to lead the forces against He; when He was about to be defeated, he regretted not accepting Jing's words.

entries.zh: 朝廷義之，其年徵為太子中庶子、通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: The court honored his loyalty, and that year summoned him as central household supporter to the crown prince and regular attendant of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The court regarded him as righteous and that year summoned him as central commoner of the crown prince and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry for direct service.

entries.zh: 俄轉司徒左長史。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to left chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to left chief clerk of the minister over the masses.

entries.zh: 尋遷左民尚書，轉都官尚書，領豫州大中正。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to minister for the left population, then transferred to minister of justice and made grand arbiter of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: He was soon promoted to minister of left people, transferred to minister of capital officials, and headed the grand arbiter of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 累遷太常卿、散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，加特進。
entries.en: He rose through chamberlain for ceremonials, regular attendant of the Secretariat, and grand master of glorious happiness with gold and purple, and received supernumerary privilege.
entries.literal: He rose successively to chamberlain for ceremonials, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and grand master of glorious happiness with gold and purple, and was given special advancement.

entries.zh: 至德三年卒，時年七十九，贈左光祿大夫，諡曰靖德。
entries.en: He died in Zhide year 3, aged seventy-nine. He was posthumously made left grand master of glorious happiness and given the posthumous name Jingde.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhide he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously granted left grand master of glorious happiness and given the posthumous name Jingde.

entries.zh: 子元友嗣。
entries.en: His son Yuanyou succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Yuanyou succeeded.

entries.zh: 弟泌自有傳。
entries.en: His younger brother Mi has his own biography.
entries.literal: His younger brother Mi has his own biography.

entries.zh: 兄子樞。
entries.en: His nephew, his elder brother's son, was Shu.
entries.literal: His elder brother's son was Shu.

entries.zh: 樞博聞彊識，明悉舊章。
entries.en: Shu was widely read, had a strong memory, and knew the old rules well.
entries.literal: Shu was broadly learned with a strong memory and clearly understood old regulations.

entries.zh: 初，高祖長女永世公主先適陳留太守錢蕆，生子岊，[7]主及岊嵭卒于梁世。
entries.en: Earlier the Founder's eldest daughter, Princess Yongshi, had married Qian Yi, administrator of Chenliu, and borne a son Jie; [7] both princess and son had died under Liang.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Founder's eldest daughter, Princess Yongshi, had first been married to Qian Yi, Administrator of Chenliu, and bore a son Jie; [7] the princess and Jie had both died in the Liang era.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，唯公主追封。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, only the princess received a posthumous enfeoffment.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, only the princess was posthumously enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 至是將葬，尚書主客請詳議，欲加蕆駙馬都尉，并贈岊官。
entries.en: As burial approached, the host-guests office of the masters of writing asked for a full ruling, proposing to make Yi commandant of the consort's carriage and to grant Jie an office as well.
entries.literal: At this time she was about to be buried; the Host-Guests Office of the Masters of Writing requested detailed deliberation, wishing to add Yi as Commandant of the Consort's Carriage and also to bestow an office on Jie.

entries.zh: 樞議曰：「昔王姬下嫁，必適諸侯，同姓為主，[8]聞於公羊之說，車服不繫，顯於詩人之篇。
entries.en: Shu argued: "Anciently a king's daughter married down only to feudal lords; that the chief wife share the surname [8] is in the Gongyang school, and that carriage and dress not be bound to rank appears in the Odes.
entries.literal: Shu argued: "In antiquity when a king's daughter married down, she was always given to a feudal lord; that the chief wife be of the same surname [8] is heard in the Gongyang tradition, and that chariots and dress not be tied to rank is plain in the poets' odes.

entries.zh: 漢氏初興，列侯尚主，自斯以後，降嬪素族。
entries.en: At Han's rise marquises married imperial daughters; afterward princesses wed common families.
entries.literal: When the Han house first rose, marquises married imperial daughters; from then on princesses were married down to plain clans.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武，[9]或以假諸功臣，或以加於戚屬，是以魏曹植表駙馬、奉車趣為一號。
entries.en: The consort commandant was created by Han Wudi; [9] it was sometimes given to meritorious ministers and sometimes to kin—hence Cao Zhi in Wei asked to merge consort commandant and carriage attendant into one title.
entries.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han; [9] sometimes it was lent to meritorious ministers, sometimes added for kin—hence in Wei, Cao Zhi petitioned to make the consort commandant and the carriage attendant a single title.

entries.zh: 齊職儀曰，凡尚公主必拜駙馬都尉，魏、晉以來，因為瞻準。
entries.en: The Qi office regulations say that a princess's husband must be made consort commandant; from Wei and Jin on that was the rule.
entries.literal: The Qi Regulations of Offices say that whoever marries a princess must receive the title Commandant of the Consort's Carriage; from Wei and Jin onward this became the standard.

entries.zh: 蓋以王姬之重，庶姓之輕，若不加其等級，寧可合劜而酳，所以假駙馬之位，乃崇於皇女也。
entries.en: A king's daughter outranked a common house; without raising the husband's rank they could not share the marriage cup—so the consort commandant honored the princess.
entries.literal: This was because the king's daughter is weighty and a common surname is light: if her husband's rank were not raised, how could they share the cup and drink together? Hence the borrowed post of consort commandant was meant to honor the imperial daughter.

entries.zh: 今公主早薨，伉儷已絕，既無禮數致疑，何須駙馬之授？
entries.en: The princess is long dead and the marriage ended; with no ritual issue left, why grant a consort commandant?
entries.literal: Now the princess died early and the marriage bond is severed; since no ritual question remains, why is the consort commandant needed?

entries.zh: 案杜預尚晉宣帝第二女高陵宣公主，晉武踐祚，而主已亡，泰始中追贈公主，元凱無復駙馬之號。
entries.en: Du Yu married Jin Xuandi's second daughter, Princess Gao Ling Xuan; when Jin Wudi came to the throne she was already dead, and though she was enfeoffed posthumously in Taishi, Yu was never called consort commandant.
entries.literal: Consider Du Yu, who married the second daughter of Jin's Emperor Xuan, Princess Gao Ling Xuan; when Jin's Emperor Wu took the throne the princess was already dead, and in the Taishi era she was posthumously enfeoffed as princess—Yu received no consort commandant title.

entries.zh: 梁
entries.en: Liang
entries.literal: Liang

entries.en: (zhi)
entries.literal: (zhi)

entries.zh: [文]帝女新安穆公主早薨，[10]天監初王氏無追拜之事。
entries.en: [Wen] Emperor's daughter Princess Xin'an Mu died young; [10] at the start of Tianjian the Wangs were given no retrospective title.
entries.literal: [Wen] Emperor's daughter, Princess Xin'an Mu, died early; [10] at the beginning of Tianjian the Wang clan received no retrospective appointment.

entries.zh: 遠近二例，足以據明。
entries.en: These two cases, ancient and recent, are proof enough.
entries.literal: These two precedents, near and far, suffice as proof.

entries.zh: 公主所生，既未及成人之禮，無勞此授，今宜追贈亭侯。」
entries.en: The princess's son had not reached adulthood and needs no such title; he should be enfeoffed posthumously as marquis of ting."
entries.literal: The princess's son had not yet reached the rites of adulthood, so this appointment is needless; now he should be posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Ting."

entries.zh: 時以樞議為長。
entries.en: The court followed Shu's opinion.
entries.literal: At the time Shu's argument was adopted.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉置由漢武 「由」字原本漫漶，今據各本補。
entries.en: On "consort commandant established by Han Wudi": the character you was faded in the base text and is restored from other editions.
entries.literal: The post of Commandant of the Consort's Carriage was established by Emperor Wu of Han—the character "by" in the original was effaced; it is now supplied from the various editions.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十七
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 17
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 17

entries.zh: 沈眾 袁泌 劉仲威 陸山才 王質 韋載 族弟翽
entries.en: Shen Zhong; Yuan Bi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi; Wei Zai; younger clansman Hui
entries.literal: Shen Zhong; Yuan Bi; Liu Zhongwei; Lu Shancai; Wang Zhi; Wei Zai; younger clansman Hui

entries.zh: 沈眾字仲師，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Shen Zhong, styled Zhongshi, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Shen Zhong, styled Zhongshi, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 祖約，梁特進。
entries.en: His grandfather Yue had been Liang's special grand master.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yue was Liang Special Grand Master.

entries.zh: 父旋，梁給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: His father Xuan was an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate under Liang.
entries.literal: His father Xuan was Liang Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 眾好學，頗有文詞，起家梁鎮衛南平王法曹參軍、太子舍人。
entries.en: Zhong loved study and wrote well. He entered service as registrar to the Prince of Nanping of the garrison guard and as household retainer to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Zhong loved learning and had considerable literary skill; he began his career as Registrar to the Prince of Nanping of the Garrison Guard and Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 是時，梁武帝制千字詩，眾為之注解。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Liang composed the Thousand-Character Poem, Zhong annotated it.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wu of Liang composed the Thousand-Character Poem, and Zhong wrote a commentary on it.

entries.zh: 與陳郡謝景同時召見于文德殿，帝令眾為竹賦，賦成，奏，帝善之，手敕答曰：[1]「卿文體翩翩，可謂無忝爾祖。」
entries.en: He and Xie Jing of Chen were summoned together to the Wende Hall. The emperor ordered Zhong to write a rhapsody on bamboo; when it was done he presented it, and the emperor praised it and wrote back in his own hand: [1] "Your style flows lightly—you truly do no dishonor to your ancestor."
entries.literal: He and Xie Jing of Chen commandery were summoned together to the Wende Hall; the Emperor ordered Zhong to compose a bamboo rhapsody; when it was finished he presented it; the Emperor praised it and replied by hand-edict: "Your literary style is light and graceful—you truly do no dishonor to your ancestor."

entries.zh: 當陽公蕭大心為郢州刺史，以眾為限內記室參軍。
entries.en: The Duke of Dangyang, Xiao Daxin, became inspector of Yingzhou and made Zhong his recorder within the commandery limits.
entries.literal: The Duke of Dangyang, Xiao Daxin, was made Inspector of Yingzhou and appointed Zhong Recorder within the commandery limits.

entries.zh: 尋除鎮南湘東王記室參軍。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong, pacifier of the south.
entries.literal: Soon he was removed and made Recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong, Pacifier of the South.

entries.zh: 遷太子中舍人，兼散騎常侍。
entries.en: He rose to household retainer in the heir's palace and was concurrently made regular attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Household Retainer in the Heir Apparent's palace, concurrently Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 聘魏，還，遷驃騎廬陵王諮議參軍，舍人如故。
entries.en: After an embassy to Wei he was made adviser to the Prince of Luling of the flying cavalry, retaining his post as retainer.
entries.literal: On embassy to Wei he returned and was made Adviser to the Prince of Luling of the Flying Cavalry and kept his post as retainer.

entries.zh: 景平，西上荊州，元帝以為太子中庶子、本州大中正。
entries.en: After Jing was suppressed, Zhong went west to Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan of Liang made him household retainer to the heir apparent and grand arbiter of his native province.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, Zhong went west to Jingzhou; Emperor Yuan of Liang made him Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent and Grand Arbiter of his native province.

entries.zh: 尋遷司徒左長史。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to left chief clerk to the minister of education.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，為西魏所虜，尋而逃還，敬帝承制，授御史中丞。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell he was captured by Western Wei, but soon escaped. Emperor Jing of Liang, under the provisional regime, made him censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell he was taken captive by Western Wei; soon he escaped and returned; Emperor Jing of Liang under the provisional regime appointed him Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，除侍中，遷左民尚書。
entries.en: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he was made palace attendant and promoted to master of the left for the people.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was made Palace Attendant and promoted to Master of the Left for the People.

entries.zh: 高祖受命，遷中書令，中正如故。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Zhong was made director of the Secretariat, retaining his post as grand arbiter.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Zhong was made Director of the Secretariat, grand arbiter unchanged.

entries.zh: 高祖以眾州里知名，甚敬重之，賞賜優渥，超於時輩。
entries.en: The Founder, knowing Zhong's name in his own country, honored him deeply, heaped gifts on him, and favored him above his peers.
entries.literal: Because Zhong was renowned in the Founder's home region, the Founder greatly respected him, favored him with generous gifts, and treated him above his contemporaries.

entries.zh: 眾性吝嗇，內治產業，財帛以億計，無所分遺。
entries.en: Zhong was miserly by nature. He amassed estates at home until his wealth in coin and silk reached hundreds of millions, yet gave nothing away.
entries.literal: Zhong was by nature miserly; inwardly he built up estates, and his wealth in coin and silk ran to hundreds of millions, yet he shared nothing with others.

entries.zh: 其自奉養甚薄，每於朝會之中，衣裳破裂，或躬提冠屨。
entries.en: He lived on almost nothing. At court his robes were often in tatters, and sometimes he carried his own cap and shoes.
entries.literal: He supported himself very meagerly; at court assemblies his clothes were often torn, and sometimes he carried his own cap and shoes.

entries.zh: 永定二年，兼起部尚書，監起太極殿。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongding (558) he was concurrently made minister of works for construction and oversaw the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was concurrently made Minister of Works for Construction and supervised the building of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 恆服布袍芒屩，以麻繩為帶，又攜乾魚蔬菜飯獨噉之，朝士共誚其所為。
entries.en: He always wore a cloth robe and straw sandals, bound himself with a hemp cord, and ate dried fish and vegetables alone. The gentlemen at court mocked him for it.
entries.literal: He always wore a cloth robe and straw sandals, used hemp rope for a belt, and carried dried fish and vegetables for his lone meal; court gentlemen together mocked his conduct.

entries.zh: [3]眾性狷急，於是忿恨，遂歷詆公卿，非毀朝廷。
entries.en: Zhong was narrow and hot-tempered. Stung by the mockery, he turned on the court, slandering dukes and ministers and reviling the government.
entries.literal: Zhong was by nature narrow and quick-tempered; thereupon in resentment he went through the ranks slandering the dukes and ministers and reviling the court.

entries.zh: 高祖大怒，以眾素有令望，不欲顯誅之，後因其休假還武康，遂於吳中賜死，時年五十六。
entries.en: The Founder was furious. Because Zhong still enjoyed a fine name, he would not kill him openly; later, when Zhong took leave to return to Wukang, he was ordered to die by his own hand in Wu. He was fifty-six.
entries.literal: The Founder was greatly angered; because Zhong had long enjoyed a fine reputation, he did not wish to execute him openly; later, on a leave to return to Wukang, he was ordered to take his own life in Wu, aged fifty-six.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，眾表於梁武，稱家代所隸故義部曲，並在吳興，求還召募以討賊，梁武許之。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong memorialized Emperor Wu of Liang, saying the loyal household troops his line had long commanded were in Wuxing, and asked leave to return and raise them against the rebel. The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong memorialized Emperor Wu of Liang, saying that the righteous household troops his family had long commanded were all in Wuxing, and asked to return to recruit them to attack the rebel; Emperor Wu approved.

entries.zh: 及景圍臺城，[2]眾率宗族及義附五千餘人，入援京邑，頓于小航，對賊東府置陣，軍容甚整，景深憚之。
entries.en: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, [2] Zhong led his kinsmen and volunteer followers—more than five thousand men—to relieve the capital. He encamped at Little Ferry and formed ranks opposite the rebels' Eastern Mansion. His troops were tightly arrayed, and Jing feared him greatly.
entries.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Zhong led his clansmen and volunteer followers—more than five thousand men—to reinforce the capital, encamped at Little Ferry, and drew up battle lines opposite the rebel Eastern Mansion; his army's bearing was very orderly, and Jing deeply feared him.

entries.zh: 梁武於城內遙授眾為太子右衛率。
entries.en: From within the city Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Zhong right commandant of the heir's guard by remote commission.
entries.literal: From within the city Emperor Wu of Liang remotely appointed Zhong Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

entries.zh: 京城陷，眾降於景。
entries.en: When the capital fell, Zhong surrendered to Jing.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, Zhong surrendered to Jing.

entries.zh: 王質字子貞，右光祿大夫通之弟也。
entries.en: Wang Zhi, styled Zizhen, was the younger brother of right grand master of the golden sigil Tong.
entries.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Zizhen, was the younger brother of Right Grand Master of the Golden Sigil Tong.

entries.zh: 少慷慨，涉獵書史。
entries.en: In youth he was bold and generous and read widely in books and histories.
entries.literal: In youth he was bold and generous and ranged widely in books and histories.

entries.zh: 梁世以武帝甥封甲口亭侯，補國子周易生，射策高第。
entries.en: Under Liang, as the emperor's sister's son, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiakou and studied the Book of Changes at the national university, ranking high in the archery examination.
entries.literal: In Liang times, as Emperor Wu's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Jiakou ting, entered the National University as student of the Book of Changes, and ranked high in the archery examination.

entries.zh: 起家祕書郎、太子舍人、尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: He began as secretary, household retainer to the heir apparent, and gentleman of the palace hall.
entries.literal: He began his career as Secretary, Household Retainer to the Heir Apparent, and Gentleman of the Palace Hall.

entries.zh: 遭母憂，居喪以孝聞。
entries.en: When his mother died he mourned her and was known for filial piety.
entries.literal: On his mother's death he observed mourning and was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 服闋，除太子洗馬、東宮領直。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was made mentor to the heir apparent and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 累遷中舍人、庶子。
entries.en: He rose through household retainer and household mentor.
entries.literal: He rose through Household Retainer and Household Mentor.

entries.zh: 仲威從弟廣德，亦好學，負才任氣。
entries.en: Zhongwei's younger cousin Guangde also loved learning and was confident in his talent and spirit.
entries.literal: Zhongwei's younger cousin Guangde also loved learning and relied on his talent and spirit.

entries.zh: 父之亨，梁安西湘東王長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: His father Zhiheng was chief clerk to Liang's Prince of Xiangdong, general who secures the west, and administrator of Nanjun.
entries.literal: His father Zhiheng was chief clerk to Liang's Prince of Xiangdong, general who secures the west, and administrator of Nanjun.

entries.zh: 廣德，承聖中以軍功官至給事黃門侍郎、湘東太守。
entries.en: During Chengsheng, Guangde rose through military merit to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and administrator of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: During Chengsheng, Guangde rose through military merit to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and administrator of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 荊州陷後，依于王琳。
entries.en: After Jingzhou fell, he attached himself to Wang Lin.
entries.literal: After Jingzhou fell, he attached himself to Wang Lin.

entries.zh: 琳平，文帝以廣德為寧遠始興王府限外記室參軍，仍領其舊兵。
entries.en: After Lin was pacified, Emperor Wen made Guangde extra-allowance records aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant, while letting him continue to command his old troops.
entries.literal: When Lin was pacified, Emperor Wen made Guangde extra-allowance records aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant, and let him continue to command his old troops.

entries.zh: 尋為太尉侯瑱湘州府司馬，歷樂山、豫章二郡太守，新安內史。
entries.en: Soon he became army marshal in the Xiangzhou office of Grand Commandant Hou Tian, and served in turn as administrator of Leshan and Yuzhang and interior minister of Xin'an.
entries.literal: Soon he became army marshal in the Xiangzhou office of Grand Commandant Hou Tian, and served in turn as administrator of Leshan and Yuzhang and interior minister of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 光大中，假節、員外散騎常侍、雲旗將軍、河東太守。
entries.en: During Guangda he became acting credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Hedong.
entries.literal: During Guangda he was acting credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Hedong.

entries.zh: 太建元年卒於郡，時年四十三，贈左衛將軍。
entries.en: In Taijian year 1 (569), he died in the commandery, aged forty-three, and was posthumously made left guard general.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 1 he died in the commandery, aged forty-three, and was posthumously presented as left guard general.

entries.zh: 京城陷後，西奔荊州，元帝承制，以質為右長史，帶河東太守。
entries.en: After the capital fell he fled west to Jingzhou. Emperor Yuan of Liang, under the provisional regime, made him right chief clerk and administrator of Hedong.
entries.literal: After the capital fell he fled west to Jingzhou; Emperor Yuan of Liang under the provisional regime made him Right Chief Clerk, concurrently Administrator of Hedong.

entries.zh: 俄遷侍中。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to palace attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 尋出為持節、都督吳州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、吳州刺史，領鄱陽內史。
entries.en: He was soon sent out with the staff as commander of military affairs over Wu, General Who Pacifies the Distance, inspector of Wu, and interior magistrate of Poyang.
entries.literal: Soon he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs over Wu province, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Inspector of Wu, concurrently Interior Magistrate of Poyang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝承制以為中書侍郎。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan of Liang, ruling provisionally, made him attendant of the secretariat.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang, assuming the provisional regime, made him Attendant of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 尋為建威將軍、尋陽太守，隨都督王僧辯東討侯景。
entries.en: He was soon made general who establishes might and administrator of Xunyang, marching east under Wang Sengbian against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: Soon he became General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xunyang, following the area commander Wang Sengbian east to attack Hou Jing.

entries.zh: 是時僧辯軍于湓城，而魯悉達、樊俊等各擁兵保境，觀望成敗。
entries.en: Sengbian then lay at Pencheng; Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held their districts with troops and waited to see who would win.
entries.literal: At that time Sengbian's army was at Pencheng, while Lu Sidada, Fan Jun, and others each held troops guarding their borders, watching the outcome.

entries.zh: 元帝以載為假節、都督太原高唐新蔡三郡諸軍事、高唐太守。
entries.en: Yuan made Zai acting commander with staff over Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai and administrator of Gaotang.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan made Zai Acting with Staff, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the three commanderies of Taiyuan, Gaotang, and Xincai, and Administrator of Gaotang.

entries.zh: 仍銜命喻悉達等令出軍討景。
entries.en: He was also charged to win Sidada and the rest over and bring them out against Hou Jing.
entries.literal: He still bore orders to persuade Sidada and the others to take the field and attack Jing.

entries.zh: 及大軍東下，載率三郡兵自焦湖出柵口，與僧辯會于梁山。
entries.en: When the main force moved east, Zai led the three commanderies' men from Jiao Lake through Shankou to meet Sengbian at Mount Liang.
entries.literal: When the great army marched east, Zai led the troops of the three commanderies out from Jiao Lake through Shankou and joined Sengbian at Mount Liang.

entries.zh: 景平，除冠軍將軍、琅邪太守。
entries.en: After Hou Jing fell he was made champion general and administrator of Langye.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was made General Who Champions and Administrator of Langye.

entries.zh: 尋奉使往東陽、晉安，招撫留異、陳寶應等。
entries.en: He was soon sent to Dongyang and Jin'an to bring Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others over.
entries.literal: Soon he was sent on mission to Dongyang and Jin'an to win over and pacify Liu Yi, Chen Baoying, and others.

entries.zh: 仍授信武將軍、義興太守。
entries.en: He was then made trustworthy-martial general and administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: He was then made Trustworthy Martial General and Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，泌欲求為將。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Bi sought a military command.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Bi wished to become a general.

entries.zh: 是時泌兄君正為吳郡太守，梁簡文板泌為東宮領直，令往吳中召募士卒。
entries.en: At that time his elder brother Junzheng was administrator of Wu commandery. Emperor Jianwen of Liang commissioned Bi as leader of direct service in the eastern palace and sent him to Wu to raise troops.
entries.literal: At that time Bi's elder brother Junzheng was Administrator of Wu commandery; Emperor Jianwen of Liang commissioned Bi as Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace and ordered him to Wu to recruit soldiers.

entries.zh: 及景圍臺城，泌率所領赴援。
entries.en: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Bi led his command to the relief.
entries.literal: When Jing besieged the Terrace City, Bi led the men under his command to the relief.

entries.zh: 京城陷，退保東陽，景使兵追之，乃自會稽東嶺出湓城，依于鄱陽嗣王蕭範。
entries.en: When the capital fell he fell back to Dongyang. Jing sent troops after him; Bi slipped out by the eastern pass of Kuaiji through Tangcheng and joined the heir of Poyang, Xiao Fan.
entries.literal: When the capital fell he withdrew to hold Dongyang; Jing sent troops in pursuit, and he went out by the eastern pass of Kuaiji through Tangcheng and attached himself to the Heir of Poyang, Xiao Fan.

entries.zh: 範卒，泌乃降景。
entries.en: When Fan died, Bi surrendered to Jing.
entries.literal: When Fan died, Bi thereupon surrendered to Jing.

entries.zh: 太清元年，除假節、寧遠將軍，領東宮兵，從貞陽侯北伐。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiqing (547) he was given the staff as General Who Pacifies the Distance, led the eastern palace troops on the Marquis of Zhenyang's northern campaign.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was made Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the Distance and led the Eastern Palace troops in the Marquis of Zhenyang's northern campaign.

entries.zh: 及貞陽敗績，質脫身逃還。
entries.en: When Zhenyang was beaten, Zhi slipped away and returned.
entries.literal: When Zhenyang was defeated, Zhi escaped and returned.

entries.zh: 侯景於壽陽構逆，質又領舟師隨眾軍拒之。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled at Shouyang, Zhi again led the river fleet with the allied armies to block him.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled at Shouyang, Zhi again led the river forces with the massed armies to resist him.

entries.zh: 景軍濟江，質便退走。
entries.en: When Jing's army crossed the Yangzi, Zhi at once fell back.
entries.literal: When Jing's army crossed the river, Zhi at once withdrew.

entries.zh: 尋領步騎頓于宣陽門外。
entries.en: He soon led foot and horse and encamped outside the Xuanyang Gate.
entries.literal: Soon he led infantry and cavalry and encamped outside the Xuanyang Gate.

entries.zh: 景軍至京師，質不戰而潰，乃翦髮為桑門，潛匿人間。
entries.en: When Jing's army reached the capital, Zhi did not fight; his troops broke and he shaved his head as a monk and hid among the people.
entries.literal: When Jing's army reached the capital, Zhi did not fight and his troops collapsed; he then shaved his head as a monk and hid among the people.

entries.zh: 及柳仲禮等會援京邑，軍據南岸，質又收合餘眾從之。
entries.en: When Liu Zhongli and others united to relieve the capital, their army held the south bank. Zhi again gathered the remnant troops and joined them.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhongli and the others united to relieve the capital, the army held the south bank; Zhi again gathered the remaining troops and joined them.

entries.zh: 景平，王僧辯表泌為富春太守，兼丹陽尹。
entries.en: After Jing was suppressed, Wang Sengbian recommended Bi as administrator of Fuchun and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, Wang Sengbian memorialized that Bi be made Administrator of Fuchun, concurrently Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，以泌為侍中，奉使於齊。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Zhenyang seized the throne, Bi was made palace attendant and sent as envoy to Qi.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne, Bi was made Palace Attendant and sent on embassy to Qi.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳據有上流，泌自齊從梁永嘉王蕭莊達琳所。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi. Bi came from Qi with Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, to join Lin.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Wang Lin held the upper reaches; Bi came from Qi with Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, to Lin's camp.

entries.zh: 及莊僭立，[4]以泌為侍中、丞相長史。
entries.en: When Zhuang declared himself emperor, [4] Bi was made palace attendant and chief clerk to the chancellor.
entries.literal: When Zhuang usurped the throne, Bi was made Palace Attendant and Chief Clerk to the Chancellor.

entries.zh: [5]天嘉二年，泌與琳輔莊至于柵口，琳軍敗，[6]眾皆奔散，唯泌獨乘輕舟送莊達于北境，屬莊於御史中丞劉仲威，令共入齊，然後拜辭而歸，詣闕請罪，文帝深義之。
entries.en: [5] In Tianjia year 2 (561), Bi and Lin escorted Zhuang to Zhakou. Lin's army was broken; [6] the troops fled in all directions. Bi alone took a light boat, saw Zhuang to the northern frontier, and placed him in the care of censor-in-chief Liu Zhongwei to enter Qi together. Then he bowed farewell, returned, and presented himself to confess fault. Emperor Wen held his conduct in high esteem.
entries.literal: [5] In Tianjia year 2, Bi and Lin escorted Zhuang to Zhakou. Lin's army was broken; [6] the troops fled in all directions. Bi alone took a light boat, saw Zhuang to the northern frontier, and placed him in the care of censor-in-chief Liu Zhongwei to enter Qi together. Then he bowed farewell, returned, and presented himself to confess fault. Emperor Wen held his conduct in high esteem.

entries.zh: 徐嗣徽、任約等引齊軍濟江，據石頭城，高祖問計於載，載曰：「齊軍若分兵先據三吳之路，略地東境，則時事去矣。
entries.en: Xu Sihui and Ren Yue brought Qi troops across the Yangzi and held Stone City. The Founder asked Zai's advice. Zai said, "If Qi splits its army and first takes the routes through the Three Wu and raids the east, the cause is lost.
entries.literal: Xu Sihui, Ren Yue, and others brought Qi troops across the river and held Stone City; the Founder asked Zai for a plan, and Zai said: "If the Qi army divides its forces and first seizes the roads of the Three Wu, overrunning the eastern borderlands, then the times are lost.

entries.zh: 今可急於淮南即侯景故壘築城，以通東道轉輸，別命輕兵絕其糧運，使進無所虜，退無所資，則齊將之首，旬日可致。」
entries.en: We should hurry to build a fort on the Huai at Hou Jing's old site to keep the eastern line open, and send light troops to cut their supplies so they cannot feed an advance or a retreat. Then the Qi commanders' heads will be ours within ten days."
entries.literal: Now we should quickly build a city on the Huai at Hou Jing's old rampart to open the eastern supply route, and separately order light troops to cut their grain transport, so that advancing they have nothing to seize and retreating they have nothing to rely on—then the heads of the Qi generals can be had within ten days."

entries.zh: 高祖從其計。
entries.en: The Founder took his advice.
entries.literal: The Founder followed his plan.

entries.zh: 高祖誅王僧辯，乃遣周文育輕兵襲載，未至而載先覺，乃嬰城自守。
entries.en: After the Founder killed Wang Sengbian he sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops against Zai. Zai saw it coming first and shut the city to resist.
entries.literal: The Founder executed Wang Sengbian and then sent Zhou Wenyü with light troops to strike Zai; before they arrived Zai had already sensed it and walled the city to hold out.

entries.zh: 文育攻之甚急，載所屬縣卒並高祖舊兵，多善用弩，載收得數十人，繫以長鎖，命所親監之，使射文育軍，約曰十發不兩中者則死，每發輒中，所中皆斃。
entries.en: Wenyü attacked hard. Zai's county levies were many of the Founder's old soldiers and crack crossbowmen. He took several dozen, chained them in a row, set trusted men over them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's host on pain of death if they missed twice in ten tries. Every bolt found its mark and every man hit went down.
entries.literal: Wenyü pressed the attack fiercely; the district soldiers under Zai were all the Founder's old troops and many were skilled with crossbows. Zai gathered several dozen men, bound them with long chains, had those he trusted supervise them, and made them shoot at Wenyü's army, stipulating that any who failed to hit twice in ten shots would die; every shot struck, and all who were hit fell dead.

entries.zh: 文育軍稍卻，因於城外據水立柵，相持數旬。
entries.en: Wenyü's men gave ground. He threw up a river palisade outside the walls, and the two sides stood off for weeks.
entries.literal: Wenyü's army gradually fell back; he therefore took the water outside the city and set up a palisade, and they faced each other for several tens of days.

entries.zh: 高祖聞文育軍不利，乃自將征之，剋其水柵。
entries.en: Hearing Wenyü was losing, the Founder came in person, stormed the river camp, and broke it.
entries.literal: The Founder heard that Wenyü's army was faring ill and then personally led a campaign against him, storming the water palisade.

entries.zh: 仍遣載族弟翽賷書喻載以誅王僧辯意，并奉梁敬帝敕，敕載解兵。
entries.en: He then sent Zai's cousin Hui with a letter explaining why Wang Sengbian had been killed and with an edict from Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to lay down arms.
entries.literal: He then sent Zai's clansman Hui bearing a letter to explain to Zai the reason for executing Wang Sengbian, and also presented an edict of Emperor Jing of Liang ordering Zai to disarm.

entries.zh: [11]載得書，乃以其眾降于高祖。
entries.en: [11] Zai opened the letter and surrendered with his force to the Founder.
entries.literal: [11] When Zai received the letter, he thereupon led his troops in surrender to the Founder.

entries.zh: 高祖厚加撫慰，即以其族弟翽監義興郡，所部將帥，並隨才任使，引載恆置左右，與之謀議。
entries.en: The Founder treated him generously, set his cousin Hui over Yixing, placed his officers each where he could best use them, and kept Zai at his side for counsel.
entries.literal: The Founder greatly comforted and reassured him, immediately put his clansman Hui in charge of Yixing commandery, assigned all the generals and officers under him according to their talents, and kept Zai always at his side to consult with him.

entries.zh: 永定元年，除和戎將軍、通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Yongding year 1 (557), he was appointed general who harmonizes with the Rong and regular attendant of direct communication.
entries.literal: In Yongding year 1, he was appointed general who harmonizes with the Rong and regular attendant of direct communication.

entries.zh: 二年，進號輕車將軍。
entries.en: In year 2, his title was advanced to light-chariot general.
entries.literal: In year 2, his title was advanced to light-chariot general.

entries.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、太子右衛率，將軍如故。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and right guard commandant to the crown prince, with his general title unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and right guard commandant to the crown prince, with his general title as before.

entries.zh: 永定二年，高祖命質率所部踰嶺出豫章，隨都督周文育以討王琳。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongding (558) the Founder ordered Zhi to lead his command over the mountains into Yuzhang and follow Commander Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongding the Founder ordered Zhi to lead his command over the ridge into Yuzhang and follow Commander Zhou Wenyu against Wang Lin.

entries.zh: 質與琳素善，或譖云於軍中潛信交通，高祖命周文育殺質，文育啟請救之，獲免。
entries.en: Zhi and Lin had long been friends. Some accused him of secret correspondence with Lin in the field. The Founder ordered Zhou Wenyu to execute him; Wenyu pleaded for his life and he was spared.
entries.literal: Zhi and Lin had long been on good terms; some slandered him, saying that in the army he secretly corresponded with Lin; the Founder ordered Zhou Wenyu to kill Zhi; Wenyu memorialized to plead for his life, and he was spared.

entries.zh: 尋授散騎常侍、晉陵太守。
entries.en: He was soon made regular attendant and administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant and Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 山才少倜儻，好尚文史，范陽張（續）纘，[8]（續）纘弟綰，並欽重之。
entries.en: In youth Shancai was free-spirited and fond of letters and history. Zhang (Xu)Zuan of Fanyang [8] and Zuan's younger brother Wan both esteemed him highly.
entries.literal: Shancai as a youth was free-spirited and valued letters and history; Zhang (Xu)Zuan of Fanyang, [8] and Zuan's younger brother Wan, both esteemed him highly.

entries.zh: 起家王國常侍，遷外兵參軍。
entries.en: He began as regular attendant in a princely state and was transferred to outer-troops aide.
entries.literal: He began as regular attendant in a princely state and was transferred to outer-troops aide.

entries.zh: 尋以父疾，東歸侍養。
entries.en: Soon, because his father was ill, he returned east to care for him.
entries.literal: Soon, because his father was ill, he returned east to serve and care for him.

entries.zh: 承聖元年，王僧辯授山才儀同府西曹掾。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year 1 (552), Wang Sengbian appointed Shancai western bureau clerk in the Yitong office.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year 1, Wang Sengbian appointed Shancai western bureau clerk in the Yitong office.

entries.zh: 高祖誅僧辯，山才奔會稽依張彪。
entries.en: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Shancai fled to Kuaiji and attached himself to Zhang Biao.
entries.literal: When the Founder killed Sengbian, Shancai fled to Kuaiji and depended on Zhang Biao.

entries.zh: 彪敗，乃歸高祖。
entries.en: When Biao was defeated, Shancai submitted to the Founder.
entries.literal: When Biao was defeated, he then submitted to Gaozu.

entries.zh: 袁泌字文洋，左光祿大夫敬之弟也。
entries.en: Yuan Bi, styled Wenyang, was the younger brother of left grand master of the golden sigil Jing.
entries.literal: Yuan Bi, styled Wenyang, was the younger brother of Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil Jing.

entries.zh: 清正有幹局，容體魁岸，志行脩謹。
entries.en: He was upright and capable, tall in bearing, and scrupulous in conduct.
entries.literal: Upright and pure, with administrative capacity, of imposing stature, and careful in conduct.

entries.zh: 釋褐員外散騎侍郎，歷諸王府佐。
entries.en: He left the commoner's dress for supernumerary regular attendant and served as aide in several princely households.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and served as aide in several princely establishments.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，侯瑱鎮于湓城，與質不協，遣偏將羊亮代質，且以兵臨之，質率所部，度信安嶺，依于留異。
entries.en: When Jing province fell, Hou Tian held Tangcheng and clashed with Zhi. He sent the subordinate general Yang Liang to replace him and advanced with troops. Zhi led his command over the Xin'an Ridge and joined Liu Yi.
entries.literal: When Jing province fell, Hou Tian held Tangcheng and was at odds with Zhi; he sent a subordinate general, Yang Liang, to replace Zhi and also pressed him with troops; Zhi led his command over the Xin'an Ridge and attached himself to Liu Yi.

entries.zh: 文帝鎮會稽，以兵助質，令鎮信安縣。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen held Kuaiji he sent troops to aid Zhi and had him guard Xin'an county.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Kuaiji he sent troops to aid Zhi and had him hold Xin'an county.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，徵守五兵尚書。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was recalled to head the ministry of war.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was summoned to hold the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 高宗為揚州刺史，以質為仁威將軍、驃騎府長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was inspector of Yangzhou he made Zhi general of benevolent prestige and chief clerk to the flying cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Inspector of Yangzhou he made Zhi General of Benevolent Prestige and Chief Clerk to the Flying Cavalry.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，除晉安太守。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 2 (561), he was made administrator of Jin'an.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 2, he was made administrator of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，以為司徒左長史，將軍如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was regent he made Zhi left chief clerk to the minister of education, retaining his general's title.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan served as regent he made Zhi Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat, general unchanged.

entries.zh: 坐公事免官。
entries.en: He was dismissed for an offense in public business.
entries.literal: He was dismissed from office for a public matter.

entries.zh: 尋為通直散騎常侍，遷太府卿、都官尚書。
entries.en: He was soon made regular attendant of direct communication and promoted to grand steward and minister of justice.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, promoted to Grand Steward and Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 太建二年卒，時年六十。
entries.en: In the second year of Taijian (570) he died, aged sixty.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taijian he died, aged sixty.

entries.zh: 贈本官，諡曰安子。
entries.en: He was posthumously given his former rank, with the posthumous name Anzi.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given his former office; posthumous name Anzi.

entries.zh: 尋授寧遠始興王府法曹參軍，轉諮議參軍，除通直散騎常侍，兼侍中，領豫州大中正。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed legal aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant. He was then transferred to advisory aide, made regular attendant of direct communication, concurrently palace attendant, and put in charge of the grand rectifier of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed legal aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant, transferred to advisory aide, made regular attendant of direct communication, concurrently palace attendant, and put in charge of the grand rectifier of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 聘于周，使還，授散騎常侍，御史中丞，其中正如故。
entries.en: He was sent on a mission to Zhou. On his return he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and censor-in-chief, with his rectifier post unchanged.
entries.literal: He was sent on a mission to Zhou; when he returned, he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and censor-in-chief, with his rectifier post as before.

entries.zh: 高宗入輔，以泌為雲旗將軍、司徒左長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, he made Bi cloud-banner general and left chief clerk to the minister of education.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, he made Bi cloud-banner general and left chief clerk to the minister of education.

entries.zh: 光大元年卒，年五十八。
entries.en: He died in Guangda year 1 (567), aged fifty-eight.
entries.literal: He died in Guangda year 1, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 臨終戒其子蔓華曰：「吾於朝廷素無功績，瞑目之後，斂手足旋葬，無得輒受贈諡。」
entries.en: As death approached, he warned his son Manhua, "I have never had merit at court. After I close my eyes, bind my hands and feet and bury me at once. Do not rashly accept posthumous offices or titles."
entries.literal: As he neared death, he warned his son Manhua, "I have never had merit at court. After I close my eyes, bind my hands and feet and bury me at once. You must not rashly accept posthumous offices or titles."

entries.zh: [7]其子述泌遺意，表請之，朝廷不許，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰質。
entries.en: [7] His son reported Bi's dying wish and memorialized to request it, but the court refused. Bi was posthumously made grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon and given the posthumous title Zhi.
entries.literal: [7] His son reported Bi's dying wish and submitted a memorial requesting it, but the court did not allow it; Bi was posthumously presented as grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon and given the title Zhi.

entries.zh: 高宗南征周迪，以山才為軍司。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan campaigned south against Zhou Di, he made Shancai army administrator.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan campaigned south against Zhou Di, he made Shancai army administrator.

entries.zh: 迪平，復職。
entries.en: After Di was pacified, Shancai was restored to office.
entries.literal: When Di was pacified, he was restored to office.

entries.zh: 余孝頃自海道襲晉安，山才又以本官之會稽，指授方略。
entries.en: When Yu Xiaoqing attacked Jin'an by sea, Shancai again went to Kuaiji in his existing office and directed the strategy.
entries.literal: When Yu Xiaoqing attacked Jin'an by the sea route, Shancai again went to Kuaiji in his existing office and directed the plans and strategy.

entries.zh: 還朝，坐侍宴與蔡景歷言語過差，為有司所奏，免官。
entries.en: After returning to court, he was impeached because his conversation with Cai Jingli while attending a banquet went beyond bounds, and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: Returning to court, he was impeached by the responsible office because his speech with Cai Jingli while attending a banquet went beyond bounds, and he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 尋授散騎常侍，遷雲旗將軍、西陽武昌二郡太守。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and transferred to cloud-banner general and administrator of Xiyang and Wuchang commanderies.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and transferred to cloud-banner general and administrator of Xiyang and Wuchang commanderies.

entries.zh: 天康元年卒，時年五十八。
entries.en: He died in Tiankang year 1 (566), aged fifty-eight.
entries.literal: He died in Tiankang year 1, aged fifty-eight.

entries.zh: 贈右衛將軍，諡曰簡子。
entries.en: He was posthumously made right guard general and given the posthumous title Jianzi.
entries.literal: He was posthumously presented as right guard general and given the title Jianzi.

entries.zh: 載族弟翽。
entries.en: Zai's younger clansman was Hui.
entries.literal: Zai's younger clansman was Hui.

entries.zh: 翽字子羽，少有志操。
entries.en: Hui, styled Ziyu, had ambition and integrity from youth.
entries.literal: Hui, styled Ziyu, had ambition and integrity from youth.

entries.zh: 祖愛，梁輔國將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Ai was Liang's General Who Assists the State.
entries.literal: His grandfather Ai was Liang general who assists the state.

entries.zh: 父乾向，汝陰太守。
entries.en: His father Ganxiang was administrator of Ruyin.
entries.literal: His father Ganxiang was administrator of Ruyin.

entries.zh: 翽弱冠喪父，哀毀甚至，養母、撫孤兄弟子，以仁孝著稱。
entries.en: Hui lost his father at about twenty and wasted himself with extreme grief. He supported his mother and cared for the orphaned sons of his brothers, becoming known for kindness and filial piety.
entries.literal: Hui lost his father at about twenty, grieved and wasted himself to the utmost, supported his mother, and cared for orphaned sons of his brothers, becoming known for kindness and filial piety.

entries.zh: 高祖為南徐州刺史，召為征北參軍，尋監義興郡。
entries.en: When the Founder was inspector of Southern Xuzhou, he summoned Hui as campaign-north aide; soon Hui supervised Yixing commandery.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was inspector of Southern Xuzhou, he summoned Hui as campaign-north aide; soon Hui supervised Yixing commandery.

entries.zh: 永定元年，授貞毅將軍、步兵校尉。
entries.en: In Yongding year 1 (557), he was appointed resolute general and infantry commandant.
entries.literal: In Yongding year 1, he was appointed resolute general and infantry commandant.

entries.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，領朱衣直閤。
entries.en: He was transferred to swift-cavalry general and administered the red-robed palace attendants.
entries.literal: He was transferred to swift-cavalry general and administered the red-robed palace attendants.

entries.zh: 驍騎之職，舊領營兵，兼統宿衛。
entries.en: The office of swift-cavalry general formerly commanded camp troops and also oversaw the palace night guard.
entries.literal: The office of swift-cavalry general formerly commanded camp troops and also oversaw the palace night guard.

entries.zh: 自梁代已來，其任踰重，出則羽儀清道，入則與二衛通直，臨軒則升殿俠侍。
entries.en: Since Liang times, its responsibilities had grown heavier: outside it cleared the road with ceremonial guards; inside it served on duty with the two guards; when the ruler appeared, it ascended the hall as attendant guard.
entries.literal: Since Liang times, its responsibilities had grown heavier: outside it cleared the road with ceremonial guards; inside it served on duty with the two guards; when the ruler appeared at the window, it ascended the hall as attendant guard.

entries.zh: 翽素有名望，每大事恆令俠侍左右，時人榮之，號曰「俠御將軍」。
entries.en: Hui had long had reputation and standing, and at every major event he was always ordered to attend at the ruler's side. People of the time honored this and called him the "Attendant-Guard General."
entries.literal: Hui had long had reputation and standing, and at every major event he was always ordered to attend at the ruler's side; people of the time honored this and called him the "Attendant-Guard General."

entries.zh: 尋出為宣城太守。
entries.en: Soon he went out as administrator of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: Soon he went out as administrator of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年，預平王琳之功，封清源縣侯，邑二百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 2 (561), he shared in the merit for pacifying Wang Lin and was enfeoffed as marquis of Qingyuan county with two hundred households.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 2, he shared in the merit for pacifying Wang Lin and was enfeoffed as marquis of Qingyuan county with two hundred households.

entries.zh: 太建中卒官，贈明、霍、羅三州刺史。
entries.en: During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously made inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.
entries.literal: During Taijian he died in office and was posthumously made inspector of Ming, Huo, and Luo provinces.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十八
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 18
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 18

entries.zh: 炯少有雋才，為當時所重。
entries.en: Jiong showed rare talent in youth and was held in esteem.
entries.literal: Jiong in youth had outstanding talent and was esteemed by his age.

entries.zh: 釋褐王國常侍，遷為尚書左民侍郎，出為吳令。
entries.en: He entered service as a kingdom regular attendant, rose to vice minister of the left for the people, and was posted as magistrate of Wu.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a kingdom regular attendant, was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Left for the People in the Secretariat, and went out as magistrate of Wu.

entries.zh: 侯景之難，吳郡太守袁君正入援京師，以炯監郡。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Yuan Junzheng, administrator of Wu, marched to relieve the capital and left Jiong to oversee the commandery.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Administrator of Wu commandery Yuan Junzheng entered to relieve the capital and made Jiong overseer of the commandery.

entries.zh: 京城陷，景將宋子仙據吳興，遣使召炯，委以書記之任。
entries.en: The capital fell. Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and summoned Jiong to keep his records.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and sent an envoy to summon Jiong, entrusting him with secretarial duties.

entries.zh: 炯固辭以疾，子仙怒，命斬之。
entries.en: Jiong pleaded illness and refused. Zixian flew into a rage and ordered his execution.
entries.literal: Jiong firmly declined on grounds of illness; Zixian was enraged and ordered him beheaded.

entries.zh: 炯解衣將就戮，礙於路間桑樹，乃更牽往他所，或遽救之，僅而獲免。
entries.en: He stripped for the blade, but a mulberry in the road blocked the stroke. They dragged him elsewhere; someone rushed to save him, and he barely lived.
entries.literal: Jiong removed his robe to await the blade; he was hindered by a mulberry tree in the road, was then dragged elsewhere, and someone hastily rescued him—he barely escaped.

entries.zh: 子仙愛其才，終逼之令掌書記。
entries.en: Zixian prized his gift for words and at last compelled him to keep the records.
entries.literal: Zixian loved his talent and in the end forced him to take charge of secretarial work.

entries.zh: 及子仙為王僧辯所敗，僧辯素聞其名，於軍中購得之，酬所獲者鐵錢十萬，自是羽檄軍書皆出於炯。
entries.en: When Zixian fell to Wang Sengbian, Sengbian, who had long known his name, bought him out of the ranks for one hundred thousand iron coins. After that every dispatch and army paper bore Jiong's hand.
entries.literal: When Zixian was defeated by Wang Sengbian, Sengbian had long heard his name and in the army ransomed him, rewarding the captor with one hundred thousand iron coins; from then on urgent dispatches and military documents all came from Jiong's hand.

entries.zh: 及簡文遇害，四方岳牧皆上表於江陵勸進，僧辯令炯製表，其文甚工，當時莫有逮者。
entries.en: After Emperor Jianwen was killed, governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging a new throne. Sengbian had Jiong draft them. None of the age could match his craft.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was killed, territorial governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging enthronement; Sengbian had Jiong draft the memorial—the writing was very skilled, and none of the time could match it.

entries.zh: 及侯景之亂，荔率親屬入臺，除鎮西諮議參軍，舍人如故。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made staff adviser to the pacifier of the west, secretariat gentleman unchanged.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made Staff Adviser to the Pacifier of the West, secretariat gentleman unchanged.

entries.zh: 臺城陷，逃歸鄉里。
entries.en: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.
entries.literal: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.

entries.zh: 侯景平，元帝徵為中書侍郎，貞陽侯，授揚州別駕，並不就。
entries.en: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan summoned him as secretariat gentleman; the Marquis of Zhenyang offered him appointment as vice governor of Yangzhou; he accepted none of it.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Secretariat Gentleman; the Marquis of Zhenyang appointed him Vice Governor of Yangzhou—none of which he accepted.

entries.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞
entries.en: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
entries.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

entries.zh: 高祖南下，與僧辯會于白茅灣，登壇設盟，炯為其文。
entries.en: When the Founder marched south he met Sengbian at Baimao Bay. They mounted the altar and swore alliance; Jiong wrote the words.
entries.literal: When the Founder marched south and met Sengbian at Baimao Bay, they ascended the altar and set the covenant; Jiong wrote its text.

entries.zh: 及侯景東奔至吳郡，獲炯妻虞氏，子行簡，並殺之，炯弟攜其母逃而獲免。
entries.en: When Hou Jing fled east into Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, Lady Yu, and his son Xingjian and killed them. Jiong's younger brother fled with their mother and lived.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing fled east to Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, née Yu, and his son Xingjian, and killed them both; Jiong's younger brother carried off their mother and escaped.

entries.zh: 侯景平，梁元帝愍其妻子嬰戮，特封原鄉縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: After Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied that his wife and children had been slaughtered, and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with five hundred households.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied that his wife and children had died in the slaughter and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 僧辯為司徒，以炯為從事中郎。
entries.en: When Sengbian became minister of education he made Jiong a secretariat retainer.
entries.literal: When Sengbian became Minister of Education, he made Jiong a retainer in his secretariat.

entries.zh: 梁元帝徵為給事黃門侍郎，領尚書左丞。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan summoned him as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned him as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，寄隨兄荔入臺，除鎮南湘東王諮議參軍，加貞威將軍。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Ji followed his elder brother Li into the Terrace City. He was appointed advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong, general who guards the south, and was additionally made resolute-prestige general.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Ji followed his elder brother Li into the Terrace City, was appointed advisory aide to the Prince of Xiangdong, general who guards the south, and was additionally made resolute-prestige general.

entries.zh: 京城陷，遁還鄉里。
entries.en: When the capital fell, he escaped back home.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, he escaped back to his home district.

entries.zh: 及張彪往臨川，彊寄俱行，寄與彪將鄭瑋同舟而載，瑋嘗忤彪意，乃劫寄奔于晉安。
entries.en: When Zhang Biao went to Linchuan, he forced Ji to go with him. Ji shared a boat with Biao's general Zheng Wei, who had once offended Biao; Wei therefore abducted Ji and fled to Jin'an.
entries.literal: When Zhang Biao went to Linchuan, he forced Ji to go with him. Ji traveled in the same boat as Biao's general Zheng Wei; Wei had once offended Biao, so he abducted Ji and fled to Jin'an.

entries.zh: 時陳寶應據有閩中，得寄甚喜。
entries.en: At the time Chen Baoying held Minzhong and was delighted to get Ji.
entries.literal: At the time Chen Baoying held Minzhong and was very pleased to get Ji.

entries.zh: 高祖平侯景，寄勸令自結，寶應從之，乃遣使歸誠。
entries.en: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing, Ji urged Baoying to bind himself to him. Baoying followed the advice and sent an envoy to offer allegiance.
entries.literal: When Gaozu pacified Hou Jing, Ji urged Baoying to bind himself to Gaozu; Baoying followed this and sent an envoy to offer allegiance.

entries.zh: 承聖元年，除和戎將軍、中書侍郎，寶應愛其才，託以道阻不遣。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year 1 (552), Ji was appointed general who harmonizes with the Rong and secretariat gentleman. Baoying admired his talent and, claiming the roads were blocked, did not send him.
entries.literal: In Chengsheng year 1, Ji was appointed general who harmonizes with the Rong and secretariat gentleman; Baoying loved his talent and, claiming the roads were blocked, did not send him.

entries.zh: 每欲引寄為僚屬，委以文翰，寄固辭，獲免。
entries.en: Whenever Baoying tried to bring Ji in as a subordinate and entrust writings and documents to him, Ji firmly declined and was spared.
entries.literal: Whenever Baoying wanted to draw Ji in as a subordinate and entrust writings and documents to him, Ji firmly declined and was spared.

entries.zh: 自天厭梁德，多難荐臻，寰宇分崩，英雄互起，不可勝紀，人人自以為得之。
entries.en: From Heaven's loathing of Liang's virtue, hardships piled up, the realm split apart, heroes rose beyond counting—each thought he had gained it.
entries.literal: From Heaven's loathing of Liang's virtue, many hardships piled up, the realm split apart, heroes rose one after another beyond counting—each man thought he had gained it.

entries.zh: 然夷凶翦亂，拯溺扶危，四海樂推，三靈眷命，揖讓而居南面者，陳氏也。
entries.en: Yet to level the barbarian and cut chaos, save the drowning and support the tottering, the four seas pushed forward, the three numina favored the mandate—who yielded and sat facing south was the house of Chen.
entries.literal: Yet to level the barbarian and cut chaos, save the drowning and support the tottering, the four seas gladly pushed forward, the three numina favored the mandate—the one who yielded and sat facing south was the house of Chen.

entries.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授，當璧應運？
entries.en: Is it not that the sequence was fixed, Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answered fortune?
entries.literal: Is it not that the sequence was fixed, Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answered the fortune?

entries.zh: 其事甚明，一也。
entries.en: The matter is very clear—first point.
entries.literal: The matter is very clear—first point.

entries.zh: 主上承基，明德遠被，天綱再張，地維重紐。
entries.en: The sovereign inherited the foundation; his bright virtue spread far, Heaven's net was spread again, and Earth's cord was newly tied.
entries.literal: The sovereign inherited the foundation; his bright virtue spread far, Heaven's net was spread again, and Earth's cord was newly tied.

entries.zh: 夫以王琳之彊，侯瑱之力，進足以搖蕩中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅。
entries.en: As for Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's force—advancing enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and spread might in a corner.
entries.literal: As for Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's force—advancing they were enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and spread might in a corner.

entries.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳則瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則厥角稽顙，委命闕廷。
entries.en: Yet whether ordering a single column or relying on one scholar's persuasion, Lin dissolved like ice and threw himself into a foreign land; Tian touched horn, bowed forehead, and entrusted fate at the palace gate.
entries.literal: Yet whether ordering a single column of troops or relying on a single scholar's persuasion, Lin then dissolved like ice, threw himself into a foreign land; Tian then touched horn and bowed forehead, entrusted his fate at the palace gate.

entries.zh: 斯又天假之威，而除其患。
entries.en: This again is Heaven lending prestige and removing their trouble.
entries.literal: This again is Heaven lending its prestige and removing their trouble.

entries.zh: 其事甚明，二也。
entries.en: The matter is very clear—second point.
entries.literal: The matter is very clear—second point.

entries.zh: 今將軍以藩戚之重，東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤？
entries.en: Now you, with a frontier kinsman's weight and the southeast's masses, exhaust loyalty serving above and join strength in diligent service to the king—is not merit higher than Dou Rong's, favor passing Wu Rui's, splitting jade tallies and judging fields, facing south and calling yourself solitary?
entries.literal: Now the general, with the weight of a frontier kinsman and the masses of the southeast, exhausts loyalty in serving above and joins strength in diligent service to the king—is not merit higher than Dou Rong's, favor passing Wu Rui's, splitting jade tallies and judging fields, facing south and calling himself solitary?

entries.zh: 其事甚明，三也。
entries.en: The matter is very clear—third point.
entries.literal: The matter is very clear—third point.

entries.zh: 且聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚得人，改過自新，咸加敘擢。
entries.en: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, is broad in gaining men; those who reform are all promoted in turn.
entries.literal: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, is broad and thick in gaining men; those who reform and renew themselves are all promoted in turn.

entries.zh: 至於余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，胸中豁然，曾無纖芥。
entries.en: As for Yu Xiaoqing, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Wei, and the rest—all were entrusted with inmost heart, employed as talon and tooth; the breast was open without the slightest mote.
entries.literal: As for Yu Xiaoqing, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Wei, and the rest—all were entrusted with inmost heart, employed as talon and tooth; the breast was open and never had the slightest mote.

entries.zh: 況將軍舋非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮於危亡，何失於富貴？
entries.en: How much more—your rising is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril, what loss of wealth and honor?
entries.literal: How much more is the general's rising not Zhang Xiu's, his crime unlike Bi Chen's—what worry of peril and extinction, what loss of wealth and honor?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，四也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, fourth point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, fourth point.

entries.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，并兵一向，匪朝伊夕，非劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之勢，何得雍容高拱，坐論西伯？
entries.en: Now Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony, beyond the borders without worry; joining troops in one direction is not morning or evening away—not Liu and Xiang contending, nor Chu and Zhao joining—how may one sit at ease with hands folded and discuss the Western Earl?
entries.literal: Now Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony, beyond the borders without worry; joining troops in one direction is not morning or evening away—it is not the moment of Liu and Xiang contending, nor the momentum of Chu and Zhao joining—how may one sit at ease with high hands folded and sit discussing the Western Earl?

entries.zh: 其事甚明，五也。
entries.en: The matter is very clear—fifth point.
entries.literal: The matter is very clear—fifth point.

entries.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。
entries.en: Moreover General Liu glares wolf-like in a corner, repeatedly beaten, fame and substance wasted, courage decayed.
entries.literal: Moreover General Liu glares wolf-like in a corner, repeatedly beaten and broken, fame and substance wasted, courage and spirit decayed.

entries.zh: 高瓖、向文政、留瑜、黃子玉，此數人者，將軍所知，首鼠兩端，唯利是視；
entries.en: Gao Zan, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several, you know them: rats with two heads, seeing only profit;
entries.literal: Gao Zan, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several men, the general knows them: rats with two heads, seeing only profit;

entries.zh: 其餘將帥，亦可見矣。
entries.en: as for the rest of the generals, they may also be seen.
entries.literal: as for the rest of the generals, they may also be seen.

entries.zh: 孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，繫馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎？
entries.en: Who can don hard armor and grasp sharp edge, drive deep in long march, tie horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and go before the soldiers?
entries.literal: Who can don hard armor and grasp sharp edge, drive deep in long march, tie horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and go before the soldiers?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，六也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, sixth point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, sixth point.

entries.zh: 且將軍之彊，孰如侯景？
entries.en: Moreover is your strength like Hou Jing's?
entries.literal: Moreover is the general's strength like Hou Jing's?

entries.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？
entries.en: Are your masses like Wang Lin's?
entries.literal: Are the general's masses like Wang Lin's?

entries.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。
entries.en: The Founder destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign broke Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human power.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign broke Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human power.

entries.zh: 且兵革已後，民皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧之計，從將軍於白刃之閒乎？
entries.en: Moreover after arms and armor the people loathe disorder—who can abandon graves, cast off wife and children, go forth on ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow you between white blades?
entries.literal: Moreover after arms and armor, the people all loathe disorder—who can abandon graves, cast off wife and children, go forth on a plan of ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow the general between white blades?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，七也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, seventh point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, seventh point.

entries.zh: 歷觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟，傾覆相尋，餘善、
entries.en: Looking through antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and
entries.literal: Looking through former antiquity and taking mirror from past affairs, Ziyang, Jimeng, overturn followed in succession; Yu Shan and

entries.en: (stone)
entries.literal: (stone)

entries.zh: 右渠，[12]危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃。
entries.en: Youqu met ruin in turn; Heaven's mandate is to be feared, and mountains and rivers cannot be relied upon.
entries.literal: Youqu met ruin in turn; Heaven's mandate is to be feared, and mountains and rivers cannot be relied upon.

entries.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地，當天下之兵，以諸侯之資，拒天子之命，彊弱逆順，可得侔乎？
entries.en: How much more when you wish with several commanderies' territory to meet the realm's troops, with a feudal lord's resources to resist the Son of Heaven's command—strong and weak, obedience and rebellion, can they be matched?
