entries.literal: How much more when the general wishes with the territory of several commanderies to meet the realm's troops, with a feudal lord's resources to resist the Son of Heaven's command—strong and weak, obedience and rebellion, can they be matched?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，八也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, eighth point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, eighth point.

entries.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異。
entries.en: Moreover those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ.
entries.literal: Moreover those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ.

entries.zh: 不愛其親，豈能及物？
entries.en: If one does not love his kin, how can he reach to things?
entries.literal: If one does not love his kin, how can he reach to things?

entries.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危急之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎？
entries.en: General Liu is bound by the state's rank, his son married to a king's daughter—yet he abandons Heaven's kin, turns his back on the bright lord and stands alone—in days of peril, how can they share worry and not turn their backs on you?
entries.literal: General Liu himself is bound by the state's rank, his son is still married to a king's daughter—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin and does not look back, turns his back on the bright lord and stands alone—in days of peril and urgency, how can they share worry and disaster and not turn their backs on the general?

entries.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之勢。
entries.en: When the army is old and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward, there must be Han and Zhi's schemes at Jinyang, Zhang and Chen's momentum at Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: As for the army old and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward, there must be the schemes of Han and Zhi at Jinyang, the momentum of Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，九也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, ninth point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, ninth point.

entries.zh: 且北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當，將軍自戰其地，人多顧後。
entries.en: Moreover the northern army fights a myriad li away; its edge cannot be withstood—you fight on your own ground and many look behind.
entries.literal: Moreover the northern army fights a myriad li away; its edge cannot be withstood—the general fights on his own ground and many men look behind.

entries.zh: 梁安背向為心，修旿匹夫之力，眾寡不敵，將帥不侔，師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。
entries.en: Liang An's heart turns away, Xiu Xu's strength is a single man—the many cannot match the few, generals cannot compare; the army goes forth without a name, the affair moves without opportunity—raising troops thus, one does not know its profit.
entries.literal: Liang An's heart turns away, Xiu Xu's strength is a single man—the many cannot match the few, generals cannot compare with commanders; the army goes forth without a name, the affair moves without opportunity—raising troops thus, one does not know its profit.

entries.zh: 夫以漢朝吳、楚，晉室穎、顒，連城數十，長戟百萬，拔本塞源，自圖家國，其有成功者乎？
entries.en: As for Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting root and blocking source to plot house and state—were there any who succeeded?
entries.literal: As for Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source to plot their own house and state—were there any who succeeded?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，十也。
entries.en: This again—the matter is very clear, tenth point.
entries.literal: This again—the matter is very clear, tenth point.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，加通直散騎常侍，中丞如故。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne he was given the added post of regular attendant for direct communication while keeping the censorate.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Jiong was given the added post of Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, censor-in-chief unchanged.

entries.zh: 以母老表請歸養，詔不許。
entries.en: He memorialized to go home and tend his aged mother; the court refused.
entries.literal: Because his mother was old he memorialized asking to return and support her; an edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 夫安危之兆，禍福之機，匪獨天時，[7]亦由人事。
entries.en: The omens of safety and danger, the mechanisms of fortune and calamity, are not only Heaven's seasons, [7] but also lie in human affairs.
entries.literal: The omens of safety and danger, the mechanisms of fortune and calamity, are not only Heaven's seasons, but also lie in human affairs.

entries.zh: 失之毫釐，差以千里。
entries.en: Miss by a hair's breadth and err by a thousand li.
entries.literal: To miss by a hair's breadth is to err by a thousand li.

entries.zh: 是以明智之士，據重位而不傾，執大節而不失，豈惑於浮辭哉？
entries.en: Therefore the wise hold heavy position without toppling, grasp great integrity without losing it—how would they be deluded by floating words?
entries.literal: Therefore the wise man holds heavy position without toppling, grasps great integrity without losing it—how would he be deluded by floating words?

entries.zh: 將軍文武兼資，英威不世，往因多難，杖劍興師，援旗誓眾，抗威千里，豈不以四郊多壘，共謀王室，匡時報主，寧國庇民乎？
entries.en: You combine civil and martial gifts, heroic prestige unmatched in the age; in former days through hardship you took sword and raised troops, lifted the banner and swore the host, resisted prestige a thousand li—was it not because the four suburbs had many ramparts, you plotted for the royal house, set the age right, repaid the lord, settled the state and sheltered the people?
entries.literal: The general combines civil and martial gifts, his heroic prestige unmatched in the age; in former days through many hardships you took sword and raised troops, lifted the banner and swore the host, resisted prestige a thousand li—was it not because the four suburbs had many ramparts and together you plotted for the royal house, set the age right and repaid the lord, settled the state and sheltered the people?

entries.zh: 此所以五尺童子，皆願荷戟而隨將軍者也。
entries.en: This is why boys five feet tall all wished to carry halberds and follow you.
entries.literal: This is why boys five feet tall all wished to carry halberds and follow the general.

entries.zh: 及高祖武皇肇基草昧，初濟艱難。
entries.en: When the Founder Martial Emperor first laid foundation in grass and darkness and first crossed hardship,
entries.literal: When the Founder Martial Emperor first laid foundation in the grass and darkness and first crossed hardship.

entries.zh: [8]于時天下沸騰，民無定主，豺狼當道，鯨鯢橫擊，海內業業，未知所從。
entries.en: [8] the realm boiled, the people had no fixed lord, wolves blocked the road, whales struck across, within the seas all were fearful and did not know whom to follow.
entries.literal: At that time the realm boiled, the people had no fixed lord, wolves and jackals blocked the road, whales and krakens struck across, within the seas all were fearful and did not know whom to follow.

entries.zh: 將軍運動微之鑒，折從衡之辯，策名委質，自託宗盟，此將軍妙筭遠圖，發於衷誠者也。
entries.en: You moved with discernment of minute signs, broke vertical-and-horizontal persuasions, registered your name and entrusted your person to the clan alliance—this is subtle reckoning and far design from a sincere heart.
entries.literal: The general moved with the discernment of minute signs, broke the persuasions of vertical and horizontal alliance, registered his name and entrusted his person, trusting himself to the clan alliance—this is the general's subtle reckoning and far design, issuing from sincere heart.

entries.zh: 及主上繼業，欽明睿聖，選賢與能，群臣輯睦，結將軍以維城之重，崇將軍以裂土之封。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven succeeded, reverent, bright, and sage, he chose the worthy and employed the able, ministers were harmonious; he bound you with a wall city's weight and honored you with enfeoffment splitting the soil.
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven succeeded the enterprise, he was reverent, bright, and sage, chose the worthy and employed the able, ministers were harmonious; he bound the general with the weight of a wall city and honored the general with enfeoffment splitting the soil.

entries.zh: 豈非宏謨廟略，推赤心於物也？
entries.en: Is it not great temple design, pushing the red heart upon things?
entries.literal: Is it not great design of the temple altars, pushing the red heart upon things?

entries.zh: 屢申明詔，款篤殷勤，君臣之分定矣，骨肉之恩深矣。
entries.en: Again and again he made clear edicts, sincere and earnest; lord and minister's division was settled, flesh-and-blood affection deep.
entries.literal: Again and again he made clear edicts, sincere and earnest in kindness; lord and minister's division was settled, flesh-and-blood affection was deep.

entries.zh: 不意將軍惑於邪說，遽生異計，寄所以疾首痛心，泣盡繼之以血。
entries.en: I did not expect you, deluded by evil persuasion, suddenly to harbor a different plan—therefore I grieve with head in pain, weeping until blood follows tears.
entries.literal: I did not expect the general, deluded by evil persuasion, suddenly to harbor a different plan—therefore Ji grieves with head in pain, weeping until blood follows the tears.

entries.zh: [9]萬全之策，竊為將軍惜之。
entries.en: [9] The plan of ten thousand completeness—your servant privately grieves for you.
entries.literal: The plan of ten thousand completeness—your servant privately grieves for the general.

entries.zh: 寄雖疾侵耄及，言無足採，千慮一得，請陳愚筭。
entries.en: Though my illness invades old age and my words are not worth gathering, in a thousand thoughts one may gain—please let me state my foolish reckoning.
entries.literal: Though Ji's illness invades old age and his words are not worth gathering, in a thousand thoughts one may gain—please let me state my foolish reckoning.

entries.zh: 願將軍少戢雷霆，賒其晷刻，使得盡狂瞽之說，披肝膽之誠，則雖死之日，由生之年也。
entries.en: I wish you would slightly curb thunder, grant a moment's delay, so I may fully speak my reckless blindness and lay bare liver and gall—then though the day of death would be the year of life.
entries.literal: I wish the general would slightly curb thunder, grant a moment's delay, so that I may fully speak my reckless blindness and lay bare liver and gall's sincerity—then though the day of death would be the year of life.

entries.zh: 張彪之據會稽也，荔時在焉。
entries.en: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.
entries.literal: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.

entries.zh: 及文帝平彪，高祖遺荔書曰：「喪亂已來，賢哲凋散，君才用有美，聲聞許、洛，當今朝廷惟新，廣求英雋，豈可栖遲東土，獨善其身？
entries.en: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder wrote: "Since the chaos, worthies have scattered. Your talent is fine and your fame heard in Xu and Luo. The court is newly ordered and seeks heroes widely—how can you linger in the east and keep goodness to yourself?
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder sent Li a letter saying: "Since the mourning and chaos, worthies have scattered; your talent and use are fine, your fame heard in Xu and Luo; today's court is newly ordered and widely seeks heroes—how can you linger in the eastern lands and keep goodness to yourself?

entries.zh: 今令兄子將接出都，想必副朝廷虛遲也。」
entries.en: I now order your elder brother's son to bring you to the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting."
entries.literal: I now order your elder brother's son to come out and meet you in the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting."

entries.zh: 文帝又與書曰：「君東南有美，聲譽洽聞，自應翰飛京許，共康時弊，而
entries.en: Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast and fame that spreads; you should brush the capital and Xu and set right the age's ills, yet
entries.literal: Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast, fame that spreads; you should yourself brush the capital and Xu, together set right the age's ills, yet

entries.en: (cut)
entries.literal: (cut)

entries.zh: 削跡丘園，[6]保茲獨善，豈使稱空谷之望邪？
entries.en: pared your traces in gardens and fields, [6] keeping solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?
entries.literal: pared your traces in gardens and fields, keeping this solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?

entries.zh: 必願便爾俶裝，且為出都之計。
entries.en: I surely wish you to pack at once and plan to leave for the capital.
entries.literal: I surely wish you at once to pack and also make plans to leave for the capital.

entries.zh: 唯遲披覯，在於茲日。」
entries.en: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon."
entries.literal: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon."

entries.zh: 迫切之不得已，乃應命至都。
entries.en: Pressed urgently and with no way out, he answered the summons and reached the capital.
entries.literal: Pressed urgently and with no way out, he then answered the summons and reached the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，文帝嗣位，除太子中庶子，仍侍太子讀書。
entries.en: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made crown prince attendant and still tutored the crown prince.
entries.literal: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made Crown Prince Attendant and still attended the crown prince in study.

entries.zh: 尋領大著作、東揚揚州二州大中正，庶子如故。
entries.en: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing and was grand arbiter for East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing and was Grand Arbiter for the two provinces of East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 初，高祖嘗稱炯宜居王佐，軍國大政，多預謀謨，文帝又重其才用，欲寵貴之。
entries.en: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.
entries.literal: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in great affairs of army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.

entries.zh: 會王琳入寇大雷，留異擁據東境，帝欲使炯因是立功，乃解中丞，加明威將軍，遣還鄉里，收合徒眾。
entries.en: When Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches, the emperor wished Jiong to win merit thereby, relieved him as censor-in-chief, made him general of bright prestige, and sent him home to gather followers.
entries.literal: It happened that Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches; the emperor wished to have Jiong win merit thereby, so relieved him as censor-in-chief, gave him the added title General of Bright Prestige, and sent him back to his home district to gather followers.

entries.zh: 以疾卒于吳中，時年五十九。
entries.en: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.
entries.literal: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 文帝聞之，即日舉哀，并遣弔祭，贈侍中，諡曰恭子。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen heard it he mourned that same day and sent condolences; he was posthumously made palace attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen heard it he at once went into mourning and also sent condolences; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.

entries.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。
entries.en: A collection of his writings in twenty rolls circulated in his time.
entries.literal: He had a collection of writings in twenty rolls circulating in the world.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，為西魏所虜，魏人甚禮之，授炯儀同三司。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell he was taken by Western Wei. They honored him and made him palace attendant of the third rank.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou fell he was captured by Western Wei; the Wei people treated him with great courtesy and appointed Jiong Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.

entries.zh: 炯以母老在東，恆思歸國，恐魏人愛其文才而留之，恆閉門卻掃，無所交遊。
entries.en: His mother was old in the east and he longed to go home, fearing the Wei would keep him for his writing. He shut his gate, swept away callers, and kept no company.
entries.literal: Because his mother was old in the east, Jiong constantly longed to return home, fearing the Wei would love his literary talent and detain him; he always shut his gate and swept no visitors, having no social ties.

entries.zh: 時有文章，隨即棄毀，不令流布。
entries.en: Whatever he wrote he destroyed at once and would not let it spread.
entries.literal: Whenever he had writings he at once destroyed them and would not let them circulate.

entries.zh: 嘗獨行經漢武通天臺，為表奏之，陳己思歸之意。
entries.en: Once he walked alone past the Han Tower of Reaching Heaven and submitted a memorial pleading to return.
entries.literal: Once, walking alone past Emperor Wu of Han's Tower of Reaching Heaven, he submitted a memorial stating his wish to return.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：「臣聞喬山雖掩，鼎湖之靈可祠，有魯既荒，大庭之跡無泯。
entries.en: He wrote: "I have heard that though Qiao Mountain is buried, the spirit at Tripod Lake may still be honored; though Youlu lies waste, the Great Court's traces are not gone.
entries.literal: The text says: "Your servant has heard that though Qiao Mountain is covered over, the spirit of the Tripod Lake may still be worshipped; though Youlu is waste, the traces of the Great Court are not lost.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下降德猗蘭，纂靈豐谷。
entries.en: I bow before Your Majesty's grace descending like orchids on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.
entries.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's descending virtue like the orchid on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.

entries.zh: 漢道既登，神仙可望，射之罘於海浦，禮日觀而稱功，橫中流於汾河，指柏梁而高宴，何其樂也，豈不然歟！
entries.en: When Han's Way had risen, immortals seemed near: shooting zhi at the sea shore, rites at Sun Terrace proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen, feasting high at Cypress Beam—what joy, was it not so!
entries.literal: When Han's Way had ascended, immortals could be hoped for; shooting the zhi at the sea shore, performing rites at Sun Terrace and proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen River, pointing to Cypress Beam and feasting high—what joy, is it not so!

entries.zh: 既而運屬上仙，道窮晏駕，甲帳珠簾，一朝零落，茂陵玉碗，宛出人間，陵雲故基，共原田而膴膴，別風餘
entries.en: Then fate turned to the transcendent lord and the imperial carriage halted; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; Maoling's jade bowl walked among men; Lingyun's old base turned to lush open fields; the remnant of the separate wind
entries.literal: Then fortune turned to the transcendent lord, the Way reached the imperial carriage's halt; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; the jade bowl of Maoling came forth among men; the old base of Lingyun shared the open fields in lush growth; the separate wind's remnant

entries.en: (toe)
entries.literal: (toe)

entries.zh: 址，[2]對陵阜而茫茫，羇旅縲臣，能不落淚。
entries.en: site, [2] facing the tomb mounds in boundless haze—a captive minister in bonds, how could tears not fall?
entries.literal: site, facing the tomb mound in boundless expanse—a captive minister in bonds, how could he not shed tears?

entries.zh: 昔承明既厭，嚴助東歸，駟馬可乘，長卿西返，恭聞故實，竊有愚心。
entries.en: When Chenming grew weary, Yan Zhu went east; four-horse carriages waited, Sima Xiangru returned west—I hear these precedents and harbor this foolish wish.
entries.literal: In old days when Chenming was weary, Yan Zhu returned east; four-horse carriages could be taken, Sima Xiangru came back west—I respectfully hear these precedents and secretly harbor this foolish wish.

entries.zh: 黍稷非馨，敢忘徼福。」
entries.en: Though the offering lacks fragrance, I dare not forget to seek blessing."
entries.literal: Though millet and millet are not fragrant, I dare not forget to seek blessing."

entries.zh: 奏訖，其夜炯夢見有宮禁之所，兵衛甚嚴，炯便以情事陳訴，聞有人言：「甚不惜放卿還，幾時可至。」
entries.en: When the memorial was done, that night he dreamed of palace precincts under strict guard. He pleaded his case and heard a voice: "We are quite willing to let you go home—when will you arrive?"
entries.literal: When the memorial was finished, that night Jiong dreamed of a place within the palace precincts where guards were very strict; he stated his case, and heard someone say: "We are quite willing to let you return—when may you arrive?"

entries.zh: 少日，便與王克等並獲東歸。
entries.en: Within days he and Wang Ke and others were all sent home to the east.
entries.literal: Within a few days he and Wang Ke and others were all able to return east.

entries.zh: 紹泰二年至都，除司農卿，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 2 (555) he reached the capital, was made director of the directorate of agriculture, then censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shaotai he reached the capital and was made Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then transferred to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，又表曰：「臣嬰生不幸，弱冠而孤，母子零丁，兄弟相長。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded he memorialized again: "From infancy I met misfortune. At twenty I was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised each other.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded he again memorialized, saying: "Your servant from infancy met misfortune; at twenty he was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised one another.

entries.zh: 謹身為養，仕不擇官，宦成梁朝，命存亂世，冒危履險，
entries.en: I kept my body to nourish them, took any office, served Liang to the end, and lived through chaos, braving danger at every step,
entries.literal: I kept my person to support them, took office without choosing rank, served to completion under Liang, my life preserved in chaotic times, braving danger and treading peril,

entries.en: (self)
entries.literal: (self)

entries.zh: 〔百〕死輕生，[3]妻息誅夷，昆季冥滅，餘臣母子，得逢興運。
entries.en: [hundred] deaths counted light, [3] wife and children slain, brothers gone; only your servant and his mother met this rising fortune.
entries.literal: [hundred] deaths counted light, wife and children executed, brothers extinguished; your servant and his mother alone met the rising fortune.

entries.zh: 臣母妾劉，今年八十有一，臣叔母妾丘，七十有五，臣門弟姪故自無人，妾丘兒孫又久亡泯，兩家侍養，餘臣一人。
entries.en: My mother, Lady Liu, is eighty-one; my uncle's wife, Lady Qiu, is seventy-five. Our younger kin are gone and Lady Qiu's grandsons are long dead—of the two households that must be served, only I remain.
entries.literal: Your servant's mother, concubine Liu, is this year eighty-one; your servant's uncle's wife, concubine Qiu, is seventy-five; your servant's younger brothers and nephews in the clan are gone, and concubine Qiu's grandsons long since perished—of the two households to be served, only your servant remains.

entries.zh: 前帝知臣之孤煢，養臣以州里，不欲使頓居草萊，又復矜臣溫凊，所以一年之內，再三休沐。
entries.en: The late emperor knew my desolation, kept me in a post near home, and would not leave me in the wild; he pitied my duty to warm and cool my elders, and within a year granted leave again and again.
entries.literal: The former emperor knew your servant's loneliness, nourished him with a post in his home district, and did not wish him to dwell suddenly in the wilds; he again pitied your servant's warmth in winter and cool in summer, so within one year he granted leave again and again.

entries.zh: 臣之屢披丹款，頻冒宸鑒，非欲苟違朝廷，遠離畿輦。
entries.en: I laid my heart bare again and again and braved the throne's gaze—not because I wished to defy the court or flee the capital.
entries.literal: Your servant's repeated laying bare of his loyal heart and frequent braving of the imperial gaze were not from wishing to defy the court or leave the capital region.

entries.zh: 一者以年將六十，湯火居心，每跪讀家書，前懼後喜，溫枕扇席，無復成童。
entries.en: First, nearing sixty, my heart is scalding water; each time I kneel to a letter from home, fear comes first and joy after; to warm the pillow and fan the mat is no longer the work of a child.
entries.literal: First, as the years approach sixty, boiling water sits in the heart; whenever kneeling to read a letter from home, fear comes before and joy after; warming the pillow and fanning the mat—no longer the ways of childhood.

entries.zh: 二者職居彝憲，邦之司直，若自虧身禮，[4]何問國章？
entries.en: Second, my post holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if I impair my own filial duty, [4] how may I judge the nation's laws?
entries.literal: Second, the office holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if one himself impairs the rites of the body, how may one inquire into the nation's laws?

entries.zh: 前德綢繆，始許哀放，內侍近臣，多悉此旨。
entries.en: Former grace was close and at first promised compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers knew that intent.
entries.literal: Former grace was close and at first allowed compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers mostly knew this intent.

entries.zh: 正以選賢與能，廣求明哲，趦趄荏苒，未始取才。
entries.en: Only because in choosing the worthy and seeking the wise I hesitated and delayed, and had not yet yielded my post.
entries.literal: It was only because in choosing the worthy and employing the able, widely seeking the wise and clear, I hesitated and delayed and had not yet taken talent.

entries.zh: 而上玄降戾，奄至今日，德音在耳，墳土遽乾，悠悠昊天，哀此罔極。
entries.en: Yet Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it is today; his gracious voice is still in my ear, the grave earth already dry—vast Heaven, pity this boundless grief.
entries.literal: Yet High Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it reached today; the virtuous voice is still in the ear, the grave earth is already dry—vast is August Heaven, pity this boundless grief.

entries.zh: 兼臣私心煎切，彌迫近時，慺慺之祈，轉忘塵觸。
entries.en: Together with my private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, earnest prayer forgets even the dust on my robe.
entries.literal: Together with your servant's private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, his earnest prayer forgets even dust on his robe.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下睿哲聰明，嗣興下武，刑于四海，弘此孝治。
entries.en: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity, raising martial virtue in succession, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial rule.
entries.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity and intelligence, succeeding and raising martial virtue, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial governance.

entries.zh: 寸管求天，仰歸帷扆，有感必應，實望聖明。
entries.en: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where feeling moves, response must come—I trust in sagely clarity.
entries.literal: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where there is feeling there must be response—I truly look to sagely clarity.

entries.zh: 特乞霈然申其私禮，則王者之德，覃及無方，矧彼翔沈，孰非涵養。」
entries.en: I beg that you grant my private rites in full; then kingly virtue reaches without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?"
entries.literal: I specially beg that you grant in full my private rites; then the kingly virtue will reach without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?"

entries.zh: 詔答曰：「省表具懷。
entries.en: The edict replied: "Your memorial is received and your meaning understood.
entries.literal: The edict replied: "I have read your memorial and take your meaning.

entries.zh: 卿譽馳咸、雒，情深宛、沛。
entries.en: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.
entries.literal: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.

entries.zh: 日者理切倚門，[5]言歸異域，復牽時役，遂乖侍養。
entries.en: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, [5] words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.
entries.literal: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.

entries.zh: 雖周生之思，每欲棄官，戴禮垂文，得遺從政，前朝光宅四海，劬勞萬機，以卿才為獨步，職居專席，方深委任，屢屈情禮。
entries.en: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to quit office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office for policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at myriad affairs—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as trust deepened, again and again feeling and rites were bent.
entries.literal: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to abandon office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office to follow policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at the myriad affairs of state—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as deep trust was placed, again and again feeling and rites were bent.

entries.zh: 朕嗣奉洪基，思弘景業，顧茲寡薄，兼纏哀疚，實賴賢哲，同致雍熙，豈便釋簡南闈，解紱東路。
entries.en: I now succeed to the great foundation and think to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on my meager worth and wound with mourning, I truly rely on the worthy to bring harmony—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?
entries.literal: I now succeed to the great foundation, thinking to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on this meager thinness and also wound with mourning grief, I truly rely on the worthy and wise to bring harmony together—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?

entries.zh: 當今馮親入舍，荀母從官，用睹朝榮，不虧家禮。
entries.en: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.
entries.literal: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.

entries.zh: 尋敕所由，相迎尊累，使卿公私得所，並無廢也。」
entries.en: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that public and private needs are met, and nothing neglected."
entries.literal: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that you may have what is fitting in public and private, and nothing will be neglected."

entries.zh: 初，荔母隨荔入臺，卒於臺內，尋而城陷，情禮不申，由是終身蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，雖任遇隆重，而居止儉素，淡然無營。
entries.en: Earlier his mother had followed him into the Terrace City and died there; soon the city fell and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and plain cloth and heard no music; though honored in office, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.
entries.literal: Earlier Li's mother had followed Li into the Terrace City and died within it; soon the city fell and feeling and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, heard no music; though his appointment was weighty, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.

entries.zh: 文帝深器之，常引在左右，朝夕顧訪。
entries.en: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, constantly kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.

entries.zh: 荔性沉密，少言論，凡所獻替，莫有見其際者，故不列于後焉。
entries.en: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom debated; whatever he offered in counsel none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.
entries.literal: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom spoke in debate; whatever he offered in counsel, none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.

entries.zh: 時荔第二弟寄寓於閩中，依陳寶應，荔每言之輒流涕。
entries.en: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min under Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.
entries.literal: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min, relying on Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.

entries.zh: 文帝哀而謂曰：「我亦有弟在遠，此情甚切，他人豈知。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is keen—how would others know?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is very keen—how would others know?"

entries.zh: 乃敕寶應求寄，寶應終不遣。
entries.en: He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying never sent him.
entries.literal: He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying in the end did not send him.

entries.zh: 荔因以感疾，帝數往臨視。
entries.en: Li fell ill with grief; the emperor visited him in person several times.
entries.literal: Li thereby fell ill with grief; the emperor several times went in person to visit him.

entries.zh: 令荔將家口入省，荔以禁中非私居之所，乞停城外，文帝不許，乃令住於蘭臺，乘輿再三臨問，手敕中使，相望於道。
entries.en: He ordered Li to bring his household into the secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private home and begged to stay outside the walls. Emperor Wen refused and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage visited again and again; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.
entries.literal: He ordered Li to bring his household into the Secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private dwelling and begged to stop outside the walls; Emperor Wen did not permit it and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage again and again visited him in person; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.

entries.zh: 又以荔蔬食積久，非羸疾所堪，乃敕曰：「能敦布素，乃當為高，卿年事已多，氣力稍減，方欲仗委，良須克壯，今給卿魚肉，不得固從所執也。」
entries.en: Because Li's vegetable diet had long continued and was not what a wasting illness could bear, an edict said: "To keep plain cloth is indeed lofty; you are advanced in years and your strength has declined—just when I wish to rely on you I need you hale; I now give you fish and meat—you must not stubbornly hold to your vow."
entries.literal: Also, because Li's vegetable diet had long continued and was not what a wasting illness could bear, an edict said: "To be able to keep plain cloth is indeed lofty; you are already advanced in years and your strength has somewhat declined—just when I wish to rely on you, I truly need you hale; I now give you fish and meat—you must not stubbornly follow what you have held to."

entries.zh: 荔終不從。
entries.en: Li in the end did not obey.
entries.literal: Li in the end did not follow.

entries.zh: 天嘉二年卒，時年五十九。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 2 (561) he died, aged fifty-nine.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 2 he died, aged fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 文帝甚傷惜之，贈侍中，諡曰德子。
entries.en: Emperor Wen grieved deeply, posthumously made him palace attendant, posthumous name Dezi.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen grieved deeply, posthumously made him Palace Attendant, posthumous name Dezi.

entries.zh: 及喪柩還鄉里，上親出臨送，當時榮之。
entries.en: When the coffin returned home the emperor went out in person to see him off—the age counted it glory.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned to his home district the emperor went out in person to see him off—the age counted it glory.

entries.zh: 子世基、世南，並少知名。
entries.en: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both known in youth.
entries.literal: His sons Shiji and Shinan were both known in youth.

entries.zh: 文帝尋敕都督章昭達以理發遣，令寄還朝。
entries.en: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to send Ji home to court.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen soon ordered Area Commander Zhang Zhaoda to arrange his dismissal and send Ji back to court.

entries.zh: 及至，即日引見，謂寄曰：「管寧無恙。」
entries.en: On arrival he was received that same day. The emperor said to Ji, "Guan Ning is well."
entries.literal: When he arrived, that very day he was granted audience; he said to Ji: "Guan Ning is unharmed."

entries.zh: 其慰勞之懷若此。
entries.en: Such was his warmth in greeting him.
entries.literal: His mind to comfort and reward was like this.

entries.zh: 頃之，文帝謂到仲舉曰：「 衡陽王既出閤，雖未置府僚，然須得一人旦夕遊處，兼掌書記，宜求宿士有行業者。」
entries.en: Soon Emperor Wen told Dao Zhongju, "Prince Hengyang has left the inner palace. Though he has no staff yet, he needs someone with him day and night who can also keep his records. We should find a senior man of real conduct."
entries.literal: Before long Emperor Wen said to Dao Zhongju: "The Prince of Hengyang has left the inner quarters; though he has not yet been given palace staff, yet there must be one man to pass the day with him morning and evening and also keep the records—I should seek an elder scholar of established conduct."

entries.zh: 仲舉未知所對，文帝曰：「吾自得之。」
entries.en: Zhongju had no answer. The emperor said, "I already have the man."
entries.literal: Zhongju did not know how to answer; the emperor said: "I have already found him."

entries.zh: 乃手敕用寄。
entries.en: He then appointed Ji by personal edict.
entries.literal: Thereupon by hand-edict he employed Ji.

entries.zh: 寄入謝，文帝曰：「所以蹔屈卿遊藩者，非止以文翰相煩，乃令以師表相事也。」
entries.en: Ji came to give thanks. The emperor said, "I bend you to the prince's household not only for paperwork but to be his teacher and example."
entries.literal: Ji entered to give thanks; the emperor said: "The reason I temporarily bend you to roam the fief is not only to trouble you with documents—it is also to have you serve him as teacher and model."

entries.zh: 尋兼散騎常侍，聘齊，寄辭老疾，不行，除國子博士。
entries.en: He was soon made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent as envoy to Qi, but Ji pleaded age and illness and did not go; he was made doctor of the national university.
entries.literal: Soon he was concurrently made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; as envoy to Qi, Ji declined on grounds of age and illness and did not go; he was made Doctor of the National University.

entries.zh: 頃之，又表求解職歸鄉里，文帝優旨報答，許其東還。
entries.en: Before long he memorialized to resign and return home; the emperor answered graciously and let him go east.
entries.literal: Before long he also memorialized requesting to leave office and return to his home village; the emperor answered with a gracious edict and permitted him to go east.

entries.zh: 仍除東揚州別駕，寄又以疾辭。
entries.en: He was then made vice-prefect of East Yangzhou; Ji again pleaded illness.
entries.literal: He was then made Vice-Prefect of East Yangzhou; Ji again declined on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，徵授揚州治中及尚書左丞，並不就。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao Zong succeeded, he was summoned as Yangzhou administrator-in-chief and left vice director of the masters of writing, but accepted neither.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao Zong succeeded, he was summoned and appointed Yangzhou Administrator-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, but he did not accept either post.

entries.zh: 乃除東中郎建安王諮議，加戎昭將軍，又辭以疾，不任旦夕陪列。
entries.en: He was then made adviser to the prince of Jian'an, eastern palace general, with the added title general who displays martial prestige, but again pleaded illness and could not attend daily.
entries.literal: He was then made Adviser to the Eastern Palace General of the Prince of Jian'an, with the added title General Who Displays Martial Prestige; again he declined on grounds of illness, unable to attend morning and evening in the train.

entries.zh: 王於是特令停王府公事，其有疑議，就以決之，但朔望牋修而已。
entries.en: The prince then stopped routine palace business for him; doubtful matters were referred to Ji for decision; he only drafted the regular memorial on the first and fifteenth of the month.
entries.literal: The prince therefore specially ordered a halt to princely-house business; when there were doubtful points, Ji was consulted to decide them—only on the first and fifteenth of the month did he draft the routine memorial.

entries.zh: 太建八年加太中大夫，將軍如故。
entries.en: In Taijian year 8 he was advanced to grand master of palace counsel, retaining his general's title.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian he was advanced to Grand Master of Palace Counsel; his general's title was unchanged.

entries.zh: 十一年卒，時年七十。
entries.en: In year 11 he died, aged seventy.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 荔幼聰敏，有志操。
entries.en: Li was clever and keen in youth, with firm will and conduct.
entries.literal: Li in youth was clever and keen, with will and conduct.

entries.zh: 年九歲，隨從伯闡候太常陸倕，倕問五經凡有十事，荔隨問輒應，無有遺失，倕甚異之。
entries.en: At nine, he accompanied his father's elder cousin Chan on a visit to Chamberlain for Ceremonials Lu Chui. Chui asked him ten questions on the Five Classics; Li answered each without error, and Chui marveled at him.
entries.literal: At age nine, he accompanied his father's elder cousin Chan to call on the Chamberlain for Ceremonials Lu Chui; Chui asked ten questions concerning the Five Classics, and Li answered each as it was put to him without missing anything. Chui marveled at him.

entries.zh: 又嘗詣徵士何胤，時太守衡陽王亦造焉，胤言之於王，王欲見荔，荔辭曰：「未有板刺，無容拜謁。」
entries.en: He once visited the recluse He Yin. The Prince of Hengyang, then administrator, also came; Yin spoke of Li to the prince, who wished to see him. Li declined: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."
entries.literal: He also once visited the recluse He Yin; at the time the Administrator, the Prince of Hengyang, also came, and Yin spoke of him to the prince; the prince wished to see Li, but Li declined, saying: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."

entries.zh: 王以荔有高尚之志，雅相欽重，還郡，即辟為主簿，荔又辭以年小不就。
entries.en: The prince, seeing Li's lofty aims, honored him deeply. Back in his commandery he summoned Li as chief clerk; Li again declined as too young.
entries.literal: The prince, because Li had lofty aims, honored him deeply; returning to his commandery he at once summoned him as chief clerk, but Li again declined on grounds of youth and did not accept.

entries.zh: 及長，美風儀，博覽墳籍，善屬文。
entries.en: Grown, he had fine bearing, read broadly in the classics, and wrote well.
entries.literal: When grown he had fine bearing, broadly read the classics, and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 釋褐梁西中郎行參軍，尋署法曹外兵參軍，兼丹陽詔獄正。
entries.en: He entered service as a traveling aide in Liang's western central commandery, soon as outer-army major in the law office and concurrent chief of the Danyang imperial prison.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a traveling aide in Liang's Western Central Commandery, soon was appointed Outer Army Major in the Law Office, and concurrently Chief of the Danyang Imperial Prison.

entries.zh: 梁武帝於城西置士林館，荔乃製碑，奏上，帝命勒之于館，仍用荔為士林學士。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars west of the city. Li composed a stele and submitted it; the emperor had it carved in the hall and made Li an academician there.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars Hall west of the city; Li composed a stele, submitted it, and the emperor ordered it carved in the hall and still employed Li as a Forest of Scholars academician.

entries.zh: 尋為司文郎，遷通直散騎侍郎，兼中書舍人。
entries.en: Soon he was editorial officer of writings, then regular attendant for direct communication and concurrent secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Editorial Officer of Writings, transferred to Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, and concurrently Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 時左右之任，多參權軸，內外機務，互有帶掌，唯荔與顧協淡然靖退，居于西省，但以文史見知，當時號為清白。
entries.en: Close attendants then mostly shared the power axis; inner and outer affairs were split among them—only Li and Gu Xie stayed calm and retired in the western secretariat, known for literature and history; the age called them pure.
entries.literal: At the time those in close attendance mostly shared in the power axis; inner and outer affairs were each partly held—only Li and Gu Xie were calm, retiring, and dwelt in the Western Secretariat, known only through literature and history; the age called them pure.

entries.zh: 尋領大著作。
entries.en: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing.
entries.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing.

entries.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。
entries.en: Grown, he loved learning and wrote well.
entries.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 性沖靜，有栖遁之志。
entries.en: By nature he was mild and still and wished to dwell in seclusion.
entries.literal: By nature he was mild and still, with the will to dwell in seclusion.

entries.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，對策高第。
entries.en: At twenty he was recommended as cultivated talent and ranked high in the policy response.
entries.literal: At twenty he was recommended as a cultivated talent and in the policy response ranked high.

entries.zh: 起家梁宣城王國左常侍。
entries.en: He began as left regular attendant in Liang's Kingdom of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Xuan[cheng] under Liang.

entries.zh: 大同中，嘗驟雨，殿前往往有雜色寶珠，梁武觀之甚有喜色，寄因上瑞雨頌。
entries.en: In the Datong era a sudden rain once left mixed-colored pearls before the hall. Emperor Wu of Liang was greatly pleased, and Ji submitted a eulogy on the auspicious rain.
entries.literal: In the Datong era, once in a sudden rain, before the hall there were often mixed-colored precious pearls; Emperor Wu of Liang viewed them with great pleasure, and Ji therefore submitted a eulogy on the auspicious rain.

entries.zh: 帝謂寄兄荔曰：「此頌典裁清拔，卿家之士龍也。
entries.en: The emperor told Ji's elder brother Li: "This eulogy is clear and lofty—your family's Shilong.
entries.literal: The emperor said to Ji's elder brother Li: "This eulogy's style is clear and lofty—your family's Shilong.

entries.zh: 將如何擢用？」
entries.en: How will you promote and employ him?"
entries.literal: How will you promote and employ him?"

entries.zh: 寄聞之，歎曰：「美盛德之形容，以申擊壤之情耳。
entries.en: When Ji heard it he sighed: "To praise flourishing virtue is only to voice the joy of beating clods.
entries.literal: When Ji heard it he sighed: "To praise the flourishing virtue's form is only to voice the joy of beating clods.

entries.zh: 吾豈買名求仕者乎？」
entries.en: Am I one who buys a name to seek office?"
entries.literal: Am I one who buys a name to seek office?"

entries.zh: 乃閉門稱疾，唯以書籍自娛。
entries.en: He shut his door and claimed illness, taking only books for pleasure.
entries.literal: He then shut his door and claimed illness, taking only books for pleasure.

entries.zh: 岳陽王為會稽太守，引寄為行參軍，遷記室參軍，領郡五官掾。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yueyang was administrator of Kuaiji he brought Ji in as traveling aide, then staff recorder, leading the commandery's five offices major.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang was Administrator of Kuaiji he brought in Ji as a traveling aide, transferred him to Staff Recorder, and had him lead the commandery's Five Offices Major.

entries.zh: 又轉中記室，掾如故。
entries.en: He was again made central staff recorder, major unchanged.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to Central Staff Recorder, major unchanged.

entries.zh: 在職簡略煩苛，務存大體，曹局之內，終日寂然。
entries.en: In office he was brief with troublesome detail and kept to the great body; within the bureau all day was silence.
entries.literal: In office he was brief with troublesome detail, keeping to the great body; within the bureau all day was silence.

entries.zh: 梁邵陵王綸為南徐州刺史，素聞其名，引為學士。
entries.en: Xiao Lun, prince of Shaoling, was inspector of South Xuzhou; he had long heard of Shu and made him an academician.
entries.literal: Liang's Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun was Inspector of South Xuzhou; having long heard his name, he summoned him as academician.

entries.zh: 綸時自講大品經，令樞講維摩、老子、周易，同日發題，道俗聽者二千人。
entries.en: Lun then lectured on the Great Perfection Sutra himself and had Shu lecture on the Vimalakirti, Laozi, and Changes the same day; two thousand clergy and laymen listened.
entries.literal: Lun at the time himself lectured on the Great Perfection Sutra and had Shu lecture on the Vimalakirti, the Laozi, and the Changes, setting topics the same day; clergy and laity who listened numbered two thousand.

entries.zh: 王欲極觀優劣，乃謂眾曰：「與馬學士論義，必使屈伏，不得空立主客。」
entries.en: The prince wished to test who was stronger and told the crowd, "In debate with Academician Ma you must make him yield; do not leave guest and host empty."
entries.literal: The prince wished to observe fully the superior and inferior; he therefore said to the assembly: "In disputation with Academician Ma, you must make him yield—do not stand empty as guest and host."

entries.zh: 於是數家學者各起問端，樞乃依次剖判，開其宗旨，然後枝分流別，轉變無窮，論者拱默聽受而已。
entries.en: Several schools of scholars each raised questions. Shu answered in turn, opened each main point, then branched into endless distinctions; the debaters bowed and listened in silence.
entries.literal: Thereupon several families of scholars each rose to pose questions; Shu then in sequence analyzed and judged, opening their main points, then branching into streams and divisions, turning and changing without end; the debaters bowed in silence and only listened.

entries.zh: 綸甚嘉之，將引薦於朝廷。
entries.en: Lun greatly praised him and meant to recommend him at court.
entries.literal: Lun wished to recommend him to the court.

entries.zh: 尋遇侯景之亂，綸舉兵援臺，乃留書二萬卷以付樞。
entries.en: Soon came Hou Jing's rebellion. Lun raised troops to aid the capital and left twenty thousand scrolls with Shu.
entries.literal: Soon he encountered Hou Jing's rebellion; Lun raised troops to aid the Terrace City and left twenty thousand scrolls of books entrusted to Shu.

entries.zh: 樞肆志尋覽，殆將周遍，乃喟然歎曰：「吾聞貴爵位者以巢、由為桎梏，愛山林者以伊、呂為管庫，束名實則芻芥柱下之言，翫清虛則糠秕席上之說，稽之篤論，亦各從其好也。
entries.en: Shu read through them almost entirely and sighed: "I hear that men who prize office take Chao Fu and Xu You as shackles, and men who love the hills take Yi and Lü as storekeepers; those who bind name to fact treat Laozi as straw, and those who play at emptiness treat banquet talk as chaff. In earnest judgment each follows his own bent.
entries.literal: Shu with full intent searched and read them, nearly covering all; he then sighed and said: "I have heard that those who prize rank and title take Chao Fu and Xu You as fetters, and those who love mountains and forests take Yi and Lü as granary keepers; binding name and reality makes Laozi's words mere hay; playing with emptiness and purity makes seat-side doctrines mere chaff; checked against earnest discourse, each also follows his own preference.

entries.zh: 然支父有讓王之介，嚴子有傲帝之規，千載美談，所不廢也。
entries.en: Yet Zhi Fu refused the throne, and Yan Zi defied his ruler—tales a thousand years old that are not forgotten.
entries.literal: Yet Zhi Fu had the manner of yielding the kingship, and Yan Zi had the plan of defying the emperor—thousand-year fine tales that are not abandoned.

entries.zh: 比求志之士，望塗而息。
entries.en: Compared with men of resolve, today's seekers gaze at the road and give up.
entries.literal: Compared with seekers of resolve today, they gaze at the road and cease.

entries.zh: 豈天之不惠高尚，何山林之無聞甚乎？」
entries.en: Does Heaven not favor the high-minded, or why are recluses so seldom heard of?"
entries.literal: Is it that Heaven does not favor the lofty, or why are the hills and forests so little heard of?"

entries.zh: 乃隱于茅山，有終焉之志。
entries.en: He then retired to Mount Mao, intending to end his days there.
entries.literal: He then hid on Mount Mao, with the will to end his days there.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，文帝徵為度支尚書，辭不應命。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia Emperor Wen summoned him as director of revenue; he declined and did not answer.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, Emperor Wen summoned him as Director of Revenue; he declined and did not answer the command.

entries.zh: 時樞親故並居京口，每秋冬之際，時往遊焉。
entries.en: His kin and friends then lived at Jingkou; each autumn and winter he visited them.
entries.literal: At that time Shu's kin and old friends all dwelt at Jingkou; each year at the turn of autumn and winter he would go to visit them.

entries.zh: 及鄱陽王為南徐州刺史，欽其高尚，鄙不能致，乃卑辭厚意，令使者邀之，前後數反，樞固辭以疾。
entries.en: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of South Xuzhou, he admired Shu's loftiness and was ashamed he could not summon him; he used humble words and rich courtesy and sent envoys again and again, but Shu firmly pleaded illness.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Poyang was Inspector of South Xuzhou, admiring his loftiness and despising his inability to summon him, he therefore used humble words and thick kindness, ordering envoys to invite him—several times back and forth—yet Shu firmly declined on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 門人或進曰：「鄱陽王待以師友，非關爵位，市朝之間，何妨靜默。」
entries.en: A disciple urged him, "The prince of Poyang treats you as teacher and friend, not for rank. What harm in quiet presence amid court and market?"
entries.literal: A disciple advanced and said: "The Prince of Poyang treats you as teacher and friend—it is not about rank; amid market and court, what harm in keeping silence?"

entries.zh: 樞不得已，乃行。
entries.en: Shu, unable to refuse further, went.
entries.literal: Shu, having no way out, then went.

entries.zh: 王別築室以處之，樞惡其崇麗，乃於竹林間自營茅茨而居焉。
entries.en: The prince built him a separate house; Shu disliked its splendor and made a thatched hut in the bamboo grove.
entries.literal: The prince separately built a chamber to house him; Shu hated its grandeur and splendor and therefore in the bamboo grove built his own thatched hut to dwell in.

entries.zh: 每王公餽餉，辭不獲已者，率十分受一。
entries.en: When princes sent gifts he could not refuse, he usually took one part in ten.
entries.literal: Whenever princes and dukes sent gifts, of those he could not decline, he generally accepted one part in ten.

entries.zh: 陳書卷十九
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 19
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 19

entries.zh: 仲舉無他藝業，而立身耿正。
entries.en: Zhongju had no special craft, but he stood upright in his conduct.
entries.literal: Zhongju had no other art or profession, yet in establishing himself he was upright and steadfast.

entries.zh: 釋褐著作佐郎、太子舍人、王府主簿。
entries.en: He entered service as editorial officer of writings, palace gentleman in attendance, and chief clerk of a princely establishment.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Editorial Officer of Writings, Palace Gentleman in Attendance, and Chief Clerk of the Prince's establishment.

entries.zh: 出為長城令，政號廉平。
entries.en: Posted as magistrate of Changcheng, he won a name for honest, even rule.
entries.literal: He went out as magistrate of Changcheng; his governance was famed for integrity and fairness.

entries.zh: 文帝居鄉里，嘗詣仲舉，時天陰雨，仲舉獨坐齋內，聞城外有簫鼓之聲，俄而文帝至，仲舉異之，乃深自結託。
entries.en: While Emperor Wen was still in the countryside he once called on Zhongju. Rain fell under a leaden sky. Zhongju sat alone in his study and heard flutes and drums beyond the wall. Then Emperor Wen arrived. Struck by the omen, Zhongju gave him his deepest trust.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was in the countryside, he once visited Zhongju. The sky was cloudy and rainy; Zhongju sat alone in his study and heard outside the walls the sound of flutes and drums. Presently Emperor Wen arrived. Zhongju thought it strange and thereafter bound himself to him in deep trust.

entries.zh: 文帝又嘗因飲，夜宿仲舉帳中，忽有神光五采照于室內，由是祇承益恭。
entries.en: Emperor Wen once spent the night in Zhongju’s tent after wine. A five-colored light suddenly filled the room. From then on Zhongju served him with still greater reverence.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen once lodged in Zhongju's tent after drinking by night. Suddenly a divine light of five colors shone within the room; from this his reverent service grew still more deferential.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，仲舉依文帝。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zhongju cast his lot with Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhongju attached himself to Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 及景平，文帝為吳興郡守，以仲舉為郡丞，與潁川庾持俱為文帝賓客。
entries.en: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju his deputy. He and Yu Chi of Yingchuan both served as Emperor Wen’s clients.
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju deputy administrator; together with Yu Chi of Yingchuan they were both Emperor Wen's clients.

entries.zh: 文帝為宣毅將軍，以仲舉為長史，尋帶山陰令。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was made general who displays martial resolution, he named Zhongju chief clerk and soon gave him the magistracy of Shanyin as well.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was General Who Displays Martial Resolution, he made Zhongju chief clerk; soon he also held concurrently the magistracy of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，授侍中，參掌選事。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Zhongju was made palace attendant and helped manage appointments.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, [Zhongju] was appointed Palace Attendant and took part in managing selection affairs.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，守都官尚書，封寶安縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made acting minister of the masters of writing for officials and enfeoffed as Marquis of Bao’an with five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was made acting Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials, enfeoffed Marquis of Bao'an county with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 三年，除都官尚書。
entries.en: In the third year he was appointed minister of the masters of writing for officials.
entries.literal: In the third year he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials.

entries.zh: 其年，遷尚書右僕射、丹陽尹，參掌並如故。
entries.en: That year he was made right vice director of the masters of writing and metropolitan governor of Danyang, with the same role in government as before.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right) and Metropolitan Governor of Danyang; his participation in government remained as before.

entries.zh: 尋改封建昌縣侯。
entries.en: Soon his title was changed to Marquis of Jianchang.
entries.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Jianchang county.

entries.zh: 仲舉既無學術，朝章非所長，選舉引用，皆出自袁樞。
entries.en: Zhongju had no learning and court law was not his field. Every appointment came from Yuan Shu.
entries.literal: Zhongju had no learning or scholarship; court regulations were not his strength—all selections and appointments issued from Yuan Shu.

entries.zh: 性疏簡，不干涉世務，與朝士無所親狎，但聚財酣飲而已。
entries.en: He was spare by nature, kept out of public business, and was close to no courtier. He only hoarded money and drank.
entries.literal: By nature he was spare and simple, did not meddle in worldly affairs, and was intimate with no court officials; he merely amassed wealth and drank deep—that was all.

entries.zh: 六年，秩滿，解尹。
entries.en: In the sixth year his term ended and he left the metropolitan governorship.
entries.literal: In the sixth year his term expired and he was relieved of the metropolitan governorship.

entries.zh: 是時，文帝積年寢疾，不親御萬機，尚書中事，皆使仲舉斷決。
entries.en: By then Emperor Wen had lain ill for years and no longer ran the realm himself. Everything in the masters of writing went to Zhongju for decision.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wen had been bedridden with illness for years and did not personally oversee the myriad affairs of state; matters within the Masters of Writing were all left to Zhongju to decide.

entries.zh: 天康元年，遷侍中、尚書僕射，參掌如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he was made palace attendant and vice director of the masters of writing, with the same powers as before.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; his participation in government remained as before.

entries.zh: 文帝疾甚，入侍醫藥。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen grew desperately ill, Zhongju entered to nurse him with medicine.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen's illness grew grave, [Zhongju] entered to attend him with medicine.

entries.zh: 及文帝崩，高宗受遺詔為尚書令入輔，仲舉與左丞王暹、中書舍人劉師知、殷不佞等，以朝望有歸，乃遣不佞矯宣旨遣高宗還東府。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Xuan took the testament as director of the masters of writing and entered to govern. Zhongju, with the left assistant Wang Xian and secretariat attendants Liu Shizhi and Yin Bujiu, judged where the court’s hopes lay and sent Bujiu to forge an edict ordering Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Mansion.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Xuan received the testamentary edict as Director of the Masters of Writing and entered to assist in government. Zhongju, together with Left Assistant Wang Xian, Secretariat Attendants Liu Shizhi and Yin Bujiu, and others—because public expectation had a direction—then sent Bujiu to counterfeit an imperial order and send Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Mansion.

entries.zh: 事發，師知下北獄賜死，暹、不佞並付治，乃以仲舉為貞毅將軍、金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: When the plot came out, Shizhi was sent to the northern prison and granted death. Xian and Bujiu were handed over for trial. Zhongju was reduced to steadfast-resolution general and grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: When the affair was exposed, Shizhi was sent to the northern prison and granted death; Xian and Bujiu were both handed over for prosecution. Then Zhongju was made General of Steadfast Resolution and Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 初，仲舉子郁尚文帝妹信義長公主，官至中書侍郎，出為宣城太守，文帝配以士馬，是年遷為南康內史，以國哀未之任。
entries.en: Earlier Zhongju’s son Yu had married Emperor Wen’s sister, the Senior Princess of Xinyi. He rose to attendant gentleman of the secretariat, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, and Emperor Wen gave him troops and horses. That year he was named interior minister of Nankang but had not yet taken office because of the state mourning.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhongju's son Yu had married Emperor Wen's younger sister, Princess Xin'an the Long of Xinyi; he reached the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, went out as Administrator of Xuancheng; Emperor Wen supplied him with warriors and horses. That year he was transferred to Interior Minister of Nankang; because of the state mourning he had not yet taken up the appointment.

entries.zh: 仲舉既廢居私宅，與郁皆不自安。
entries.en: Zhongju, dismissed and living at home, and Yu both felt uneasy.
entries.literal: Zhongju, having been set aside and living in a private residence, and Yu both felt ill at ease.

entries.zh: 時韓子高在都，人馬素盛，郁每乘小輿蒙婦人衣與子高謀。
entries.en: Han Zigao was then in the capital with a large following of men and horses. Yu would ride in a small carriage dressed as a woman to plot with him.
entries.literal: At that time Han Zigao was in the capital; his men and horses had always been numerous. Yu each time rode in a small carriage, cloaked in women's dress, to plot with Zigao.

entries.zh: 子高軍主告言其事，高宗收子高、仲舉及郁並付廷尉。
entries.en: One of Zigao’s army commanders reported the affair. Emperor Xuan seized Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and sent them to the court of trials.
entries.literal: Zigao's army commander reported the affair. Emperor Xuan arrested Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and handed them over to the Court of Trials.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「到仲舉庸劣小才，坐叨顯貴，受任前朝，榮寵隆赫，父參王政，子據大邦，禮盛外姻，勢均戚里。
entries.en: An edict declared: “Dao Zhongju is a mediocre man raised by luck. The former court heaped rank on him: father in the government, son in a great commandery, affinal honors as grand as kinship, power to match the imperial clan.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Dao Zhongju is a mediocre, petty talent who by chance enjoyed high rank; he received office from the former court and glory and favor were lofty and bright—father participating in royal government, son holding a great commandery, ritual grand in affinal kinship, power equal to the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 而肆此驕闇，凌慠百司，遏密之初，擅行國政，排黜懿親，欺蔑台羇。
entries.en: Yet he grew arrogant and dark, insulting every office. At the start of the mourning silence he seized the government, drove out worthy kin, and mocked the Terrace.
entries.literal: Yet he indulged this arrogant darkness, insulted and defied the hundred offices; at the beginning of the mourning silence he usurped state government, expelled worthy kin, and scorned the Terrace posts.

entries.zh: 韓子高蕞爾細微，擢自卑末，入參禁衛，委以腹心，蜂蠆有毒，敢行反噬。
entries.en: Han Zigao is a nothing raised from the gutter. He entered the palace guard and won the innermost trust, yet like a bee or scorpion he turned to bite.
entries.literal: Han Zigao is a trifling, minute man, promoted from the lowest ranks, entered to join the palace guard, entrusted with the innermost confidence—yet the bee and scorpion have poison, and he dared turn to bite.

entries.zh: 仲舉、子高，共為表裏，陰構姦謀，密為異計。
entries.en: Zhongju and Zigao worked as outer shell and inner core, weaving treason in secret.
entries.literal: Zhongju and Zigao, together outer and inner, secretly wove treacherous plots and in secret made separate plans.

entries.zh: 安成王朕之叔父，親莫重焉，受命導揚，稟承顧託，以朕沖弱，屬當保祐。
entries.en: The Prince of Ancheng is my uncle, the closest of kin. He was charged to guide the state and bear the late emperor’s trust. Because I am young, he should protect me.
entries.literal: The Prince of Ancheng is Our uncle; in kinship none is heavier. He received the charge to guide and uplift, inherited the entrusted care; because We are young and weak, he ought to protect and preserve Us.

entries.zh: 家國安危，事歸宰輔，伊、周之重，物無異議，將相舊臣，咸知宗仰。
entries.en: The realm’s safety belongs to its chief ministers. The weight of Yi and Zhou is beyond dispute. Every old general and minister knows to look to him.
entries.literal: The safety of house and state rests with the chief ministers; the weight of Yi and Zhou—no one disputes it; the old ministers among generals and chancellors all know to look up to him as the standard.

entries.zh: 而率聚凶徒，欲相掩襲，屯據東城，進逼崇禮，規樹仲舉，以執國權，陵斥司徒，意在專政，潛結黨附，方危社稷。
entries.en: Yet they gathered villains for a surprise strike, massed at the Eastern City and pressed Chongli, meant to set up Zhongju and seize power, drive off the minister of works and rule alone, knit secret factions, and were about to endanger the dynasty.
entries.literal: Yet they gathered wicked followers, intending a surprise attack; they massed at the Eastern City and pressed upon Chongli, planning to set up Zhongju to seize state power, to drive off the Minister of Works with intent to monopolize government, secretly joining factions and parties, and were about to endanger the altars of state.

entries.zh: 賴祖宗之靈，姦謀顯露。
entries.en: Thanks to the ancestors’ spirits, the plot came to light.
entries.literal: Relying on the spirits of the ancestors, the treacherous plot was exposed.

entries.zh: 前上虞令陸昉等具告其事，並有據驗，并剋今月七日，縱其凶謀。
entries.en: The former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and others laid out the whole affair with proof. They had set the seventh of this month for the crime.
entries.literal: The former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and others fully reported the affair, and there is corroborating evidence; they fixed the seventh day of this month to carry out their wicked plot.

entries.zh: 領軍將軍明徹，左衛將軍、衛尉卿寶安及諸公等，又並知其事。
entries.en: Area commander Mingche, left guard general and commandant of the guards Bao’an, and the other dukes knew it as well.
entries.literal: Area Commander Mingche, Left Guard General and Commandant of the Guards Bao'an, and the various dukes and others also all knew of the affair.

entries.zh: 二三舋跡，彰於朝野，反道背德，事駭聞見。
entries.en: Their tracks show in court and country alike. Their treason shocks every eye and ear.
entries.literal: Two or three traces are plain in court and countryside; their contrary way and betrayed virtue horrify all who hear and see.

entries.zh: 今大憝克殲，罪人斯得，並可收付廷尉，肅正刑書。
entries.en: Now the great villain is cut down and the guilty taken. Let all be sent to the court of trials and judged by law.
entries.literal: Now the great villain is destroyed and the guilty are caught; all may be taken and handed to the Court of Trials to rectify the penal code.

entries.zh: 罪止仲舉父子及子高三人而已，其餘一從曠蕩，並所不問。」
entries.en: Guilt ends with Zhongju, his son, and Zigao—three people only. All others are wholly pardoned and will not be questioned.”
entries.literal: Guilt stops with Zhongju, father and son, and Zigao—three persons only; the rest are wholly pardoned and will not be questioned."

entries.zh: 仲舉及郁並於獄賜死，時年五十一。
entries.en: Zhongju and Yu were granted death in prison. He was fifty-one.
entries.literal: Zhongju and Yu were both granted death in prison; he was fifty-one years old.

entries.zh: 郁諸男女，以帝甥獲免。
entries.en: Yu’s sons and daughters were spared as the emperor’s affinal kin.
entries.literal: Yu's sons and daughters, as the emperor's affinal kin, were pardoned.

entries.zh: 韓子高，會稽山陰人也。
entries.en: Han Zigao came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Han Zigao was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 家本微賤。
entries.en: His family was very lowborn.
entries.literal: His family was originally of very low status.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，寓在京都。
entries.en: During Hou Jing’s rebellion he stayed in the capital.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he sojourned in the capital.

entries.zh: 景平，文帝出守吳興，子高年十六，為總角，容貌美麗，狀似婦人，於淮渚附部伍寄載欲還鄉，文帝見而問之，曰：「能事我乎？」
entries.en: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen went out to hold Wu Commandery. Zigao was sixteen, still wearing the boy’s knot, beautiful as a woman. At Huai Ford he joined a convoy bound home. Emperor Wen saw him and asked, “Will you serve me?”
entries.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Wen went out to hold Wu Commandery. Zigao was sixteen, in the age of the hair knot; his appearance was beautiful and his bearing like a woman's. At Huai Ford he attached to a convoy wishing to return home. Emperor Wen saw him and asked, "Can you serve me?"

entries.zh: 子高許諾。
entries.en: Zigao agreed.
entries.literal: Zigao agreed.

entries.zh: 子高本名蠻子，文帝改名之。
entries.en: His name had been Manzi; Emperor Wen renamed him.
entries.literal: Zigao's original name was Manzi; Emperor Wen changed his name.

entries.zh: 性恭謹，勤於侍奉，恆執備身刀及傳酒炙。
entries.en: He was respectful and careful, always at hand with the belt knife, pouring wine and serving roast meat.
entries.literal: By nature he was respectful and careful, diligent in service, always holding the belt knife for personal attendance and passing wine and roasted meat.

entries.zh: 文帝性急，子高恆會意旨。
entries.en: Emperor Wen was quick-tempered; Zigao always read his mind.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen was quick-tempered by nature; Zigao always grasped his intent.

entries.zh: 及長，稍習騎射，頗有膽決，願為將帥，及平杜龕，配以士卒。
entries.en: As he grew he learned riding and archery, showed daring, and wanted to be a commander. When Du Kan fell, he was given troops.
entries.literal: When he grew older he gradually learned horsemanship and archery; he had considerable daring and resolution and wished to be a commander; when Du Kan was pacified he was given troops.

entries.zh: 文帝甚寵愛之，未嘗離於左右。
entries.en: Emperor Wen doted on him and never let him leave his side.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen cherished him exceedingly and never let him leave his side.

entries.zh: 文帝嘗夢見騎馬登山，路危欲墮，子高推捧而升。
entries.en: Emperor Wen once dreamed he rode uphill on a perilous path about to fall. Zigao pushed and lifted him up.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen once dreamed he rode a horse up a mountain; the road was perilous and he was about to fall; Zigao pushed and supported him so he ascended.

entries.zh: 文帝之討張彪也，沈泰等先降，文帝據有州城，周文育鎮北郭香
entries.en: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered. Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered; Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang

entries.en: (Yan)
entries.literal: (Yan)

entries.zh: 巖寺。
entries.en: Yan Temple.
entries.literal: Yan Temple.

entries.zh: [1]張彪自剡縣夜還襲城，文帝自北門出，倉卒闇夕，軍人擾亂，文育亦未測文帝所在，唯子高在側，文帝乃遣子高自亂兵中往見文育，反命酬答，於闇中又往慰勞眾軍。
entries.en: [1] Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to storm the city. Emperor Wen slipped out the north gate. In the sudden dark the troops panicked. Wenyü did not know where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao stood beside him. Emperor Wen sent Zigao through the chaos to Wenyü to bring back his orders, then go again in the dark to steady the army.
entries.literal: Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. Emperor Wen went out through the northern gate. In the sudden rush of dark evening the soldiers were in turmoil; Wenyü too had not yet determined where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao was at his side. Emperor Wen then sent Zigao from amid the disorderly troops to go see Wenyü, return with orders and replies, and in the dark go again to comfort the armies.

entries.zh: 文帝散兵稍集，子高引導入文育營，因共立柵。
entries.en: Emperor Wen’s scattered men slowly gathered. Zigao led him into Wenyü’s camp and together they threw up palisades.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they built palisades.

entries.zh: 明日，與彪戰，彪將申縉復降[2]，彪奔松山，浙東平。
entries.en: The next day they fought Biao. Biao’s general Shen Jin surrendered again. [2] Biao fled to Song mountain and eastern Zhe was pacified.
entries.literal: The next day they fought Biao; Biao's general Shen Jin surrendered again Biao fled to Song mountain; eastern Zhe was pacified.

entries.zh: 文帝乃分麾下多配子高，子高亦輕財禮士，歸之者甚眾。
entries.en: Emperor Wen then gave Zigao many of his own followers. Zigao was generous and courteous to officers, and men flocked to him.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also was generous with wealth and courteous to officers; those who came to him were very numerous.

entries.zh: 文帝嗣位，除右軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Han Zigao became General of the Right Army.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Han Zigao was appointed General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，封文招縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia 1 (560), he was made Viscount of Wenzhao County with a three-hundred-household fief.
entries.literal: In Tianjia 1, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao County, with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 王琳至于柵口，子高宿衛臺內。
entries.en: When Wang Lin reached Zhankou, Zigao guarded the palace precincts.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin reached Zhankou, Zigao served as guard inside the palace precinct.

entries.zh: 及琳平，子高所統益多，將士依附之者，子高盡力論進，文帝皆任使焉。
entries.en: After Wang Lin was pacified, Zigao's command grew. He strongly recommended the officers and soldiers who joined him, and Emperor Wen put them all to use.
entries.literal: After Lin was pacified, those under Zigao's command increased; officers and soldiers who attached themselves to him were all earnestly recommended for advancement by Zigao, and Emperor Wen appointed and employed them all.

entries.zh: 二年，遷員外散騎常侍、壯武將軍、成州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year, he was promoted to Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of Mighty Valor, and Inspector of Chengzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of Mighty Valor, and Inspector of Chengzhou.

entries.zh: 及征留異，隨侯安都頓桃支嶺巖下。
entries.en: During the campaign against Liu Yi, he accompanied Hou Andu and camped below Taozhi Ridge.
entries.literal: When Liu Yi was campaigned against, he followed Hou Andu and encamped below the cliffs of Taozhi Ridge.

entries.zh: 時子高兵甲精銳，別御一營，單馬入陳，傷項之左，一髻半落。
entries.en: Zigao's troops were elite. Commanding a separate camp, he rode alone into the enemy line, where he was wounded on the left side of the neck and half his topknot was cut away.
entries.literal: At the time Zigao's troops and armor were elite; he separately commanded one camp, rode alone into the enemy formation, was wounded on the left side of the neck, and half of his topknot was cut away.

entries.zh: 異平，除假節、貞毅將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: After Liu Yi was pacified, he was appointed Acting with Staff, General of Resolute Constancy, and Administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: After Yi was pacified, he was appointed Acting with Staff, General of Resolute Constancy, and Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 五年，章昭達等自臨川征晉安，子高自安泉嶺會于建安，諸將中人馬最為彊盛。
entries.en: In the fifth year, when Zhang Zhaoda and the others marched from Linchuan against Jin'an, Zigao came over Anquan Ridge to meet them at Jian'an; of all the generals, his men and horses were the strongest.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Zhang Zhaoda and others marched from Linchuan against Jin'an; Zigao came from Anquan Ridge to join them at Jian'an, and among the generals his men and horses were the strongest.

entries.zh: 晉安平，以功遷通直散騎常侍，進爵為伯，增邑并前四百戶。
entries.en: After Jin'an was pacified, he was promoted for merit to Cavalier Attendant for Direct Service, advanced to Earl, and received an additional four hundred households counting the previous grant.
entries.literal: After Jin'an was pacified, for his merit he was promoted to Cavalier Attendant for Direct Service, advanced in noble rank to Earl, and his fief was increased, together with the former grant, by four hundred households.

entries.zh: 六年，徵為右衛將軍，至都，鎮領軍府。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was summoned as General of the Right Guard and, on reaching the capital, took up station at the Leading Army headquarters.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned to be General of the Right Guard; upon reaching the capital, he took station at the Headquarters of the Leading Army.

entries.zh: 文帝不豫，入侍醫藥。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen fell ill, Zigao attended him and oversaw his medicines.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was unwell, he entered to attend on his medicines.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，遷散騎常侍，右衛如故，移頓于新安寺。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Zigao became Cavalier Attendant while retaining the Right Guard post, and moved his quarters to Xin'an Monastery.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant, with the Right Guard as before, and moved his station to Xin'an Monastery.

entries.zh: 華皎，晉陵暨陽人。
entries.en: Hua Jiao was from Jiyang in Jinling.
entries.literal: Hua Jiao was a man of Jiyang in Jinling.

entries.zh: 世為小吏。
entries.en: His family had served for generations as minor officials.
entries.literal: For generations his family had been minor officials.

entries.zh: 皎，梁代為尚書比部令史。
entries.en: Under Liang, Jiao served as a clerk in the Bibu section of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: During Liang, Jiao served as a clerk of the Bibu section of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，事景黨王偉。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he served Wang Wei, an associate of Jing.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he served Wang Wei, one of Jing's faction.

entries.zh: 高祖南下，文帝為景所囚，皎遇文帝甚厚。
entries.en: When Gaozu marched south, Emperor Wen was being held by Jing, and Jiao treated him with great kindness.
entries.literal: When Gaozu went south, Emperor Wen was held prisoner by Jing, and Jiao treated Emperor Wen very generously.

entries.zh: 景平，文帝為吳興太守，以皎為都錄事，軍府穀帛，多以委之。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing and made Jiao chief recorder, entrusting much of the military office's grain and silk to him.
entries.literal: After Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing and made Jiao chief recorder; much of the army office's grain and silk was entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 皎聰慧，勤於簿領。
entries.en: Jiao was intelligent and diligent in handling records and accounts.
entries.literal: Jiao was intelligent and diligent with registers and accounts.

entries.zh: 及文帝平杜龕，仍配以人馬甲仗，猶為都錄事。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen pacified Du Kan, he assigned Jiao men, horses, armor, and weapons while keeping him as chief recorder.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Du Kan, he still assigned Jiao men, horses, armor, and weapons, and Jiao remained chief recorder.

entries.zh: 御下分明，善於撫養。
entries.en: He managed his subordinates with clarity and was good at looking after them.
entries.literal: In governing subordinates he was clear and orderly, and was good at caring for and sustaining them.

entries.zh: 時兵荒之後，百姓饑饉，皎解衣推食，多少必均，因稍擢為暨陽、山陰二縣令。
entries.en: In the aftermath of war and famine, when the people were starving, Jiao shared out clothing and food evenly, and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Jiyang and Shanyin counties.
entries.literal: At that time, after war and famine, the common people were hungry; Jiao shared clothing and food, making large and small portions equal, and was gradually promoted to magistrate of the two counties Jiyang and Shanyin.

entries.zh: 文帝即位，除開遠將軍，左軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Jiao was appointed General Who Opens the Distant and General of the Left Army.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Jiao was appointed General Who Opens the Distant and General of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，封懷仁縣伯，邑四百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia 1 (560), he was made Earl of Huairen County with a four-hundred-household fief.
entries.literal: In Tianjia 1, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huairen County, with a fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 王琳東下，皎隨侯瑱拒之。
entries.en: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Tian to resist him.
entries.literal: Wang Lin marched east; Jiao followed Hou Tian to resist him.

entries.zh: 琳平，鎮湓城，知江州事。
entries.en: When Lin fell, Jiao garrisoned Pen city and ran Jiangzhou affairs.
entries.literal: When Lin was pacified, [Jiao] garrisoned Pen city and oversaw Jiangzhou affairs.
