entries.zh: 時南州守宰多鄉里酋豪，不遵朝憲，文帝令皎以法馭之。
entries.en: Southern prefects and magistrates were often local strongmen who ignored the court. Emperor Wen ordered Jiao to bring them to heel by law.
entries.literal: At that time the prefects and magistrates of the southern provinces were mostly local chieftains and strongmen who did not obey court law; Emperor Wen ordered Jiao to rein them in by law.

entries.zh: 王琳奔散，將卒多附於皎。
entries.en: When Wang Lin’s army broke up, his officers and men mostly joined Jiao.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin was routed and scattered, generals and soldiers mostly attached themselves to Jiao.

entries.zh: 三年，除假節、通直散騎常侍、仁武將軍、新州刺史資，監江州。
entries.en: In the third year he was given provisional credentials, direct-communication regular attendant, benevolent and martial general, and inspector of Xinzhou’s salary while supervising Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year he was appointed provisional credentials, Regular Attendant Direct Communication, Benevolent and Martial General, and salary as Inspector of Xinzhou, supervising Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 尋詔督尋陽太原高唐南北新蔡五郡諸軍事、尋陽太守，假節、將軍、州資、監如故。
entries.en: Soon he was ordered to command armies in Xunyang, Taiyuan, Gaotang, and North and South Xincai and was made administrator of Xunyang, keeping his credentials, general’s title, salary, and supervision.
entries.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to supervise military affairs in the five commanderies of Xunyang, Taiyuan, Gaotang, South and North Xincai, and made him Administrator of Xunyang; provisional credentials, general, provincial salary, and supervision remained as before.

entries.zh: 周迪謀反，遣其兄子伏甲於船中，偽稱賈人，欲於湓城襲皎。
entries.en: Zhou Di rebelled and sent his nephew with hidden troops aboard ship, posing as merchants, to strike Jiao at Pen city.
entries.literal: Zhou Di plotted rebellion and sent his elder brother's son to lie in ambush aboard ship, falsely claiming to be merchants, intending to strike Jiao at Pen city.

entries.zh: 未發，事覺，皎遣人逆擊之，盡獲其船仗。
entries.en: Before they moved, the plot was found out. Jiao sent men against them and took all their ships and weapons.
entries.literal: Before it was launched the affair was discovered; Jiao sent men to intercept them and seized all their ships and arms.

entries.zh: 其年，皎隨都督吳明徹征迪，迪平，以功授散騎常侍、平南將軍、臨川太守，進爵為侯，增封并前五百戶。
entries.en: That year Jiao followed area commander Wu Mingche against Di. When Di fell, he was made regular attendant, general who pacifies the south, and administrator of Linchuan, raised to marquis with five hundred households in all.
entries.literal: That year Jiao followed Area Commander Wu Mingche to campaign against Di; when Di was pacified, by merit he was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Linchuan, advanced in rank to marquis, his fief increased together with the previous to five hundred households.

entries.zh: 未拜，入朝，仍授使持節、都督湘巴等四州諸軍事、湘州刺史，常侍、將軍如故。
entries.en: Before he took office he went to court and was given credentials as area commander over Xiang, Ba, and the other provinces and made inspector of Xiangzhou, retaining his attendant and general titles.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment he entered court and was thereupon given credentials, made Area Commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Xiang, Ba, and others, and Inspector of Xiangzhou; regular attendant and general remained as before.

entries.zh: 皎起自下吏，善營產業，湘川地多所出，所得並入朝廷，糧運竹木，委輸甚眾；
entries.en: Jiao rose from a petty clerk and knew how to build wealth. The Xiang region yields much, and he sent it all to court—grain, bamboo, timber, and convoys beyond count;
entries.literal: Jiao rose from a low clerk, was skilled at managing property; the lands of the Xiang river region produce much, and what he obtained all entered the court—grain transport, bamboo and timber, the deliveries entrusted were very numerous;

entries.zh: 至于油蜜脯菜之屬，莫不營辦。
entries.en: As for oil, honey, cured meats, and vegetables—nothing was left unprovided.
entries.literal: as for oil, honey, dried meats, vegetables, and the like, there was nothing he did not supply.

entries.zh: 又征伐川洞，多致銅鼓、生口，並送于京師。
entries.en: He also fought the hill peoples and sent bronze drums and captives to the capital in great numbers.
entries.literal: He also campaigned in the river valleys and cave settlements and brought in many bronze drums and captives, all sent to the capital.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，進號安南將軍，改封重安縣侯，[4]食邑一千五百戶。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Jiao was made general who pacifies the south and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong’an [4] with one thousand five hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, [Jiao's] title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, his enfeoffment changed to Marquis of Chong'an county, fief one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 文帝以湘州出杉木舟，使皎營造大艦金翅等二百餘艘，并諸水戰之具，欲以入漢及峽。
entries.en: Emperor Wen, since Xiangzhou furnished fir for ships, ordered Jiao to build more than two hundred Golden-Wing great ships and all river-war gear, intending to enter the Han and the gorges.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen, because Xiangzhou produced fir timber for boats, ordered Jiao to build more than two hundred great ships of the Golden-Wing type and all equipment for river warfare, intending to enter the Han and the Gorges.

entries.zh: 高宗入輔，子高兵權過重，深不自安，好參訪臺閣，又求出為衡、廣諸鎮。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan entered to govern, Zigao’s military power weighed too heavy. Uneasy, he frequented the Terrace offices and asked to be posted to Heng and Guang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered to assist in government, Zigao's military authority was excessive; he felt deeply ill at ease, liked to visit the Terrace offices, and also sought to go out to the garrisons of Heng and Guang.

entries.zh: 光大元年八月，前上虞縣令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反，高宗在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子，子高預焉，平旦入省，執之，送廷尉，其夕與到仲舉同賜死，時年三十。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Guangda year 1 (567), the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and one of Zigao’s army commanders reported a plot to rebel. Emperor Xuan was in the masters of writing office and called the officials to discuss the crown prince. Zigao came at dawn, was seized and sent to the court of trials, and that evening was granted death with Dao Zhongju. He was thirty.
entries.literal: Eighth month, first year of Guangda: the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and Zigao's army commander reported his plotting rebellion. Emperor Xuan was in the Masters of Writing office and thereupon summoned civil and military officials in post to discuss establishing the crown prince. Zigao was among them; at dawn he entered the office, was seized, and sent to the Court of Trials. That evening he was granted death together with Dao Zhongju; he was thirty years old.

entries.zh: 父延慶及子弟並原宥。
entries.en: His father Yanqing and his brothers and sons were all pardoned.
entries.literal: His father Yanqing and sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.

entries.zh: 延慶因子高之寵，官至給事中、山陰令。
entries.en: Through Zigao’s favor Yanqing rose to secretariat attendant and magistrate of Shanyin.
entries.literal: Yanqing, because of Zigao's favor, reached Attendant of the Secretariat and Magistrate of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 韓子高誅後，皎內不自安，繕甲聚徒，厚禮所部守宰。
entries.en: After Zigao’s death Jiao grew uneasy, armored men and gathered followers, and lavished gifts on his subordinate officials.
entries.literal: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao felt ill at ease within and repaired armor and gathered followers, treating the prefects and magistrates under him with lavish courtesy.

entries.zh: 高宗頻命皎送大艦金翅等，推遷不至。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan repeatedly ordered him to send the Golden-Wing great ships. Jiao stalled and would not deliver.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan repeatedly ordered Jiao to send the great Golden-Wing ships and the like; he put off and delayed and did not arrive.

entries.zh: 光大元年，密啟求廣州，以觀時主意，高宗偽許之，而詔書未出。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda (567) he secretly asked for Guangzhou to test the court’s mind. Emperor Xuan pretended to agree, but no edict had yet gone out.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized asking for Guangzhou to observe the court's intent; Emperor Xuan falsely assented, but the edict had not yet been issued.

entries.zh: 皎亦遣使句引周兵，又崇奉蕭巋為主，士馬甚盛。
entries.en: Jiao also sent envoys to draw in Northern Zhou troops and set up Xiao Kui as his sovereign. His army grew very large.
entries.literal: Jiao also sent envoys to draw in Northern Zhou troops and further honored Xiao Kui as sovereign; his warriors and horses were very numerous.

entries.zh: 詔乃以吳明徹為湘州刺史，實欲以輕兵襲之。
entries.en: An edict then named Wu Mingche inspector of Xiangzhou, intending in truth to strike Jiao with a light force.
entries.literal: An edict then made Wu Mingche Inspector of Xiangzhou, in fact intending to strike him with light troops.

entries.zh: 是時慮皎先發，乃前遣明徹率眾三萬，乘金翅直趨郢州，又遣撫軍大將軍淳于量率眾五萬，乘大艦以繼之，又令假節、冠武將軍楊文通別從安
entries.en: Fearing Jiao would move first, they sent Mingche with thirty thousand men in Golden-Wing ships straight for Yingzhou, and pacifying-the-army grand general Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand in great ships behind him, and ordered provisional-credentials crowned-with-martiality general Yang Wentong by a separate route from An
entries.literal: At that time, fearing Jiao would strike first, they first sent Mingche at the head of thirty thousand men, riding Golden-Wing [ships] straight for Yingzhou, and also sent Pacifying-the-Army Grand General Chunyu Liang at the head of fifty thousand men, riding great ships to follow after, and also ordered Provisional Credentials, Crowned-with-Martiality General Yang Wentong to set out separately from An

entries.en: (Cheng)
entries.literal: (Cheng)

entries.zh: 成步道出茶陵，[5]又令巴山太守黃法慧別從宜陽出澧陵，往掩襲，出其不意，并與江州刺史章昭達、郢州刺史程靈洗等參謀討賊。
entries.en: Cheng by the foot-path through Chaling, [5] and ordered Bashan administrator Huang Fahui from Yiyang through Liling for a surprise blow, together with Jiangzhou inspector Zhang Zhaoda, Yingzhou inspector Cheng Lingxi, and others to plan the suppression.
entries.literal: Cheng by the foot-path out through Chaling, and also ordered Administrator of Bashan Huang Fahui to set out separately from Yiyang through Liling to make a surprise attack, taking him unawares, and together with Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda, Inspector of Yingzhou Cheng Lingxi, and others to consult on suppressing the rebel.

entries.zh: 是時蕭巋遣水軍為皎聲援。
entries.en: Xiao Kui then sent a river fleet to support Jiao.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao Kui sent a river fleet to support Jiao.

entries.zh: 周武又遣其弟衛國公宇文直率眾屯魯山，又遣其柱國長胡公拓跋定人馬三萬，攻圍郢州。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou also sent his brother the Duke of Weiguo, Yuwen Zhi, to camp at Lushan, and his pillar of state Tuoba Ding with thirty thousand troops to besiege Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou also sent his younger brother the Duke of Weiguo, Yuwen Zhi, at the head of troops garrisoned at Lushan, and also sent his Pillar of State the Duke of Chang, Tuoba Ding, with thirty thousand men and horses to attack and besiege Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 蕭巋授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔，衡陽內史任蠻奴，巴陵內史潘智虔，岳陽太守章昭裕，
entries.en: Xiao Kui made Jiao minister of works and set Dai Sengshuo over Ba, Ren Mannu over Hengyang, Pan Zhiquan over Baling, and Zhang Zhaoyu over Yueyang;
entries.literal: Xiao Kui appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Administrator of Ba; Ren Mannu, Interior Minister of Hengyang; Pan Zhiquan, Interior Minister of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang;

entries.en: (Du)
entries.literal: (Du)

entries.zh: 桂陽太守曹宣，[6]湘東太守錢明，並隸於皎。
entries.en: Guiyang administrator Cao Xuan, [6] Xiangdong administrator Qian Ming, and others—all under Jiao’s command.
entries.literal: Guiyang Administrator Cao Xuan, Administrator of Xiangdong Qian Ming, and all were placed under Jiao.

entries.zh: 又長沙太守曹慶等本隸皎下，因為之用。
entries.en: Changsha administrator Cao Qing and others had already been Jiao’s men and now served him.
entries.literal: Also Administrator of Changsha Cao Qing and others had originally been under Jiao and therefore served his use.

entries.zh: 帝恐上流宰守並為皎扇惑，乃下詔曰：「賊皎輿皂微賤，特逢獎擢，任據藩牧，屬當寵寄，背斯造育，興構姦謀，樹立蕭氏，盟約彰露，鴆毒存心，志危宗社，扇結邊境，驅逼士庶，蟻聚巴、湘，豕突鄢、郢，逆天反地，人神忿嫉。
entries.en: The emperor feared upstream governors would side with Jiao and issued an edict: “The traitor Jiao rose from cart and stable. Promoted by chance to a frontier post, he should have been grateful. Instead he rebelled, enthroned the Xiao line, sealed open pacts, and aimed at the dynasty. He stirred the borders, drove the people, swarmed Ba and Xiang like ants, and charged Yan and Ying like boars—heaven and earth alike revile him.
entries.literal: The Emperor feared that the officials commanding the upper Yangtze would all be swayed by Jiao, and thereupon issued an edict saying: "The rebel Jiao is of cart-and-servant mean birth; he happened to meet with reward and promotion, was entrusted with a frontier post and ought to have received favored care, yet he turned against what nurtured him and raised treacherous plots, set up the Xiao house, their covenant and pact plain to see, poison and malice in his heart, his aim to endanger the altars of state, inciting the border regions, driving and pressing scholars and commoners, ants massed in Ba and Xiang, pigs charging at Yan and Ying, opposing Heaven and turning against earth—men and spirits alike rage.

entries.zh: 征南將軍量、安南將軍明徹、郢州刺史靈洗，受律專征，備盡心力，撫勞驍雄，舟師俱進，義烈爭奮，凶惡奔殄，獻捷相望，重氛載廓，言念泣罪，思與惟新。
entries.en: Campaigning-south general Liang, pacifying-south general Mingche, and Yingzhou inspector Lingxi took the law and marched with all their strength, heartening the brave as the fleets advanced together. Valor flared, the wicked were crushed, victory reports came in waves, and the foul air cleared. In judging guilt I look to renewal.
entries.literal: Campaigning-South General Liang, Pacifying-South General Mingche, and Inspector of Yingzhou Lingxi received the law and led the dedicated campaign, exhausting mind and strength, comforting and encouraging the fierce and heroic; the river forces advanced together; righteous valor vied in ardor; the vicious and wicked ran to destruction; reports of victory came one after another; heavy miasma was cleared away again and again. Speaking of weeping over guilt, We think of renewal.

entries.zh: 可曲赦湘、巴二州：凡厥為賊所逼制，預在凶黨，悉皆不問；
entries.en: Let Xiang and Ba be partly pardoned: all who were forced into the rebel ranks and joined the guilty faction shall go unquestioned;
entries.literal: A partial pardon may be granted to the two provinces of Xiang and Ba: all who were compelled by the rebels and took part in the wicked faction are wholly not to be questioned;

entries.zh: 其賊主帥節
entries.en: their rebel chieftains, commanders, and
entries.literal: their rebel chieftains', commanders', and

entries.en: (xiang)
entries.literal: (xiang)

entries.zh: 將，[7]並許開恩出首，一同曠蕩。」
entries.en: generals [7] may all surrender with clemency and share in a general amnesty."
entries.literal: jiang, [7] all are permitted to turn themselves in with grace and receive a general pardon together."

entries.zh: 曹慶本王琳將，蕭莊偽署左衛將軍、吳州刺史，部領亞於潘純陀。
entries.en: Cao Qing had been one of Wang Lin's generals; the puppet ruler Xiao Zhuang made him left guard general and inspector of Wu commandery, ranking below Pan Chuntuo.
entries.literal: Cao Qing had originally been a Wang Lin general; Xiao Zhuang falsely appointed him Left Guard General and Inspector of Wu commandery, and his command ranked below Pan Chuntuo's.

entries.zh: 琳敗，文帝以配皎，官至長沙太守。
entries.en: After Lin's defeat Emperor Wen placed him under Jiao; he rose to administrator of Changsha.
entries.literal: When Lin was defeated, Emperor Wen assigned him to Jiao; he rose to Administrator of Changsha.

entries.zh: 錢明，本高祖主帥，後歷湘州諸郡守。
entries.en: Qian Ming had once been a chief commander under the Founder and later held several posts as prefect in the Xiang region.
entries.literal: Qian Ming had originally been a chief commander under the Founder; afterward he successively held governorships in the Xiang region.

entries.zh: 潘智虔，純陀之子，少有志氣，年二十為巴陵內史。
entries.en: Pan Zhiquan was Chuntuo's son—spirited from youth and made inner administrator of Baling at twenty.
entries.literal: Pan Zhiquan was Chuntuo's son; from youth he had ambition and resolve, and at twenty he became Inner Administrator of Baling.

entries.zh: 魯閑，吳郡錢塘人。
entries.en: Lu Xian was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Xian was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 席慧略，安定人。
entries.en: Xi Huilüe was from Anding.
entries.literal: Xi Huilüe was a man of Anding.

entries.zh: 閑本張彪主帥，慧略王琳部下，文帝皆配于皎，官至郡守。
entries.en: Xian had served Zhang Biao as chief commander and Huilüe had been under Wang Lin; Emperor Wen gave both to Jiao, and each became a commandery governor.
entries.literal: Xian had originally been a Zhang Biao chief commander, and Huilüe a Wang Lin subordinate; Emperor Wen assigned both to Jiao, and each rose to a commandery governorship.

entries.zh: 並伏誅。
entries.en: All were put to death.
entries.literal: All were executed.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：韓子高、華皎雖復瓶筲小器，輿臺末品，文帝鑒往古之得人，救當今之急弊，達聰明目之術，安黎和眾之宜，寄以腹心，不論冑閥。
entries.en: The historian writes: Han Zigao and Hua Jiao were trifling men of humble birth, yet Emperor Wen—seeing how past ages chose talent and how pressing his own troubles were—used sharp judgment and policies that calmed the realm, and gave them his full trust without asking after their pedigrees.
entries.literal: The historian says: Although Han Zigao and Hua Jiao were but petty vessels and the lowest ranks of servitors, Emperor Wen, discerning how the ancients gained men and remedying the urgent ills of his own day, applied the art of keen sight and clear hearing and the policy of settling the people and harmonizing the masses—entrusting them with his inmost counsel without regard to pedigree.

entries.zh: 皎早參近昵，[8]嘗預艱虞，知其無隱，賞以悉力，有見信之誠，非可疑之地。
entries.en: Jiao had long served him closely [8], had shared danger, and showed he had nothing to hide; the emperor repaid him with full trust—grounds for confidence, not for doubt.
entries.literal: Jiao early took part in intimate service, [8] once shared in hardship and peril; [the emperor] knew that he had nothing to hide and rewarded him for exerting his full strength—there was the sincerity of one trusted, not ground for suspicion.

entries.zh: 皎據有上游，忠於文帝。
entries.en: Jiao held the upper river and had been loyal to Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Jiao held the upper Yangtze and was loyal to Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 仲舉、子高亦無爽於臣節者矣。
entries.en: Dao Zhongju and Zigao, too, had not failed in subject's duty.
entries.literal: Dao Zhongju and Zigao likewise did not fall short in the duty of a subject.

entries.zh: 章昭裕，昭達之弟；
entries.en: Zhang Zhaoyu was Zhaoda's younger brother;
entries.literal: Zhang Zhaoyu was Zhaoda's younger brother;

entries.zh: 劉廣業，廣德之弟；
entries.en: Liu Guangye was Guangde's younger brother;
entries.literal: Liu Guangye was Guangde's younger brother;

entries.zh: 曹宣，高祖舊臣；
entries.en: Cao Xuan was an old minister of the Founder;
entries.literal: Cao Xuan was an old minister of the Founder;

entries.zh: 任蠻奴嘗有密啟於朝廷；
entries.en: Ren Mannu had once sent a secret memorial to the court;
entries.literal: Ren Mannu had once sent a secret memorial to the court;

entries.zh: 由是並獲宥。
entries.en: for which they were all spared.
entries.literal: for this reason they all received pardon.

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 20
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 20

entries.zh: 性耿介，絕請託，雖儲副之尊，公侯之重，溺情相及，終不為屈。
entries.en: By nature he was unyielding and refused all private requests; neither the heir's rank nor the weight of dukes and marquises could make him bend.
entries.literal: By nature he was unyielding and cut off all private requests; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises, if feeling overflowed toward him, in the end he would not bend.

entries.zh: 始興王叔陵之在湘州，累諷有司，固求台鉉。
entries.en: While Prince Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly pressed the offices and demanded capital ministerial posts.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, was in Xiangzhou, he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and firmly sought capital ministerial posts.

entries.zh: 奐曰：「羇章之職，本以德舉，未必皇枝。」
entries.en: Huan said, "Capital memorial-review posts are raised by virtue and need not go to imperial kin."
entries.literal: Huan said: "Capital memorial-review posts are by nature raised through virtue and need not be imperial kin."

entries.zh: 因抗言於高宗。
entries.en: He then spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: He thereupon spoke boldly to Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 高宗曰：「始興那忽望公，且朕兒為公，須在鄱陽王後。」
entries.en: Emperor Xuan said, "How could Shixing suddenly want such a post? Even if my son held it, he would rank after the Prince of Poyang."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan said: "How could Shixing suddenly aspire to such a post? Besides, if my son were to hold it, he would have to come after the Prince of Poyang."

entries.zh: 奐曰：「臣之所見，亦如聖旨。」
entries.en: Huan said, "What I see agrees with Your Majesty's intent."
entries.literal: Huan said: "What your servant sees is also as in the sacred edict."

entries.zh: 後主時在東宮，欲以江總為太子詹事，令管記陸瑜言之於奐。
entries.en: Houzhu was then in the eastern palace and wanted Jiang Zong as grand tutor; he had recorder Lu Yu raise it with Huan.
entries.literal: Houzhu was then in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he had Recorder Lu Yu speak of it to Huan.

entries.zh: 奐謂瑜曰：「江有潘、陸之華，而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲宮，竊有所難。」
entries.en: Huan told Yu, "Jiang has Pan Yue and Lu Ji's brilliance, but not Qiuyuan and Chaofu's solid worth; as tutor to the heir I find it hard to approve."
entries.literal: Huan told Yu: "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan Yue and Lu Ji, but not the solid worth of Qiuyuan and Chaofu; to assist and support the heir's palace, I privately find it difficult."

entries.zh: 瑜具以白後主，後主深以為恨，乃自言於高宗。
entries.en: Yu reported this fully to Houzhu, who deeply resented it and then spoke to Emperor Xuan himself.
entries.literal: Yu reported it fully to Houzhu; Houzhu deeply resented it and thereupon spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 高宗將許之，奐乃奏曰：「江總文華之人，今皇太子文華不少，豈藉於總！
entries.en: Emperor Xuan was about to agree when Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a literary man, but the crown prince already has brilliance enough—why need Zong?
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to assent; Huan then memorialized, saying: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the present crown prince already has no little literary brilliance—why rely on Zong!

entries.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導。」
entries.en: In my humble view, choose a man of solid weight for the tutor's post."
entries.literal: In your servant's foolish view, I wish to choose a man of solid weight to occupy the post of guidance."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「即如卿言，誰當居此？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "If that is so, who should hold it?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "If it is as you say, who should hold this?"

entries.zh: 奐曰：「 都官尚書王廓，世有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。」
entries.en: Huan said, "Wang Kuo, minister of justice, comes from a family of fine virtue and is solid and quick in judgment—he can hold it."
entries.literal: Huan said: "Minister of Justice Wang Kuo, of a family with fine virtue through generations, knowing and by nature solid and quick, can hold it."

entries.zh: 後主時亦在側，乃曰：「廓王泰之子，不可居太子詹事。」
entries.en: Houzhu, who was also present, said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot be grand tutor."
entries.literal: Houzhu was then also at the side and said: "Kuo is the son of Wang Tai—he cannot hold the post of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince."

entries.zh: 奐又奏曰：「宋朝范廚即范泰之子，亦為太子詹事，前代不疑。」
entries.en: Huan memorialized again: "Under Liu Song, Fan Chu, Fan Tai's son, was grand tutor, and earlier ages raised no objection."
entries.literal: Huan again memorialized, saying: "In Liu Song, Fan Chu was the son of Fan Tai and also served as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; former ages did not doubt it."

entries.zh: 後主固爭之，帝卒以總為詹事，由是忤旨。
entries.en: Houzhu argued stubbornly; the emperor finally made Zong grand tutor, and Huan fell foul of the throne.
entries.literal: Houzhu stubbornly disputed it; the Emperor in the end made Zong Grand Tutor, and from this Huan went against the imperial intent.

entries.zh: 其梗正如此。
entries.en: His unyielding character was like this.
entries.literal: His unyielding uprightness was like this.

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十一
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 21
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 21

entries.zh: 子隆少慷慨，有志功名。
entries.en: As a youth Zilong was open-handed and ambitious, hungry for achievement and renown.
entries.literal: Zilong in youth was generous and high-minded and aspired to merit and fame.

entries.zh: 起家東宮直後。
entries.en: He entered service as a direct attendant in the eastern palace.
entries.literal: He began his career as a direct attendant in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，於鄉里聚徒。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled he raised men in his home district.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered followers in his home district.

entries.zh: 是時張彪為吳郡太守，引為將帥。
entries.en: Zhang Biao was then administrator of Wu and made him a field commander.
entries.literal: At that time Zhang Biao was Administrator of Wu commandery and took him on as a commander.

entries.zh: 彪徙鎮會稽，子隆隨之。
entries.en: When Biao shifted his headquarters to Kuaiji, Zilong went with him.
entries.literal: When Biao moved his garrison to Kuaiji, Zilong followed him.

entries.zh: 及世祖討彪，彪將沈泰、吳寶真、申縉等皆降，而子隆力戰敗績，世祖義之，復使領其部曲，板為中兵參軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen moved against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and the rest surrendered—but Zilong fought on and lost. Emperor Wen admired his constancy, restored him to his old troops, and brevetted him military adjutant of the central guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and others all surrendered, but Zilong fought hard and was defeated; Emperor Wen honored his loyalty, had him again lead his old command, and commissioned him military adjutant of the central guard.

entries.zh: 歷始豐、永興二縣令。
entries.en: He served in turn as magistrate of Shifeng and Yongxing.
entries.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Shifeng and Yongxing counties.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，子隆領甲仗宿衛。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, Zilong commanded the armored palace guard.
entries.literal: When Shizu succeeded to the throne, Zilong commanded the armored guards on palace watch.

entries.zh: 尋隨侯安都拒王琳於柵口。
entries.en: Soon he accompanied Hou Andu in resisting Wang Lin at Zhankou.
entries.literal: Soon he followed Hou Andu in resisting Wang Lin at Zhankou.

entries.zh: 王琳平，授左中郎將。
entries.en: After Wang Lin was subdued, he was appointed General of the Left Gentlemen-of-the-Household.
entries.literal: After Wang Lin was pacified, he was appointed General of the Left Gentlemen-of-the-Household.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，封益陽縣子，邑三百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia 1 (560), he was made Viscount of Yiyang County with a three-hundred-household fief.
entries.literal: In Tianjia 1, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiyang County, with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 出為高唐郡太守。
entries.en: He was then sent out as Administrator of Gaotang Commandery.
entries.literal: He went out to serve as Administrator of Gaotang Commandery.

entries.zh: 二年，除明威將軍、廬陵太守。
entries.en: In the second year, he became General of Brilliant Might and Administrator of Luling.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was appointed General of Brilliant Might and Administrator of Luling.

entries.zh: 時周迪據臨川反，東昌縣人脩行師應之，率兵以攻子隆，其鋒甚盛。
entries.en: When Zhou Di rebelled from Linchuan, Xiu Xingshi of Dongchang County answered his call and led a powerful attack against Zilong.
entries.literal: At the time Zhou Di occupied Linchuan and rebelled; Xiu Xingshi of Dongchang County responded to him and led troops to attack Zilong, with a very strong vanguard.

entries.zh: 子隆設伏於外，仍閉門偃甲，示之以弱。
entries.en: Zilong set an ambush outside the city, then shut the gates and hid his armor to make himself look weak.
entries.literal: Zilong set an ambush outside, then closed the gates and laid down armor, showing weakness to him.

entries.zh: 及行師至，腹背擊之，行師大敗，因乞降，子隆許之，送于京師。
entries.en: When Xingshi arrived, Zilong attacked him from front and rear, routed him, accepted his plea to surrender, and sent him to the capital.
entries.literal: When Xingshi arrived, Zilong struck him front and rear; Xingshi was greatly defeated and then begged to surrender, which Zilong allowed, sending him to the capital.

entries.zh: 四年，周迪引陳寶應復出臨川，子隆隨都督章昭達討迪。
entries.en: In the fourth year, Zhou Di brought Chen Baoying back into the field at Linchuan, and Zilong joined Commander Zhang Zhaoda's campaign against him.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, Zhou Di brought Chen Baoying back out to Linchuan, and Zilong followed Commander Zhang Zhaoda in campaigning against Di.

entries.zh: 迪退走，因隨昭達踰東興嶺，討陳寶應。
entries.en: After Di retreated, Zilong followed Zhaoda across Dongxing Ridge to attack Chen Baoying.
entries.literal: When Di withdrew and fled, Zilong then followed Zhaoda over Dongxing Ridge to campaign against Chen Baoying.

entries.zh: 軍至建安，以子隆監郡。
entries.en: When the army reached Jian'an, Zilong was put in charge of the commandery.
entries.literal: When the army reached Jian'an, Zilong was made supervisor of the commandery.

entries.zh: 寶應據建安之湖際以拒官軍，子隆與昭達各據一營，昭達先與賊戰，不利，亡其鼓角，子隆聞之，率兵來救，大破賊徒，盡獲昭達所亡羽儀甲仗。
entries.en: Baoying held the lakeside at Jian'an against the government army, while Zilong and Zhaoda occupied separate camps. Zhaoda engaged first, was defeated, and lost his drums and horns; Zilong heard of it, led troops to the rescue, routed the rebels, and recovered all the insignia, armor, and equipment Zhaoda had lost.
entries.literal: Baoying occupied the lakeside of Jian'an to resist the government army; Zilong and Zhaoda each occupied one camp. Zhaoda first fought the rebels and was unsuccessful, losing his drums and horns; when Zilong heard of it, he led troops to rescue him, greatly defeated the rebel band, and recovered all the banners, insignia, armor, and weapons that Zhaoda had lost.

entries.zh: 晉安平，子隆功最，遷假節、都督武州諸軍事，將軍如故。
entries.en: After Jin'an was pacified, Zilong received the highest credit and was promoted to Acting with Staff and Commander of military affairs in Wuzhou, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: After Jin'an was pacified, Zilong's merit was greatest; he was promoted to Acting with Staff and Commander of all military affairs in Wuzhou, with his generalship as before.

entries.zh: 尋改封朝陽縣伯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: Soon his fief was changed to Earl of Chaoyang County, with five hundred households.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred in enfeoffment as Earl of Chaoyang County, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，進號智武將軍，加員外散騎常侍，餘如故。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, he was advanced to General of Wise Valor and additionally made Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant; his other posts remained unchanged.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, his title was advanced to General of Wise Valor and he was additionally made Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant, the rest as before.

entries.zh: 牙年十二，宗人有善相者，云「此郎容貌非常，必將遠致」。
entries.en: At twelve a clansman skilled in faces said, "This lad's looks are not ordinary. He will go far."
entries.literal: At twelve, a kinsman skilled in physiognomy said, "This boy's countenance is extraordinary; he will surely reach far."

entries.zh: 梁太清末，世祖嘗避地臨安，牙母陵，[4]睹世祖儀表，知非常人，賓待甚厚。
entries.en: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.

entries.zh: 及世祖為吳興太守，引牙為將帥，因從平杜龕、張彪等，每戰輒先鋒陷陣，[5]勇冠眾軍，以功授直閤將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen became administrator of Wuxing he made Ya a commander. Ya followed him against Du Kan, Zhang Biao, and the rest, always first through the breach; [5] his bravery outshone every unit. For merit he was made direct-gate general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing he took Ya on as a commander; Ya followed him in pacifying Du Kan, Zhang Biao, and others; in every battle he always took the van and broke the line, his courage topped all the armies; for merit he was made Direct-Gate General.

entries.zh: 太平二年，以母憂去職。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiping (557) he left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiping he left office for his mother's mourning.

entries.zh: 世祖鎮會稽，起為山陰令。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen held Kuaiji he was recalled as magistrate of Shanyin.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Kuaiji he was recalled to serve as magistrate of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 永定三年，除安東府中兵參軍，出鎮冶城。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongding (559) he was made central-guard military adjutant in the pacifying-east staff and went out to hold Yecheng.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongding he was made military adjutant of the central guard in the Pacifying East establishment and went out to garrison Yecheng.

entries.zh: 尋從世祖拒王琳於南皖。
entries.en: Soon he followed Emperor Wen against Wang Lin at South Wan.
entries.literal: Soon he followed Emperor Wen in resisting Wang Lin at South Wan.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，授假節、威虜將軍、員外散騎常侍，封常安縣侯，[6]邑五百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was given credentials as might-subduing general and supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an [6] with five hundred households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne he was given credentials, made Might-Subduing General and Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an county, fief five hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋為臨安令，遷越州刺史，餘並如故。
entries.en: Soon he was magistrate of Lin'an, then inspector of Yue, his other titles unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he was made magistrate of Lin'an, then transferred to Inspector of Yue; the rest unchanged.

entries.zh: 道戢少以孝行著聞，及長，頗有幹略，高祖微時，以從妹妻焉。
entries.en: Daoji was known early for filial piety and, grown, showed real capacity. In the Founder's lean years the Founder married him to a cousin.
entries.literal: Daoji in youth was famed for filial conduct; when grown he had considerable resource and plan; in the Founder's early days the Founder gave him a cousin in marriage.

entries.zh: 從平盧子略於廣州，除濱江令。
entries.en: He took part in pacifying Lu Zilue at Guangzhou and was made magistrate of Binjiang.
entries.literal: He followed in the pacification of Lu Zilue at Guangzhou and was made magistrate of Binjiang.

entries.zh: 高祖輔政，遣道戢隨世祖平張彪于會稽，以功拜直閤將軍，除員外散騎常侍、假節、東徐州刺史，封永安縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: While the Founder held regency he sent Daoji with Emperor Wen to crush Zhang Biao at Kuaiji. For merit he was made direct-gate general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant with credentials, and inspector of East Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with five hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Founder acted as regent he sent Daoji to follow Emperor Wen in pacifying Zhang Biao at Kuaiji; for merit he was made Direct-Gate General, Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant with credentials, and Inspector of East Xuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 仍領甲卒三千，隨侯安都鎮防梁山，尋領錢塘、餘杭二縣令。
entries.en: He still commanded three thousand armored men, joined Hou Andu in garrisoning Liangshan, and soon held Qiantang and Yuhang as well.
entries.literal: He still led three thousand armored troops, followed Hou Andu to garrison and defend Liangshan, and soon also held the magistracies of Qiantang and Yuhang counties.

entries.zh: 永定三年，隨世祖鎮于南皖口。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongding (559) he followed Emperor Wen to garrison South Wan Ford.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongding he followed Emperor Wen in garrisoning at South Wan Ford.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，又領剡令，鎮于縣之南巖，尋為臨海太守，鎮巖如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he added the magistracy of Shan and garrisoned the county's Southern Cliff. Soon he was made administrator of Linhai while keeping that post.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he also held the magistracy of Shan, garrisoning at the county's Southern Cliff; soon he was made Administrator of Linhai, his garrison at the cliff unchanged.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：陸子隆、錢道戢，或舉門願從，或舊齒樹勳，有統領之才，充師旅之寄。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Lu Zilong and Qian Daoji—one brought his house to follow, one stood with the Founder from the first—both could lead and were trusted with the armies.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Lu Zilong and Qian Daoji—one brought his whole household to follow, the other was an old companion who raised merit from the first—both had talent to command and were fit to bear the army's trust.

entries.zh: 至於受任藩屏，功績並著，美矣！
entries.en: Given frontier command and shared achievement—how fine indeed!
entries.literal: As to receiving border appointments and achieving merit together—how fine!

entries.zh: 駱牙識真有奉，知世祖天授之德，蓋張良之亞歟？
entries.en: Luo Ya saw true worth and served it; he knew Emperor Wen bore heaven's mandate—was he not Zhang Liang's peer?
entries.literal: Luo Ya recognized true worth and served it; he knew Emperor Wen's heaven-granted virtue—was he not next to Zhang Liang?

entries.zh: 牙母智深先覺，符柏谷之禮，君子知鑒識弘遠，其在茲乎！
entries.en: Ya's mother, wise before the fact, matched the courtesy of Bo Valley. A gentleman will say that vision reaching far lived here.
entries.literal: Ya's mother, wise and foreseeing, matched the rite of Bo Valley; the gentleman knows that keen judgment reaching far—was it not here?

entries.zh: 高宗即位，徵歐陽紇入朝，紇疑懼，乃舉兵來攻衡州，道戢與戰，卻之。
entries.en: When Gaozong took the throne, he summoned Ouyang He to court. Suspicious and afraid, He raised troops against Hengzhou, but Daoji fought him off.
entries.literal: When Gaozong ascended, he summoned Ouyang He to court; He became suspicious and afraid, and raised troops to attack Hengzhou. Daoji fought him and drove him back.

entries.zh: 及都督章昭達率兵討紇，以道戢為步軍都督，由間道斷紇之後。
entries.en: When Commander Zhang Zhaoda led the campaign against He, he put Daoji in command of the infantry; Daoji took a side road and cut off He's rear.
entries.literal: When Commander Zhang Zhaoda led troops to campaign against He, he made Daoji commander of the infantry, and by a bypath cut off He's rear.

entries.zh: 紇平，除左衛將軍。
entries.en: After He was subdued, Daoji was appointed General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: After He was pacified, Daoji was appointed General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 太建二年，又隨昭達征蕭巋於江陵，道戢別督眾軍與陸子隆焚青泥舟艦，仍為昭達前軍，攻安蜀城，降之。
entries.en: In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Anshu City, and received its surrender.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Anshu City, and reduced it.

entries.zh: 以功加散騎常侍、仁武將軍，增邑并前九百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and benevolent-martial general, his fief rising to nine hundred households in all.
entries.literal: For merit he was advanced to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Benevolent Martial General; his fief was increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.

entries.zh: 其年，遷仁威將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: That year he was made benevolent-prestige general and administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Benevolent Prestige General and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 未行，改授使持節、都督郢巴武三州諸軍事、郢州刺史。
entries.en: Before he went out he was reassigned with the staff as commander of Ying, Ba, and Wu and inspector of Ying.
entries.literal: Before he took up the post he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Ying, Ba, and Wu, and Inspector of Ying.

entries.zh: 王師北討，道戢與儀同黃法𣰋圍歷陽。
entries.en: When the imperial troops marched north, Daoji and the yitong officer Huang Faqu besieged Liyang.
entries.literal: When the imperial army marched north to campaign, Daoji with the yitong officer Huang Faqu besieged Liyang.

entries.zh: 歷陽城平，因以道戢鎮之。
entries.en: When Liyang fell he was left to hold the city.
entries.literal: When Liyang city was pacified, Daoji was left to garrison it.

entries.zh: 以功加雲麾將軍，增邑并前一千五百戶。
entries.en: For merit he was promoted to cloud-banner general, his fief brought to one thousand five hundred households in all.
entries.literal: For merit he was advanced to Cloud-Banner General; his fief was increased together with the previous to one thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 其年十一月遘疾卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: That year, in the eleventh month, he sickened and died, aged sixty-three.
entries.literal: That year, in the eleventh month, he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 贈本官，諡曰肅。
entries.en: He was posthumously granted his last office, with the posthumous name Su.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given his former office; his posthumous name was Su.

entries.zh: 子邈嗣。
entries.en: His son Miao succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Miao inherited.

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十二
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 22
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 22

entries.zh: 沈君理字仲倫，吳興人也。
entries.en: Shen Junli, whose style name was Zhonglun, came from Wuxing.
entries.literal: Shen Junli, styled Zhonglun, was a native of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 祖僧畟，梁左民尚書。
entries.en: His grandfather Sengji had served the Liang as director of the left bureau of the people.
entries.literal: His grandfather Sengji served the Liang as Director of the Left Bureau of the People.

entries.zh: 父巡，素與高祖相善，梁太清中為東陽太守。
entries.en: His father Xun had long been on friendly terms with the Founder and, during the Liang Taiqing era, served as administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: His father Xun had long been on good terms with the Founder; in the Taiqing era of the Liang he served as Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 侯景平後，元帝徵為少府卿。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was defeated, Emperor Yuan summoned him to serve as minister steward.
entries.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Minister Steward.

entries.zh: 荊州陷，蕭詧署金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell, Xiao Cha appointed him grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou fell, Xiao Cha appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 繕幼有志尚，以雅正知名。
entries.en: From youth Shan had high aims and was known for elegance and integrity.
entries.literal: From youth Shan had ambition and principle, and he was known for elegance and uprightness.

entries.zh: 起家梁宣惠武陵王法曹參軍。
entries.en: He began his career as legal affairs aide to the Liang Prince Xuanhui of Wuling.
entries.literal: He began his career as legal affairs aide to the Liang Prince Xuanhui of Wuling.

entries.zh: 承聖中，授中書侍郎，掌東宮管記。
entries.en: In the Chengsheng era he was appointed Secretariat attendant and put in charge of Eastern Palace records.
entries.literal: During Chengsheng, he was appointed Secretariat attendant and managed records for the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，繕微服遁還京師。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Shan slipped away in plain clothes and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Shan escaped in plain clothes and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 紹泰元年，除司徒右長史，御史中丞，以父任所終，固辭不就。
entries.en: In Shaotai year 1 he was appointed right chief clerk to the minister of education and imperial censor-in-chief, but since his father Ren had died in that office, he firmly declined it.
entries.literal: In Shaotai year 1, he was appointed right chief clerk to the minister of education and imperial censor-in-chief, but because his father Ren had died in that office, he firmly declined and did not take it up.

entries.zh: 高祖引繕為司徒司馬，遷給事黃門侍郎、領步兵校尉、通直散騎常侍，兼侍中。
entries.en: Gaozu brought Shan in as marshal to the minister of education, then transferred him to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, concurrently commandant of infantry, attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, and acting palace attendant.
entries.literal: Gaozu brought Shan in as marshal to the minister of education, then transferred him to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, concurrently commandant of infantry, attendant-in-ordinary of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, and acting palace attendant.

entries.zh: 永定元年，遷侍中。
entries.en: In Yongding year 1 he was transferred to palace attendant.
entries.literal: In Yongding year 1, he was transferred to palace attendant.

entries.zh: 時留異擁割東陽，新安人向文政與異連結，因據本郡，朝廷以繕為貞威將軍、新安太守。
entries.en: At the time Liu Yi controlled Dongyang as a separatist, and Xiang Wenzheng of Xin'an joined him and occupied his home commandery. The court made Shan general of steadfast prestige and administrator of Xin'an.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Yi held and partitioned Dongyang, and Xiang Wenzheng of Xin'an allied with Yi and occupied his home commandery; the court made Shan general of steadfast prestige and administrator of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 君理美風儀，博涉經史，有識鑒。
entries.en: Junli possessed fine bearing and appearance, read widely in the classics and histories, and showed sound judgment.
entries.literal: Junli had fine bearing and appearance, ranged widely through the classics and histories, and possessed discernment.

entries.zh: 起家湘東王法曹參軍。
entries.en: He began his career as legal affairs aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: He began his career as Legal Affairs Aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮南徐州，巡遣君理自東陽謁于高祖，高祖器之，命尚會稽長公主，辟為府西曹掾。
entries.en: When the Founder was posted to Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli from Dongyang to call on him. The Founder took a liking to him, had him marry the elder princess of Kuaiji, and appointed him western bureau aide in his headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Founder held Southern Xuzhou, Xun sent Junli from Dongyang to pay his respects to the Founder; the Founder valued him, had him marry the Elder Princess of Kuaiji, and recruited him as Western Bureau Aide in his headquarters.

entries.zh: 稍遷中衛豫章王從事中郎，尋加明威將軍，兼尚書吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was gradually promoted to attendant gentleman under the Prince of Yuzhang in the central guard, and soon received the additional rank of general of illustrious prestige while serving concurrently as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was gradually promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Prince of Yuzhang in the Central Guard, and soon added the title General of Illustrious Prestige while concurrently serving as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，監吳郡。
entries.en: He was transferred to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate and given supervisory duties over Wu commandery.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and supervised Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，拜駙馬都尉，封永安亭侯。
entries.en: When the Founder accepted the abdication, Junli was appointed commandant of the stable for the imperial son-in-law and enfeoffed as marquis of Yong'an village.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Junli was appointed Commandant of the Stable for the Imperial Son-in-Law and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an Village.

entries.zh: 出為吳郡太守。
entries.en: He was posted as administrator of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 是時兵革未寧，百姓荒弊，軍國之用，咸資東境，君理招集士卒，脩治器械，民下悅附，深以幹理見稱。
entries.en: Warfare had not yet ended and the people were impoverished; the costs of army and state all fell on the eastern territories. Junli recruited soldiers, repaired arms and equipment, and won the people's willing attachment, earning high praise for his administrative skill.
entries.literal: At that time warfare had not yet subsided and the people were destitute; military and state expenses all depended on the eastern territories. Junli gathered troops, repaired weapons, and the populace gladly attached themselves to him; he was deeply praised for his administrative ability.

entries.zh: 高祖入輔，以為司徒左長史。
entries.en: When the Founder entered the capital as regent, Yang was appointed left chief clerk of the ministry of education.
entries.literal: When the Founder entered the capital as regent, Yang was appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

entries.zh: 永定元年，遷守五兵尚書。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongding he was transferred to serve as acting minister of the five arms.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongding he was transferred to serve as Acting Minister of the Five Arms.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，授散騎常侍，領太子庶子，侍東宮。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Yang was granted the rank of attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, appointed chief tutor to the heir apparent, and attended the eastern palace.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Yang was granted the title Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Chief Tutor to the Heir Apparent, attending the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 遷領左驍騎將軍、太子中庶子，常侍、侍中如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to command the left valiant cavalry and appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, while retaining his posts as attendant-in-ordinary and palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to command the Left Valiant Cavalry and appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; his posts as attendant-in-ordinary and palace attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 瑒為侍中六載，父沖嘗為瑒辭領中庶子，世祖顧謂沖曰：「所以久留瑒於承華，政欲使太子微有瑒風法耳。」
entries.en: Yang had served as palace attendant for six years. His father Chong once asked that Yang be relieved of the concurrent post of junior tutor. Emperor Wen turned to Chong and said, 'The reason I have kept Yang at Chenghua so long is simply that I want the heir apparent to absorb even a little of Yang's bearing and standards.'
entries.literal: Yang had served as Palace Attendant for six years; his father Chong once petitioned on Yang's behalf to resign the concurrent post of junior tutor; the Emperor Wen turned to Chong and said: 'The reason I have long kept Yang at Chenghua is simply that I wish the Heir Apparent to acquire even a little of Yang's manner and standards.'

entries.zh: 廢帝嗣位，以侍中領左驍騎將軍。
entries.en: When the deposed emperor succeeded to the throne, Yang served as palace attendant while commanding the left valiant cavalry.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded to the throne, Yang served as Palace Attendant while commanding the Left Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 光大元年，以父憂去職。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda he left office to observe mourning for his father.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda he left office on account of his father's death.

entries.zh: 王瑒字子璵，司空沖之第十二子也。
entries.en: Wang Yang, whose style name was Ziyu, was the twelfth son of Wang Chongzhi, minister of works.
entries.literal: Wang Yang, styled Ziyu, was the twelfth son of Chongzhi, minister of works.

entries.zh: 沈靜有器局，美風儀，舉止醞藉。
entries.en: He was calm and composed, with broad capacity, handsome bearing, and restrained, gracious manners.
entries.literal: He was calm and composed, with breadth of capacity; his bearing was handsome and his movements restrained and gracious.

entries.zh: 梁大同中，起家祕書郎，遷太子洗馬。
entries.en: In the Liang Datong era he began as secretary gentleman and was transferred to groom to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: During Liang's Datong era, he began his career as secretary gentleman and was transferred to groom to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 元帝承制，徵為中書侍郎，直殿省，仍掌相府管記。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan exercised provisional authority, he summoned Wang Yang as Secretariat attendant; Yang served in the palace offices and managed records for the chancellery.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan acted under provisional authority, he summoned Wang Yang as Secretariat attendant; Yang served on duty in the palace offices and also managed records in the chancellery.

entries.zh: 出為東宮內史，[2]遷太子中庶子。
entries.en: He was posted as interior minister of the Eastern Palace [2] and then transferred to junior tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was sent out as interior minister of the Eastern Palace [2] and was transferred to junior tutor to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 丁所生母憂，歸于丹陽。
entries.en: When his birth mother died, he returned to Danyang for mourning.
entries.literal: He encountered mourning for his birth mother and returned to Danyang.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，梁敬帝承制，除仁威將軍、尚書吏部郎中。
entries.en: After Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang, acting under provisional authority, appointed him general of humane prestige and director in the personnel bureau of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang, acting under provisional authority, appointed him general of humane prestige and director in the personnel bureau of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 貞陽侯僭位，以敬帝為太子，授瑒散騎常侍，侍東宮。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne and made Emperor Jing crown prince, Yang was appointed attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and assigned to serve in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang usurped the throne and made Emperor Jing heir apparent, he appointed Yang attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry to serve in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 尋遷長（史）兼侍中。
entries.en: Before long he was transferred to senior acting palace attendant.
entries.literal: Before long he was transferred to senior acting palace attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，徵為侍中，遷守左民尚書，未拜，為明威將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Junli was summoned as palace attendant and transferred to act as minister of the left bureau of the people. Before he took up the post, he was made general of bright prestige and intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: When Shizu succeeded to the throne, Junli was summoned as palace attendant, then transferred to act as minister of the left bureau of the people; before taking office, he was made general of bright prestige and intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 天嘉三年，重授左民尚書，領步兵校尉，尋改前軍將軍。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 3 he was again made minister of the left bureau of the people and concurrently commandant of infantry; soon his title was changed to general of the forward army.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 3, he was again appointed minister of the left bureau of the people and concurrently commandant of infantry; before long this was changed to general of the forward army.

entries.zh: 四年，侯安都徙鎮江州，以本官監南徐州。
entries.en: In year 4, when Hou Andu was moved to garrison Jiangzhou, Junli retained his office and supervised South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In year 4, when Hou Andu was transferred to garrison Jiangzhou, Junli, with his existing office, supervised South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 六年，出為仁威將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: In year 6 he was posted as general of humane prestige and administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: In year 6, he was sent out as general of humane prestige and administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 天康元年，以父憂去職。
entries.en: In Tiankang year 1 he left office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: In Tiankang year 1, he left office because of mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 君理因自請往荊州迎喪柩，朝議以在位重臣，難令出境，乃遣長兄君嚴往焉。
entries.en: Junli asked to go to Jingzhou to receive the coffin, but the court judged that a senior serving minister could not easily be sent beyond the frontier, so his elder brother Junyan went instead.
entries.literal: Junli then personally requested permission to go to Jingzhou to receive the coffin, but court discussion held that, as a weighty minister in office, it was difficult to let him leave the borders, so his elder brother Junyan was sent instead.

entries.zh: 及還，將葬，詔贈巡侍中、領軍將軍，諡曰敬子。
entries.en: When the coffin returned and burial was near, an edict posthumously honored Xun as palace attendant and general commanding the army, with the posthumous title Jingzi.
entries.literal: When it returned and the burial was about to take place, an edict posthumously granted Xun the titles palace attendant and general commanding the army, with the posthumous title Jingzi.

entries.zh: 其年起君理為信威將軍、左衛將軍。
entries.en: That same year Junli was recalled from mourning as general of trustworthy prestige and general of the left guard.
entries.literal: That year Junli was recalled from mourning as general of trustworthy prestige and general of the left guard.

entries.zh: 又起為持節、都督東衡衡二州諸軍事、仁威將軍、東衡州刺史，領始興內史。
entries.en: He was again recalled as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in East Heng and Heng provinces, general of humane prestige, and inspector of East Hengzhou, concurrently interior minister of Shixing.
entries.literal: He was again recalled as bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in East Heng and Heng provinces, general of humane prestige, and inspector of East Hengzhou, concurrently interior minister of Shixing.

entries.zh: 又起為明威將軍、中書令。
entries.en: He was again recalled as general of bright prestige and director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was again recalled as general of bright prestige and director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 前後奪情者三，並不就。
entries.en: Three times he was ordered to cut short mourning, and each time he refused to take office.
entries.literal: Three times in all he was ordered to set aside mourning, but he did not take up any of the posts.

entries.zh: 太建元年，服闋，除太子詹事，行東宮事，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: In Taijian year 1, after mourning ended, he was made steward of the heir apparent with authority over Eastern Palace affairs, then transferred to minister of personnel.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 1, when mourning ended, he was appointed steward of the heir apparent and put in charge of Eastern Palace affairs, then transferred to minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 二年，高宗以君理女為皇太子妃，賜爵望蔡縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In year 2, Emperor Xuan made Junli's daughter consort to the crown prince and granted Junli the title marquis of Wangcai county, with five hundred households.
entries.literal: In year 2, Gaozong made Junli's daughter consort to the imperial heir apparent and granted Junli the title marquis of Wangcai county, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 四年，加侍中。
entries.en: In year 4 he was additionally made palace attendant.
entries.literal: In year 4, he was additionally made palace attendant.

entries.zh: 五年，遷尚書右僕射，領吏部，侍中如故。
entries.en: In year 5 he became right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and took charge of personnel, while retaining his post as palace attendant.
entries.literal: In year 5, he was transferred to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and put in charge of personnel; his post as palace attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 其年有疾，輿駕親臨視，九月卒，時年四十九。
entries.en: That year he fell ill, and the emperor visited him in person. He died in the ninth month, at age forty-nine.
entries.literal: That year he fell ill; the imperial carriage personally came to see him. He died in the ninth month, aged forty-nine.

entries.zh: 詔贈侍中、太子少傅。
entries.en: An edict posthumously honored him as palace attendant and junior mentor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the titles palace attendant and junior mentor to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 喪事所須，隨由資給。
entries.en: Funeral expenses were supplied as needed.
entries.literal: Whatever was needed for the funeral was supplied as required.

entries.zh: 重贈翊左將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。
entries.en: He was further posthumously honored as general assisting the left and grandee with the same ceremonial as the three excellencies with office established, while retaining palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was further posthumously granted the titles general assisting the left and grandee with the same ceremonial as the three excellencies with office established; palace attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 諡曰貞憲。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Zhenxian.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Zhenxian.

entries.zh: 君理子遵儉早卒，以弟君高子遵禮為嗣。
entries.en: Junli's son Zunjian died young, so Zunli, son of his younger brother Jungao, was made heir.
entries.literal: Junli's son Zunjian died early, so his younger brother Jungao's son Zunli was made heir.

entries.zh: 世祖嗣位，徵為太子中庶子，領步兵校尉，掌東宮管記。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Shan was summoned as junior tutor to the heir apparent, concurrently commandant of footsoldiers, with charge of the eastern palace records.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Shan was summoned as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Commandant of Footsoldiers, and managed the Eastern Palace records.

entries.zh: 繕儀表端麗，進退閑雅，世祖使太子諸王咸取則焉。
entries.en: Shan had a handsome, dignified bearing and moved with graceful ease. Emperor Wen had the heir apparent and all the princes take him as their model.
entries.literal: Shan had a handsome and dignified appearance and moved with graceful ease in advancing and withdrawing; the Emperor Wen had the Heir Apparent and all the princes take him as their model.

entries.zh: 其趨步躡履，皆令習繕規矩。
entries.en: Even their gait and the way they set down their feet were made to follow Shan's standards.
entries.literal: Their gait in walking and treading in step were all made to follow Shan's standards.

entries.zh: 除尚書吏部郎中，步兵如故，仍侍東宮。
entries.en: He was appointed director in the personnel bureau of the Department of State Affairs; his post as commandant of footsoldiers remained unchanged, and he continued to attend the eastern palace.
entries.literal: He was appointed Director in the Personnel Bureau of the Ministry of Works; his post as commandant of footsoldiers remained as before, and he still attended the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 陳寶應平後，出為貞毅將軍、建安太守。
entries.en: After Chen Baoying was defeated, he was posted as general of upright resolution and administrator of Jian'an.
entries.literal: After Chen Baoying was pacified, he was sent out as General of Upright Resolution and Administrator of Jian'an.

entries.zh: 秩滿，為散騎常侍、御史中丞，猶以父之所終，固辭，不許，乃權換廨宇徙居之。
entries.en: When his term expired he was appointed attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and imperial censor-in-chief. Because his father had died in that office, he firmly declined, but permission was refused; he therefore temporarily exchanged quarters and moved his residence.
entries.literal: When his term expired he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Imperial Censor-in-Chief; because it was where his father had died, he firmly declined, but was not permitted; he therefore temporarily exchanged offices and moved his residence.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，太建元年，復除侍中，領左驍騎將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, in the first year of Taijian Yang was again appointed palace attendant and commander of the left valiant cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, in the first year of Taijian Yang was again appointed Palace Attendant and commanded the Left Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遷度支尚書，領羽林監。
entries.en: He was transferred to minister of revenue and appointed supervisor of the forest of feathers.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue and appointed Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.

entries.zh: 出為信威將軍、雲麾始興王長史，行州府事。
entries.en: He was posted as general of trustworthy prestige and chief clerk to the Prince of Shixing, cloud banner, with authority over the prefecture and headquarters.
entries.literal: He was sent out as General of Trustworthy Prestige and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shixing, Cloud Banner, with authority over the prefecture and headquarters.

entries.zh: 未行，遷中書令，尋加散騎常侍，除吏部尚書，常侍如故。
entries.en: Before he could take up the post he was transferred to director of the secretariat; soon he was additionally granted attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and appointed minister of personnel, while retaining his attendant rank.
entries.literal: Before he departed he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; soon he was additionally granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and appointed Minister of Personnel, his attendant post remaining as before.

entries.zh: 瑒性寬和，及居選職，務在清靜，謹守文案，無所抑揚。
entries.en: Yang was mild and conciliatory by nature. In personnel selection he aimed at quiet correctness, kept strictly to the records, and made no arbitrary promotions or demotions.
entries.literal: Yang was mild and conciliatory by nature; when he held office in personnel selection, he sought quiet correctness, carefully maintained the documents, and made no arbitrary promotions or demotions.

entries.zh: 尋授尚書右僕射，未拜，加侍中，遷左僕射，參掌選事，侍中如故。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; before he could assume the post he was additionally made palace attendant and transferred to left vice director, with a share in personnel selection, while retaining his palace attendant rank.
entries.literal: Before long he was granted the post of Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; before he could assume it he was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to Left Vice Director, participating in personnel selection; his post as palace attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 瑒兄弟三十餘人，居家篤睦，每歲時饋遺，遍及近親，敦誘諸弟，並稟其規訓。
entries.en: Yang had more than thirty brothers. At home they lived in deep harmony; at each season they exchanged gifts that reached all their close kin. He earnestly guided his younger brothers, and all followed his rules and instruction.
entries.literal: Yang had more than thirty brothers; at home they were deeply harmonious; every year at the seasons they exchanged gifts, extending to all close kin; he earnestly guided his younger brothers, and all received his rules and instruction.

entries.zh: 太建
entries.en: In the Taijian era
entries.literal: Taijian

entries.en: (six)
entries.literal: (six)

entries.zh: 〔八〕年卒，[3]時年五十四。
entries.en: In the [eighth] year he died,[3] at the age of fifty-four.
entries.literal: [eight]th year he died,[3] aged fifty-four.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、特進、護軍將軍。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant, special advance, and general who protects the army.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Palace Attendant, Special Advance, and General Who Protects the Army.

entries.zh: 喪事隨所資給。
entries.en: The funeral expenses were met from official funds as needed.
entries.literal: The funeral was supplied according to what was required.

entries.zh: 諡曰光子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Guangzi.
entries.literal: His posthumous name was Guangzi.

entries.zh: 繕子辯惠，年數歲，詔引入殿內，辯惠應對進止有父風，高宗因賜名辯惠，字敬仁云。
entries.en: Shan's son Bianhui was only a few years old when an edict summoned him into the palace. In his replies and bearing he showed his father's manner, and Emperor Xuan therefore bestowed the name Bianhui, with the style Jingren.
entries.literal: Shan's son Bianhui was only a few years old when an edict summoned him into the palace hall; Bianhui's replies and bearing showed his father's manner; the Emperor Xuan therefore bestowed the name Bianhui, with the style Jingren.

entries.zh: 君理第六弟君高，字季高，少知名，性剛直，有吏能。
entries.en: Junli's sixth younger brother Jungao, styled Jigao, was known from youth. He was firm and upright, with talent for administration.
entries.literal: Junli's sixth younger brother Jungao, styled Jigao, was known from youth; his nature was firm and upright, and he had ability as an administrator.

entries.zh: 以家門外戚，早居清顯，歷太子舍人、洗馬、中舍人、高宗司空府從事中郎、廷尉卿。
entries.en: Because his family were imperial in-laws, he early held prestigious clean posts: secretary to the heir apparent, groom, inner secretary, attendant gentleman in Emperor Xuan's minister of works office, and minister of justice.
entries.literal: Because his family were imperial relatives by marriage, he early held pure and prominent posts, serving successively as secretary to the heir apparent, groom, inner secretary, attendant gentleman in Gaozong's minister of works office, and minister of justice.

entries.zh: 太建元年，東境大水，百姓飢弊，乃以君高為貞威將軍、吳令。
entries.en: In Taijian year 1, when floods devastated the east and the people were starving and worn out, Jungao was made general of steadfast prestige and magistrate of Wu.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 1, floods struck the eastern territory and the people suffered hunger and exhaustion, so Jungao was made general of steadfast prestige and magistrate of Wu.

entries.zh: 尋除太子中庶子、尚書吏部郎、衛尉卿。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, gentleman of the personnel bureau in the Department of State Affairs, and chamberlain for the palace garrison.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, gentleman of the personnel bureau of the Department of State Affairs, and chamberlain for the palace garrison.

entries.zh: 出為宣遠將軍、平南長沙王長史、南海太守，行廣州事。
entries.en: He was posted as general proclaiming distance, chief clerk to the Prince of Changsha, pacifier of the south, and administrator of Nanhai, with authority over Guangzhou.
entries.literal: He was sent out as general proclaiming distance, chief clerk to the Prince of Changsha, pacifier of the south, and administrator of Nanhai, with authority over Guangzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 以女為王妃，固辭不行，復為衛尉卿。
entries.en: Because his daughter was the prince's consort, he firmly declined and did not take the post, returning instead as chamberlain for the palace garrison.
entries.literal: Because his daughter was the prince's consort, he firmly declined and did not go, and was again made chamberlain for the palace garrison.

entries.zh: 八年，詔授持節、都督廣等十八州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: In year 8 an edict made him bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Guang and eighteen other provinces, general pacifying distance, central gentleman general who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: In year 8, an edict appointed him bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Guang and eighteen other provinces, general pacifying distance, central gentleman general who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 嶺南俚、獠世相攻伐，君高本文吏，無武幹，推心撫御，甚得民和。
entries.en: In Lingnan the Li and Lao peoples had fought one another for generations. Jungao was a civil official, not a soldier, but he governed with open sincerity and won the people's deep goodwill.
entries.literal: The Li and Lao of Lingnan had attacked one another for generations; Jungao was fundamentally a civil official and had no military talent, but he treated them with sincerity and governed them gently, greatly winning the people's harmony.

entries.zh: 十年，卒于官，時年四十七。
entries.en: In year 10 he died in office, at the age of forty-seven.
entries.literal: In year 10, he died in office, aged forty-seven.

entries.zh: 贈散騎常侍，諡曰祁子。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, with the posthumous title Qizi.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the title attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, with the posthumous title Qizi.

entries.zh: 繕兄子見賢，亦方雅，高宗為揚州牧，乃以為治中從事史，深被知遇。
entries.en: Shan's nephew Jianxian was likewise upright and refined. When Emperor Xuan was governor of Yangzhou, he appointed him clerk for administration, and Jianxian enjoyed his deep favor.
entries.literal: Shan's elder brother's son Jianxian was likewise upright and refined; when the Emperor Xuan was Governor of Yangzhou, he appointed him Clerk for Administration, and Jianxian was deeply favored.

entries.zh: 歷給事黃門侍郎，長沙鄱陽二王長史，帶尋陽太守，少府卿。
entries.en: He served in turn as gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, chief clerk to the princes of Changsha and Poyang, concurrently administrator of Xunyang, and minister steward.
entries.literal: He served successively as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Chief Clerk to the Princes of Changsha and Poyang, concurrently Administrator of Xunyang, and Minister Steward.

entries.zh: 太建十年卒，時年五十。
entries.en: He died in the tenth year of Taijian, at the age of fifty.
entries.literal: He died in the tenth year of Taijian, aged fifty.

entries.zh: 贈廷尉卿，諡曰平子。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as minister of justice; his posthumous title was Pingzi.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Justice; his posthumous name was Pingzi.

entries.zh: 陸繕字士繻，吳郡吳人也。
entries.en: Lu Shan, whose style name was Shiru, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Shan, styled Shiru, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 祖惠曉，齊太常卿。
entries.en: His grandfather Huixiao had served Qi as minister of ceremonies.
entries.literal: His grandfather Huixiao served Qi as minister of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 父任，梁御史中丞。
entries.en: His father Ren had served Liang as imperial censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: His father Ren served Liang as imperial censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十三
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 23
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 23

entries.zh: 中大通三年，梁昭明太子薨，其嗣華容公不得立，乃以晉安王為皇太子，弘正乃奏記曰：
entries.en: In Zhong Datong 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died. His heir, the Duke of Huarong, could not be installed, so the Prince of Jin'an was made crown prince, and Hongzheng submitted a memorandum:
entries.literal: In Zhong Datong 3, Crown Prince Zhaoming of Liang died; his heir, the Duke of Huarong, could not be established, and so the Prince of Jin'an was made crown prince. Hongzheng then submitted a memorandum:

entries.zh: 累遷國子博士。
entries.en: He rose repeatedly to erudite of the National University.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the National University.

entries.zh: 時於城西立士林館，弘正居以講授，聽者傾朝野焉。
entries.en: At that time the Forest of Scholars Hall was built west of the city. Hongzheng lived there to teach, and listeners filled court and countryside.
entries.literal: At that time the Forest of Scholars Hall was established west of the city; Hongzheng dwelt there to lecture, and listeners filled court and countryside.

entries.zh: 弘正啟梁武帝周易疑義五十條，又請釋乾坤二繫曰：「臣聞易稱立象以盡意，繫辭以盡言，然後知聖人之情，幾可見矣。
entries.en: Hongzheng submitted to Emperor Wu of Liang fifty doubtful points on the Book of Changes and asked to explain the two Appended Phrases on Qian and Kun. He said, "I have heard that the Changes says, 'Establish images to exhaust meaning; attach words to exhaust speech'—then the sage's feeling may be known and the subtle seen.
entries.literal: Hongzheng submitted to Emperor Wu of Liang fifty items of doubtful points in the Book of Changes, and also asked to explain the two Appended Phrases on Qian and Kun, saying: "Your servant has heard that the Changes says, 'Establish images to exhaust meaning; attach words to exhaust speech'—then one knows the sage's feeling and the subtle can be seen.

entries.zh: 自非含微體極，盡化窮神，豈能通志成務，探賾致遠。
entries.en: Unless one embraces the subtle, embodies the utmost, and exhausts transformation and spirit, how can one penetrate intent, accomplish tasks, and reach the hidden afar?
entries.literal: Unless one embraces the subtle, embodies the utmost, exhausts transformation and probes spirit, how can one penetrate intent and accomplish tasks, plumb the hidden and reach afar?

entries.zh: 而宣尼比之桎梏，絕韋編於漆字，軒轅之所聽瑩，遺玄珠於赤水。
entries.en: Yet Confucius called it fetters and broke the leather cords at the lacquered text; what the Yellow Emperor polished, he left as the dark pearl in Red Water.
entries.literal: Yet Confucius compared it to fetters and broke the leather thongs at the lacquered characters; what Xuanyuan heard and polished, he left the dark pearl in Red Water.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下一日萬機，匪勞神於瞬息，凝心妙本，常自得於天真，聖智無以隱其幾深，明神無以淪其不測。
entries.en: I bow before Your Majesty, who handles ten thousand affairs in a day without taxing your spirit in an instant; who concentrates on the subtle root and constantly attains natural truth; whose sage wisdom cannot hide its depths and whose bright spirit cannot be lost in the unfathomable.
entries.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's ten thousand affairs in a day, not taxing spirit in an instant; you concentrate mind on the subtle root and constantly attain the natural truth; sage wisdom cannot hide its subtle depths, bright spirit cannot sink into what cannot be fathomed.

entries.zh: 至若爻畫之苞於六經，文辭之窮於兩繫，名儒劇談以歷載，鴻生抵掌以終年，莫有試遊其藩，未嘗一見其涘。
entries.en: As for the trigrams wrapped in the Six Classics and the words exhausted in the two Appended Phrases—famous scholars debated for years, great scholars talked for a year end—none had tried their outer fence, none had seen their far shore.
entries.literal: As for the trigrams wrapped in the Six Classics and words exhausted in the two Appended Phrases—famous scholars debated heatedly for years, great scholars clapped hands for a year end—none tried to wander their outer fence, none ever saw their far shore.

entries.zh: 自制旨降談，裁成易道，析至微於秋毫，渙曾冰於幽谷。
entries.en: Since Your Majesty's own instructions came down and shaped the Way of the Changes, splitting the utmost subtle to an autumn hair and melting layered ice in a dark valley.
entries.literal: Since Your Majesty's own instructions descended in discussion and shaped the Way of the Changes, splitting the utmost subtle to an autumn down and melting layered ice in a dark valley.

entries.zh: 臣親承音旨，職司宣授，後進詵詵，不無傳業。
entries.en: Your servant personally received your tone and intent and had the duty of proclaiming it; the later students were many and not without a transmitted school.
entries.literal: Your servant personally received the tone and intent and had the duty of proclaiming and transmitting; the later students were numerous and not without transmitted learning.

entries.zh: 但乾坤之蘊未剖，繫表之妙莫詮，使一經深致，尚多所惑。
entries.en: But the profundity of Qian and Kun was not yet opened and the subtlety of the Appended Tables not yet explained, so that one classic's deep reach still left much doubt.
entries.literal: But the profundity of Qian and Kun was not yet opened, the subtlety of the Appended Tables not yet explained, so that one classic's deep reach still left much doubt.

entries.zh: 臣不涯庸淺，輕率短陋，謹與受業諸生清河張譏等三百一十二人，於乾坤二繫象爻未啟，伏願聽覽之閑，曲垂提訓，得使微臣鑽仰，成其篤習，後昆好事，專門有奉。
entries.en: Your servant, not measuring his shallowness, respectfully joins Zhang Ji of Qinghe and three hundred twelve fellow students. On the image-lines of Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases, which are not yet opened, we bow and hope that in the leisure of your hearing you will instruct us—so that we may study in earnest and later generations who love learning may have a school to uphold.
entries.literal: Your servant, not measuring his shallowness, lightly and rashly short and crude, respectfully together with his students Zhang Ji of Qinghe and three hundred twelve others, on the image-lines of Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases not yet opened, bow and hope in the leisure of your hearing you will bend to instruct—so that your humble servant may drill and look up and complete his earnest study, and later generations who love the matter may have a lineage to uphold.

entries.zh: 自惟多幸，懽沐道於堯年，肄業終身，不知老之將至。
entries.en: Reflecting on my great fortune, I rejoice to bathe in the Way in an age like Yao's; I study all my life and do not know that old age is coming.
