entries.literal: Reflecting on my great fortune, I rejoice to bathe in the Way in the years of Yao; I study to the end of life and do not know old age is coming.

entries.zh: 天尊不聞，而冒陳請，冰谷寘懷，罔識攸厝。」
entries.en: Heaven's honor does not hear, yet I rashly submit this request. Ice and valley fill my breast and I know not where to turn."
entries.literal: Heaven's honor does not hear, yet I rashly submit this request; ice and valley fill my breast and I know not where to place myself."

entries.zh: 詔答曰：「設卦觀象，事遠文高，作繫表言，辭深理奧，東魯絕編之思，西伯幽憂之作，事逾三古，人更七聖，自商瞿稟承，子庸傳授，篇簡湮沒，歲月遼遠。
entries.en: An edict replied: "Setting hexagrams and observing images—the matter is remote and the text lofty; composing the Appended Phrases—the words are deep and the principle abstruse. The thought of cut silken cords in eastern Lu, the writing in western Bo's deep sorrow—the matter exceeds the Three Antiquities; men have changed through seven sages. From Shang Qu's receiving and Ziyong's transmitting, the slips were lost and the years far away.
entries.literal: An edict replied: "Setting hexagrams and observing images—the matter is remote and the text high; composing the Appended Phrases and displaying words—the phrasing is deep and the principle abstruse. The thought of the silken cords cut in eastern Lu, the writing in western Bo's deep sorrow—the matter exceeds the Three Antiquities, men have changed through seven sages. From Shang Qu's receiving and Ziyong's transmitting, the bamboo slips were drowned and the years far away.

entries.zh: 田生表菑川之譽，梁丘擅琅邪之學，代郡范生，山陽王氏，人藏荊山之寶，各盡玄言之趣，說或去取，意有詳略。
entries.en: Master Tian won fame in Zichuan; Liangqiu excelled in Langye; Master Fan of Dai and the Wang of Shanyang—each hid the treasure of Jing Mountain and exhausted the flavor of dark learning. Explanations differed in what they kept or dropped; intent had its detail and brevity.
entries.literal: Master Tian won fame in Zichuan; Liangqiu excelled in Langye learning; Master Fan of Dai commandery and the Wang clan of Shanyang—men hid the treasure of Jing Mountain; each exhausted the flavor of dark speech; explanations differed in what they took or left and intent had detail or brevity.

entries.zh: 近搢紳之學，咸有稽疑，隨答所問，已具別解。
entries.en: Recently the learning of the gentry has had doubts to examine; answers to each question have already been prepared in separate explanations.
entries.literal: Recently gentry learning all had doubts to examine; answering each question, separate explanations have already been prepared.

entries.zh: 知與張譏等三百一十二人須釋乾坤文言及二繫，萬機小暇，試當討論。」
entries.en: I know that you and Zhang Ji and three hundred twelve others need the Wenyan on Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases explained. When the ten thousand affairs allow a little leisure, I will try to discuss them."
entries.literal: I know that you and Zhang Ji and three hundred twelve others need the words of the Wenyan on Qian and Kun and the two Appended Phrases explained; when the ten thousand affairs allow a little leisure, I will try to discuss them."

entries.zh: 弘正博物知玄象，善占候。
entries.en: Hongzheng was broadly learned and knew the dark images; he was skilled at divination and observation.
entries.literal: Hongzheng was broadly learned and knew dark images; he was skilled at divination and observation.

entries.zh: 大同末，嘗謂弟弘讓曰：「國家厄運，數年當有兵起，吾與汝不知何所逃之。」
entries.en: Near the end of Datong he once told his younger brother Hongrang, "The state's fortune is ill. In a few years war will rise—we do not know where we shall flee."
entries.literal: At the end of Datong he once told his younger brother Hongrang: "The state's fortune is ill; in a few years there will be war rising—we and you do not know where to flee."

entries.zh: 及梁武帝納侯景，弘正謂弘讓曰：「亂階此矣。」
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Liang received Hou Jing, Hongzheng told Hongrang, "The stair of disorder starts here."
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang received Hou Jing, Hongzheng told Hongrang: "The stair of disorder is here."

entries.zh: 京城陷，弘直為衡陽內史，元帝在江陵，遺弘直書曰：「適有都信，賢兄博士平安。
entries.en: When the capital fell, Hongzhi was administrator of Hengyang. Emperor Yuan was at Jiangling and sent Hongzhi a letter: "There is capital news: your worthy elder brother the erudite is safe.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, Hongzhi was Administrator of Hengyang; Emperor Yuan was at Jiangling and sent Hongzhi a letter saying: "There is just now capital news: your worthy elder brother the Erudite is safe.

entries.zh: 但京師搢紳，無不附逆，王克已為家臣，陸緬身充卒伍，唯有周生，確乎不拔。
entries.en: But of the capital gentry none failed to join the rebels. Wang Ke had become a household servant; Lu Mian's body filled the ranks of soldiers. Only Master Zhou stood firm and unbending.
entries.literal: But the gentry of the capital, none failed to join the rebels; Wang Ke had become a household servant, Lu Mian's body filled the ranks of soldiers—only Master Zhou stood firm and unbending.

entries.zh: 言及西軍，潺湲掩淚，恆思吾至，如望歲焉，松柏後凋，一人而已。」
entries.en: Speaking of the western army, his tears flowed like a stream. He constantly longed for my coming as one longs for harvest. Of pines and cypresses that wither last—he alone."
entries.literal: Speaking of the western army, his tears flowed like a stream; he constantly longed for my coming as one longs for harvest; of pines and cypresses that wither last—he alone."

entries.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，弘正與弘讓自拔迎軍，僧辯得之甚喜，即日啟元帝，元帝手書與弘正曰：「獯醜逆亂，寒暑亟離，海內相識，零落略盡。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Hongzheng and Hongrang broke out on their own to welcome his army. Sengbian was greatly pleased and that day reported to Emperor Yuan. Emperor Yuan wrote Hongzheng in his own hand: "The savage rebel has torn cold from heat again and again; acquaintances within the seas are nearly all gone.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Hongzheng and Hongrang broke out on their own to welcome the army; Sengbian was greatly pleased and that same day reported to Emperor Yuan; Emperor Yuan wrote Hongzheng in his own hand: "The savage ugliness rebelled and disorder separated cold and heat again and again; acquaintances within the seas were nearly all gone.

entries.zh: 韓非之智，不免秦獄，劉歆之學，猶弊亡新，音塵不嗣，每以耿灼。
entries.en: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin. Voice and dust do not continue—I burn with grief.
entries.literal: Han Fei's wisdom did not escape Qin's prison; Liu Xin's learning still perished in Xin; voice and dust do not continue—I am often burning with grief.

entries.zh: 常欲訪山東而尋子雲，問關西而求伯起，遇有今信，力附相聞，遲比來郵，慰其延佇。」
entries.en: I had long wished to search Shandong for Zhong Jun and inquire west of the Pass for Yang Zhen. Now that a messenger has arrived, I have urgently entrusted him with this word. I await the next courier to ease my long suspense."
entries.literal: I had long wished to search Shandong for Ziyun and inquire west of the Pass for Boqi. Now that a messenger has arrived, I have urgently entrusted him with this word. I await the next courier to console my protracted waiting."

entries.zh: 仍遣使迎之，謂朝士曰：「晉氏平吳，喜獲二陸，今我破賊，亦得兩周，今古一時，足為連類。」
entries.en: He then sent an envoy to welcome him and told the court gentlemen, "When the Jin house pacified Wu, they rejoiced to gain the two Lus. Now in breaking the bandit I too have gained the two Zhous—ancient and modern in one moment, enough to be paired."
entries.literal: He then sent an envoy to welcome him and told the court gentlemen: "When the Jin house pacified Wu, they rejoiced to gain the two Lus; now in breaking the bandit I too have gained the two Zhous—one time in ancient and modern, enough to be paired."

entries.zh: 及弘正至，禮數甚優，朝臣無與比者。
entries.en: When Hongzheng arrived, the honors were very generous; no court minister could compare.
entries.literal: When Hongzheng arrived, the ritual and courtesy were very generous; no court minister could compare.

entries.zh: 授黃門侍郎，直侍中省。
entries.en: He was made gentleman of the yellow gate, attached to the secretariat.
entries.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and attached to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 俄遷左民尚書，尋加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to minister of the left for the people and shortly after made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister of the Left for the People and shortly after made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 及高宗不豫，憲與吏部尚書毛喜俱受顧命。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, Xian and minister of personnel Mao Xi both received his deathbed charge.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, Xian and the minister of the board of civil office Mao Xi both received testamentary charge.

entries.zh: 始興王叔陵之肆逆也，憲指麾部分，預有力焉。
entries.en: When Prince Shixing Shuling rebelled, Xian directed the response and played a leading part in suppressing him.
entries.literal: When Prince Shixing Shuling committed his outrage, Xian directed deployments and took part with force.

entries.zh: 後主被瘡病篤，執憲手曰：「我兒尚幼，後事委卿。」
entries.en: The Later Lord, badly wounded, took Xian's hand and said, "My son is still young; I leave what follows to you."
entries.literal: The Later Lord, wounded and gravely ill, grasped Xian's hand and said: "My son is still young; I entrust what follows to you."

entries.zh: 憲曰：「群情喁喁，冀聖躬康復，後事之旨，未敢奉詔。」
entries.en: Xian said, "All hearts pray for Your Majesty's recovery; I dare not yet accept a deathbed charge."
entries.literal: Xian said: "All hearts murmur in hope that Your Sagely Person will recover; as to testamentary charge, I dare not yet receive the edict."

entries.zh: 以功封建安縣伯，邑四百戶，領太子中庶子，餘並如故。
entries.en: For his service he was made baron of Jian'an with four hundred households and chief aide to the crown prince; his other posts were unchanged.
entries.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jian'an county with a fief of four hundred households, appointed concurrently chief aide to the crown prince; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 尋除侍中、信威將軍、太子詹事。
entries.en: He was soon made palace attendant, trustworthy-martial general, and steward of the crown prince's household.
entries.literal: Soon he was made palace attendant, trustworthy-martial general, and steward of the crown prince's household.

entries.zh: 元帝嘗著金樓子，曰：「余於諸僧重招提琰法師，隱士重華陽陶貞白，士大夫重汝南周弘正，其於義理，清轉無窮，亦一時之名士也。」
entries.en: Emperor Yuan once wrote in Master of the Golden Tower: "Among monks, I esteem Master Yan of Zhaoti; among recluses, Tao Hongjing of Huayang; among gentlemen, Zhou Hongzheng of Runan. Hongzheng's exposition of principle is lucid, fluent, and inexhaustible; he too is a distinguished scholar of his age."
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan once wrote in Master of the Golden Tower: "Among monks, I esteem Master Yan of Zhaoti; among recluses, Tao Zhenbai of Huayang; among gentlemen, Zhou Hongzheng of Runan. His treatment of principle is clear, fluid, and inexhaustible; he too is a distinguished scholar of his age."

entries.zh: 及侯景平，僧辯啟送祕書圖籍，敕弘正讎校。
entries.en: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengbian reported and sent the secretariat's books and registers. An edict ordered Hongzheng to collate them.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Sengbian reported and sent the secretariat's books and registers; an edict ordered Hongzheng to collate them.

entries.zh: 時朝議遷都，朝士家在荊州者，皆不欲遷，唯弘正與僕射王裒言於元帝曰：「若束脩以上諸士大夫微見古今者，知帝王所都本無定處，無所與疑。
entries.en: At that time the court debated moving the capital. Court gentlemen whose families were in Jingzhou all wished to stay—only Hongzheng and Minister of Works Wang Pou said to Emperor Yuan, "Gentry of full learning who know past and present understand that an emperor's seat has no fixed place. There is nothing to doubt.
entries.literal: At that time the court debated moving the capital; court gentlemen whose families were in Jingzhou all did not wish to move—only Hongzheng and the Minister of Works Wang Pou spoke to Emperor Yuan: "If gentry above the age of full study who slightly know past and present understand that where an emperor dwells has no fixed place, there is nothing to doubt.

entries.zh: 至如黔首萬姓，若未見輿駕入建鄴，謂是列國諸王，未名天子。
entries.en: As for the common people, if they have not seen the imperial carriage enter Jianye, they will think you a feudal prince among the states and not yet call you Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: As for the black-haired masses, if they have not seen the imperial carriage enter Jianye, they will think this a feudal prince among the states and not yet call you Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 今宜赴百姓之心，從四海之望。」
entries.en: Now you should follow the people's hearts and accord with the hope of the four seas."
entries.literal: Now you should follow the people's hearts and accord with the hope of the four seas."

entries.zh: 時荊、陝人士咸云王、周皆是東人，志願東下，恐非良計。
entries.en: At that time men of Jing and Shanxi all said Wang and Zhou were easterners who wished to go east and feared it was not a good plan.
entries.literal: At that time men of Jing and Shanxi all said Wang and Zhou were both easterners wishing to go east and feared it was not a good plan.

entries.zh: 弘正面折之曰：「若東人勸東，謂為非計，君等西人欲西，豈成良策？」
entries.en: Hongzheng confronted them and said, "If easterners urge east and you call it a bad plan, you westerners wish west—how is that a good plan?"
entries.literal: Hongzheng confronted them face to face and said: "If easterners urge east and you call it a bad plan, you westerners wish west—how is that a good plan?"

entries.zh: 元帝乃大笑之，竟不還都。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan laughed greatly at this and in the end did not return the capital.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan then laughed greatly at this and in the end did not return the capital.

entries.zh: 及江陵陷，弘正遁圍而出，歸於京師，敬帝以為大司馬王僧辯長史，行揚州事。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Hongzheng broke through the siege and returned to the capital. Emperor Jing made him chief clerk to Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian, acting for Yang province.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Hongzheng broke through the siege and came out, returning to the capital; Emperor Jing made him chief clerk to Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian, acting for Yang province affairs.

entries.zh: 太平元年，授侍中，領國子祭酒，遷太常卿、都官尚書。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiping (556) he was made palace attendant and concurrently national university libationer, then promoted to minister of ceremonies and minister of justice.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently National University Libationer, promoted to Minister of Ceremonies and Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，授太子詹事。
entries.en: When the Founder received the abdication, Hongzheng was made grand mentor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, [Hongzheng] was appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，遷侍中、國子祭酒，往長安迎高宗。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was promoted to palace attendant and national university libationer and went to Chang'an to welcome Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was promoted to Palace Attendant and National University Libationer and went to Chang'an to welcome Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 三年，自周還，詔授金紫光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，領慈訓太僕。
entries.en: In year 3 he returned from Zhou. An edict made him grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and concurrently grand steward of Cixun.
entries.literal: In the third year he returned from Zhou; an edict appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon and made him concurrently Grand Steward of Cixun.

entries.zh: 廢帝嗣位，領都官尚書，總知五禮事。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, he concurrently served as minister of justice and oversaw the five rites.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, [Hongzheng] concurrently held the post of Minister of Justice and oversaw the five rites.

entries.zh: 仍授太傅長史，加明威將軍。
entries.en: He was then made chief clerk to the grand tutor and bright-prestige general.
entries.literal: He was then appointed Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor and made Bright-Prestige General.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，遷特進，重領國子祭酒，豫州大中正，加扶。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was promoted to special grand master, again made national university libationer, and chief rectifier for Yu province; he was given attendants.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was promoted to Special Grand Master, again held the National University Libationership, and was Chief Rectifier for Yu province; he was given attendants.

entries.zh: 太建五年，授尚書右僕射，祭酒、中正如故。
entries.en: In Taijian year 5 (573) he was made right vice director of the secretariat, with libationer and chief rectifier unchanged.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; libationer and chief rectifier as before.

entries.zh: 尋敕侍東宮講論語、孝經。
entries.en: Soon an edict ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace to lecture on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace to lecture on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 太子以弘正朝廷舊臣，德望素重，於是降情屈禮，橫經請益，有師資之敬焉。
entries.en: The heir apparent, because Hongzheng was an old minister whose virtue and standing were weighty, lowered his manner and bent ritual, spread the classics and asked for instruction—with the respect due a teacher.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent, because Hongzheng was an old minister of the court whose virtue and standing had long been weighty, therefore lowered his manner and bent ritual, spread the classics and asked for benefit—there was the respect due a teacher.

entries.zh: 確字士潛，美容儀，寬大有行檢，博涉經史，篤好玄言，世父弘正特所鍾愛。
entries.en: Que, styled Shiqian, was handsome, broad-minded, and disciplined. He read widely in the classics and histories, loved abstruse discussion, and was especially cherished by his senior kinsman Hongzheng.
entries.literal: Que, styled Shiqian, was handsome in appearance, broad-minded, and had conduct and restraint; he read widely in the classics and histories, deeply loved abstruse discourse, and was especially cherished by his elder kinsman Hongzheng.

entries.zh: 解褐梁太學博士、司徒祭酒、晉安王主簿。
entries.en: He began his career as an erudite at the Liang Imperial University, then served as libationer to the minister of education and chief clerk to the Prince of Jin'an.
entries.literal: He entered office as Erudite of the Liang Imperial University, libationer to the Minister of Education, and chief clerk to the Prince of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，除尚書殿中郎，累遷安成王限內記室。
entries.en: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Que was appointed palace gentleman in the Department of State Affairs and later rose to inner secretary to the Prince of Ancheng.
entries.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Que was appointed palace gentleman in the Department of State Affairs and was repeatedly promoted to inner secretary to the Prince of Ancheng.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，授東宮通事舍人，丁母憂，去職。
entries.en: When Gaozong took the throne, Que became communications attendant in the Eastern Palace, but left office when his mother died.
entries.literal: When Gaozong ascended, Que was appointed communications attendant in the Eastern Palace; when his mother died, he left office.

entries.zh: 及歐陽紇平，起為中書舍人，命於廣州慰勞，服闋，為太常卿。
entries.en: After Ouyang He was subdued, Que was recalled as secretariat attendant and sent to Guangzhou to console and reward the region. When his mourning ended, he became minister of ceremonies.
entries.literal: After Ouyang He was pacified, Que was recalled as secretariat attendant and ordered to Guangzhou to console and reward; after mourning ended, he became Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 歷太子中庶子、尚書左丞、太子家令，以父憂去職。
entries.en: He later served as chief aide to the crown prince, left assistant in the Department of State Affairs, and steward of the crown prince's household, before leaving office to mourn his father.
entries.literal: He served successively as chief aide to the crown prince, left assistant in the Department of State Affairs, and household steward to the crown prince, then left office for mourning for his father.

entries.zh: 尋起為貞威將軍、吳令，確固辭不之官。
entries.en: He was soon recalled as General of Steadfast Might and magistrate of Wu, but firmly declined and never took up the post.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as General of Steadfast Might and magistrate of Wu, but Que firmly declined and did not take office.

entries.zh: 至德元年，授太子左衛率、中書舍人，遷散騎常侍，加貞威將軍、信州南平王府長史，行揚州事。
entries.en: In Zhide 1, he became left guard commander to the crown prince and secretariat attendant, then was promoted to Cavalier Attendant, additionally named General of Steadfast Might and chief steward of the Prince of Nanping's office in Xinzhou, and put in charge of Yangzhou affairs.
entries.literal: In Zhide 1, he was appointed left guard commander to the crown prince and secretariat attendant; he was promoted to Cavalier Attendant, additionally made General of Steadfast Might and chief steward of the Prince of Nanping's office in Xinzhou, and acted in Yangzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 為政平允，稱為良吏。
entries.en: His administration was fair and even-handed, and he was praised as a good official.
entries.literal: His governance was even and fair, and he was called a good official.

entries.zh: 遷都官尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of the Bureau of Justice.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Bureau of Justice.

entries.zh: 禎明初，遘疾，卒于官，時年五十九。
entries.en: Early in the Zhenming era, he fell ill and died in office at the age of fifty-nine.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming, he contracted illness and died in office, aged fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 詔贈散騎常侍、太常卿，官給喪事。
entries.en: By edict he was posthumously granted the titles Cavalier Attendant and minister of ceremonies, with funeral expenses supplied by the state.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously bestowed Cavalier Attendant and Minister of Ceremonies, and the government supplied the funeral expenses.

entries.zh: 弘正特善玄言，兼明釋典，雖碩學名僧，莫不請質疑滯。
entries.en: Hongzheng was especially skilled in dark discourse and also understood Buddhist scriptures. Great scholars and famous monks all came to him to resolve doubts.
entries.literal: Hongzheng was especially skilled in dark discourse and also understood Buddhist scriptures; though great scholars and famous monks, none failed to ask him to resolve doubts.

entries.zh: 六年，卒于官，時年七十九。
entries.en: In year 6 he died in office, aged seventy-nine.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he died in office, aged seventy-nine.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「追遠褒德，抑有恆規。
entries.en: An edict said, "To pursue the distant and praise virtue—indeed there is a constant rule.
entries.literal: An edict said: "To pursue the distant and praise virtue—indeed there is a constant rule.

entries.zh: 故尚書右僕射、領國子祭酒、豫州大中正弘正，識宇凝深，藝業通備，辭林義府，國老民宗，道映庠門，望高禮閣，卒然殂殞，朕用惻然。
entries.en: The late right vice director of the secretariat, concurrent national university libationer and chief rectifier for Yu province, Hongzheng—his knowledge was deep and settled, his arts complete; a forest of letters and storehouse of righteousness, elder of the state and teacher of the people; the Way shone at the school gate, his repute high in the ritual hall. Suddenly he has fallen—we are deeply moved.
entries.literal: The late Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent National University Libationer and Chief Rectifier for Yu province, Hongzheng—his knowledge and breadth were deep and settled, his arts and calling complete; forest of letters and storehouse of righteousness, elder of the state and teacher of the people; the Way shone at the school gate, his repute high in the ritual hall; suddenly he has fallen—We are deeply moved.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、中書監，喪事所須，量加資給。」
entries.en: He may be posthumously made palace attendant and director of the secretariat. What the funeral requires shall be supplied in full measure."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; what the funeral requires shall be supplied in measured addition."

entries.zh: 便出臨哭。
entries.en: The Emperor then went out to mourn him in person.
entries.literal: The Emperor then went out to attend the mourning in person.

entries.zh: 諡曰簡子。
entries.en: Posthumous title: Master Jian.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Master Jian.

entries.zh: 所著周易講疏十六卷，論語疏十一卷，莊子疏八卷，老子疏五卷，孝經疏兩卷，集二十卷，行于世。
entries.en: His writings include sixteen scrolls of commentary on the Book of Changes, eleven on the Analects, eight on Zhuangzi, five on the Laozi, two on the Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty scrolls of collected works—in circulation in the world.
entries.literal: His writings include sixteen scrolls of Exegesis and Commentary on the Book of Changes, eleven scrolls of Commentary on the Analects, eight scrolls of Commentary on Zhuangzi, five scrolls of Commentary on the Laozi, two scrolls of Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, and twenty scrolls of collected works—in circulation in the world.

entries.zh: 子墳，官至吏部郎。
entries.en: His son Fen rose to gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: His son Fen rose to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 弘直字思方，幼而聰敏。
entries.en: Hongzhi, styled Sifang, was clever and keen from childhood.
entries.literal: Hongzhi, styled Sifang, was clever and keen from childhood.

entries.zh: 解褐梁太學博士，稍遷西中郎湘東王外兵記室參軍，與東海鮑泉、南陽宗懍、平原劉緩、沛郡劉瑴同掌書記。
entries.en: He entered office as a Liang grand-academy doctor, then rose to secretary on Prince Xiangdong's outer military staff, sharing record-keeping with Bao Quan of Donghai, Zong Lin of Nanyang, Liu Huan of Pingyuan, and Liu Yue of Pei.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the sackcloth he was a Liang Grand Academy Doctor; he was gradually promoted to secretary in the outer military staff office of the Western Central Commander, Prince of Xiangdong, and together with Bao Quan of Donghai, Zong Lin of Nanyang, Liu Huan of Pingyuan, and Liu Yue of Pei commandery shared charge of secretarial records.

entries.zh: 入為尚書儀曹郎。
entries.en: He was made gentleman of the ceremonies bureau in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He entered [capital] service as Gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 湘東王出鎮江、荊二州，累除錄事諮議參軍，帶柴桑、當陽二縣令。
entries.en: When Prince Xiangdong took up Jiang and Jing, he was repeatedly made recording secretary and advising aide, and concurrently magistrate of Chaisang and Dangyang.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Xiangdong went out to govern the two provinces Jiang and Jing, [Hongzhi] was repeatedly promoted to recording secretary and advising aide, concurrently serving as magistrate of Chaisang and Dangyang counties.

entries.zh: 及梁元帝承制，授假節、英果將軍、世子長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regime, he was made acting-with-staff bearer, stalwart-fruits general, and the heir's chief steward.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regime, [he] was appointed acting-with-staff, stalwart-fruits general, and heir-apparent chief steward.

entries.zh: 尋除智武將軍、衡陽內史。
entries.en: He was soon made wise-martial general and inner administrator of Hengyang.
entries.literal: Soon he was made wise-martial general and inner administrator of Hengyang.

entries.zh: 遷貞毅將軍、平南長史、長沙內史，行湘州府州事，湘濱縣侯，邑六百戶。
entries.en: He became steadfast-resolve general, chief steward of the pacify-the-south army, inner administrator of Changsha, acting prefect of Xiangzhou, and marquis of Xiangbin with six hundred households.
entries.literal: He was transferred to steadfast-resolve general, chief steward of the Pacify-the-South [army], inner administrator of Changsha, acting in the prefectural and regional affairs of Xiangzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangbin county with a fief of six hundred households.

entries.zh: 歷邵陵、零陵太守、雲麾將軍、昌州刺史。
entries.en: He served in turn as administrator of Shaoling and Lingling, cloud-banner general, and inspector of Chang.
entries.literal: He successively served as administrator of Shaoling and Lingling, cloud-banner general, and inspector of Chang prefecture.

entries.zh: 王琳之舉兵也，弘直在湘州，琳敗，乃還朝。
entries.en: When Wang Lin rebelled, Hongzhi was in Xiangzhou; after Lin's defeat he returned to court.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin raised troops, Hongzhi was in Xiangzhou; when Lin was defeated he returned to court.

entries.zh: 天嘉中，歷國子博士、廬陵王長史、尚書左丞、領羽林監、中散大夫、祕書監，掌國史。
entries.en: Under Tianjia he was in turn grand-academy doctor, chief steward to the prince of Luling, left assistant in the masters of writing, superintendent of the feathered forest guard, palace scatterer grandee, and director of the secretariat in charge of the national history.
entries.literal: In the Tianjia era he successively served as grand-academy doctor, chief steward to the Prince of Luling, left assistant in the Masters of Writing, concurrently superintendent of the Feathered Forest guard, palace scatterer grandee, and director of the Secretariat, in charge of the national history.

entries.zh: 遷太常卿、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of rites and grand master for the glorious, with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: He was promoted to minister of rites and grand master for the glorious, with the added golden seal and purple ribbon.

entries.zh: 袁憲字德章，尚書左僕射樞之弟也。
entries.en: Yuan Xian, styled Dezhi, was the younger brother of Yuan Shu, left vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Yuan Xian, style Dezhi, was the younger brother of Yuan Shu, left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏，好學，有雅量。
entries.en: As a boy he was bright and eager to learn, with a calm, generous bearing.
entries.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, loved learning, and had refined capacity.

entries.zh: 梁武帝脩建庠序，別開五館，其一館在憲宅西，憲常招引諸生，與之談論，每有新議，出人意表，同輩咸嗟服焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Liang rebuilt the schools and opened five halls, one stood west of Xian's house. He often gathered students to debate; his fresh readings surprised everyone, and his peers admired him.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang repaired and built the school precinct, separately opening five halls; one hall lay west of Xian's residence. Xian often summoned and led students, debating with them; whenever he had a new interpretation it exceeded people's expectations, and his peers all sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 大同八年，武帝撰孔子正言章句，詔下國學，宣制旨義。
entries.en: In Datong year eight the emperor composed his commentary on the Correct Sayings of Confucius and ordered the National University to expound the imperial interpretation.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Datong the Emperor composed section-and-clause commentary on the Correct Sayings of Confucius and ordered it sent down to the National University to proclaim the imperial meaning.

entries.zh: 憲時年十四，被召為國子正言生，謁祭酒到溉，溉目而送之，愛其神彩。
entries.en: Xian was fourteen when he was made a Correct Sayings student at the National University. He visited libationer Dao Gai, who watched him leave and admired his bearing.
entries.literal: Xian was then fourteen and was summoned as a Correct Sayings student of the National University; he called on the libationer Dao Gai, who watched him departing and admired his spirit and bearing.

entries.zh: 在學一歲，國子博士周弘正謂憲父君正曰：「賢子今茲欲策試不？」
entries.en: After a year of study, National University doctor Zhou Hongzheng asked Xian's father Junzheng, "Will your worthy son sit for the examination this year?"
entries.literal: After one year in study, National University doctor Zhou Hongzheng said to Xian's father Junzheng: "Does your worthy son wish to undergo the examination this year?"

entries.zh: 君正曰：「經義猶淺，未敢令試。」
entries.en: Junzheng replied, "His classical learning is still shallow; I dare not let him try yet."
entries.literal: Junzheng said: "His understanding of the classics is still shallow; I do not dare let him try."

entries.zh: 居數日，君正遣門下客岑文豪與憲候弘正，會弘正將登講坐，弟子畢集，乃延憲入室，授之麈尾，令憲樹義。
entries.en: A few days later Junzheng sent his retainer Cen Wenhao with Xian to see Hongzheng. Hongzheng was about to lecture with all disciples present; he brought Xian in, gave him a fly-whisk, and told him to open the discussion.
entries.literal: After several days Junzheng sent his retainer Cen Wenhao with Xian to wait on Hongzheng. Meeting Hongzheng about to ascend the lecture seat with disciples all assembled, he brought Xian into the room, handed him a fly-whisk, and had Xian set forth the theme.

entries.zh: 時謝岐、何妥在坐，弘正謂曰：「二賢雖窮奧賾，得無憚此後生耶！」
entries.en: Xie Qi and He Tuo were in the audience. Hongzheng said, "You two have plumbed the depths—will you not fear this youth?"
entries.literal: At that time Xie Qi and He Tuo were seated; Hongzheng said: "You two worthies, though you have exhausted the profound depths—will you not fear this young man!"

entries.zh: 何、謝於是遞起義端，深極理致，憲與往復數番，酬對閑敏。
entries.en: He and Xie took turns pressing hard questions to the limits of doctrine; Xian answered several exchanges with easy, sharp replies.
entries.literal: He and Xie then in turn raised points of doctrine, probing the utmost reaches of principle; Xian went back and forth several rounds, replying with ease and keenness.

entries.zh: 弘正謂妥曰：「恣卿所問，勿以童稚相期。」
entries.en: Hongzheng told He Tuo, "Question him as you will—do not treat him as a child."
entries.literal: Hongzheng said to Tuo: "Ask as you please; do not measure him as a child."

entries.zh: 時學眾滿堂，觀者重沓，而憲神色自若，辯論有餘。
entries.en: The hall was packed and spectators crowded in, yet Xian remained composed and still had answers to spare.
entries.literal: At that time students filled the hall and onlookers piled in layers, yet Xian's expression was calm and his debate had surplus.

entries.zh: 弘正請起數難，終不能屈，因告文豪曰：「卿還咨袁吳郡，此郎已堪見代為博士矣。」
entries.en: Hongzheng raised difficulty after difficulty but could not defeat him. He told Wenhao, "Tell Administrator Yuan of Wu that this boy is already fit to succeed me as doctor."
entries.literal: Hongzheng repeatedly raised difficult points but in the end could not bend him; he therefore told Wenhao: "Go back and consult Administrator Yuan of Wu—this lad is already fit to replace me as doctor."

entries.zh: 時生徒對策，多行賄賂，文豪請具束脩，君正曰：「我豈能用錢為兒買第耶？」
entries.en: Students then often bribed their way through policy examinations. Wenhao asked to prepare the ritual gift; Junzheng said, "Would I buy my son a degree with money?"
entries.literal: At that time students answering policy questions often gave bribes; Wenhao asked to prepare the ritual gift; Junzheng said: "How could I use money to buy my son a place?"

entries.zh: 學司銜之。
entries.en: The academic office resented this.
entries.literal: The academic office bore a grudge.

entries.zh: 及憲試，爭起劇難，憲隨問抗答，剖析如流。
entries.en: At Xian's examination they all pressed fierce questions; he answered on the spot, reasoning as fluently as flowing water.
entries.literal: When Xian was examined, they all raised fierce difficulties; Xian answered each challenge as it came, analyzing like flowing water.

entries.zh: 到溉顧憲曰：「袁君正其有後矣。」
entries.en: Dao Gai looked at Xian and said, "Yuan Junzheng will have worthy descendants."
entries.literal: Dao Gai looked at Xian and said: "Yuan Junzheng truly has posterity."

entries.zh: 及君正將之吳郡，溉祖道於征虜亭，謂君正曰：「昨策生蕭敏孫、徐孝克，非不解義，至於風神器局，去賢子遠矣。」
entries.en: When Junzheng was leaving for Wu commandery, Gai saw him off at the Campaign-Slayer Pavilion and said, "Yesterday's candidates Xiao Minsun and Xu Xiaoke know their texts, but in spirit and bearing they are far below your son."
entries.literal: When Junzheng was about to go to Wu commandery, Gai saw him off at the campaign-slayer pavilion and said to Junzheng: "Yesterday's policy candidates Xiao Minsun and Xu Xiaoke are not without understanding of doctrine, but in spirit, instrument, and bearing they fall far short of your worthy son."

entries.zh: 尋舉高第。
entries.en: He soon placed in the top grade.
entries.literal: Soon he was ranked in the top grade.

entries.zh: 以貴公子選尚南沙公主，即梁簡文之女也。
entries.en: As a nobleman's son he was chosen to marry Princess Nansha, daughter of Liang's Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: As a nobleman's son he was chosen to marry the Princess of Nansha—the daughter of Liang's Emperor Jianwen.

entries.zh: 大同元年，釋褐祕書郎。
entries.en: In Datong 1, Xian entered office as a secretary gentleman.
entries.literal: In Datong 1, Xian removed his plain clothes and became secretary gentleman.

entries.zh: 太清二年，遷太子舍人。
entries.en: In Taiqing 2, he was promoted to attendant to the crown prince.
entries.literal: In Taiqing 2, he was promoted to attendant to the crown prince.

entries.zh: 侯景寇逆，憲東之吳郡，尋丁父憂，哀毀過禮。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, Xian went east to Wu Commandery. Soon afterward his father died, and his grief exceeded the demands of ritual.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing invaded and rebelled, Xian went east to Wu Commandery; soon he encountered mourning for his father, and his grief injured him beyond ritual requirements.

entries.zh: 敬帝承制，徵授尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing assumed provisional authority, Xian was summoned and appointed palace gentleman in the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing acted under provisional authority, Xian was summoned and appointed palace gentleman in the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 高祖作相，除司徒戶曹。
entries.en: When Gaozu became chief minister, Xian was appointed household bureau officer under the minister of education.
entries.literal: When Gaozu served as chief minister, Xian was appointed household bureau officer under the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 永定元年，授中書侍郎，兼散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Yongding 1, he was appointed secretariat gentleman while concurrently serving as Cavalier Attendant.
entries.literal: In Yongding 1, he was appointed secretariat gentleman and concurrently Cavalier Attendant.

entries.zh: 與黃門侍郎王瑜使齊，數年不遣，天嘉初乃還。
entries.en: He went as envoy to Qi with Huangmen Gentleman Wang Yu. They were detained for several years and returned only at the beginning of Tianjia.
entries.literal: He went as envoy to Qi with Huangmen Gentleman Wang Yu; for several years they were not sent back, and only at the beginning of Tianjia did they return.

entries.zh: 四年，詔復中書侍郎，直侍中省。
entries.en: In the fourth year, he was restored by edict as secretariat gentleman and assigned to duty in the Palace Attendant office.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, an edict restored him as secretariat gentleman, serving on duty in the Palace Attendant office.

entries.zh: 太建元年，除給事黃門侍郎，仍知太常事。
entries.en: In Taijian 1, he became service-providing Huangmen gentleman while continuing to oversee Ministry of Ceremonies affairs.
entries.literal: In Taijian 1, he was appointed service-providing Huangmen gentleman and remained in charge of Ministry of Ceremonies affairs.

entries.zh: 二年，轉尚書吏部侍郎，尋除散騎常侍，侍東宮。
entries.en: In the second year, he was transferred to the personnel bureau of the Department of State Affairs, then soon appointed Cavalier Attendant and assigned to serve in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to be personnel bureau gentleman in the Department of State Affairs, and soon was appointed Cavalier Attendant, serving in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 三年，遷御史中丞，領羽林監。
entries.en: In the third year, he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and concurrently superintendent of the Feathered Forest Guard.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and concurrently superintendent of the Feathered Forest Guard.

entries.zh: 時豫章王叔英不奉法度，逼取人馬，憲依事劾奏，叔英由是坐免黜，自是朝野皆嚴憚焉。
entries.en: At the time Prince Shuying of Yuzhang ignored the law and forcibly seized men and horses. Xian impeached him on the facts, leading to Shuying's dismissal and demotion; from then on, court and country alike stood in awe of Xian.
entries.literal: At the time Prince Shuying of Yuzhang did not observe laws and regulations and forcibly seized men and horses; Xian impeached him according to the facts, and Shuying was thereby dismissed and demoted. From then on, court and countryside all sternly feared Xian.

entries.zh: 憲詳練朝章，尤明聽斷，至有獄情未盡而有司具法者，即伺閑暇，常為上言之，其所申理者甚眾。
entries.en: Xian knew court law thoroughly and was especially skilled at judgment. When investigators had not finished a case but officials had already drafted the sentence, he would use spare moments to speak to the throne; the cases he corrected were very many.
entries.literal: Xian was thoroughly versed in court regulations and especially clear in hearing and deciding cases; whenever the facts of a prison case were not exhausted but the clerks had already prepared the statutory penalty, he would seize leisure moments and often speak to the ruler about it—the cases he set right were very numerous.

entries.zh: 嘗陪醼承香閣，賓退之後，高宗留憲與衛尉樊俊徙席山亭，談宴終日。
entries.en: Once, after a banquet in the Fragrant-Accepting Pavilion, the other guests withdrew. Emperor Gaozong asked Xian and Commandant of the Guards Fan Jun to remain, moved with them to the mountain pavilion, and talked and feasted with them all day.
entries.literal: He once attended a feast in the Fragrant-Accepting Pavilion. After the other guests withdrew, Emperor Gaozong asked Xian and Commandant of the Guards Fan Jun to remain, moved with them to the mountain pavilion, and talked and feasted with them all day.

entries.zh: 高宗目憲而謂俊曰「袁家故為有人」，其見重如此。
entries.en: The emperor looked at Xian and told Fan Jun, "The Yuan family has always had real men in it"—such was the esteem in which he was held.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong fixed his gaze on Xian and said to Jun, "The Yuan house has always produced men"; he was honored thus.

entries.zh: 五年，入為侍中。
entries.en: In year five he became palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he entered [capital service] as palace attendant.

entries.zh: 六年，除吳郡太守，以父任固辭不拜，改授明威將軍、南康內史。
entries.en: In year six he was appointed Administrator of Wu, but firmly declined because his father had held the same post; he was made General of Illustrious Might and Inner Administrator of Nankang instead.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Administrator of Wu, but firmly declined because his father had held the same post; he was instead made General of Illustrious Might and Inner Administrator of Nankang.

entries.zh: 九年，秩滿，除散騎常侍，兼吏部尚書，尋而為真。
entries.en: When his term ended in year nine he became scattered-cavalry regular attendant and acting minister of personnel, then received the full appointment.
entries.literal: In the ninth year his term ended; he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and concurrent minister of the board of civil office; soon after he held the full post.

entries.zh: 憲以久居清顯，累表自求解任。
entries.en: Having long held a high, unsullied post, Xian repeatedly asked to resign.
entries.literal: Xian, having long occupied a pure and eminent post, repeatedly memorialized asking to be released from office.

entries.zh: 高宗曰：「諸人在職，屢有謗書。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong said, "Others in office are often attacked in memorials.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Others in office have often had defamatory memorials.

entries.zh: 卿處事已多，可謂清白，別相甄錄，且勿致辭。」
entries.en: You have served many years with a clean record; I will mark that separately—do not resign."
entries.literal: You have handled affairs for many years and may be called unsullied; I will separately note and reward you—do not decline."

entries.zh: 十三年，遷右僕射，參掌選事。
entries.en: In year thirteen he was promoted to right vice director and took part in appointments.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to right vice director, participating in selection affairs.

entries.zh: 先是憲長兄簡懿為左僕射，至是憲為右僕射，臺省內目簡懿為大僕射，憲為小僕射，朝廷榮之。
entries.en: Earlier, Xian's eldest brother Yuan Shu, posthumously known as Jianyi, had served as Left Vice Director; now Xian was Right Vice Director. Within the Secretariat, Yuan Shu was called the Senior Vice Director and Xian the Junior Vice Director, and the court considered this an honor.
entries.literal: Earlier, Xian's eldest brother Yuan Shu, posthumously known as Jianyi, had served as Left Vice Director; now Xian was Right Vice Director. Within the Secretariat, Yuan Shu was called the Senior Vice Director and Xian the Junior Vice Director, and the court considered this an honor.

entries.zh: 至德元年，太子加元服，二年，行釋奠之禮，憲於是表請解職，後主不許，給扶二人，進號雲麾將軍，置佐史。
entries.en: In Zhide 1, the crown prince was capped, and in the second year he performed the libation ceremony. Xian then memorialized asking to resign, but the Later Lord refused, assigned him two attendants, advanced him to General of the Cloud Banner, and established a staff for him.
entries.literal: In Zhide 1, the crown prince received the capping ceremony; in the second year, he performed the libation ceremony. Xian then submitted a memorial asking to resign, but the Later Lord did not permit it, gave him two aides for support, advanced his title to General of the Cloud Banner, and established a staff for him.

entries.zh: 皇太子頗不率典訓，憲手表陳諫凡十條，皆援引古今，言辭切直，太子雖外示容納，而心無悛改。
entries.en: The crown prince often failed to follow proper instruction, so Xian personally submitted ten admonitory memorials, each citing ancient and recent examples in direct language. The crown prince outwardly accepted them but did not change.
entries.literal: The crown prince was rather unwilling to follow canonical instruction; Xian personally memorialized ten admonitions, all citing ancient and recent examples, with words urgent and direct. Although the crown prince outwardly showed acceptance, in his heart he did not reform.

entries.zh: 後主欲立寵姬張貴妃子始安王為嗣，嘗從容言之，吏部尚書蔡徵順旨稱賞，憲厲色折之曰：「皇太子國家儲嗣，億兆宅心。
entries.en: The Later Lord wanted to make the Prince of Shi'an, son of his favorite consort Noble Consort Zhang, his heir, and once mentioned it casually. Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng echoed his wishes and praised the idea, but Xian sternly rebuked him: "The crown prince is the heir of the state, and the hearts of the people rest on him.
entries.literal: The Later Lord wished to establish the Prince of Shi'an, son of his favored consort Noble Consort Zhang, as heir, and once spoke of it at leisure. Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng followed his intent and praised the idea, but Xian sternly rebuked him, saying: "The crown prince is the state's reserve heir, on whom the hearts of all the people are fixed.

entries.zh: 卿是何人，輕言廢立！」
entries.en: Who are you to speak lightly of deposing and enthroning!"
entries.literal: Who are you, to speak lightly of deposing and enthroning!"

entries.zh: 夏，竟廢太子為吳興王。
entries.en: That summer, the crown prince was finally deposed and made Prince of Wuxing.
entries.literal: In summer, the crown prince was finally deposed and made Prince of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 後主知憲有規諫之事，歎曰「袁德章實骨鯁之臣」，即日詔為尚書僕射。
entries.en: When the Later Lord learned of Xian's remonstrance, he sighed, "Yuan Dezhang is truly a minister with backbone," and that same day appointed him vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When the Later Lord learned that Xian had remonstrated, he sighed and said, "Yuan Dezhang is truly a minister of bone and backbone," and that same day issued an edict making him Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 禎明三年，隋軍來伐，隋將賀若弼進燒宮城北掖門，宮衛皆散走，朝士稍各引去，惟憲衛侍左右。
entries.en: In Zhenming 3, the Sui invaded. The Sui general He Ruobi advanced and burned the palace city's North Wing Gate; the guards fled and courtiers gradually slipped away, while only Xian stayed at the emperor's side.
entries.literal: In Zhenming 3, Sui armies came to attack; Sui general He Ruobi advanced and burned the North Wing Gate of the palace city. The palace guards all fled, and court officials gradually withdrew one by one; only Xian guarded and attended at the ruler's side.

entries.zh: 後主謂憲曰：「我從來待卿不先餘人，今日見卿，可謂歲寒知松柏後凋也。」
entries.en: The Later Lord told Xian, "I have always favored you above others; today you prove that pines and cypresses are the last to fade in winter."
entries.literal: The Later Lord said to Xian: "From the first I have treated you before others; seeing you today—one may say that in cold years one knows the pine and cypress are last to wither."

entries.zh: 後主遑遽將避匿，憲正色曰：「北兵之入，必無所犯，大事如此，陛下安之。
entries.en: As the emperor panicked and prepared to flee, Xian said sternly, "The northerners will not harm you. The matter is settled—Your Majesty, stay calm.
entries.literal: The Later Lord in panic was about to hide; Xian with stern countenance said: "When the northern troops enter they certainly will not violate [you]; the great affair is thus—Your Majesty, be at peace.

entries.zh: 臣願陛下正衣冠，御前殿，依梁武見侯景故事。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to dress properly, sit in the front hall, and follow Emperor Wu of Liang's example when he received Hou Jing."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to straighten robes and cap, mount the front hall, and follow the precedent of Liang's Emperor Wu receiving Hou Jing."

entries.zh: 後主不從，因下榻馳去，憲從後堂景陽殿入，後主投下井中，憲拜哭而出。
entries.en: The emperor refused, leapt from his couch, and fled. Xian went in through the rear Jingyang Palace hall; finding the emperor had thrown himself into a well, he bowed, wept, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Later Lord did not follow; he thereupon left the couch and galloped away. Xian entered from the rear hall, Jingyang Palace; the Later Lord cast himself into a well; Xian bowed, wept, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 京城陷，入于隋，隋授使持節、昌州諸軍事、開府儀同三司、昌州刺史。
entries.en: After the capital fell he entered Sui service as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Chang, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Chang.
entries.literal: When the capital fell he entered Sui service; Sui appointed him bearer of the staff, commander of all military affairs in Chang prefecture, opener of the mansion equal in honor to the three dukes, and inspector of Chang prefecture.

entries.zh: 開皇十四年，詔授晉王府長史。
entries.en: In Kaihuang year fourteen he was made chief steward of the prince of Jin's household.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaihuang an edict appointed him chief steward of the Prince of Jin's household.

entries.zh: 十八年卒，時年七十。
entries.en: He died in Kaihuang year eighteen, aged seventy.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he died, aged seventy.

entries.zh: 贈大將軍，安城郡公，諡曰簡。
entries.en: Posthumously he was made grand general and duke of Ancheng, with the posthumous name Jian.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was made grand general and Duke of Ancheng commandery; posthumous title Jian.

entries.zh: 長子承家，仕隋至祕書丞、國子司業。
entries.en: His eldest son Chengjia served the Sui, rising to secretary aide and vice director of the National University.
entries.literal: His eldest son Chengjia served the Sui, rising to Secretary Aide and Vice Director of the National University.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：梁元帝稱士大夫中重汝南周弘正，信哉斯言也！
entries.en: The historian writes: Emperor Yuan of Liang said that among scholar-officials he especially valued Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—how true that was!
entries.literal: The historian says: Emperor Yuan of Liang said that among scholar-officials he especially valued Zhou Hongzheng of Runan—how true those words are!

entries.zh: 觀其雅量標舉，尤善玄言，亦一代之國師矣。
entries.en: In breadth of mind and mastery of arcane learning he was a national teacher of his age.
entries.literal: Observing his refined capacity and elevated standards, especially his mastery of arcane discourse, he was also a national teacher of a generation.

entries.zh: 袁憲風格整峻，徇義履道。
entries.en: Yuan Xian's manner was austere and upright; he lived by duty and the Way.
entries.literal: Yuan Xian's style was ordered and severe; he followed righteousness and trod the Way.

entries.zh: 韓子稱為人臣委質，心無有二。
entries.en: Han Fei said that when a minister pledges himself to his lord, his heart must not be divided.
entries.literal: Han Fei said that when a man as minister commits his person [to a lord], his heart has no second [loyalty].

entries.zh: 憲弗渝終始，良可嘉焉。
entries.en: Xian never wavered from first to last—worthy of praise indeed.
entries.literal: Xian did not swerve from start to finish—truly praiseworthy.

entries.zh: 〔四〕 中大通
entries.en: Collation note 4: Zhong Datong
entries.literal: [4] Zhong Datong

entries.en: (two)
entries.literal: (two)

entries.zh: 〔三〕年梁昭明太子薨 按梁昭明太子卒於中大通三年，今補「中」字，「二」改「三」。
entries.en: On "[3] year the Heir Apparent Zhao Ming died": Zhao Ming died in Zhong Datong year three; zhong is supplied and two is changed to three.
entries.literal: [3] year the Heir Apparent Zhao Ming died—comment: the Heir Apparent Zhao Ming died in the third year of Zhong Datong; the character "zhong" is now supplied and "two" is changed to "three."

entries.zh: 南史亦脫「中」字，「三」字不訛。
entries.en: The Southern Dynasties history also omits "zhong"; "three" is correct.
entries.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties also lacks "zhong"; the character "three" is not in error.

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十四
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 24
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 24

entries.zh: 裴忌字無畏，河東聞喜人也。
entries.en: Pei Ji, styled Wuwei, was from Wenxi in Hedong.
entries.literal: Pei Ji, styled Wuwei, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.

entries.zh: 祖髦，梁中散大夫。
entries.en: His grandfather Mao was a Liang grand master for palace leisure.
entries.literal: His grandfather Mao was a Liang grand master for palace leisure.

entries.zh: 父之平，倜儻有志略，召補文德主帥。
entries.en: His father Zhiping was bold and strategic, and was summoned to serve as commander of the Wende guards.
entries.literal: His father Zhiping was free-spirited and had ambition and strategy; he was summoned to fill the post of commander of the Wende guards.

entries.zh: 梁普通中眾軍北伐，之平隨都督夏侯亶克定渦、潼，以功封費縣侯。
entries.en: During Liang's Putong era the armies campaigned north. Zhiping followed Commander Xiahou Dan in taking Guo and Tong, and for that merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fei county.
entries.literal: During Liang's Putong era, when the armies campaigned north, Zhiping followed Commander Xiahou Dan in capturing and pacifying Guo and Tong, and for this merit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fei county.

entries.zh: 會衡州部民相聚寇抄，詔以之平為假節、超武將軍、都督衡州五郡征討諸軍事。
entries.en: When Hengzhou locals gathered to raid and plunder, an edict made Zhiping acting bearer of the staff, General of Surpassing Martiality, and commander of the campaigns in Hengzhou's five commanderies.
entries.literal: When the people attached to Hengzhou gathered together to raid and plunder, an edict made Zhiping acting bearer of the staff, General of Surpassing Martiality, and commander of punitive military affairs in the five commanderies of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 及之平至，即皆平殄，梁武帝甚嘉賞之。
entries.en: When Zhiping arrived, he put them all down at once, and Emperor Wu of Liang praised and rewarded him highly.
entries.literal: When Zhiping arrived, he immediately pacified and destroyed them all, and Emperor Wu of Liang praised and rewarded him greatly.

entries.zh: 元帝承聖中，累遷散騎常侍、右衛將軍、晉陵太守。
entries.en: During Emperor Yuan's Chengsheng era he rose through regular attendant of the Secretariat, right guard general, and administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: During Emperor Yuan's Chengsheng era he rose successively to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, right guard general, and administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，除光祿大夫，慈訓宮衛尉，並不就，乃築山穿池，植以卉木，居處其中，有終焉之志。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Zhiping was appointed grand master of glorious happiness and chamberlain for the guards of Cixun Palace, but accepted neither. Instead he built hills, dug ponds, planted flowers and trees, and settled there, meaning to end his days in retirement.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Zhiping was appointed grand master of glorious happiness and chamberlain for the guards of Cixun Palace, but he accepted neither; instead he built hills, dug ponds, planted flowers and trees, lived among them, and intended to end his days there.

entries.zh: 天康元年卒，贈仁威將軍、光祿大夫，諡曰僖子。
entries.en: He died in Tiankang year 1. He was posthumously made General of Benevolent Prestige and grand master of glorious happiness, with the posthumous title Xizi.
entries.literal: In Tiankang year 1 he died; he was posthumously granted General of Benevolent Prestige and grand master of glorious happiness, with the posthumous title Xizi.

entries.zh: 〔四〕 瑒助防張世（責）貴舉外城以應之 據通鑑陳文帝天嘉元年及元龜三九九改。
entries.en: Note 4, on "Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shigui opened the outer city in response": emended from the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wendi, Tianjia year 1, and Yuan Gui 399.
entries.literal: Note 4, on "Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shigui opened the outer city in response": emended according to the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wendi, Tianjia year 1, and Yuan Gui 399.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，徵為左衛將軍。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne Ji was summoned as left guard general.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Ji was summoned as Left Guard General.

entries.zh: 天嘉初，出為持節、南康內史。
entries.en: At the opening of Tianjia (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.

entries.zh: 時義安太守張紹賓據郡反，世祖以忌為持節、都督嶺北諸軍事，率眾討平之。
entries.en: Zhang Shaobin, administrator of Yian, rebelled and held his commandery. Emperor Wen made Ji bearer of the staff and commander of the armies north of the range, and he led troops to crush him.
entries.literal: At that time Zhang Shaobin, Administrator of Yian, held the commandery in rebellion; Emperor Wen made Ji Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the North of the Range, and he led the host to campaign and pacify him.

entries.zh: 還除散騎常侍、司徒左長史。
entries.en: Returning, he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and left chief clerk of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On his return he was removed and made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 五年，授雲麾將軍、衛尉卿，封東興縣侯，邑六百戶。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was made cloud-banner general and chamberlain for the palace, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with six hundred households.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was given Cloud-Banner General and Chamberlain for the Palace, enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of six hundred households.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，授使持節、散騎常侍、安南將軍、湘州刺史，封定襄縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 瑒懷不自安，乃固請入朝，徵為散騎常侍、中領軍。
entries.en: Yang could not rest easy and begged to come to court. He was summoned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and central army commander.
entries.literal: Yang was uneasy at heart and firmly asked to enter court; he was summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander.

entries.zh: 〔五〕未拜，而世祖從容謂瑒曰：「昔朱買臣願為本郡，卿豈有意乎？」
entries.en: [5] Before he took office, Emperor Wen said to him gently: "Zhu Maichen once longed to govern his home commandery. Do you feel the same?"
entries.literal: Before he took the appointment, Emperor Wen spoke to Yang at ease and said: "Of old Zhu Maichen wished to be magistrate of his home commandery—do you have such a wish?"

entries.zh: 仍改授持節、安東將軍、吳郡太守，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was then made bearer of the staff, pacifying-the-east general, and administrator of Wu commandery, with a suite of martial pipes and drums.
entries.literal: He was thereupon reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Pacifying-the-East General, and Administrator of Wu commandery, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 及將之鎮，乘輿幸近畿餞送，鄉里榮之。
entries.en: As he set out for his post the emperor's carriage came to the near suburbs to feast and send him off. His home district took it as glory.
entries.literal: When he was about to go to his post the imperial carriage came to the near suburbs to see him off and feast him; his home district was glorified.

entries.zh: 秩滿，徵拜散騎常侍、中護軍，鼓吹如故。
entries.en: When his term ended he was recalled as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and central guard commander, keeping his pipes and drums.
entries.literal: When his term ended he was summoned and appointed Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Guard Commander, martial pipes and drums as before.

entries.zh: 留異之反東陽，詔瑒督舟師進討。
entries.en: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict put Yang in command of the river fleet to attack him.
entries.literal: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict ordered Yang to command the river fleet in advance to campaign.

entries.zh: 異平，遷鎮右將軍，常侍、鼓吹並如故。
entries.en: After Yi was crushed he was made general who guards the right, retaining his attendant post and pipes and drums.
entries.literal: When Yi was pacified he was transferred to General Who Guards the Right, regular attendant and martial pipes and drums unchanged.

entries.zh: 頃之，出為使持節、安東將軍、建安太守。
entries.en: Soon he was sent out as bearer of the staff, pacifying-the-east general, and administrator of Jian'an.
entries.literal: Before long he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Pacifying-the-East General, and Administrator of Jian'an.

entries.zh: 光大中，以公事免，尋起為通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the Guangda era (567) he was dismissed on official grounds, then soon restored as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the Guangda era he was removed for public business; soon he was raised again as Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 忌少聰敏，有識量，頗涉史傳，為當時所稱。
entries.en: As a youth Ji was quick and perceptive, with sound judgment; he had dipped deep into histories and won praise in his day.
entries.literal: Ji in youth was clever and keen, had judgment and capacity, had read widely in histories and annals, and was praised by men of the day.

entries.zh: 解褐梁豫章王法曹參軍。
entries.en: His first post was law officer on the staff of Liang's Prince of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as law officer in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，忌招集勇力，隨高祖征討，累功為寧遠將軍。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled Ji raised fighting men and marched with the Founder. Merit piled up until he was made pacifying-distance general.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Ji gathered bold fighters, followed the Founder on campaigns, and by accumulated merit was made Pacifying-Distance General.

entries.zh: 及高祖誅王僧辯，僧辯弟僧智舉兵據吳郡，高祖遣黃他率眾攻之，僧智出兵於西昌門拒戰，他與相持，不能克。
entries.en: After the Founder killed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's brother Sengzhi seized Wu commandery. The Founder sent Huang Ta with an army against him. Sengzhi marched out the Xichang Gate to fight. Ta held him at bay and could not break him.
entries.literal: When the Founder executed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's younger brother Sengzhi raised troops and held Wu commandery; the Founder sent Huang Ta at the head of the host to attack him; Sengzhi led troops out at the Xichang Gate to resist; Ta locked with him and could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 高祖謂忌曰：「三吳奧壤，舊稱饒沃，雖凶荒之餘，猶為殷盛，而今賊徒扇聚，天下搖心，非公無以定之，宜善思其策。」
entries.en: The Founder told Ji: "The Three Wu are the empire's rich core. Even after famine they stay prosperous, yet rebels now gather and the realm wavers. No one but you can settle this. Think hard on your plan."
entries.literal: The Founder said to Ji: "The Three Wu are a vital land, of old called rich and fertile; though in the wake of famine and ruin they remain abundant and thriving, yet now the rebels gather and sway the hearts of the realm—without you they cannot be settled. You should think well on your plan."

entries.zh: 忌乃勒部下精兵，輕行倍道，自錢塘直趣吳郡，〔一〕夜至城下，鼓譟薄之。
entries.en: Ji mustered his best troops, traveled light at forced march from Qiantang straight for Wu commandery, [1] and in a single night was under the walls beating drums and storming the gate.
entries.literal: Ji then mustered picked troops of his command, marched light and by double stages, went straight from Qiantang toward Wu commandery, and in one night reached below the walls, beat drums, clamored, and pressed the assault.

entries.zh: 僧智疑大軍至，輕舟奔杜龕，忌入據其郡。
entries.en: Sengzhi thought a great host had arrived, fled by light boat to Du Kan, and Ji entered and took the commandery.
entries.literal: Sengzhi suspected a great army had come, fled in a light boat to Du Kan, and Ji entered and held the commandery.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉之，表授吳郡太守。
entries.en: The Founder praised him and memorialized his appointment as administrator of Wu commandery.
entries.literal: The Founder commended him and memorialized him appointed Administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 瑒少倜儻，好謀略，博涉經史，尤便書翰。
entries.en: As a youth Yang was bold and fond of strategy; he read widely in the classics and histories and excelled at correspondence.
entries.literal: Yang in youth was free and bold, loved strategy, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially skilled at letters.

entries.zh: 起家梁輕車臨川嗣王行參軍，累遷為安西邵陵王水曹中兵參軍事。
entries.en: He entered service as acting aide to Liang's Heir of Linchuan in the light-chariot office, then rose to water-and-arms clerk on the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, pacifier of the west.
entries.literal: He began his career as acting aide in the light-chariot service of Liang's Heir of Linchuan, and was promoted in succession to water-and-arms clerk in the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, Pacifier of the West.

entries.zh: 王出鎮郢州，瑒盡室隨府，甚被賞遇。
entries.en: When the prince took up his post at Yingzhou, Yang brought his whole household to the headquarters and won high favor.
entries.literal: When the prince went out to garrison Yingzhou, Yang moved his whole household with the headquarters and was greatly favored.

entries.zh: 太清之難，授假節、宣猛將軍、軍主。
entries.en: In the Taiqing turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
entries.literal: In the turmoil of Taiqing he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.

entries.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，王琳為前軍，琳與瑒同門，乃表薦為戎昭將軍、宜都太守，仍從僧辯救徐文盛於武昌。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian attacked Hou Jing, Wang Lin led the van. Lin and Yang were schoolmates; Lin recommended him as martial-announcements general and administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to relieve Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Wang Lin was vanguard; Lin and Yang were of the same gate, and Lin memorialized recommending him as Martial-Announcements General and Administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to rescue Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.

entries.zh: 會郢州陷，乃留軍鎮巴陵，脩戰守之備。
entries.en: When Yingzhou fell he stayed behind to hold Baling and strengthened its defenses.
entries.literal: When Yingzhou fell he remained with the army to garrison Baling and repaired preparations for battle and defense.

entries.zh: 俄而侯景兵至，日夜攻圍，瑒督所部兵悉力拒戰，賊眾奔退。
entries.en: Soon Hou Jing's troops came and besieged him day and night. Yang led his men in a full defense and drove the rebels back.
entries.literal: Soon Hou Jing's troops arrived and attacked day and night; Yang supervised his command in full strength to resist; the rebel host broke and fled.

entries.zh: 瑒從大軍沿流而下，及克姑熟，瑒力戰有功，除員外散騎常侍，封富陽縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: He followed the main fleet downstream. At the taking of Guni he fought with distinction and was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and Marquis of Fuyang with one thousand households.
entries.literal: Yang followed the great army downriver; when Guni was taken Yang fought hard with merit; he was removed and made Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 尋授假節、雄信將軍、衡陽內史，未及之官，仍遷衡州平南府司馬。
entries.en: Soon he received acting staff as trustworthy-faith general and interior minister of Hengyang. Before he took office he was made marshal of the pacify-the-south headquarters in Heng province.
entries.literal: Soon he was given acting staff, made Trustworthy Faith General and Interior Minister of Hengyang; before he could take up the post he was transferred to marshal of the Pacify-the-South headquarters in Heng province.

entries.zh: 破黃洞蠻賊有功，除東莞太守，行廣州刺史。
entries.en: For breaking the Yellow-Cave rebels he was made administrator of Dongguan and acting administrator of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: For merit in breaking the Yellow-Cave Man rebels he was removed and made Administrator of Dongguan, acting Administrator of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 尋除智武將軍，監湘州事。
entries.en: Soon he was made intelligent-martial general and overseer of Xiang province.
entries.literal: Soon he was removed and made Intelligent Martial General and overseer of Xiang province affairs.

entries.zh: 敬帝嗣位，授持節、仁威將軍、巴州刺史。
entries.en: When the Honored Emperor succeeded he received the staff as benevolent-prestige general and administrator of Ba.
entries.literal: When the Honored Emperor succeeded he was given staff, made Benevolent Prestige General, and Administrator of Ba.

entries.zh: 〔一〕 自錢塘直趣吳郡 按通鑑梁敬帝紹泰元年胡注云：「按陳霸先自義興還建康，遣裴忌助黃他攻吳郡，自錢塘直趣吳郡，非路也。『錢塘』必誤。」
entries.en: Note 1, on "went straight from Qiantang toward Wu commandery": Hu Sanxing notes in the Comprehensive Mirror that Chen Baxian returned from Yixing to Jiankang and sent Pei Ji to help Huang Ta attack Wu commandery; a route straight from Qiantang to Wu commandery makes no sense, so Qiantang must be an error.
entries.literal: Note 1, on "went straight from Qiantang toward Wu commandery": Hu Sanxing's note to the Comprehensive Mirror, Liang Jingdi, Shaotai year 1, says: "Chen Baxian returned from Yixing to Jiankang and sent Pei Ji to assist Huang Ta in attacking Wu commandery; going straight from Qiantang to Wu commandery is not the route. Qiantang must be wrong."

entries.zh: 〔三〕 徵瑒為太府卿 「太府卿」南史作「少府卿」，通鑑陳武帝永定三年同。
entries.en: On "summoned Yang as minister of the grand storehouse": the Southern Dynasties history reads minister of the lesser storehouse; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.
entries.literal: Summoned Yang as Minister of the Grand Storehouse—"Minister of the Grand Storehouse" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Minister of the Lesser Storehouse"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊於郢州，徵瑒為太府卿，〔三〕加通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin enthroned Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou. Yang was summoned as grand steward [3] and promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Wang Lin set up Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou; Yang was summoned as Grand Steward, and promoted to Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 及王琳入寇，以瑒為使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢荊巴武湘五州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史，總留府之任。
entries.en: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Ying, with full charge of the rear headquarters.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, Pacifying-the-West General, and Inspector of Ying, with overall charge of the rear headquarters.

entries.zh: 周遣大將史寧率眾四萬，乘虛奄至，瑒助防張世貴舉外城以應之〔四〕，所失軍民男女三千餘口。
entries.en: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning with forty thousand men in a sudden rush. Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi Gui opened the outer city to them. [4] More than three thousand soldiers and civilians, men and women, were lost.
entries.literal: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning at the head of forty thousand men, who came by surprise in force; Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi Gui raised the outer city to welcome them, and there were lost among soldiers and people, men and women, more than three thousand persons.

entries.zh: 周軍又起土山高梯，日夜攻逼，因風縱火，燒其內城南面五十餘樓。
entries.en: The Zhou army raised siege mounds and scaling ladders and pressed day and night. They used the wind to fire the inner city's southern face and burned more than fifty towers.
entries.literal: The Zhou army again raised earthen hills and high ladders and attacked day and night; they took advantage of the wind to set fire and burned more than fifty towers on the inner city's south face.

entries.zh: 時瑒兵不滿千人，乘城拒守，瑒親自撫巡，行酒賦食，士卒皆為之用命。
entries.en: Yang had fewer than a thousand men. He held the walls himself, walking the battlements with wine and food. Every soldier fought for him to the last.
entries.literal: At that time Yang's troops were fewer than a thousand; he manned the walls to resist; Yang personally went about encouraging them, walking the ramparts with wine and food; the soldiers all fought to the death for him.

entries.zh: 周人苦攻不能克，乃矯授瑒柱國、郢州刺史，封萬戶郡公。
entries.en: The Zhou attacked hard and failed. They then falsely invested him as pillar of state, inspector of Ying, and duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery.
entries.literal: The Zhou men attacked bitterly and could not overcome him; they then falsely invested him as Pillar of State, Inspector of Ying, and Duke of a Ten-Thousand-Household Commandery.

entries.zh: 瑒偽許以緩之，而潛修戰具，樓雉器械，一朝嚴設，周人甚憚焉。
entries.en: Yang feigned acceptance to buy time while secretly readying arms. Towers, parapets, and engines stood complete by morning, and the Zhou were deeply afraid.
entries.literal: Yang pretended to agree to gain time, while secretly repairing war gear; towers, parapets, and engines were in one morning set in strict array; the Zhou men greatly feared him.

entries.zh: 及聞大軍敗王琳，乘勝而進，周兵乃解。
entries.en: When word came that the main army had broken Wang Lin and was marching in triumph, the Zhou lifted the siege.
entries.literal: When he heard the great army had defeated Wang Lin and was advancing in victory, the Zhou troops then lifted the siege.

entries.zh: 瑒於是盡有中流之地，集其將士而謂之曰：「吾與王公陳力協義，同獎梁室，亦已勤矣。
entries.en: Yang then held the entire mid-Yangzi. He assembled his officers and said: "We served the princes in righteousness and upheld Liang together. We have labored long enough.
entries.literal: Yang then held all the midstream lands; he gathered his generals and said to them: "I and the princes exerted strength together in righteousness and jointly upheld the house of Liang—we have already toiled enough.

entries.zh: 今時事如此，天可違乎！」
entries.en: The times stand as they do. Who defies Heaven?"
entries.literal: Now the times are thus—can Heaven be defied!"

entries.zh: 遂遣使奉表詣闕。
entries.en: He sent envoys with a memorial to court.
entries.literal: He then sent envoys with a memorial to the court.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：在梁之季，寇賊寔繁，高祖建義杖旗，將寧區夏，裴忌早識攀附，每預戎麾，摧鋒卻敵，〔九〕立功者數矣。
entries.en: The historiographer writes: In Liang's last years rebels swarmed. The Founder raised the banner of righteousness to pacify the realm. Pei Ji saw early whom to follow and was ever in the field, smashing the enemy's van and driving them back [9] again and again.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: In the last years of Liang, bandits and rebels were truly numerous; the Founder raised righteousness and bore the standard, about to bring peace to the realm; Pei Ji early recognized whom to follow and was always in the military entourage; smash the enemy's edge and drive them back, he achieved merit many times.

entries.zh: 孫瑒有文武幹略、見知時主，及行軍用兵，師司馬之法，至於戰勝攻取，屢著勳庸，加以好施接物，士咸慕向。
entries.en: Sun Yang had civil and military talent and won his sovereign's trust. In command he followed the marshal's art; in battle he took cities and won repeated glory. He was generous and approachable, and soldiers admired him.
entries.literal: Sun Yang had civil and military capacity and plan, was known to the ruler of the age; in marching armies and using troops he followed the methods of the Marshal; as to defeating the enemy in battle and taking by assault, he repeatedly achieved merit and fame; moreover he loved giving and received people well—officers and men all admired and turned to him.

entries.zh: 然性不循恆，頻以罪免，蓋亦陳湯之徒焉。
entries.en: Yet he was not steady by nature and was often dismissed for fault—perhaps a man in Chen Tang's mold.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he did not keep to constancy and was repeatedly removed for crimes—he was perhaps of Chen Tang's kind.

entries.zh: 及華皎稱兵上流，高宗時為錄尚書輔政，盡命眾軍出討，委忌總知中外城防諸軍事。
entries.en: When Hua Jiao rebelled upriver, Emperor Xuan was regent as recorder of the Secretariat. He sent every army against Jiao and put Ji in charge of all city defenses, within and without.
entries.literal: When Hua Jiao raised troops upriver, Emperor Xuan was then Recorder of the Secretariat assisting in government; he ordered all armies out to campaign and entrusted Ji with overall command of inner and outer city defense and military affairs.

entries.zh: 及皎平，高宗即位，太建元年，授東陽太守，改封樂安縣侯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: After Jiao fell, Emperor Xuan succeeded. In the first year of Taijian (569) Ji was made administrator of Dongyang and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Le'an with one thousand households.
entries.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Emperor Xuan took the throne; in the first year of Taijian he was given Administrator of Dongyang, changed in enfeoffment to Marquis of Le'an county with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 四年，入為太府卿。
entries.en: In the fourth year he entered court as grand steward.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he entered office as Grand Steward.

entries.zh: 五年，轉都官尚書。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was transferred to minister of justice.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，以瑒功名素著，深委任焉。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yang's record and fame were already great, and the emperor relied on him heavily.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, because Yang's achievement and fame had long been outstanding, he deeply entrusted affairs to him.

entries.zh: 太建四年，授都督荊信二州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史，出鎮公安。
entries.en: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was made commander of Jing and Xin, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Jing, and marched out to hold Gong'an.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was given command of military affairs in Jing and Xin provinces, made Pacifying-the-West General and Inspector of Jing, and went out to garrison Gong'an.

entries.zh: 瑒增脩城池，懷服邊遠，為鄰境所憚。
entries.en: He strengthened walls and moats, won over distant peoples, and neighboring states feared him.
entries.literal: Yang further repaired the walls and moats, won over the distant borders, and was feared by neighboring territories.

entries.zh: 居職六年，又以事免，更為通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: After six years in post he was dismissed again on official grounds and returned as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: After six years in office he was again removed for an affair and made Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant once more.

entries.zh: 及吳明徹軍敗呂梁，授使持節、督緣江水陸諸軍事、鎮西將軍，給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: When Wu Mingche was broken at Lüliang he was made bearer of the staff, commander of frontier river and land forces, general who guards the west, with a suite of pipes and drums.
entries.literal: When Wu Mingche's army was defeated at Lüliang he was given Bearer of the Staff and command of river and land forces along the frontier, made General Who Guards the West, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.

entries.zh: 尋授散騎常侍、都督荊郢巴武湘五州諸軍事、郢州刺史，持節、將軍、鼓吹並如故。
