entries.en: Soon he was scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Jing, Ying, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, and inspector of Ying, keeping staff, rank, and pipes and drums.
entries.literal: Soon he was given Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and command of military affairs in the five provinces of Jing, Ying, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, and Inspector of Ying; staff, general, and martial pipes and drums were as before.

entries.zh: 十二年，坐疆埸交通抵罪。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was punished for illicit dealings on the border.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was punished for trafficking at the frontier.

entries.zh: 孫瑒字德璉，吳郡吳人也。
entries.en: Sun Yang, styled Delian, came from Wu in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Sun Yang, styled Delian, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 祖文惠，齊越騎校尉、清遠太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Wenhui had been Qi colonel of the Yue cavalry and administrator of Qingyuan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Wenhui was Qi Colonel of the Yue Cavalry and Administrator of Qingyuan.

entries.zh: 父循道，〔二〕梁中散大夫，以雅素知名。
entries.en: His father Xundao [2] was a Liang palace attendant, known for refined simplicity.
entries.literal: His father Xundao, was Liang Palace Attendant and was famed for refined simplicity.

entries.zh: 江總字總持，濟陽考城人也，晉散騎常侍統之十世孫。
entries.en: Jiang Zong, styled Zongchi, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery, a tenth-generation descendant of Jin's regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, Jiang Tong.
entries.literal: Jiang Zong, styled Zongchi, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang, tenth-generation descendant of Jin Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Tong.

entries.zh: 五世祖湛，宋左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，忠簡公。
entries.en: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan had been Song's left grand master of the palace and a grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices, posthumously titled the loyal and simple duke.
entries.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan was Song Left Grand Master of the Palace, Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, the loyal and simple Duke.

entries.zh: 祖蒨，梁光祿大夫，有名當代。
entries.en: His grandfather Qian had been Liang's minister of the household and was famed in his generation.
entries.literal: His grandfather Qian was Liang Minister of the Household, famed in his generation.

entries.zh: 父紑，本州迎主簿，少居父憂，以毀卒，在《梁書孝行傳》。
entries.en: His father, Jiang Fou, was summoned by his home province to serve as Chief Clerk. While still young, he entered mourning for his father and died from wasting grief; his biography appears in the Book of Liang's Biographies of Filial Conduct.
entries.literal: His father Fou was summoned by his home province to serve as Chief Clerk. While still young, he entered mourning for his father and died from wasting grief; his biography appears in the Book of Liang's Biographies of Filial Conduct.

entries.zh: 〔二〕 侯之王父晉護軍將軍
entries.en: [2] The marquis's grandfather, Jin Protector-General of the Army
entries.literal: [2] The marquis's grandfather, Jin Protector-General of the Army

entries.en: (Biao)
entries.literal: (Biao)

entries.zh: 虨 按江虨晉書有傳，為江統之子，曾官護軍將軍，今據改。
entries.en: On "Biao": Jiang Biao has a biography in the Jin History; he was Jiang Tong's son and once served as protector-general; now emended accordingly.
entries.literal: Biao—According to Jiang Biao's biography in the Jin History he was the son of Jiang Tong and once served as protector-general; now changed accordingly.

entries.zh: 總七歲而孤，依于外氏。
entries.en: Zong was orphaned at seven and lived with his mother's family.
entries.literal: Zong was orphaned at seven and lived with his mother's family.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏，有至性。
entries.en: As a child he was clever and keen, with an utmost nature.
entries.literal: As a child he was clever and keen, with utmost nature.

entries.zh: 舅吳平光侯蕭勱〔一〕，名重當時，特所鍾愛，嘗謂總曰：「爾操行殊異，神采英拔，後之知名，當出吾右。」
entries.en: His maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping, [1] enjoyed a weighty reputation in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong, "Your conduct is wholly unlike that of others, and your spirit is striking and elevated; when you become famous hereafter, you will stand above me."
entries.literal: His maternal uncle Xiao Mai, Marquis Guang of Wuping, enjoyed a weighty reputation in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong: "Your conduct is wholly unlike that of others, and your spirit is striking and elevated; when you become famous hereafter, you will stand above me."

entries.zh: 及長，篤學有辭采，家傳賜書數千卷，總晝夜尋讀，未嘗輟手。
entries.en: When grown he studied diligently and had literary grace. The family held several thousand volumes of imperial grants; Zong read day and night without ever laying them down.
entries.literal: When grown he studied diligently and had literary grace. The family held several thousand volumes of imperial grants; Zong read day and night without ever laying them down.

entries.zh: 年十八，解褐宣惠武陵王府法曹參軍。
entries.en: At eighteen he entered official service as Legal Officer on the staff of the Prince of Wuling, General Who Proclaims Favor.
entries.literal: At eighteen he entered official service as Legal Officer on the staff of the Prince of Wuling, General Who Proclaims Favor.

entries.zh: 中權將軍、丹陽尹何敬容開府，置佐史，並以貴冑充之，仍除敬容府主簿。
entries.en: When central authority general and governor of Danyang He Jingrong opened his mansion and appointed staff clerks, all posts were filled with noble scions; Zong was furthermore made chief clerk in Jingrong's establishment.
entries.literal: When Central Authority General and Governor of Danyang He Jingrong opened his mansion and appointed staff clerks, all were filled with noble scions; Zong was furthermore made chief clerk in Jingrong's establishment.

entries.zh: 遷尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to palace retainer in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Promoted to Master of Writing Palace Retainer.

entries.zh: 梁武帝撰正言始畢，製述懷詩，總預同此作，帝覽總詩，深降嗟賞。
entries.en: When Liang's Emperor Wu had just finished compiling the Correct Language, he composed a poem expressing his feelings; Zong took part in the composition. The emperor read Zong's poem and deigned to express profound admiration and praise.
entries.literal: When Liang's Emperor Wu had just finished compiling the Correct Language, he composed a poem expressing his feelings; Zong took part in the composition. The Emperor read Zong's poem and deigned to express profound admiration and praise.

entries.zh: 仍轉侍郎。
entries.en: He was then transferred to gentleman-attendant.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to gentleman-attendant.

entries.zh: 尚書僕射范陽張纘，度支尚書琅邪王筠，都官尚書南陽劉之遴，並高才碩學，總時年少有名，纘等雅相推重，為忘年友會。
entries.en: Vice director of the masters of writing Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, revenue commissioner Wang Yun of Langya, and discipline commissioner Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were all men of eminent talent and great learning. Zong at the time was young and already famed; Zuan and the rest warmly esteemed him, and they formed friendships across the generations.
entries.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, Revenue Commissioner Wang Yun of Langya, and Discipline Commissioner Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were all men of eminent talent and great learning. Zong at the time was young and already famed; Zuan and the rest warmly esteemed him, and they formed friendships across the generations.

entries.zh: 之遴嘗酬總詩，其略曰：「上位居崇禮，寺署鄰栖息。
entries.en: Liu Zhilin's poem in reply to Zong, in summary: "You occupy a lofty rank and receive honored ritual; your office adjoins where I dwell.
entries.literal: Liu Zhilin's poem in reply to Zong, in summary: "You occupy a lofty rank and receive honored ritual; your office adjoins where I dwell.

entries.zh: 忌聞曉騶唱，每畏晨光赩。
entries.en: I dread to hear the dawn outrider's cry; each morning I fear the blazing light.
entries.literal: I dread to hear the dawn outrider's cry; each morning I fear the blazing light.

entries.zh: 高談意未窮，晤對賞無極。
entries.en: High talk whose meaning is not exhausted, meetings face to face whose appreciation has no end.
entries.literal: High talk whose meaning is not exhausted, meetings face to face whose appreciation has no end.

entries.zh: 探急共遨遊，休沐忘退食。
entries.en: We probe what is urgent and roam together; on rest days we forget to withdraw and eat.
entries.literal: We probe what is urgent and roam together; on rest days we forget to withdraw and eat.

entries.zh: 曷用銷鄙吝，枉趾覯顏色。
entries.en: How could we wear away vulgar grudges? You deigned to set your feet in view and see my face.
entries.literal: How could we wear away vulgar grudges? You deigned to set your feet in view and see my face.

entries.zh: 下上數千載，揚搉吐胸臆。」
entries.en: Surveying thousands of years above and below, we discuss them and pour forth what is in our breast."
entries.literal: Surveying thousands of years above and below, we discuss them and pour forth what is in our breast."

entries.zh: 其為通人所欽挹如此。
entries.en: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.
entries.literal: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.

entries.zh: 遷太子洗馬，又出為臨安令，還為中軍宣城王府限內錄事參軍，轉太子中舍人。
entries.en: He was promoted to groom of the heir apparent; then sent out as magistrate of Lin'an, returned as records clerk with limited commission in the central army Prince of Xuancheng's establishment, and transferred to attendant of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: Promoted to groom of the heir apparent; then sent out as magistrate of Lin'an, returned as records clerk with limited commission in the Central Army Prince of Xuancheng's establishment, transferred to attendant of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 察幼有至性，事親以孝聞。
entries.en: As a child Cha had an utmost nature; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.
entries.literal: As a child Cha had utmost nature; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 六歲，誦書萬餘言。
entries.en: At six he could recite more than ten thousand words of books.
entries.literal: At six he could recite more than ten thousand words of books.

entries.zh: 弱不好弄，博弈雜戲，初不經心。
entries.en: In youth he did not care for play; gambling and miscellaneous games never touched his mind.
entries.literal: In youth he did not care for play; gambling and miscellaneous games never touched his mind.

entries.zh: 勤苦厲精，以夜繼日。
entries.en: With painful zeal he sharpened his spirit, continuing from night into day.
entries.literal: With painful zeal he sharpened his spirit, continuing from night into day.

entries.zh: 年十二，便能屬文。
entries.en: At twelve he could already compose literary pieces.
entries.literal: At twelve he could already compose literary pieces.

entries.zh: 父上開府僧垣，〔六〕知名梁武代，二宮禮遇優厚，每得供賜，皆回給察兄弟，為遊學之資，察並用聚蓄圖書，由是聞見日博。
entries.en: His father Sengyuan, superior grandee opening the mansion, [6] was famed under Liang's Emperor Wu; both palaces treated him with exceptional courtesy. Whenever he received provisions and gifts he would turn them to Cha and his brothers for travel-study funds; Cha used them all to gather and store books, and so his learning and sight grew daily broader.
entries.literal: His father, the Commissioner with the Upper Office, Sengyuan, was famed in the age of Liang's Emperor Wu; both palaces treated him with exceptional courtesy. Whenever he received provisions and gifts he would turn them to Cha and his brothers for travel-study funds; Cha used them all to gather and store books, and so his learning and sight grew daily broader.

entries.zh: 年十三，梁簡文帝時在東宮，盛脩文義，即引於宣猷堂聽講論難，為儒者所稱。
entries.en: At thirteen, when Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace and lavishly cultivated literary doctrine, Cha was at once brought into the Hall of Propagating Virtue to hear lectures and disputations, and Confucians praised him.
entries.literal: At thirteen, when Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace and lavishly cultivated literary doctrine, Cha was at once brought into the Hall of Propagating Virtue to hear lectures and disputations, and Confucians praised him.

entries.zh: 及簡文嗣位，尤加禮接。
entries.en: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne he showed Cha still more courtesy and reception.
entries.literal: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne he showed Cha still more courtesy and reception.

entries.zh: 起家南海王國左常侍，兼司文侍郎。
entries.en: He began his career as left regular attendant to the Prince of Nanhai and concurrently gentleman of the secretariat for texts.
entries.literal: He began his career as left regular attendant to the Prince of Nanhai and concurrently gentleman of the Secretariat for texts.

entries.zh: 除南郡王行參軍，兼尚書駕部郎。
entries.en: He was made acting aide in the Prince of Nanjun's establishment and concurrently gentleman of the masters of writing for the carriage-office.
entries.literal: He was made acting aide in the Prince of Nanjun's establishment and concurrently gentleman of the Masters of Writing for the carriage-office.

entries.zh: 遷尚書祠部侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice director of the ministry of rites for sacrificial affairs.
entries.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites for Sacrificial Affairs.

entries.zh: 此曹職司郊廟，昔魏王肅奏祀天地，設宮縣之樂，八佾之舞，爾後因循不革。
entries.en: That bureau oversaw suburban altars. Once Wang Su of Wei had memorialized on sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, setting up palace music and eight rows of dancers; afterward the practice was followed unchanged.
entries.literal: This bureau oversaw suburban altars; in the past Wei Wang Su memorialized on sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, establishing palace music and eight rows of dancers, and afterward custom was followed without change.

entries.zh: 梁武帝以為事人禮縟，事神禮簡，古無宮縣之文。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang held that rites toward men should be elaborate and rites toward the gods simple, and that antiquity had no precedent for palace music.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang held that rites for men were elaborate and rites for gods simple, and that antiquity had no text for palace music.

entries.zh: 陳初承用，莫有損益。
entries.en: When Chen was founded the court kept the practice as it was.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chen they continued the practice without change.

entries.zh: 高宗欲設備樂，付有司立議，以梁武帝為非。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong wanted full ritual music and ordered the offices to debate, taking Liang Wu to have been mistaken.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong wished to prepare full music and charged the offices to debate, holding Liang Wu in the wrong.

entries.zh: 時碩學名儒、朝端在位者，咸希上旨，並即注同。
entries.en: Leading scholars and officials at court all read the emperor's mind and at once sided with him.
entries.literal: Then eminent scholars and worthies at court all hoped for the emperor's intent and immediately noted agreement.

entries.zh: 察乃博引經籍，獨違群議，據梁樂為是，當時驚駭，莫不慚服，僕射徐陵因改同察議。
entries.en: Cha cited the classics at length, stood alone against the consensus, and argued that Liang's music was right. The court was astonished and ashamed into agreement; Vice Director Xu Ling then adopted Cha's position.
entries.literal: Cha cited the classics at length, stood alone against the consensus, and held that Liang's music was correct. The court was astonished and ashamed into agreement; Vice Director Xu Ling then adopted Cha's position.

entries.zh: 其不順時隨俗，皆此類也。
entries.en: His refusal to bend to fashion was always of this sort.
entries.literal: His refusal to follow the times and fashion were all of this kind.

entries.zh: 及魏國通好，敕以總及徐陵攝官報聘，總以疾不行，侯景寇京都，詔以總權兼太常卿，守小廟。
entries.en: When friendship was restored with Wei, an edict appointed Zong and Xu Ling as acting officials on a return embassy. Zong did not go because of illness. When Hou Jing raided the capital, an edict made Zong acting minister of ceremonies in charge of the lesser altars.
entries.literal: When friendship was restored with Wei, an edict appointed Zong and Xu Ling as acting officials on a return embassy. Zong did not go because of illness. When Hou Jing raided the capital, an edict made Zong acting Minister of Ceremonies in charge of the lesser altars.

entries.zh: 臺城陷，總避難崎嶇，累年至會稽郡，憩於龍華寺，乃製修心賦，略序時事。
entries.en: When the palace city fell, Zong fled in hardship over many years until he reached Kuaiji commandery and rested at Longhua Monastery, whereupon he composed the Cultivating the Mind rhapsody, briefly narrating the affairs of the time.
entries.literal: When the palace city fell, Zong fled in hardship over many years until he reached Kuaiji commandery and rested at Longhua Monastery, whereupon he composed the Cultivating the Mind rhapsody, briefly narrating the affairs of the time.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: Its words run:
entries.literal: Its words run:

entries.zh: 總第九舅蕭勃先據廣州，總又自會稽往依焉。
entries.en: Zong's ninth maternal uncle Xiao Bo had first seized Guangzhou; Zong again went from Kuaiji to rely on him.
entries.literal: Zong's ninth uncle by marriage Xiao Bo had first seized Guangzhou; Zong again went from Kuaiji to rely on him.

entries.zh: 梁元帝平侯景，徵總為明威將軍、始興內史，以郡秩米八百斛給總行裝。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Zong as resplendent might general and interior governor of Shixing, granting eight hundred piculs of the commandery salary for Zong's travel expenses.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Zong as Resplendent Might General and interior governor of Shixing, granting eight hundred piculs of the commandery salary for Zong's travel expenses.

entries.zh: 會江陵陷，遂不行，總自此流寓嶺南積歲。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell he could not go; from this Zong lodged in Lingnan for years on end.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell he could not go; from this Zong lodged in Lingnan for years on end.

entries.zh: 天嘉四年，以中書侍郎徵還朝，直侍中省。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 4 he was summoned back to court as gentleman of the secretariat and attended at the palace secretariat.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 4, he was summoned back to court as gentleman of the Secretariat and attended at the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 累遷司徒右長史，掌東宮管記，給事黃門侍郎，領南徐州大中正。
entries.en: He rose in repeated promotions to Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, keeper of Eastern Palace records, Attendant in the Yellow Gate, and concurrently Chief Rectifier for Southern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He rose in repeated promotions to Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, keeper of Eastern Palace records, Attendant in the Yellow Gate, and concurrently Chief Rectifier for Southern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 授太子中庶子、通直散騎常侍，東宮、中正如故。
entries.en: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and direct, clear-scattered-cavalry attendant; his eastern-palace and rectifier posts remained as before.
entries.literal: Made junior mentor of the heir apparent and direct, clear-scattered-cavalry attendant; eastern-palace and rectifier posts as before.

entries.zh: 遷左民尚書，轉太子詹事，中正如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of the masters of writing for households and transferred to grand mentor of the heir apparent; his rectifier post remained as before.
entries.literal: Promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Households, transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; rectifier post as before.

entries.zh: 以與太子為長夜之飲，養良娣陳氏為女，太子微行總舍，上怒免之。
entries.en: Because he drank with the heir through the night and reared the worthy concubine Lady Chen as his daughter, and the heir would slip out to Zong's quarters, Emperor Xuan was angry and dismissed him.
entries.literal: Because he drank with the heir through the night and reared the worthy concubine Lady Chen as his daughter, and the heir would slip out to Zong's quarters, the Emperor was angry and dismissed him.

entries.zh: 尋為侍中，領左驍騎將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was made attendant and concurrently general of the left nimble cavalry.
entries.literal: Soon he was made attendant and concurrently general of the left nimble cavalry.

entries.zh: 復為左民尚書，領左軍將軍，未拜，又以公事免。
entries.en: Again minister for households and concurrently general of the left army; before he took the seal he was again dismissed on official business.
entries.literal: Again Minister for Households and concurrently general of the left army; before he took the seal he was again dismissed on official business.

entries.zh: 尋起為散騎常侍、明烈將軍、司徒左長史，遷太常卿。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Illustrious Valor, and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Illustrious Valor, and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 中書侍郎領著作杜之偉與察深相眷遇，表用察佐著作，仍撰史。
entries.en: Du Zhiwei, vice director of the secretariat who also headed the directorate of history, was deeply attached to him; he memorialized to appoint Cha as an assistant compiler, and Cha went on writing history.
entries.literal: Du Zhiwei, Vice Director of the Secretariat who concurrently headed the Directorate of History, was deeply fond of him; he memorialized to employ Cha as assistant in the directorate, and Cha continued composing history.

entries.zh: 永定初，拜始興王府功曹參軍，尋補嘉德殿學士，轉中衛、儀同始興王府記室參軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yongding he was appointed Merit Officer on the staff of the Prince of Shixing. Soon he was made an Academic of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, then transferred to Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Shixing, General of the Central Guard with Ceremonial Parity.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongding he was appointed Merit Officer on the staff of the Prince of Shixing. Soon he was made an Academic of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, then transferred to Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Shixing, General of the Central Guard with Ceremonial Parity.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書徐陵時領著作，復引為史佐，及陵讓官致仕等表，並請察製焉，陵見歎曰「吾弗逮也」。
entries.en: Xu Ling, minister of personnel, was then also in charge of the history office and again took Cha on as a history assistant; when Ling's memorials declining office and seeking retirement were drafted, Cha wrote them all. Ling sighed, "I cannot equal him."
entries.literal: Xu Ling, Minister of Personnel, then concurrently headed the directorate; he again recruited Cha as a history assistant, and when Ling's memorials declining office and retiring were all drafted, Cha was asked to compose them; Ling sighed and said, "I do not match him."

entries.zh: 太建初，補宣明殿學士，除散騎侍郎、左通直。
entries.en: Early in Taijian he was made an academic of the Hall of Bright Illumination and appointed vice attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and left direct communicator.
entries.literal: Early in the Taijian era he was made an academic of the Hall of Bright Illumination and appointed Vice Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Left Direct Communicator.

entries.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，報聘于周。
entries.en: Soon he was also regular attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry for direct communication and sent on a return mission to Zhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was concurrently Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry for Direct Communication and sent as envoy on a return mission to Zhou.

entries.zh: 江左耆舊先在關右者，咸相傾慕。
entries.en: Elders of the southeast already living in the Guan region all admired him.
entries.literal: Elders of the southeast already in the Guan region all admired him.

entries.zh: 沛國劉臻竊於公館訪漢書疑事十餘條，並為剖析，皆有經據。
entries.en: Liu Zhen of Pei privately came to the embassy lodge and asked more than ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha explained them all with solid textual grounds.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen of Pei privately at the embassy lodge asked over ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha analyzed them all, each with textual basis.

entries.zh: 臻謂所親曰「名下定無虛士」。
entries.en: Zhen told those close to him, "A settled reputation never rests on an empty scholar."
entries.literal: Zhen told his intimates, "When a reputation is settled, there is no empty scholar."

entries.zh: 著西聘道里記，所敘事甚詳。
entries.en: He wrote the Record of Roads on the Western Mission, narrating the journey in great detail.
entries.literal: He wrote the Record of Roads on the Western Mission; the matters he narrated were very detailed.

entries.zh: 初，梁季淪沒，父僧垣入于長安，察蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，至是凶問因聘使到江南。
entries.en: Earlier, when Liang fell, his father Sengyuan had gone to Chang'an. Cha lived on vegetables and plain cloth and would not hear music. Now word of his father's death reached the south with the returning envoys.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Liang age fell, his father Sengyuan went to Chang'an; Cha ate only vegetables and wore plain cloth and heard no music; now news of his death came via the envoys to the south.

entries.zh: 時察母韋氏喪制適除，後主以察羸瘠，慮加毀頓，乃密遣中書舍人司馬申就宅發哀，仍敕申專加譬抑。
entries.en: At the time, Cha had just completed mourning for his mother, Lady Wei. Houzhu, seeing how emaciated Cha was, feared further grief would ruin his health and secretly sent Secretariat Attendant Sima Shen to express condolences at his home, with orders to counsel restraint.
entries.literal: At the time, Cha had just completed mourning for his mother, Lady Wei. Houzhu, seeing Cha emaciated, feared he would collapse from further grief and secretly sent Secretariat Attendant Sima Shen to express condolences at his home, ordering Shen especially to counsel restraint.

entries.zh: 爾後又遣申宣旨誡喻曰：「知比哀毀過禮，甚用為憂。
entries.en: Later he again sent Shen with an edict of admonition: "I know your mourning goes beyond the rites, and I am deeply troubled.
entries.literal: Later he again sent Shen with an edict of admonition, saying: "Knowing that your grief exceeds the rites, I am very concerned.

entries.zh: 卿迥然一身，宗奠是寄，毀而滅性，聖教所不許。
entries.en: You stand alone, and the clan sacrifices depend on you. To ruin yourself is what the sages forbid.
entries.literal: You stand alone; the clan sacrifices rest on you; to destroy yourself and annihilate your nature is what the sage teaching does not permit.

entries.zh: 宜微自遣割，以存禮制。
entries.en: You should restrain yourself a little and keep within the rites.
entries.literal: You should slightly restrain yourself to preserve the ritual order.

entries.zh: 憂懷既深，故有此及。」
entries.en: My concern is great, and so I send you this word."
entries.literal: My worry being deep, hence this message."

entries.zh: 拜宣惠宜都王中錄事參軍，帶東宮學士。
entries.en: He was made central recorder of the princedom of Yidu under splendid favor, while retaining his eastern palace academic post.
entries.literal: He was appointed Central Recorder of the Princedom of Yidu under Splendid Favor, concurrently an eastern palace academic.

entries.zh: 歷仁威淮南王、平南建安王二府諮議參軍，丁內憂去職。
entries.en: He served as consulting colonel to the princes of Huainan and Jian'an, then left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He served as consulting colonel for the princes of Huainan and Jian'an and left office on mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 俄起為戎昭將軍，知撰梁史事，固辭不免。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as rongzhao general and put in charge of compiling the history of Liang; he pleaded hard to be excused but could not.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as Rongzhao general and charged with compiling the history of Liang; he firmly declined but could not escape.

entries.zh: 後主纂業、敕兼東宮通事舍人，將軍、知撰史如故。
entries.en: When Houzhu took the throne he ordered Cha to serve concurrently as eastern palace communicating affairs attendant; his general's rank and charge over history stayed the same.
entries.literal: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne he ordered Cha concurrently Eastern Palace Communicating Affairs Attendant; his generalship and charge over history remained as before.

entries.zh: 又敕專知優冊謚議等文筆。
entries.en: He was also ordered to handle posthumous titles, eulogies, and similar court writings.
entries.literal: He was also ordered to specialize in posthumous titles, eulogies, and such writing.

entries.zh: 至德元年，除中書侍郎，轉太子僕，餘並如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhide he was made vice director of the secretariat, then steward of the heir apparent; his other posts were unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Steward of the Heir Apparent; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 仁壽二年，詔曰：「前祕書丞北絳郡開國公姚察，彊學待問，博極群典，脩身立德，白首不渝，雖在哀疚，宜奪情禮，可員外散騎常侍，封如故。」
entries.en: In Renshou year 2, an edict said, "Yao Cha, former secretary assistant and founding duke of Beijiang commandery, is learned and ready for inquiry, has mastered the classics, cultivated himself, and held to virtue into old age. Though he is in mourning, the normal mourning rules should be set aside; he may serve as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, with his fief as before."
entries.literal: In Renshou year 2, an edict said: "Former secretary assistant and founding duke of Beijiang commandery Yao Cha is strong in learning and ready for questions, has ranged through all the classics, cultivated himself and established virtue, and has not wavered though white-haired. Although he is in mourning, the rites of feeling should be set aside; he may be made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, with his fief as before."

entries.zh: 又敕侍晉王昭讀。
entries.en: He was also ordered to attend Prince of Jin Zhao as reader.
entries.literal: He was also ordered to attend on the Prince of Jin and read and explain texts for him.

entries.zh: 煬帝初在東宮，數被召見，訪以文籍。
entries.en: When Emperor Yang was first in the Eastern Palace, Cha was repeatedly summoned and consulted on books and records.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang was first in the Eastern Palace, Cha was repeatedly summoned and consulted about books and documents.

entries.zh: 即位之始，詔授太子內舍人，餘並如故。
entries.en: At the beginning of the reign, he was appointed inner attendant to the heir apparent by edict, with his other posts unchanged.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the reign, an edict appointed him inner attendant to the heir apparent, with all his other posts as before.

entries.zh: 車駕巡幸，恆侍從焉。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Cha always attended him.
entries.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, he always attended it.

entries.zh: 及改易衣冠，刪正朝式，切問近對，察一人而已。
entries.en: When court dress was changed and court ritual revised, Cha alone was summoned for close questioning and direct answers.
entries.literal: When dress and caps were changed and court ceremonies were revised and corrected, the close questioning and nearby answers involved Cha alone.

entries.zh: 宗元饒 司馬申 毛喜 蔡徵
entries.en: Zong Yuanrao; Sima Shen; Mao Xi; Cai Zheng
entries.literal: Zong Yuanrao; Sima Shen; Mao Xi; Cai Zheng

entries.zh: 司馬申字季和，河內溫人也。
entries.en: Sima Shen, styled Jihe, came from Wen in Henei commandery.
entries.literal: Sima Shen, styled Jihe, was a native of Wen in Henei commandery.

entries.zh: 祖慧遠，梁都水使者。
entries.en: His grandfather Huiyuan was Liang's commissioner of waterways.
entries.literal: His grandfather Huiyuan was Liang's commissioner of waterways.

entries.zh: 父玄通，梁尚書左民郎。
entries.en: His father Xuantong was Liang's left director in the masters of writing for the people.
entries.literal: His father Xuantong was Liang's Left Director in the Masters of Writing for the People.

entries.zh: 申早有風概，十四便善弈棋，嘗隨父候吏部尚書到
entries.en: Shen from early on had presence of spirit; at fourteen he was already skilled at weiqi. He once followed his father to call on the minister of personnel, Dao
entries.literal: Shen from early on had presence of spirit; at fourteen he was already skilled at weiqi. He once followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao

entries.zh: （仲舉）
entries.en: Collation variant: (Zhongju).
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Zhongju).

entries.zh: 溉，〔一〕時梁州刺史陰子春、領軍朱异在焉。
entries.en: Collation variant: (Gai), [1] At that time Liang inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and director of the palace guard Zhu Yi were present.
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Gai), At that time Liang Inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and Director of the Palace Guard Zhu Yi were present.

entries.zh: 子春素知申，即於坐所呼與為對，〔二〕申每有妙思，异觀而奇之，因引申遊處。
entries.en: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, [2] Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.
entries.literal: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.

entries.zh: 梁邵陵王為丹陽尹，以申為主簿。
entries.en: When Liang's Prince of Shaoling served as governor of Danyang, he made Shen his chief clerk.
entries.literal: When Liang's Prince of Shaoling served as governor of Danyang, he made Shen his chief clerk.

entries.zh: 屬太清之難，父母俱沒，因此自誓，菜食終身。
entries.en: When the Taqing turmoil came, both his parents died; on this account he vowed to himself and ate vegetables for life.
entries.literal: When the Taqing turmoil came, both his parents died; on this account he vowed to himself and ate vegetables for life.

entries.zh: 及叔陵之肆逆也，事既不捷，出據東府，申馳召右衛蕭摩訶帥兵先至，追斬之，因入城中，收其府庫，後主深嘉之。
entries.en: When Shuling's violent outrage took place, the affair did not succeed and he went out to hold the eastern palace; Shen galloped to summon right guard Xiao Mohe to lead troops and arrive first, pursued and beheaded him, then entered the city and seized his treasury stores—Houzhu deeply commended him.
entries.literal: When Shuling's violent outrage took place, the affair did not succeed and he went out to hold the eastern palace; Shen galloped to summon Right Guard Xiao Mohe to lead troops and arrive first, pursued and beheaded him, then entered the city and seized his treasury stores—Houzhu deeply commended him.

entries.zh: 以功除太子左衛率，封文
entries.en: For his merit he was made left leader of the heir apparent's guard, enfeoffed as Wen
entries.literal: For his merit he was made Left Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard, enfeoffed as Wen

entries.en: Collation variant: (Shi).
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Shi).

entries.zh: 招縣伯，〔三〕邑四百戶，兼中書通事舍人。
entries.en: Collation variant: (Zhao) county baron, [3] fief four hundred households, and concurrently secretariat communicating affairs attendant.
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Zhao) County Baron, fief four hundred households, and concurrently Secretariat Communicating Affairs Attendant.

entries.zh: 尋遷右衛將軍，加通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to general of the right guard, with additional unimpeded scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of the Right Guard, with additional Unimpeded Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 以疾還第，就加散騎常侍，右衛、舍人如故。
entries.en: Because of illness he returned to his residence; he was then given additional scattered-cavalry regular attendant, with right guard and attendant posts as before.
entries.literal: Because of illness he returned to his residence; he was then given additional Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, with right guard and attendant posts as before.

entries.zh: 至德四年卒，後主嗟悼久之，下詔曰：「慎終追遠，欽若舊則，闔棺定諡，抑乃前典。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhide (586) he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these are indeed the former canons.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide he died; Houzhu mourned him long and issued an edict saying: "Care in the end and remembrance of the distant, reverence for old norms, closing the coffin and fixing the posthumous title—these suppress former canons.

entries.zh: 故散騎常侍、右衛將軍、文
entries.en: The late scattered-cavalry regular attendant, general of the right guard, Wen
entries.literal: The late Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, General of the Right Guard, Wen

entries.en: Collation variant: (Shi).
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Shi).

entries.zh: 招縣開國伯申，忠肅在公，清正立己，治繁處約，投軀殉義。
entries.en: Collation variant: (Zhao) county founding baron Shen was loyal and solemn in public service, pure and upright in his person, governing complexity with restraint and casting his body to follow righteousness.
entries.literal: Collation variant: (Zhao) County Founding Baron Shen was loyal and solemn in public service, pure and upright in his person, governing complexity with restraint and casting his body to follow righteousness.

entries.zh: 朕任寄情深，方康庶績，奄然化往，傷惻于懷。
entries.en: We entrusted him with deep feeling and were about to bring peace to the people's labors; suddenly he transformed and went—grief pierces the breast.
entries.literal: We entrusted him with deep feeling and were about to bring peace to the people's labors; suddenly he transformed and went—grief pierces the breast.

entries.zh: 可贈侍中、護軍將軍，進爵為侯，增邑為五百戶，諡曰忠。
entries.en: He may be posthumously made palace attendant and protector general, his rank advanced to marquis, his fief increased to five hundred households, posthumous title Zhong.
entries.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant and Protector General, his rank advanced to marquis, his fief increased to five hundred households, posthumous title Zhong.

entries.zh: 給朝服一具，衣一襲，剋日舉哀，喪事所須，隨由資給。」
entries.en: Give one set of court robes, one suit of garments; fix a day for mourning; whatever the funeral requires, supply as needed."
entries.literal: Give one set of court robes, one suit of garments; fix a day for mourning; whatever the funeral requires, supply as needed."

entries.zh: 及葬，後主自製誌銘，辭情傷切。
entries.en: At the burial Houzhu himself composed the epitaph inscription; the words were painfully moving.
entries.literal: At the burial Houzhu himself composed the epitaph inscription; the words were painfully moving.

entries.zh: 卒章曰：「嗟乎！
entries.en: The closing lines say, "Alas!
entries.literal: The closing lines say: "Alas!

entries.zh: 天不與善，殲我良臣。」
entries.en: Heaven does not grant good fortune—it destroys my fine minister."
entries.literal: Heaven does not grant good fortune—it destroys my fine minister."

entries.zh: 其見幸如此。
entries.en: Such was the favor shown him.
entries.literal: Such was the favor shown him.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，除安東臨川王諮議參軍。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Shen was made advising officer in the establishment of Pacification East Prince of Linchuan.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Shen was made advising officer in the establishment of Pacification East Prince of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 天嘉三年，遷征北諮議參軍，兼廷尉監。
entries.en: In the third year of Tianjia (562), he was promoted to advising officer of the northern expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianjia, he was promoted to advising officer of the Northern Expedition and concurrently supervisor of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 五年，除鎮東諮議參軍，兼起部郎。
entries.en: In year 5, he was made advising officer of the eastern expedition and concurrently initiating officer in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: In year 5, he was made advising officer of the Eastern Expedition and concurrently initiating officer in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 出為戎昭將軍、江乘令，甚有治績。
entries.en: He went out as general of martial splendor and magistrate of Jiangcheng; his governance had outstanding results.
entries.literal: He went out as General of Martial Splendor and magistrate of Jiangcheng—his governance had outstanding results.

entries.zh: 入為尚書金部郎。
entries.en: He entered court as gold section director in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He entered court as Gold Section Director in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 遷左民郎，以公事免。
entries.en: He was promoted to director for the people on the left and removed from office for public affairs.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Director for the People on the left; removed from office for public affairs.

entries.zh: 太建初，起為貞威將軍、征南鄱陽王諮議參軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taijian he was summoned as general of firm prestige and advising officer of the southern expedition Prince of Poyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was summoned as General of Firm Prestige and advising officer of the Southern Expedition Prince of Poyang.

entries.zh: 九年，除秣陵令，在職以清能見紀，有白雀巢于縣庭。
entries.en: In year 9, he was made magistrate of Moling; in office he was recorded for integrity and ability, and a white sparrow nested in the county courtyard.
entries.literal: In year 9, he was made magistrate of Moling; in office he was recorded for integrity and ability, and a white sparrow nested in the county courtyard.

entries.zh: 秩滿，頃之，預東宮賓客，尋兼東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: When his term ended, shortly thereafter he joined the eastern-palace guest staff; soon he also served concurrently as eastern-palace communicating affairs attendant.
entries.literal: When his term ended, shortly thereafter he joined the eastern-palace guest staff; soon he also served concurrently as eastern-palace communicating affairs attendant.

entries.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍，舍人如故。
entries.en: Promoted to extraordinary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, attendant post as before.
entries.literal: Promoted to Extraordinary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, attendant post as before.

entries.zh: 梁元帝承制，起為開遠將軍，遷鎮西外兵記室參軍。
entries.en: When Liang's Emperor Yuan assumed the provisional mandate, Shen was summoned as general who opens the distance and promoted to recorder in the outer military staff of the army on the western wall.
entries.literal: When Liang's Emperor Yuan assumed the provisional mandate, Shen was summoned as General Who Opens the Distance and promoted to recorder in the outer military staff of the Army on the Western Wall.

entries.zh: 及侯景寇郢州，申隨都督王僧辯據巴陵，每進籌策，皆見行用。
entries.en: When Hou Jing attacked Yingzhou, Shen followed commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he advanced was adopted.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing attacked Yingzhou, Shen followed Commander Wang Sengbian in holding Baling; every plan he advanced was adopted.

entries.zh: 僧辯歎曰：「此生要鞬汗馬，或非所長，若使撫眾守城，必有奇績。」
entries.en: Sengbian sighed and said, "This man wants the saddle and a sweating horse—perhaps not his strength; if one had him pacify troops and hold a city, there would surely be extraordinary achievement."
entries.literal: Sengbian sighed and said: "This man wants the saddle and a sweating horse—perhaps not his strength; if one had him pacify troops and hold a city, there would surely be extraordinary achievement."

entries.zh: 僧辯之討陸納也，申在軍中，于時賊眾奄至，左右披靡，申躬蔽僧辯，蒙楯而前，會裴之橫救至，賊乃退，僧辯顧申而笑曰：「仁者必有勇，豈虛言哉！」
entries.en: When Sengbian campaigned against Lu Na, Shen was in the army; at that time the rebel masses suddenly arrived and those left and right were scattered; Shen personally shielded Sengbian, covered himself with a shield and went forward; when Pei Zhiheng's rescue arrived, the rebels withdrew. Sengbian looked back at Shen and laughed, saying, "The humane surely have courage—is this an empty saying!"
entries.literal: When Sengbian campaigned against Lu Na, Shen was in the army; at that time the rebel masses suddenly arrived, those left and right were scattered; Shen personally shielded Sengbian, covered himself with a shield and went forward; when Pei Zhiheng's rescue arrived, the rebels then withdrew. Sengbian looked back at Shen and laughed, saying: "The humane surely have courage—is this an empty saying!"

entries.zh: 除散騎侍郎。
entries.en: He was made scattered-cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: He was made Scattered Cavalry Attendant.

entries.zh: 紹泰初，遷儀同侯安都從事中郎。
entries.en: At the beginning of Shaotai, he was promoted to retainer to Hou Andu with ceremonial parity to the three offices.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shaotai, he was promoted to Retainer to Hou Andu with ceremonial parity to the Three Offices.

entries.zh: 申歷事三帝，內掌機密，至於倉卒之閒，軍國大事，指麾斷決，無有滯留。
entries.en: Shen served three emperors and inwardly held confidential affairs; even in hurried moments, on great affairs of army and state, his direction and decisions had no delay.
entries.literal: Shen served three emperors and inwardly held confidential affairs; even in hurried moments, on great affairs of army and state, his direction and decisions had no delay.

entries.zh: 子琇嗣，官至太子舍人。
entries.en: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to eastern-palace attendant.
entries.literal: His son Xiu succeeded him and rose to eastern-palace attendant.

entries.zh: 初，後主為始興王所傷，及瘡愈而自慶，置酒於後殿，引江總以下，展樂賦詩，醉而命喜。
entries.en: Earlier Houzhu had been wounded by the Prince of Shixing. When his wounds healed he celebrated alone, set wine in the rear hall, summoned Jiang Zong and others, spread music and composed verse, and when drunk called for Xi.
entries.literal: Earlier, Houzhu had been wounded by the Prince of Shixing; when his sores healed he celebrated by himself, set wine in the rear hall, summoned Jiang Zong and others below, spread music and composed verse, and when drunk summoned Xi.

entries.zh: 于時山陵初畢，未及踰年，喜見之不懌，欲諫而後主已醉，喜升階，陽為心疾，仆于階下，移出省中。
entries.en: The imperial tomb had only just been completed and a full year had not yet passed. Xi was displeased and wished to remonstrate, but Houzhu was already drunk. Xi mounted the steps, feigned heart trouble, collapsed on the steps, and was carried out of the secretariat.
entries.literal: At that time the imperial tomb had only just been completed and not yet a full year had passed. Xi, displeased at seeing this, wished to remonstrate but Houzhu was already drunk. Xi mounted the steps, feigned heart illness, fell on the steps below, and was moved out of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 後主醒，乃疑之，謂江總曰：「我悔召毛喜，知其無疾，但欲阻我懽宴，非我所為，故姦詐耳。」
entries.en: When Houzhu woke he grew suspicious and said to Jiang Zong, "I regret calling Mao Xi. I know he is not ill—he only wanted to spoil my feast. That is not my way; he is deceitful."
entries.literal: When Houzhu woke he grew suspicious and said to Jiang Zong: "I regret summoning Mao Xi. I know he has no illness—he only wished to block my merry feast. That is not what I would do; he is deceitful."

entries.zh: 乃與司馬申謀曰：「此人負氣，吾欲將乞鄱陽兄弟聽其報讎，可乎？」
entries.en: He then plotted with Sima Shen and said, "This man is proud. I want to hand him to the Poyang brothers to let them take revenge—is that acceptable?"
entries.literal: He then plotted with Sima Shen, saying: "This man is proud. I wish to hand him over to the Poyang brothers to let them take revenge—is that acceptable?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「終不為官用，願如聖旨。」
entries.en: He replied, "He will never serve the state again. I bow to Your Majesty's will."
entries.literal: He replied: "In the end he will not serve the state. I wish it as Your Majesty commands."

entries.zh: 傅縡爭之曰：「不然。
entries.en: Fu Zai objected, "That will not do.
entries.literal: Fu Zai contested this, saying: "That will not do.

entries.zh: 若許報讎，欲置先皇何地？」
entries.en: If you allow revenge, where does that leave the late emperor?"
entries.literal: If revenge is granted, where does that leave the late emperor?"

entries.zh: 後主曰：「當乞一小郡，勿令見人事耳。」
entries.en: Houzhu said, "Give him a small commandery and keep him from court affairs."
entries.literal: Houzhu said: "He shall be begged off to a small commandery and not allowed to see state affairs."

entries.zh: 乃以喜為永嘉內史。
entries.en: Xi was then made interior minister of Yongjia.
entries.literal: Xi was then made interior minister of Yongjia.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：宗元饒夙夜匪懈，濟務益時。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Zong Yuanrao never slackened from dawn to night, aiding affairs and benefiting the age.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Zong Yuanrao from dawn to night never slackened, aiding affairs and benefiting the age.

entries.zh: 司馬申清恪在朝，攻苦立行，加之以忠節，美矣。
entries.en: Sima Shen was pure and strict at court, toiling in hardship to establish his conduct; with loyal integrity added, he was admirable.
entries.literal: Sima Shen was pure and strict in court, toiling at hardship to establish conduct, and with loyal integrity added—beautiful indeed.

entries.zh: 毛喜深達事機，匡贊時主。
entries.en: Mao Xi deeply understood circumstances and aided the ruler of his time.
entries.literal: Mao Xi deeply understood circumstances and aided the ruler of the age.

entries.zh: 蔡徵聰敏才贍，而擅權自躓，惜哉。
entries.en: Cai Zheng was clever and richly talented, yet by seizing power he tripped himself—a pity.
entries.literal: Cai Zheng was clever and talented in abundance, yet by seizing power he stumbled himself—pity.

entries.zh: 〔三〕 封文
entries.en: [3] Enfeoffed as
entries.literal: [3] Enfeoffed as

entries.en: (Shi)
entries.literal: (Shi)

entries.zh: 招縣伯 據百衲本南史本傳改。
entries.en: On "Zhao county marquis": emended per the patchwork Southern History biography.
entries.literal: Zhao county marquis—changed according to the biography in the patchwork Southern History.

entries.zh: 殿本南史亦作「始」。
entries.en: The Hall edition Southern History also reads "Shi".
entries.literal: The Hall edition Southern History also reads "Shi".

entries.zh: 張元濟校勘記云作「招」是。
entries.en: Zhang Yuanji's collation note says "Zhao" is correct.
entries.literal: Zhang Yuanji's collation note says reading "Zhao" is correct.

entries.zh: 南齊書州郡志文招縣屬廣州晉康郡。
entries.en: The Book of Southern Qi, Geography of Commanderies and Counties, places Wenzhao county in Jin'kang commandery of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: In the Geography of Commanderies and Counties in the Book of Southern Qi, Wenzhao county belonged to Jin'kang commandery of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 三八八頁同。
entries.en: Page 388 agrees.
entries.literal: Page 388 is the same.

entries.zh: 宗元饒，南郡江陵人也。
entries.en: Zong Yuanrao was from Jiangling in Nan commandery.
entries.literal: Zong Yuanrao was a man of Jiangling in Nan commandery.

entries.zh: 少好學，以孝敬聞。
entries.en: As a youth he loved learning and was known for filial respect.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning and was known for filial reverence.

entries.zh: 仕梁世，解褐本州主簿，遷征南府行參軍，仍轉外兵參軍。
entries.en: He entered service under Liang as chief clerk of his home province, was promoted to acting staff officer in the Expedition South headquarters, and then transferred to staff officer for external troops.
entries.literal: Serving under Liang, he first put off commoner clothes as chief clerk of his home province, was promoted to acting staff officer in the Expedition South headquarters, and then transferred to staff officer for external troops.

entries.zh: 及司徒王僧辯幕府初建，元饒與沛國劉師知同為主簿。
entries.en: When Minister of Works Wang Sengbian first established his headquarters, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei both served as chief clerks.
entries.literal: When Minister of Works Wang Sengbian first established his headquarters, Yuanrao and Liu Shizhi of Pei were both chief clerks.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，除晉陵令。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne by abdication, Yuanrao was appointed magistrate of Jinling.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Yuanrao was appointed magistrate of Jinling.

entries.zh: 入為尚書功論郎。
entries.en: He entered court as merit-evaluation gentleman in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He entered court as merit-evaluation gentleman in the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 使齊還，為廷尉正。
entries.en: After returning from an embassy to Qi, he became rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: After returning from an embassy to Qi, he became rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 遷太僕卿，領本邑大中正，中書通事舍人。
entries.en: He was promoted to chamberlain for the imperial stables and concurrently served as grand arbiter of his home district and communicating-affairs attendant in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was promoted to chamberlain for the imperial stables and concurrently held the posts of grand arbiter of his home district and communicating-affairs attendant in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 尋轉廷尉卿，加通直散騎常侍，兼尚書左丞。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to chamberlain for judicial review, given the additional title regular attendant of the scattered cavalry for direct service, and concurrently served as left assistant director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to chamberlain for judicial review, given the additional title regular attendant of the scattered cavalry for direct service, and concurrently served as left assistant director of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 時高宗初即位，軍國務廣，事無巨細，一以咨之，臺省號為稱職。
entries.en: At the time Emperor Xuan had just come to the throne, and military and state affairs were extensive; on matters great and small he consulted Yuanrao, and the central offices called him equal to his office.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan had just come to the throne, and military and state affairs were extensive; in matters great and small he consulted Yuanrao, and the central offices called him equal to his office.

entries.zh: 喜少好學，善草隸。
entries.en: Xi loved learning from youth and was skilled in cursive and clerical scripts.
entries.literal: Xi loved learning from youth and was skilled in cursive and clerical scripts.

entries.zh: 起家梁中衛西昌侯行參軍，尋遷記室參軍。
entries.en: He began his career as acting staff officer to the Marquis of Xichang, central guard under Liang, and soon was promoted to records staff officer.
entries.literal: He began his career as acting staff officer to the Marquis of Xichang, central guard under Liang, and soon was promoted to records staff officer.

entries.zh: 高祖素知於喜，及鎮京口，命喜與高宗俱往江陵，仍敕高宗曰：「汝至西朝，可諮稟毛喜。」
entries.en: The Founder had long known Xi, and when he was stationed at Jingkou he ordered Xi to go with Emperor Xuan to Jiangling, telling Emperor Xuan, "When you reach the western court, you may consult Mao Xi."
entries.literal: The Founder had long known Xi, and when he was stationed at Jingkou he ordered Xi to go with Emperor Xuan to Jiangling, telling Emperor Xuan: "When you reach the western court, you may consult Mao Xi."

entries.zh: 喜與高宗同謁梁元帝，即以高宗為領直，喜為尚書功論侍郎。
entries.en: Xi and Emperor Xuan together had audience with Emperor Yuan of Liang, who then made Emperor Xuan leader of direct service and Xi merit-evaluation gentleman attendant in the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Xi and Emperor Xuan together had audience with Emperor Yuan of Liang, who then made Emperor Xuan leader of direct service and Xi merit-evaluation gentleman attendant in the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 及江陵陷，喜及高宗俱遷關右。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Xi and Emperor Xuan were both moved west of the passes.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Xi and Emperor Xuan were both moved west of the passes.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，喜自周還，進和好之策，朝廷乃遣周弘正等通聘。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Xi returned from Zhou and offered a plan for peace; the court then sent Zhou Hongzheng and others to open diplomatic exchange.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Xi returned from Zhou and offered a plan for peace, and the court then sent Zhou Hongzheng and others to open diplomatic exchange.

entries.zh: 及高宗反國，喜於郢州奉迎。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan returned to Chen, Xi welcomed him at Yingzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan returned to the state, Xi respectfully welcomed him at Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 又遣喜入關，以家屬為請。
entries.en: Xi was again sent into the passes to request the return of Emperor Xuan's family.
entries.literal: Xi was again sent into the passes to make a request concerning the imperial family members.

entries.zh: 周冢宰宇文護執喜手曰：「能結二國之好者，卿也。」
entries.en: Yuwen Hu, Zhou's chief minister, took Xi by the hand and said, "The one who can bind friendship between our two states is you."
entries.literal: Yuwen Hu, Zhou's chief minister, took Xi by the hand and said: "The one who can bind friendship between the two states is you."

entries.zh: 仍迎柳皇后及後主還。
entries.en: He then escorted Empress Liu and the future Last Emperor back.
entries.literal: He then escorted Empress Liu and the future Last Emperor back.

entries.zh: 天嘉三年至京師，高宗時為驃騎將軍，仍以喜為府諮議參軍，領中記室。
entries.en: They reached the capital in Tianjia year 3. Emperor Xuan was then general of agile cavalry, and he made Xi advising staff officer in his headquarters and put him in charge of the central records office.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 3 they reached the capital. Emperor Xuan was then general of agile cavalry, and he made Xi advising staff officer in his headquarters and put him in charge of the central records office.

entries.zh: 府朝文翰，皆喜詞也。
entries.en: The headquarters' court documents were all drafted by Xi.
entries.literal: The headquarters' court documents were all Xi's wording.

entries.zh: 梁承聖初，高祖為南徐州刺史，召補迎主簿，尋授太學博士。
entries.en: At the start of Liang's Chengsheng era the Founder was inspector of South Xuzhou, summoned him as reception chief clerk, and soon made him erudite of the National University.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Chengsheng era the Founder was inspector of South Xuzhou, summoned him to fill the post of reception chief clerk, and soon made him erudite of the National University.

entries.zh: 天嘉初，遷始興王府法曹行參軍，歷外兵參軍事、尚書主客郎，所居以幹理稱。
entries.en: At the start of Tianjia he became acting legal-cadre staff officer in the Prince of Shixing's household, then outside-troops staff officer and master of guests in the masters of writing; wherever he served he was praised for able administration.
entries.literal: In the beginning of Tianjia he was moved to acting legal-cadre staff officer in the Prince of Shixing's household; he served through outside-troops staff officer and master of guests in the masters of writing, and wherever he was stationed he was praised for able administration.

entries.zh: 太建初，遷太子少傅丞、新安王主簿、通直散騎侍郎、晉安王功曹史、太子中舍人，兼東宮領直，中舍人如故。
entries.en: At the start of Taijian he was aide in the heir apparent's junior tutor's office, steward of the Prince of Xin'an, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on direct communication, registrar in the Prince of Jin'an's household, heir-apparent palace attendant, and concurrently head of straight service in the eastern palace; palace attendant as before.
entries.literal: In the beginning of Taijian he was moved to aide in the heir apparent's junior tutor's office, steward of the Prince of Xin'an, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry on direct communication, registrar in the Prince of Jin'an's household, heir-apparent palace attendant, and concurrently leader of straight service in the eastern palace; palace attendant as before.

entries.zh: 丁父憂去職，服闋，襲封新豐縣侯，授戎昭將軍、鎮右新安王諮議參軍。
entries.en: He left office to mourn his father; when mourning ended he inherited as Marquis of Xinfeng and was made sagely-dawn general and advising officer on the staff of the right-pacifying Prince of Xin'an.
entries.literal: He left office to mourn his father; when mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Xinfeng and was appointed sagely-dawn general and advising officer on the staff of the right-pacifying Prince of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，除給事黃門侍郎，兼中書舍人，典軍國機密。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Xi was appointed attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently secretariat attendant, managing confidential military and state affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Xi was appointed attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently secretariat attendant, managing confidential military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 高宗將議北伐，敕喜撰軍制，凡十三條，詔頒天下，文多不載。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was preparing to deliberate on the northern campaign, he ordered Xi to draft military regulations in thirteen articles, which were promulgated throughout the realm; much of the text is not preserved here.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to deliberate on the northern campaign, he ordered Xi to draft military regulations in thirteen articles, which were promulgated throughout the realm; much of the text is not preserved here.

entries.zh: 尋遷太子右衛率、右衛將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to right guard commandant of the heir apparent and right guard general.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to right guard commandant of the heir apparent and right guard general.

entries.zh: 以定策功，封東昌縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: For his merit in settling the succession plan, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang county with five hundred households.
entries.literal: For his merit in settling the plan, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongchang county with five hundred households.

entries.zh: 又以本官行江夏、武陵、桂陽三王府國事。
entries.en: In his existing post he also acted in charge of state affairs for the princely households of Jiangxia, Wuling, and Guiyang.
entries.literal: In his existing post he also acted in charge of state affairs for the princely households of Jiangxia, Wuling, and Guiyang.

entries.zh: 太建三年，丁母憂去職，詔追贈喜母庾氏東昌國太夫人，賜布五百匹，錢三十萬，官給喪事。
entries.en: In Taijian year 3 he left office to mourn his mother. An edict posthumously granted his mother, Lady Yu, the title Grand Lady of Dongchang State, bestowed five hundred bolts of cloth and three hundred thousand cash, and had officials provide for the funeral.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 3 he left office to mourn his mother. An edict posthumously granted Xi's mother, Lady Yu, the title Grand Lady of Dongchang State, bestowed five hundred bolts of cloth and three hundred thousand cash, and had officials provide for the funeral.

entries.zh: 又遣員外散騎常侍杜緬圖其墓田，高宗親與緬案圖指畫，其見重如此。
entries.en: The court also sent supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry Du Mian to draw a plan of her burial land; Emperor Xuan personally reviewed the plan with Mian and marked it out. Such was the esteem shown Xi.
entries.literal: The court also sent supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry Du Mian to draw a plan of her burial land; Emperor Xuan personally reviewed the plan with Mian and marked it out. Such was the esteem shown Xi.

entries.zh: 尋起為明威將軍，右衛、舍人如故。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as General of Manifest Prestige, retaining the right guard and secretariat attendant posts as before.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled as General of Manifest Prestige, retaining the right guard and secretariat attendant posts as before.

entries.zh: 改授宣遠將軍、義興太守。
entries.en: He was reassigned as General Who Proclaims Afar and administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: He was reassigned as General Who Proclaims Afar and administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 尋以本號入為御史中丞。
entries.en: Soon, with that same rank, he entered court as censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: Soon, with that same rank, he entered court as censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 服闋，加散騎常侍、五兵尚書，參掌選事。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and minister of the five arms, and shared control of official selection.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was additionally made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and minister of the five arms, and shared control of official selection.

entries.zh: 十二年，加侍中。
entries.en: In year 12 he was given additional palace attendant.
entries.literal: In year 12 he was given additional Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 十三年，授散騎常侍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: In year 13 he was appointed scattered-cavalry regular attendant and governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In year 13 he was appointed Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 遷吏部尚書，常侍如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of the masters of writing for personnel, regular attendant as before.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Personnel, regular attendant as before.

entries.zh: 及高宗崩，叔陵構逆，敕中庶子陸瓊宣旨，令南北諸軍，皆取喜處分。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted treason; an order had central palace attendant Lu Qiong proclaim the intent, ordering northern and southern armies alike to take Xi's disposition.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Shuling plotted treason; an order had Central Palace Attendant Lu Qiong proclaim the intent, ordering northern and southern armies alike to take Xi's disposition.

entries.zh: 賊平，又加侍中，增封并前九百戶。
entries.en: When the rebels were pacified he was again given additional palace attendant, his enfeoffment increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.
entries.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was again given additional Palace Attendant, his enfeoffment increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.

entries.zh: 至德元年，授信威將軍、永嘉內史，加秩中二千石。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhide (583) he was appointed trustworthy prestige general and interior administrator of Yongjia, with additional stipend of middle two thousand piculs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed Trustworthy Prestige General and Interior Administrator of Yongjia, with additional stipend of middle two thousand piculs.

entries.zh: 初，高宗委政於喜，喜亦勤心納忠，多所匡益，數有諫諍，事並見從，由是十餘年閒，江東狹小，遂稱全盛。
entries.en: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi also devoted his heart in loyal service, with much correction and benefit; he often remonstrated and his advice was followed—in more than ten years, though the Jiangdong realm was small, it was called fully flourishing.
entries.literal: At first Emperor Xuan entrusted government to Xi; Xi also devoted his heart in loyal service, with much correction and benefit; he often remonstrated and his advice was followed—in more than ten years, though the Jiangdong realm was small, it was called fully flourishing.

entries.zh: 唯略地淮北，不納喜謀，而吳明徹竟敗，高宗深悔之，謂袁憲曰：「不用毛喜計，遂令至此，朕之過也。」
entries.en: Only in seizing land north of the Huai did he not take Xi's advice; Wu Mingche was defeated in the end. Emperor Xuan deeply regretted it and told Yuan Xian, "Had I followed Mao Xi's plan, this would not have happened—it is my fault."
entries.literal: Only in seizing land north of the Huai did he not adopt Xi's plan; Wu Mingche in the end was defeated. Emperor Xuan deeply regretted it and said to Yuan Xian: "Not using Mao Xi's plan has brought matters to this—it is my fault."

entries.zh: 喜既益親，乃言無回避，而皇太子好酒德，每共幸人為長夜之宴，喜嘗為言，高宗以誡太子，太子陰患之，至是稍見疏遠。
entries.en: As Xi grew closer still, he spoke without reserve. Yet the heir apparent loved wine and nightly revels with his favorites. Xi often remonstrated; Emperor Xuan used this to warn the heir, who secretly resented him and by then had grown somewhat distant.
entries.literal: As Xi grew still closer, he spoke without holding back. Yet the heir apparent was fond of wine and revelry; every night he held long feasts with his favorites. Xi often spoke on it; Emperor Xuan used this to warn the heir, who secretly resented him; by then he was somewhat estranged.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗謂高宗曰：「我諸子皆以『伯』為名，汝諸兒宜用『叔』為稱。」
entries.en: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan, "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' in their style."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen once told Emperor Xuan: "All my sons take 'Bo' in their names; your sons should use 'Shu' in their style."

entries.zh: 高宗以訪于喜，喜即條牒自古名賢杜叔英、虞叔卿等二十餘人以啟世祖，世祖稱善。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and reported them to Emperor Wen, and Emperor Wen praised it.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan consulted Xi; Xi at once listed more than twenty famous men of antiquity such as Du Shuying and Yu Shuqing and reported them to Emperor Wen, and Emperor Wen praised it.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，廢帝沖昧，高宗錄尚書輔政，僕射到仲舉等知朝望有歸，乃矯太后令遣高宗還東府，當時疑懼，無敢措言。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor was young and ignorant; Emperor Xuan assumed the recorded affairs of the masters of writing as regent; vice director Dao Zhongju and others knew that court expectation had a direction and therefore forged an empress dowager order sending Emperor Xuan back to the eastern palace; at the time there was doubt and fear, and none dared speak.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor was young and ignorant; Emperor Xuan assumed the recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing as regent; Vice Director Dao Zhongju and others knew that court expectation had a direction and therefore forged an empress dowager order sending Emperor Xuan back to the eastern palace; at the time there was doubt and fear, and none dared speak.

entries.zh: 喜即馳入，謂高宗曰：「陳有天下日淺，海內未夷，兼國禍併鍾，萬邦危懼。
entries.en: Xi at once galloped in and told Emperor Xuan, "Chen has held the realm only a short time; within the seas it is not yet pacified; moreover national misfortune has struck together, and the myriad states are in peril and fear.
entries.literal: Xi at once galloped in and told Emperor Xuan: "Chen has held the realm only a short time; within the seas it is not yet pacified; moreover national misfortune has struck together, and the myriad states are in peril and fear.

entries.zh: 皇太后深惟社稷至計，令王入省，方當共康庶績，比德伊、周。
entries.en: The empress dowager deeply weighs the plan for the altars of soil and grain and has ordered the prince to enter the secretariat; we should together bring peace to the people's labors and match the virtue of Yi and Zhou.
entries.literal: The empress dowager deeply weighs the plan for the altars of soil and grain and has ordered the prince to enter the Secretariat; we should together bring peace to the people's labors and match the virtue of Yi and Zhou.

entries.zh: 今日之言，必非太后之意。
entries.en: Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent.
entries.literal: Today's words surely are not the empress dowager's intent.

entries.zh: 宗社之重，願加三思。
entries.en: The weight of the ancestral altars—please add further thought.
entries.literal: The weight of the ancestral altars—please add further thought.

entries.zh: 以喜之愚，須更聞奏，無使奸賊得肆其謀。」
entries.en: In my foolishness I must hear the matter reported again, and not let treacherous villains carry out their plot."
entries.literal: In my foolishness I must hear the matter reported again, and not let treacherous villains carry out their plot."

entries.zh: 竟如其策。
entries.en: It turned out as he had planned.
entries.literal: It turned out as he had planned.

entries.zh: 右衛將軍韓子高始與仲舉通謀，其事未發，喜請高宗曰：「宜簡選人馬，配與子高，并賜鐵炭，使脩器甲。」
entries.en: Right guard general Han Zigao at first conspired with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken out; Xi asked Emperor Xuan, "You should select men and horses, assign them to Zigao, and also grant iron and charcoal so he may repair weapons and armor."
entries.literal: Right Guard General Han Zigao at first conspired with Zhongju; the affair had not yet broken out; Xi asked Emperor Xuan: "You should select men and horses, assign them to Zigao, and also grant iron and charcoal so he may repair weapons and armor."

entries.zh: 高宗驚曰：「子高謀反，即欲收執，何為更如是邪？」
entries.en: Emperor Xuan was startled and said, "Zigao plots rebellion—we should at once seize him; why do this further?"
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan was startled and said: "Zigao plots rebellion—we should at once seize him; why do this further?"

entries.zh: 喜答曰：「山陵始畢，邊寇尚多，而子高受委前朝，名為杖順，然甚輕狷，恐不時授首，脫其稽誅，或愆王度。
entries.en: Xi replied, "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many; Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as holding to obedience, yet he is very frivolous and impetuous—I fear he will not promptly surrender his head; if we hasten to punish him, we may transgress royal measure.
entries.literal: Xi replied: "The imperial tomb has only just been completed and border enemies are still many; Zigao was entrusted by the former court and is known as holding to obedience, yet he is very frivolous and impetuous—I fear he will not promptly surrender his head; if we hasten to punish him, we may transgress royal measure.

entries.zh: 宜推心安誘，使不自疑，圖之一壯士之力耳。」
entries.en: You should push aside suspicion and peacefully entice him so he does not doubt himself; to take him is the strength of one stout warrior."
entries.literal: You should push aside suspicion and peacefully entice him so he does not doubt himself; to take him is the strength of one stout warrior."

entries.zh: 高宗深然之，卒行其計。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan deeply approved and in the end carried out the plan.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan deeply approved and in the end carried out the plan.

entries.zh: 及眾軍北伐，得淮南地，喜陳安邊之術，高宗納之，即日施行。
entries.en: When the mass of armies marched north and gained the lands south of the Huai, Xi presented methods for securing the border; Emperor Xuan adopted them and put them into effect that very day.
entries.literal: When the mass of armies marched north and gained the lands south of the Huai, Xi presented methods for securing the border; Emperor Xuan adopted them and put them into effect that very day.

entries.zh: 又問喜曰：「我欲進兵彭、汴，於卿意如何？」
entries.en: He again asked Xi, "I wish to advance troops to Peng and Bian—what do you think?"
entries.literal: He again asked Xi: "I wish to advance troops to Peng and Bian—what do you think?"

entries.zh: 喜對曰：「臣實才非智者，安敢預兆未然。
entries.en: Xi replied, "My talent is truly not that of the wise; how would I dare to foretell what has not yet happened?
entries.literal: Xi replied: "Your servant's talent is truly not that of the wise; how would I dare to foretell what has not yet happened?

entries.zh: 竊以淮左新平，邊氓未乂，周氏始吞齊國，難與爭鋒，豈以弊卒疲兵，復加深入。
entries.en: I privately think that south of the Huai has only just been pacified and the border people are not yet settled; Zhou has only begun to swallow Qi and is hard to contend with in the blade—how could one with worn troops and weary soldiers press the advance further?
entries.literal: I privately think that south of the Huai has only just been pacified and the border people are not yet settled; Zhou has only begun to swallow Qi and is hard to contend with in the blade—how could one with worn troops and weary soldiers press the advance further?

entries.zh: 且棄舟楫之工，踐車騎之地，去長就短，非吳人所便。
entries.en: Moreover to abandon the craft of boats and oars and tread the ground of chariots and horses is to leave the long for the short—not what men of Wu find convenient.
entries.literal: Moreover to abandon the craft of boats and oars and tread the ground of chariots and horses is to leave the long for the short—not what men of Wu find convenient.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為不若安民保境，寢兵復約，然後廣募英奇，順時而動，斯久長之術也。」
entries.en: In my foolish view it would be better to settle the people and secure the borders, let the weapons sleep and renew the covenant, then broadly recruit outstanding men and move according to the times—that is the method for long endurance."
entries.literal: In your servant's foolish view it would be better to settle the people and secure the borders, let the weapons sleep and renew the covenant, then broadly recruit outstanding men and move according to the times—that is the method for long endurance."

entries.zh: 高宗不從。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan did not follow him.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan did not follow him.

entries.zh: 後吳明徹陷周，高宗謂喜曰：「卿之所言，驗於今矣。」
entries.en: Later Wu Mingche was defeated by Zhou; Emperor Xuan told Xi, "What you said has been verified today."
entries.literal: Later Wu Mingche was defeated by Zhou; Emperor Xuan told Xi: "What you said has been verified today."

entries.zh: 徵美容儀，有口辯，多所詳究。
entries.en: Zheng was handsome and eloquent and had studied many fields deeply.
entries.literal: Zheng had fine looks and eloquence and investigated many subjects deeply.

entries.zh: 至於士流官宦，皇家戚屬，及當朝制度，憲章儀軌，戶口風俗，山川土地，問無不對。
entries.en: On gentry and officials, imperial kin, current institutions, statutes and ritual, household registers and customs, mountains, rivers, and land—whatever one asked, he answered correctly.
entries.literal: As to gentry and official families, imperial clansmen, current institutions, statutes and ritual norms, household registers and customs, mountains and rivers and land—ask and he had no wrong answer.

entries.zh: 然性頗便佞進取，不能以退素自業。
entries.en: Yet by nature he was given to flattery and advancement and could not rest in modest retirement.
entries.literal: Yet by nature he was rather given to flattery and advancement and could not make modest retirement his calling.

entries.zh: 初拜吏部尚書，啟後主借鼓吹，後主謂所司曰「鼓吹軍樂，有功乃授，蔡徵不自量揆，紊我朝章，然其父景歷既有締構之功，宜且如所啟，拜訖即追還」。
entries.en: When he was first made minister of personnel he asked Houzhu to lend him ceremonial music. Houzhu told the office, "Ceremonial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not know his place and confuses court rules—yet since his father Jingli helped found the state, grant it for now, but take it back as soon as the appointment rite is done."
entries.literal: When he was first appointed minister of personnel he memorialized Houzhu to borrow ceremonial music escort. Houzhu told the responsible office: "Ceremonial music is military music, granted only for merit. Cai Zheng does not measure himself and confuses our court regulations—yet since his father Jingli had merit in founding the state, it is fitting to grant as requested for now, but recall it immediately after the appointment ceremony."

entries.zh: 徵不脩廉隅，皆此類也。
entries.en: Zheng did not keep his conduct clean—this was typical.
entries.literal: Zheng did not cultivate moral corners—all was of this kind.

entries.zh: 隋文帝聞其敏贍，召見顧問，言輒會旨，然累年不調，久之，除太常丞。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his quick mind, summoned him for consultation, and his words always hit the mark—yet for years he received no post; after long delay he was made aide in the directorate of ceremonial affairs.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his keen ability, summoned him for consultation, and his words always met the point—yet for many years he received no posting; after long delay he was made aide in the directorate of ceremonial affairs.

entries.zh: 歷尚書民部儀曹郎，轉給事郎，〔五〕卒，時年六十七。
entries.en: He served as gentleman in the civil-affairs and ritual sections of the Masters of Writing, was transferred to Gentleman for Service, and died at sixty-seven.
entries.literal: He served through gentleman in the civil-affairs and ritual sections of the Masters of Writing, was transferred to Gentleman for Service, and died, aged sixty-seven.

entries.zh: 子翼，治尚書，官至司徒屬、德教學士。
entries.en: His son Yi studied the Documents and rose to clerk on the Three Dukes' staff and academician of virtuous instruction.
entries.literal: His son Yi studied the Documents and rose to clerk on the Three Dukes' staff and academician of virtuous instruction.

entries.zh: 入隋，為東宮學士。
entries.en: Under Sui he was an eastern-palace academician.
entries.literal: Entering Sui he was an eastern-palace academician.

entries.zh: 〔一〕 嘗隨父候吏部尚書到
entries.en: [1] Once when he followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao
entries.literal: [1] Once when he followed his father to call on the Minister of Personnel, Dao

entries.zh: （仲舉）
entries.en: (Zhongju)
entries.literal: (Zhongju)

entries.zh: 溉 據南史改。
entries.en: On "Gai": emended per the Southern History.
entries.literal: Gai—changed according to the Southern History.

entries.zh: 按到仲舉為到洽之子，見梁書到洽傳，未嘗為吏部。
entries.en: Dao Zhongju was Dao Qia's son; see the Book of Liang biography of Dao Qia—he never served as minister of personnel.
entries.literal: Comment: Dao Zhongju was the son of Dao Qia; see the biography of Dao Qia in the Book of Liang—he never served as minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 梁書到溉傳云溉以建安內史遷中書郎兼吏部。
entries.en: The Book of Liang biography of Dao Gai says he moved from interior minister of Jian'an to secretariat gentleman, concurrently minister of personnel.
entries.literal: The biography of Dao Gai in the Book of Liang says Gai moved from interior minister of Jian'an to secretariat gentleman, concurrently minister of personnel.

entries.zh: 又云梁武帝每與對棋，從夕達旦。
entries.en: It also says Emperor Wu of Liang played chess with him from evening until dawn.
entries.literal: It also says Emperor Wu of Liang played chess with him every time from evening until dawn.

entries.zh: 是「到仲舉」明為「到溉」之訛。
entries.en: Thus "Dao Zhongju" is plainly an error for "Dao Gai."
entries.literal: Thus "Dao Zhongju" is plainly an error for "Dao Gai."

entries.zh: 陳書卷二十九
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 29
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 29

entries.zh: 蕭濟 陸瓊 子從典 顧野王 傅縡 章華
entries.en: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; his son Congdian; Gu Yewang; Fu Zai; Zhang Hua
