entries.literal: Xiao Ji; Lu Qiong; his son Congdian; Gu Yewang; Fu Zai; Zhang Hua

entries.zh: 蕭濟字孝康，東海蘭陵人也。
entries.en: Xiao Ji, styled Xiaokang, came from Lanling in Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: Xiao Ji, styled Xiaokang, was a native of Lanling in Donghai.

entries.zh: 少好學，博通經史，諮梁武帝左氏疑義三十餘條，尚書僕射范陽張纘、太常卿南陽劉之遴並與濟討論，纘等莫能抗對。
entries.en: From boyhood he loved books and mastered the classics and histories. He put more than thirty questions on the Zuo Commentary before Liang's Emperor Wu; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, vice director of the masters of writing, and Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang, minister of ceremonies, debated them with him—and could not hold their ground.
entries.literal: From youth he loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories; he submitted more than thirty items of doubt in the Zuo Commentary to Liang's Emperor Wu, and the Masters of Writing for the People Zhang Zuan of Fanyang and the Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang both discussed them with Ji—Zuan and the others could not stand against him.

entries.zh: 解褐梁祕書郎，遷太子舍人。
entries.en: He entered service as a Liang secretariat gentleman, then became groom of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: On doffing coarse cloth he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 預平侯景之功，封松陽縣侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: He shared in the campaign that crushed Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang, with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: He took part in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang, fief five hundred households.

entries.zh: 及高祖作鎮徐方，以濟為明威將軍、征北長史。
entries.en: When the Founder was holding Xuzhou as his command, he made Ji bright-prestige general and chief secretary on the northern campaign staff.
entries.literal: When the Founder held the frontier post at Xuzhou, he made Ji Bright Prestige General and chief secretary on the northern campaign staff.

entries.zh: 承聖二年，徵為中書侍郎，轉通直散騎常侍。
entries.en: In Chengsheng year 2 (553) he was summoned as secretariat vice director, then made regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was summoned as Secretariat Vice Director and moved to regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 世祖為會稽太守，又以濟為宣毅府長史，遷司徒左長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，授侍中。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen succeeded, Ji was made palace attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Ji was made palace attendant.

entries.zh: 尋遷太府卿，丁所生母憂，不拜。
entries.en: Soon he was named grand steward of the imperial household, but mourning his birth mother he declined the appointment.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to grand steward of the imperial household; he mourned his birth mother and did not accept the post.

entries.zh: 濟毗佐二主，恩遇甚篤，賞賜加於凡等。
entries.en: Ji served two sovereigns with uncommon trust; rewards and gifts outstripped the usual measure.
entries.literal: Ji assisted two rulers and received favor of exceptional depth; rewards and gifts exceeded the common run.

entries.zh: 歷守蘭陵、陽羨、臨津、臨安等郡，所在皆著聲績。
entries.en: He governed in turn Lanling, Yangxian, Linjin, and Lin'an, and everywhere left a name for solid achievement.
entries.literal: In succession he held Lanling, Yangxian, Linjin, and Lin'an—wherever he went his reputation and achievement stood out.

entries.zh: 太建初，入為五兵尚書，與左僕射徐陵、特進周弘正、度支尚書王瑒、[1]散騎常侍袁憲俱侍東宮。
entries.en: At the start of Taijian (569) he entered court as minister of the five armies, and with left vice director Xu Ling, special emeritus Zhou Hongzheng, minister of revenue Wang Chang, [1] and scattered-cavalry regular attendant Yuan Xian he attended the eastern palace together.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he entered court as Minister of the Five Armies; together with Left Vice Director Xu Ling, Special Emeritus Zhou Hongzheng, Minister of Revenue Wang Chang, Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant Yuan Xian, he all attended the eastern palace.

entries.zh: 復為司徒長史。
entries.en: He again became chief secretary of the secretariat.
entries.literal: He again became chief secretary of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 尋授度支尚書，領羽林監。
entries.en: Soon he was made minister of revenue and also led the feathered forest guard.
entries.literal: Soon he was given Minister of Revenue and additionally led the Feathered Forest guard.

entries.zh: 遷國子祭酒，領羽林如故。
entries.en: He was moved to libationer of the national university while still leading the feathered forest.
entries.literal: He was moved to libationer of the National University, still leading the Feathered Forest as before.

entries.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫，兼安德宮衛尉。
entries.en: He was further made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon and concurrently defender of the secure virtue palace.
entries.literal: He was given the additional posts of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and concurrently Defender of the Secure Virtue Palace.

entries.zh: 尋遷仁威將軍、揚州長史。
entries.en: Soon he was made benevolent-prestige general and chief secretary of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to Benevolent Prestige General and chief secretary of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 高宗嘗敕取揚州曹事，躬自省覽，見濟條理詳悉，文無滯害，乃顧謂左右曰「我本期蕭長史長於經傳，不言精練繁劇，乃至於此」。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan once ordered the Yangzhou bureau papers brought for his own reading. Ji had arranged everything with meticulous clarity, the documents flowing without snag or tangle. The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "I expected Chief Secretary Xiao to shine in the classics—not that he would master tangled administration to this degree."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan once ordered the Yangzhou bureau records taken for his own inspection; seeing Ji's entries orderly and thorough, the documents without obstruction or harm, he turned to those beside him and said, "I had expected Chief Secretary Xiao to excel in the classics—who would have said he was this skilled at intricate administration as well?"

entries.zh: 遷祠部尚書，加給事中，復為金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: He was made minister of ceremonies, given the additional post of supervising censor, and again made grand master with golden seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: He was moved to Minister of Ceremonies, given the additional post of Supervising Censor, and again made Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 未拜而卒，時年六十六。
entries.en: Before he could take office he died, at sixty-six.
entries.literal: Before he could take up the appointment he died, aged sixty-six.

entries.zh: 詔贈本官，官給喪事。
entries.en: An edict granted his last office posthumously and supplied his funeral from the treasury.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously granted his last office and supplied funeral expenses from the government.

entries.zh: 瓊幼聰惠有思理，六歲為五言詩，頗有詞采。
entries.en: Qiong as a child was quick and thoughtful. At six he wrote pentasyllabic verse with real polish.
entries.literal: Qiong in childhood was clever and thoughtful; at six he composed pentasyllabic verse with considerable literary grace.

entries.zh: 大同末，雲公受梁武帝詔校定棋品，到溉、朱异以下並集，瓊時年八歲，於客前覆局，由是京師號曰神童。
entries.en: Near the end of Datong, Yungong received Emperor Wu of Liang's order to fix the grades of weiqi players. Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and the rest assembled; Qiong was eight and, before the guests, reconstructed a game from memory. The capital thereafter called him a prodigy.
entries.literal: At the end of Datong, Yungong received Liang's Emperor Wu's order to collate weiqi rankings; Dao Gai, Zhu Yi, and others below all gathered—Qiong was then eight sui and before the guests replayed a game from memory, whereupon the capital styled him a divine child.

entries.zh: 异言之武帝，有敕召見，瓊風神警亮，進退詳審，帝甚異之。
entries.en: Zhu Yi spoke of him to the throne, and an edict called him in. Qiong's presence was keen and luminous; he moved with careful grace. The emperor was deeply struck.
entries.literal: Yi spoke of him to the Emperor; an edict summoned him for audience. Qiong's bearing was alert and bright, his advance and retreat measured and careful—the Emperor marveled greatly.

entries.zh: 十一，丁父憂，毀瘠有至性，從祖襄歎曰「此兒必荷門基，所謂一不為少」。
entries.en: At eleven he mourned his father, wasting away with a grief that showed his deepest nature. His father's cousin Xiang sighed and said, "This boy will carry the clan. As they say, one such son is not too few."
entries.literal: At eleven he mourned his father; his wasting grief showed utmost filial nature. His father's cousin Xiang sighed and said, "This boy will surely bear up the house—what people call 'one is not too few.'"

entries.zh: 及侯景作逆，攜母避地于縣之西鄉，勤苦讀書，晝夜無怠，遂博學，善屬文。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Qiong took his mother to refuge in the county's western hamlets and read without rest by day or lamp by night, until he was broadly learned and sure with the brush.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he took his mother to refuge in the western township of the county, toiled at reading day and night without slack, and thereby became broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 及侯景之亂，野王丁父憂，歸本郡，乃召募鄉黨數百人，隨義軍援京邑。
entries.en: When Hou Jing's rebellion broke out, Yewang was mourning his father and went home; he then recruited several hundred men of his township and marched with the loyal army to relieve the capital.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing's turmoil came, Yewang was mourning his father and returned to his home commandery; he then recruited several hundred men of his native place and followed the loyal army to relieve the capital.

entries.zh: 野王體素清羸，裁長六尺，又居喪過毀，殆不勝衣，及杖戈被甲，陳君臣之義，逆順之理，抗辭作色，見者莫不壯之。
entries.en: Yewang had always been slight of build, barely six feet, and in mourning had wasted until his robes hung loose—yet when he took spear and donned armor, spoke of the bond between ruler and minister and the line between loyalty and rebellion, and flushed with defiance as he spoke, every witness felt his spirit rise.
entries.literal: Yewang's frame had always been slight and frail; he was barely six chi tall, and in mourning he had wasted beyond bearing clothes—yet when he took spear and donned armor, set forth the righteousness of ruler and minister and the principle of obedience and rebellion, and spoke with defiant color, all who saw him felt emboldened.

entries.zh: 京城陷，野王逃會稽，尋往東陽，與劉歸義合軍據城拒賊。
entries.en: When the capital fell, Yewang fled to Kuaiji, then went to Dongyang and joined Liu Guiyi in holding the city against the rebels.
entries.literal: When the capital fell, Yewang fled to Kuaiji, then went on to Dongyang, and with Liu Guiyi united armies to hold the city and resist the rebels.

entries.zh: 侯景平，太尉王僧辯深嘉之，使監海鹽縣。
entries.en: After Hou Jing was crushed, grand marshal Wang Sengbian praised him deeply and made him overseer of Haiyan county.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian praised him deeply and had him oversee Haiyan county.

entries.zh: 高祖作宰，為金威將軍、安東臨川王府記室參軍，尋轉府諮議參軍。
entries.en: When the Founder served as chief minister, Yewang became General of Golden Might and records staff officer in the household of the Prince of Linchuan, General Who Pacifies the East; soon he transferred to advising staff officer in the same household.
entries.literal: When the Founder served as chief minister, Yewang became General of Golden Might and records staff officer in the household of the Prince of Linchuan, General Who Pacifies the East; soon he transferred to advising staff officer in the same household.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，敕補撰史學士，尋加招遠將軍。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, an edict appointed him historiographical scholar; soon he was additionally made General Who Summons From Afar.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 1, an edict appointed him historiographical scholar; soon he was additionally made General Who Summons From Afar.

entries.zh: 光大元年，除鎮東鄱陽王諮議參軍。
entries.en: In Guangda year 1, he was appointed advising staff officer to the Prince of Poyang, General Who Guards the East.
entries.literal: In Guangda year 1, he was appointed advising staff officer to the Prince of Poyang, General Who Guards the East.

entries.zh: 太建二年，遷國子博士。
entries.en: In Taijian year 2, he was promoted to erudite of the National University.
entries.literal: In Taijian year 2, he was promoted to erudite of the National University.

entries.zh: 後主在東宮，野王兼東宮管記，本官如故。
entries.en: When Houzhu was in the Eastern Palace, Yewang concurrently handled Eastern Palace records, with his original post unchanged.
entries.literal: When Houzhu was in the Eastern Palace, Yewang concurrently handled Eastern Palace records, with his original post unchanged.

entries.zh: 六年，除太子率更令，尋領大著作，掌國史，知梁史事，兼東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: In year 6, he was appointed commandant of the heir apparent's carriage schedule, soon headed the grand authors, managed national history, oversaw Liang history, and concurrently served as communicating-affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: In year 6, he was appointed commandant of the heir apparent's carriage schedule, soon headed the grand authors, managed national history, oversaw Liang history, and concurrently served as communicating-affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 時宮僚有濟陽江總，吳國陸瓊，北地傅縡，吳興姚察，並以才學顯著，論者推重焉。
entries.en: Among the palace staff at the time were Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Lu Qiong of Wu commandery, Fu Zai of Beidi, and Yao Cha of Wuxing; all were distinguished for talent and learning, and commentators esteemed them.
entries.literal: Among the palace staff at the time were Jiang Zong of Jiyang, Lu Qiong of Wu commandery, Fu Zai of Beidi, and Yao Cha of Wuxing; all were distinguished for talent and learning, and commentators esteemed them.

entries.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，光祿卿，知五禮事，餘官並如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to Yellow Gate attendant gentleman and chamberlain for attendants, and put in charge of the five rites, with his remaining offices unchanged.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Yellow Gate attendant gentleman and chamberlain for attendants, and put in charge of the five rites, with his remaining offices unchanged.

entries.zh: 十三年卒，時年六十三。
entries.en: He died in year 13, aged sixty-three.
entries.literal: He died in year 13, aged sixty-three.

entries.zh: 詔贈祕書監。
entries.en: An edict posthumously presented him as director of the palace library.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously presented him as director of the palace library.

entries.zh: 至德二年，又贈右衛將軍。
entries.en: In Zhide year 2, he was also posthumously presented as right guard general.
entries.literal: In Zhide year 2, he was also posthumously presented as right guard general.

entries.zh: 永定中，州舉秀才。
entries.en: During Yongding, the province recommended him as a cultivated talent.
entries.literal: During Yongding, the province recommended him as a cultivated talent.

entries.zh: 天嘉元年，為寧遠始興王府法曹行參軍。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 1, he became acting legal-section staff officer in the household of the Prince of Shixing, General Who Pacifies the Distant.
entries.literal: In Tianjia year 1, he became acting legal-section staff officer in the household of the Prince of Shixing, General Who Pacifies the Distant.

entries.zh: 尋以本官兼尚書外兵郎，以文學轉兼殿中郎，滿歲為真。
entries.en: Soon, while keeping his existing post, he concurrently served as external-troops gentleman in the masters of writing; because of his literary ability, he transferred to concurrently serve as palace attendant gentleman, and after a full year the appointment became regular.
entries.literal: Soon, in his existing office, he concurrently served as external-troops gentleman in the masters of writing; because of his literary ability, he transferred to concurrently serve as palace attendant gentleman, and after a full year the appointment became regular.

entries.zh: 瓊素有令名，深為世祖所賞。
entries.en: Qiong had long had a fine reputation and was deeply appreciated by Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Qiong had long had a fine reputation and was deeply appreciated by Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 及討周迪、陳寶應等，都官符及諸大手筆，並中敕付瓊。
entries.en: During the campaigns against Zhou Di, Chen Baoying, and the others, all official tally dispatches and major compositions were entrusted to Qiong by inner decree.
entries.literal: During the campaigns against Zhou Di, Chen Baoying, and the others, all official tally dispatches and major compositions were entrusted to Qiong by inner decree.

entries.zh: 遷新安王文學，掌東宮管記。
entries.en: He was promoted to literary officer to the Prince of Xin'an and managed the records of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: He was promoted to literary officer to the Prince of Xin'an and managed the records of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 縡幼聰敏，七歲誦古詩賦至十餘萬言。
entries.en: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies totaling more than a hundred thousand words.
entries.literal: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies to more than a hundred thousand words.

entries.zh: 長好學，能屬文。
entries.en: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.
entries.literal: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.

entries.zh: 梁太清末，攜母南奔避難，俄丁母憂，在兵亂之中，居喪盡禮，哀毀骨立，士友以此稱之。
entries.en: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother; soon his mother died. Amid the chaos of war he observed mourning rites fully and wasted to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for it.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother to escape disaster; soon he suffered his mother's mourning; amid martial chaos he observed mourning rites fully, wasting away to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for this.

entries.zh: 後依湘州刺史蕭循，循頗好士，廣集墳籍，縡肆志尋閱，因博通群書。
entries.en: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou. Xun favored scholars and gathered many books; Zai read at will and came to master all fields of learning.
entries.literal: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou; Xun greatly favored scholars and broadly gathered canonical writings; Zai indulged his will in seeking and reading and thus mastered all books.

entries.zh: 王琳聞其名，引為府記室。
entries.en: Wang Lin heard his fame and made him recorder of the staff.
entries.literal: Wang Lin heard his fame and brought him in as recorder of the staff.

entries.zh: 琳敗，隨琳將孫瑒還都。
entries.en: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.
entries.literal: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.

entries.zh: 時世祖使顏晃賜瑒雜物，瑒託縡啟謝，詞理優洽，文無加點，晃還言之世祖，尋召為撰史學士。
entries.en: At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wen, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wen, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.

entries.zh: 除司空府記室參軍，遷驃騎安成王中記室，撰史如故。
entries.en: He was appointed record-office aide in the Minister of Works bureau, then became central record-office aide for Prince Ancheng, General of Agile Cavalry, while continuing to compile history.
entries.literal: He was appointed Record-Office Aide in the bureau of the Minister of Works, then transferred to Central Record-Office Aide for Prince Ancheng, General of Agile Cavalry, compiling history as before.

entries.zh: 及高宗為司徒，妙簡僚佐，吏部尚書徐陵薦瓊於高宗曰：「新安王文學陸瓊，見識優敏，文史足用，進居郎署，歲月過淹，左西掾缺，允膺茲選，階次小踰，其屈滯已積。」
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan was Minister of Works, he chose his staff with care. Minister of personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to him, saying, "Lu Qiong, literary officer to the Prince of Xin'an, is sharp in judgment and quick in mind; his command of letters and history is ample. He has lingered in the secretariat too long. The left western aide post stands open and he should fill it; only his rank is a little low, and the delay has pressed on him too long."
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was Minister of Works, he carefully selected his staff. Minister of personnel Xu Ling recommended Qiong to him, saying: "Lu Qiong, literary officer to the Prince of Xin'an, is sharp in judgment and quick in mind; his command of letters and history is ample. He has served in the secretariat too long. The left western aide post stands open and he should fill this selection; his rank order is slightly low, but his stagnation has already built up."

entries.zh: 乃除司徒左西掾。
entries.en: He was then made left western aide in the office of the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was then made left western aide in the office of the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，聘齊。
entries.en: Soon he also held regular attendant of the communicating scattered cavalry and went on embassy to Qi.
entries.literal: Soon he additionally held Regular Attendant of the Communicating Scattered Cavalry and went on embassy to Qi.

entries.zh: 太建元年，重以本官掌東宮管記。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian (569) he again held his former post and directed the eastern palace records.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian he again held his former office and directed records of the eastern palace.

entries.zh: 除太子庶子，兼通事舍人。
entries.en: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and also communicating affairs attendant.
entries.literal: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and additionally Communicating Affairs Attendant.

entries.zh: 轉中書侍郎、太子家令。
entries.en: He was moved to secretariat vice director and steward of the heir apparent's household.
entries.literal: He was moved to Secretariat Vice Director and steward of the heir apparent's household.

entries.zh: 長沙王為江州刺史，不循法度，高宗以王年少，授瓊長史，行江州府國事，帶尋陽太守。
entries.en: The Prince of Changsha, as inspector of Jiangzhou, ignored law and precedent. Emperor Xuan, judging him young, made Qiong his chief secretary to run the Jiangzhou establishment and the commandery's state affairs, and concurrently interior administrator of Xunyang.
entries.literal: The Prince of Changsha was inspector of Jiangzhou and did not follow law and measure; because the prince was young, Emperor Xuan gave Qiong the post of chief secretary to conduct the Jiangzhou establishment and state affairs of the commandery, and concurrently made him interior administrator of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 瓊以母老，不欲遠出，太子亦固請留之，遂不行。
entries.en: Qiong's mother was old and he did not wish to travel far; the heir apparent also pressed to keep him—and so he never went.
entries.literal: Qiong because his mother was old did not wish to go far; the heir apparent also firmly asked to keep him—so in the end he did not go.

entries.zh: 累遷給事黃門侍郎，領羽林監。
entries.en: He rose in turn to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard.
entries.literal: In succession he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard.

entries.zh: 轉太子中庶子，領步兵校尉。
entries.en: He was transferred to Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household and concurrently Commandant of Footsoldiers.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household and concurrently Commandant of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 又領大著作，撰國史。
entries.en: He also led the grand composition office and compiled the national history.
entries.literal: He additionally led the Grand Composition office and compiled the national history.

entries.zh: 後主即位，直中書省，掌詔誥。
entries.en: When Houzhu succeeded, Qiong served in the secretariat itself and directed edicts and proclamations.
entries.literal: When Houzhu took the throne, Qiong served directly in the Secretariat and directed edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 俄授散騎常侍，兼度支尚書，領揚州大中正。
entries.en: Soon he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, additionally minister of revenue, and grand rectifier of Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was given Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, additionally Minister of Revenue, and led the grand rectifier of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 至德元年，除度支尚書，參掌詔誥，并判廷尉、建康二獄事。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhide (583) he was made minister of revenue, shared in directing edicts and proclamations, and jointly judged cases in the court of review and the two Jiankang prisons.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was made Minister of Revenue, took part in directing edicts and proclamations, and jointly decided cases in the Court of Review and the two prisons of Jiankang.

entries.zh: 初，瓊父雲公奉梁武帝敕撰嘉瑞記，瓊述其旨而續焉，自永定訖于至德，勒成一家之言。
entries.en: Earlier his father Yungong, on Liang Emperor Wu's order, had begun the Record of Auspicious Omens. Qiong took up his aim and carried it on from Yongding through Zhide until it stood complete as a single tradition.
entries.literal: Earlier Qiong's father Yungong had received Liang's Emperor Wu's order to compile the Record of Auspicious Omens; Qiong set forth its intent and continued it, from Yongding down to Zhide, and brought it to completion as a work in one tradition.

entries.zh: 遷吏部尚書，著作如故。
entries.en: He was moved to minister of personnel while still directing composition.
entries.literal: He was moved to Minister of Personnel, his direction of composition unchanged.

entries.zh: 瓊詳練譜諜，雅鑒人倫，先是，吏部尚書宗元饒卒，右僕射袁憲舉瓊，高宗未之用也，至是居之，號為稱職，後主甚委任焉。
entries.en: Qiong knew genealogies and registers down to the last line and judged men with a quiet eye. When Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao died, right vice director Yuan Xian had recommended him, but Emperor Xuan had not yet appointed him. Now that he held the office, men said he filled it; Houzhu entrusted him without reserve.
entries.literal: Qiong was thorough in genealogies and registers and refined in judging human worth. Earlier, when Minister of Personnel Zong Yuanrao died, Right Vice Director Yuan Xian had recommended Qiong, but Emperor Xuan had not yet used him; now that he held the post, he was called fully equal to the charge, and Houzhu relied on him deeply.

entries.zh: 時有吳興章華，字仲宗，家世農夫，至華獨好學，與士君子遊處，頗覽經史，善屬文。
entries.en: At the time Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong, came from a farming family—he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, read widely in the classics and histories, and wrote well.
entries.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，乃遊嶺南，居羅浮山寺，專精習業。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's turmoil he fled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.
entries.literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing he then traveled to Lingnan, lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, and devoted himself to study.

entries.zh: 歐陽頠為廣州刺史，署為南海太守。
entries.en: Ouyang Wei, inspector of Guangzhou, appointed him administrator of Nanhai.
entries.literal: Ouyang Wei was inspector of Guangzhou and appointed him Administrator of Nanhai.

entries.zh: 及歐陽紇敗，乃還京師。
entries.en: When Ouyang He was defeated he returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When Ouyang He was defeated he then returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 太建中，高宗使吏部侍郎蕭引喻廣州刺史馬靖，令入子為質，引奏華與俱行。
entries.en: In the Taijian era, Emperor Xuan sent vice minister of personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany the mission.
entries.literal: In the Taijian era, Emperor Xuan sent vice minister of personnel Xiao Yin to instruct Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing to send in his son as hostage; Yin memorialized that Hua should accompany him.

entries.zh: 使還，而高宗崩。
entries.en: When the mission returned, Emperor Xuan had died.
entries.literal: When the mission returned, Emperor Xuan had died.

entries.zh: 後主即位，朝臣以華素無伐閱，競排詆之，乃除大市令，既雅非所好，乃辭以疾，鬱鬱不得志。
entries.en: When Houzhu took the throne, court gentlemen—Hua had no record of merit—competed to slander him; he was made director of the great market. That post ill suited him; he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and thwarted.
entries.literal: When Houzhu took the throne the court gentlemen, because Hua by nature had no meritorious background, all competed to slander him; he was therefore made director of the great market. As it was utterly not to his liking, he pleaded illness and resigned, depressed and without achieving his aim.

entries.zh: 禎明初，上書極諫，其大略曰：「昔高祖南平百越，北誅逆虜；
entries.en: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance, saying in gist: "In the past the Founder pacified the Hundred Yue in the south and punished the rebel captives in the north;
entries.literal: Early in Zhenming he submitted a memorial of extreme remonstrance; its general purport said: "In the past the Founder southward pacified the Hundred Yue and northward punished the rebellious captives;

entries.zh: 世祖東定吳會，西破王琳；
entries.en: Emperor Wen eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;
entries.literal: Emperor Wen eastward settled Wu and Kuaiji and westward broke Wang Lin;

entries.zh: 高宗克復淮南，辟地千里：三祖之功，亦至勤矣。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was utmost diligence.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan recovered Huainan and opened land for a thousand li—the merit of the three ancestors was also utmost diligence.

entries.zh: 陛下即位，于今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏，溺於嬖寵，惑於酒色，祠七廟而不出，拜妃嬪而臨軒，老臣宿將，棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪，昇之朝廷。
entries.en: Your Majesty has reigned five years without remembering the former emperor's hardships or fearing Heaven's mandate, drowning in favorites and delusion of wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, casting old ministers and veteran generals to the wilds and raising flatterers and slanderers.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not thinking of the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared, drowning in favorites, deluded by wine and sex, sacrificing at the seven temples yet not going out, bowing to consorts yet holding court, old ministers and veteran generals cast to the wild grass, flatterers and slanderous villains raised into the court.

entries.zh: 今疆埸日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改絃易張，臣見麋鹿復遊於姑蘇臺矣。」
entries.en: Now the frontier shrinks daily and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change course, I see deer roaming the Gusu Terrace again."
entries.literal: Now the frontier daily narrows and Sui troops press the border—if Your Majesty does not change the string and ease the bow, I see deer again roaming the Gusu Terrace."

entries.zh: 書奏，後主大怒，即日命斬之。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived Houzhu was furious and ordered him beheaded that same day.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted Houzhu was greatly enraged and that same day ordered him beheaded.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：蕭濟、陸瓊，俱以才學顯著，顧野王博極群典，傅縡聰警特達，並一代之英靈矣。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both shone for talent and learning; Gu Yewang mastered the canon; Fu Zai was brilliantly sharp—all spirits of an age.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Ji and Lu Qiong both for talent and learning were illustrious; Gu Yewang's learning exhausted the canon; Fu Zai was sharp-witted and outstanding—all spirits of an age.

entries.zh: 然縡不能循道進退，遂寘極網，悲夫！
entries.en: Yet Zai could not advance and withdraw by the Way and so fell into the utmost net—pitiable!
entries.literal: Yet Zai could not follow the Way in advancing and withdrawing and therefore fell into the utmost net—pitiable!

entries.zh: 陳書卷三十
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 30
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 30

entries.zh: 猛字智武，毅之弟也。
entries.en: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.
entries.literal: Meng, styled Zhiwu, was Yi's younger brother.

entries.zh: 幼俶儻，有幹略。
entries.en: In youth he was bold and unconventional, with capacity and stratagem.
entries.literal: In youth he was bold and unconventional and had capacity and stratagem.

entries.zh: 既壯，便弓馬，膽氣過人。
entries.en: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.
entries.literal: When grown he was skilled at bow and horse and his daring surpassed others.

entries.zh: 青溪之戰，猛自旦訖暮，與虜短兵接，殺傷甚眾。
entries.en: At Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.
entries.literal: In the battle at Qingxi, from dawn to dusk Meng fought the enemy at close quarters and killed and wounded very many.

entries.zh: 臺城陷，隨兄毅西上京，累戰功為威戎將軍。
entries.en: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital and by accumulated battle merit became might-of-armies general.
entries.literal: When the capital fell he followed his brother Yi west to the western capital; by accumulated battle merit he became Might-of-Armies General.

entries.zh: 梁
entries.en: Liang
entries.literal: Liang

entries.en: Collation variant: (An).
entries.literal: (An).

entries.zh: 南安侯蕭方矩為湘州刺史，〔一０〕以猛為司馬。
entries.en: Southern An marquis Xiao Fangju was made inspector of Xiangzhou [10], and Meng was made marshal of the staff.
entries.literal: Southern An Marquis Xiao Fangju was made Inspector of Xiangzhou, and Meng was made Marshal of the Staff.

entries.zh: 會武陵王蕭紀舉兵自漢江東下，方矩遣猛率湘、郢之卒，隨都督陸法和進軍以拒之。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following area commander Lu Fahe to resist him.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji raised troops from the Han River eastward, Fangju sent Meng to lead the troops of Xiang and Ying, following Area Commander Lu Fahe in an advance to resist him.

entries.zh: 時紀已下，樓船戰艦據巴江，爭峽口，相持久之，不能決。
entries.en: Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth in a long stalemate that could not be decided.
entries.literal: At the time Ji had already come downriver; tower ships and war vessels held the Ba River and contested the gorge mouth; they faced each other for a long stalemate and could not decide it.

entries.zh: 法和揣紀師老卒墯，因令猛率驍勇三千，輕舸百餘乘，衝流直上，出其不意，鼓譟薄之。
entries.en: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack and ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats straight upstream, taking him unawares with drums and clamor pressing close.
entries.literal: Fahe judged Ji's army weary and troops slack; he therefore ordered Meng to lead three thousand elite men in more than a hundred light boats upstream straight up, taking him unawares, with drums and clamor pressing close.

entries.zh: 紀眾倉卒驚駭，不及整列，皆棄艦登岸，赴水死者以千數。
entries.en: Ji's host was startled in haste and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.
entries.literal: Ji's host in haste was startled and had no time to form ranks; all abandoned their ships and went ashore, and those who drowned numbered in the thousands.

entries.zh: 時紀心膂數百人，猶在左右，猛將部曲三十餘人，蒙楯橫戈，直登紀舟，瞋目大呼，紀侍衛皆披靡，相枕藉不敢動。
entries.en: Several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side. Meng led more than thirty private troops, shields up and spears level, straight onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.
entries.literal: At the time several hundred of Ji's closest advisers were still at his side; Meng led more than thirty men of his private troops, shielded and spear in hand, straight up onto Ji's boat, glaring and shouting; Ji's attendants all scattered, lying atop one another and not daring to move.

entries.zh: 猛手擒紀父子三人，斬於舟中，盡收其船艦器械。
entries.en: Meng seized Ji and his father and son—three men—and beheaded them in the boat, and gathered all their ships and equipment.
entries.literal: Meng with his own hand seized Ji and his father and son, three men, and beheaded them in the boat; he gathered all their ships and equipment.

entries.zh: 以功授游騎將軍，封安山縣伯，邑一千戶。
entries.en: For merit he was made roaming-cavalry general and enfeoffed as baron of Anshan county with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: For merit he was made Roaming-Cavalry General and enfeoffed as Baron of Anshan County with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 仍進軍撫定梁、益，蜀境悉平。
entries.en: He still advanced to pacify Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.
entries.literal: He still advanced to pacify and settle Liang and Yi; the Shu borderlands were all pacified.

entries.zh: 軍還，遷持節、散騎常侍、輕車將軍、司州刺史，進爵為侯，增邑并前二千戶。
entries.en: When the army returned he was made bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, light-carriage general, and inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced to marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.
entries.literal: When the army returned he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Light-Carriage General, and Inspector of Sizhou; he was advanced in rank to Marquis and his fief was increased with the former to two thousand households.

entries.zh: 陳書卷三十一
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 31
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 31

entries.zh: 年十七，仕梁廷尉平。
entries.en: When seventeen he entered Liang service as an assistant in the Court Tribunal.
entries.literal: At seventeen he entered Liang service as an assistant in the Court Tribunal.

entries.zh: 不害長於政事，兼飾以儒術，名法有輕重不便者，輒上書言之，多見納用。
entries.en: Buhai excelled at governmental affairs and additionally adorned himself with Confucian learning. Where statutes and punishments had weights and measures that were inconvenient, he would submit a memorial, and many were adopted.
entries.literal: Buhai excelled at governmental affairs and additionally adorned himself with Confucian learning. Where statutes and punishments had weights and measures that were inconvenient, he would submit a memorial on them, and many were adopted.

entries.zh: 大同五年，遷鎮西府記室參軍，尋以本官兼東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: In Datong year 5 (539) he was moved to recorder of the staff in the Pacify-West establishment, and soon held his original post concurrently as communicating affairs attendant of the eastern palace.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was moved to recorder of the staff in the Pacify-West establishment, and soon held his original post concurrently as communicating affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 是時朝廷政事多委東宮，不害與舍人庾肩吾直日奏事，梁武帝嘗謂肩吾曰：「卿是文學之士，吏事非卿所長，何不使殷不害來邪？」
entries.en: At that time many court and government affairs were entrusted to the eastern palace. Buhai and attendant Yu Jianwu attended on the days of direct audience to report affairs. Emperor Wu of Liang once told Jianwu, "You are a man of letters; clerical business is not your strength—why not have Yin Buhai come instead?"
entries.literal: At that time many court and government affairs were entrusted to the Eastern Palace. Buhai with the attendant Yu Jianwu attended on the days of direct audience to report affairs. Emperor Wu of Liang once told Jianwu: "You are a man of letters; clerical business is not your strength—why not have Yin Buhai come instead?"

entries.zh: 其見知如此。
entries.en: He was known and valued to this degree.
entries.literal: He was known and valued to this degree.

entries.zh: 簡文又以不害善事親，賜其母蔡氏錦裙襦、氈席、被褥，單復畢備。
entries.en: Emperor Jianwen of Liang also, because Buhai was skilled at serving his parents, bestowed on his mother Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, quilts, and bedding, single and double layers all complete.
entries.literal: Emperor Jianwen of Liang also, because Buhai was skilled at serving his parents, bestowed on his mother the Lady Cai brocade skirts and jackets, felt mats, quilts, and bedding, single and double layers all complete.

entries.zh: 七年，除東宮步兵校尉。
entries.en: In year 7 he was made footsoldiers commandant of the eastern palace.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was made footsoldiers commandant of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 太清初，遷平北府諮議參軍，舍人如故。
entries.en: At the start of Taiqing (547) he was moved to staff adviser of the Pacify-North establishment, his attendant post remaining as before.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he was moved to staff adviser of the Pacify-North establishment, his attendant post remaining as before.

entries.zh: 司馬暠字文昇，河內溫人也。
entries.en: Sima Hao, styled Wensheng, came from Wen in Henei.
entries.literal: Sima Hao, styled Wensheng, was a native of Wen in Henei.

entries.zh: 高祖晉侍中、光祿勳柔之，以南頓王孫紹齊文獻王攸之後。
entries.en: His founding ancestor Rouzhi had been Jin palace attendant and director of the imperial secretariat; as grandson of the Prince of Nandun he descended from Prince Xian of Qi, Wang You.
entries.literal: His founding ancestor Rouzhi was Jin Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; as grandson of the Prince of Nandun he continued the line of Prince Xian of Qi, Wang You.

entries.zh: 父子產，梁尚書水部侍郎、岳陽太守，即梁武帝之外兄也。
entries.en: His father Zichan had been Liang minister of the masters of writing for the water bureau and administrator of Yueyang—the maternal elder brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
entries.literal: His father Zichan was Liang Minister of the Masters of Writing for the Water Bureau and Administrator of Yueyang—namely, the maternal elder brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.

entries.zh: 暠幼聰警，有至性。
entries.en: Hao was clever and alert from youth, with a deeply filial nature.
entries.literal: Hao from youth was clever and alert, with utmost nature.

entries.zh: 年十二，丁內艱，孺慕過禮，水漿不入口，殆經一旬。
entries.en: At twelve he mourned his mother; his grief exceeded the rites, and for nearly ten days he took no food or drink.
entries.literal: At age twelve he suffered inner mourning; childlike devotion exceeded the rites, and for nearly ten days he took no water or gruel.

entries.zh: 每至號慟，必致悶絕，內外親戚，皆懼其不勝喪。
entries.en: Each time he wailed he would faint; kin far and near feared he could not survive the mourning.
entries.literal: Whenever he wailed in grief he would fall into stupefaction; kin inside and outside all feared he could not endure the mourning.

entries.zh: 父子產每曉喻之，逼進饘粥，然毀瘠骨立。
entries.en: His father Zichan urged him repeatedly and forced gruel on him, yet he was wasted to the bone.
entries.literal: Father Zichan repeatedly exhorted him and forced him to take gruel, yet he was wasted to the bone.

entries.zh: 服闋，以姻戚子弟，預入問訊，梁武帝見暠羸瘦，歎息良久，謂其父子產曰；
entries.en: When mourning ended he entered audience as a kinsman by marriage. Emperor Wu of Liang saw how thin Hao was, sighed long, and said to Zichan:
entries.literal: When mourning ended, as a kinsman by marriage and a younger clansman he was admitted to audience; Emperor Wu of Liang saw Hao emaciated, sighed a long while, and said to his father Zichan:

entries.zh: 「昨見羅兒面顏憔悴，使人惻然，便是不墜家風，為有子矣。」
entries.en: "Yesterday I saw Luo'er's haggard face and pitied him; he does not betray the family tradition—here is a true son."
entries.literal: "Yesterday I saw Luo'er's face haggard—it moves one to pity; he does not fall short of the family tradition—he is a son indeed."

entries.zh: 羅兒，即暠小字也。
entries.en: Luo'er was Hao's childhood name.
entries.literal: Luo'er was Hao's childhood name.

entries.zh: 釋褐太學博士，累遷正員郎。
entries.en: He began as erudite of the imperial academy and rose to regular attendant.
entries.literal: On first appointment he was Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀逾甚，廬于墓側，一日之內，唯進薄麥粥一升。
entries.en: When his father died his mourning was still more severe; he built a hut by the tomb and ate only one sheng of thin wheat gruel a day.
entries.literal: On father's mourning his grief-destruction was still more severe; he built a hut beside the tomb, and within a single day took only one sheng of thin wheat gruel.

entries.zh: 墓在新林，連接山阜，舊多猛獸，暠結廬數載，豺狼絕跡。
entries.en: The tomb was at Xinlin among hills once full of beasts; Hao kept his hut for years and wolves and jackals vanished.
entries.literal: The tomb was at Xinlin, adjoining mountain heights where formerly there were many fierce beasts; Hao built his hut for several years and wolves and jackals vanished.

entries.zh: 常有兩鳩棲宿廬所，馴狎異常，新林至今猶傳之。
entries.en: Two doves always roosted at the hut, unusually tame; Xinlin still tells of it.
entries.literal: Two turtledoves always roosted at the hut, tame beyond the ordinary; in Xinlin the tale is still told.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，不害從簡文入臺。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen of Liang into the Inner City.
entries.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Buhai followed Emperor Jianwen of Liang into the Inner City.

entries.zh: 及臺城陷，簡文在中書省，景帶甲將兵入朝陛見，過謁簡文。
entries.en: At the time, the Inner City fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat. Jing, in armor and leading troops, entered court for audience at the steps and passed by to pay respects to Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: When the Inner City fell, Emperor Jianwen was in the Secretariat. Jing, in armor and leading troops, entered court for audience at the steps and passed by to pay respects to Emperor Jianwen.

entries.zh: 景兵士皆羌、胡雜種，衝突左右，甚不遜，侍衛者不驚恐辟易，唯不害與中庶子徐摛侍側不動。
entries.en: Jing's troops were Qiang and Hu of mixed stock; they jostled those on either side with great insolence. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood unmoved at the emperor's side.
entries.literal: Jing's soldiers were all mixed breeds of Qiang and Hu; they charged left and right, very insolent. The guards were startled and gave way—only Buhai and palace attendant Xu Chi stood at the side unmoved.

entries.zh: 及簡文為景所幽，遣人請不害與居處，景許之，不害供侍益謹。
entries.en: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was confined by Jing, he sent someone to request that Buhai dwell with him; Jing assented, and Buhai waited on him with ever greater care.

entries.zh: 簡文夜夢吞一塊土，意甚不悅，以告不害，不害曰：「昔晉文公出奔，野人遺之塊，卒反晉國，陛下此夢，事符是乎？」
entries.en: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said, "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?"
entries.literal: Emperor Jianwen one night dreamed he swallowed a clod of earth and was very displeased. He told Buhai, and Buhai said: "In old times Duke Wen of Jin went into exile; a rustic gave him a clod, and in the end he returned to Jin. Your Majesty's dream—does the matter match this?"

entries.zh: 簡文曰：「若天有徵，冀斯言不妄。」
entries.en: Emperor Jianwen said, "If Heaven sends a sign, I hope these words are not in vain."
entries.literal: Emperor Jianwen said: "If Heaven sends a sign, I hope these words are not in vain."

entries.zh: 梁元帝立，以不害為中書郎，兼廷尉卿，因將家屬西上。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne, he made Buhai a Secretariat gentleman and concurrently director of the Court Tribunal, and thus led his household west.

entries.zh: 江陵之陷也，不害先於別所督戰，失母所在。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, Buhai was elsewhere directing battle and lost track of where his mother was.
entries.literal: At the fall of Jiangling, Buhai was first at another place directing battle and lost track of where his mother was.

entries.zh: 于時甚寒，冰雪交下，老弱凍死者填滿溝塹‵不害行哭道路，遠近尋求，無所不至，遇見死人溝水中，即投身而下，扶捧閱視，舉體凍濕，水漿不入口，號泣不輟聲，如是者七日，始得母屍。
entries.en: The season was bitterly cold; ice and snow fell together, and the old and weak who had frozen to death filled ditches and moats. Buhai walked the roads weeping and searched near and far without rest. Whenever he came upon a corpse in a ditch or stream he threw himself down, lifted and examined the body, his whole person frozen and soaked. He took no food or drink, and his cries never ceased. After seven days thus he found his mother's corpse.
entries.literal: The season was bitterly cold; ice and snow fell together, and the old and weak who had frozen to death filled ditches and moats. Buhai walked the roads weeping and searched near and far, going everywhere. Whenever he came upon a corpse in a ditch or stream he threw himself down, lifted and examined the body; his whole person was frozen and soaked. He took no food or drink, and his cries never ceased. After seven days thus he found his mother's corpse.

entries.zh: 不害憑屍而哭，每舉音輒氣絕，行路無不為之流涕。
entries.en: Buhai leaned on the corpse and wept; each time he raised his voice he would lose breath. Every passerby on the road shed tears for him.
entries.literal: Buhai leaned on the corpse and wept; each time he raised his voice he would lose breath. Passersby on the road none but shed tears for him.

entries.zh: 即於江陵權殯，與王裒、庾信俱入長安，自是蔬食布衣，枯槁骨立，見者莫不哀之。
entries.en: He then held a temporary burial at Jiangling and, with Wang Pou and Yu Xin, entered Chang'an. From then on he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, wasting away until he was skin and bone; all who saw him pitied him.
entries.literal: He then held a temporary burial at Jiangling and, with Wang Pou and Yu Xin, entered Chang'an. From then on he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, wasting away until he was skin and bone; all who saw him pitied him.

entries.zh: 不佞字季卿，不害弟也。
entries.en: Buning, styled Jiqing, was Buhai's younger brother.
entries.literal: Buning, styled Jiqing, was Buhai's younger brother.

entries.zh: 少立名節，居父喪以至孝稱。
entries.en: In youth he established a reputation for integrity; in mourning his father he was famed for supreme filial piety.
entries.literal: In youth he established a reputation for integrity; in his father's mourning he was famed for supreme filial piety.

entries.zh: 好讀書，尤長吏術，仕梁起家為尚書中兵郎，甚有能稱。
entries.en: He loved reading and especially excelled at the arts of office. Entering Liang service he began as director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat and was greatly praised for ability.
entries.literal: He loved reading and especially excelled at the arts of office. Entering Liang service he began as director of the central arms bureau in the Secretariat and was greatly praised for ability.

entries.zh: 梁元帝承制，授戎昭將軍、武陵王諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, he was appointed martial-proclamation general and staff adviser to the Prince of Wuling.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency, he was appointed martial-proclamation general and staff adviser to the Prince of Wuling.

entries.zh: 承聖初，遷武康令。
entries.en: At the start of Chengsheng (552) he was moved to magistrate of Wukang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Chengsheng he was moved to magistrate of Wukang.

entries.zh: 時兵荒飢饉，百姓流移，不佞巡撫招集，繈負而至者以千數。
entries.en: At the time arms and famine ravaged the land and the people drifted in flight. Buning toured to comfort and gather them in, and those who came swaddled on the back numbered in the thousands.
entries.literal: At the time arms and famine ravaged the land and the people drifted in flight. Buning toured to comfort and gather them in, and those who came swaddled on the back numbered in the thousands.

entries.zh: 會江陵陷，而母卒，道路隔絕，久不得奔赴，四載之中，晝夜號泣，居處飲食，常為居喪之禮。
entries.en: It happened that Jiangling fell and his mother died; roads were cut off and for long he could not hurry to the funeral. Within four years he wept and cried day and night; in dwelling, food, and drink he constantly kept the rites of mourning.
entries.literal: It happened that Jiangling fell and his mother died; roads were cut off and for long he could not hurry to the funeral. Within four years he wept and cried day and night; in dwelling, food, and drink he constantly kept the rites of mourning.

entries.zh: 高祖受禪，起為戎昭將軍，除婁令。
entries.en: When the Founder received the abdication, he was summoned as martial-proclamation general and made magistrate of Lou.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was summoned as martial-proclamation general and made magistrate of Lou.

entries.zh: 至是，第四兄不齊始之江陵，迎母喪柩歸葬。
entries.en: By then his fourth elder brother Buqi had first gone to Jiangling and brought back their mother's coffin for burial.
entries.literal: By then his fourth elder brother Buqi had first gone to Jiangling and brought back their mother's coffin for burial.

entries.zh: 不佞居處之節，如始聞問，若此者又三年。
entries.en: Buning's observances in dwelling were as at the first news of bereavement; he did so for another three years.
entries.literal: Buning's observances in dwelling were as at the first news of bereavement; he did so for another three years.

entries.zh: 身自負土，手植松柏，每歲時伏臘，必三日不食。
entries.en: He himself carried earth and with his hands planted pine and cypress. At each year's seasonal sacrifices at the solstices he would fast for three days without eating.
entries.literal: He himself carried earth and with his hands planted pine and cypress. At each year's seasonal sacrifices at the solstices he would fast for three days without eating.

entries.zh: 太清之亂，親屬散亡，貞於江陵陷沒，暠逃難番禺，貞母出家於宣明寺。
entries.en: In the turmoil of Taiqing kin scattered. Zhen was caught in Jiangling's fall; Hao fled to Panyu, and Zhen's mother took the tonsure at Xuaming Temple.
entries.literal: In the turmoil of Taiqing, kin scattered and fled. Zhen was lost in the fall of Jiangling; Hao fled in distress to Panyu, and Zhen's mother took the tonsure at Xuaming Temple.

entries.zh: 及高祖受禪，暠還鄉里，供養貞母，將二十年。
entries.en: When the Founder received the abdication, Hao returned to his home district and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.
entries.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Hao returned to his home district and supported Zhen's mother for nearly twenty years.

entries.zh: 太建五年，貞乃還朝，除智武府外兵參軍事。
entries.en: In Taijian year 5 (573) Zhen then returned to court and was made outside arms officer on the staff of the Intelligent Martial establishment.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian Zhen then returned to court and was made outside arms officer on the staff of the Intelligent Martial establishment.

entries.zh: 俄遷尚書駕部郎中，尋遷侍郎。
entries.en: Shortly he was moved to director of the chariot bureau in the Secretariat, and soon moved to vice director.
entries.literal: Shortly he was moved to director of the chariot bureau in the Secretariat, and soon moved to vice director.

entries.zh: 及始興王叔陵為揚州刺史，引祠部侍郎阮卓為記室，辟貞為主薄，貞不得已乃行。
entries.en: When the Prince of Shixing Shuling was made inspector of Yangzhou, he brought in vice director of the rites bureau Ruan Zhuo as recorder of the staff and summoned Zhen as chief clerk; Zhen had no choice but to go.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Shixing Shuling was made inspector of Yangzhou, he brought in vice director of the rites bureau Ruan Zhuo as recorder of the staff and summoned Zhen as chief clerk; Zhen had no choice but to go.

entries.zh: 尋遷府錄事參軍，領丹陽丞。
entries.en: Soon he was moved to recorder of the staff and concurrently magistrate of Danyang.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to recorder of the staff and concurrently magistrate of Danyang.

entries.zh: 貞度叔陵將有異志，因與卓自疏於王，每有宴遊，輒辭以疾，未嘗參預，叔陵雅欽重之，弗之罪也。
entries.en: Zhen judged that Shuling would harbor a rebellious intent and therefore, with Zhuo, kept themselves distant from the prince. Whenever there were feasts or outings he would plead illness and never take part. Shuling had long held him in esteem and did not blame him.
entries.literal: Zhen judged that Shuling would harbor a rebellious intent and therefore, with Zhuo, kept themselves distant from the prince. Whenever there were feasts or outings he would plead illness and never take part. Shuling had long held him in esteem and did not blame him.

entries.zh: 俄而高宗崩，叔陵肆逆，府僚多相連逮，唯貞與卓獨不坐。
entries.en: Shortly Emperor Xuan died and Shuling committed outrage; many staff members were implicated and seized—only Zhen and Zhuo were not charged.
entries.literal: Shortly Emperor Xuan died and Shuling committed outrage; many staff members were implicated and seized—only Zhen and Zhuo were not charged.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，除尚書左民郎，不就，後為始興王諮議參軍，兼尚書右丞，遷東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made director of the left bureau for the people in the Secretariat but did not accept; later he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing and concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat, then moved to communicating affairs attendant of the eastern palace.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made director of the left bureau for the people in the Secretariat but did not accept; later he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing and concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat, then moved to communicating affairs attendant of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 及世祖崩，廢帝嗣立，高宗為太傅，錄尚書輔政，甚為朝望所歸。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor succeeded; Emperor Xuan was grand tutor and recorded affairs of the Secretariat to assist in government, and was greatly where court expectation turned.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the Deposed Emperor succeeded; Emperor Xuan was Grand Tutor and recorded affairs of the Secretariat to assist in government, and was greatly where court expectation turned.

entries.zh: 不佞素以名節自立，又受委東宮，乃與僕射到仲舉、中書舍人劉師知、尚書右丞王暹等，謀矯詔出高宗。
entries.en: Buning had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the eastern palace. He therefore joined vice director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Buning had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the Eastern Palace. He therefore joined Vice Director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 眾人猶豫，未敢先發，不佞乃馳詣相府，面宣敕，令相王還第。
entries.en: The others hesitated and dared not move first; Buning galloped to the chief minister's residence, proclaimed the edict in person, and ordered the prince regent back to his mansion.
entries.literal: The crowd hesitated and did not dare act first; Buning then galloped to the chief minister's residence and in person proclaimed the edict, ordering the prince regent to return to his mansion.

entries.zh: 及事發，仲舉等皆伏誅，高宗雅重不佞，特赦之，免其官而已。
entries.en: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buning and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.
entries.literal: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buning and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，以為軍師始興王諮議參軍，加招遠將軍。
entries.en: At the time, emperor Xuan took the throne, he was made staff adviser and military strategist to the Prince of Shixing, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he was made staff adviser and military strategist to the Prince of Shixing, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general.

entries.zh: 尋除大匠卿，未拜，加員外散騎常侍，又兼尚書右丞。
entries.en: Soon he was made grand master of works but did not accept the appointment; he was additionally made irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and again concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Soon he was made grand master of works but did not accept the appointment; he was additionally made irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and again concurrently right vice director in the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 俄遷通直散騎常侍，右丞如故。
entries.en: Shortly he was moved to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, his vice directorship remaining as before.
entries.literal: Shortly he was moved to direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, his vice directorship remaining as before.

entries.zh: 太建五年卒，時年五十六。
entries.en: In Taijian year 5 (573) he died, aged fifty-six.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian he died, aged fifty-six.

entries.zh: 詔贈祕書監。
entries.en: An edict posthumously made him director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: An edict posthumously made him director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太建八年，自周還朝，高宗特降殊禮，賞錫有加。
entries.en: In Taijian year 8, returning from Zhou, Emperor Xuan granted him special honors and rich rewards.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Taijian, returning from Zhou to court, Emperor Xuan especially granted him special honors and increased rewards.

entries.zh: 除宜都王諮議參軍事，徙安德宮長秋卿、通直散騎常侍、太中大夫、司州大中正，卒于官。
entries.en: He was made staff adviser to the Prince of Yidu, then director of the long autumn office of the Andre palace, direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, grand master of the palace, and senior rectifier of Sizhou, and died in office.
entries.literal: He was made Staff Adviser to the Prince of Yidu, moved to Director of the Long Autumn Office of the Andre Palace, Direct and Upright Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace, and Senior Rectifier of Sizhou, and died in office.

entries.zh: 有集十卷。
entries.en: He left a collection in ten fascicles.
entries.literal: He had a collection in ten fascicles.

entries.zh: 高宗世有太原王知玄者，僑居于會稽剡縣，居家以孝聞。
entries.en: In Emperor Xuan's time Wang Zhixuan of Taiyuan lived as a sojourner in Yan county, Kuaiji, and was famed at home for filial piety.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xuan's time there was one Wang Zhixuan of Taiyuan, sojourning in Yan county of Kuaiji commandery; at home he was famed for filial piety.

entries.zh: 及丁父憂，哀毀而卒，高宗嘉之，詔改其所居清苦里為「孝家里」云。
entries.en: When his father died he mourned himself to death; Emperor Xuan praised him and renamed his lane, Qingku, "Filial Home Lane."
entries.literal: When he suffered father's mourning he died from grief-destruction; Emperor Xuan commended this and ordered that the lane where he lived, Qingku Lane, be changed to "Filial Home Lane."

entries.zh: 謝貞字元正，陳郡陽夏人，晉太傅安九世孫也。
entries.en: Xie Zhen, styled Yuanzheng, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Jin grand tutor An.
entries.literal: Xie Zhen, styled Yuanzheng, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.

entries.zh: 祖綏，[1]梁著作佐郎、太子舍人。
entries.en: His grandfather Sui [1] served Liang as editorial assistant and crown prince attendant.
entries.literal: His grandfather Sui, was a Liang editorial assistant and crown prince attendant.

entries.zh: 父藺，正員外郎，兼散騎常侍。
entries.en: His father Lin was a regular outside gentleman who also served as irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: His father Lin was a regular outside gentleman and concurrently irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 祖綏 「綏」梁書、南史謝藺傳並作「經」。
entries.en: On "Zu Sui": the character sui in the Book of Liang and the Southern History biography of Xie Lin both read jing.
entries.literal: Zu Sui: the character "sui" in the Book of Liang and the Southern History biography of Xie Lin both read "jing."

entries.zh: 後主仍詔貞入掌中宮管記，遷南平王友，加招遠將軍，掌記室事。
entries.en: Houzhu then had Zhen enter to manage the inner-palace records, made him friend to the Prince of Nanping, added recruit-the-distance general, and put him in charge of recorder affairs.
entries.literal: Houzhu then ordered Zhen to enter and take charge of the inner palace records, moved him to friend of the Prince of Nanping, with the additional rank of recruit-the-distance general, in charge of recorder affairs.

entries.zh: 府長史汝南周確新除都官尚書，請貞為讓表，後主覽而奇之。
entries.en: The establishment's chief recorder Zhou Que of Runan had newly been made director of the capital offenses bureau in the Secretariat and asked Zhen to draft his letter of declination; Houzhu read it and marveled.
entries.literal: The establishment's chief recorder Zhou Que of Runan had newly been made director of the capital offenses bureau in the Secretariat and asked Zhen to draft his letter of declination; Houzhu read it and marveled.

entries.zh: 嘗因宴席問確曰：「卿表自製邪？」
entries.en: Once at a banquet he asked Que, "Did you compose the memorial yourself?"
entries.literal: Once at a banquet he asked Que: "Did you compose the memorial yourself?"

entries.zh: 確對曰：「臣表謝貞所作。」
entries.en: Que replied, "Your servant's memorial was composed by Xie Zhen."
entries.literal: Que replied: "Your servant's memorial was composed by Xie Zhen."

entries.zh: 後主因敕舍人施文慶曰[2]：「謝貞在王處，未有祿秩，可賜米百石。」
entries.en: Houzhu thereupon ordered attendant Shi Wenqing [2], "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; grant him one hundred piculs of grain."
entries.literal: Houzhu thereupon ordered the attendant Shi Wenqing, [to say]: "Xie Zhen at the prince's establishment has no salary or rank; one hundred piculs of grain may be granted."

entries.zh: 至德三年，以母憂去職。
entries.en: In Zhide year 3 (585) he left office on his mother's mourning.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhide he left office on his mother's mourning.

entries.zh: 頃之，敕起還府，仍加招遠將軍，掌記室。
entries.en: Shortly an edict recalled him to the establishment and again added recruit-the-distance general, in charge of the recorder's office.
entries.literal: Shortly an edict recalled him to the establishment and again added recruit-the-distance general, in charge of the recorder's office.

entries.zh: 貞累啟固辭，敕報曰：「省啟具懷，雖知哀煢在疚，而官俟得才，禮有權奪，可便力疾還府也。」
entries.en: Zhen repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining. The edict in reply said, "I have read your memorial and take your meaning. Though I know your solitary grief lies in affliction, offices await the able and rites allow expedient suspension; you may force yourself despite illness and return to the establishment."
entries.literal: Zhen repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining. The edict in reply said: "I have read your memorial and take your meaning. Though I know your solitary grief lies in affliction, offices await the able and rites allow expedient suspension; you may force yourself despite illness and return to the establishment."

entries.zh: 貞哀毀羸瘠，終不能之官舍。
entries.en: Zhen's mourning had wasted him to emaciation; in the end he could not go to the government offices.
entries.literal: Zhen's mourning had wasted him to emaciation; in the end he could not go to the government offices.

entries.zh: 時尚書右丞徐祚、尚書左丞沈客卿俱來候貞，見其形體骨立，祚等愴然歎息，徐喻之曰：「弟年事已衰，禮有恆制，小宜引割自全。」
entries.en: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him, "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."
entries.literal: At the time right vice director Xu Zuo and left vice director Shen Keqing of the Secretariat both came to visit Zhen. Seeing his frame wasted to bone standing alone, Zuo and the rest sighed in sorrow. Xu admonished him: "Brother, your years are already advanced; rites have a constant measure—you should slightly restrain your cutting grief and preserve yourself."

entries.zh: 貞因更感慟，氣絕良久，二人涕泣，不能自勝，憫默而出。
entries.en: Zhen thereupon was moved to grief again and for long lost breath; the two men wept and could not master themselves, and went out in silent pity.
entries.literal: Zhen thereupon was moved to grief again and for long lost breath; the two men wept and could not master themselves, and went out in silent pity.

entries.zh: 祚謂客卿曰：「信哉，孝門有孝子。」
entries.en: Xu said to Keqing, "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."
entries.literal: Xu said to Keqing: "It is true—a house of filial piety has a filial son."

entries.zh: 客卿曰：「謝公家傳至孝，士大夫誰不仰止，此恐不能起，如何？」
entries.en: Keqing said, "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"
entries.literal: Keqing said: "The Xie house transmits utmost filial piety; which scholar-official does not look up to it? I fear he cannot rise—what then?"

entries.zh: 吏部尚書吳興姚察與貞友善，及貞病篤，察往省之，問以後事，貞曰：「孤子舋禍所集，將隨灰壤。
entries.en: Minister of personnel Yao Cha of Wuxing was friendly with Zhen. When Zhen's illness grew critical, Cha went to visit him and asked about affairs after death. Zhen said, "This orphaned son has gathered calamity upon himself and will soon follow dust and earth.
entries.literal: Minister of Personnel Yao Cha of Wuxing was friendly with Zhen. When Zhen's illness grew critical, Cha went to visit him and asked about affairs after death. Zhen said: "This orphaned son has gathered calamity upon himself and will soon follow dust and earth.

entries.zh: 族子凱等粗自成立，已有疏付之，此固不足仰塵厚德。
entries.en: My clansman Kai and the rest have roughly established themselves; I have already left a written instruction with them—this truly is not enough to bear up your thick virtue.
entries.literal: My clansman Kai and the rest have roughly established themselves; I have already left a written instruction with them—this truly is not enough to bear up your thick virtue.

entries.zh: 即日迷喘，時不可移，便為永訣。
entries.en: Today I am lost in gasping breath; the time cannot be shifted—let this be a final parting.
entries.literal: Today I am lost in gasping breath; the time cannot be shifted—let this be a final parting.

entries.zh: 弱兒年甫六歲，名靖，字依仁，情累所不能忘，敢以為託耳。」
entries.en: My weak son is just six years old; his name is Jing, his style Yiren—the ties of feeling I cannot forget; I venture to entrust him to you."
entries.literal: My weak son is just six years old; his name is Jing, his style Yiren—the ties of feeling I cannot forget; I venture to entrust him to you."

entries.zh: 是夜卒，敕賻米一百斛，布三十匹。
entries.en: That night he died. An edict granted one hundred hu of grain for funeral expenses and thirty bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: That night he died. An edict granted one hundred hu of grain for funeral expenses and thirty bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 後主問察曰：「謝貞有何親屬？」
entries.en: Houzhu asked Cha, "What kin does Xie Zhen have?"
entries.literal: Houzhu asked Cha: "What kin does Xie Zhen have?"

entries.zh: 察因啟曰：「貞有一子年六歲。」
entries.en: Cha thereupon reported, "Zhen has one son, six years old."
entries.literal: Cha thereupon reported: "Zhen has one son, six years old."

entries.zh: 即有敕長給衣糧。
entries.en: Thereupon an edict long supplied clothing and grain.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict long supplied clothing and grain.

entries.zh: 初，貞之病亟也，遺疏告族子凱曰：「吾少罹酷罰，十四傾外蔭，十六鍾太清之禍，流離絕國，二十餘載。
entries.en: Earlier, when Zhen's illness was critical, he left a written instruction telling his clansman Kai, "I in youth suffered harsh punishment; at fourteen I lost the shelter of kin outside, and at sixteen I met the calamity of Taiqing, drifting in exile and cut off from my state for more than twenty years.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhen's illness was critical, he left a written instruction telling his clansman Kai: "I in youth suffered harsh punishment; at fourteen I lost the shelter of kin outside, and at sixteen I met the calamity of Taiqing, drifting in exile and cut off from my state for more than twenty years.

entries.zh: 號天蹐地，遂同有感，得還侍奉，守先人墳墓，於吾之分足矣。
entries.en: I cried to heaven and stamped the earth and shared the grief of all who feel; to return and serve and guard my forefathers' tombs is enough for my portion.
entries.literal: I cried to heaven and stamped the earth, and thus shared in the grief of all who feel; to return and serve, to guard my forefathers' tombs—for my portion that is enough.

entries.zh: 不悟朝廷採拾空薄，累致清階，縱其殞絕，無所酬報。
entries.en: I did not realize the court would gather up my emptiness and thinness and repeatedly raise me to clear ranks; even if I die utterly, there is nothing with which to repay.
entries.literal: I did not realize the court would gather up my emptiness and thinness and repeatedly raise me to clear ranks; even if I die utterly, there is nothing with which to repay.

entries.zh: 今在憂棘，晷漏將盡，斂手而歸，何所多念。
entries.en: Now in the thorns of mourning the clepsydra's drip is nearly spent; I fold my hands and return—what is there to think much upon?
entries.literal: Now in the thorns of mourning the clepsydra's drip is nearly spent; I fold my hands and return—what is there to think much upon?

entries.zh: 氣絕之後，若直棄之草野，依僧家尸陀林法，是吾所願，正恐過為獨異耳。
entries.en: After I die, if the body is simply left in the wild per the Buddhist charnel-ground practice, that is my wish—I only fear it would seem too odd.
entries.literal: After the breath is cut off, if one simply abandons [the body] in the wild, following the Buddhist dharma of the charnel ground, that is my wish—only I fear it would be too singular.

entries.zh: 可用薄板周身，載以靈車，覆以葦席，坎山而埋之。
entries.en: Wrap the body in thin boards, carry it on a funeral cart, cover it with a reed mat, and bury it in a hillside grave.
entries.literal: Thin boards may be used all around the body, carried on a spirit carriage, covered with reed matting, and buried in a mountain hollow.

entries.zh: 又吾終尠兄弟，無他子孫，靖年幼少，未閑人事，但可三月施小床，設香水，盡卿兄弟相厚之情，即除之，無益之事，勿為也。」
entries.en: I have few brothers and no other heirs; Jing is young and knows nothing of the world. For three months only, set out a small couch and incense to show your brotherly bond, then put them away—do not do anything needless."
entries.literal: Moreover I ultimately have few brothers and no other descendants; Jing is young and does not yet understand affairs—only for three months set out a small couch and incense, fulfilling your brothers' mutual affection, then remove them; do not do useless things.

entries.zh: 初，貞在周嘗侍趙王讀，王即周武帝之愛弟也，厚相禮遇。
entries.en: Earlier, while Zhen was in Zhou, he served as reader to the Zhao prince, Emperor Wu of Zhou's beloved younger brother, who treated him with great courtesy.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhen was in Zhou he once attended the Zhao Prince in study; the prince was the beloved younger brother of Emperor Wu of Zhou and treated him with great courtesy.

entries.zh: 王嘗聞左右說貞每獨處必晝夜涕泣，因私使訪問，知貞母年老，遠在江南，乃謂貞曰：「寡人若出居藩，當遣侍讀還家供養。」
entries.en: The prince heard from attendants that Zhen wept day and night whenever alone. He sent privately to inquire and learned Zhen's mother was old and far off in the south. He told Zhen, "If I am posted to my fief, I shall send you home to support her."
entries.literal: The prince once heard attendants say that whenever Zhen was alone he wept day and night; he therefore privately sent to inquire and learned that Zhen's mother was old and far away in the southland, and then said to Zhen: "If I go out to reside in my fief, I shall send the reader home to support [your mother]."

entries.zh: 後數年，王果出，因辭見，面奏曰：「謝貞至孝而母老，臣願放還。」
entries.en: Years later the prince was indeed posted out. On leave he memorialized in person: "Xie Zhen is deeply filial and his mother is old; I ask that he be released."
entries.literal: Several years later the prince indeed went out; on taking leave he memorialized face to face, saying: "Xie Zhen is supremely filial and his mother is old; your servant wishes to release him."

entries.zh: 帝奇王仁愛而遣之，因隨聘使杜子暉還國。
entries.en: The emperor admired the prince's kindness and let Zhen go; he returned with the envoy Du Zihui.
entries.literal: The emperor marveled at the prince's kindness and released him, and he returned to the state with the envoy Du Zihui.

entries.zh: 所有文集，值兵亂多不存。
entries.en: His collected writings were mostly lost in the wars.
entries.literal: His collected writings, because of the military turmoil, for the most part did not survive.

entries.zh: 承聖中，除太子庶子。
entries.en: In the Chengsheng era he was made junior tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the Chengsheng era he was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，隨例入關，而梁室屠戮太子，瘞殯失所，暠以宮臣，乃抗表周朝，求還江陵改葬，辭甚酸切。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell he went to the north as others did. The Liang house had slaughtered the crown prince and left the burial lost; as a palace officer Hao submitted a bold memorial to Zhou to return and rebury him, in words very bitter.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell he followed the usual course into the Pass; the Liang house slaughtered the crown prince and burial was lost, and Hao as a palace officer therefore submitted a bold memorial to the Zhou court requesting return to Jiangling for reburial—the wording was very bitter.

entries.zh: 周朝優詔答曰：「昔主父從戮，孔車有長者之風，彭越就誅，欒布得陪臣之禮。
entries.en: Zhou replied graciously: "When Zhufu Yan was executed, Kong Che showed an elder's bearing; when Peng Yue was put to death, Luan Bu received a subject's rites.
entries.literal: The Zhou court replied with a gracious edict, saying: "In old times when Zhufu Yan followed execution, Kong Che had an elder's bearing; when Peng Yue met execution, Luan Bu received a subject's rites.

entries.zh: 庶子鄉國已改，猶懷送往之情，始驗忠貞，方知臣道，即敕荊州，以禮安厝。」
entries.en: Though the junior tutor's country has changed, he still feels the duty of escorting the dead—thus loyalty and subjecthood are proved; let Jingzhou bury him with full rites."
entries.literal: Though the Junior Tutor's native state has changed, he still cherishes the feeling of seeing one off on the journey—only thus is loyalty tested and the way of the subject known; let Jingzhou at once bury him with rites."

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「夫聖人之德，何以加於孝乎！」
entries.en: Confucius said, "Of the sage's virtue, what can be added to filial piety!"
entries.literal: Confucius said: "Of the sage's virtue, what can be added to filial piety!"

entries.zh: 孝者百行之本，人倫之至極也。
entries.en: Filial piety is the root of the hundred conduct, the utmost of human relations.
entries.literal: Filial piety is the root of the hundred conduct, the utmost of human relations.

entries.zh: 凡在性靈，孰不由此。
entries.en: Every sentient being draws on this root.
entries.literal: All who possess a sentient nature—who does not proceed from this?

entries.zh: 若乃奉生盡養，送終盡哀，或泣血三年，絕漿七日，思蓼莪之慕切，追顧復之恩深，或德感乾坤，誠貫幽顯，在於歷代，蓋有人矣。
entries.en: Whether in fully sustaining life in nurture or fully mourning at the send-off, in weeping blood for three years or abstaining from gruel for seven days, in the keen longing of "The Mugwort" or the deep grace of a parent's watchful care, or in virtue that moves heaven and earth and sincerity that pierces the hidden and manifest—in every age there have surely been such men.
entries.literal: As for fully sustaining life in nurture and fully mourning at the send-off, or weeping blood for three years and abstaining from gruel for seven days, thinking with the keen longing of "The Mugwort" and pursuing the deep grace of looking back in care, or virtue moving heaven and earth and sincerity penetrating the hidden and manifest—in every age, surely there have been such men.

entries.zh: 陳承梁室喪亂，風漓化薄，及跡隱閻閭，無聞視聽，今之採綴，以備闕云。
entries.en: Chen inherited Liang's age of mourning and turmoil; customs dissolved and transformation grew thin, and when traces lay hidden in lanes and alleys they went unheard. What is gathered here is to supply what is lacking.
entries.literal: Chen inherited Liang's age of mourning and turmoil; customs were dissolving and transformation grew thin, and when traces lay hidden in lanes and alleys they went unheard by sight or hearing. What is gathered here now is to supply what is lacking.

entries.zh: 告臨川郡士庶：昔西京為盛，信、越背誕；
entries.en: To the people of Linchuan: In old days the Western Capital stood in glory, yet Xin and Yue turned traitor;
