entries.literal: To the gentry and commoners of Linchuan commandery: In ancient times the Western Capital flourished, yet Xin and Yue turned disloyal;

entries.zh: 東都中興，萌、寵違戾。
entries.en: when the Eastern Capital rose again, Yin and Chong broke faith.
entries.literal: when the Eastern Capital revived, Yin and Chong defied allegiance.

entries.zh: 是以鷹鸇競逐，效醢極誅，自古有之，其來尚矣。
entries.en: So hawk and eagle hunt one another, and the extreme penalty of mincing has been known from of old—its roots run deep.
entries.literal: Therefore hawk and eagle contend in pursuit, and punishments of mincing extend to execution—since antiquity this has existed, and its origins are very old.

entries.zh: 逆賊周迪，本出輿臺，有梁喪亂，暴掠山谷。
entries.en: The rebel Zhou Di sprang from humble ranks; in Liang's collapse he plundered the hills.
entries.literal: The rebel Zhou Di was originally of low station; in Liang's time of ruin he ravaged the mountain valleys.

entries.zh: 我高祖躬率百越，師次九川，濯其泥沙，假以毛羽，裁解豚佩，仍剖獸符，[4]卵翼之恩，方斯莫喻。
entries.en: Our Founder himself led the hundred Yue, halted at the nine rivers, washed mud from them and lent them feather and down, cut the pig tally and split the beast seal—[4]—a brooding kindness none could match.
entries.literal: Our Founder personally led the hundred Yue, halted his army at the nine rivers, washed away their mud and sand and lent them feather and down, cut the pig tally and apportioned the beast seal fostering kindness such as no other equals.

entries.zh: 皇運肇基，頗布誠款，國步艱阻，竟微效力。
entries.en: When the dynasty's fortune began he showed good faith, yet in the state's distress he barely served.
entries.literal: When the imperial fortune first took root, he broadly showed good faith, yet amid the state's hard straits he scarcely rendered service.

entries.zh: 龍節繡衣，藉王爵而御下，熊旗組甲，因地險而陵上。
entries.en: Dragon tally and embroidered robe let him rule from borrowed rank; bear banner and mail let him tower from rugged ground over his betters.
entries.literal: With dragon tally and embroidered robe he borrowed royal rank to rule those below; with bear banner and linked armor he relied on rugged ground to look down on his superiors.

entries.zh: 日者王琳始貳，蕭勃未夷，西結三湘，南通五嶺，衡、廣戡定，既安反側，江、郢紛梗，復生攜背，擁據一郡，苟且百心，志貌常違，言跡不副。
entries.en: When Wang Lin first wavered and Xiao Bo still stood, he tied to the three Xiang westward and the five ranges southward; Heng and Guang were quieted and rebels steadied, yet Jiang and Ying stirred again—he clutched one commandery with a hundred fickle hearts, face and deed ever at odds, word and trail never aligned.
entries.literal: When Wang Lin first turned disloyal and Xiao Bo was not yet pacified, he joined the three Xiang in the west and the five ranges in the south; when Heng and Guang were settled and the rebellious were calmed, the Jiang and Ying regions were again in turmoil and treachery rose anew—he held a single commandery, clinging to a hundred shifting hearts, his intent and bearing always at odds, his words and tracks never matching.

entries.zh: 特以新吳未靜，地遠兵彊，互相兼并，成其形勢。
entries.en: Only while Xinwu stayed unsettled and distant ground bred strong arms did mutual swallowing build his strength.
entries.literal: Only because Xinwu was not yet settled and the land was remote with strong troops did mutual swallowing make his power.

entries.zh: 收獲器械，俘虜士民，並曰私財，曾無獻捷。
entries.en: Arms he gathered, people he seized, and called it all private spoil—never once reporting victory to the throne.
entries.literal: He collected arms and gear and captured gentry and commoners, calling them all private property, and never once reported victory.

entries.zh: 時遣一介，終持兩端。
entries.en: When the court sent one envoy, he still straddled both sides.
entries.literal: When the court sent a single envoy, he always held to two sides.

entries.zh: 朝廷光大含弘，引納崇遇，遂乃位等三槐，任均四嶽，富貴隆赫，超絕功臣。
entries.en: The court, broad in mercy, drew him close with honor until he ranked with the Three Hushes and shared the Four Peaks' burden—wealth and title towering above every merit-holder.
entries.literal: The court in its vast forbearance drew him in with high honor; he then stood equal to the Three Hushes and shared duty with the Four Peaks—wealth and rank towering, surpassing all meritorious servants.

entries.zh: 加以出師逾嶺，遠相響援，按甲斷江，翻然猜拒。
entries.en: When armies crossed the hills he answered from afar; he held his men and barred the river, then turned sudden and defiant.
entries.literal: Moreover, when armies crossed the ranges he answered from afar; he held his troops and blocked the river, then suddenly turned suspicious and defiant.

entries.zh: 故司空愍公，敦以宗盟，情同骨肉，城池連接，勢猶脣齒，彭亡之禍，坐觀難作，階此舋故，結其黨與。
entries.en: The late lamented Minister of Works treated him as sworn kin, bone to bone; their walls touched, strength like lips and teeth—yet at Pengwang's ruin he only watched trouble grow, and on that grudge knit his faction.
entries.literal: The late Minister of Works, the Lamented Duke, treated him as kin by clan pact, close as flesh and bone; their walled cities adjoined, their strength like lips and teeth; yet at the disaster of Pengwang he sat and watched difficulty arise—on that grievance he bound his faction.

entries.zh: 于時北寇侵軼，西賊憑陵，屝屨糇糧，悉以資寇，爵號軍容，一遵偽黨。
entries.en: Northern raiders then pressed the frontier and western rebels leaned on the land; sandals and grain he fed the foe; rank and martial show he copied the rebel host.
entries.literal: At that time northern invaders pressed the borders and western rebels leaned on the land; sandals and grain he wholly supplied to the enemy; rank and military display he wholly followed the false party.

entries.zh: 及王師凱振，大定區中，天網恢弘，棄之度外，璽書綸誥，撫慰綢繆，冠蓋縉紳，敦授重疊。
entries.en: When the imperial host returned victorious and the realm was largely settled, heaven's net was wide and set him outside it—yet edict on edict soothed him, honors on honors from the girdled ranks.
entries.literal: When the imperial army returned in triumph and greatly settled the realm, the heavenly net was broad and cast him beyond its mesh; with imperial writs and edicts the court soothed him again and again; caps and girdles of office-holders were heaped upon him in layers.

entries.zh: 至於熊曇朗勦滅，豐城克定，蓋由儀同法𣰋之元功，安西周敷之效力，司勳有典，懋賞斯舊，惡直醜正，自為仇讎，悖禮姦謀，因此滋甚。
entries.en: The fall of Xiong Tanlang and Fengcheng came chiefly from Fading's founding merit and Fu's exertion—the Ministry of Awards keeps its rule and rich reward is ancient custom—yet he hated the upright, made enemies of the true, and against ritual and in secret plot grew worse still.
entries.literal: As for the slaughter of Xiong Tanlang and the taking of Fengcheng, that was chiefly the founding merit of Equal-in-Honor Fading and the exertion of pacifying-the-west Zhou Fu; the Ministry of Awards has its canon and rich reward is the old rule—yet he hated the upright and loathed the true, making himself their enemy; against ritual and in secret plot he therefore grew worse.

entries.zh: 徵出湓城，歷年不就，求遣侍子，累載未朝。
entries.en: Called from Pencheng, he would not come for years; asked for a son at court, the boy stayed away for years.
entries.literal: Summoned to leave Pencheng, for years he would not come; asked to send a son to attend court, for years the boy did not present himself.

entries.zh: 外誘逋亡，招集不逞，中調京輦，規冀非常。
entries.en: Outside he lured fugitives and gathered rowdies; inside he stirred the capital, scheming the unthinkable.
entries.literal: Outwardly he lured fugitives and gathered the ungoverned; inwardly he stirred the capital, scheming for the extraordinary.

entries.zh: 擅斂征賦，罕歸九府，擁遏二賈，害及四民。
entries.en: He taxed on his own and seldom sent coin to the nine treasuries; he choked the two trade roads and hurt the four orders of folk.
entries.literal: He levied taxes on his own authority and rarely sent revenue to the nine treasuries; he blocked the two merchant routes and harmed the four classes of people.

entries.zh: 潛結賊異，共為表裏，同惡相求，密加應援。
entries.en: He secretly joined rebel Liu Yi, outer and inner as one coat; alike in evil, they answered each other in secret.
entries.literal: He secretly joined the rebel Yi, inside and outside as one garment; seeking the same evil, they aided each other in secret.

entries.zh: 謂我六軍薄伐，三越未寧，屠破述城，虜縛妻息，分襲湓鎮，稱兵蠡邦，拘逼酋豪，攻圍城邑，幸國有備，應時衄殄。
entries.en: He judged our six hosts' light campaign and the three Yue still restless—yet when we broke Shucheng, seized wives and children, and struck the Pencheng garrison separately, he raised arms in the Li lands, coerced chiefs, and besieged towns; the state was ready, and he was crushed at once.
entries.literal: He thought our six armies' shallow campaign and the three Yue not yet settled—when we slaughtered and broke Shucheng, bound wives and children, and separately struck the Pencheng garrison, he raised arms in the Li country, coerced tribal chiefs, and besieged walled cities; fortunate that the state was prepared, he was beaten and destroyed at once.

entries.zh: 陳書卷三十五
entries.en: Book of Chen, Volume 35
entries.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 35

entries.zh: 始興王叔陵字子嵩，高宗之第二子也。
entries.en: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, styled Zisong, was Emperor Gaozong's second son.
entries.literal: Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, styled Zisong, was the second son of Emperor Gaozong.

entries.zh: 梁承聖中，高宗在江陵為直閤將軍，而叔陵生焉。
entries.en: During Liang's Chengsheng reign, Emperor Gaozong was at Jiangling as direct-gate general when Shuling was born.
entries.literal: In the Chengsheng era of Liang, Emperor Gaozong was at Jiangling as direct-gate general, and Shuling was born there.

entries.zh: 江陵陷，高宗遷關右，叔陵留于穰城。
entries.en: After Jiangling fell, Emperor Gaozong withdrew to Guanzhong while Shuling stayed behind at Rangcheng.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Gaozong removed to Guanzhong; Shuling remained at Rangcheng.

entries.zh: 高宗之還也，以後主及叔陵為質。
entries.en: On Emperor Gaozong's return, the Last Ruler and Shuling were held as hostages.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozong returned, the Last Ruler and Shuling were left as hostages.

entries.zh: 天嘉三年，隨後主還朝，封康樂侯，邑五百戶。
entries.en: In Tianjia year 3 he followed the Last Ruler home to court and was made Marquis of Kangle with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianjia, he followed the Last Ruler back to court, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 及高宗不豫，太子諸王並入侍疾。
entries.en: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, the crown prince and all princes came in to attend him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gaozong fell ill, the crown prince and all the princes entered to attend the sickness.

entries.zh: 高宗崩于宣福殿，翌日旦，後主哀頓俯伏，叔陵以剉藥刀斫後主中項。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong died in the Hall of Extending Blessings; at dawn the next day, as the Last Ruler lay prostrate in grief, Shuling struck him in the back of the neck with a medicine knife.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong died in the Hall of Extending Blessings; on the morrow at dawn, as the Last Ruler in grief collapsed prostrate, Shuling with a medicine-grinding knife hacked the Last Ruler in the nape of the neck.

entries.zh: 太后馳來救焉，叔陵又斫太后數下。
entries.en: The empress dowager rushed to save him; Shuling hacked her several times as well.
entries.literal: The empress dowager rushed to save him; Shuling also hacked the empress dowager several times.

entries.zh: 後主乳媼吳氏，時在太后側，自後掣其肘，後主因得起。
entries.en: The Last Ruler's wet nurse, Lady Wu, stood beside the empress dowager and pulled his elbow from behind, so the Last Ruler was able to rise.
entries.literal: The Last Ruler's wet nurse, Lady Wu, was then at the empress dowager's side; from behind she pulled his elbow, and the Last Ruler was thereby able to rise.

entries.zh: 叔陵仍持後主衣，後主自奮得免。
entries.en: Shuling still clutched the Last Ruler's robe, but the Last Ruler wrenched free.
entries.literal: Shuling still held the Last Ruler's garment; the Last Ruler by struggling broke free.

entries.zh: 長沙王叔堅手搤叔陵，奪去其刀，仍牽就柱，以其褶袖縛之。
entries.en: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian grappled Shuling, snatched away his knife, dragged him to a pillar, and bound him with his own robe sleeve.
entries.literal: Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian seized Shuling by hand, wrested away his knife, and still dragged him to a pillar and bound him with the sleeve of his robe.

entries.zh: 時吳媼已扶後主避賊，叔堅求後主所在，將受命焉。
entries.en: By then Lady Wu had helped the Last Ruler escape; Shujian looked for the Last Ruler to receive orders.
entries.literal: By then Lady Wu had already helped the Last Ruler flee the assailant; Shujian sought where the Last Ruler was, intending to receive his command.

entries.zh: 叔陵因奮袖得脫，突走出雲龍門，馳車還東府，呼其甲士，散金銀以賞賜，外召諸王將帥，莫有應者，唯新安王伯固聞而赴之。
entries.en: Shuling shook free his sleeve, bolted out the Cloud Dragon Gate, raced to the Eastern Mansion, rallied his guards, scattered gold and silver as bounty, and called the princes and generals—but only Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu came when he heard.
entries.literal: Shuling then by flinging his sleeve broke free, burst out through the Cloud Dragon Gate, galloped in his carriage back to the Eastern Mansion, called up his armored men, scattered gold and silver as reward, and summoned the princes and generals from outside—but none responded except Prince of Xin'an Chen Bogu, who on hearing came to join him.

entries.zh: 叔陵少機辯，徇聲名，彊梁無所推屈。
entries.en: As a youth Shuling was sharp and argumentative, hungry for fame, and so overbearing that no one could stand up to him.
entries.literal: Shuling in youth was quick-witted and disputatious, pursued reputation, and was overbearing—none could make him yield.

entries.zh: 光大元年，除中書侍郎。
entries.en: In the first year of Guangda he was made vice director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangda, he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二年，出為持節、都督江州諸軍事、南中郎將、江州刺史。
entries.en: In year 2 he went out bearing the staff, as commander of Jiang military affairs, southern central-guard general, and inspector of Jiang.
entries.literal: In the second year, he went out as credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in Jiang province, southern central-guard general, and inspector of Jiang.

entries.zh: 太建元年，封始興郡王，奉昭烈王祀。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian he was made Prince of Shixing to carry on the sacrifices to Prince Zhaolie.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing to maintain the cult of Prince Zhaolie.

entries.zh: 進授使持節、都督江郢晉三州諸軍事、軍師將軍，刺史如故。
entries.en: He was further granted the credential staff, command over Jiang, Ying, and Jin, and the rank of army mentor general while keeping the inspectorate.
entries.literal: He was further given the credential staff, command of all military affairs in Jiang, Ying, and Jin provinces, and the post of army mentor general; his inspectorate was unchanged.

entries.zh: 叔陵時年十六，政自己出，僚佐莫預焉。
entries.en: Shuling was then sixteen; policy came only from him, and his aides were shut out.
entries.literal: Shuling was then sixteen; government issued from himself alone, and his staff had no part in it.

entries.zh: 性嚴刻，部下懾憚。
entries.en: He was harsh by nature, and his subordinates lived in dread.
entries.literal: By nature he was harsh and severe; his subordinates were awed and fearful.

entries.zh: 諸公子姪及罷縣令長，皆逼令事己。
entries.en: Imperial nephews and dismissed county and prefectural heads alike were forced into his service.
entries.literal: The various princes' sons and nephews and dismissed county magistrates and prefects were all forced to serve him.

entries.zh: 豫章內史錢法成詣府進謁，即配其子季卿將領馬仗，季卿慚恥，不時至，叔陵大怒，侵辱法成，法成憤怨自縊而死。
entries.en: When Yuzhang inner administrator Qian Facheng came to the princely residence to pay court, Shuling immediately detailed Facheng's son Jiqing to lead horse and arms. Jiqing, mortified, delayed; Shuling flew into a rage and abused Facheng until Facheng, bitter and aggrieved, hanged himself.
entries.literal: Yuzhang inner administrator Qian Facheng came to the mansion to pay his respects; Shuling at once assigned Facheng's son Jiqing to lead horse equipage; Jiqing, ashamed, did not come in good time; Shuling in great anger insulted and humiliated Facheng, and Facheng in resentment and grievance hanged himself and died.

entries.zh: 州縣非其部內，亦徵攝案治之，朝貴及下吏有乖忤者，輒誣奏其罪，陷以重辟。
entries.en: He even hauled in and prosecuted counties and prefectures outside his command; any court noble or petty official who offended him he would falsely denounce and trap in a capital sentence.
entries.literal: Counties and prefectures outside his jurisdiction he also summoned and tried; court nobles and lower officials who crossed him he at once falsely memorialized for crimes and trapped them in capital punishment.

entries.zh: 尋進號雲麾將軍，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to cloud-banner general with the added title of scattered-cavalry regular attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced in rank to cloud-banner general and given the additional post of scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

entries.zh: 三年，加侍中。
entries.en: In year 3 he was also made palace attendant.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was given the additional post of palace attendant.

entries.zh: 四年，遷都督湘衡桂武四州諸軍事、平南將軍、湘州刺史，侍中、使持節如故。
entries.en: In year 4 he was moved to command Xiang, Heng, Gui, and Wu, made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiang, while retaining palace attendant and the credential staff.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to command all military affairs in Xiang, Heng, Gui, and Wu provinces, made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiang; palace attendant and credential staff were unchanged.

entries.zh: 諸州鎮聞其至，皆震恐股慄。
entries.en: Garrisons throughout the provinces shook with terror when they heard he was coming.
entries.literal: When the garrisons of the provinces heard he was coming, all trembled in terror, their legs shaking.

entries.zh: 叔陵日益暴橫，征伐夷獠，所得皆入己，絲毫不以賞賜。
entries.en: Shuling grew daily more brutal; on campaigns against the Yi he kept every prize for himself and never gave the least reward.
entries.literal: Shuling daily grew more violent and overbearing; in campaigns against the Yi tribesmen everything taken went into his own purse—he never rewarded with the slightest share.

entries.zh: 徵求役使，無有紀極。
entries.en: His demands for labor and corvée knew no bounds.
entries.literal: His levies for labor and service had no limit or end.

entries.zh: 夜常不臥，燒燭達曉，呼召賓客，說民間細事，戲謔無所不為。
entries.en: He seldom slept at night, kept candles burning till dawn, called in guests, and gossiped over village trifles, joking without restraint.
entries.literal: At night he often did not lie down; he burned candles until dawn, summoned guests, and spoke of petty matters among the people—jest and banter of every sort.

entries.zh: 性不飲酒，唯多置餚胾，晝夜食噉而已。
entries.en: He did not drink, but heaped the table with meats and ate constantly, day and night.
entries.literal: By nature he did not drink wine; he only set out many dishes of meat and ate and gnawed day and night.

entries.zh: 自旦至中，方始寢寐。
entries.en: Only from morning till noon did he finally sleep.
entries.literal: Only from dawn to midday did he finally sleep.

entries.zh: 其曹局文案，非呼不得輒自呈。
entries.en: Office papers might not be submitted unless he called for them.
entries.literal: Documents in his offices—unless summoned, clerks might not present them on their own.

entries.zh: 笞罪者皆繫獄，動數年不省視。
entries.en: Anyone flogged was thrown into prison and often left unvisited for years.
entries.literal: Those flogged for punishment were all imprisoned; for years on end he often did not look in on them.

entries.zh: 瀟、湘以南，皆逼為左右，㙻里殆無遺者。
entries.en: South of the Xiao and Xiang he pressed everyone into personal service until the hamlets were nearly emptied.
entries.literal: South of the Xiao and Xiang, he forced all into his personal service; in hamlet after hamlet almost none were left.

entries.zh: 其中脫有逃竄，輒殺其妻子。
entries.en: Any who escaped he killed along with their wives and children.
entries.literal: If among them any escaped, he at once killed their wives and children.

entries.zh: 州縣無敢上言，高宗弗之知也。
entries.en: Local officials dared not report up the chain, and Emperor Gaozong never learned of it.
entries.literal: The prefectures and counties dared not report upward; Emperor Gaozong did not know of it.

entries.zh: 尋進號鎮南將軍，給鼓吹一部，遷中衛將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to general who guards the south with a suite of pipes and drums and transferred to central guard general.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to general who guards the south and given a set of martial pipes and drums; he was moved to central guard general.

entries.zh: 九年，除使持節、都督揚徐東揚南豫四州諸軍事、揚州刺史，侍中、將軍、鼓吹如故。
entries.en: In year 9 he received the credential staff, command of Yang, Xu, Eastern Yang, and Southern Yu, and the Yangzhou inspectorate, while keeping palace attendant, his general's rank, and the pipes and drums.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed credential-bearing, commander of all military affairs in Yang, Xu, Eastern Yang, and Southern Yu provinces, and inspector of Yang; palace attendant, general, and pipes and drums were unchanged.

entries.zh: 十一年，丁所生母彭氏憂去職。
entries.en: In year 11 he left office to mourn his birth mother, Lady Peng.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he left office in mourning for his birth mother, Lady Peng.

entries.zh: 頃之，起為中衛將軍，使持節、都督、刺史如故。
entries.en: Soon he was recalled as central guard general with the same credential staff, command, and inspectorate.
entries.literal: Before long he was recalled as central guard general; credential staff, command, and inspectorate were unchanged.

entries.zh: 晉世王公貴人，多葬梅嶺，及彭卒，叔陵啟求於梅嶺葬之，乃發故太傅謝安舊墓，棄去安柩，以葬其母。
entries.en: In Jin many nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died Shuling asked to bury her there, opened Grand Tutor Xie An's old tomb, cast out An's coffin, and laid his mother in the grave.
entries.literal: In Jin times many lords and nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died, Shuling memorialized asking to bury her at Meiling. He then opened the old tomb of Grand Tutor Xie An, cast out An's coffin, and buried his mother there.

entries.zh: 初喪之日，偽為哀毀，自稱刺血寫涅槃經，未及十日，乃令庖廚擊鮮，日進甘膳。
entries.en: On the first day of mourning he faked grief, claiming he copied the Nirvana Sutra in his own blood; within ten days he had the kitchen serve fresh slaughter and daily delicacies.
entries.literal: On the first day of mourning he feigned grief and ruin, claiming he pricked his blood to copy the Nirvana Sutra; before ten days had passed he ordered the kitchen to slaughter fresh meat and daily sent rich delicacies.

entries.zh: 又私召左右妻女，與之姦合，所作尤不軌，侵淫上聞。
entries.en: He secretly summoned attendants' wives and daughters and lay with them; his conduct was utterly lawless, and word reached the throne.
entries.literal: He also secretly summoned the wives and daughters of his attendants and fornicated with them; his conduct was especially beyond the bounds, and the offense reached the emperor's ears.

entries.zh: 高宗譴責御史中丞王政，以不舉奏免政官，又黜其典籤親事，仍加鞭捶。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong rebuked censor-in-chief Wang Zheng for not reporting him, stripped Zheng of office, dismissed his recorder and personal staff, and had them flogged besides.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong reprimanded censor-in-chief Wang Zheng for failing to memorialize and report, removed Zheng from office, also dismissed his recorder and personal attendant, and still added flogging.

entries.zh: 高宗素愛叔陵，不繩之以法，但責讓而已。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozong had long favored Shuling and would not restrain him by law, only scold him.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong had long loved Shuling and did not bind him with law, but only reproved him.

entries.zh: 服闋，又為侍中、中軍大將軍。
entries.en: When mourning ended he again became palace attendant and grand general of the central army.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he again became palace attendant and grand general of the central army.

entries.zh: 尚書八座奏曰：「逆賊故侍中、中軍大將軍、始興王叔陵，幼而很戾，長肆貪虐。
entries.en: The eight secretariat ministers memorialized: "The traitor, the late palace attendant and grand general of the central army, Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, was savage from childhood and in manhood wallowed in greed and cruelty.
entries.literal: The eight seats of the Secretariat memorialized: "The rebel traitor, the late palace attendant and grand general of the central army, Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling, was perverse in youth and in age indulged greed and cruelty.

entries.zh: 出撫湘南，及鎮九水，兩藩甿庶，掃地無遺。
entries.en: As governor south of Xiang and later on the Nine Waters, he left both regions' common folk swept bare.
entries.literal: Sent out to pacify south of Xiang and when he held the Nine Waters, in both jurisdictions the common people were swept clean, none left.

entries.zh: 蜂目豺聲，狎近輕薄，不孝不仁，阻兵安忍，無禮無義，唯戮是聞。
entries.en: With bee eyes and jackal voice he consorted with the worthless; unfilial, unkind, he trusted to arms and delighted in cruelty; without rite or right, only killing followed his name.
entries.literal: Bee eyes and jackal voice, intimate with the frivolous; unfilial and unkind, he relied on arms and was cruel by nature; without rites and without righteousness—only slaughter was heard of him.

entries.zh: 及居偏憂，婬樂自恣，產子就館，日月相接。
entries.en: During his mother's mourning he abandoned himself to lust; when sons were born he lodged them in guest quarters, one birth after another without pause.
entries.literal: When he dwelt in partial mourning, he gave himself to lust and pleasure; sons born, he lodged them in guest houses—day and night in succession.

entries.zh: 晝伏夜遊，恆習姦詭，抄掠居民，歷發丘墓。
entries.en: He hid by day and prowled by night, ever scheming, plundering townsfolk and opening grave after grave.
entries.literal: By day he hid, by night he roamed, constantly practicing treachery and deceit, plundering the people, repeatedly opening tombs.

entries.zh: 謝太傅晉朝佐命，草創江左，斲棺露骸，事驚聽視。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Xie had aided Jin in founding the realm and shaping the southeast; to break open his coffin and bare his bones horrified all who heard.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Xie aided Jin in founding the mandate and helped create the southeast; to chop open the coffin and expose the bones shocked every ear and eye.

entries.zh: 自大行皇帝寢疾，翌日未瘳，叔陵以貴介之地，參侍醫藥，外無戚容，內懷逆弒。
entries.en: From the day the late emperor fell ill, by the morrow he had not recovered; Shuling, in honored rank at the bedside, showed no sorrow outwardly while nursing regicide within.
entries.literal: From the time the late emperor took to his sickbed, on the morrow he did not recover; Shuling, in a position of high honor, attended the medicines—outwardly without grief, inwardly harboring regicide.

entries.zh: 大漸之後，聖躬號擗，遂因匍匐，手犯乘輿。
entries.en: When the emperor was failing, as the sacred person wailed and beat his breast, Shuling used the prostration to lay hands on the imperial person.
entries.literal: After the final decline, as the sacred person wailed and beat his breast, he took advantage of prostration and with his hand violated the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 皇太后奉臨，又加鋒刃，窮凶極逆，曠古未儔。
entries.en: When the empress dowager came in person he struck her again; such extreme villainy had no parallel in antiquity.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager came in person, he again added the blade; utterly vicious, extreme in treason—unmatched since antiquity.

entries.zh: 賴長沙王叔堅誠孝懇至，英果奮發，手加挫拉，身蔽聖躬。
entries.en: Only Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian, utterly earnest in loyalty, seized him with his own hands and shielded the emperor with his body.
entries.literal: Thanks to Prince of Changsha Chen Shujian, whose filial devotion was earnest to the utmost and whose heroic resolve flared up, who with his hands seized and crushed him and with his body shielded the sacred person.

entries.zh: 叔陵仍奔東城，招集凶黨，餘毒方熾，自害妻孥。
entries.en: Shuling still fled to the eastern quarter, rallied his ruffians, and even murdered his own wife and children.
entries.literal: Shuling still fled to the eastern city, gathered vicious partisans—the poison not yet spent—and killed his wife and children himself.

entries.zh: 雖應時梟懸，猶未攄憤怨，臣等參議，請依宋代故事，流尸中江，汙潴其室，并毀其所生彭氏墳廟，還謝氏之塋。」
entries.en: Though he was promptly beheaded, our rage is not spent. We jointly ask, as in Song precedent, to cast his corpse into mid-river, befoul his house, destroy his mother Lady Peng's tomb and shrine, and restore the Xie burial mound."
entries.literal: Though in due time he was beheaded and hung up, our indignant grief is not yet vented; we your subjects jointly deliberate and ask, following the Song dynasty precedent, to float the corpse in the middle of the river, befoul his dwelling with filth, and also destroy the tombs and temples of his birth mother Lady Peng and restore the mound of the Xie clan."

entries.zh: 制曰：「凶逆梟獍，反噬宮闈，賴宗廟之靈，時從仆滅。
entries.en: The edict read: "The traitor, more beast than man, turned to savage the inner palace; thanks to the imperial ancestors' spirits he was swiftly destroyed.
entries.literal: The edict said: "The vicious traitor, owl and cur, turned to bite the palace apartments; thanks to the imperial ancestors' spirits, he was quickly cut down.

entries.zh: [2]撫情語事，酸憤兼懷，朝議有章，宜從所奏也。」
entries.en: [2] Considering the matter in grief and speaking to the facts, bitterness and indignation fill my breast; the court's deliberation is in order, and it is fitting to follow what was memorialized."
entries.literal: When I consider the matter with feeling and speak to the facts, bitterness and indignation are both in my breast; the court deliberation has proper regulations—it is fitting to follow what was memorialized."

entries.zh: 叔陵諸子，即日並賜死。
entries.en: Shuling's sons were all ordered to die that same day.
entries.literal: Shuling's sons, that same day, were all granted death.

entries.zh: 前衡陽內史彭暠、諮議參軍兼記室鄭信、中錄事參軍兼記室韋諒、典籤俞公喜，並伏誅。
entries.en: Former Hengyang inner administrator Peng Hao, deliberation officer and recorder Zheng Xin, central recorder and recorder Wei Liang, and recorder Yu Gongxi were all put to death.
entries.literal: Former Hengyang inner administrator Peng Hao, deliberation staff officer and concurrent recorder Zheng Xin, central recorder staff officer and concurrent recorder Wei Liang, and recorder Yu Gongxi were all executed.

entries.zh: 暠，叔陵舅也，初隨高宗在關中，頗有勤效，因藉叔陵將領歷陽、衡陽二郡。
entries.en: Hao was Shuling's uncle on his mother's side; he had followed Emperor Gaozong in Guanzhong with some merit and, through Shuling's favor, held command over Liyang and Hengyang.
entries.literal: Hao was Shuling's maternal uncle; he had early followed Emperor Gaozong in Guanzhong and had considerable merit, and through Shuling's patronage commanded troops and held Liyang and Hengyang, two commanderies.

entries.zh: 信以便書記，有寵，謀謨皆預焉。
entries.en: Xin was skilled at shorthand and enjoyed favor; he took part in every plan.
entries.literal: Xin, because he was skilled in shorthand, was favored; in planning and counsel he had a part in everything.

entries.zh: 諒，京兆人，梁侍中、護軍將軍粲之子也，以學業為叔陵所引。
entries.en: Liang came from Jingzhao, son of Liang attendant-in-ordinary and protector-general Can, and was recruited by Shuling for his scholarship.
entries.literal: Liang was a native of Jingzhao, son of Liang attendant-in-ordinary and protector-general Can; he was brought in by Shuling for his learning.

entries.zh: 太建元年，進號智武將軍，尹如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Taijian he was promoted to general of intelligent martiality while keeping the Danyang post.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taijian, he was advanced to general of intelligent martiality; his governorship was unchanged.

entries.zh: 秩滿，進號翊右將軍。
entries.en: When his term expired he was promoted to general who assists the right.
entries.literal: When his term ended, he was advanced to general who assists the right.

entries.zh: 尋授使持節、都督吳興諸軍事、平東將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: Soon he received the credential staff and was made area commander of Wuxing military affairs, Pacify-the-East general, and administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: Soon he was given the credential staff, made area commander of all military affairs in Wuxing, Pacify-the-East General, and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 四年，入為侍中、翊前將軍，遷安前將軍、中領軍。
entries.en: In year 4 he entered the capital as palace attendant and forward aide general, then became pacify-the-front general and central army inspector.
entries.literal: In year 4 he entered the capital as Palace Attendant and Forward Aide General; he was moved to Pacify-the-Front General and Central Army Inspector.

entries.zh: 七年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南徐南豫南北兗四州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史。
entries.en: In year 7 he went out bearing the credential staff as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, area commander of South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, pacify-the-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In year 7 he went out with the credential staff as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, area commander of all military affairs in the four provinces South Xu, South Yu, North Xu, and North Yan, Pacify-the-North General, and Inspector of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 伯固性嗜酒，而不好積聚，所得祿俸，用度無節，酣醉以後，多所乞丐，於諸王之中，最為貧窶，高宗每矜之，特加賞賜。
entries.en: Bogu loved wine and would not save; his salary vanished without plan, and when drunk he often begged from others. Among the princes he was the poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave special gifts.
entries.literal: Bogu by nature loved wine and did not like to hoard; the salary he received was spent without measure; after deep drunkenness he often begged from others; among all the princes he was poorest, and Emperor Gaozong often pitied him and gave him special rewards.

entries.zh: 伯固雅性輕率，好行鞭捶，在州不知政事，日出田獵，或乘眠轝至於草間，輒呼民下從遊，動至旬日，所捕獐鹿，多使生致，高宗頗知之，遣使責讓者數矣。
entries.en: Bogu was frivolous by nature and fond of the whip. In his province he ignored government, hunted by day, sometimes rode a sleeping litter into the meadows, and called commoners to join him for outings that could last ten days. The deer and boar he took he mostly had brought in alive. Emperor Gaozong knew of it and sent envoys to rebuke him more than once.
entries.literal: Bogu's natural disposition was frivolous; he liked to wield the whip; in the province he paid no heed to government affairs; by day he went out hunting, sometimes riding a sleeping litter into the grass, then calling commoners to follow his excursions—often for ten days at a stretch; the deer and boar he caught he mostly had brought in alive; Emperor Gaozong knew of this fairly well and several times sent envoys to rebuke him.

entries.zh: 後主初在東宮，與伯固甚相親狎，伯固又善嘲謔，高宗每宴集，多引之。
entries.en: When the Last Ruler was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very close. Bogu was also skilled at banter, and Emperor Gaozong often summoned him to feasts.
entries.literal: When the Last Ruler was first in the Eastern Palace, he and Bogu were very intimate; Bogu was also skilled at banter and raillery; whenever Emperor Gaozong held a feast, he often had him brought in.

entries.zh: 叔陵在江州，心害其寵，陰求疵瑕，將中之以法。
entries.en: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and resented Bogu's favor; he secretly looked for faults and meant to bring him down by law.
entries.literal: Shuling was in Jiangzhou and inwardly resented Bogu's favor; he secretly sought flaws and intended to strike him down by law.

entries.zh: 及叔陵入朝，伯固懼罪，諂求其意，乃共訕毀朝賢，歷詆文武，雖耆年高位，皆面折之，無所畏忌。
entries.en: When Shuling came to court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned on him to learn his mind; together they slandered court worthies and abused civil and military men in turn—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to the face without fear.
entries.literal: When Shuling entered court, Bogu feared punishment and fawned to learn his intent; thereupon together they slandered court worthies, reviling in turn civil and military men—even elders of years and high rank they confronted to their faces, fearing nothing.

entries.zh: 伯固性好射雉，叔陵又好開發冢墓，出遊野外，必與偕行，於是情好大協，遂謀不軌。
entries.en: Bogu loved shooting pheasants and Shuling loved opening tombs; abroad in the wilds they always went together, their feelings matched, and they plotted treason.
entries.literal: Bogu by nature loved shooting pheasants; Shuling also loved opening and rifling tombs; when they went out into the wilds they always went together; their feelings therefore greatly harmonized, and they plotted rebellion.

entries.zh: 伯固侍禁中，每有密語，必報叔陵。
entries.en: Bogu attended within the palace; whenever there was a secret word he reported it to Shuling.
entries.literal: Bogu attended within the forbidden quarters; whenever there was a secret word, he always reported it to Shuling.

entries.zh: 及叔陵出奔東府，遣使告之，伯固單馬馳赴，助叔陵指揮。
entries.en: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace he sent word to Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped direct the fighting.
entries.literal: When Shuling fled to the Eastern Palace, he sent a messenger to tell Bogu; Bogu rode alone at full speed to join him and helped Shuling direct operations.

entries.zh: 知事不捷，便欲遁走，會四門已閉不得出，因同趣白楊道。
entries.en: Seeing the cause was lost, he meant to flee; the four gates were already shut and he could not leave, so together they made for Baiyang Road.
entries.literal: Knowing affairs would not succeed, he wished to flee; it happened that the four gates were already shut and he could not get out, so together they made for Baiyang Road.

entries.zh: 臺馬
entries.en: Platform horse
entries.literal: Platform horse

entries.en: Collation variant: (guest).
entries.literal: (guest)

entries.zh: 容至，為亂兵所殺，尸於東昌館門，時年二十八。
entries.en: When the court cavalry arrived, he was killed by mutinous troops; his body lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.
entries.literal: Rong arrived; he was killed by mutinous troops; his corpse lay at the gate of the Dongchang hostel; he was twenty-eight.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「伯固同茲悖逆，殞身途路。
entries.en: An edict said, "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Bogu shared in this rebellion and perished on the road.

entries.zh: 今依外議，意猶弗忍，可特許以庶人禮葬。」
entries.en: Following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may be buried with commoner rites as a special grace."
entries.literal: Now, following outside opinion, our mind still cannot bear it; he may specially be allowed burial with commoner rites."
